standard.npc: Welcome to the Emir's Arena! Are you interested in 1v1 Tournaments? We organise ranked Tournaments here, or alternatively you can organise your own unranked Tournaments.

steps.npc: A group of fighters is divided into pairs of opponents, and they all fight their opponent. The winners of those fights proceed to the next round, where they're divided into pairs, and they each fight their new opponent.
The number of surviving fighters is halved each time, until eventually only one person is left standing. They're the winner of the Tournament.

steps.text: other

options.text: Ranked or unranked? What does that mean?

steps.player: Ranked or unranked? What does that mean?

steps.npc: Everyone has a rank. It's meant to indicate how good they are at fighting, compared to other people.
In ranked fights, the winners gain rank and the losers lose rank. The Arena staff will decide who'll be fighting in each ranked Tournament, and send the invitations.
But if you just want some casual fun, you can have an unranked Tournament, where no-one gains or loses rank. You can organise your own unranked Tournament, and decide for yourself who'll fight in it.
Only the ranked fights offer access to the other rewards of the Arena.

options.text: How do I get invited into a Tournament?

steps.player: How do I get invited into a Tournament?

steps.npc: You'll need to sign up to a recruitment group...

steps.text: This is the icon for the Grouping tab. Within it you'll find the PvP Arena options.
There, you can click Find to seek the official group for ranked Tournaments. Alternatively, you could look for another player's group, for an unranked Tournament.
Once you've found a suitable group for you, click Sign up to sign up to it, and you'll be considered for an invitation to a Tournament, whenever one begins.

steps.npc: You can carry on with your adventures while you're waiting for a Tournament to begin, since it may be a while before suitable fighters are available.

steps.npc: I'm Abigaila, from Morytania. It's a terrible place, run by the vampyres. They visit the towns and collect everyone's blood for food!
I tried for years to escape, with my son, Suro, to make a better life for ourselves in Misthalin. I scraped together enough money to bribe a boatman to get us out.
The journey was tough. Some men in pink hoods attacked our boat, shouting at us to go back where we belonged, and to keep out of their country. In the struggle, the boat overturned.
It was dark, and I couldn't find Suro in the water. I swam as deep as I could, until my lungs screamed, but I couldn't find him. He wasn't good at swimming.
Eventually I got myself to the shore. The sun was rising, and I found Suro there. On the shore, where the water had dumped his... body.
sob*
I've done alright in Misthalin, I guess. I know a bit of magic, and the local gentry pay me well for my scrying skills. I'm good at turning a profit on Grand Exchange trades too.
Anyway, I'm able to rent a room in Lumbridge, and to buy food. I'm not being a burden on anyone, and there are no vampyres coming for my blood.
I am free!
But I haven't forgotten my people in the east. There's one vampyre there who runs a place she calls the Theatre of Blood, challenging humans to face monsters in her arena.
My husband went there, trying to win freedom from the blood-gatherers by surviving her arena, but he never returned. No-one does.
So now I pass my spare time scrying on the Theatre of Blood, watching other adventurers there. You can have a look, if you like.

options.text: How can I keep my account secure?

steps.player: How can I keep my account secure?

steps.npc: There are many ways you can strengthen your account security, which would you like to hear more about?
Your password is the first line of defence in keeping your account secure.
When choosing a password, make sure to keep it unique. You can do this by using a mix of letters and numbers. You could even use numbers in the middle of your password.
For extra security, you should make sure you use a different password for your account and email.
You should keep your password safe and tell no one. Not even your friends or family.
Is there anything else you would like to know?

steps.text: other

options.text: Tell me about securing my email.

steps.player: Tell me about securing my email.

steps.npc: Make sure you use a separate password for your email account. This will help boost your security and make it less likely for hijackers to steal your account.
You should also enable two-step authentication on your email account, if your email supports it.
This could be done through an authenticator app supplied by your email provider, or it could be done using your mobile phone number.
The type of authenticator changes based on provider, but when active, hijackers will find it hard to access your account. Also, if you get any backup codes, keep them safe.
Is there anything else you would like to know?

steps.text: other

steps.npc: The RuneScape authenticator will provide your account with another layer of security against hijackers who might want to steal your account.
As well as requiring a password to enter your account, you will also need a randomly generated number from the authenticator app to login.
You can enable the authenticator by checking your account page on the official RuneScape website.
If you like, I can take you to a useful web page about the RuneScape authenticator.

options.text: How do I manage the kingdom?

steps.player: How do I manage the kingdom?

steps.npc: Your loyal subjects work hard to collect resources for you. Every day they bring what they have collected to the castle. The resources which they collect are coal from the rocks to the north, maple logs from the trees

to the east, herbs from the garden just outside the castle, and tuna and swordfish fished at the port to the south. Etceteria has also pledged you teak and mahogany logs from their trees to the north, and seeds

from their farm to the south. They are paid from the money in the coffers; each day, one-tenth of the money in the coffers is distributed to them. A maximum of 75k is paid to your subjects and the Etceterians, and the

coffers can store up to 7.5 million gp. Another thing which affects the amounts of resources collected is your approval rating. The more your subjects love you, the more they will be motivated to work hard. King Vargas

would often go and help out his subjects in their daily tasks, when he was still able to do so, and they loved him dearly for it. Finally, you can choose how much of their efforts your subjects devote to each resource; of
course, the harder they work at collecting one, the less time they have to spend collecting the others.

recognised as the highest skilled in the land at any particular skill.

steps.player: What's the Dummy Room all about?

steps.npc: Ahh yes, the dummies. Another ingenious invention of the noble Dwarf Gamfred. They're mechanical you see and pop up out of the floor. You have to hit them with the correct attack mode before they disappear again.

steps.player: So how do I tell which one is which?

steps.npc: There are two different ways. One indication is their colour, the other is the pose and weapons they are holding, for instance, the one holding daggers you will need to hit with a piercing attack.
In the room you will find a poster on the wall which can help you recognise each different dummy.
Indeed, you may find that you need several weapons to be successful 100% of the time, but keep trying. The weapons shop upstairs may help you there.

steps.player: What do I have to do in this room?

steps.npc: In this room you will see various cupboards. It is your task to search the cupboards to find items to turn into gold using your low or high alchemy spells. You can deposit the money in the receptacle at the end of the

hall in order to receive your Alchemist Pizazz Points. This money is used for the upkeep of the training arena as well as magic shops all around Gielinor. Keep an eye on the costs of each item as these will change
from time-to-time, as will the location of the items. Occasionally one of the items will be indicated as costing no runestones to convert to money.

You will get magic experience from casting the alchemist spells, as well as 1 Alchemist Pizazz Point for every 100 coins you deposit, and 10% of the coins you deposit will be given to you as you leave. Keep in mind that you
will not be able to take more than 1000 coins back out with you.

options.text: Can you give me any farming advice?

steps.player: Can you give me any farming advice?

steps.npc: You can put up to five tomatoes, strawberries, apples, bananas or oranges into a fruit basket, although you can't have a mix in the same basket.

There are seven main Farming areas - Elstan's area near Falador, Dantaera's area near Catherby, Kragen's area near Ardougne, Lyra's area in Morytania, Marisi's area in Hosidius, Alan's area in the Farming Guild and
Oswallt's area in Prifddinas.
Supercompost is far better than normal compost, but more expensive to make. You need to rot the right type of item; show me an item, and I'll tell you if it's super- compostable or not.
Vegetables, hops and flowers need constant watering - if you ignore my advice, you will sooner or later find yourself in possession of a dead farming patch.
There is a special patch for growing Belladonna - I believe that it is somewhere near Draynor Manor, where the ground is a tad 'unblessed'.

Hops are good for brewing ales. I believe there's a brewery up in Keldagrim somewhere, and I've heard rumours that a place called Phasmatys used to be good for that type of thing. 'Fore they all died, of course.
Bittercap mushrooms can only be grown in a special patch in Morytania, near the Mort Myre swamp. There the ground is especially dank and suited to growing poisonous fungii.
You can buy all the farming tools from farming shops, which can be found close to the allotments.
Tree seeds must be grown in a plantpot of soil into a sapling, and then transferred to a tree patch to continue growing to adulthood.
The only way to cure a bush or tree of disease is to prune away the diseased leaves with a pair of secateurs. For all other crops I would just apply some plant-cure.
You can fill plantpots with soil from any empty patch, if you have a gardening trowel.
If you need to be rid of your fruit trees for any reason, all you have to do is chop them down and then dig up the stump.
Don't just throw away your weeds after you've raked a patch - put them in a compost bin and make some compost.
Applying compost to a patch will not only reduce the chance that your crops will get diseased, but you will also grow more crops to harvest.
If you want to make your own sacks and baskets you'll need to use the loom that's near the Farming shop in Falador. If you're a good enough craftsman, that is.
You don't have to buy all your plantpots you know, you can make them yourself on a pottery wheel. If you're a good enough craftsman, that is.
You can put up to ten potatoes, cabbages or onions in vegetable sacks, although you can't have a mix in the same sack.

steps.player: Could I have a Construction guide book?

steps.text: If the player has a guide book in their inventory:

steps.npc: You've already got one!

steps.text: If the player does not have enough inventory space:

steps.npc: Not until you free up some inventory space.
Certainly.

steps.text: a Construction guide

steps.npc: It all came out of the wizards' experiments. They found a way to fold space, so that they could pack many acres of land into an area only a foot across.
They created several folded-space regions across Gielinor. Each one contains hundreds of small plots where people can build houses.

steps.player: Ah, so that's how everyone can have a house without them cluttering up the world!

steps.npc: Quite. The wizards didn't want to get bogged down in the business side of things so they hired me to sell the houses.
There are various other people across Gielinor who can help you furnish your house.
You should start by buying planks from a sawmill operator. Sawmills are located in north-east Varrock, the Woodcutting Guild located in south-west Hosidius and north-east Prifddinas.

options.text: Tell me about that skillcape you're wearing.
options.condition: If player doesn't have level 99 Construction:

steps.player: Tell me about that skillcape you're wearing.

steps.npc: As you may know, skillcapes are only available to masters in a skill. I have spent my entire life building houses and now I spend my time selling them! As a sign of my abilities I wear this Skillcape of Construction.
If you ever have enough skill to build a demonic throne, come and talk to me and I'll sell you a skillcape like mine.
The Cape of Construction also provides you with as many teleports as you like to any of the house portals or even directly inside!

options.text: Can you sell me a Skillcape of Construction?
options.condition: If player has level 99 Construction:

steps.player: Can you sell me a Skillcape of Construction?

steps.npc: Alright, that'll be 99000 coins, please. A small price to pay for such an illustrious cape that can teleport you to any of the house portals or even directly inside your house!
Suit yourself. There are many other heroes who would love the opportunity to purchase one. You can find me here if you change your mind.

steps.text: If the player does not have at least 99,000 coins:

steps.player: But, unfortunately, I don't have enough money with me.

steps.npc: Well, come back and see me when you do.

steps.text: If the player has at least 99,000 coins but not enough inventory space:

steps.npc: Unfortunately all Skillcapes are only available with a free hood, it's part of a skill promotion deal; buy one get one free, you know. So you'll need to free up some inventory space before I can sell you one.

steps.text: If the player has at least 99,000 coins and enough inventory space:
a Construction cape and hood

steps.npc: Excellent! Wear that cape with pride my friend.

standard.npc: Hello, if you've something important to tell me, be out with it! I'm a busy woman.

steps.npc: How very nice of you. However, I'm sure there are less busy people who'd love to chat.
Chin up love and go adventure, that's what you lot do right?
I'm Alyssa the housekeeper and this castle needs constant attention! I've enough trouble with the guards messing up my carpets without you adding to the problem.

steps.player: Hmm, yeah sorry about that. Speaking of carpets, ever thought how strange that there are carpets beneath the stairs?

steps.npc: It's cut to fit! If I had a gold piece for everytime I was asked that question!

steps.player: Sure... Cut to fit... Not an oversight at all.

steps.npc: Alright, believe what you like. I've a castle to clean.

using-kharedst-s-memoirs-on-her.player: Are you the Alyssa this entry mentions?
Got anything to say about it?

using-kharedst-s-memoirs-on-her.npc: Why should I tell you anything? There are private matters of a late royal family! It wouldn't be proper to divulge such information to an adventurer like you.

using-kharedst-s-memoirs-on-her.text: If the player has not added all six missing pages of the memoir:

steps.player: ...Most people don't know when to stop sharing. I guess you have a point though.

steps.npc: Yes, I do indeed. Off with you, I've had my fair share of nosy adventurers for one day.

steps.player: Alright, sorry for disturbing you. Bye.

steps.npc: Bye.

using-kharedst-s-memoirs-on-her.text: If the player has added all six pages of the memoir:

steps.player: ...Most people don't know when to stop sharing. It's probably worth mentioning that I've found all entries of this memoir.

steps.npc: Yes, how did you come across this? I'm fairly certain it was destroyed... At least, I recall seeing a man removing the pages...

steps.player: Honestly, I've never really questioned it. I do things for people and they give me things.

steps.npc: Well, I suppose if you've already nosily rifled through the princesses personal memoirs, I can tell you a little more.

steps.player: Fantastic! I've got to say, there's some great little gems in this old book. I think I'm unravelling a great mystery!

steps.npc: Well, if I were you I'd keep shush on the whole matter.
You must be new here. When the king died, everyone assumed the princess would take the throne when she came of age.
Indeed, and poor young Rose was shipped off and labelled as crazy.
I do very much miss her, but one can't change the past.

steps.player: What if I were to say she's still out there! Read this entry that I found hidden within a secret part of the memoir.

steps.npc: I'm sorry adventurer, but what does this prove exactly? For all you know someone else wrote this to mislead you.

steps.player: Ah, you do make a good point...

steps.npc: If she did write this I'm afraid to say she must be mad after all.
Are all adventurers as dense as you? If you were in danger, do you really think leaving a hidden message in an old lost book for any stranger to pick up is the best way to get help?

steps.player: It's certainly peculiar, but it should be investigated regardless. Y'know, just in case...

steps.npc: Alright, spring the trap! Don't come crying to me when it all turns sour.

steps.player: Don't you worry! I'm a brave adventurer with a damsel in distress to rescue! This is my bread and butter.

steps.npc: Yes, yes, of course. Well, I'd be glad to hear of her being safe but perhaps you should heed the warning.
Tread carefully.

steps.player: Oh, of course! Thanks for chatting with me Alyssa, I'll see you around.

steps.npc: Farewell.

using-any-other-item-besides-kharedst-s-.npc: I'm sorry, but I'm not paid to serve every lazy adventurer who walks their dirty feet through my halls!

steps.speaker: Ur-tag
steps.text: For trade, and for fostering goodwill between races! I am sure that it will benefit both our races.

steps.npc: It's funny... whenever we dwarves have ventured onto the surface, we've found ourselves at war with the goblins there.
But now we meet these goblins underground, and they're no threat at all. Maybe this will herald a change in our relations with the surface goblins as well.
I can't stand these goblins sometimes! I come up with suggestions to make their city more efficient, and they just say it would spoil their precious way of life!
Trade with the goblins is going well at the moment. It's a pity they don't seem as interested in our beer as in your food, though!
Thank you again for helping us complete the train link. Further delays would have cost the Consortium a lot of money.
Oh, and I hear you saved someone's life as well. Well done on that count too.
I miss Keldagrim. This city is all very well, but no one makes an underground city like the dwarves!

standard.npc: Hello. Do you need something?

standard.player: Nope. Just thought I'd say hi.

during-dragon-slayer-ii.player: Hello there. Have you heard of Camorra?
Well she was a great hero during the Dragonkin Conflicts. I think she travelled to Kourend before the war ended. I'm trying to find out more about her.

during-dragon-slayer-ii.npc: Well Shayzien was founded by those fleeing the Dragonkin Conflicts. And the city has never been short of heroes. There's a good chance she was from Shayzien.

during-dragon-slayer-ii.player: But you've never heard of her?

during-dragon-slayer-ii.npc: No but that's not surprising. Most of our history was lost during Xeric's reign. There is somewhere you might find answers though.
The Shayzien Crypts. They were built before the kingdom even existed. Some of the oldest Shayzien heroes are buried there.

during-dragon-slayer-ii.player: Let me guess. There's a catch isn't there?

during-dragon-slayer-ii.npc: I'm afraid so. For hundreds of years, the crypts have been overrun by the dead. We've tried clearing them out but they just come back again.

during-dragon-slayer-ii.player: Well thankfully I'm afraid of no ghost. Where do I start?

during-dragon-slayer-ii.npc: They're zombies, not ghosts. You'll find the entrance to the crypts in the Graveyard of Heroes, south of our chapel. Be careful.

during-dragon-slayer-ii-talking-to-ameli.player: Hello there. Have you heard of Camorra?

during-dragon-slayer-ii-talking-to-ameli.npc: I'm sure we've already spoken about this.

during-dragon-slayer-ii-talking-to-ameli.player: We probably have. I'm very forgetful.

during-dragon-slayer-ii-talking-to-ameli.npc: The most likely place to find answers is the Shayzien Crypts. You'll find the entrance in the Graveyard of Heroes, south of our chapel. Be careful, it's filled with zombies.

standard.speaker: Amelia
standard.text: Greetings and welcome to my seed shop. Do you want to buy some seeds?

standard.npc: Greetings, young one, how may I be of assistance?

steps.npc: My name is Amergin and this here is my canoe station.

steps.player: What does a wizard want with a canoe station?

steps.npc: I am not a mere wizard, I am a druid. I once belonged to the tower next to me, but not anymore. They are a bit of a crazy bunch, so instead I keep them at bay and look after this canoe station as well.
Want to know more about canoes?
No problem, come back anytime.

options.text: Can you teach me about canoes?

steps.player: Could you teach me about canoes?

steps.text: With 1-11 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: No I can't, I sense you lack the experience to make any canoe. You will need to keep training with the axe.
Once you do, you will be able to make a canoe to travel the river.

steps.text: With 12-26 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: Of course I can, use your axe to chop down this tree here. You may then use your axe to shape the log into a canoe.

By the looks of it, you do not contain the required knowledge to build more than a log. This won't get you very far. Practice some more with the axe and you'll be able to make sturdier canoes one day.

steps.text: With 27-41 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: Of course I can, use your axe to chop down this tree here. You may then use your axe to shape the log into a canoe.
Hmm, it seems you should be able to make a reasonably durable canoe with your knowledge. A dugout, to be precise.

steps.player: How far will I be able to go in a dugout canoe?

steps.npc: Around two stops before it will meet its end.

steps.text: With 42-56 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: Of course I can, use your axe to chop down this tree here. You may then use your axe to shape the log into a canoe.
Hmm good, I sense you are one that should be able to make a decent canoe.

steps.player: Really, how far will I be able to go?

steps.npc: Very far, although it will not reach the whole way down the river.

steps.text: With 57-99 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: Of course I can, use your axe to chop down this tree here. You may then use your axe to shape the log into a canoe.
I see it, you have the makings of a woodsman? You will be able to craft nothing but the best canoes that will get you anywhere along the river!

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Hey I'm Amy, how may I help you?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: What do you do here?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: I'm the founder of Mahogany Homes, Gielinor's first Construction company!
We've currently got branches in Falador, Varrock, Hosidius and Ardougne.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: So people contact you for help with their homes?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Yep! They'll get in contact if they want assistance, whether it's fixing parts of their house or requesting nicer furniture, and then we will go and help them out.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: That sounds quite enjoyable and satisfying to do, are you hiring at all?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: If you have the supplies, I can tell you where one of our clients is that needs some work doing.

standard.npc: Welcome to the Moonrise Brewery and Winery, the oldest and largest producer of alcohol in all of Varlamore.

steps.npc: Certainly!

options.text: Could you tell me more about this place?

steps.player: Could you tell me more about this place?

steps.npc: Of course! The Moonrise Winery was originally opened over 400 years ago by Bracus Ramio.
While we originally started off as just a winery, the brewing side of the business was established by Bracus' grandson, Ludovic, when he created the now famous sunbeam ale!

steps.player: So it was a family business? Do the family still own it today?

steps.npc: Unfortunately not. Ludovic found himself in a tragic and unexpected wine-related incident before ever having children himself. After his death, the business was taken over by a collective.
That's right. Some of the most influential people all across Varlamore have a stake in the Moonrise Brewery and Winery these days, though most prefer to stay anonymous.
Ah, well their reasoning is something only they know.

steps.player: I see. Thanks for the information.

steps.npc: Not at all. Now, is there anything else I can do for you?

options.text: I'd better be on my way.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-not-.npc: Cleaning, cleaning, always cleaning. This apprenticeship isn't all that it was cracked up to be.
Oh, Aadeela, the sorceress upstairs, said she'd teach me magic, she did. And here I am scrubbing floors without a spell to help me.

options.text: I could cast a Water Blast or a Wind Blast spell?

steps.player: I could cast a Water Blast or a Wind Blast spell to hurry things along if you'd like?

steps.npc: No, no, she'd kill me or worse if she knew I was using Magic to do chores. Her last apprentice - well I'd rather not say.

steps.player: Oh go on, what happened to them?

steps.npc: They say she turned them into little spiders.

steps.player: Oh, that's too bad. I had better leave you to it.

options.text: Surely there must be upsides to the task?

steps.player: Surely there must be upsides to the task?

steps.npc: Nope. Clean this, clean that. When I'm finished cleaning here I have to go help out in the garden.
Oh, I shouldn't have told you.
Well, if you don't mind then, I'm busy and have to get back to work.

options.text: Oh, you can talk to me. I can see you're having a bad day.

steps.player: Oh, you can talk to me. I can see you're having a bad day.

steps.npc: You know you're right. Nobody listens to me.

options.text: I can't blame them, all you do is whine.

steps.player: I can't blame them, all you do is whine.

steps.text: The apprentice is clearly hurt and ignores you.

options.text: A sympathetic ear can do wonders.

steps.player: A sympathetic ear can do wonders.

steps.npc: Yes, if I just let my frustrations out, I'd feel a lot better. Now what was I saying?

options.text: I don't know. You were whining about something or other.

steps.npc: It would take too long to explain and, to be honest, I don't really understand how it works.

standard.npc: Hello friend. I wish to slay evil and avail them of their loot! Take me to Burgh de Rott!

options.text: Are you prepared enough to fight the evil down there?

steps.npc: I think so? At least my heart knows courage and that should be sufficient for the meantime. I expect that when we get to Burgh de Rott, we'll be able to purchase suitable provisions.

steps.player: But you do realise that the vampyres in Morytania are immune to everything except silver?

steps.npc: Er...well, I've not heard mention of that fact, but I have faith that Saradomin will provide the means to furnish me with suitable weapons when I reach Burgh de Rott.

steps.player: And if we happen to run into some vampyres on the journey down there?

steps.npc: I trust that you will help us to avoid them. You are a guide after all, aren't you? Anyway, you look like you can handle yourself. I presume you've fought such creatures before and won? How hard can it be?

steps.player: It can be pretty difficult, actually. But you're right, I'll be your guide so I should be able to handle the situation.

Oh, I hate this trip, but it's better than the opulet life styles forced on us adventurer types. I'd much rather be up to my eyes in mud and having a good fight!

steps.npc: Yes, powerful artefacts of The Abyss. We have accumulated a small collection of them from all of the fighting.

steps.npc: Absolutely not. We know how powerful they are, yet their magic is too unknown to us to risk using.

steps.player: What's that rift guardian doing over there?

steps.npc: They're great, aren't they? I don't know their name, if they even have one, so I just call them Rifty.
That rift they have is a folded-space storage rift, just like the ones Traiborn uses! Small on the outside, but big on the inside!
The guardians use it to store things. If you help hold back the Abyss, they'll let you take things from the rift in return.

steps.npc: Sedridor told us to make sure there was plenty of incentive for people to help us. He also wants us to gather abyssal pearls for research purposes. I thought this would be a good way of doing both!

steps.player: So you sell things in exchange for abyssal pearls?

steps.npc: Exactly! I've got some interesting things from the Wizards' Tower, along with some cool stuff the Guardians of the Rift gave us. Want to take a look?

steps.text: other

options.text: Could you tell me more about this place.

steps.player: Could you tell me more about this place.

steps.npc: Well, I only really know what the Great Guardian told us. This is the Temple of the Eye, or at least, what's left of it. It was built long ago to house the Eye, a powerful Saradominist artefact.
Apparently, servants of some 'Fallen Empire' desired this artefact. However, in their attempt to steal it, they accidently opened a rift into a deadly area of the Abyss called the Scar.
Were it not for the Justiciar of the Lion, the rift would have endangered all of Gielinor. She used the Eye to close it and then created the Guardians of the Rift to protect this temple.
Of course, the rift is open again now, but with our help, the Guardians of the Rift are keeping it under control.
Anyway, did you want to trade?

talking-to-the-scout-in-vampyrium-s-cast.player: Hello there. What do you do around here?

talking-to-the-scout-in-vampyrium-s-cast.npc: I conduct expeditions for Father Sugadinti upon his request. When I am not busy with my duties, I help others collect or retrieve things from difficult to reach places.

talking-to-the-scout-in-vampyrium-s-cast.player: Well, there are definitely plenty of those around here. So does that mean you'd be able to retrieve some things for me if I ever needed?

talking-to-the-scout-in-vampyrium-s-cast.npc: Certainly, though I am afraid my services aren't free.
Well, Darkmeyer is always in need of more vials of blood. I am also willing to help those that show they've contributed to controlling the stymphike population here.
Of course, if neither of those are adequate, Father Sugadinti can always find a use for gold.

talking-to-the-scout-in-vampyrium-s-cast.player: Thanks, I'll keep that in mind.

steps.text: If the player has an active gravestone inside Vampyrium, but cannot afford the payment:

steps.npc: I'm afraid you lack the required payment for me to do so, my friend. I will accept either a vial of blood, 150 stymphike feathers or 50,000 coins.

steps.npc: Your gravestone does not seem to be in Vampyrium, my friend. Im afraid I am unable to retrieve it.

options.text: What is there to do around here?

steps.player: What is there to do around here?

steps.npc: Well, you have stymphikes, bloodwood trees, leechfin, venators, and of course, the Maggot King.
They are birds that prey upon many of the other creatures here. However, their population is so great that they have been causing issues for Father Sugadinti's research.
As such, we'd be grateful if you could help us control their numbers.

steps.player: And how do I do that?

steps.npc: There are some stymphike trees just east of Sangvesti. The trees are named for the birds themselves, for they like to use the spiked branches to impale their prey, giving them easy access to the blood within.
Go to those trees and bait them with something that will attract the stymphikes. We have found that letvek work best. They are small insects that you can catch across the river south of Sangvesti.

steps.player: And once I've baited the tree?

steps.npc: Find somewhere to hide nearby so the stymphikes can't see you, then strike when they come for the bait.

steps.text: other

options.text: Tell me more about bloodwood trees.

steps.player: Tell me more about bloodwood trees.

steps.npc: Well, Father Sugadinti has been using their sap in his research, but it also has other benefits that you might appreciate.
We have found that when applied to arrows, the sap makes them more powerful.

steps.player: Interesting... And how do I get this sap?

steps.npc: You will need to cut through the trunk of the tree until the sap begins to seep out. Be warned, the trees are tough, so it will take a bit more work than the trees you're probably used to.
Before you start cutting them though, make sure to put a bucket down. You'll need it to collect the sap in. Some of my fellow disciples keep buckets on hand. Seek them out if needed.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: As you've no doubt realised by now, blood is quite the commodity here in Vampyrium, and leechfin have more blood than creatures twice their size.
You can fish them in the river to the far east. Catch enough of them, and you'll be able to collect up their blood in a vial.
I believe that vials of blood are quite useful in potion making. Unsurprisingly, they are also of great use to Father Sugadinti.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Father Sugadinti believes they are the closest living relative to vampyres, making them very useful indeed. However, their population has diminished significantly. We are working to address that.

steps.player: And is that something I can help with?

steps.npc: Quite possibly. While we need to restore their numbers, it is also important we ensure only the strongest are able to breed. As such, with a Slayer Master's permission, we will allow you to slay them.
Alternatively, if you bring some stymphike feathers to either myself or one of my fellow disciples, we will allow you to kill some venators in return.

steps.text: other

options.text: Tell me more about the Maggot King.

steps.player: Tell me more about the Maggot King.

steps.npc: Ah, yes. A Maggot King is the final form of one of Vampyrium's most disgusting creatures, the ur-maggot. They are thankfully very rare, but very destructive.
Dealing with it is unfortunately beyond our abilities, but if you feel you are able, it would be highly beneficial to our work here for you to do so instead.
If you take the path north east of Sangvesti, that should lead you right to it.

steps.text: other

steps.player: Could you tell me about the old Wizards' Tower?

steps.npc: Of course. The first Wizards' Tower was built at the same time the Order of Wizards was founded. It was at the dawn of the Fifth Age, when the secrets of runecrafting were rediscovered.
For years, the tower was a hub of magical research. Wizards of all races and religions were welcomed into our order.
Alas, that openness is what ultimately led to disaster. The wizards who served Zamorak, the evil god of chaos, tried to claim our magical discoveries in his name.
They failed, but in retaliation, they burnt the entire tower to the ground. Years of work was destroyed.
The tower was soon rebuilt of course, but even now we are still trying to regain knowledge that was lost.
That's why I spend my time down here, in fact. This basement is all that is left of the old tower, and I believe there are still some secrets to discover here.
Of course, one secret I am no longer looking for is the teleportation incantation to the Rune Essence Mine. We have you to thank for that.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: Who are you?

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: Me? I am the Archpriest who was responsible for the running of this place! I am impressed that you managed to reach my resting place on the lowest level.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: Well it wasn't easy for sure. You wouldn't believe how difficult it was to overcome some of those traps.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: The intention was that they should've been impossible to pass. I should know. After all, it was I who was responsible for overseeing the safeguarding of this place.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: Why did you need the safeguards? Surely they made it more difficult to do your work down here?

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: I'm not sure if I should say... I wouldn't want to compromise the trust that the Justiciar of the Unicorn has in me. Afterall, we did what we did for the safety of Hallowvale.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: So... about that. Hallowvale no longer exists. The Hallowed Sepulchre is now beneath the vampyre capital of Darkmeyer within the lands of Morytania.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: I see... So we lost then? In that case, I suppose it doesn't hurt to tell you after all.
One day the justiciar sent word to me that I should begin work on securing the Sepulchre. He feared an invasion from the followers of the Dark Lord.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: Do you mean Zamorak?

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: Yes, I do. The justiciar said he was going to confront these forces but that I should stay to protect the secrets within this place. I wish I could have joined him on the battlefield. I carried out my duties though.
I never told the others what was really happening. Day by day we worked our way down to the final floor.
As we progressed further, we became more experienced at creating the traps. Each one was more deadly than the last.
Eventually, when our work was done, I performed the last rites for each of my followers and sealed them within the coffins on the final floor.
Finally, I did the same for myself. The knowledge of how to disarm the traps died with us.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: You buried yourselves alive? That's... horrible!

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: No, I think at that point most of us were already dead. We died knowing that we sacrificed ourselves for the good of holy Saradomin and the justiciars who follow him.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.player: Well, at the very least you succeeded at keeping the vampyres out of the Sepulchre. From what I have seen, none of them have been able to enter.

standard-dialogue-with-an-amulet-of-ghos.npc: I am glad adventurer. Perhaps that information will allow my spirit to pass on peacefully soon.

upon-using-a-ring-of-endurance-on-the-ar.npc: The Justiciar of the Unicorn bestowed it upon me to help with my work within this place.
I had to work for many hours each day to ensure that everything ran smoothly. As I got older, I found it more and more difficult.
This ring allowed me to continue my work without feeling the effects that aging was having on my body. I suppose I have no use for it now. I guess you can keep it.

upon-using-a-ring-of-endurance-on-the-ar.player: Why did you try to destroy it?

upon-using-a-ring-of-endurance-on-the-ar.npc: When I got word that we had to protect this place from the Zamorakian invaders, I was worried that the ring would fall into the wrong hands.
You don't seem to be too bad though. I hope you put the ring to good use!

steps.player: Tell me about the Calamity Coven.

steps.npc: The Calamity Coven were three brigands, followers of an ancient and derelict religion. Through their foul arts, they turned this Arena into a hotbed of corruption.
Maoma was a captain of the Emir's guard, but she abused her authority to rig fights so that the Coven would get rich at the people's expense.
Saika was the brains behind their operation, forging the Arena's accounts so that the Coven could keep all the profits, starving the Emir's public works of all funding.
Koriff used her charms to act as a gracious hostess, whipping up the crowds' excitement so that they'd gamble more and more unwisely, enriching the Coven.
The Calamity Coven are long gone now; some of their old possessions are even being sold as rewards. Now, we are here to prevent a resurgence in such crime. But is there something I can do for you?

standard.npc: Respect the souls, traveller.

options.text: Why are all these souls here?

steps.player: Why are all these souls here?

steps.npc: A corporeal body is a mere flesh-temple in which the soul dwells. As the body fails, the soul loses its home. Without guidance, it would drift into oblivion.
However, the Soul Altar provides a beacon, drawing the souls to this place where they may join the River.
The River leads the souls through unchartable realms, transcending the plane of the world as you see it, but the three-headed Guardian keeps them safe.
The souls are the dead of Kourend - ensure you respect the souls.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: I am here to salute the dead of Kourend whose souls are joining the River. Ensure you respect the souls.

steps.text: other

options.condition: If the player has not yet found the Soul bearer:

steps.player: I've been reading your book: 'The Journey of Souls'

steps.npc: Let me guess, traveller... did you come to ask me where the soul bearer was buried? Every mortal who reads my book seems to want to get their hands on it.
Mortals are so predictable. This is the kind of thinking that led that adventurer to break into the Guardian's cave and damage the soul bearer in the first place.
It occurs to me, though, that even if you dig it up, the artefact is damaged. Although the Elders of Arceuus never had the knowledge to repair it, there is one who may be able to help.
I speak of the Key Master, he who watches over the cave of the three-headed Guardian of the River. He has been there for countless years, and will have absorbed power from the River in that time.

Now, we buried the artefact in the crypt of the Arceuus church. As I have revealed this secret to you, you will no longer be affected by the spells that prevent unwary explorers from stumbling across it.

options.text: No, I don't want your smelly soul bearer.

steps.player: No, I don't want your smelly soul bearer.

steps.npc: Hmmph! So what do you want? I trust you will respect the souls while you are in this hallowed place.

steps.npc: Beginner clues are the lowest tier of clue scroll and as such only require a couple of steps to solve.
Beginner clues are gained through various activities. Those activities are as follows.
Slaying monsters for a chance at a clue being dropped. I hear goblins are sneaky, maybe they have some clue scrolls on them ripe for the taking.
Maybe someone left one in the cow field, who knows where you could obtain them.
Beginner clues have also been known to be left in geodes while mining, as well as sometimes in bottles that you may fish up from time to time and from nests which fall out of trees.
Although this is a much rarer occurrence.
Unlike more advanced clues, you should not expect to get very valuable items from completing a beginner clue.
Advanced clues have tiers between easy and master.
You can gain advanced clues the same way you would get a beginner clue. But to get higher tier scrolls you will need to defeat more powerful foes.

The chance to get a higher tier clue from geodes, bottles and nests is lower the higher the tier. But if you chop down higher-level trees you will have a higher chance of receiving a nest which contains a clue. Same with fishing and mining.
The only exception to this is master clue scrolls.
Master clues can only be obtained as a rare chance when opening your casket or by handing in one of every type of clue, apart from beginner, to Watson who resides in Hosidius.
But with more advanced tiers of clue, come better loot.

options.text: Ask about the types of clues.

steps.npc: This type of clue has you talk to someone around Gielinor. Although the clue does not tell you exactly who to talk to.
You will see a couple of words that may or may not make sense together. You will have to rearrange the letter to make the name of the person you need to talk to.
This type of clue has you work out a logical problem for the person you need to talk to. This type of challenge only appears in clue tiers medium, hard and elite.
There are also challenges that will involve you gathering an item or crafting an item for a certain person.
This type of clue has you talk to someone around Gielinor. Although the clue does not tell you exactly who to talk to. This type of challenge only appears in clue tiers medium, hard and elite.
A cipher is a string of letters that have been scrambled using the shift cipher method.
An example of this would be ZCZL which, shifted forward by one, would be Adam.
This type of clue will have you use a sextant, chart and a watch to find out the place you will need to dig. This type of challenge only appears in clue tiers medium and above.
After you find the place you need to dig, you may find a casket or another scroll.
This type of clue can be as simple as talk to the specified person or searching a crate in a specified location.
But the higher the tier of clue, the more steps you will have to do beforehand. An example of this would be needing to find a key before opening a chest.
This type of clue will give you a location that you will need to visit, along with some items you will need.
At this location you will need to perform an emote, as well as wear the items that you had to bring along.
Some clues may have you wear nothing at all.
But please don't do that in public!
This type of challenge only appears in clue tiers medium and above.
Depending on the tier of clue, you will need to obtain a strange device from either Reldo, located in Varrock, or Jorral, located south of Tree Gnome Stronghold.
You will then need to use this device to find the location you will need to dig.
There are many different puzzles that you can come across while doing clues. These range from light boxes to puzzle boxes.
Puzzle boxes are puzzles that will have you complete a slider puzzle that, when complete, will look like an image in game.
Light boxes are a puzzle which contains a 5 by 5 grid of lights with some lights on and some lights off.
The puzzle will have you click the buttons below to turn on or off some of the lights with the end goal being, having all the lights turned on.
This type of clue will show you a map of an area.
This map will show you where you will need to dig, or what you will need to search to get the next clue.
This type of clue will show you which fairy ring code you will need to use to get to the right place to dig.
You will then need to use the numbers to figure our where you will need to dig after arriving to your destination.

The entrance was hidden from sight by all these vines and stuff, and it was full of zombies and crazy tribesmen and stuff.
That wasn't the worst thing though! There were all these crazy traps that were hidden around the place too!
Well anyway, I found the secret entrance, fought my way in through the zombies and tribesmen, and came to a big pedestal with a statue of solid gold sat on top of it!
That's right! It was a cunning trap though! As soon as I picked up the statue, a trapdoor opened up underneath me, and I fell into a darkened room, full of
bones, and the biggest meanest tribesman you ever did see!
Huge he was, and real ugly looking! He had this huge sword too, and he came running towards me screaming something in some language I didn't understand!
Well, while he was screaming at me, and swinging his sword around in front of me, trying to intimidate me before attacking, I cooly and calmly...
All the while, knowing that if I died in this spot nobody would even know where I was...
I knew, if this tribesman killed me, that would be the end of Asgarnia Smith, and all of his treasure hunting...
Well, while he was screaming and waving his sword around, I stood behind a nearby stalactite, then shot him with my shortbow.
And that was how I recovered the Golden Monkey of Tee-Ta-Toh.

options.text: Tell me how you became an Archaeologist

steps.player: So... How exactly did you get into this line of work anyway?
It seems an odd choice of career for a man like yourself.

steps.npc: Thinking of joining your pal Asgarnia in the wonderful world of treasure hun- um, archaeology, huh?
Well, it all started the day I was fishing in catherby, funnily enough.
Ah yes, I remember it well... I was just sat there, hoping to catch a bass or two, when I made the most amazing discovery!
In my fishing nets, I had found an ancient casket, marred and worn by centuries underwater!
With trembling hands, I slowly and cautiously opened it, wondering what ancient secret may have been kept inside...
What valuable heirloom may have been dredged up by my nets that had not decayed underwater long ago...
And you know what I found inside?
I found 320 coins! Just like that! Just by fishing I had found 320 coins! 320 coins! Can you believe it?
Well, it might not seem much to us now kid, but back then, it was a revelation!
Why waste my time fishing when there were secret treasures from long ago hidden around the world?
I immediately applied to the Museum of Varrock as a field agent, and the rest is history!
Hey, thanks kid. Looking snazzy is an important part of being a treasure hunter!

steps.player: Well, I'll see you again sometime maybe. Sorry I couldn't get you any treasure...

steps.npc: Ah, don't sweat it kid. I'll be honest with ya - I'm already rich many times over, and its more the kicks of being a treasure hunter I do it for than the actual cash!

standard.npc: Hello, [player name].

steps.npc: Long ago, these lands were dominated by a great empire, ruled over by an ancient god. The Empty Lord is what they often called him, but his true name was Zaros.
At the height of his power, Zaros seemed untouchable, but he was eventually defeated by those he trusted the most. With him gone, the empire collapsed. War broke out soon after.
Although their god was gone, many Zarosians fought to keep his empire alive. Among them was Nex. She was Zaros' most powerful weapon, and she led a great army to try and restore his empire.
Not that she needed an army of course. Nex alone was powerful enough to hold back hundreds of lesser beings.

steps.player: So how did she end up here?

steps.npc: The forces of Saradomin knew that Nex needed to be dealt with. They were able to lure her into these caverns.
After great effort and sacrifice, they managed to place Nex and her followers into a frozen, enchanted sleep.
Once Nex was no longer an immediate threat, they built the Temple of Lost Ancients around her. Most of the temple has since fallen to ruin, but you can still see some of the remains.

steps.player: But she wasn't frozen forever, was she? You said you were fooled into freeing her.

steps.npc: Yes. Later in the war, a great battle broke out in the Temple of Lost Ancients. I was a Saradominist soldier at the time, and I was among those who fought for him in that battle.

By then, many of us had grown tired of war. One of our priests discovered this. He came to us and revealed that he felt the same way, and that he had secretly converted to Guthix. He encouraged us to join him.
We abandoned the cause of Saradomin and became followers of Guthix. Our new leader taught us the ways of the druids, including an ancient ritual that had the power to awaken Guthix himself.
We believed this ritual to be the only way to end the war.

steps.player: But I'm guessing that's not how things went?

steps.npc: No... When our leader led us to perform the ritual, it was not Guthix we woke, but Nex and her forces. The ritual also destroyed the protective enchantments on their prison.

steps.player: And that was exactly what your leader wanted?

steps.npc: It was. He had never been a follower of Guthix, or Saradomin. His real goal had always been to free Nex.

The rest is as I already told you. Nex posed such a danger, that the four armies temporarily joined forces to drive her back into the prison. They resealed it, but were unable to fix the enchantments we destroyed.

As for me, I was one of the first to fall after Nex was freed, but I didn't truly die. Something about our ritual tied me to this place. I've been trapped here ever since. Not dead, but not really alive either.
Don't be. This is the punishment for my sins.

steps.player: What of the one that led the ritual. What came of him?

steps.npc: He'd achieved his goal, so he left. I never saw him again.
He never gave us his true name, but as Nex was freed, she spoke to him.
It seemed that way. I heard little of what they said, but I did hear what she called him.
Sliske.
Forgive me, but this conversation has brought back many memories. Let us speak no more of this.

steps.npc: What am I, a historian?

steps.player: No, but you're the only dwarf here that might be willing to share that sort of information with me.

steps.npc: Hmph. Very well. The Varlamorians won't mention this, but we were the first to settle here. Our ancestors saw the writing on the wall when Xeric came to power in Kourend. They chose not to stick around.

steps.player: Must have been a big thing for them, leaving their home.

steps.npc: Doubtful. My people are all too familiar with that sort of thing. The Lovakengj dwarves have mostly forgotten their history, but we Dwarves of Cam Torum remember it all too well.
Before Lovakengj, there was Imcandoria. Our ancestors there were forced to abandon their home, just as we were forced to leave Kourend.
If you humans had had your way, we might have had to abandon Cam Torum by now as well.
But I do know that. As I said, we remember our history, and we know that those who don't are doomed to repeat it.
The Varlamorians nearly destroyed themselves in their War of Betrayal, but it was not them who were betrayed, it was us.
I was a young dwarf when their war risked destroying our home. I saw the results of their pride. Meanwhile, they've all but forgotten it.

steps.player: Sorry. I didn't mean to dig up old wounds.

steps.npc: Hmph. It's fine. Your intentions are good, [player name], which is more than can be said for most of your kind. Who knows, maybe one or two dwarves here might even grow to tolerate you.

options.text: Can you give me any farming advice?

steps.player: Can you give me any farming advice?

steps.npc: You can buy all the farming tools from farming shops, which can be found close to the allotments.
Supercompost is far better than normal compost, but more expensive to make. You need to rot the right type of item; show me an item, and I'll tell you if it's super- compostable or not.
Tree seeds must be grown in a plantpot of soil into a sapling, and then transferred to a tree patch to continue growing to adulthood.
You can put up to ten potatoes, cabbages or onions in vegetable sacks, although you can't have a mix in the same sack.
You can fill plantpots with soil from any empty patch, if you have a gardening trowel.
Bittercap mushrooms can only be grown in a special patch in Morytania, near the Mort Myre swamp. There the ground is especially dank and suited to growing poisonous fungii.
Vegetables, hops and flowers need constant watering - if you ignore my advice, you will sooner or later find yourself in possession of a dead farming patch.
You don't have to buy all your plantpots you know, you can make them yourself on a pottery wheel. If you're good enough at crafting, that is.
If you want to make your own sacks and baskets you'll need to use the loom that's near the Farming shop in Falador. If you're good enough at crafting, that is.

There are many Farming areas out there. I know of Elstan's area near Falador, Dantaera's area near Catherby, Kragen's area near Ardougne, Lyra's area in Morytania, Marisi's area in Hosidius and Alan's area in
the Farming Guild. That said, I'm sure there's plenty more that I don't know about.
If you want to grow fruit trees you could try a few places: Catherby, Brimhaven, Gnome Stronghold and the Farming Guild all have fruit tree patches.
You can put up to five tomatoes, strawberries, apples, bananas or oranges into a fruit basket, although you can't have a mix in the same basket.
There is a special patch for growing Belladonna - I believe that it is somewhere near Draynor Manor, where the ground is a tad 'unblessed'.
Applying compost to a patch will not only reduce the chance that your crops will get diseased, but you will also grow more crops to harvest.
The only way to cure a bush or tree of disease is to prune away the diseased leaves with a pair of secateurs. For all other crops I would just apply some plant-cure.
Hops are good for brewing ales. There's a brewery over on Aldarin if you fancy trying it.
Don't just throw away your weeds after you've raked a patch - put them in a compost bin and make some compost.
That depends on whether I have it to sell. What is it that you're looking for?

steps.npc: Just a few bits of information before you run away to persecute rock crabs or cows.
Firstly, your new device won't work if you are wearing certain metallic chest armours.
The magnetic attraction required for operation would cause feedback, so the device does not allow such incompatible item equip page.
Secondly, although the device is calibrated to attract only arrow heads, there is a chance that other magnetically active items will be attracted.

The arrow recovery function of the devices is slightly different and relies upon a harmonic bond between your arrows and the chicken's magnet. You'll thus only recover arrows which you have fired rather than those
fired by nearby folks.
You'll also need to move about if you want to collect arrows since the gathering of long-lost arrowheads can't work otherwise.
Finally, the device will only work when worn. It automatically deactivates in other circumstances.
I was worried about what would happen if you were to place it in a bank in its active state, so I've made sure it only works when it's on your back.

steps.npc: Wonderful!
Well, I was going through some ancient documents recently, expanding my knowledge of our great ancestors...
Hmm, actually, I think I had better go further back, so you will understand.
You know of our ancient war with the Fremennik that you recently healed?

steps.player: Of course! I am a great diplomat, aren't I?

steps.npc: Some diplomat. Did you even discover WHY we were at war for so long?

steps.player: Errr... You couldn't see eye to eye about magic, or something like that.

steps.npc: Not too far off; it goes deeper than that.
The Fremennik were actually the first to discover how to make runes, but there was disagreement within the tribe about the implications of making such powerful objects.

Most Fremennik felt we were stealing power from the gods. They could not see past that to the great things we could do with such power, so we split from them and became the Moon Clan. Our ancient leader, who first

discovered the rune essence mine here on Lunar Isle, travelled far and wide searching for more places of power. He and his followers built altars all over Gielinor - which you use today to create runes - and at their

height they made runes by the crateful. They had perfected the process and even advanced it, creating altars that could create any type of rune regardless of the crafter's ability. But the strife between the Moon

Clan and the Fremennik heightened. The Fremennik had grown strong in body, while our clan had grown stong in mind. They overpowered our tribe and we retreated to Lunar Isle, where we had lived ever since.
The Fremennik then swept over Gielinor destroying the altars we had made, in an attempt to remove all trace of magic from the land.

steps.player: That's all very interesting, but what's it got to do with this spell?

steps.npc: I'm getting to that!

The Fremennik were not as thorough as they thought. They destroyed only the entrances to the altars, for the altars themselves were on a different plane, but they were successful in wiping out our ability to create
runes. That ability has only recently been rediscovered on the mainland, so I hear.

Our people were left isolated on Lunar Isle but we used it to our advantage. Our control over Magic advanced beyond the need for runes and all knowledge of the altar locations passed from memory. Fortunately,

some records survived... The manuscript I discovered contains the teleportation spell to an advanced altar called Ourania. It's an altar that allows the user, regardless of their Runecrafting ability, to craft any
type of rune upon it. Ourania is a powerful altar indeed. What state it is in after so many millennia, I know not, but it's interesting all the same.

steps.player: So, will you teach me the spell?

steps.npc: Certainly.
*Baby Yaga whispers in your ear*

steps.text: other

options.text: What did you ask me to do again?
options.condition: After completing the "So, what do you make of all of this?" dialogue:

steps.player: What did you ask me to do again?

steps.npc: Every adventurer seems to destroy without any thought as to what they are doing, nor with any intent to restore what was lost.
If you can do that, then that would prove to me that you are infact different from the rest.

steps.player: So you want me to restore what was lost?

steps.npc: Indeed.

steps.text: other

options.condition: After properly dealing with the four MvP items and using the dawn scarab egg on the High Priest of Scabaras:

steps.npc: Oh? Do tell.

steps.player: Well, while us adventurers have been doing our best to fight against the Devourer's corruption, we've been neglecting what has been lost to achieve that goal. Namely, the four guardians we defeated along the way.
Ba-Ba was a proud baboon who wished for her troop to flourish. To honour her, I made sure that they won't be forgotten by telling their story to the monkeys of Ape Atoll.
Akkha was cruelly denied death by the Devourer, so I gave his ashes to the High Priest of Icthlarin to give him a proper send-off.
Zebak was fooled into leaving his home and confined within the tomb, so I took his fang and buried it on an island surrounded by crocodiles.
Kephri was promised a future for her race, but it was all a lie. I found a scarab egg within some of her dung, and I gave it to the High Priest of Scabaras to try and nurture it.

steps.npc: Well well, colour me impressed adventurer. It seems that you do care after all.
It's a shame that much of the damage cannot truly be undone, but I know that Het, Apmeken, Crondis and even Scabaras will be grateful for your actions.

steps.player: I just wish there was more I could do.

steps.npc: We always do, but you have still done more than most.
Now, I have something for you. I've been looking for someone worthy enough to pass this on to.

steps.text: The bank camel gives you a strange key.

steps.npc: I'll leave that as another puzzle for you to solve.

steps.player: Well thanks, I guess... You know, out of all the camels I've met, you're definitely the strangest one.

steps.npc: Well, it does take a special kind of camel to master the portal magic used for bank access.

steps.text: other

options.text: I've lost that key you gave me.

steps.npc: And it conveniently found its way back to me. Try not to lose it this time.

steps.text: The bank camel takes the grain, but quickly spits it out in disgust!

steps.npc: Bleh, this grain is disgusting! Do you think I am but a simple cow, adventurer?
This is why I eat the grain in that sack over there. It's specially grown out here in the desert. Once harvested, it goes through a preparation process of several years that...

steps.text: The bank camel talks at length about the process of producing such fine grain...

steps.npc: ...and that's why this grain is so special. Not to mention so hard to come by.

steps.text: The bank camel happily takes the grain before looking at you as if contemplating something.

steps.npc: My, this is some good grain, adventurer! Great flavour profile, not too salty and with just a hint of sweetness. It almost reminds me of...

steps.text: The bank camel looks at you for a moment as if lost in thought.

steps.npc: Oh, never mind, I was just thinking about something.

steps.text: The bank camel stares at you in silence for an uncomfortably long time.

steps.player: Well, I can't stand around here all day. I've got some things I need to take care of.

steps.text: The bank camel takes the acorn from you and stores it away.

steps.npc: I won't be eating this, but I do like to collect them. Thank you.

steps.text: You show the banana to the bank camel.

steps.npc: Quite the banana you have there! Ba-Ba and her baboon troop were always known for finding the biggest of these. It's a shame that their memory will now disappear into history.

steps.text: You show the fang to the bank camel.

You show the fang to the bank camel.

steps.npc: Ah, the fang of the mighty Zebak. What a cruel fate to be consumed by ever-lasting hunger.

steps.text: You show the ashes to the bank camel.
The bank camel looks at you with piqued interest, then rolls their eyes as they realise you can't understand them.
You show the ashes to the bank camel.

steps.npc: Ah, the ashes of Akkha, a great warrior. It's a shame that his soul never got to experience the release of death.

steps.text: You show the dung to the bank camel.

You show the dung to the bank camel.

steps.npc: Faeces! How lovely. If I'm not mistaken, this dung is from Kephri herself, last of the dawn scarabs. It's a shame that her kind have long been lost to the world.

steps.npc: Hey, get your hands off my food! Unless you'd like me to start eating the contents of your bank instead!

standard.npc: Good day, how may I help you?

options.text: How do I use the bank?

steps.player: Using the bank itself. I'm not sure how....?

steps.npc: Speak to any banker and ask to see your bank account. If you have set a PIN you will be asked for it, then all the belongings you have placed in the bank will appear in the window. To withdraw one item, left-
click on it once.

To withdraw many, right-click on the item and select from the menu. The same for depositing, left-click on the item in your inventory to deposit it in the bank. Right-click on it to deposit many of the same items.

To move things around in your bank: firstly select Swap or Insert as your default moving mode, you can find these buttons on the bank window itself. Then click and drag an item to where you want it to appear.
You may withdraw 'notes' or 'certificates' when the items you are trying to withdraw do not stack in your inventory. This will only work for items which are tradable.

For instance, if you wanted to sell 100 logs to another player, they would not fit in one inventory and you would need to do multiple trades. Instead, click the Note button to do withdraw the logs as 'certs' or 'notes',
then withdraw the items you need.

steps.player: Using Bank deposit boxes.... what are they?

steps.npc: They look like grey pillars, there's one just over there, near the desk. Bank deposit boxes save so much time. If you're simply wanting to deposit a single item, 'Use' it on the deposit box.
Otherwise, simply click once on the box and it will give you a choice of what to deposit in an interface very similar to the bank itself. Very quick for when you're simply fishing or mining etc.

options.text: What's this PIN thing that people keep talking about?

steps.player: What's this PIN thing that people keep talking about?

steps.npc: The PIN - Personal Identification Number - can be set on your bank account to protect the items there in case someone finds out your account password. It consists of four numbers that you remember and tell
no one.
So if someone did manage to get your password they couldn't steal your items if they were in the bank.

options.text: How do I set my PIN?

steps.player: How do I set my PIN?

steps.npc: You can set your PIN by talking to any banker, they will allow you to access your bank pin settings. Here you can choose to set your pin and recovery delay. Remember not to set it to anything personal such as
your real life bank PIN or birthday.

The recovery delay is to protect your banked items from account thieves. If someone stole your account and asked to have the PIN deleted, they would have to wait a few days before accessing your bank account to
steal your items. This will give you time to recover your account.
There will also be a delay in actually setting the PIN to be used, this is so that if your account is stolen and a PIN set, you can cancel it before it comes into use!

options.text: How do I remove my PIN?

steps.player: How do I remove my PIN?

steps.npc: Talking to any banker will enable you to access your PIN settings. There you can cancel or change your PIN, but you will need to wait for your recovery delay to expire to be able to access your bank. This
can be set in the settings page and will protect your items should your account be stolen.

standard-dialogue-avium-savannah-trio-gr.player: Hey there. What are you lot doing out here?

standard-dialogue-avium-savannah-trio-gr.npc: We're from the College of Bards in Tempestus. We thought we'd set up camp here to do some performances for anyone travelling through the savannah.
With the kingdom now open to tourists, we've had plenty of new fans!

standard-dialogue-avium-savannah-trio-tr.npc: Thanks! I made it myself. The College of Bards insist that we all have the ability to create and maintain our own instruments. I'm quite proud of what I came up with!

standard-dialogue-avium-savannah-trio-tr.player: Well I hope it serves you well.

standard-dialogue-avium-savannah-trio-ma.npc: Think you've got what it takes to join the College of Bards?

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-the-on.npc: I'm not sure exactly. All I know is that it's not running at the moment.

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-the-on.npc: We should be back at the College of Bards already, but I'm sure they'll understand why we got delayed.

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-the-on.player: Oh, you're a bard? Could you sing for me?

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-the-on.npc: Maybe. Can you take us to Temptestus?
Then I'm afraid you don't get any singing this time.

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-spirit.npc: Nilsal! Have you come to hear a song from the Sister Songstresses of the College of Bards?

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-spirit.player: Sister Songstresses? So you're a group of sisters who sing together?

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-spirit.npc: Don't be silly! Of course we aren't!

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-spirit.player: Oh... The name did suggest otherwise...

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-spirit.npc: Well, we realised when we met that we were all very similar, so we've been using it as a selling point! Everyone loves Snappy Sister, Stormy Sister, and of course me, Spirited Sister!
People love a nice story about a trio of sisters coming together! So yes, it works rather well.
It's all storytelling! Songs, appearance, history. We're telling a story and people want to hear it!

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-spirit.player: I'm not sure if people wanting to hear it makes it entirely ethical.

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-spirit.npc: Is it made better if our songs are good?

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-spirit.player: Now that you mention it... no of course it isn't.

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-spirit.npc: Well, you're just no fun, iknami.

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-the-li.player: You seem a little down. What's up?

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-the-li.npc: I just want to get back to the College of Bards. It's like my spark has gone out being away from such a creative environment.

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-the-li.player: I'm sure you'll be back there before long.
It doesn't hurt to be hopeful, does it? Not to mention, hope can be a great inspiration!

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-the-li.npc: Hope can be a great inspiration... Perfect! I'll use that!

standard-dialogue-tal-teklan-trio-the-li.player: Oh... Well, I'm happy to have helped.

steps.text: If the player doesn't meet of the following criteria: a trowel, a rock pick and a specimen brush in their inventory; leather boots and leather gloves equipped:

steps.npc: Well, you'll need to get your equipment first - it's all there on the tool rack. Use what you learned from your Earth Sciences exams. You'll need to be wearing your leather gloves and boots as well as have access to
your trowel, rock pick and specimen brush.

steps.text: If the player has a trowel, a rock pick and a specimen brush in their inventory and also have leather boots and leather gloves equipped:

steps.npc: I see you have your equipment - well done.

To really give us a hand, you could clean some finds for us. They're mostly done - just some fine work to finish off. Take a find from the pile that the workmen are bringing in, then there are spare tables over there
to clean them on. If you find anything interesting, let us know and we'll see if it's good enough to go on display.
Oh? Let's take a look...

steps.text: If the player has a Clean necklace in their inventory:

steps.npc: Interesting...yes...yes...hmmm.... It looks like it's enchanted.

Oh, I think it's just a benign teleportation spell. I tinker in magic when I'm not doing archaeology. I can teach you how to make more necklaces like this. Amazing that they had this kind of knowledge back then.

steps.player: That would be good. Where is the teleport to?

steps.npc: Hmm...all the indications are that it's somewhere to the east of us, but I'm not sure how far. Perhaps it was a teleport back to Saranthium. Let me just take a closer look.

steps.text: The archaeologist takes the necklace and turns it over in his hands, studying it closely.

The archaeologist shows you the techniques for this particular spell, which requires five fire runes arranged around one cosmic rune - and level 49 Magic - then casting the spell on a crafted ruby necklace of your
own.  You can make enchanted ruby necklaces.

steps.player: So I just make a ruby necklace and use five fire runes and one cosmic rune to enchant it.

steps.npc: Yes, indeed. Well done, youngster, thanks for helping us.

steps.speaker: Bartender
steps.text: Like I said, this is Nemus Retreat. Back during the War of Betrayal, this was a military camp for Imafore's army, run by none other than General Nemus himself!

steps.speaker: Bartender
steps.text: General Nemus is something of a hero in these parts. Towards the end of the war, the forces of Kourend had mostly taken the Auburn Valley.

steps.speaker: Bartender
steps.text: As a result, Imafore ordered General Nemus to burn the entire valley to the ground to stop the Kourend advance. Many would have died on both sides, but Nemus refused the order.

steps.speaker: Bartender
steps.text: Imafore had him executed as a traitor, but in doing so he lost the support of all of Nemus' troops.

steps.player: Sounds like a bit of a shortsighted decision.

steps.speaker: Bartender
steps.text: Indeed. Imafore presumably hoped to make an example of Nemus, but instead his decision was one of the final mistakes that ultimately led to his defeat a few months later.

Well, there you go.

standard.npc: I might be able to - what do you need to know?

steps.npc: Well first off you need to fill the vat with water - two bucketfuls should do the trick. Then you'll need to put in two handfuls of barley malt - that's roasted barley by the way.
After that you'll be putting your main ingredient in - this will decide which ale it is you're brewing. There should be some good guides around with recipes in.
Lastly you pour a pot full of ale yeast in, which'll start it off fermenting. Then all you have to do is wait for the good stuff.
First you'll need some apples. You'll need to crush them using this cider-press - four apples should make a full bucket of apple-mush. Take four buckets of mush and fill up the vat.
After that you pour a pot full of ale yeast in, which'll start it off fermenting. Then all you have to do is wait for the good stuff.

steps.npc: You are here to help work the blast furnace, aren't you?

The blast furnace is the pinnacle of dwarven metal- processing! Ore goes in the top and comes out as metal bars almost at once! And it's so efficient it only takes half as much coal to purify it as a regular furnace.
But we've got a bit of a labour shortage at the moment, which is why I have to rely on immigrant workers to keep the furnace going. So, are you here to start work?

options.text: How can I help work the blast furnace?
Can I use the furnace to smelt ore?
How can I help work the blast furnace?

steps.player: How can I help work the blast furnace?

steps.npc: The blast furnace will only work if there is a group of people keeping it going. Let me explain...

steps.text: (The Blast Furnace Plan interface opens, with the X next to the stove flashing.)

steps.npc: Firstly, the stove needs to be kept filled with coal. If this runs out the furnace will not work.

steps.text: (The X next to the Air Pump starts flashing.)

steps.npc: Secondly, someone needs to operate the pump that keeps the hot air blast circulating through the furnace.

steps.text: (The X next to the Temp Gauge starts flashing.)

steps.npc: Thirdly, someone needs to keep an eye on the temperature gauge. They should tell the pumper to start or stop so that the temperature stays in the right range.

steps.text: (The X next to the Cogs starts flashing.)

steps.npc: Lastly, someone needs to be on the pedals to power the conveyor belt that puts ore into the furnace.
Someone will also need to be on standby with a hammer in case the machine breaks!
While that's going, anyone else can put their ore on the conveyor belt to have it smelted.

steps.text: (The Blast Furnace Plan interface closes.)

options.text: So what do I get out of it?

steps.player: So what do I get out of it?

steps.npc: Keeping the furnace going is valuable experience in itself!
Keeping the stove alight will train your Firemaking, working the pump will train your Strength, pedalling the conveyor belt will train your Agility and repairing the furnace will train Crafting.
Plus, everyone working the furnace will get a bit of experience in Smithing whenever anyone smelts ore in it.

options.text: So I don't actually get paid then?

steps.player: So I don't actually get paid then?

steps.npc: I offer you the privilege of working on the greatest example of dwarven engineering and you want to be PAID?

If you co-operate with a group of people you can all get your smelting done pretty quickly. Or perhaps some humans who need to do some smelting will pay you, since you humans are all so obsessed with money.
