standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-a-ca.text: Butchered!!! I think not. Cats are easily as tough as sheep. Cats were the second thing Guthix brought here, after sheep of course.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-a-ca.player: Weird. I thought Gnomes and the Dwarves were the first ones. Oh well back to school for me.

location-specific-falador.player: Hi Bob. I didn't think I would ever see you round here. Long way from home isn't it?

location-specific-falador.speaker: Bob
location-specific-falador.text: Yes I guess so. But I've been asked to get some coal for Dunstan. He ran out, you see.

location-specific-falador.player: Anything I can do to help?

location-specific-falador.speaker: Bob
location-specific-falador.text: No thanks. I'm on my way back now.

location-specific-lumbridge.player: Hi Bob. I didn't think I would ever see you round here. Long way from home isn't it?

location-specific-lumbridge.speaker: Bob
location-specific-lumbridge.text: Yes, but the fish round here are oh so tasty! And there's nobody who can make a good old fashioned seafood gumbo like the Lumbridge cook!

location-specific-lumbridge.speaker: Bob
location-specific-lumbridge.text: Oh yes, an old recipe passed down from generation to generation of cooks. But this might be the last generation since the Duke's current cook doesn't have any children.

location-specific-lumbridge.player: Ah, I will have to ask him for the recipe then.

location-specific-lumbridge.speaker: Bob
location-specific-lumbridge.text: Oh, I wouldn't do that if I were you, he's very sensitive about his gumbo responsibilities. I'm sure that if you're a good enough fisherman and cook the knowledge will reach you one day.

location-specific-lumbridge.player: OK, I shan't bring it up with him. Cheers for the chat Bob.

location-specific-lumbridge.speaker: Bob
location-specific-lumbridge.text: No problem. Just make sure you bring me some of you ever get the chance to make it. I love that gumbo!

location-specific-taverley.player: Hi Bob. What are you doing here?

location-specific-taverley.speaker: Bob
location-specific-taverley.text: Ah, another person who thinks I want to talk to them just because they can understand me.

location-specific-taverley.speaker: Bob
location-specific-taverley.text: OK, you asked what I'm doing here.

location-specific-taverley.speaker: Bob
location-specific-taverley.text: I'm here to study the druids. They're boring, but they know how to treat animals, and they don't go around bothering you just because they've got a silly gadget that lets them understand what you say!

location-specific-varrock.player: Hi Bob. What are you doing hanging around Varrock?

location-specific-varrock.speaker: Bob
location-specific-varrock.text: Not much. Just came to see how things are going. Not visited here in a while you see. Me and Roald used to talk all the time.

location-specific-varrock.speaker: Bob
location-specific-varrock.text: Well, those white knights are far more complicated than you might imagine. Not the ‘goodie goodies' they claim to be. Just watch your back.

location-specific-seers-village.player: Hi Bob. I didn't think I would ever see you round here. Long way from home isn't it?

location-specific-seers-village.speaker: Bob
location-specific-seers-village.text: Yikes!! Where did you pop up from?

location-specific-seers-village.player: Oh sorry Bob, didn't mean to make you jump.

location-specific-seers-village.speaker: Bob
location-specific-seers-village.text: Noooooo. Now that mouse I was chasing has got away. Can you be a bit more sneaky next time? You know, sneaky sneaky stick da chompy as my old friend Rantz often says.

location-specific-ardougne.player: Hi Bob. I didn't think I would ever see you round here. Long way from home isn't it?

location-specific-ardougne.speaker: Bob
location-specific-ardougne.text: Argh! My thumbs have gone weird!

location-specific-ardougne.player: But Bob, you don't have any thumbs!

location-specific-ardougne.speaker: Bob
location-specific-ardougne.text: Exactly!! Clearly I must go home, the sky's beginning to bruise, night must fall and I shall be forced to camp.

location-specific-ardougne.speaker: Bob
location-specific-ardougne.text: No, not really. I've just had a severe disappointment.

location-specific-ardougne.player: Whats up Bob, lost your favorite toy?

location-specific-ardougne.speaker: Bob
location-specific-ardougne.text: No, it's just that there comes a time in every cats life where he realises how much time he has wasted just.... playing with rats.

location-specific-ardougne.player: Doesn't sound like a waste of time to me! They deserve it!

location-specific-ardougne.speaker: Bob
location-specific-ardougne.text: Ahh, I guess your right. Thanks!

location-specific-port-sarim.player: Hi Bob. I didn't think I would ever see you round here. Long way from home isn't it?

location-specific-port-sarim.speaker: Bob
location-specific-port-sarim.text: Actually no. I come from round here originally. Back then all this was just fields.

location-specific-port-sarim.player: Back then? How old are you Bob?

location-specific-port-sarim.speaker: Bob
location-specific-port-sarim.text: Ha! How old indeed. How old are the trees? How old are the waves that crash against the shore? How old is the stone we walk on?

location-specific-port-sarim.player: I see. Cryptic as ever. Cheers Bob.... I think.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: If a player falls down in a forest and nobody is there, do they make any noise?

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Now, where did the rest of my PK clan go?

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Be wery, wery quiet... I'm hunting pwayers.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Ah, don't mind me. I'm just looting bodies.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Look out!! He's over there!! Run!!

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: You know, my feet are knackered. This walking lark isn't all it's cracked up to be. Give me a nice monitor to sleep on any day.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: In this place it's not HOW you die that matters. It's who you take with you.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Those who live by the sword, die by the mage.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Did you see that? Someone with a big shiny new halberd hiding behind that rock. I thought only rangers acted as cowardly as that.

steps.player: Are you really just a cat Bob?

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Apparently so yes. Well, that's what they told me after the experiment.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Yes. There was this professor called 'Oddenstein' I think. He must have tricked me into that machine of his, then the next thing I knew I was feline!

steps.player: Oddenstein? I am sure I have heard that name...

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Yes. Once the authorities found out about his experiments he ran away. Lucky for him or I would scratch his eyes out.

steps.player: Is this really all true? Sounds a bit suspicious to me.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Never question the logic of a cat, however flawed.

steps.player: Flawed? So it isn't true... so, erm, eh?

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Perhaps one day you will learn the truth. Until then, the Oddenstein story is what we will tell the 'others'. Understood?

steps.player: OK. Your secrets safe with me Bob.
This is a long way from Burthorpe. What you doing out here?

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: I am drawing a picture of that thing over there.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: That gullible thing over there. Next to that tree where that man sometimes stands.

steps.player: Wow. Could you be any more vague and sarcastic?

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Probably. It's just no challenge these days.

steps.player: It's not safe here Bob. You should leave.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: No way. I am here catching mice.

steps.player: But there aren't any mice in the Wilderness.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Ahh, the human shows signs of a brain. Why do you think that is?

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Exactly. Well done!

wisdom.player: Hey Bob. Got any wisdom to share?

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: If a player falls down in a forest and nobody is there, do they make any noise?

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Sorry, I am far too busy marking my territory.

steps.player: Your territory? This place is ruled by the Grand Highmage Gower and his minions.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: I think not. They are my minions, and I let him think that he's in charge. I'm the real power behind the throne.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Yeah, it keeps them happy that way, but don't tell anyone!

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Dogs believe they are human. Cats believe they are Guthix!

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Well, I don't believe much really since I know I am Zar... erm, well, no, I erm, meow?

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Don't get distracted so easily! See, I'm distracting you right now!

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Sorry, I'm far too busy calculating thermal vectors.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Oh, sorry... I meant, erm, meow?

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Nothing interesting happens.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Ahh, but it is you see. It does all sorts of wonderous things.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Well, it's more to do with what happens when you hear that being said. You see, something interesting happens somewhere else.

steps.player: So what you're saying is that if nothing interesting happens to me, then something interesting is happening for someone else somewhere that IS interesting?

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Yes, that's about it.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Cats are rather delicate creatures and they are subject to a good many ailments, but I never heard of one who suffered from insomnia.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: So, you want to know how us cats keep so clean all day?

steps.player: Must be all that washing you do.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: You would think so wouldn't you. But is being covered in spit really clean?

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Anything not nailed down is a cat toy.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: If at first you don't succeed, take a short nap.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Yeah, I could tell you something really useful, but then I would have to '1-hit you' to death.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Care to place a wager on that? Sorry, hang on, I've got no pockets. Maybe next time.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Dogs have owners, cats have staff.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: I have studied many philosophers and many cats. The wisdom of cats is infinitely superior.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: There are many intelligent species in the universe. They are all owned by cats.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Cats and teleporting just don't mix well. That's why I walk everywhere. Messes my hair up terribly.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Cats are smarter than dogs. You can't get eight cats to pull a sled through snow.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Sorry, no time for chat. Still got mouse bones stuck in my teeth. How awkward.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: You know, cats are the first species to fully evolve. We're perfect.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Preserve nature. Pickle a dog!

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Do you like dogs?

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Me too. Care to swap recipes? I have a rather unique hotdog sauce.

steps.player: Bob, you're a bit messed up really aren't you.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: No, I just know what I like. Besides, it was a joke.

steps.player: A joke? I doubt the dogs are laughing.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: What dogs? I have already rid this place of dogs. Have you ever seen one?

steps.player: Yes actually. I heard there are a few wild dogs about here somewhere.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Right!! Fellow cats, prepare for war!!

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Mmm. Maybe another time.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Cat Rule number 1: Always act afraid when near dogs, especially if you're near a human. They will pick you up and fuss you, then shout at the dog. Most amusing!

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Cat Rule number 2: When assisting a human at work, make sure you sit behind its right leg. You stand a much better chance of getting picked up and stroked. Also, it's very amusing

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Cat Rule number 3: If you ever make a mistake, which is rare and probably involves a dog, make sure you wash yourself immediately. This will give everyone the impression that

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: it was done on purpose.

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Cat Rule number 4: Beware the bag monster. These things live in small bags and under newspapers, sometimes even hidden in shoes if they are very clever. They will be very small and

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: take on the same colour as the hiding place. Attack these things on sight - stop at nothing. If you see a bag or shoe you have not inspected recently, pounce!!

steps.player: Do you like all the monsters around here?

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: No, not really. I'm actually signed up with all those HAM fanatics. Kill the whole lot of 'em!!

steps.player: That's a bit cruel isn't it?

steps.speaker: Bob
steps.text: Yeah, that's one of my best qualities. Just behind sneaky and vicious. Besides, after a few doses of catnip, they all look like mice to me!

You know, a fake mouse on a string.

reclaiming-mouse-toy.speaker: Bob
reclaiming-mouse-toy.text: An Advanced Combat Training Device, every cat should have one. Here's another one.

standard.speaker: Monkey

standard.speaker: Monkey

standard.npc: Yeah?

steps.npc: Granddad's fruit farm. It's a right dump. This whole corner of the city is a dump.

options.text: So why are you here if it's a dump?

steps.player: So why are you here if it's a dump?

steps.npc: My cow of a sister kicked me out of her bar. Said I was getting the place a bad name. So I'm staying here until I'm old enough to get my own place.
I want to move to Arceuus. It's properly awesome up there. I'll do bartending or something until I can learn to be a necromancer.
Anyway, why are you here? Do you want something?
Yeah, you're in the biggest dumpster of Dumpsterville. Now you know. Anyway, do you want something?
Yeah, alright...
I am Bologa Gricoller, seeker of forbidden wisdom, wanderer of the dark pathways, thinker of the unthinkable. I can do bartending too.
I used to work at The Golden Field. That's my sister's bar. It's mostly farmhands drinking there, but you get some interesting people as well.
See, most Hosidius people are Saradominists. My sister, she's always listening to Father Jean at the church with his goodie-goodie sermons.
But some of us in the bar thought we'd give Zamorak a try. Like, you gotta be open-minded, right? What did Saradomin ever do for us anyway?
So we'd meet in the bar, sharing books that the Piscarilius smugglers would bring us, learning what the Saradominists don't want us to know.
Anyway, my sister - she's a right cow, by the way - she fired me and kicked me out. Said I was bringing bad sorts to her bar.
Bad sorts, she said! Like, morality is totally subjective, right? So who's she to call us bad sorts just 'cos we're not afraid to think differently?
Anyway, I've learnt all this cool stuff about Zamorak, and being stuck in a fruit farm doesn't stop me being his loyal servant, right?
In fact I've invented a Zamorakian blessing that works on fruit! You can use it to make Zamorak's wine out of grapes from the Vinery.

options.text: Can you help me to make Zamorak's wine?

steps.player: Can you help me to make Zamorak's wine?

steps.npc: I'll let you have access to the Zamorakian blessing I invented, so you can invoke Zamorak's unholy power upon the grapes... if I think you're up to it.
I'll want 75,000 coins too.

steps.player: And do you think I'm up to it?

steps.text: If the player has less than level 50 Prayer:

steps.npc: Nah, I bet you couldn't even bless an unholy symbol - you're not going to get very far with my grape blessing.

steps.text: You need a Prayer level of 50 to use Bologa's blessing.
If the player has at least level 50 Prayer while wearing other god items:

steps.npc: Not likely - I can see from your kit that you're supporting other gods. Dress Zamorakian if you want to impress me. And I'll still want 75,000 coins.

steps.npc: You don't look much like a Zamorakian to me. Dress Zamorakian if you want my help. And I'll still want 75,000 coins.

steps.text: If the player has at least level 50 Prayer while wearing a Zamorakian item but does not have 75,000 coins:

steps.npc: Yeah, I guess you'll do. But I want 75,000 coins. One day I'll need to buy my own house, y'know!

The power consumes the scroll on which the blessing is written, so you'll need one for each grape. I suggest you take a stack of blessings with you.
By the way, Lord Zamorak's chaotic power is quite volatile. You'll likely get a smaller harvest from your vine if you're using these blessings.
I'll give the scrolls to Granddad downstairs. You can get them off him as a reward if you work on his farm. Hey, it's a dump, but he's family. So, do you accept?

steps.player: And do you think I'm up to it?

steps.player: Tell me the story about yourself again.

steps.npc: Yeah, okay. It's nice of you to ask...
I am Bologa Gricoller, seeker of forbidden wisdom, wanderer of the dark pathways, thinker of the unthinkable. I can do bartending too.
I used to work at The Golden Field. That's my sister's bar. It's mostly farmhands drinking there, but you get some interesting people as well.
See, most Hosidius people are Saradominists. My sister, she's always listening to Father Jean at the church with his goodie-goodie sermons.
But some of us in the bar thought we'd give Zamorak a try. Like, you gotta be open-minded, right? What did Saradomin ever do for us anyway?
So we'd meet in the bar, sharing books that the Piscarilius smugglers would bring us, learning what the Saradominists don't want us to know.
Anyway, my sister - she's a right cow, by the way - she fired me and kicked me out. Said I was bringing bad sorts to her bar.
Bad sorts, she said! Like, morality is totally subjective, right? So who's she to call us bad sorts just 'cos we're not afraid to think differently?
Anyway, I've learnt all this cool stuff about Zamorak, and being stuck in a fruit farm doesn't stop me being his loyal servant, right?
So that's how I came to invent that Zamorakian blessing for making Zamorak's wine out of grapes from the Vinery.

steps.player: What does this seed pod do?

steps.npc: Ah, the seed pod of the Grand Tree is a fascinating spirit artefact. It is a very useful thing, though one must treat it with respect, since the Grand Tree has a connection with all of its parts, however distant they
may be. How do you think the Spirit Trees work?

If you launch its seeds in a far flung location, you will be helping the tree survive, so the grand tree will help a gnome glider pilot find you, using the seed burst itself (which marks the sky) and a little magic, and bring you
back home as an act of gratitude. Budding farmers will also find their link with plants to be just a little bit better than before.
However, it takes time for a pilot to find you, and if you are in a real hurry, and I mean a real emergency, you can just squash the seed pod. The Grand Tree doesn't like this, but will pull you back

home straight away. Don't do this if you need to do anything with plants straight away, though - your fingers will be considerably less green for a while after using the seed pod this way, and the journey is not
very pleasant...

healed.npc: Thanks for helping me. Is there anything you'd like to know about this temple? If you find anything in here, show it to me and I'll tell you what I know about it.

steps.npc: This place probably had a name at some point but it has long since been forgotten. The Arceuus librarians refer to this place as the Forthos Dungeon.
It is rumoured that this place used to be of religious significance to druidic followers of both Ralos and Ranul.
According to religious texts, Ralos is the god of the sun and Ranul, his brother, is the god of the moon.
If you find any artifacts or relics from within this temple, I would be very interested in seeing them.

steps.player: I'll see what I find. Although, I've never heard of Ralos and Ranul.

steps.npc: You need only to look up and see their greatness above you when you return to the surface.
My name is Brother Aimeri, I am a travelling monk from the distant land of Varlamore on a journey to uncover the secrets of this temple.
I worship Ralos, a common practice where I am from. However, I found out that our order may have originated from this temple. If you find anything of interest, please let me know.
You have my gratitude. Any information you do find would also be of interest to the Arceuus Library. I hope we can uncover the secrets of this place for the greater good.
I found out about this place from Logosia in the Arceuus Library. I came to investigate but was ambushed by the spiders in the room to the north.
I'm a scholar not a fighter. I didn't have time to think through my options so I did what came naturally and ran away.

steps.player: Why didn't you decide to run back the way you came from instead of running further into the dungeon where there could be more dangerous creatures?

steps.npc: See, the problem with that... Is that it is an excellent idea I wish I had thought of at the time.

steps.player: You've been trapped here for a while! No wonder you were hungry!

steps.npc: How strange. Tell me, what did the creature look like?

steps.player: It was a dark black creature with a white skull on its head and curved horns.

steps.npc: Let me see... According to my notes that appears to have been a Shaeded Beast, a vile creature which posseses people and corrupts their minds.
Only the power of Ralos can remove such a curse. I suggest making an offering to Ralos somewhere within this temple.

steps.player: What kind of sacrifice should I offer?

steps.npc: As Ralos is the sun god, any normal bone just won't do. I'd recommend the bones of any dragon.
I'd advise staying away from the altar in the mean time.

steps.player: Thanks. I'll have a look around.

options.text: Tell me of the finding of Koschei

steps.player: I'm interested in finding out about that mysterious warrior I fought as part of Thorvalds' combat trial. His name is Koschei I believe.

steps.npc: Ah... the deathless one... We do not even know if Koschei is his name, when we found him he had no memory, he was simply repeating that single word.
Whatever happened to him must have rattled his soul so hard that his memory ran away from him, and he has not yet found it's hiding place.

steps.player: So how exactly did you find him?

steps.npc: Well, it was a raiding party like any other. We had just struck one of the smaller northern islands to harvest supplies by combat, as our laws allow,
when we saw a figure in the icey waters. As we were at least a 3 week sail from any port, and saw no other ships nearby, he must have been there some time.
We could not leave someone to the cold death of the ocean, even an outerlander, so we fished him aboard. He muttered continually, but his words made no sense.
He had no clothes or possessions with him, and seemed to have been burnt somehow before he had landed in the water.
I cannot help but wonder what burnt him, for as you may have seen, he is incredibly powerful and resistant to damage by any means I know of!
Anyway, we decided to bring him back to Rellekka, for he did not seem of good health or sound mind, and simply repeated the word Koschei over and over.
Yrsa tended to him for many weeks, until one day it was as though a new soul had entered his burnt and broken body.
He suddenly left her house one day, fully healed, and able to speak to us as though nothing had happened to him.
He still had no recollection of how he had come to be in the icey ocean, or of who he was, or where he had come from, but this did not matter to us or him.
He took his trials of adulthood, as you did, and has been a boon to our clan ever since. Someday I fear he may regain his memory, and leave us for his past...
But I will always respect any decision he decides to make should that day ever come upon us. Until then, he is more than welcome to stay here.
So, [Fremennik name]. Was there anything more you wished to hear?

steps.text: other

options.text: Tell me of the lands to the North

steps.player: I would like to hear of the lands across the ocean to the North.

steps.npc: Well, I think the best thing for you would be to go to the docks and ask to join one of our longboats on a journey.
My affairs are concentrated mostly on Rellekka, so my knowledge is not great, but I will happily share what I do know with you [Fremennik name].
North of this town the atmosphere becomes bitterly cold. There are a number of small inhabited islands that we have sea routes with.
The largest of these is possibly Miscellania, although I hear that there has been some recent incident with their monarch, but I don't know the details.
There is also of course the island of the moon clan, who change with the tides. They are our bitterest enemies, and we are currently at war with them.
They are an evil people, equally cursed and blessed by the magic in their blood. Beyond those islands, there is the large frozen wasteland we call Acheron.
It is an inhospitable land, and you will need an agile and sturdy body just to keep alive in it's perils.
As I say, my knowledge outside of this town is rather limited, and I know no more than this. Was there anything else you wished to hear tell of?

steps.text: other

steps.player: I would like to hear a little of the history between the Fremenniks and the outerlanders.

steps.npc: Ah, now that is something I know a great deal about. Believe it or not, all outerlanders were once orginally Fremenniks.
When first man came to these lands all were Fremenniks, and followed our ways. We lived a happy life, and never settled in one place for long.
We travelled by boat along the coastlines, never taking more from the land than could be regrown by the same time in the following year.
However, many moons past, some of our tribesmen were weary of constantly travelling the lands, and decided to build themselves permanent homes.
Unfortunately, the other races that had also migrated here did not like this. They waged war against us at every opportunity.
We were driven mostly to the coastlines, where we could escape by boat when attacked. Remember, at this time we had no real way to defend against constant attack.
Then one day one of our Seers, whose name has been lost in the telling of this tale, discovered a cave full of strange rocks.
This rock would never be consumed, no matter how much we took, and sparkled at its peak, and broke off in small and regular sized chunks when mined.
Stranger than this, we found that these rocks would become filled with power when taken to certain places across this land!
There was a terrible argument in our tribe! Some said that we should take as many of these rocks as we could, and use them in defending against our enemies attacks!
Others said that we had found a place that belonged only to the gods, and that should we steal what was not ours we would find only torment and misery.
We voted on this, and decided that it was in the best interests of the tribe to leave these strange rocks where they lay, for the gods can be spiteful and cruel,
especially to those who do not treat them with the respect they desire. Some of our number refused to accept this ruling by our council however.
They began to mine these rocks, and set up transport systems to the various places of power that enchanted them.
They even created temples at each of these places! This was going too far! We had no choice, but to expel them from our tribe forever!
We turned our backs upon them, and let them know they would never be welcome back to our tribes until they had released themselves from the rocks.
This is the tale of how the outerlanders came about; through stealing from the gods, and from betraying our ideals. This is why we show them no trust.
Was there something else you wished to hear?

2021-christmas-event-before-talking-to-l.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-before-talking-to-l.text: Hello sir, are you going to make a snowman?

2021-christmas-event-before-talking-to-l.player: Maybe, I'm not sure I'd be very good at it!

2021-christmas-event-before-talking-to-l.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-before-talking-to-l.text: I want to make a snowman, but I can't reach high enough to stack the snowballs properly.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Hello Buoy and Gurl!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Hello sir!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: How do you know our names?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: I had a chat with your dad. He's super busy, so he's asked me to help you build a snowman!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Really? We get to make a snowman?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Yes! And I'm going to build whatever snowman you want!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Yay! Can it be three snowballs tall?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: But I want it to be five tall!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Five is a bad number, it should be three tall!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: You're a bad number. Five is so much better.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Okay, okay, wait a second. Why don't we meet in the middle. How about four snowballs tall?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Buoy and Gurl think for a second.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Fine, it can be four tall.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Yes, four tall is okay.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Great. Now, we need to pick what size snowballs we want for each tier. Why don't you take it in turns? You can do two each.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: The bottom one should be a huge snowball!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: The next one should be big!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: This is working nicely, we're half way! What about the top two parts?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: The next one should be a small snowball!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: No, it should be little!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: But it needs to be small, little would look bad.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: It wouldn't look bad. Small is better for decorations.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: My decorations will fit on a little one.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Why do you always ruin everything?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: You ruin everything with your silly ideas!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Okay, okay, wait. This clearly isn't working, and I don't want you two to fall out. It's Christmas, we shouldn't be arguing!
How about I make you both a snowman? It can be whatever height and size you like. One each!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: So mine can be five snowballs tall?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: And mine can be three snowballs tall?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Yes, I'll make you both whatever snowman you like!
What would you both like?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: I'd like mine to be three snowballs tall please! And I want the bottom one to be small, the middle one big, and the top one huge!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: I'd like mine to be five snowballs tall please! I want the bottom one to be humongous, then large, then normal, then big, and then a little one for the top!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: That's two very different snowmen, I see why this didn't work before!
What do all these different sizes mean? Humongous? Normal? Little? How big are those?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: You silly billy! Humongous is the biggest snowball of course!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Normal is the normal size that you get when you make a snowball normally. It's easy!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Right, thank you for clearing that up. I'll figure something out.
What are you two going to do for decorations?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: I already know what I want mine to look like!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Me too!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Why don't you guys find some decorations while I build the snowmen? Then you can add them once I'm done.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Okay sir!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: We will do that!
Buoy and Gurl go back to playing in the snow.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Well, that seems sorted. I should speak to Larry again, and see if he has any advice about building the snowmen.
Hello there!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Have you started making the snowmen yet?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: You should talk to dad if you need some help, he knows how to make snowmen!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Yeah, he always used to make really big ones with us!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Maybe I'll go talk to him and see what advice he has.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: He'll say, make them really tall!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: He'll say make them shorter, because that's better!
Buoy and Gurl wander off, arguing about what size snowman is the best.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: I should go and speak to Larry. I'm sure he has some handy advice for me!

2021-christmas-event-making-snowmen.speaker: Buoy/Gurl
2021-christmas-event-making-snowmen.text: That looks good! It needs a [size] snowball next!

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.text: Yay! Can we decorate them now?

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.text: Yes! Can we decorate them now please [player name]?

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.player: Of course you can. Are they what you wanted?

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.text: Mine too. It's just how I wanted it.

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.player: I am happy to hear that. It was harder work than I thought.

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.text: You did a good job. Thank you very much [sir/madam].

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.player: It was no problem. Merry Christmas to you both!

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.text: Buoy and Gurl go to their snowmen to start decorating.

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.player: I should go and speak to Larry. Hopefully he has that festive white wine ready for me.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Those snowmen look amazing!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Thank you! Decorating them was quite hard!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Yeah, they took ages to do! Do you like mine?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: It's really good! Reminds me of something actually.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: What about mine? Do you like it?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: I like yours too. They both remind me of something!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Mine is Thermy! My favourite monster! She's so big and scary, makes me go woah!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Mine is Tempy! My favourite monster! He lives in the water, a huge mass of angry wet!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: They're both amazing! I didn't know you guys would be so good at decorating.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Dad lets us decorate every year. We get a lot of practice!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Last year we made them into the Fragment of Seren and the King Black Dragon!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: What... really??? I'd like to have seen that. Those sound even more difficult than these two!
How do you know all these monsters anyway? There is no way your dad would let you anywhere near them!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Dad reads us lots of stories, and we hear about them from passing adventurers, like you.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: You must meet some interesting and cool adventurers!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Not as cool as you though; none of them helped us make our snowmen!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Yes, you're the first to help us make them!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Well, you're welcome. I really enjoyed it. What are you guys going to do now you're finished?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Gurl
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: We're going to go and play! And maybe visit the festival. Will you be there?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: I sure will be. Maybe see you there!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Bye sir, Merry Christmas.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Merry Christmas, have fun!

standard-dialogue.npc: Good day, [sir/madam]. Would [sir/madam] care to hire a good butler for 5000 coins?

steps.npc: I can fulfill all [sir/madam]'s domestic service needs with efficiency and impeccable manners. I hate to boast, but I can say with confidence that no mortal can make trips to the bank or sawmill faster than I!

options.text: Tell me about your previous jobs

steps.player: Tell me about your previous jobs.

steps.npc: From a humble beginning as a dish-washer I have worked my way up through the ranks of domestic service in the households of nobles from Varrock and Ardougne. As a life-long servant I have naturally

suppressed any personality of my own and trained myself never to use the second person when talking to a superior. I have usually worked in the large households of the aristocracy, but now that such a large
number of private persons are building their own houses I decided to offer them my services.

steps.npc: I must respectfully decline, [sir/madam]. I offer a very exclusive service and will only work for people with over level 40 Construction.

standard.npc: Hello. How are you today?
Very well, thank you.

after-hazeel-cult.npc: It's an honour to be in your presence again, adventurer. I hope things are well?
Unfortunately, I am still forced to deal with this insufferable family. Many generations have passed, but they are still the enemy. As such, they must be kept a close eye on.
Still, I have no doubt that the time will soon come for me to leave this place. Our lord will certainly have need of me elsewhere once his current work is complete.

after-hazeel-cult.player: I see. Well good luck with it all.

steps.speaker: Butterfly

steps.speaker: Butterfly

other

steps.speaker: Butterfly

steps.speaker: Butterfly

other

steps.speaker: Butterfly

other

standard.speaker: c0lect0r890
standard.text: Urgh, it just happened again! Every time I almost have it my hand slips.

standard.player: Oh, that's unfortunate. Are you using a lockpick?

standard.speaker: c0lect0r890
standard.text: Yes. Well actually, I'm using a Strange old lockpick. I found it while looting one of these coffins and I typically have better luck with it.

standard.player: Oh, that's interesting. I'll keep my eyes out for one.

standard.speaker: c0lect0r890
standard.text: I've found a few of them while raiding this place. There appear to be more of them on this floor than the floors above.

standard.player: I see. If you don't mind me asking, you already have dark graceful so why are you still looking for hallowed marks?

standard.speaker: c0lect0r890
standard.text: Oh, it's because of this little fellow following me. I've heard that the Dark acorn sold by the guy upstairs will transform him into a Dark Squirrel.
If the player does not have a Dark squirrel following them:

steps.player: Wow, I didn't know that! That sounds pretty cool.

steps.speaker: c0lect0r890
steps.text: Yeah, that's what I thought but that mysterious stranger is asking for 3,000 Hallowed marks for it.

steps.speaker: c0lect0r890
steps.text: Yeah, that's what I thought. Feels like he set the price just to keep me down here for longer. Still, it's not like I have anything better to do.

steps.player: I see, well best of luck. Hopefully you survive long enough to finish your goal.

steps.speaker: c0lect0r890
steps.text: I'm sure I'll be fine.

standard.text: If the player has a Dark squirrel following them:

steps.player: Yeah, I ended up buying one myself and fed it to my Giant Squirrel. It took a while but it was definitely worth it.

steps.speaker: c0lect0r890
steps.text: Wow, I'm impressed! How long did it take you to get the 3,000 marks?

steps.player: Long enough... Still, at least I feel much more agile now than when I started.

steps.speaker: c0lect0r890
steps.text: I don't think I'm going to get any more agile while looking for it myself. I'm glad you received some benefit from the grind though.

steps.player: I see, well best of luck. Hopefully you survive long enough to finish your goal.

steps.text: If the player has a trowel, a rock pick and a specimen brush in their inventory and also have leather boots and leather gloves equipped:

steps.npc: I see you have your equipment - well done.

To really give us a hand, you could clean some finds for us. They're mostly done - just some fine work to finish off. Take a find from the pile that the workmen are bringing in, then there are spare tables over there
to clean them on. If you find anything interesting, let us know and we'll see if it's good enough to go on display.
Oh? Let's take a look...

steps.text: If the player has a Clean necklace in their inventory:

steps.npc: Interesting...yes...yes...hmmm.... It looks like it's enchanted.

Oh, I think it's just a benign teleportation spell. I tinker in magic when I'm not doing archaeology. I can teach you how to make more necklaces like this. Amazing that they had this kind of knowledge back then.

steps.player: That would be good. Where is the teleport to?

steps.npc: Hmm...all the indications are that it's somewhere to the east of us, but I'm not sure how far. Perhaps it was a teleport back to Saranthium. Let me just take a closer look.

steps.text: The archaeologist takes the necklace and turns it over in his hands, studying it closely.

The archaeologist shows you the techniques for this particular spell, which requires five fire runes arranged around one cosmic rune - and level 49 Magic - then casting the spell on a crafted ruby necklace of your
own.  You can make enchanted ruby necklaces.

steps.player: So I just make a ruby necklace and use five fire runes and one cosmic rune to enchant it.

steps.npc: What have we here?

Oh! This is very interesting...and confusing at the same time. This coin means that the city that we're excavating on the Digsite - Saranthium - was actually inhabited much, much earlier by followers of Zamorak,
at which time, the city was known as Senntisten.

This is a most remarkable discovery, as we have other evidence indicating that Zarosian followers were resident before the Saradominists took over, but it also seems that Zamorakian forces used it during a battle of some
sort. Still, it allows us to roughly date when the city changed from following Zaros and Zamorak to following Saradomin. Put it in display case 44.

steps.npc: Out of glass.  The more advanced lanterns have a metal component as well.
Firstly you can make a simple candle lantern out of glass.  It's just like a candle, but the flame isn't exposed, so it's safer.
Then you can make an oil lamp, which is brighter but has an exposed flame.  But if you make an iron frame for it you can turn it into an oil lantern.
Finally there's the bullseye lantern.  You'll need to make a frame out of steel and add a glass lens.
Once you've made your lamp or lantern, you'll need to make lamp oil for it.  The chemist near Rimmington has a machine for that.
For any light source, you'll need a tinderbox to light it. Keep your tinderbox handy in case it goes out!

standard.npc: Hello there, I'm Captain Bruce. Do you want to serve in the Shayzien Army and defend our kingdom?

steps.npc: Wonderful! To get started, you need to answer a few questions.
Are you a resident of Kourend?
Ah. Then you cannot join I'm afraid.
It's in the rules I'm afraid. Only citizens of Kourend are allowed to join the Shayzien Army.
Well at one time only citizens of Shayzien could join the army. It wasn't until the reign of King Byrne I that people from other parts of the kingdom were allowed to enlist.
Of course, many people in Kourend still like to stick to tradition. After all, the five cities of Kourend have always had very defined roles within the kingdom.

steps.player: Interesting. So most people in the army are still from Shayzien?

steps.npc: Indeed. While the Shayzien Army is by far the largest military force in Kourend, the other cities still have some form of militia, apart from Arceuus of course.
Even if someone from elsewhere in the kingdom wants to become a soldier, they're far more likely to join their local city force than come to us.
Still, times are slowly changing. Every year we see more people from outside Shayzien enlist.

steps.text: If the player is carrying food items or a coloured satchel:
You can't enter the game with any food; the Healer will cure you.
If the player is carrying any Barbarian mixes or leaping fish:
You can't enter the game with any brutal potions or ingredients; the Healer will cure you.
If the player is carrying any Phoenix necklaces:
There is no reason to take a phoenix necklace into the arena, as you won't lose any items if you die in the minigame.
If the player is carrying runes or a rune pouch:
You can't enter the game with any runes - there are free ones in there.
If the player is carrying arrows:
You can't take arrows into a game - there are free ones in there.
If the player is carrying a pet:
The barbarians don't want you to take your follower in.
If the player is carrying logs:
You can't take your own logs with you - you have to use the ones the barbarians provide.
If the player is carrying parts of the Dwarven multicannon:
The barbarians don't want you using artillery down there.
If the player is carrying a looting bag:
The barbarians don't trust whatever you may have stored in your looting bag. They won't let you in with it.
If the player is carrying Saradomin brews:
The barbarians don't want you using Saradomin brews down there. You will have to restore your health as they intend.

at-tempoross-cove.npc: What do you need, adventurer? There is a battle to fight!

steps.npc: Get yerself a harpoon from the crate on the ship, then go fish around the island t' catch some harpoonfish. They make fer fine ammo against Tempoross!
Once ye caught some, ye can cook 'em at the shrines on the island if ye want 'em to pack more of a punch. Then come back t' the ship an' load 'em in the ammunition crates next to the cannons.
Our cannoneers will get t' firin' the harpoonfish at Tempoross. When it's weak an' submerges to recover its energy, get down to the jetty next t' the ship an' fish those spirit pools.

Be quick with fishin' those spirit pools though, or it'll come back so strong we'll have to abandon the fight! With any luck, we'll weaken those spirit fish enough t' subdue Tempoross. Now get t' the fight, sailor!

options.text: What should I watch out for?

steps.player: What should I watch out for?

steps.npc: If Tempoross electrocutes a cannon t' stop it from firin', ya better load your harpoonfish into the other ammunition crates t' keep them cannons firin' instead.

Also, make sure t' grab a rope from the ship crates an' keep an eye out for big waves. We'll make sure t' shout about them. Then ye best quickly tether yerself t' an island totem pole or ship mast with that rope.
If the waves break the totem pole or ship mast, ye can grab a hammer from the ship crates t' fix 'em up before the next big wave hits.
Oh, an' keep an eye out for lightnin' clouds causin' fires. Get a bucket from the ship crates, fill it with water at a pump, and get t' puttin it out before it spreads.
If ye get hit by the waves or fire, don't be surprised when ye lose those fish an' tools ye gathered. Now get t' the fight, sailor!

at-ruins-of-unkah-initial-dialogue.npc: Ahoy! I'm Cap'n Pudi, currently assisting the Spirit Anglers in their effort against Tempoross.

at-ruins-of-unkah-initial-dialogue.player: Tempoross? Spirit Anglers? Who are they?

at-ruins-of-unkah-initial-dialogue.npc: You 'aven't heard?! The freak storms? Sailors running into trouble? Ye really must be a landlubber!
Tempoross is some kind o' great sea spirit that's been spookin' sailors and causing crazy storms!
Taiman and his crew were one of the first t' run into it. Washed up outside Al Kharid amongst piles of debris, they did. 'Tis a troublin' time to be a cap'n!

at-ruins-of-unkah-initial-dialogue.player: Oh that doesn't sound good at all!

at-ruins-of-unkah-initial-dialogue.npc: It isn't, but worry not. The Spirit Anglers 'ave been formed t' tackle this beastie! We're recruiting all skilled sailors and fisherfolk t' help us.

at-ruins-of-unkah-initial-dialogue.text: If the player does not have the required Fishing level:

steps.npc: Are you sure? It's pretty rough out there and you look like you could do with more experience.

steps.text: You need a Fishing level of 35 to fight Tempoross.

at-ruins-of-unkah-initial-dialogue.text: If the player has the required Fishing level:

steps.npc: Excellent!
The ships on the dock regularly embark to Tempoross Cove. Once there, you'll need to keep the cannons loaded with Harpoonfish t' weaken the Spirit. You can fish 'em on the island.
When Tempoross submerges, get up close and clear the fish from its whirlpools; they're how it gets its energy.
Aye, that be the easy part!
The storm of Tempoross will rage around you, so you better be ready to deal with lightning strikes and avoid getting zapped when Tempoross attacks the cannons.
Also, watch out for those mighty waves! You'll want t' tether yourself t' something solid so you don't find yourself lost in the deep blue when they come crashing down!

steps.player: Oh... Well, I suppose I can do that.
Will I need any special equipment?

steps.npc: Everythin' you need can be found on-board. Though if you have a favourite harpoon, you can always bring that!
The complete Spirit Anglers outfit also has an 'andy harness built-in, so you won't need a rope if you're wearin' it. You can speak t' Gita about getting one.
Ye can find Gita just east of 'ere, next t' some fishin' equipment.
When you're ready, just board the ship and we'll set sail soon!

options.text: Are there any benefits to helping the Spirit Anglers?

steps.player: Are there any benefits to helping the Spirit Anglers?

steps.speaker: Captain Pudi:
steps.text: Other than maintainin' safe passage and savin' lives?!
The captain laughs.

steps.npc: I'm just messin' with ye! Of course there are benefits!
We find all sorts washed up by the storms. Aside from the usual junk, we often find old chests from merchant supply ships, as well as the odd artefact here and there.
If it's not needed for the Spirit Anglers' research, it's yours to keep!
Some of the more resourceful Spirit Anglers also discovered a fishing use for the spirit energised scales shed by the fish within Tempoross. You're free t' keep any you find.

Can you tell me more about the Spirit Anglers?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about the Spirit Anglers?

steps.npc: Well, as I mentioned before, Taiman and his fishing crew from Al Kharid 'ad a tussle with Tempoross. They barely made it back.
I was sitting down by the shore enjoying one of Karim's kebabs at the time, when suddenly the crew washed up amongst a pile of debris. Looked like they'd just seen a ghost!
As soon as they could talk sense they went to the Chancellor and within days more shockin' tales of the Sea Spirit's wrath came in.
The Chancellor called a meeting for all us local seafarin' folk and we agreed action must be taken!
Ain't nothin' goin' t' take the seas from me, even if it is a powerful spirit!
Anyway, it was decided that we'd setup a base 'ere amongst these ruins, and so the Spirit Anglers was formed!
Don't ask me what the ruins used to be. And it's not like Menaphos can 'ave a say!
Whatever they are, they make a fine base for the Spirit Anglers!
Since moving in, we've been recruiting fisherfolk from all over, and some of the readin' types 'ave been studyin' Tempoross durin' our trips to subdue it.
I like t' get stuck in, me-self; face off toe t' toe with the beastie. I'll be right by your side when you go out there!
I'm still 'ere, ain't I?
Anyway, there's plenty o' research going on, so maybe you can find some notes lyin' around if ye want to know more.

at-tempoross-cove.npc: What do you need, adventurer? There is a battle to fight!

steps.npc: Get yerself a harpoon from the crate on the ship, then go fish around the island t' catch some harpoonfish. They make fer fine ammo against Tempoross!
Once ye caught some, ye can cook 'em at the shrines on the island if ye want 'em to pack more of a punch. Then come back t' the ship an' load 'em in the ammunition crates next to the cannons.
Our cannoneers will get t' firin' the harpoonfish at Tempoross. When it's weak an' submerges to recover its energy, get down to the jetty next t' the ship an' fish those spirit pools.

Be quick with fishin' those spirit pools though, or it'll come back so strong we'll have to abandon the fight! With any luck, we'll weaken those spirit fish enough t' subdue Tempoross. Now get t' the fight, sailor!

options.text: What should I watch out for?

steps.player: What should I watch out for?

steps.npc: If Tempoross electrocutes a cannon t' stop it from firin', ya better load your harpoonfish into the other ammunition crates t' keep them cannons firin' instead.

Also, make sure t' grab a rope from the ship crates an' keep an eye out for big waves. We'll make sure t' shout about them. Then ye best quickly tether yerself t' an island totem pole or ship mast with that rope.
If the waves break the totem pole or ship mast, ye can grab a hammer from the ship crates t' fix 'em up before the next big wave hits.
Oh, an' keep an eye out for lightnin' clouds causin' fires. Get a bucket from the ship crates, fill it with water at a pump, and get t' puttin it out before it spreads.
If ye get hit by the waves or fire, don't be surprised when ye lose those fish an' tools ye gathered. Now get t' the fight, sailor!
Really? You will receive no reward if you do.

standard.npc: Beyond this wall you'll find the Kebos Lowlands. Most of the region is lizardman territory. We're here to keep them from entering Kourend.
We used to keep this passage properly barricaded shut, but then the fancy historians from the Arceuus Library wanted to go do some research out there.
Soon the farmers joined them, and before you knew it, everyone wanted to go explore. Some of them have even started living out there.
I can see it all ending badly, but that's the problem with intellectuals - they always think they know better.
Anyway, maybe they'll all get themselves killed. Then we can put the barricade back up.
If you go out there yourself, give the lizardmen a kicking from me. They've killed too many of my soldiers.

after-corsair-curse.npc: Arrr, 'tis the young [lad/lass] who helped save my crew from that scoundrel, Ithoi! How be ye this fine day?

steps.npc: Arrr, ye looks fine. Stiff in the spine, firm in the mind an' long in the leg. 'Tis good to see ye again.

steps.text: other

options.text: What is there to do here?

steps.player: What is there to do here?

steps.npc: Well, ye could maybe explore the ogre caves. Arsen says the ogres be fearsome, though, so watch yer step. An' there be places for ye to train yer skills, over to the west.

standard.npc: Do you need something?
Move along then. I have a lot of work to be doing.

after-the-final-dawn.npc: Good day to you, adventurer. Do you need something?

after-the-final-dawn.player: No. Just thought I'd come and see how things are going.

after-the-final-dawn.npc: Things are very well thank you. Prince Itzla has tasked me with keeping an eye on the remaining Emissaries.
Swift justice must be dealt if they try anything, but until then, the Prince would prefer we not stir the pot. They no longer pose a real threat now their leaders have gone.

after-the-final-dawn.player: Well, I'm glad to hear all is well. Until next time.

after-the-final-dawn.npc: Indeed. May the sun light your way, adventurer.

sitting-at-the-picnic.text: The capybara uses its nose to roll an orange towards you.

performing-the-jig-emote-at-the-picnic-0.text: The capybara and hippo don't seem to care for your moves.

performing-the-jig-emote-at-the-picnic-1.text: The hippo seems to find your moves interesting, but isn't totally sold on them. The capybara doesn't seem to care.

performing-the-jig-emote-at-the-picnic-2.text: The hippo seems to like your moves, but the capybara isn't convinced.

performing-the-jig-emote-at-the-picnic-3.text: The hippo seems to really enjoy your moves, but while the capybara likes them, it doesn't appear to quite love them.

after-completing-monkey-madness-ii.npc: Well, I figured that with Glough being gone and all...

steps.npc: You know, there are so many different ways to greet people. Hello, 'ello, hello there...

steps.player: That still only counts as one!

steps.npc: Hello. How are you today?
Hello! What a day it is in the crystal city, huh?
What can I do for ya?

options.text: What is there to do around here?

steps.player: What is there to do around here?

steps.npc: All kinds of things! The towers are a wonderful sight to see.
On a day like today, I'd recommend visiting the market.

overhead-dialogue-failed-pickpocket-atte.npc: What do you think you're doing?

standard.npc: Hello! You're not from around here, are you? It's exciting to see that even people from outside of Varlamore are looking to join the Emissaries!

standard.player: Well after I heard about all the good work they were doing, I could hardly say no! What about you? What made you want to join them?

standard.npc: Well it's our duty of course! The Church of Ralos has become lost, but the Emissaries know the truth. Ximoua will not come to be unless we make it so!

standard.player: So you're quite eager to see the end of the world then?

standard.npc: End? Ximoua is no end! It is the beginning! We will all come together as one and bring about a new world! I can't wait!

standard.player: Well I'm glad to see you're so excited. Good luck with the tests.

standard.npc: And you!
We serve Crombwick's finest Bloody Bracer, that is all.
99 of you finest coins.

options.text: Alright, one Bloody Bracer, if that's all you have.

steps.player: Alright, one Bloody Bracer, if that's all you have.

steps.text: If the player has less than 99 coins:

steps.npc: I said 99 coins! You haven't got 99 coins!

steps.player: Sorry, I'll come back another day.

steps.text: If the player has at least 99 coins:

steps.npc: What can I say? The ingredients are locally sourced so it's high quality, I promise.

steps.player: Well, I guess I shouldn't shoot the messenger.

steps.npc: So...

steps.text: other

options.text: What can you tell me about this town?

steps.player: What can you tell me about this town?

steps.npc: I've not been here long myself, so I'm afraid I may not be of much help.

steps.player: What happened to the previous barkeep?

steps.npc: Oh, he had to leave.
Scared of turning.
Yes, into a sleeper.

steps.player: Oh right! You see, for a second there I thought you were talking about vampyres.

steps.npc: Ha ha! We, err, don't see many of those types around here. No, no, not at all.
I do. So...

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Oh, the red thirst will be upon you soon.
Just a jest, traveller.

standard.npc: Oh, hello.
My son fell ill with the plague...
It would be easier to cope with if I could have spent his last few days with him.
Those mourners came and whisked him away. He didn't even seem that ill, I thought it was a common cold... But the mourners said that he was infected and had to be taken away.
Two days later the mourners returned and told me he had died.

standard.player: Again, I'm sorry. Life can be harsh.

options.text: Where did the plague come from?

steps.player: Where did the plague come from?

steps.npc: It's down to King Tyras. He and his men brought the plague here from the west, and then left us to suffer. One day he'll pay for what he's done!

options.text: Have there been many victims of the plague?

steps.player: Have there been many victims of the plague?

steps.npc: You could say that... I've heard reports that half of West Ardougne is infected! Many have lost friends and family...

steps.player: It sounds an awful way to live.

steps.npc: People are very depressed and scared. I've never met anyone fully infected though. I suppose we should be grateful to the mourners for that.

options.text: I hope things get easier for you.

steps.player: I hope things get easier for you.

steps.npc: Me too...

standard-dialogue-after-song-of-the-elve.player: Hey Carla, how are you doing?

standard-dialogue-after-song-of-the-elve.npc: I'm okay. The loss of my son is something that I'll never be over. At least no one else has to suffer at the hands of those mourners though.

standard-dialogue-after-murder-mystery.npc: Apparently you aren't as stupid as you look.

standard.npc: Is there any chance you could help me?
It's my husband, he works on a fishing platform. Once a month he takes our son, Kennith, out with him.
They usually write to me regularly, but I've heard nothing all week. It's very strange.
Maybe, but no-one's heard from the other fishermen on the platform. Their families are becoming quite concerned.
Is there any chance you could visit the platform and find out what's going on?

standard.prompt: Start the Sea Slug quest?

steps.player: I suppose so, how do I get there?

steps.npc: That's very good of you [player name]. My friend Holgart will take you there.

steps.player: Ok, I'll go and see if they're ok.

steps.npc: I'll reward you for your time. It'll give me peace of mind to know Kennith and my husband, Kent, are safe.
That's a shame.
Bye.

after-sea-slug.npc: I'm good. Busy as always looking after Kent and Kennith but no complaints.

standard-dialogue-after-finishing-icthla.player: Hey there. How're you holding up?

standard-dialogue-after-finishing-icthla.npc: Not too bad. Still, I hope we can get rid of these spots soon.

standard-dialogue-after-finishing-contac.player: Hey there. How're you holding up?

standard-dialogue-after-finishing-contac.npc: Not too bad. Still, I hope we can get rid of these spots soon.
The embalmer has been importing a soothing balm from a merchant called Ali M. It's meant to stop the itching.
Not even remotely, but it sure does keep the flies away.

standard-dialogue-after-finishing-beneat.player: Hey there. How're you holding up?

standard-dialogue-after-finishing-beneat.npc: Much better now that we've finally got rid of those spots.

standard-dialogue-after-finishing-beneat.player: That's great to hear! All the best.

using-a-potion-on-him.player: I thought this acne potion might help ease your spots.

using-a-potion-on-him.npc: What? You intolerable, insufferable idiot. That won't work! I would say get out of my sight but that's not far enough away!

using-a-potion-on-him.player: I was just trying to help.

using-a-potion-on-him.npc: Clear off before I give you something to feel sorry about!

standard.player: Good day. What are you doing?

standard.npc: I'm cutting down mahogany and teak trees to make into furniture. It takes a while.

steps.player: You say there are a few different things I might want to track. What are they?

steps.npc: Well, you have both big and small points of interest, water currents, sea depths, weather patterns, and then there's also drink crates. They're a curious one that Steve likes people to track.

options.text: Can you tell me about charting smaller points of interest?

steps.player: Can you tell me about charting smaller points of interest?

steps.npc: Well, you'll likely spot some interesting things in the sea and on some of the less explored islands that you find whilst out sailing.
Charting these things is simple. All you need to do is just make a note of them as you find them!

steps.text: Many points of interest don't require any tools to chart. Just interact with them from your boat or while on foot when close enough to them.
other

options.text: Can you tell me about charting larger points of interest?

steps.player: Can you tell me about charting larger points of interest?

steps.npc: Ah, for them, you'll want to find a good spot and use a spyglass to take it all in.

steps.player: But how do I know where a good spot is?

steps.npc: That can take a bit of practice, but if you pay close attention, you might find some very subtle, definitely not obvious signs of where the best places are...

steps.text: The spyglass can be used to chart larger points of interest. You can do so either from your boat or while on foot. Keep an eye out for the sparkly white circles that show where a spyglass can be used.
other

options.text: Can you tell me about drink crates?

steps.player: Can you tell me about drink crates?

steps.text: If the player has not completed Prying Times:

steps.npc: They're a bit of an interesting one. It's been argued that they're not actually completely essential for charting the sea, but Steve thinks otherwise. Probably best you talk to him if you want to know more.

steps.text: You need to complete the Prying Times quest to learn about drink crates.
If the player has completed Prying Times:

steps.npc: They're a bit of an interesting one. On your travels, you may spot some sealed crates floating in the sea.
Once you find one, just pry it open with your crowbar. If you're lucky, there will be a refreshing beverage inside for you to try.
Be careful though, as some of them can be a tinge on the ripe side...

steps.player: I must admit, I'm not totally sure what these crates have to do with charting...

steps.npc: Yes, that opinion has come up before. However, according to Steve, it's an unwritten rule in this world that alcohol is the key to solving all problems.
It's also been said that these crates add a bit of much needed danger to the whole charting effort.

steps.text: Floating crates of drink can be found at sea and pried open with a crowbar. Once open, you can sample what you find inside. However, take care, for expired alcohol can be dangerous...
other

options.text: Can you tell me about tracking currents?

steps.player: Can you tell me about tracking currents?

steps.npc: Absolutely! Understanding the various currents around the seas is essential. As you sail around, you'll likely spot many currents of potential interest.

steps.text: If the player has not completed Current Affairs:

steps.player: But once I spot them, how do I track them?

steps.npc: Ah, for that, you'll need the right tool. Well, I suppose in this case, it's less of a tool and more of a friend.
It will probably make more sense if you head out and discover the art of tracking currents for yourself!
We had someone passing through recently who said that Arhein in Catherby was looking to track some currents. I'd suggest you go and speak to him.

steps.text: You need to complete the Current Affairs quest to learn about tracking currents.
If the player has completed Current Affairs:

steps.npc: To track them, you'll need to make use of your good friend, the current duck! Specifically, once you've found some currents you want to track, you'll want to let your current duck head out for a swim.
He'll track the currents for you, so all you need to do is follow him wherever he goes. Once he's done, just pick him up again and let him share what he discovered with you.

steps.player: Is this really the standard way of doing this?

steps.npc: Of course! I simply can't think of any alternatives!

steps.text: A current duck can be used to track currents. To do so, find an area of circularly expanding currents and release your duck there. Then just follow the duck with your boat and collect it again once it stops.
other

options.text: Can you tell me about checking sea depths?

steps.player: Can you tell me about checking sea depths?

steps.text: If the player does not have 38 Sailing:

steps.npc: Ah, for that, you'll need to go diving. However, you don't want to rush it. You'll need to make sure you're skilled enough for that sort of thing before you... dive in.

steps.text: You require 38 Sailing to learn about checking sea depths.
If the player does has 38 Sailing:

steps.npc: Ah, for that, you'll need to go diving. Doing so will let you take a record of the sea depth, but it's also great for learning more about the local underwater flora and fauna.
However, I wouldn't reccomend going it alone. Fortunately, a lot of mermaids have been popping up recently, interested in the extra sea traffic.
I hear they will guide you for a price, and for some inexplicable reason, that price seems to be solving a word-based puzzle for them.
Indeed, so get your thinking cap on... under your diving gear of course. It's very important you don't forget that.

steps.text: To check sea depths, you'll need to find a mermaid in the ocean, don some diving gear and then answer her puzzle. She'll then guide you down to the bottom of the sea for you to document your findings.
other

options.text: Can you tell me about tracking weather patterns?

steps.player: Can you tell me about tracking weather patterns?

steps.text: If the player does not have 57 Sailing:

steps.npc: Well, all good captains need to have a strong understanding of the weather out at sea. However, it requires a fair bit of skill to do it well. I'd suggest you wait until you're more experienced.

steps.text: You require 57 Sailing to learn about tracking weather patterns.
If the player has 57 Sailing:

steps.npc: Of course! All good captains need to have a strong understanding of the weather out at sea. However, to do it well, you'll probably want to enlist the help of a meteorologist.

steps.player: Where can I find one of those?

steps.npc: Well, it's a bit of an odd one, but I've been told there's a troll who has started working as one recently.
Indeed. It's a bit unusual, but who am I to judge! Anyway, apparently she's aquired a portable weather station, a very fine piece of equipment for measuring weather data.
If you come across this troll, she'll hopefully allow you to use this weather station for yourself.
Well, what you'll find is that the wind typically blows in large circles. What you need to do is find the middle of this circle, or the eye as we often call it.

You can use the weather station to work out the wind direction. If you follow it for a bit, you should be able to work out which way the circle is curving, and from that, you should be able to find the eye.
Just remember not to keep following the wind forever, or you'll just keep going around in circles!
Anyway, once you reach the eye, you can use the weather station to take the readings you need. After that, just make sure to return the weather station to the troll.

steps.text: To track weather patterns, you'll need to find the troll meteorologist, take her portable weather station and use it to find the eye of a circular wind storm. Once there, you can use the weather station to record your data.
other

steps.npc: Very well.

options.text: What do I get from charting the sea?

steps.player: What do I get from charting the sea?

steps.npc: Other than the thrill of exploration?
Well, the more you know about the sea, the more you'll be able to take advantage of it. Specifically, learning about the seas will offer the discerning captain a shortcut or two.
And for the less discerning captain, I have a stock of alcohol I'd be willing to part with for up to date charting information, along with some coins of course.
My observational skills are not what they used to be after all!

steps.text: You get the distinct impression you were just winked at by a blindfolded eye.

steps.npc: Finally, in return for charting information, I can offer some training that will help you improve your sailing abilities. Just let me know any time you completely chart an ocean.

steps.npc: Of course! There's the kraken ink stout, the perildance bitter, the trawler's trust, and of course, the horizon's lure! Which do you want to hear more about?
Well, kraken ink stout is the perfect drink if you consider yourself a bit of a magical sailor as it's said to improve both your sailing and magical abilities.
Many claim that it also increases the likelihood of encountering interesting things while out at sea. I'm not sure how a drink does that, but the world works in strange ways.

steps.speaker: Clerk
steps.text: My name is Clerk. I work on gathering people together to form what we call clans.

steps.speaker: Clerk
steps.text: Ah, clans. Where do I begin? Clans are groups of people gathered together for numerous reasons. Usually they have shared interests, like activities they enjoy together.

steps.speaker: Clerk
steps.text: These activities could include improving certain skills, battling the same monsters, or even battling other clans!

steps.speaker: Clerk
steps.text: Other clans form together because they just enjoy the company of other like-minded people. The clan community can be a great resource if you should ever need help with anything.

options.text: How do I join a clan?

steps.player: How do I join a clan?

steps.speaker: Clerk
steps.text: You can either form your own clan with your friends, or apply to an already existing clan.

steps.speaker: Clerk
steps.text: Should you choose to form your own clan you will need four friends to join you, and it is recommended that you have spent a good amount of time in this world first. Leadership is not for everyone.

steps.speaker: Clerk
steps.text: However, fret not. There are plenty of interesting and exciting clans out there! Check out the clan recruitment board to see which clans are currently accepting applications.

steps.speaker: Clerk
steps.text: You can either form your own clan with your friends, or apply to an already existing clan.

options.text: What can a clan offer me?

steps.player: What can a clan offer me?

steps.speaker: Clerk
steps.text: Clans offer you the ability to have an official gathering of friends or like-minded individuals in a hierarchical structure.

steps.speaker: Clerk
steps.text: In other words, you and your friends get an exclusive chat channel and a Clan Hall, as well as the ability to assign ranks to members.

steps.speaker: Clerk
steps.text: Ranks can be assigned from custom pre-sets, which then determine what permissions that person has.

steps.speaker: Clerk
steps.text: For example: One person may have the rank to kick players from the chat, while another has the rank to access the Clan Coffer.

steps.speaker: Clerk
steps.text: The Clan Coffer is a shared coin store, used by members of the clan. Highly ranked members can assign who has permission to deposit and withdraw coins.

steps.speaker: Clerk
steps.text: A Clan Hall is a private area only accessible for the people with the permission to enter. High ranked members of the clan can restrict it to only allow certain ranks in, or open it up to even allow guests.

steps.player: Why would I need a Clan Hall? Can't I get a house instead?

steps.speaker: Clerk
steps.text: The beauty of it is that you can have both. You can keep your house for private guests and your own personal use, but when you wish to see larger groups then the Clan Hall may be more fitting.

options.text: I'm in a clan. Can you give me anything?
I'm in a clan. Can you give me anything?

steps.speaker: Clerk
steps.text: My mission is to administer clans; I help form them and can tell you anything you need to know about them.

options.text: Sure, but why are you here specifically?

steps.player: Sure, but why are you here specifically?

steps.speaker: Clerk
steps.text: Why does anyone go anywhere? As a gatherer of people, I go where people gather. The Grand Exchange is known to be a place where people come together. What better place to bring them even closer?

steps.player: I suppose this usually is a crowded place.
