steps.text: Very much so. I was lucky to find this charming corner to set up the clan hub.

steps.speaker: Clerk
steps.text: The clan hub is what I call this area, my little corner of the Grand Exchange. This is where every clan is born, as well as the best place to look for new recruits.

steps.speaker: Clerk
steps.text: If you're in a clan you can also access your Clan Hall from here.

steps.npc: I'm Commissioner Anwar. I'm in charge of the Shayzien Constabulary. With Lord Shayzien currently busy with the war efforts, I'm also assisting him with his duties here in the city.

The Shayzien Army is split into six regiments plus the Shayzien Constabulary. While the six regiments are jointly responsible for protecting Kourend from external threats, we deal with issues closer to home.

The Intelligence Corps, the Medical Corps, the Engineering Corps, the Logistics Corps, the Rangers and of course, the Infantry. Each regiment is led by a general who reports directly to Lord Shayzien.

steps.player: It feels like there must be a bit of overlap between the Constabulary and the regiments, especially the Intelligence Corps.

steps.npc: On paper we're totally separate from the regiments. However, in reality you are correct. The distinction between internal and external threats grows murkier by the day.
More and more we find ourselves working alongside the Intelligence Corps and the other regiments. In particular, they've been supporting us in combating the rising gang threat in Port Piscarilius.
This is the Shayzien Administration. The city of Shayzien is run from here.
A lot of focus right now is on the war with the lizardmen. Most senior members of the Shayzien Army, including Lord Shayzien himself, are working out of the Shayzien Encampment instead.

steps.player: So the Shayzien Army are also responsible for running the city?

steps.npc: Indeed. There's more of a separation between the city of Shayzien and the Shayzien Army now than there used to be, but this will likely always be a military settlement.

steps.npc: Kourend's last King, Kharedst IV, had only one child when he died. She was too young to take the throne, so the Kourend Council was formed to look after things until she came of age.
Alas, she was very close to her father and his sudden death drove her to insanity. With no suitable ruler, the Kourend Council was made permanent.
The Kourend Council is made up of four councillors. Every four years there is an election for the people to decide who the councillors should be.
One of the councillors holds the position of Head Councillor and this rotates every year. I am the current Head Councillor.

steps.npc: The other councillors are Councillor Unkar and Councillor Orson. The fourth seat on the Council is currently vacent after the recent arrest of Councillor Hughes.

steps.player: So where do the five houses fit in?

steps.npc: The five houses of Kourend each have their own leader who rules over their city. The leaders of the individual houses must enforce and obey the laws set out by the Kourend Council, but can otherwise rule as they see fit.
I hope that helps.
Good day citizen.

after-completing-a-kingdom-divided.player: Well I do enjoy it when people get what they deserve.

after-completing-a-kingdom-divided.speaker: David Andrews
after-completing-a-kingdom-divided.text: You'll never know what it's like to be on top of the world. The power I had was unconquerable. I'd do it all again without hesitation.

after-completing-a-kingdom-divided.player: You never had any power. You were just a puppet. You've always been nothing, and that's all you'll ever be.
Enjoy your cell, puppet. Won't be seeing you.

standard.npc: Welcome to the Catherby Council Office. Your views are important to us.
Unfortunately, all of our operatives are too busy to help you today. Please try again soon.
I've been better.

steps.npc: You may or may not be aware, but a plague has spread across West Ardougne. Now, so far, our efforts to contain it have been largely successful, for the most part.
However, some sheep recently escaped from a farm near the city. When they were found, we noticed that they were strangely discoloured, so we asked the mourners to examine them.
They believe that the sheep have become infected with the plague.

steps.player: Are you sure it's the plague?

steps.npc: Well the mourners seemed convinced and they're the experts. Even if it's not though, the sheep are clearly diseased in some way.
As the councillor responsible for public health and safety here in East Ardougne, I am in charge of dealing with this problem.
We need someone to herd these sheep into a safe enclosure, kill them quickly and cleanly and then dispose of the remains hygienically in a special incinerator.
Unfortunately, nobody wants to risk catching the plague, and I am unable to find someone willing to undertake this mission for me.

steps.prompt: Start the Sheep Herder quest?

steps.player: I can do that for you.

steps.npc: You will? That is excellent news! Head to the enclosure we have set up on Farmer Brumty's land to the north of the city; the four infected sheep should still be somewhere in that vicinity.
Before you will be allowed to enter the enclosure, however, you must ensure you have some kind of protective clothing to prevent contagion.

steps.player: Where can I find some protective clothing then?

steps.npc: Doctor Orbon should have something suitable. You should be able to find him in the chapel just north of here.
Please also take this poisoned sheep feed; we believe poisoning the sheep will minimise the risk of airborne contamination, and is of course also more humane to the sheep.

steps.text: The councillor gives you some poisoned sheep feed.

steps.player: How will I know which sheep are infected?

steps.npc: The poor creatures have developed strangely discoloured wool and flesh. You should have no trouble spotting them. There should be four in total.

steps.player: That's not a job for me.

steps.npc: I do not blame you adventurer. It is not particularly pleasant work. My problem remains however. If you know of anyone suitable please send them this way; time is of the essence.
That's what concerns me... There might not be much life around here soon.

standard-dialogue-after-sheep-herder.npc: Well hello again adventurer! How are you today?
I'm okay. Sadly some more diseased sheep have appeared so I have them to deal with.

standard-dialogue-after-sheep-herder.player: Do you need me to help again?

standard-dialogue-after-sheep-herder.npc: Thank you for the kind offer. You've done enough though. We'll find someone else to deal with these ones.

standard-dialogue-after-sheep-herder-whi.npc: Hello, is there any news about how our sheep keep getting infected with the plague?

standard-dialogue-after-sheep-herder-whi.player: Not that I know of, sorry.

standard-dialogue-after-sheep-herder-whi.npc: I'd sure like to know why we can't contain it. Please raise the issue next time you see the Head Mourner.

standard-dialogue-after-song-of-the-elve.npc: Well hello again adventurer! How are you today?
Not too bad, I've a lot to do though. King Lathas left plenty of things for us to clean up.

after-completing-the-forsaken-tower-ques.npc: Thank you for helping to repair the Doors of Dinh. Kourend is a safer place because of you.

steps.npc: I'm Councillor Unkar, one of the members of the Kourend Council. We are responsible for running the entire Kingdom of Great Kourend.

steps.player: What brings you to Lovakengj then?

steps.npc: It's important for the council to maintain a good relationship with the rulers of the five houses. Although it is the council that rules, we can only do so with their support.
I'm here to help Lady Lovakengj out and to make sure she has everything she needs to rule effectively.

steps.text: other

options.text: What are the Doors of Dinh?

steps.player: What are the Doors of Dinh?

steps.npc: They are a great set of doors built by the legendary smith, Dinh, in the early days of Kourend. They were created to imprison a deadly beast known as the Wintertodt.
Unfortunately, the doors were recently damaged, putting Kourend at risk. The master smith Undor, managed to repair them though, something he couldn't have done without you.

steps.text: other

after-completing-the-a-kingdom-divided-q.speaker: Kubec Unkar
after-completing-the-a-kingdom-divided-q.text: A step down from what I'm used to.

after-completing-the-a-kingdom-divided-q.player: Well you'd better get used to it. This is where you'll spend the rest of your life, however long that ends up being.

after-completing-the-a-kingdom-divided-q.speaker: Kubec Unkar
after-completing-the-a-kingdom-divided-q.text: Oh, I'm all too aware of that. Here, I will fade into obscurity as the world forgets my actions. I've accepted it. Besides, it's for the best that I not be remembered.

after-completing-the-a-kingdom-divided-q.speaker: Kubec Unkar
after-completing-the-a-kingdom-divided-q.text: I only hope that the work I did for my home endures. Everything I did was to ensure that Lovakengj prospered.

after-completing-the-a-kingdom-divided-q.player: I'm sure they'll be just fine. If anything, I imagine they're better off without you.

after-completing-the-a-kingdom-divided-q.speaker: Kubec Unkar
after-completing-the-a-kingdom-divided-q.text: Don't be so sure. I've no doubt the new king has good intent, but our intentions mean little compared to our actions.

after-completing-the-a-kingdom-divided-q.player: Something you're all too aware of, I'm sure.

after-completing-the-a-kingdom-divided-q.speaker: Kubec Unkar
after-completing-the-a-kingdom-divided-q.text: Indeed. But I guess only time will tell. Farewell human.

standard.npc: Ahahahaha! I am Count Check, the renowned security expert. Would you like me to check your account to see if it is secure?

steps.text: If the player's account has a Bank PIN and is attached to a Jagex Account:

steps.npc: You have a Jagex Account, and you have set a Bank PIN, so you pass my checks! As you've passed my check for the first time, I award you a prize.

steps.text: lamp

steps.npc: You have a Jagex Account, and you have set a Bank PIN, so you pass my checks! As you've passed my check before, there's no prize now.

steps.text: If the player's account has a Bank PIN, but is not attached to a Jagex Account:

steps.npc: You do not have a Jagex Account, so you fail my checks! You should upgrade before we meet again.

options.text: Can you give me any advice?

steps.player: Can you give me any advice?

steps.npc: I can! Count with the Count as I count the steps to securing your account:
ONE... unique password!
Never use the same password for different accounts, or on different websites. If it got leaked, all of your accounts would become vulnerable at once!
TWO... step verification for your email account!
Good email providers let you set up two-step verification, maybe by generating security codes on a second device, or by sending codes to your phone. Make sure you've enabled this.

steps.text: If the player's account is attached to a Jagex Account:

steps.npc: THREE... Um... Use a Jagex Account. I can see you already do this.

steps.text: continue

options.text: What's that got to do with THREE?

steps.player: What's that got to do with THREE?

steps.npc: Look, I'd got something for ONE, TWO and FOUR, and I like counting, okay? Don't interrupt my flow!

steps.text: continue
If the player's account is not attached to a Jagex Account:

steps.npc: THREE... Um... Use a Jagex Account.
Visit the RuneScape website and log in to update your Account settings.

options.text: What's that got to do with THREE?

steps.text: continue

steps.text: continue

steps.npc: So may I check your account for you?

steps.text: If the player has visited the Stronghold of Security:

steps.npc: The Stronghold of Security, in Barbarian Village. There is much to learn there. But while you are here, may I check your account for you?
As you may see, I am a vampyre, from Morytania. I left there when I heard the terrible news and now I choose to spend my days warning others of the perils that lay in wait for them.
Yes, be warned! The travellers of these lands face danger from outside. Accounts can be stolen, and when that happens one can lose everything one has worked for.
I've left my vampyric ways behind me, and now I spend my days letting everyone know of this terrible danger.
In return for my dedication, I have been blessed with the ability to check if adventurers are ready to defend themselves against these account thieves.

I used to stalk the night drinking blood like vampyres do, and I am certainly not just a role-playing enthusiast in a costume! Never question that!

standard.npc: Hello there! Are you interested in hearing all about crafting?

options.text: How can I train my crafting?

steps.player: How can I train my crafting?

steps.text: If the player has level 1-9 Crafting:

steps.npc: To get started, you might like to try your hand at crafting some armour from cow's leather. There's a tanner just over in Al Kharid who could tan any hides for you.
Once you've managed to get your hand on some kind of leather, you just need a needle and some thread to get to work!
If that doesn't take your fancy, you could try your hand at spinning wool right here on the spinning wheel.
Come to think of it... Farmer Fred, just north of here, sounds like he could use a hand shearing some of his sheep. Maybe you could help him out, and get some practice while you're at it.
Is there anything else you want to know?

steps.text: other
If the player has level 10-19 Crafting:

steps.player: How can I train my crafting?

steps.npc: Lots of budding craftsmen seem to spend their time here spinning Flax into bow strings on the wheel, if that takes your fancy.
Or you might like to try your hand at crafting some armour from cow's leather. There's a tanner just over in Al Kharid who could tan any hides for you.
Is there anything else you want to know?

steps.text: other
If the player has level 20-99 Crafting:
If the player has below 99 Crafting:

steps.npc: Now that you've got a little experience under your belt, the world's your oyster!

steps.text: continue
If the player has 99 Crafting:

steps.npc: I can't help but feel like I should be the one asking you! At this point, the world's your oyster!

steps.text: continue

steps.npc: If you wanted to try your hand at making some jewellery, you'll want to get your hand on some gold and some kind of gem, with a mould to work with and a chisel at hand.
But if that's not your thing, maybe you'd like to try making some more armour!
Cow's leather's a good place to start, but you can try all other kinds of hides, like a dragon's!
Glass blowing seems to be a popular trade, too. You can forge molten glass from some sand and soda ash, then make all kinds of things using a glass blowing pipe.
Is there anything else you want to know

steps.text: other

options.text: What kinds of things can be crafted?

steps.player: What kinds of things can be crafted?

steps.npc: All kinds of things, really! You can make armour from leather, make some pottery, try your hand at glass blowing, make some jewellery, weapons even...
What would you like to hear about?
Sure thing! Most armour you can craft just involves taking a needle and some thread to whatever material you can get your hands on.
You might like to try with different kinds of animal hide, from cows, yaks, snakes, dragons... Or any other sort of fabric you can find!
Some crafty types have started making some leather- covered wooden shields recently, too!
You might find some creatures make for a pretty sturdy helmet, too. The best way to make something like that's just to take a good old chisel to it!
Would you like to hear about anything else I mentioned?

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Of course! Pottery's all kind of the same, it just takes a lot of getting used to.
All that there really is to it is getting your hands on some clay, getting it wet and getting to work on a potter's wheel.
Once you've got the shape you want out of it, you want to put it in a pottery oven to fire it up.
The barbarians west of Varrock seem to be pretty keen on their pottery. I'd take a look around there, if you wanted to try it out!
Once you get the hang of it, you can make pots, pie dishes, bowls... You know.
Would you like to hear about anything else I mentioned?

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Glass blowing? Well, to get started you'll need to get yourself some molten glass. You can make some for yourself by heating sand and soda ash in a furnace.
Once you've got a hold of that, you'll want a glass blowing pipe to blow it out in to shape, before it cools down.
It's not the easiest thing to get to grips with, but it shouldn't be too difficult!
Would you like to hear about anything else I mentioned?

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Sure. All it boils down to is a bar of gold or silver, some kind of cut gem if you're feeling fancy, and a mould to help shape the thing.
You can use a chisel to make a gem really shine and sparkle. You wouldn't want to use an uncut one for any jewellery.
Once you've got all of your materials together, you'll want to use a furnace to actually craft whatever it is you're trying to make!
Wizards seem to like enchanting their jewellery to do all kinds of things, too, but I don't know a lot about that.
Would you like to hear about anything else I mentioned?

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Well, there aren't too many weapons that people tend to craft, but there are a couple worth noting!
Battlestaves are probably the most common. It boils down to fastening an orb of some kind onto the end of a battlestaff.
You do need to get the orb in the first place, though... You can make one through glass blowing, but it's not much use without being charged.
I can't help much with crafting it, though! There's a little more magic involved there than I'm familiar with.
Aside from battlestaves, there are a couple of weapons that people like to make from silver... Sickles and bolts, usually.
Would you like to hear about anything else I mentioned?

steps.text: other

standard.npc: Hello there!

steps.npc: I'm the crew registrar. Here to cut through the red tape of crew management for anyone who needs it!

steps.player: A lot of paperwork in managing a crew is there?

steps.npc: You'd be surprised. Quality assurance guideline QA-275 states all crew must be appropriately fit and healthy after being subjected to QA form QA-275.

standard.speaker: Curator
standard.text: Nilsal to you, iknami. Welcome to the Grand Museum. I hope your visit is a pleasant one. If you have any questions about Varlamore, I'm happy to help.

options.text: Could you tell me more about the early history of Varlamore?

steps.player: Could you tell me more about the early history of Varlamore?

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Certainly! When it comes to the existence of Varlamore, it is Xeric we have to thank. During his Age of Strife, many refugees fled Kourend over the previously unexplored Custodia Mountains.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: There were three notable groups of these refugees. The first group, the Talkasti, settled in the Tlati Rainforest.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: While they initially lived nomadic lives, they eventually started to establish more permanent settlements, with Tal Teklan being the first.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: The next group were the Pericans. They first settled right here, building the town of Fortis, or Civitas illa Fortis as it eventually became.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Finally we have the dwarves. These were refugees from Lovakengj who established a home beneath Ralos' Rise, becoming known as the Dwarves of Cam Torum.

steps.player: Was there any friction between these groups initially?

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Oh yes, very much so. The dwarves, just as they do today, mostly kept to themselves. However, the Talkasti and Pericans came into regular conflict over various matters.

steps.player: But that's not the case now, right? What brought them together?

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: As you may well have already guessed, it was religion. Long before leaving Kourend, the Talkasti had taken to secretly worshipping Ralos and Ranul.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: After arriving here, they were able to openly practice their religion for the first time. Over time, the Pericans started to adopt this religion as well.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: As the two groups came together, the population of the region started to rapidly expand. This eventually led to the construction of Tempestus, and with it, the founding of Varlamore.

steps.player: So are there still distinctions between the Talkasti and the Pericans now?

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Yes and no. Those terms are no longer used to describe people today. Since we united, we have all been Varlamorians. However, you'll still find many traces of our previous divide.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: For example, here in Fortis, you'll find yourself surrounded by Perican architecture, whereas over in the Tlati Rainforest, the influence of the Talkasti remains clear.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Names are another good example. Indeed, look no further than our rulers. For most of our history, we were ruled by the Tullus dynasty, with Tullus very much being a name of Perican origin.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: However, we are now ruled by the Arkan dynasty, whose name can be traced back to early Talkasti nomads.

steps.player: I see. So where did the name Varlamore come from.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: The name comes from the River Varla that separated Talkasti and Perican territory. What was once a symbol of our divide, became the symbol of our unification.

steps.player: That was all super interesting! Thanks for the information.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Not a problem, iknami!

options.text: Could you tell me more about religion in Varlamore?
Could you tell me more about Varlamore's recent history?
I'd better get going. Thanks again.

steps.player: I'd better get going. Thanks again.

options.text: Could you tell me more about religion in Varlamore?

steps.player: Could you tell me more about religion in Varlamore?

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Of course! Whereas in other parts of the world you'll likely find followers of many gods, here in Varlamore, you'll only really find those dedicated to Ralos and Ranul.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Losanium is the official term for this religion, though it is not a term you'll find used very often.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Losanium encompasses the worship of both Ralos and Ranul, and while they do indeed go hand in hand, it is rare to find individuals equally dedicated to both.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Instead, most people focus their worship on one of the two, with Ralos being by far the more popular. Something that isn't too surprising given Ranul's association with death.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Now that said, you might actually find a higher than normal number of Ranul worshippers right here in the museum.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Something that is easily forgotten is that while Ranul is indeed a god of death, he is also a god of learning and knowledge.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: If you wish to learn more, you may well want to seek out one of the teoki in the temple to the south. Though of course, they may well have somewhat biased takes on their religious practices.

steps.player: I'll keep that in mind. Thanks.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Don't mention it.

options.text: Could you tell me more about Varlamore's recent history?

steps.player: Could you tell me more about Varlamore's recent history?

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: I can indeed! When it comes to recent events in the kingdom, the best place to start is with the War of Betrayal. It all started around 100 years ago when Imafore Tullus ascended to the throne.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: He soon reorganised the kingdom into the Varlamorian Empire, a controversial choice to say the least, though it soon became clear that controversial choices were quite popular with Imafore.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: While public opinion was always mixed, nothing he did resulted in outright conflict until his sudden and brutal murder of the Kourend Royal Family. War was quickly declared.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Until that day, Varlamore had successfully managed to avoid conflict since before the kingdom was officially established. To say the war was unpopular would be an understatement.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Imafore soon found himself facing as much resistance from within as he did from Kourend. The end result was predictable.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Imafore and his forces found themselves trapped between two armies at the Battle of the Proudspire. He was captured and executed, bringing an end to the Tullus dynasty.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: This brings us to a fun little fact. After his death, Imafore was succeeded by King Mezpah Arkan. One of his first acts was to call for the beheading of every statue of Imafore in the kingdom.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: The statues remain to this day. It's actually a crime to try and remove them. They exist as a reminder of our history, and a warning to any who would try to follow in Imafore's footsteps.

steps.player: I'll have to keep an eye out for them.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Indeed. I often like to challenge people to try and find them all!

steps.player: So how has the kingdom changed since Imafore died?

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: The War of Betrayal was very much seen as a wake- up call. While Varlamore had once flourished under the traditions of the Tullus dynasty, by the end, it's fair to say we were stagnating.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: King Mezpah set to work on transforming the kingdom. His ambitions were high, to the point that much of what he desired never came to pass in his lifetime.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: One of his most notable goals was to see Varlamore open more widely to the outer world. A goal which thanks to his great-granddaughter, has now finally been achieved!

steps.player: Well then I should be very thankful. Without him, I might never have been allowed to visit!

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: Indeed. We would often send our students on trips to the east prior to the opening of the borders. The amount of paperwork needed was astounding! Now we can just hop on a ship any time we like!

steps.player: That definitely sounds much more fun. Thanks for all the information.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.text: It's not a problem, iknami.

upon-losing-any-items-while-dying-for-th.text: So, mortal... you have died, as all mortals do. As you have suffered the loss of some items on this occasion, I have brought you here to explain for you how that works.

upon-losing-any-items-while-dying-for-th.player: I lost items? Can I get them back?

upon-losing-any-items-while-dying-for-th.speaker: Death
upon-losing-any-items-while-dying-for-th.text: Let me explain... Across most of the land of Gielinor, when you die, some of the items you're carrying are dropped.
A gravestone appears on the ground near where you died. You can go there and retrieve your items by clicking on it.
Your gravestone would be marked with an arrow to help to spot it. A grave icon appears on the world map too, if your grave is in a mapped area.
Gravestones charge a small fee to return especially valuable items, but most things are returned free of charge. Conveniently, a gravestone can take its fee straight from your bank.
A gravestone does not last forever. After about 15 minutes, a gravestone will collapse. Anything in it will be sent here, to me.

upon-losing-any-items-while-dying-for-th.speaker: Death
upon-losing-any-items-while-dying-for-th.text: I will look after such items, without a time limit. However, I do charge more for my services. It would be cheaper to retrieve them from the gravestone directly, if you can reach it in time.

standard.text: Pardon me, there are important duties which require my attention. Good day to you.

dialogue-after-unlocking-butler-s-bell.speaker: Demon butler
dialogue-after-unlocking-butler-s-bell.text: Ah [player name], a pleasure to see you here. Do you need anything?

dialogue-after-unlocking-butler-s-bell.speaker: Demon butler
dialogue-after-unlocking-butler-s-bell.text: If so, please do ring the bell as agreed. I cannot serve you otherwise.

dialogue-after-unlocking-butler-s-bell.speaker: Demon butler
dialogue-after-unlocking-butler-s-bell.text: It is a contractual matter, I'm sure that you understand.

dialogue-after-unlocking-butler-s-bell.player: Actually, I do have one question if you don't mind?
If I ring my bell in here, won't there be two of you?

dialogue-after-unlocking-butler-s-bell.speaker: Demon butler
dialogue-after-unlocking-butler-s-bell.text: Ah! This is always a sore point for mortals. The answer is both yes and no.

dialogue-after-unlocking-butler-s-bell.speaker: Demon butler
dialogue-after-unlocking-butler-s-bell.text: Presence is more complicated than you might think! There are ways to inhabit many places, and indeed many times, within what you would call the same moment.

dialogue-after-unlocking-butler-s-bell.speaker: Demon butler
dialogue-after-unlocking-butler-s-bell.text: Oh but it does! Though I fear that to you, it may never.

dialogue-after-unlocking-butler-s-bell.speaker: Demon butler
dialogue-after-unlocking-butler-s-bell.text: I must see to my other tasks now. Goodbye.

eastern-scholar.npc: Ah mortal, tell me, would you prefer to have your arms attached to the bottom of your feet, or your legs attached to the palms of your hands?
I wish to gain insight into your wants, so that I may provide enticing relics to your kind.

eastern-scholar.player: Well honestly, neither option is appealing. I like my limbs where they are.

eastern-scholar.npc: Prudish as expected. I must return to my work.

western-scholar.npc: Fool! Losing my focus due to your interruption! Leave now or I will break you.

western-scholar.player: Fine. No need to be rude about it.

standard.npc: Get out of my way, you fool! Never again interrupt Denadu!
Monkeys these days... you'll be acting like one of those awful Gnomes next...

standard-dialogue-undisguised-with-monke.npc: The Marimbo Guard will kill you on the spot, foolish human!

standard.npc: Hello citizen, how can I help?

options.text: Do you have any quests for me?

steps.player: Do you have any quests for me?

steps.npc: I don't know if you can help us!
The trolls have taken up camp on Death Plateau! They are using it to launch raids at night on the village. We have tried to attack the camp but the main path is heavily guarded!

steps.player: Perhaps there is a way you can sneak up at night?

steps.npc: If there is another way I do not know of it.
Do you know of such a path?

steps.prompt: Start Death Plateau?

steps.player: No but perhaps I could try and find one?

steps.npc: Citizen you would be well rewarded!
If you go up to Death Plateau be very careful as the trolls will attack you on sight!
One other thing.
All of our equipment is kept in the castle on the hill.
The stupid guard that was on duty last night lost the combination to the lock! I told the Prince that the Imperial Guard should've been in charge of security!

steps.player: No problem, what does the combination look like?

steps.npc: The equipment room is unlocked when the stone balls are placed in the correct order on the stone mechanism outside it. The right order is written on a piece of paper the guard had.
Well citizen, the Prince is fond of puzzles. Why he couldn't just have a key is beyond me!

steps.player: I'll get on it right away!

steps.npc: Never mind citizen.
Can I assist you with anything else?
Welcome to Principality of Burthorpe!
We are the Imperial Guard for his Royal Highness Prince Anlaf of Burthorpe.
Can I assist you with anything else?

options.text: Do you have any quests for me?
How goes your fight with the trolls?

steps.player: How goes your fight with the trolls?

steps.npc: I'm afraid I have bad news. We made our attack as planned, but we met unexpected resistance.
We were ambushed by trolls coming from the north. They captured Dunstan's son, Godric, who we enlisted at your request, we tried to follow but we were repelled at the foot of their stronghold.

steps.prompt: Start Troll Stronghold Quest?

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help?

steps.npc: The way tto the stronghold is treacherous, friend. Even if you manage to climb your way up, there will be many trolls defending the stronghold.
God speed friend! I would send some of my me with you, but none of them are brave enough to follow.

options.text: I thought the White Knights controlled Asgarnia?

steps.npc: God speed friend!

options.text: How goes your fight with the trolls?

steps.player: How goes your fight with the trolls?

steps.npc: We are busy preparing for an attack by night. Godric knows of a secret entrance to the stronghold. Once we destroy the stronghold Burthorpe will be safe! Friend, we are indebted to you!

options.text: I thought the White Knights controlled Asgarnia?

steps.player: I thought the White Knights controlled Asgarnia?

steps.npc: You are right citizen. The White Knights have taken advantage of the old and weak king, they control most of Asgarnia, including Falador. However they do not control Burthorpe!
We are the prince's elite troops! We keep Burthorpe secure!

The White Knights have overlooked us, until now! They are pouring money into their war against the Black Knights, they are looking for an excuse to stop our funding and I'm afraid they may have found it!
If we can not destroy the troll camp on Death Plateau then the Imperial Guard will be disbanded and Burthorpe will come under control of the White Knights. We can not let this happen!
God speed friend!
The plants! They're alive!
The doors won't stay closed forever!
They came from the ground! They came from the ground!!!
Round and round and round and round!
Time is running out! She will rise again!!!
They're cheering! Why are they cheering?

standard.npc: Good day, [Sir/Madam/ ]. Can I help you with anything?

steps.npc: You may.

standard-dialogue-after-throne-of-miscel.npc: Good day, Your Highness. Can I help you with anything?

steps.npc: Of course, Your Royal Highness.
Aye, indeed I am.

steps.player: What brings you to this place? I can't imagine anyone coming here by choice.

steps.npc: You're right, I did not come here by choice. I came here for vengeance.

steps.player: Vengeance? Against whom? Did someone take your gardening equipment?

steps.npc: My mission is not against another man and I will not have it mocked.

steps.player: Okay, sorry, I was just trying to lighten the mood. Care to tell me what it is against then?

steps.npc: Callisto, the great bear of the wilderness.

steps.text: With no Callisto kills:

steps.player: Can't say I've come across it before.

steps.npc: I'm not surprised, you'd do well to avoid him. Callisto is a great bear, his strength and size enhanced by the corruption of the Wilderness.

steps.text: continues
With at least one Callisto kill:

steps.player: Ah, I've had a few run ins with him myself.

steps.npc: Then you'll know he's not something to mock. I'm surprised you survived your encounter with such a great and corrupted beast.

steps.player: I'm stronger than I look, I've seen my fair share of monsters.

steps.text: continues

steps.player: Why are you so intent on taking him down?

steps.npc: Callisto killed my father. After hearing of a great beast in the heart of the Wilderness, he took it upon himself to bring him down.
He left our family home in Hosidius to hunt it down and...
... I haven't seen my father since. I swore I would avenge him and have dedicated my whole life to training for that moment.

steps.player: What happens after? When you do take Callisto down that is.

steps.npc: Oh... uh... I never thought about that...
My whole life has been spent preparing to avenge my father, I never thought about anything else...

steps.player: You seem like you've got a lot to think about then. I'll leave you to it.

options.condition: If the player has Craw's bow or the Fangs of Venenatis:

steps.text: With only Craw's bow in the inventory:

steps.player: Hey. Do you know anything about this?

steps.text: You show the bow to Derse Venator.

steps.npc: Ah, a fellow marksman. That's a unique bow you have there.

steps.player: Do you know anything about it?

steps.npc: I've done my fair bit of fletching in my day. I'd say this bow can be improved upon.
See those etches on it? You could put something sharp in there to improve the bow's strength.

steps.player: Interesting! I'll be on the lookout for a powerful enhancement like that.

steps.text: With only the Fangs of Venenatis in the inventory:

steps.player: Hey. Do you know anything about this?

steps.text: You show the Fangs of Venenatis to Derse Venator.

steps.npc: Those look like strong fangs. You could probably attach them to a bow to make it stronger.

steps.player: Interesting! I'll be on the lookout for a suitable bow.

steps.text: With both in the inventory:

steps.player: Hey. Do you know anything about this?

steps.text: You show the bow to Derse Venator.

steps.npc: Ah, a fellow marksman. That's a unique bow you have there.

steps.player: Do you know anything about it?

steps.npc: I've done my fair bit of fletching in my day. I'd say this bow can be improved upon.
See those etches on it? You could put something sharp in there to improve the bow's strength.

steps.text: You show the Fangs of Venenatis to Derse Venator.

steps.npc: Yes. Those look like they could be attached to the weapon.
Sure I can. For the right price.
500,000 coins would do nicely.

steps.prompt: Pay 500,000 coins to combine the fangs and bow?

steps.text: If the player does not have enough coins:

steps.player: I don't have the money for that.

steps.npc: Feel free to come back when you do.

steps.text: If the player has enough coins:
Derse Venator combines the items and gives you the Webweaver bow (u).

steps.npc: There we go! All done.

using-items-on-him-claws-of-callisto.player: Hey. Do you know anything about this?

using-items-on-him-claws-of-callisto.text: You show the claws to Derse Venator.

using-items-on-him-claws-of-callisto.player: Yeah. I got them from a really big bear.

using-items-on-him-claws-of-callisto.npc: By the gods... This bear must be even bigger than I imagined.

using-items-on-him-claws-of-callisto.player: So do you know if the claws would be useful at all?

using-items-on-him-claws-of-callisto.npc: I... have a lot to think about. Perhaps Andros Mai over there can help you while I think.

using-items-on-him-skull-of-vet-ion.player: Hey. Do you know anything about this?

using-items-on-him-skull-of-vet-ion.text: You show the skull to Derse Venator.

using-items-on-him-skull-of-vet-ion.npc: That looks like any skull to me. Who's is it?

using-items-on-him-skull-of-vet-ion.player: It's mine. I picked it up.

using-items-on-him-skull-of-vet-ion.npc: I meant... Sigh. Never mind. What do you want with the skull?

using-items-on-him-skull-of-vet-ion.player: I'm trying to find out if it's useful.

using-items-on-him-skull-of-vet-ion.npc: Don't know much about skulls, myself. That mage over there might know.
She's into some weird stuff, that one. Think she said her name was Phabelle Bile.

using-items-on-him-voidwaker-part.player: Hey. Do you know anything about this?

using-items-on-him-voidwaker-part.text: You show the weapon piece to Derse Venator.

using-items-on-him-voidwaker-part.player: Oh. Do you know someone who might know more?

using-items-on-him-voidwaker-part.npc: Just earlier I saw this lady run down into the basement of this pub.
I don't know who she is, but she looks like a strange one.
Strange attracts strange, so I reckon she might know about your strange weapon piece.

standard.speaker: Derwen
standard.text: You're a long way from home, traveller! How about some food to keep you going?

steps.speaker: Derwen
steps.text: I'll be here if you find yourself hungry!

standard-dialogue-after-the-completion-o.player: Can I go in the Arboretum?

standard-dialogue-after-the-completion-o.npc: Yes. Now leave me alone.

standard.npc: Yes?
Blood.
Yes, by the pint. Now, do you want one or not?

steps.npc: Two coins.

steps.text: If the player doesn't have at least two coins:

steps.player: Oh dear, I don't seem to have enough money.

steps.npc: Clear off then.

steps.text: If the player has at least two coins:
You buy a pint of blood.
blood pint

steps.npc: Clear off then.

if-the-player-is-disguised-but-has-not-c.npc: You're new here. I don't sell to new blood. Make a name for yourself and maybe I'll reconsider.

if-the-player-is-not-disguised.npc: Human! Get back to the slave pens before I call the guards!

standard-dialogue-after-the-queen-of-thi.player: So can I go in now?

standard-dialogue-after-the-queen-of-thi.npc: Yes! Now get out of my sight!

standard.npc: Sorry, but this is NOT a good morning!
I'm going to lose my job!

standard.player: What have you done to deserve that?

standard.npc: Nothing! But the Piscatoris Fishing Colony is going to go out of business, and I'll have to go back to the east.
If you want to help, you can get Kathy to take you up to the Colony. Herman's looking for someone to run an important errand for him.

after-swan-song.npc: Hello! What can I do for you?

options.text: How are things going for the Colony?

steps.player: How are things going for the Colony now the trolls have all gone away?

steps.npc: Well, it's been fairly quiet around here, but there's always repair work to keep us busy.
Oh yes, lots of them. Their population's been swelling ever since you wiped out the trolls in the area. They've hardly got any natural predators now.

steps.player: I was just wondering what you're doing.

steps.npc: Franklin's got me fixing this wall. You did a pretty good patch-job, but it could do with some work.

steps.player: I'm not surprised - iron sheets won't last any time at all with all that salt water around.

steps.npc: Yes, that's right. I'll probably get Arnold to order some fancy protective paint from the dwarves.

options.text: You know all your doors get stuck open?

steps.player: You know all your doors get stuck open?

steps.npc: Yes, the salt does terrible things to the hinges. I've been meaning to deal with them, but I never seem to get around to it.
Enjoy your fishing.

without-a-ghostspeak-amulet.text: When spoken to without a ghostspeak amulet:

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Wooo?  Woooo woo woooooo wooooo woooowooo wooo woooooo woo!

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Woo! WOO WOOOOO WOOWOOWOO WOO WOOOOO!

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Wooowoowoooooo.... Woowoowoo? Woooo, wooowoo wooowooowooo!

steps.player: Well, I guess you didn't say.

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Wooo?  Woooo woo woooooo wooooo woooowooo wooo woooooo woo!

steps.player: Yeah, I don't want to brag, but seriously: I am SOOOO rich....

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Woo! WOO WOOOOO WOOWOOWOO WOO WOOOOO!

steps.player: Yeah, I know they say money doesn't bring you happiness, but sometimes I just like to open my bank account and look at all of the stuff I own and just think to myself:

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Wooowoowoooooo.... Woowoowoo? Woooo, wooowoo wooowooowooo!

steps.player: Well, us rich alive people don't want to waste all day spending time with you poor dead people, because I'm just sooooo rich I have to go now, and very possibly make myself even richer.

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Wooo?  Woooo woo woooooo wooooo woooowooo wooo woooooo woo!

steps.player: Yeah, I heard about that, ha-ha-ha!

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Woo! WOO WOOOOO WOOWOOWOO WOO WOOOOO!

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Wooowoowoooooo.... Woowoowoo? Woooo, wooowoo wooowooowooo!

steps.player: Well, it was fun. Let's do it again sometime.

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Wooo?  Woooo woo woooooo wooooo woooowooo wooo woooooo woo!

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Woo! WOO WOOOOO WOOWOOWOO WOO WOOOOO!

steps.player: I know, but what are you going to do?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Wooowoowoooooo.... Woowoowoo? Woooo, wooowoo wooowooowooo!

steps.player: Well, I guess that's always true in the long run. See you around, weird invisible dead person!

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Wooo?  Woooo woo woooooo wooooo woooowooo wooo woooooo woo!

steps.player: Yeah it's not bad, but I prefer cooked chicken.

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Woo! WOO WOOOOO WOOWOOWOO WOO WOOOOO!

steps.player: Maybe, but nothing beats a home cooked pie!

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Wooowoowoooooo.... Woowoowoo? Woooo, wooowoo wooowooowooo!

steps.player: You don't say? I never knew that. Well, I must be going, see you around.

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Wooo?  Woooo woo woooooo wooooo woooowooo wooo woooooo woo!

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Woo! WOO WOOOOO WOOWOOWOO WOO WOOOOO!

steps.player: Somebody set up us the bomb!

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Wooowoowoooooo.... Woowoowoo? Woooo, wooowoo wooowooowooo!

steps.player: You have no chance to survive make your time.

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Woo?

steps.player: All your base are belong to us.
Hey, don't think you can talk to me like that!

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Woo! WOO WOOOOO WOOWOOWOO WOO WOOOOO!

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Wooowoowoooooo.... Woowoowoo? Woooo, wooowoo wooowooowooo!

steps.player: Just because you're already dead, doesn't mean I can't find a way to hurt you ghosty!
No, I've never been there in my life and CERTAINLY didn't steal anything when I was!

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Woo! WOO WOOOOO WOOWOOWOO WOO WOOOOO!

steps.player: Are you calling me a liar?!?! I have never stolen a thing in my life, and I resent the implication that I am the kind of morally depraved individual that would steal someone else's hard earned
Or cakes. Or fur. Repeatedly. For long periods at a time.

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Wooowoowoooooo.... Woowoowoo? Woooo, wooowoo wooowooowooo!

steps.player: Well if you are going to take that attitude, then I have nothing further to say on the matter, and bid you good day!
Dhalak, where can I find the swordsman Viggora?

steps.text: If Viggora is in the Rogues' Castle:

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Ah, the evil swordsman Viggora... A rogue like him would probably flock to his own kind.

steps.player: Okay, well I'll try and find him for you then.

steps.text: If Viggora is in the Slayer Tower:

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Ah, the evil swordsman Viggora... Perhaps he has returned to his castle in the dark lands?

steps.player: Okay, well I'll try and find him for you then.

steps.text: If Viggora is in the Edgeville Dungeon:

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Ah, the evil swordsman Viggora... Paddewwa was where he fought many battles, perhaps he has returned to one of his old haunts?

steps.player: Okay, well I'll try and find him for you then.
Could I have more of those ghostly robes you gave me?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: It seems as though the curse that keeps me here extends to my very clothing... which piece do you want?
the requested piece(s) of ghostly robes

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Here you go.

speaking-to-the-wrong-dhalak.text: When spoken to in a location not in the player's Curse of the Empty Lord sequence:

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: The endless tragedy of fate... Why must you torment me so?

steps.player: Alright, alright, calm down, calm down. All I said was 'hello'!

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: You can see me?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: And you understand my words?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: This is incredible! How can such a thing have come to pass?

steps.player: What can I say? I'm a professional.

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Hello back at you.

steps.player: So what's a nice ghost like you doing in a place like this?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: I suppose you think that's funny?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: I don't think I want to talk to you anymore.

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Hello stranger. It is rare indeed that I meet one who can see my presence, let alone one who can understand my words.

steps.player: Soooo.... Is it fun being a ghost?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Does it look like fun to you?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Then you are a fool, and I will waste no more words upon you.

steps.player: Sheesh, what a grouch. You'd think you'd have more of a sense of humour being dead and all.

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Mortal... Take heed of my example, and waste not your life, lest you may suffer the same fate as myself...

steps.player: Huh? You mean someone did this to you?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: You have ascertained the truth in my words...

steps.player: So who did it to you? And why?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Events of moons past, I remember not clearly...

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Hello stranger.

steps.player: So.... Invisible ghost haunting the same place for thousands of years, huh?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: You have no idea...

steps.player: Well, bad luck and all that. See ya around!

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Hello.

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Apparently.

steps.player: In which case I only have one thing to say to you:

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: ...what?

steps.player: Guess you don't have the amulet of humanspeak, huh?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: ...huh?

steps.player: Yeah, that's right. WOO! WOOOWOOO WOO WOOOOWOO! Got no comeback for that, have you?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: You are very strange...

standard.npc: Now then. Looking to buy some weaponry?

steps.npc: I'll be here if you change your mind.

standard.player: Hello there! You look like a hunter. What are you on the hunt for?

standard.speaker: Diana
standard.text: Nilsal! I'm actually out here writing reports on the animals of the forest.

standard.player: I see. Made any interesting observations so far?

standard.speaker: Diana
standard.text: Well, it would appear that a number of them are somewhat incorporeal...

standard.player: Yes, I'd actually made that observation myself. I imagine being incorporeal means they're somewhat harder to hunt?

standard.speaker: Diana
standard.text: You could say that.

standard.player: What about the ents? Anything interesting to note on them?

standard.speaker: Diana
standard.text: Yes, in between avoiding being stepped on by them, I've been trying to see how they interact with the other animals... specifically the corporeal ones.

standard.speaker: Diana
standard.text: Truth be told though, they don't really seem to be affected by them. They just keep on their merry way.
If the player has completed any Hunters' Rumours:

steps.player: Interesting... Well, if you need any help with any of this stuff, do let me know. It wouldn't be the first time I've dealt with guild reports.

steps.speaker: Diana
steps.text: Oh, are you familiar with the guild?

steps.player: I've helped out a touch here and there.

steps.speaker: Diana
steps.text: Good, good. Well, thank you for the offer, but I think I'm good for the moment.

standard.text: If the player has not completed any Hunters' Rumours:

steps.player: Interesting... Well, if you need any help with any of this stuff, do let me know.

steps.speaker: Diana
steps.text: Thank you for the offer, but I think I'm good for the moment.

standard.npc: Howdy there partner! Want to see my spinning plates? Or did ya want a holiday item back?

steps.npc: That's right. There's a funny story behind them, their shipment was held up by thieves.
The crate was marked 'Dragon Plates'. Apparently they thought it was some kind of armour, when really it's just a plate with a dragon on it!

options.text: I'd like to check holiday items please!

steps.player: I'd like to check holiday items please!

steps.npc: Sure thing, let me just see what you're missing.

steps.text: Diango's Holiday Item Retrieval opens.

standard-dialogue-obtaining-banana-hat.npc: Howdy there partner! You came at just the right time! I've got something for ya!
Well, I did some rooting around in my house and found this really neat hat.

standard-dialogue-obtaining-banana-hat.player: A hat? What sort of hat...

standard-dialogue-obtaining-banana-hat.npc: A banana hat! Would you like it?

steps.text: If the player has no inventory space:

steps.npc: Looks like you've got no space for it, I'll hold onto it till you do. Just come to me to claim it.

steps.text: continues
If the player has inventory space:

steps.npc: There you go amigo, enjoy!

steps.text: continues

steps.npc: So what else can I do for you partner? Want to see my spinning plates? Or did ya want a holiday item back?

steps.player: No thanks, I don't want it right now.

steps.npc: No problem amigo, come back to me to claim it if you change your mind.

standard-dialogue-obtaining-mystic-cards.npc: Oh wow, you did it! Well done!
I was wondering when someone would complete this. I've been holding on to the reward for a while.
The being who gave it to me was... rather strange.
They didn't say. But they did give me some sage advice before they left.
I don't remember exactly. Something about making the most of your time...

standard-dialogue-obtaining-mystic-cards.player: I... don't worry. Thank you for the reward, see you around!

standard.npc: Good day; what can I do for you?

steps.npc: I am involved in various stages of the dig, from the initial investigation to the installation of the mine shafts.
Well, let me know when you are.
You can only use a site you have the appropriate exam level for.
Yes, only persons with the correct Earth Sciences certificate can dig here. A level 1 certificate will let you dig in a level 1 site and so on.

options.text: I am already skilled in digging.

steps.player: I am already skilled in digging.

steps.npc: Well that's nice for you. You can't dig around here without a certificate though.
Oh yeah? And whose errand is that then? Where is your specimen jar?
And you reckon you have been sent on an errand - without a specimen jar? Sorry, I can't let you do that!
Oh you are, are you? Well where's your specimen jar?
Well how can you handle the specimens without it? As you should know, specimens are to be kept in specimen jars to keep them safe and preserved. Next time bring it along!

Find something worthwhile and he might let you use the winches. Until then, get lost!

standard-dialogue-digging-with-a-spade-i.npc: Oi! What do you think you're doing? There's fragile specimens around here!

standard-dialogue-using-a-specimen-brush.npc: Use your brush on specimens to clean them, not the dirt!

standard-dialogue-using-a-trowel-on-soil.npc: Hey, where are your leather gloves?
Well get some and put them on first!
Oi! No boots! No leather boots: no digging!
Sorry, you must use a rock pick to dig at a level 2 site.

standard-dialogue-using-a-trowel-on-the-.npc: Excuse me! No digging in the specimen trays please.

standard-dialogue-using-a-rock-pick-on-a.npc: No, no; rock picks should only be used to dig at a level 2 site.

after-the-dig-site.npc: Ah, it's the great archaeologist! Congratulations on your discovery.

getting-caught-when-thieving.npc: What do you think you're doing?

standard.npc: Hello. My name is Dimintheis, of the noble family Fitzharmon.

options.text: Why would a nobleman live in a dump like this?

steps.player: Why would a nobleman live in a dump like this?

steps.npc: The King has taken my estate from me until such time as I can show my family crest to him.

Well, there is a long standing rule of chivalry amongst the Varrockian aristocracy, where each noble family is in possession of a unique crest, which signifies the honour and lineage of the family. More than this

however, it also represents the lawful rights of each family to prove their ownership of their wealth and lands. If the family crest is lost, then the family's estate is handed over to the current monarch until the crest is
restored.

This dates back to the times when there was much in-fighting amongst the noble families and their clans, and was introduced as a way of reducing the bloodshed that was devestating the ranks of the ruling classes at that
time. When you captured a rival family's clan, you also captured their lands and wealth.
Well, my three sons took it with them many years ago when they rode out to fight in the war against the undead necromancer and his army in the battle to save Varrock.

For many years I had assumed them all dead, as I had heard no word from them, but recently I heard word that my son Caleb is alive and well, and trying to earn his fortune as a great chef in the lands beyond White
Wolf Mountain, although I know not where.

steps.prompt: Start the Family Crest quest?

steps.npc: I thank you greatly adventurer! Also... if you find Caleb... please... let him know his father still loves him...

steps.player: I'm not interested in that adventure right now.

steps.npc: I realise it was a lot to ask of a stranger.

options.text: You're rich then? Can I have some money?

steps.player: You're rich then? Can I have some money?

steps.npc: Gah! Lousy beggar! Your sort is what's ruining this great land! Why don't you just go and get a job if you need money so badly?

options.text: Hi, I am a bold adventurer.

steps.player: Hi, I am a bold adventurer.

steps.npc: An adventurer hmmm? How lucky. I may have an adventure for you. I desperately need my family crest returning to me. It is of utmost importance.

options.text: Why are you so desperate for it?

options.text: Have you got any quests for me?

steps.player: Do you have any quests for me? I really want one. I really want to help out!

steps.text: You murmur under your breath something about how great the rewards were last time you did a quest for Dimintheis.

steps.npc: My family consider what you did for us a great service. We couldn't possibly trouble you further.

steps.player: There must be SOMETHING you need help with. I am a great adventurer after all.

steps.npc: There really isn't anything, I am very content with life right now.

options.text: I guess money does buy happiness.

steps.player: I guess money really does buy happiness.

steps.npc: What was that? I didn't quite catch that.

options.text: Oh come on, however menial, I want to help!

steps.player: Oh come on, surely there's something I can help out with! I want to help, however menial it is.

steps.npc: Okay okay. Fine then. Whilst I don't have anything for you, how about you try my sons, they are always wanting something done.

steps.player: Fantastic! I'll get straight to it!

steps.text: You smell the sweet smell of the great rewards that may soon come.

steps.npc: You have my eternal gratitude for all you have done in saving my family's honour, adventurer. Perhaps some day my sons will overcome their differences.

steps.npc: Hello again, adventurer. I hope that Shield of Arrav business marks the start of something big for my family. Maybe it will help me finally get out of this hole!

steps.player: Do you have any gauntlets for me?

steps.npc: Combine that with the whole Shield of Arrav business and things are really starting to look up for us!

options.text: Could I get some more gauntlets, please?

steps.player: Your new master, that would be...?

steps.npc: Yama! I sold my soul you see, well, I guess that Ox-headed guy down there forcibly removed it.

steps.player: That doesn't sound like a fair trade...

steps.npc: Oh, don't worry, I'm perfectly fine with the outcome. Sure, the loss of vision is a shame but it could be worse.

steps.player: Perhaps it's a good thing you can't see...

steps.npc: What was that?

steps.text: other

steps.npc: The voice demanded that we stare into the fire until we saw enlightenment.

steps.npc: Blindingly so.

steps.player: Wait! Did you say human sacrifice?

steps.npc: Why, of course! We're Zamorakians, we're evil...

options.text: Well, I'll leave you to it.

steps.npc: It came from the west somewhere. It is extremely quick spreading, and utterly deadly.

Unfortunately if you reach this stage of infection then no one can save you.
You do that adventurer. You do not want to become infected by the plague.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-no-d.npc: Welcome to the Nightmare Zone! Would you like me to create a dream for you?

steps.npc: My name's Dominic Onion but you can call me Dom, or Mr Onion.

steps.player: Mr Oni...Dom, how did you get that name?

steps.npc: Well that's a long story...but I can tell you that it involved my parents, 3 blurberry specials, and a chinchompa.
Oh yes, Nigel played a crucial role in the whole debacle. It's all very amusing now that I think back to it.
Good times...
This is the Nightmare Zone!
Don't worry, it's not as bad as it sounds...most of the time.
Truth be told, that name wasn't my first choice, it's what the local folk have been calling it and so it sort of stuck.
My original plan came to me in a vivid dream when I was younger you see, I saw myself running a successful business from a great structure in a strange land.
Well, I say strange, but I'd never left Lunar Isle at the time and this place was very hot and dry, unlike anything I'd seen before.
When I told my father about the dream he laughed and said I should become a banker like him and his father before him but in that moment I knew that it wasn't the life for me.
I had to find out what this dream meant and if it was a vision of the future or not.
Growing up, I studied hard to find out more about magic, especially oneiromancy and the interpretation of dreams.
Having learned as much as I could on Lunar Isle I set out to find and learn from other great wizards I'd heard of in stories as a child.
I set off to travel the world, discovering more about dreams to enable me to understand the dream I'd had as a child.
I needed to know what this dream meant and if it was truly a vision of the future.
If so I knew I had to try and find this location and build the huge tower I saw.
I was going to call it 'Dom Onion's Tower', but I've not found this strange place or gathered enough money to build it just yet.
That's why I've setup this small business venture in the mean time selling dreams to people. I just need a big enough crowd to kickstart my business.
It's all part of my five year plan, and who knows, perhaps my dream will come true; I'll discover this place and build Dom Onion's Tower!

options.text: Can you tell me about the dreams?

steps.player: Can you tell me about the dreams?

steps.npc: Certainly. I can delve into your memories and search for the key events that have affected you on your adventures.
I then take the essence of these memories and put that in the vial you see on the plinth.
I imbue a bit of magic, then give the vial a bit of a shake, and when you drink it you'll be able to re-live an encounter close to the original.
Don't worry though, when you're in a dream, you're perfectly safe even if it does seem very real.
If you sucessfully overcome the dream or die trying, you'll leave the dream state and return to normal with your grey matter and appendages intact.

steps.player: Are all dreams the same or are there different options?

steps.npc: Oh no, they can vary wildly! You can choose from one of three main options.
Firstly, I can create a one-on-one encounter with an adversary you've defeated in your adventures. People like to practice in these dreams.
Then there's a sort of Endurance dream, where you face enemies in encounter after encounter, and try to survive to the end.
And finally there's something I like to call a Rumble, where you face multiple adversaries at the same time. I imbue a bit more magic and shake the vial harder to create that one!
You can invite friends to fight alongside you in a Rumble dream. Once I've set up the dream for you, step into the enclosure and invite up to 4 friends.
For the Endurance and Rumble dreams, I charge a fee for my work. I don't like handling the money directly, so instead I've set up a secure coffer.
After you've asked me to set up a dream, put some money in my coffer. I'll deduct the fee from the coffer when you start the dream.
There's a red vial on the other plinth. Your friends can drink from it to enter your dream as a spectator to observe your progress.
Finally here's one other option you get, and that's how difficult the encounters are. As well as the normal dreams, the bravest adventurers can choose a harder version*.
Certainly. You can practice for free, but the larger dreams require more skill to imbue the potions and so there's a fee for those.

options.text: What's the giant tree stump all about?

steps.player: What's the giant tree stump all about?

steps.npc: This stump is all that remains of the Great Auburn Redwood. It was, and in many ways still is, one of the key holy sites of Varlamore.
The tree was destroyed during the War of Betrayal many years ago. It was here in the Auburn Valley that the fighting was at its most fierce.
Both sides resorted to tactics that most would consider to be beyond horrifying. The tree was sadly a casualty of such tactics.
That has never been clear. Ranul teaches us to find and preserve the truth, but in war, the truth is sadly left behind.

steps.player: So the battles that took place here... Is that why all these animal spirits are here now?

steps.npc: Yes. They are the spirits of the animals that died here during the War of Betrayal. They did not pass on to Mictl, for they have unfinished business in these lands.
That is beyond our understanding. We believe they are here to guide the ents that live in the valley so that they may one day regrow the Great Auburn Redwood.
Much of the valley was destroyed during the war. Most of what you see around you was regrown by the ents.
Indeed it is, my child. That is why it is our duty to ensure the ents are protected. The events of the war cannot be repeated.

options.text: What's it like living so close to the wilderness?

steps.player: What's it like living so close to the wilderness?

steps.npc: Oh, it's not all that bad. It was a bit scary at first but as long as I don't go past the warning signs I'm all right.
It's actually pretty quiet here. I used to live in Lumbridge and, let me tell you, that's the dangerous place for people like me.
Thieves were picking people's pockets with impunity, and killing them on the streets in broad daylight!
And there weren't even any guards to protect us! Not that the guards in the other cities do much good to protect people from what I've heard.
I just thank goodness I haven't got an Attack option any more! I wouldn't last five minutes!

options.text: How did Dave come to be evil?

steps.player: How did Dave come to be evil?

steps.npc: Oh, I don't know really. He's always been evil, I think. Maybe growing up so close to the wilderness has affected him in some way.
When he was little he used to want to go into Edgeville dungeon. You know how kids are, always wanting to be dungeon adventurers! But he didn't want to be a hero, he wanted to be a monster!
And then he spent all summer building a tree-house. Except it wasn't a tree-house, of course, it was his Tower of Fear!
Of course I was hoping he'd have grown out of it by now and maybe even left home. But at least it keeps him happy.

steps.npc: Everyone has a rank. It's meant to indicate how good they are at fighting, compared to other people.
In ranked fights, the winners gain rank and the losers lose rank. The Arena staff will decide who'll be fighting in each ranked Duel, and send the invitations.
But if you just want some casual fun, you can have an unranked Duel, where no-one gains or loses rank. You can organise your own unranked Duel against whoever you want to fight.

steps.text: This leads deeper into the guild.  Through here you'll find even more rocks including runite and amethyst!

steps.speaker: Dwarf
steps.text: Of course. Go right ahead.

standard-dialogue-inside-the-mining-guil.speaker: Dwarf
standard-dialogue-inside-the-mining-guil.text: Sorry, but you're not allowed in there.

standard.speaker: Dwarf
standard.text: Hello there. Do you need anything?

standard.speaker: Dwarf
standard.text: This cave leads to the Mining Guild, home to the finest mining site around. Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: What have you got in the Guild?

steps.player: What have you got in the guild?

steps.speaker: Dwarf
steps.text: All sorts of things! There's plenty of coal rocks along with some iron, mithril and adamantite as well.

steps.speaker: Dwarf
steps.text: Deeper in the guild you'll find even more rocks including some runite! The best bit though is our amethyst mine, the only one in the land!

steps.speaker: Dwarf
steps.text: There's no better mining site anywhere!
other

options.text: What do you dwarves do with the ore you mine?

steps.player: What do you dwarves do with the ore you mind?

steps.speaker: Dwarf
steps.text: What do you think? We smelt it into bars, smith the metal to make armour and weapons, then we exchange them for goods and services.

steps.player: I don't see many dwarves selling armour or weapons here.

steps.speaker: Dwarf
steps.text: No, this is only a mining outpost. We dwarves don't much like to settle in human cities. Most of the ore is carted off to Keldagrim, the great dwarven city. They've got a special blast furnace up there - it makes

steps.speaker: Dwarf
steps.text: smelting the ore so much easier. There are plenty of dwarven traders working in Keldagrim. Anyway, can I help you with anything else?
other

standard-dialogue-attempting-to-exit-thr.speaker: Dwarf
standard-dialogue-attempting-to-exit-thr.text: Sorry, but you're not experienced enough to go in there.
You need a Mining level of 60 to access the Mining Guild.

steps.speaker: Dwarf
steps.text: I hope the goblins are properly maintaining their stretch of track! I'd hate to see them spoil good Dwarven workmanship.

steps.speaker: Dwarf
steps.text: You're [player name], aren't you? It's a good job you did helping to get this train link open.

steps.speaker: Dwarf
steps.text: Y'know, at first I didn't like the idea of visiting a goblin city, but these cave goblins are alright.

steps.speaker: Dwarf
steps.text: These goblins have so much more advanced technology than us. Take a look at their magical lights! We could never create something like them.

steps.speaker: Dwarf
steps.text: Dorgesh-Kaan's very nice to visit, but I don't think I'd want to live there.

standard.npc: Yeah...whada you want?

steps.npc: I'm nobody you need to worry about...who are you? Why are you asking so many questions? Are you with the Varrock guards?

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Well, as if it's any of your business, I'm an associate of Hammerspike. He's a great dwarf you know. You could learn a lot from a dwarf like him.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: I have an ongoing contract with Hammerspike, when he gives the word, the hammer starts flying.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Excellent! I'm just waiting for my ship to arrive and then we can go.

If the player has no gold ore:

steps.player: I don't have any, I'm afraid.

standard.text: If the player has 1 gold ore:

steps.player: Well, I have this one piece of ore...

steps.speaker: Dwarven Boatman
steps.text: That wouldn't do you much good, I'm afraid. My minimum fee is one piece of gold ore, there wouldn't be anything left for you.

options.text: Yes, please take my gold to the city.

steps.npc: Well, I suppose I do keep getting captured by the trolls and thrown in prison...But they always release me in the end, I'm far too old and skinny for their tastes.
In any case, this is my home, and I'm not leaving it. And this area has the tastiest goats!

2019-easter-event-starting-the-2019-east.npc: Oh no, why today of all days?
I'm having an eggceptionally bad day. But if you must know, my Egg making machine is shell dry and the next shipment of fuel will not be here for a while!
I would love it if a cracking adventurer, such as yourself, would help a Bunny in need.

2019-easter-event-starting-the-2019-east.prompt: Will you help the Easter Bunny?

steps.player: I would love to help you mix up some more fuel.

steps.npc: Thanks for eggreeing to help me.
There are three ingredients that are needed to make the fuel.
The first ingredient is Dried cocoa. During any other time of year this ingredient would be eggceptionally hard to get.
But if I'm spot on with my information, there should be a merchant rolling into Al Kharid soon. He should sell you some.
Try not to bring me camel dung, they do look similar.
The second ingredient is really high quality milk.
The most eggceptional milk around has got to be milk from Hosidius, I'm sure Duke Horacio's cook can help you out.
The third ingredient is some cracking spices, very special ones. Can't go into detail, trade secret and all.
I'm sure if you talk to Martin in Draynor, he'll be a good egg and help you out if you ask for Special spices.
Since you're doing errands for me. Feel Free to use my tunnels to get around.
But don't make a yolk out of it, you may only use each tunnel once. Can't have you interrupting my workers any more than that.
Also, if you ever forget what you need, there will be a worker nearby who can remind you.

steps.player: I'll get right on it. Be back soon.

steps.npc: See you soon!
I'll have you know this is no yolking matter.
