when-first-spoken-to-after-starting-the-.player: Easter Bunny! I knew I would find you here.

when-first-spoken-to-after-starting-the-.npc: Easter Bunny... Now there's a name I haven't heard in a long time...

when-first-spoken-to-after-starting-the-.player: What have people been calling you instead?

when-first-spoken-to-after-starting-the-.npc: Many times have I walked past Varrock West Bank and been called 'Sellin lobbies 200gp'.
I don't really understand that one.

when-first-spoken-to-after-starting-the-.player: Do you think perhaps they weren't talking to you?

when-first-spoken-to-after-starting-the-.npc: Who could blame them? I'm a failure!

when-first-spoken-to-after-starting-the-.player: Oh come on now, what do you mean?

when-first-spoken-to-after-starting-the-.npc: You call me the Easter Bunny? What right do I have to that name?
I don't feel the spirit of Easter within me.
I'm just a big dumb rabbit!

when-first-spoken-to-after-starting-the-.text: The Easter Bunny is clearly very upset and needs cheering up. Perhaps the other people in the Rabbit Hole have some ideas?

when-spoken-to-a-second-time.player: Hello Easter Bunny, how are you feeling?

when-spoken-to-a-second-time.npc: Maybe I'll make my way through this sorry old world as a clown...

cheering-up-easter-bunny-with-bowley-mol.speaker: Bowley Moley
cheering-up-easter-bunny-with-bowley-mol.text: Hello! Have you come to take part in the festivities?

options.text: The Easter Bunny is looking awfully glum this year.

steps.player: The Easter Bunny is looking awfully glum this year.
Perhaps we can help raise the Easter spirits?

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: You want to do some necromancy... To cheer up the Easter Bunny?

steps.player: No no no! It's just a figure of speech.
I just wonder if we could do anything to help.

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: Leave it to me boss.

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: I happen to know the E.B. is a big fan of bowling. In fact, he used to be a wizard on the lanes. A champion!

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: I also happen to have the ability to...

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: ...Rig the game in his favour.

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: Which is handy, he's very out of practise nowadays.

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: Oh no! You see, I have these gears set up just here.

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: Wait, are you just trying to get my trade secrets?

steps.player: This is strictly a humanitarian effort!
Look, I just want to get Easter back on track.
You can keep your hustle going, I just want to help the Easter Bunny.

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: Oh alright, since I do owe the big softie. But I've got my whiskers on you!
Small cutscene ensues...

steps.npc: So, what is it you wanted to show me, [player name]?

steps.player: Well, Bowley here let me in on your secret. Bowling champion three years in a row.

steps.npc: Oh. Those were the days, I haven't partaken for while now though...
I just haven't had the spring in my step with my egg responsibilities.
What do you mean? It's hardly fun without decent competition.
And nobody here quite likes bowling.

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: They what now?

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: I've only just gone and spent ages digging out this place and installing the machinery!

steps.player: Nothing to worry about I'm sure!

steps.npc: Ah Bowley, it is good to see you again.

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: Long Ears Johnson. Come to terrorise me pins again?

steps.npc: Oh yes, [player name] is apparently quite good.
It's been so long since I've had a decent set with a worthy opponent.

steps.player: Chin up bucko, I'm here and ready to challenge your rule of these alleys!

steps.npc: Well, I suppose I'm not doing anything else. Why not?

steps.text: The player bowls down 3 carrot pins.

steps.npc: A fine shot, but not quite enough!
Watch this!

steps.text: Thunk
The Easter Bunny bowls a strike.

steps.player: I'd better shape up or this will be quite one sided.
And that would be no fun at all.

steps.text: Clang
The player bowls down the middle 6 pins.

steps.npc: Ah, so you have some fight in you.

steps.player: I could do this all day.

steps.npc: That's exactly what I wanted to hear!

steps.text: The screen fades black with the text "Some time later..."

steps.npc: I'm surprised I hadn't heard about your prowess before, [player name].

steps.player: Ah you know me, the most modest adventurer in Gielinor.

steps.npc: Ah, well I suppose I should pack it in while I'm ahead.
But we should do this again.

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: Aye we should! Also if you could get the word out about my establishment, I'll be raking it in!

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: I mean... The Rabbit Hole will enjoy all the visitors?

steps.player: It was a close match. How are you feeling now?

steps.npc: Oh it was fun but I think I'm just going to sit in the Rabbit Hole a bit longer.
I should be off. Always a pleasure, Bowley.

steps.speaker: Bowley Moley
steps.text: Aye, till next time.

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-after-bowlin.player: Hello Easter Bunny, how are you feeling?

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-after-bowlin.npc: I feel less horrible I suppose...

using-a-fancy-carrot-on-the-easter-bunny.player: Hey Bunny, would you like a fancy carrot?

using-a-fancy-carrot-on-the-easter-bunny.npc: Not really, I've eaten a lot of carrots recently.

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-while-holdin.player: Hello! I have a surprise for you.

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-while-holdin.npc: Oh? A surprise? It's not something horrible I hope.

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-while-holdin.player: Oh no, it's something quite delicious actually.
A lovely mug of carrot juice!
Don't worry, this is fancy carrot juice. I made it myself with some fantastic carrots.

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-while-holdin.npc: You made it? Well in that case I suppose I might give it a try. As long as Wheeler hasn't been near it.

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-while-holdin.player: I made sure of that. Go on!

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-while-holdin.npc: That was delicious, nothing like the usual slop.
Thank you, [player name], I really needed that.

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-while-holdin.player: How are you feeling now? Any better?

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-while-holdin.npc: Hmm... I'm feeling a bit more hopeful. Like spring is about to, well, spring! But I'm not sure if Easter is really my thing any more.

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-while-holdin.player: I'm sure I can help you remember how wonderful it is.

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-after-giving.player: Hello Easter Bunny, how are you feeling?

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-after-giving.npc: Hmm... I'm feeling a bit more hopeful. Like spring is about to, well, spring! But I'm not sure if Easter is really my thing any more.

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-after-giving.player: I'm sure I can help you remember how wonderful it is.

trying-to-talk-to-easter-bunny-with-east.player: Hmmm... I should check in with Eggus before I give one of these buns to the Easter Bunny. Quality control or something.

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-after-having.player: Hi! I'm back with an Easter treat, just for you.

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-after-having.npc: Special eh? Why would you give me something special?
I don't know if I deserve anything.

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-after-having.player: Here, it's an Easter bun. Fresh out of the oven.

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-after-having.npc: An Easter bun? I like those!
Yum! That was lovely. Thanks, [player name].

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-after-having.player: You are most welcome. Do you feel a bit more Easter- ey now?

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-after-having.npc: Oh, I'm starting to remember now! Easter is great! But I just... Hmm, I don't know...
I feel like I need one more little treat before I do anything to help with Easter.

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-after-having.player: Alright, let me think of something.

easter-bunny-after-cheered-up-two-times.npc: One more treat and I'll be ready to work on Easter again.

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-after-the-pe.npc: That dance was amazing! Well done. I feel so... Invigorated!

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-after-he-men.npc: Lawks! Look at the time, I should get back to Varrock to set up the Eggs!

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-near-varrock.npc: Thanks for saving our bacon and eggs again, [player name]!

talking-to-the-easter-bunny-near-varrock.text: You've completed the Easter event: One glum bunny

It is often speculated that Xeric and his predecessor, King Shayzien VII, were in fact the same person.
Like Xeric, King Shayzien VII was fascinated with the Dark Altar.
The King was killed at the Battle of the Concourse during the 37th decade. We have many accounts of this, yet his body was never recovered.
Just days after his death, we have the first recorded mention of Xeric, an incredibly powerful mage who resembled the King.
It is written that Xeric killed the rulers of Kourend's five cities and claimed the kingdom as his own.

steps.npc: They remain loyal to Xeric. Even to this day they continue to attack the kingdom, as you may have seen.
Fortunately, the Shayzien Army keeps them under control.

steps.player: Why do they keep fighting? Surely after a thousand years they must know Xeric is gone?

steps.npc: Without examining their minds, we will never know for sure. However, we assume Xeric genetically altered them to enforce that their duty is to serve him.

steps.player: But if they are serving Xeric, why do they attack the kingdom?

steps.npc: A good question. One that I'm afraid I do not know the answer to.
Is there anything else you would like to know?

steps.text: other

steps.npc: During the 47th decade, after ten decades of oppression, the people revolted against Xeric and his army of lizardmen.

steps.player: Why did the people suffer for so long?

steps.npc: The events were triggered through the courage of one man, Byrne. He was not a man of particular stature of nobility, though he did proceed to become king.
'Twas the 312th day of decade 47. Byrne, a farmer by trade, is said to have witnessed a lizardman guard murder a child whilst working his farm.
Outraged at what he had just seen, Byrne grabbed his pitchfork and sprinted towards the guard.
Blinded by fury, Byrne attacked the guard, slaughtering the lizardman in plain sight of all around.
Legend has it Byrne then gave a galvanizing speech, standing over the butchered guard with his bloodied pitchfork held aloft in the air, urging the people to fight back.

steps.player: Do you know what he said?

steps.npc: Sadly no. While we have many witness accounts, they all differ, so we can not verify it at all.
Whatever Byrne said, the people responded. Together, the citizens of Kourend revolted, grabbing whatever they could use as a weapon. They fought the lizardmen.
The lizardmen, while strong and powerful, were simply outnumbered. In a matter of days, they had been driven back into the Kebos Lowlands.
During the battle, the temple surrounding the Dark Altar was destroyed, weakening Xeric's power. We believe he fled to Quidamortem.
Some say Xeric was actually killed during the revolt, but we have no record of his remains being discovered.

steps.player: So no one knows what really happened to him?

steps.text: If the player has not completed Tale of the Righteous:

steps.npc: Xeric was incredibly powerful but we can reasonably assume that he soon perished. Without the power of the Dark Altar, Xeric would have become mortal.

steps.npc: Indeed. Is there anything else I can help you with?

steps.player: Can you give me any farming advice?

steps.npc: You can put up to five tomatoes, strawberries, apples, bananas or oranges into a fruit basket, although you can't have a mix in the same basket.

There are seven main Farming areas - Elstan's area near Falador, Dantaera's area near Catherby, Kragen's area near Ardougne, Lyra's area in Morytania, Marisi's area in Hosidius, Alan's area in the Farming Guild and
Oswallt's area in Prifddinas.
Supercompost is far better than normal compost, but more expensive to make. You need to rot the right type of item; show me an item, and I'll tell you if it's super- compostable or not.
Vegetables, hops and flowers need constant watering - if you ignore my advice, you will sooner or later find yourself in possession of a dead farming patch.
There is a special patch for growing Belladonna - I believe that it is somewhere near Draynor Manor, where the ground is a tad 'unblessed'.

Hops are good for brewing ales. I believe there's a brewery up in Keldagrim somewhere, and I've heard rumours that a place called Phasmatys used to be good for that type of thing. 'Fore they all died, of course.
Bittercap mushrooms can only be grown in a special patch in Morytania, near the Mort Myre swamp. There the ground is especially dank and suited to growing poisonous fungii.
You can buy all the farming tools from farming shops, which can be found close to the allotments.
Tree seeds must be grown in a plantpot of soil into a sapling, and then transferred to a tree patch to continue growing to adulthood.
The only way to cure a bush or tree of disease is to prune away the diseased leaves with a pair of secateurs. For all other crops I would just apply some plant-cure.
You can fill plantpots with soil from any empty patch, if you have a gardening trowel.
If you need to be rid of your fruit trees for any reason, all you have to do is chop them down and then dig up the stump.
Don't just throw away your weeds after you've raked a patch - put them in a compost bin and make some compost.
Applying compost to a patch will not only reduce the chance that your crops will get diseased, but you will also grow more crops to harvest.
If you want to make your own sacks and baskets you'll need to use the loom that's near the Farming shop in Falador. If you're a good enough craftsman, that is.
You don't have to buy all your plantpots you know, you can make them yourself on a pottery wheel. If you're a good enough craftsman, that is.
You can put up to ten potatoes, cabbages or onions in vegetable sacks, although you can't have a mix in the same sack.

steps.npc: That's a very interesting question. My best guess is that they are relatives to imps, which is why there are imps here as well.
Implings do appear to like collecting objects and, as my clients have noted, have no concept of ownership. However, I do not sense any malicious intent.
It is my observation that they collect things that other creatures want, rather than they want them themselves. It seems to provide them with sustenance.

steps.player: So they feed off our desire for things?

steps.npc: Possibly. Either way, it seems that they almost exclusively collect things that people want, except their younglings who I infer haven't learnt the best things to collect yet.

steps.player: So the more experienced implings have the more desirable items?

steps.npc: That is my observation. Yes.

options.text: Can I catch these implings then?

steps.player: Can I catch these implings, then?

steps.npc: Indeed you may. In fact I encourage it. You will, however, require some equipment.
Firstly you will need a butterfly net in which to catch them and at least one special impling jar to store an impling.

You will also require some experience as a Hunter since these creatures are elusive. The more immature implings require less experience, but some of the rarer implings are extraordinarily hard to find and catch.

Once you have caught one, you may break the jar open and obtain the object the impling is carrying. Alternatively, you may exchange certain combinations of jars with me. I will return the jars to my clients. In
exchange I will be able to provide you with some equipment that may help you hunt butterflies more effectively.
Also, beware. Those imps walking around the maze do not like the fact that their kindred spirits are being captured and will attempt to steal any full jars you have on you, setting the implings free.

Once you have caught one, you may break the jar open and obtain the object the impling is carrying. Alternatively, you may exchange certain combinations of jars with me. I will return the jars to my clients. In

options.text: Tell me more about these jars.

steps.npc: You cannot use an ordinary butterfly jar as a container as the implings will escape from them with ease. However, I have done some investigation and have come up with a solution - if a butterfly jar is coated
with a thin layer of a substance noxious to them they become incapable of escape.
I have tried a few experiments with the help of a friend back home, and it turns out that a combination of anchovy oil and flowers - marigolds, rosemary or nasturtiums - will work.

steps.player: How do you make anchovy oil then?

steps.npc: I'd grind up some cooked anchovies and pass them through a sieve.

steps.player: Where do I make these jars?

steps.npc: Well, I believe there is a chemist in Rimmington that has a small still that you could use.

steps.player: Is there anywhere I can buy these jars?

steps.npc: Well I may be able to let you have a few - if it means you will start hunting these implings - although I do not have an infinite supply.

options.text: Tell me more about these thieving imps.

steps.player: Tell me more about these thieving imps.

steps.npc: Imps and implings appear to be related, and the imps here are quite protective of their smaller relations. If you allow them to get too close then they will attempt to steal jarred implings from your pack, if you have them.
They will then set them free, dropping your jar on the floor. So, if you're quick, you may be able to catch it again.
I have some impling deterrent which I may trade if you prove that you can catch implings well.

options.text: So what's this equipment you can give me then?

steps.player: So what's this equipment you can give me, then?

steps.npc: I have been given permission by my clients to give three pieces of equipment to able hunters.

Firstly, I have some imp deterrent. If you bring me three baby implings, two young implings and one gourmet impling already jarred, I will give you a vial. Imps don't like the smell, so they will be less likely to
steal jarred implings from you.

Secondly, I have magical butterfly nets. If you bring me three gourmet implings, two earth implings and one essence impling I will give you a new net. It will help you catch both implings and butterflies.

Lastly, I have magical jar generators. If you bring me three essence implings, two eclectic implings and one nature impling I will give you a jar generator. This object will create either butterfly or impling jars (up to
a limited number of charges) without having to carry a pack full of them.

steps.npc: Ahh, there's nothing like a nice cuppa tea. I know what, I'll tell you a story to thank you for the lovely tea...

A long time ago, when I was a little girl, there was a handsome young man living in Varrock. I saw him here in the church quite often. Everyone said he was going to become a priest, and we girls were so sad about that.

But young Dissy - that was the young man's nickname - he was a wild young thing. One night he gathered some lads together, and after the evening prayer- meeting they all put on masks and sneaked down to the
evil temple in the south of the city, the evil one. The next day, there was quite a hubbub. The guards told us that someone had painted 'Saradomin pwns' on the wall of the Zamorakian temple!

Now, we'd always been taught to keep well away from that dreadful place, but it really did us all good to see someone wasn't afraid of the scum who live at that end of town. Old Father Packett was furious, but Dissy just
laughed it off.
Dissy left town after that, saying he wanted to see the world. It was such a shame, he had the most handsome shoulders...

A young man came here looking for stories about Dissy - of course, that's not his proper name, but his friends called him Dissy - and I told him that one. He said Dissy had become a really famous man and there was

going to be a book about him. Well, that's all good, but I do wish Dissy had just come back to Varrock. I did miss him so much... well, until I met my Freddie and we got married, but that's another story.

steps.npc: In this chamber you will see various piles of shapes. You can pick up these shapes and enchant them using the enchant jewelry spells. By enchanting these shapes, you'll be converting them into orbs which you can be placed in the hole in the centre. You will get Enchantment Pizazz Points for every ten shapes that you convert and the points you get depends on the level of enchantment spell you cast. You will get a bonus Pizazz Point for enchanting a certain shape at a certain time, which I will periodically shout out. You will also be rewarded with an item for every so many orbs you deposit into the hole.

As well as the magic experience from casting your enchantment spells, you will get Enchantment Pizazz Points for converting so many shapes, plus a bonus point for converting a shape of the correct type. You should also note that you will occasionally be rewarded with items when you put one of the enchanted orbs in the floor.

standard.npc: Well met, fellow adventurer! How can I help you?

steps.npc: How frightfully rude of me, my dear [chap/lady]. My name is Eniola and I work for that most excellent enterprise, the Bank of Gielinor.

options.text: If you work for the bank, what are you doing here?

steps.player: If you work for the bank, what are you doing here?

steps.npc: My presence here is the start of a new enterprise of travelling banks.
I, and others like me, will provide you with the convenience of having banking facilities where they will be of optimum use to you.

The Z.M.I., that is, the Zamorakian Magical Institute, requested my services upon discovery of this altar. We at the Bank of Gielinor are a neutral party and are willing to offer our services regardless of affiliation.
So that is why I am here.

steps.player: Can I access my bank account by speaking to you?

steps.npc: Of course, dear [sir/lady].
However, I must inform you that because the Z.M.I. are paying for my services, they require anyone not part of the Institute to pay an access fee to open their bank account.

But, as our goal as travelling bankers is to make our customers' lives more convenient, we have accomodated to your needs. We know you will be busy creating runes and do not wish to carry money with you. The
charge to open your account is the small amount of twenty of one type of rune. The type of rune is up to you.
Would you like to pay the price of twenty runes to open your bank account?

steps.npc: It's not that I don't trust you, old [chap/girl], but as the old adage goes: 'Payment comes before friends.'

steps.npc: I'm sorry to hear that, [sir/madam]. If you should reconsider, because I believe this service offers excellent value for money, do not hesitate to contact me.

standard.npc: Greetings. What wisdom do you seek?

options.text: I'm new to this place. Where am I?

steps.player: I'm new to this place. Where am I?

steps.npc: Well young one, you have entered the Magic Training Arena. It was built at the start of the Fifth Age, when runestones were first discovered. It was made because of the many pointless accidents caused by inexperienced
mages.

Good question. It was originally made by the ancestors of the wizards in the Wizards Tower. However, it was destroyed by melee and ranged warriors who took offence at the use of this new 'Magic Art'. Recently,
the current denizens of the Wizards Tower have resurrected the arena including various Guardians you will see as you look around. We are here to help and to ensure things run smoothly.

steps.player: Interesting. So what can I do here?

steps.npc: You may train up your skill in the magic arts by travelling through one of the portals at the back of this entrance hall. By training up in one of these areas you will be awarded special Pizazz Points unique to
each room. With these points you may claim a variety of items from my fellow guardian up the stairs.

steps.player: How do you record the points I have earned?

steps.npc: You really are full of questions! You will need a special Pizazz Progress Hat! I can give you one if you so wish to train here.

steps.text: If the player does not have inventory space:

steps.npc: Ah, I'm afraid I can't give it to you as you don't have room to carry it!

steps.text: If the player has inventory space:
Progress hat

steps.npc: Here you go. Talk to the hat to find out your current Pizazz Point totals.
Well of course, it's a magic Pizazz Progress Hat! Mind your manners though, hats have feelings too!

Oh, and a word of warning: should you decide to leave the rooms by any method other than the exit portals, you will be teleported to the entrance and have any items that you picked up in the room removed.

steps.player: Can you explain the different portals?

steps.npc: They lead to four areas to train your magic: The Telekinetic Theatre, The Alchemists' Playground, The Enchanting Chamber, and The Creature Graveyard.
In there you can earn Telekinetic Pizazz Points for trade upstairs.

steps.player: What will I be doing in there?

steps.npc: That depends on how much of a time-waster you are! You are required to use the Telekinetic Grab spell in order to move a statue through a maze. Casting the spell will move the statue towards you until it reaches
a wall. So by standing on the different sides of the maze you can move the statue North, East, South or West. You will be rewarded Pizazz Points for each maze successfully solved.

It will be clearer when you arrive and there's a Guardian through the portal that will be able to tell you more. There's a book you can buy from the Rewards Guardian upstairs that will explain it all.
In the playground you can earn Alchemist Pizazz Points for trading with the rewards guardian upstairs.

You'll find eight cupboards containing items you can turn to gold using the low and high alchemy spells. The money you earn will be taken from you upon leaving the playground to pay for the upkeep of this training

arena and to help fund magic shops around Gielinor. You will be rewarded with 1 Pizazz Point for every 100 coins deposited and a percentage of the money you create. Keep in mind that you will not be able to take
more than 1000 coins back out with you.
I am afraid not, for the cost of the items varies, as does their locations in the cupboards. You'll see a list of item costs that will help you decide what you should be converting to gold.

Fear not, it will be clearer when you arrive and there's a Guardian through the portal that will be able to tell you more. You can also buy a book from the Rewards Guardian upstairs that will explain it all.
In here you will be able to earn Enchantment Pizazz Points for trade upstairs.

steps.player: What will I have to do?

steps.npc: You will find yourself amongst various piles of shapes. You can pick up these shapes and use one of your enchanting spells upon it to morph it into an orb. You'll also see a hole in the centre of the room; put the orbs
in here and for every 20 we will credit you with a gift. You will get Pizazz Points for every 10 shapes that you convert and the amount of points depends on the spell you use.

steps.player: What's the difference between the shapes?

steps.npc: Ah, you will be notified of a different shape that will give you a bonus Pizazz Point when you convert that shape. You should also look out for dragon stones, as these will give you more Pizazz Points when you
convert them.
It will be clearer when you arrive and there's a Guardian through the portal that will be able to tell you more. You can also buy a book from the Rewards Guardian upstairs that will explain it all.
In here you will be able to earn Graveyard Pizazz Points for trade upstairs.

steps.player: But what do I have to do in there?

steps.npc: Patience young one. A great many creatures die in this world and much of their remains can cause clutter. We have taken it upon ourselves to teleport many bones from these creatures into this graveyard for a

use. It's up to you to practice your bones to bananas spell in order to put these bones into immediate use - nutritious food for monsters! Just convert the bones and put them in the holes in the walls. There is a

drawback to this room however, the bones often fall on people so you may want to eat some of those bananas to stay alive. When people die we confiscate Pizazz Points for the effort of teleporting incompetent mages.

steps.player: What else do I get from this besides bruises?

steps.npc: As well as the Pizazz Points for giving us the bananas, you will be credited with runestones for your efforts, and you may be able to save up for a new kind of spell to use in the graveyard!

It will be clearer when you arrive and one of my fellow guardians through the portal will be able to tell you more. You can also buy a book from the Rewards Guardian upstairs that will explain it all.
Use what you have learned.
You won't gain with that attitude.

steps.npc: I travelled down here with my friend Olbertus in search for treasure. When we didn't find anything except his strange structure, he decided to prise off a coin from the stone relief in the other room. Before I knew it the entrance had closed and I was stuck down here.
I tried calling out to Olbertus but he must not have heard me. I don't know what would've happened if you hadn't shown up and saved me.

steps.player: Well, it turns out Olbertus was corrupted by the coin he stole, I managed to get the coin from him and returned it to the relief, he should be fine now.

steps.npc: Well, you must be a new arrival. I am Erdan, a descendant of Uhld.

steps.player: Uhld? I've seen that inscribed on that big old statue down below. What's that about?

steps.npc: It's also on the fountain in the dungeon below, it displays their emblem.
The Sect of Uhld, the founders of this here guild. I may not have gained entrance to this guild in the usual fashion, but I'd expect that they'd at least inform new members of this guild's history.

steps.player: Perhaps they expected you, a descendant of Uhld, to fill me in on the matter.

steps.npc: Aye, that may well be the case.
Look, I'm awfully busy, what with the recent influx of members, so I'll give you the short version for now.
The story my father told me was of a war on magic. Of god fearing men who believed nothing good would come of wielding a power that was never meant for them.
And so the rune temples that man had created were under threat. Before long, all were destroyed and thus forgotten.
But the wrath that these Gunnites embraced rippled through the pocket dimensions. Supposedly, a new altar of power was discovered.
Indeed. The temple was destroyed just as construction had finished, and a nearby nomadic group called the Sect of Uhld were not pleased with the brutality they witnessed.
They quickly established this guild with information preservation as their core goal, for men are recorders of history and magic is key for this to last.
Of course they did, but the Sect of Uhld had used the information gained from the wrath altar, and with a spell of their own making, they destroyed the southern runecrafting crusade with much ease.
Indeed it is, but I best get back to work, so unless you wish to trade, that is all.

standard.npc: Are you here to fight the cold?
Great! Ask me anything you like about the Bruma tree, I'm an expert.

steps.npc: Some would say that ice preserves while fire destroys, but no amount of fire is destroying the Wintertodt. That's a cold that will freeze the air in your lungs.
Even the heat generated from burning the Bruma roots only weakens it, and that doesn't last very long nowadays.

steps.player: Looks like an angry snow storm to me...

steps.npc: What you see in that pit is not the Wintertodt at full strength. It never will be while the Bruma tree still burns and the Doors of Dinh remain closed.

steps.text: other

options.text: Tell me about the Bruma tree.

steps.player: Tell me about the Bruma tree.

steps.npc: The Bruma tree is what keeps the Wintertodt weak. The prison was built here by Dinh because of its usefulness against the Wintertodt.
Some legends say that Xeric is the cause for the Doors weakening, or maybe he made the Wintertodt stronger?

steps.player: Is Xeric really such a bad guy?

steps.npc: It's a known fact that he was interested in the Bruma tree. For what purpose... there are only rumours.
Regardless, the Bruma tree definitely contains powerful magic. I've been studying the sap for years and it has truly astounding properties.
There's not many fires that burn green now, are there?

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Me? I'm a member of the Woodcutting Guild. More of a researcher though... I'm currently tasked with growing a new Bruma tree.
Poorly. I believe the Bruma tree can only be grown in a freezing cold climate.
It's just an idea really. For all I know, it could be magic way beyond me, beyond even the Pyromancers.

options.text: Although you're here, you're also still in the time freeze.

steps.npc: If your hope is that I can tell you about a whole race, then I am likely to disappoint you, iknil. The masters were secretive individuals. They rarely divulged information that I did not require.

steps.player: That's still something. What were they like?

steps.npc: They were kind, but filled with sadness. As you know, they summoned me after another of their kind unleashed the Moons of Peril.
It was a dark time. Their people had suffered great calamity years earlier and their extinction was inevitable.
It seems that many, such as the shaman who summoned the Moons, felt that the only salvation left was destruction.
My masters, however, felt differently. They fought for a world that was no longer their own. They believed in preserving these lands for those who would inhabit them afterwards.
Yes. Humans and dwarves were recent arrivals here, but the masters saw you as inheritors. I believe in some ways, you offered them hope in a time filled with pain.

steps.player: I see. Than you for sharing that with me.

steps.npc: It is not a problem, iknil.

standard.npc: Nilsal. I'm afraid I must ask not to be disturbed. There are many things that one in my position must contemplate. If you seek conversation, I'm sure my companion would be willing.

steps.npc: Oh very, very fascinating, for instance my great grandfather Howard...

steps.player: Yawn. Oh, I'm sorry but I really must be getting on. I think my giraffe needs feeding.

options.text: You are a bit too strange for me. Bye.

steps.player: You are a bit too strange for me. Bye.

steps.npc: Sniff. Yes, everyone says that.

standard.npc: Hello there, traveller.

standard.player: What's going on here? Where is everyone?

standard.npc: Most are in the city. As for the rest, hopefully somewhere nicer than this place.
Yes. When we heard they were going to lock Menaphos down and shut the gates, most people here decided they'd be better off behind the walls than outside them.
We didn't get much warning. People had to rush to gather whatever they could. Some things had to be left behind, along with some people...
It could have been worse. Had we been in Sophanem, we'd have had no warning at all. I just hope it won't be long before things are back to normal.
Thank you, traveller. Stay safe out there. These are troubling times.

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.npc: I can't belive Xilo hasn't shown up.

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.player: Were you expecting to meet someone here?

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.npc: My... friend, Xilo. I told her to meet me by the magic trees of the rainforest. We don't often have a chance to meet without a crowd of people around.

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.player: Why? Is she not particularly local to you?

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.npc: Unfortunately not. I'm from Aldarin, but she lives in Tal Teklan. It usually takes a special event being hosted for us both to be in the same place.

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.player: So you never really get any privacy?
Not at all. Sorry if it seemed like I was.

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.npc: It's okay... Sorry... I just miss her.

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.text: If the player has not already talked to Xilo:

steps.player: Do you think she's just running a little late?

steps.npc: It's possible.

steps.player: Could she maybe have considered another tree magical?

steps.npc: I suppose she may be where we first met... but this is where we shared our first... you know...

steps.player: Well, I'll keep my fingers crossed for you. I'm sure you'll be able to find one another soon!

steps.npc: Thank you, iknami.

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.text: If the player has already talked to Xilo:

steps.player: Hang on... I think I might have met this Xilo.

steps.npc: You have? Where is she?

steps.player: By a tree to the north of here.

steps.npc: Oh, Xilo! She's gone to where we first met instead! Thank you, iknami. I'll head over there at once!

steps.text: Fabia departs.

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.speaker: Xilo
standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.text: Hello again, iknami! Thank you for helping us find each other!

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.npc: To think we were waiting by different trees! It was so silly of us!

standard-dialogue-if-xilo-and-fabia-have.player: Well, I'm happy to see you together again. Now, I'm sure you have a lot of catching up to do. I'll leave you to it.

standard.npc: Don't bother me, can't you see I'm busy?

standard.player: No, I can't... can I go into the factory?

standard.npc: You can go in. The Consortium, in their infinite wisdom, has decided to open up the factory to all and sundry.
We've built a new blast furnace and always have a shortage of people to work on it.
Just don't go causing any trouble, I still run this factory!

unsectioned.player: I'm sorry, I'm looking for the blast furnace?

unsectioned.npc: Do I look like a guide to you?

unsectioned.player: No, you look like a hard-working dwarf, but can you please tell me where the blast furnace is?

unsectioned.npc: Alright, just head down the stairs, it's easy to find.

unsectioned.player: If you were any shorter you wouldn't exist.
What are you dwarves doing in this factory?

unsectioned.npc: Working of course, can't you see that?
Refining the ore that is being brought into the factory, of course.
It means you should stop asking so many questions and get back to work!
The Consortium does and that's all you need to know.

unsectioned.player: But what company? I thought there were all these different companies?

unsectioned.npc: Oh yes, all the major companies own this plant. It's too vital to be in the hands of one company alone.

unsectioned.player: And what exactly are you doing here?

unsectioned.npc: I tire of these questions. Let me get back to work!

standard.npc: What?

steps.npc: You can store your stuff here if you want. You can dump anything you don't want to carry whilst you're fighting duels and then pick it up again on the way out.
To be honest I'm wasted here.
I should be winning duels in an arena! I'm the best warrior in Al Kharid!
Isn't it obvious?
This is the Emir's Arena...duh!

options.text: I'd like to access my bank, please.

steps.player: I'd like to access my bank, please.

steps.npc: Sure.
Yeah, okay.
When I can. I used to throw rotten fruit at them, though I can't do that anymore. Wanna buy some? I've plenty to spare.

options.text: Sure, I'll buy some rotten fruit.

steps.player: Sure, I'll buy some rotten fruit.

options.text: No, I'm not giving you money for rotten fruit.

steps.player: No, I'm not giving you money for rotten fruit.

steps.npc: Suit yourself.
Have you got any idea where Burthorpe is? The co- ordinator says I need to go there and paint all the leaves yellow, but I've never heard of that place!
Be careful when you pick mushrooms near the strange ruins to the south. Some of them will try to eat you!
Err, hello. Do you have any idea what a Winter Fairy actually does?
Oh, pity. Neither do I, but I'm supposed to be one this week.
Sorry, I can't talk I'm looking for Sarah-Jane!
Is your name Freddie, and are you loosing your teeth?
Oh, right.
You don't have any idea where I can find him do you?

steps.player: No, I don't know that either.

steps.npc: Oh, ok then. If you do find out please let me know. The co-ordinator has sent me to find him.
I'm afraid I can't stop to chat. I've just been told to get ready to go to Etceteria for some reason or other!
Picking mushrooms near the forge will probably end quite badly for you.
I don't want to go back! That orc tried to kill me!
We must find a way to fight back! To throw those villains out of our homes.
I can't believe that there are orcs in Zanaris.
Have you heard? The Godfather has allowed orcs into Zanaris!
Those fairies that side with the Godfather are all traitors! The Queen is the true ruler of Zanaris!
Have you seen Fairy Cake? She went to talk to the Godfather and I haven't seen her since.
How is the Queen? Has she woken up yet?
The Queen is the true ruler of Zanaris! We shall over- throw the tyrant!
Is the council finished yet?
Once the council of war is finished we shall go and get rid of the Godfather.
I'm so looking forward to going back home!
Thank you for waking our queen.
Now that the Queen is awake everything will be alright.

initial-dialogue.player: Hello, my name is [player name]. Who are you?

initial-dialogue.npc: Oh hello [player name]. I'm Aeryka. Aery for short.

initial-dialogue.player: Airy Fairy?

initial-dialogue.npc: That's right. What can I do for you?

initial-dialogue.player: What's that crop circle thing doing here?

initial-dialogue.npc: Crop circle? Oh, you mean the Puromantic portal?

initial-dialogue.player: The pyromanic what?

initial-dialogue.npc: The Puromantic portal. At least that's what we call them. It's the way the implings travel from Puro-Puro to other planes.

initial-dialogue.player: Puro-Puro?

initial-dialogue.npc: The impling home. We call it Puro-Puro. The implings just call it home, I think.

options.text: So what are these implings then?
I've heard I may find dragon equipment in Puro-Puro.

standard.npc: It's still here.
It's still here. The crop circle is still here.

standard.player: Oh yes, thanks Aery. It didn't go anywhere in the meantime, then?

standard.npc: Nope. It just sat there.

standard.player: Jolly good. I can come back and visit Puro-Puro whenever I want then. Brilliant!

steps.npc: Implings...and wheat.
Not really. Though I have noticed quite a lot of you humans travelling through the portal recently. I suppose you must like wheat.

steps.player: Well, most of us prefer lobsters to be perfectly honest, but there must be something interesting there.

steps.npc: Oh, I did notice a very serious-looking gnome go into the portal. Maybe he knows what's going on.

steps.player: Do you remember what his name was?

steps.npc: Errm, Egg-nog, or something like that.

steps.player: Right, thanks! I'll have a chat with him when I go. Maybe he'll know what's going on.

options.text: So what are these implings then?

steps.player: So what are these implings then?

steps.npc: Well, no-one knows for sure. The mischievous little creatures are probably related to imps. And they fly as well.
Also, like imps, they love collecting things. I'm not sure why, though. They also seem to like being chased.

steps.player: So how would I get hold of what they are carrying, then?

steps.npc: Catch them, I suppose. I don't know really. Why would you want to?

steps.player: Well, if they were carrying something useful. Maybe I could catch them with a big net - like butterflies.

steps.npc: Sounds a bit cruel to me, but I suppose that's possible.

options.text: I've heard I may find dragon equipment in Puro-Puro.

steps.player: I've heard I may find dragon equipment in Puro-Puro.

steps.npc: Really? You humans like that stuff a lot, don't you? I don't like really old stuff myself.
Yes, dragon stuff feels really old.
From its magical aura, obviously. Oh, I forget you humans can't feel auras.
Really, really, old.

steps.player: Can you be any more precise?

steps.npc: Not really. Time doesn't really mean a lot round here. Hundreds, maybe thousands of your human lifespans, I suppose. Anyway, it would have to be old since it all comes from the Necrosyrtes.
Old and powerful creatures. I don't think there have been any around here for aeons. I haven't seen one. I don't think they are very nice. Not like me. Anyway, this is all ancient history. Boooring!

steps.player: While I'm on the subject do you have any dragon stuff I can have?

steps.npc: Oh, I did have loads, but I threw it away.
Only joking.

No, sorry, I can't help you there. You'll have to look for it yourself. Although, maybe if you find Necrosyrtes then they'll give you some. I heard they give dragon stuff away to people they like. Not fairies. We're too
nice.
See you around!

standard.npc: What is it, human? Busy busy busy!

options.text: Why are you carrying that toolbox?

steps.player: Why are you carrying that toolbox?

steps.npc: It's the fizgog! It's picking up cable again!

steps.player: Uh, right. So is it safe to use the fairy rings then?

steps.npc: Sure, as long as you have been given permission to use them. You should just be aware that using the fairy rings sometimes has strange results, the locations that you have been to may affect the locations you are
trying to reach. I could fix it by replacing the fizgog and the whosprangit, I've put in a request for some new parts but they're pretty hard to get hold of, it seems.

standard-dialogue-after-fairytale-ii-cur.npc: Pssst! Human! I've got something for you.

options.text: What have you got for me?

steps.player: What have you got for me?

steps.npc: They said you'd helped cure our Queen. I haven't got a lot of rewards to offer, but my enchantment scrolls might help if you're working with fairy rings in your home.

options.text: Why are you carrying that toolbox?

standard-dialogue-after-fairytale-ii.player: Err, Godfather, I can't help noticing that there seems to be Orcs wandering around Zanaris.

standard-dialogue-after-fairytale-ii.npc: Yous just-a better keep-a your nose outa my business. I's da Godfather and I's da one who's inna charge here.

using-nuff-s-certificate-on-him.text: You show the certificate to the Godfather.

using-nuff-s-certificate-on-him.player: Do you know what these strange marks mean?

using-nuff-s-certificate-on-him.npc: For why you show-a me dat? Eez very nice to see yous learning to draw! Bravo!

treasure-trails-hard.npc: Ah, iz-a you. I make-a you an offer, eh? Iz-a good offer. You can't-a refuse it.
You tell-a me ze answer to dis, si?

treasure-trails-hard.text: The Fairy Godfather has given you a challenge scroll!
a challenge scroll

treasure-trails-hard-when-spoken-to-agai.npc: You tell-a me your answer, si?

steps.npc: Iz-a no good.
Grazie infinite!

initial-dialogue-before-fairytale-part-1.player: What do you do around here?

initial-dialogue-before-fairytale-part-1.npc: Oh, I'm the resident healer. My name is Nuff, Fairy Nuff. Who are you?

Pleased to meet you, [player name]. As I was saying, I'm the healer in Zanaris. I graduated over 200 human years ago. Look, there's my Advanced Healing Certificate on the wall. I never go anywhere without it.
It's my job to look after the sick, wounded or dying fairies around here. Of course, fairies being magical by nature, not many of them get hurt, so I don't normally have much to do.

initial-dialogue-before-fairytale-part-1.player: What about healing humans? Lots of adventurers must get hurt fighting the Otherworldly beings.

initial-dialogue-before-fairytale-part-1.npc: Yes they do. Silly isn't it? I do use my healing magic on humans sometimes, but I don't like them attacking our other guests, so I charge them for the service.

initial-dialogue-before-fairytale-part-1.player: How much do you charge to heal someone, then?

initial-dialogue-before-fairytale-part-1.npc: Well, the gold that you humans are so fond of has no real value in Zanaris, so I ask my patients to pay me in gems.
I will heal 4 hitpoints for an opal, 5 hitpoints for either a sapphire or a piece of jade, 7 hitpoints for an emerald or red topaz, 9 for a ruby and 11 for a diamond.

initial-dialogue-before-fairytale-part-1.player: Only 11 hitpoints for a diamond? Doesn't that seem a bit steep?

initial-dialogue-before-fairytale-part-1.npc: Maybe to you, but you'd be surprised how many adventurer's are willing to pay those prices.
Hello [player name], do you need any assistance?
Sure, how many hitpoints would you like me to heal?

steps.npc: That will cost you 1 opal.
You don't have a opal to pay me!
Ok, suit yourself.
That will cost you 1 sapphire or 1 piece of jade.
You don't have a sapphire or a piece of jade with you!
That will cost you 1 emerald or 1 red topaz.
You don't have an emerald or a red topaz to pay me with!
That will cost you 1 diamond.
You don't have a diamond to pay me!
That will cost you 1 ruby.
You don't have a ruby to pay me!
Ok. If you want to know anything, just ask.

after-fairytale-part-1.player: How is the Fairy Queen doing?

after-fairytale-part-1.npc: Not too well; the Godfather hasn't given me those secateurs yet.

after-fairytale-part-2.player: Why aren't you in the war room with the Fairy Queen and her advisors?

after-fairytale-part-2.npc: I don't like war! I don't believe that violence is ever justified, that's why I became a healer.

options.text: How do crops and such survive down here?

steps.player: How do crops and such survive down here? Surely they need a bit of sunlight?

steps.npc: Clearly you come from a plane dependent on sunlight. Down here, the plants grow in the aura of faerie.

options.text: What's so good about this place?

steps.player: What's so good about this place?

steps.npc: Zanaris is a meeting point of cultures. Those from many worlds converge here to exchange knowledge and goods.

standard-dialogue-after-finishing-fairyt.player: Have you managed to work out a plan yet?

standard-dialogue-after-finishing-fairyt.npc: Not yet, [player name], but it looks like we'll need to ask you for your help again, I'm afraid. I'll be able to tell you more once we have finished making our battle plans.

treasure-trails-hard.npc: Please solve this for me. I have other things to be thinking about.

treasure-trails-hard.text: The Fairy Queen has given you a puzzle box!
a puzzle box

treasure-trails-hard-while-holding-the-p.text: If the puzzle box is not solved:

steps.npc: Sorry but you haven't solved the puzzle yet.

treasure-trails-hard-while-holding-the-p.text: If the puzzle box is solved:

steps.npc: Thanks [player name]!

standard.player: How goes the council of war?

standard.npc: Slowly, I'm afraid. We're still trying to come up with a reasonable plan.
'Ello, sugar. I'm afraid I can't gossip right now, I've got a cake in the oven.

attempting-to-take-the-nearby-chocolate-.npc: Oi you! Did you think I didn't see that? That's my chocolate bar, that is!

attempting-to-take-the-nearby-chocolate-.player: Oh, sorry. I didn't realise it belonged to anybody.

attempting-to-take-the-nearby-chocolate-.npc: That's alright, honey. You look a bit thin anyway. Take it if you need it.

using-nuff-s-certificate-on-her.text: You show the certificate to the Fairy chef.

using-nuff-s-certificate-on-her.player: Do you know what these strange marks mean?

using-nuff-s-certificate-on-her.npc: Sorry dearie, no, but I have seen a sign with similar marks near the mysterious ruins. You know, the ones that lead you to the Cosmic Rune Altar.

standard.npc: Can I help you at all?

options.text: Yes please. What are you selling?

standard.npc: Can I help you at all?

options.text: Yes please. What are you selling?

steps.text: If the player has started Fremennik Trials

steps.npc: Hi there [player name]. I am Falo the bard! Like my brother Olaf, who lives in Rellekka, I also write music.

steps.text: If the player has completed Fremennik Trials

steps.npc: Hi there [Fremennik name]. I am Falo the bard! Like my brother Olaf, who lives in Rellekka, I also write music.

standard.player: Do you write about anything in particular?

standard.npc: Oh most certainly! I write about all the objects in the lands. From weapons and armour to palm trees and sands. That's why I wander far from Rellekka to seek inspiration.
I have one problem though. I am very forgetful, I can never remember which particular object a song was about.

standard.player: Surely the lyrics for such a song would be enough to help you remember?

standard.npc: I am afraid not. It saddens me deeply, so I often send out messages to adventurers to help me discreetly.

standard.player: I'll keep a look out for them! Goodbye Falo.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-not-.npc: Get away! I do not speak to outlanders.

treasure-trails-master.npc: Thank you for coming [Fremennik name], I need your help.
I have one of my old songs stuck in my head, but I cannot remember what the object it refers to is. I am so forgetful. I'll sing it to you.
Here goes... [one of his random songs]
You have very kind words. I would be extremely grateful if you could remind me which object the song was about.

treasure-trails-master-when-talked-to-ag.npc: I really hope you can help me. Please show me the object my song is about!

treasure-trails-master-when-talked-to-ag.player: Can you sing me the song again?

treasure-trails-master-when-the-correct-.text: You show your object to Falo.

treasure-trails-master-when-the-correct-.npc: Yes yes yes! That is it, thank you so much [Fremennik name]. The memories have come flooding back. I get why the lyrics are what they are now.

treasure-trails-master-when-the-correct-.text: You've been given a new clue!

treasure-trails-master-when-the-correct-.player: I'm glad to have helped, hopefully you'll never forget again!

treasure-trails-master-when-an-incorrect.text: You show your object to Falo.
Falo's eyes fail to light up.

treasure-trails-master-when-an-incorrect.npc: No no no! That's not it. Please have another think about it, [Fremennik name].

standard.npc: Arr!
Is there something I can help ye with?

options.text: I would like to join your crew.

steps.player: I would like to join your crew.

steps.npc: Of course you would!

steps.text: If the player has something equipped in the helmet slot:

steps.npc: However, I don't let anyone on the team if they are wearing a hat or a helmet.
You can go and store it in the deposit box next to Jimmy's stall.
Well, in order to tell my crew from San Fan's I will need to give you a hat like mine.
If you are wearing a hat it might get lost when I give you my crew's hat.
You wouldn't want that would you?

steps.player: No, that sounds very reasonable in fact.

steps.text: If the player has items in their inventory:

steps.npc: Well, I'll be glad to have you aboard, but you will need to go and store all of your gear first.
Well, you will need all of your inventory space for the ingredients, and all of the other things I'll need you to haul about.
There is a bank deposit box next to Jimmy's stall if you need it. Come and see me when you have a fully empty inventory.

steps.text: If Fancy Dan's team has more players than San Fan's team:

steps.npc: Sadly for you however, I have more than enough people on my crew.

steps.text: If the player has a cat following them:

steps.npc: Is that...thing yours?
Yes, I mean your cat! I HATE cats! Get it out of here!
Filthy things, no better than the rats that they catch.

steps.text: If the player has a different follower out:
If the player does not have anything equipped in the helmet slot and no items in their inventory:

steps.npc: Arr, well we'll get you sorted out with a team hat right away.
Go wait in the waiting room, I'll call you when we are ready to begin.

steps.text: The player is teleported into the Trouble Brewing waiting room.

options.text: Who are you, and what is this place?

steps.player: Who are you, and what is this place?

steps.npc: Arrharrharr!
Do you not recognise me? I am the famous dandy pirate 'Fancy' Dan!

steps.player: Yes, of course, any pirate knows who you are.

steps.npc: But of course.
As for what this place is, it is my glorious still, producing the best quality 'rum' this side of Braindeath Island.
Oh, and the run-down swill-producing ditch that San Fan over there calls a still.

steps.player: So with two stills you have plenty of 'rum' right?

steps.npc: Well we would do, if that hatchet-faced harridan wouldn't keep trying to torch the place!
A little while ago we had some real problems getting rum to the island, hence the two stills.
However, after a little misunderstanding involving San's still and a barrel of gunpowder our relationship seems to have become a little strained.
Apparently it is perfectly within the pirate code to burn each others stills, so long as nobody directly attacks the other person's crew, so rum production has taken a slight dip of late.
Yes, probably. I have a bunch of jobs that need doing, if you feel up to it.
What would you like to know about?

steps.player: How do I help you brew 'Rum'?

steps.npc: Well the stills we have set up are based on the ones on Braindeath island... well roughly at any rate.
All you have to do is help put the ingredients into the hoppers and keep the boilers burning.
If you add enough ingredients to the hoppers then you have the ability to pick up a single bottle of rum when it brews.

So, if ye add 5 buckets of water to the hoppers, then ye get access to one bottle. If you add 3 bowls of coloured water you get access to one bottle, and if you add one of anything else you get access to one bottle.
This is cumulative, meaning that if you add (for example) 10 buckets of water, 3 sweetgrubs and 6 bowls of coloured water, then you have a chance to collect 7 bottles of rum for the team.
The boilers are easy as pie to sort out. You just put some logs in, light them with a tinderbox, and then keep putting logs in until they are good and hot.
Three logs should do it, but it's best to keep heaping them in just in case.
The ingredients are; Bitternuts, Scrapey Tree Bark, Sweetgrubs, Buckets of Water and some Coloured Water.
There are plenty of Bitternut trees inside this walled off area. The problem is that the trees are too tricky for a human to climb.
You will need to catch a monkey and send it up the tree to get the nut for you.

steps.player: Send it up the tree? How does that work?

steps.npc: Well, if you were a monkey, and some random person grabbed you, dumped some dye in your fur and shoved you up a tree, you would hurl the closest heavy object at them too.
Yes, you'll need to get a bowl of coloured water and pour it on the monkey. Otherwise you won't be able to tell which team the monkey belongs too.
Anything else?

options.text: Can I ask about something else?

steps.player: Can I ask about something else?

steps.npc: Ok, what else?

steps.player: So...how would I go about sabotaging the enemy still?

options.text: Ok, I think I've heard enough
Where can I get Scrapey Tree Bark?
Where can I get buckets of water?
Where can I get coloured water?
Where can I get Scrapey Tree Bark?

steps.player: Where can I get Scrapey tree bark...and why do I get the feeling I won't like the answer?

steps.npc: Inside this walled area there are a few Scrapey trees. They are the big, ill looking ones, you can't miss them.
Basically, you cut them down and then carve the bark off with a knife.
It's pretty simple, except the sap tends so make people feel kind off ill if they get any on themselves.

steps.player: Can you give me any farming advice?

steps.npc: The only way to cure a bush or tree of disease is to prune away the diseased leaves with a pair of secateurs. For all other crops I would just apply some plant-cure.
Don't just throw away your weeds after you've raked a patch - put them in a compost bin and make some compost.

There are many Farming areas out there. I know of Elstan's area near Falador, Dantaera's area near Catherby, Kragen's area near Ardougne, Lyra's area in Morytania, Marisi's area in Hosidius and Alan's area in the Farming Guild. That said, I'm sure there's plenty more that I don't know about.
Supercompost is far better than normal compost, but more expensive to make. You need to rot the right type of item; show me and item, and I'll tell you if it's super-compostable or not.
There is a special patch for growing Belladonna - I believe that it is somewhere near Draynor Manor, where the ground is a tad 'unblessed'.
If you want to grow fruit trees you could try a few places: Catherby, Brimhaven, Gnome Stronghold and the Farming Guild all have fruit tree patches.
You don't have tp buy all your plantpots you know, you can make them yourself on a pottery wheel. If you're good enough at crafting, that is.
You can put up to five tomatoes, strawberries, apples, bananas or oranges into a fruit basket, although you can't have a mix in the same basket.

Hops are good for brewing ales. I believe there's a brewery up in Keldagrim somewhere, and I've heard rumours that a place called Phasmatys used to be good for that type of thing. 'Fore they all died, of course.
Applying compost to a patch will not only reduce the chance that your crops will get diseased, but you will also grow more crops to harvest.
You can put up to ten potatoes, cabbages or onions in vegetable sacks, although you can't have a mix in the same sack.
You can fill plantpots with soil from  any empty patch, if you have a gardening trowel.
Vegetables, hops and flowers need constant watering - if you ignore my advice, you will sooner or later find yourself in possession of a dead farming patch.
You can buy all the farming tools from farming shops, which can be found close to the allotments.
If you want to make your own sacks and baskets you'll need to use the loom that's near the Farming shop in Falador. If you're good enough at crafting, that is.
Bittercap mushrooms can only be grown in a special patch in Morytania, near the Mort Myre swamp. There the ground is especially dank and suited to growing poisonous fungii.
Tree seeds must be grown in a plantpot of soil into a sapling, and then transferred to a tree patch to continue growing to adulthood.

steps.npc: This is an Anima patch, the only one of its kind. Here, you can grow Iasor, Kronos and Attas plants.
Three unique plants with a special affinity to the Anima Mundi, the life force of our world.
When planted, all three of these plants have a unique impact on the Anima Mundi. Their effects will likely be very useful to you when farming.
Iasor plants will reduce the chance of your other crops becoming diseased, Kronos plants will increase the speed at which they grow and Attas plants will improve the yield when harvesting.
Choose wisely though, as you can only have one of them at a time.
Eventually, they'll start to wither and die as their impact on the Anima Mundi is limited. You'll have to plant another when they do.

standard-dialogue-monologue-1.npc: So there I was, minding my own business on the boat, when I feel us slow to a halt.
This man walks over to me and says that it's my stop, absurd though that is.
So they all sort of... toss me onto this island with a meagre amount of survival objects.
I think they were laughing whilst they did it.
Either way, there I was. Alone. On this island.
I'd paid quite handsomely for my passage too!
A tour to the rainforest, and then dinner in Tal Teklan.
This crew were all so very willing to get me where I wanted to go.
Very helpful as they collected my belongings. Eager, even.
It felt exclusive. I was the only passenger they took aboard.
I do see now that I was perhaps foolish.
Drawn in by their charms, throwing money around.
I just really wanted that dinner in Tal Teklan, you know?
Now I'm going to die alone on an island, bereft of my worldly possessions.
Perhaps the bards of Temptestus will write of my sorrow, should they hear my tale.

standard-dialogue-monologue-2.npc: Excuse me! Hello! I appear to have found myself in a situation here.
Can you see any way for me to... defamiliarise myself with this island?
I'm getting rather bored being stuck here waiting for the tide to swallow me.
Though, that is reliant on me not throwing myself into the dark sea first.
But fear not! I shan't do that, for it would be improper.
Though if it rains again, I may be tempted.
Observe how I have nothing here on this island.
There's myself and the occasional crab, but I've been left here... Abandoned! Forgotten!
I don't suppose you could send for a boat to retrieve me?
Yes, this predicament needs excessive force to be resolved peacefully.
Maybe I should pack a flag next time. Claim this land for myself.

standard-dialogue-monologue-3.npc: No! I can't be stuck here! It's far too small.
Are you finding the air just chokes you here? It is the air, isn't it?
Gosh, it feels as if my skin is just crawling.
Nobody's going to find me here... I'm going to rot on this island alone.
My regular baker will realise I've not come by in a day. He will send a search party!
They will send a search party, won't they?
This island is too small though... They won't be able to see it.
I'd start a fire, if only I had the tools to do so.
This isn't how I was meant to die!
I was meant to go down gloriously in the Colosseum!

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: No I need you to carry out just one task for me.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Well experience has taught me to expect as much, what must I do?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Nothing too difficult, just rid the port of every single rat, with just one action.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: What?
Are you serious?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Deadly.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.text: You see a manic glint in her eye which you had previously missed.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: But why? Why one stroke, why not a slow eradication?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: I want to write a new poem.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: But...
I am touched that you want to write an epic poem about me, but why can't you write the poem about seagulls or daffodils or something?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Well seagulls rarely make good central characters. They're a bit too ... uhm.... flighty.
Besides the poem is about me not you.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Sorry I don't follow.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: I myself carried out the very same feat once upon a time.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: So why do you need me to repeat your most heroic of feats?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: It's all about objectivity and integrity. I need to be utterly divorced from the process.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Umm... ok, I suppose.
So can you tell me how you went about achieving this?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: No. Therein lies the challenge.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Sigh* Why does it always have to be like this?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-b.npc: You haven't completed the task yet.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-b.player: What do I have to do again?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-b.npc: Rid the port of all its rats with one action.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-b.player: I'd better get to it then.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: I think I know how to carry out the task.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Has the face being telling tall tales again?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Oh no, she didn't say a word.
Really she didn't.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-o.player: Ha! I did it. Did you see me?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-o.npc: Yes I saw that, now what can I do for you? Don't keep me overly long, I'm trying to complete my poem.

options.text: Do you have any pointers for me and my cat?

steps.player: Do you have any pointers for me and my cat?

steps.npc: You should wear an amulet of catspeak. It will allow you to organise tactics with your cat.

steps.player: What would be the best tactic to adopt then?

steps.npc: Well, that depends on your outlook, whether you're ready to risk your cat's life or not and how defensive or aggressive you want your cat to be.

options.text: I will not risk my cat's life.

steps.player: I will not risk my cat's life.

steps.npc: Well if that's the case then your are left with two choices.
You can adopt an ultra defensive strategy, which increases your cat's hitpoints and defence, the drawback to this is that your cat will flee sooner.
Your other option is to adopt a less defensive strategy which will allow your cat to stay in the pit for longer.

options.text: I think I would adopt a very defensive strategy.

steps.player: I think I would adopt a very defensive strategy

steps.npc: In that case you should tell your cat, 'Just take care of yourself cat.'

options.text: I think I would adopt a less defensive strategy.

steps.npc: In that case you should tell your cat, 'Stay in for as long as you can.'

options.text: I am willing to risk my cat if it improves my chances.

steps.player: I am willing to risk my cat, if it increases my chances of victory.

steps.npc: In that case you are left with two choices.
You could go for all out attack which will boost your cat's attack and strength, but weaken it
or go for a less aggressive stance which will increase your cat's strength and attack to a lesser degree, but carries no defensive penalties.

options.text: I think I would adopt a very aggressive strategy.

steps.npc: It depends on what kind of cat you have.

options.text: Can you tell me more about wily cats?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about Wily cats?

steps.npc: Of course, of course, they're the highest form of cat that I know of.
They're tougher, stronger and faster than other variations of cat, they can catch butterflies and kalphite larva and are far superior to any other type of cat at hunting.

steps.player: So is there any drawbacks to owning them?

steps.npc: Wily cats need looking after or else they get fat and lazy.

steps.player: So how do I look after them then?

steps.npc: The key is to keep it active, bring it hunting or to the ratpits regularly.
Try keep it happy too, they can be a little nasty when they're cranky.

steps.player: What happens if I neglect my cat.. not that I would or anything?

steps.npc: They would get fat and lazy, be much worse at hunting and would show you up as a really poor cat trainer.

steps.player: Can I retrain my lazy cat?

steps.npc: Yes you can get your lazy cat back in shape with a lot of rat catching, but you really shouldn't let it get into that state in the first place.

steps.player: If it's a ruin, what's the point in being here?

steps.npc: I search for knowledge. I want to know what happened to this part of the world.
Whilst looking for answers, I slowly turned this broken town into a safe haven for travellers. Welcome to Ferox Enclave.

steps.player: Quite a dangerous place for a town, don't you think?

steps.npc: It is, but that's why it's needed! Look around, you can see how many others share my opinion.
You'll find yourself quite safe inside my enclave - the protective barriers should keep any troublemakers out.
I will warn you though, if you've had Teleblock cast upon you, I will not allow you back into the Enclave. You'd be a danger to the others gathered here.

steps.npc: Well, if you'd like, I can make it so you respawn in our Enclave. It'll put you right in the heart of all the chaos that surrounds us.

I won't be able to do anything if you die somewhere like Castle Wars or the Emir's Arena; they have their own magic to keep you safe.

I don't know, sorry. You'd better ask one of the dwarves about it.

standard.speaker: Finn
standard.text: Hello, human.

standard.speaker: Finn
standard.text: How are you finding the Conch so far?

standard.player: Very nice, thank you. It's a remarkable island you have here.

standard.speaker: Finn
standard.text: It is, isn't it? Still, I must admit, I'm keen to get out into the wider world. Coco and Torgan say it won't be long now until it's time for my Trial by Water.

standard.player: Well, in that case, I wish you good luck.

standard.speaker: Finn
standard.text: Thank you, human.

standard.npc: Can I help you at all?

options.text: Yes please. What are you selling?

steps.player: Yes please. What are you selling?

steps.npc: Take a look.

standard.npc: Relaxing after a long day at the factory.
If I keep up this winning streak, I mightn't have to go into work tomorrow.

standard.player: Do you mind me asking how much you have won?

standard.npc: Not at all, I'm up 10 coins so far.

standard.player: So how do these rat pits work?

standard.npc: The Keldagrim pits cater for those with the larger variety of cats.
If you have an overgrown cat and a couple of coins you can challenge someone else who also has an overgrown cat and some spare change.

standard.player: That sounds simple enough so far.

standard.npc: You then agree on a wager. It's rumoured that some ratcatchers can talk to their own cats and give them tactics to aid them.

standard.player: So then how do you win the challenge?

standard.npc: I was just getting to that. Both the challengers' cats are placed inside the arena, and whichever kills 9 rats first wins.

steps.npc: It's a cruel world and the pits are no exception.
Each to their own, I say.

options.text: It sounds a little dangerous for my cat.

steps.player: It sounds a little dangerous for my cat.

steps.npc: I agree. Cats have been known to be killed in fights.

steps.player: Oh how terrible. Is there nothing you can do to save your cat?

steps.npc: Of course there is, you can instruct it to be cautious, and it will leave once it feels as if it is in danger.
That depends on how you value your cat.
Well if your cat dies or it runs away you lose.
So the longer it stays in the fight the better chance you have of winning.
I don't know about that.
One thing I know though is that it's a quick way to make and lose money.

options.text: Is there a limit to how much you can bet?

steps.player: Is there a limit to how much you can bet?

steps.npc: Hmmm... let me think. I don't think that's ever arisen but I think it's 20,000.

steps.player: Hmm, that sounds like a silly amount of money to bet on a cat fight.

steps.npc: You'd be surprised what some people would be willing to bet.
There is a minimum bet of 100 coins too.

options.text: Can I challenge you and your cat?

steps.player: Can I challenge you and your cat?

steps.npc: No, not now, we don't really bet with outsiders.

steps.player: But I'm not an outsider, am I not inside in the pits now?

steps.npc: I don't know, maybe once you've done something to win over my trust.
What?
No. Regular townsfolk don't like us, which leads us to distrust them and anyone else.

options.text: It sounds a little dangerous for my cat.
Is there a limit to how much you can bet?
Can I challenge you and your cat?

standard.npc: Ahoy there! Here for a drink? You've picked the right place for it. Steve is thankfully a much better bartender than he was a sailor.

standard.player: Sounds like there's a story here?

standard.npc: Indeed there is. Steve fancied himself a pirate, but on his first proper voyage he managed to crash his ship, the Pandemonium, right here.
He claims it was an unavoidable accident caused by the Storm Tempor, but I heard it was actually because he got distracted by a large flock of angry parrots.

standard.player: So he crashed the boat and then decided to open a bar?

standard.npc: Pretty much.
What do you need, adventurer? There is a battle to fight!

steps.npc: Get yerself a harpoon from the crate on the ship, then go fish around the island t' catch some harpoonfish. They make fer fine ammo against Tempoross!
Once ye caught some, ye can cook 'em at the shrines on the island if ye want 'em to pack more of a punch. Then come back t' the ship an' load 'em in the ammunition crates next to the cannons.
Our cannoneers will get t' firin' the harpoonfish at Tempoross. When it's weak an' submerges to recover its energy, get down to the jetty next t' the ship an' fish those spirit pools.

Be quick with fishin' those spirit pools though, or it'll come back so strong we'll have to abandon the fight! With any luck, we'll weaken those spirit fish enough t' subdue Tempoross. Now get t' the fight, sailor!

options.text: What should I watch out for?

steps.player: What should I watch out for?

steps.npc: If Tempoross electrocutes a cannon t' stop it from firin', ya better load your harpoonfish into the other ammunition crates t' keep them cannons firin' instead.

Also, make sure t' grab a rope from the ship crates an' keep an eye out for big waves. We'll make sure t' shout about them. Then ye best quickly tether yerself t' an island totem pole or ship mast with that rope.
If the waves break the totem pole or ship mast, ye can grab a hammer from the ship crates t' fix 'em up before the next big wave hits.
Oh, an' keep an eye out for lightnin' clouds causin' fires. Get a bucket from the ship crates, fill it with water at a pump, and get t' puttin it out before it spreads.
If ye get hit by the waves or fire, don't be surprised when ye lose those fish an' tools ye gathered. Now get t' the fight, sailor!
Really? You will receive no reward if you do.

options.text: Yes, I really want to leave.
No, I don't want to leave.
I'll get on with the fighting.

steps.player: I'll get on with the fighting.

standard-dialogue-after-subduing-temporo.npc: We did it! Tempoross has been sudbued once again. Well done!
Take a well deserved rest but don't get too comfy, it'll regain its energy soon enough!

steps.npc: We usually find some debris washed up near the docks back at Unkah. Feel free t' have a look. Ya might find somethin' useful!
It won't be long before Tempoross regains enough energy to be a problem and we'll have to wrangle it again. Hopefully we can count on you to 'elp!
Aye aye!

steps.text: The player returns to the Ruins of Unkah.
