standard.player: What does it take to become first mate on a ship?

standard.npc: Good question. We have a diplomatic consession at the turn of the financial year. Said pirate is chosen should the existing mate be absent without leave.

standard.player: I had no idea. I always figured it was all about popularity.

standard.npc: It is. I'm just pulling your leg.
I don't sell to outerlanders.

standard.text: Only Fremenniks may purchase fish here.

before-the-fremennik-trials-attempting-t.text: Only Fremenniks may purchase fish here.

after-the-fremennik-trials.npc: Hello there [Fremennik name]. Looking for fresh fish?

after-the-fremennik-trials-catching-the-.npc: Hey! Get your hands off there!

after-the-fremennik-trials-interacting-w.npc: You're the one who stole something from me!

options.text: Where do you get your fish from?

steps.player: Where do you get your fish from?

steps.speaker: Fish monger
steps.text: Some questions are best left unanswered.

steps.speaker: Fish monger
steps.text: So would you like to buy some fish?

steps.speaker: Fish monger
steps.text: Suit yourself.

steps.npc: Hello! Nice day for fishing!
Well given how good today's catch was, I'd say it's going pretty well!
Nilsal! It's going well, thanks.
I'm fine, how are you?
Not too bad thanks.

standard.text: His eyes are staring vacantly into space.

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: You are not part of our family...

steps.player: Umm. Not last time I checked.

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: Soon you will be... Soon you will...

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: Lost to us.. She is Lost to us...

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: Trapped by the light... Lost and trapped...

steps.player: Ermm... So you don't want to tell me then?

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: Trapped... In stone and darkness...

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: Must find family...

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: Soon we will all be together...

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: Must find family... They are all under the blue... Deep deep under the blue...

steps.player: Ermm... I'll leave you to it then.

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: Free of the deep blue we are...

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: We must find...

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: a new home...

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: We must leave this place...

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: Away.. Away to her...

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: Below the deep, deep blue she waits...

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: They came to her with fire and faith...

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: Too many... Too many...

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: Locked away for all eternity...

steps.player: You'd better start making sense Sonny Jim or I'll...

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: Free... Soon to be free...

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: Must escape the blue.. Deep deep blue

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: Family... Under the blue... Must escape the blue...

standard.speaker: Fisherman
standard.text: What do you want?

options.text: What are you doing out here?

steps.player: What are you doing out here?

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: Catching anglerfish! This is the only place you can find them!
If the player does not have level 82 Fishing:

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: I have heard good things about you, outsider, however, you will need to train your fishing skill before catching these.
If the player has level 82 Fishing:

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: You will need a fishing rod and some sandworms to use as bait. If you need supplies, try Tynan's shoreside store.

steps.player: Thanks. I'll let you get back to fishing.

options.text: I'll let you get back to it.
I'll let you get back to it.

steps.player: I'll let you get back to it.

standard.speaker: Fisherman
standard.text: Don't talk to me outerlander. Anything you have to say to me, you can say to the Chieftain. Goodbye.

after-the-fremennik-trials.speaker: Fisherman
after-the-fremennik-trials.text: Welcome back [brother/sister] [Fremennik name]. It has been too long since last we spoke! The fish are really biting today!

standard.npc: Good day, Your Royal Highness.

standard.player: Good day. What are you doing?

standard.npc: You know very well what I'm doing, Your Royal Highness.

right-click-check-approval.player: Can you tell me how the kingdom approves of me?

if-the-storerooms-are-full.npc: The storerooms are full, your Highness. You should talk to Advisor Ghrim to collect what we've gathered for you.

options.text: Can you teach me the basics of fishing please?
options.condition: If the player has level 1-28 Fishing:

steps.player: Can you teach me the basics of fishing please?

steps.text: If the player has inventory space and no small fishing net:

steps.npc: Ah, you've lost your net have you? Have another!

steps.text: If the player is holding a small fishing net:

steps.npc: I see you already have a net.

steps.text: Look for this icon on the minimap to find fishing spots, they will move as the fish swim around so you can't be lazy.

steps.npc: Ahoy, to fish, you click on the shrimp fishin' spot while ye'r carrying a net.
There's far more as you progress - not just shrimps. You get more equipment, bigger fish and other things too...
When you have a full inventory, you can cook it or take it to the bank. You can find a bank on the roof of the castle in Lumbridge and a cookin' range in the castle kitchen.

steps.text: If the player is on a members world and hasn't started Fishing Contest:

steps.npc: Arrr.. if yer lookin' fer quests you should head over to the Mountain Dwarf who lies north-west of Taverley and have a chat with him, I'm sure he can point you in the right direction.
I can show ye on that map of yours if ya like?

steps.text: (Map opens.)

options.text: I already know about the basics of fishing, got any tips?
options.condition: If the player has level 29-38 Fishing:

steps.player: I already know about the basics of fishing, got any tips?

steps.text: If the player has inventory space and no small fishing net:

steps.npc: Ah, you've lost your net have you? Have another!

steps.text: If the player is holding a small fishing net:

steps.npc: I see you already have a net.
Arrr, chose carefully where and what you fish, you can get different fish in different places throughout the land.
Make sure you hang on to your fish, don't throw them away as you can get valuable cooking experience from them, gar! Look out for other things too...

steps.text: If the player is on a members world:

steps.npc: Then of course there is always the trawler...

If you venture to Port Khazard north of Yanille and speaks to me cabin boy Murphy, he can let you and a bunch of friends use his trawler to fish with... Just make sure you take a bailing bucket or two.
I can show ye on that map of yours if ya like?

steps.text: (Map opens.)

options.text: Any advice for an advanced fisher?
options.condition: If the player has level 39-99 Fishing:

steps.player: Any advice for an advanced fisher?

steps.text: If the player has inventory space and no small fishing net:

steps.npc: Ah, you've lost your net have you? Have another!

steps.text: If the player is holding a small fishing net:

steps.npc: I see you already have a net.
Aye, as you get better and better you'll find that you can fish for things like Tuna and Swordfish. These be very good for combat.

steps.text: If the player is on a members world:

steps.npc: Of course, after that you will get Shark, and if you venture out onto the Trawler from Port Khazard, you can then get Manta Ray or Sea Turtle, very good eatin' on one of them.
You can also use a fishing potion if you can get your hands on one and just need that little edge.. ask someone who is familiar with herblore.
Now.. quests...

steps.text: If the player hasn't started Sea Slug:

steps.npc: Head over to south of the Legends Guild and East of Ardougne and find Caroline. This will have you investigating some strange happenings on the fishing platform.

steps.text: Else if the player hasn't started Tai Bwo Wannai Trio:

steps.npc: Head over to Tai Bwo Wannai Village on the Isle of Karamja and speak to Timfraku to solve a strange mystery.

steps.text: If the player was told about a quest:

steps.npc: I can show ye on that map of yours if ya like?

steps.text: (Map opens.)
If the player had no quests available:

steps.npc: Can't rightly say's there's any I know of that you could handle at the moment, but come back when you're a bit more experienced and I'm sure I can give you a clue.

options.condition: If the player has level 1-38 fishing:

steps.text: Ahoy, small net fishin' you can do just south of Draynor Village and in these very spots here. Aye.
Shrimp and anchovies can be caught with your small fishin' net.

options.condition: If the player is on a members world:

steps.text: Aye, you can net yourself some big fish in Catherby, which is a good place to fish for most things, Gar!
Mackrel and Cod will form the backbone of your catch when big net fishin'.. except for the added extras...

steps.npc: Some rich rewards for big net fishin', make sure you be using a big net fishing spot though...

steps.text: Aye, rod fishin' can be practiced here at these spots, as well as south of Draynor Village and in the Lumbridge river, depending upon your experience. You can get bait at any fishin' shop, there be one in Port Sarim.
With a rod you can catch pike, sardines and herring. Good eating on them.
The art of fly fishin' can be done in rivers, so the Lumbridge river here would suffice.
Aye, you can catch yourself a delicious trout or salmon.

options.condition: If the player has level 25 fishing:

steps.text: Arrr, Lobster pots can be used from the pier on the island of Karamja.
In Lobster pots you can catch lobsters. They're tasty after thems cooked.

options.condition: If the player has level 35 fishing:

steps.text: Arrr, you can also use your harpoon from the pier on the island of Karamja.
With it you can catch Tuna and Swordfish.
If the player is on a members world:
... and shark.

steps.npc: Ahoy, there's also the fishin' guild if ya skilled enough, you can find it south west of Seers' Village.

options.text: Where and what should I fish?

steps.player: Where and what should I fish?

steps.text: If the player has level 1-9 Fishing:

steps.npc: A young and enthusiastic fisher. Try south of Draynor Village or the pier on the island of Karamja to fish for Shrimp at level 1 or Sardines at level 5. Aye, me parrot concurs.
Me parrot Percy on me shoulder thar! Arr!

steps.player: Oookay...sure, a parrot, on your shoulder.

steps.npc: Arrr!

steps.text: If the player is on a non-members world and has level 10-15 Fishing:

steps.npc: Herrin' can be fished from south of Draynor Village or the pier on the island of Karamja when you reach level 10.

steps.text: If the player is on a non-members world and has level 15-29 Fishing:

steps.npc: You can use your small net to catch Anchovies from south of Draynor when you reach level 15.

steps.text: If the player is on a non-members world and has level 20-24 Fishing:

steps.npc: You can practice your fly fishin' in the Lumbridge river to catch Trout at level 20.

steps.text: If the player is on a non-members world and has level 25-34 Fishing:

steps.npc: Pike can be fished from Lumbridge river using your fishing rod and some bait with at least level 25 fishing.

steps.text: If the player is on a non-members world and has level 35-39 Fishing:

steps.npc: Use your harpoon and see if you can catch yourself a few Tuna from the pier on the island of Karamja at level 35.

steps.text: If the player is on a non-members world and has level 40-49 Fishing:

steps.npc: You can use that Lobster pot from the pier on the island of Karamja to get yourself a whole bunch of the little critters once you reach level 40.

steps.text: If the player is on a non-members world and has level 50-99 Fishing:

steps.npc: Congratulations, you can now harpoon Swordfish after level 50. Try the pier on the island of Karamja.

steps.text: If the player is on a members world and has level 10-15 Fishing:

steps.npc: Herrin' can be fished from Catherby and some other places when you reach level 10.

steps.text: If the player is on a members world and has level 16-22 Fishing:

steps.npc: You can use a big net to catch Mackerel from Catherby when you reach level 16.

steps.text: If the player is on a members world and has level 23-27 Fishing:

steps.npc: Cod can be fished from Catherby and some other places once you reach level 23.

steps.text: If the player is on a members world and has level 28-37 Fishing:

steps.npc: You can use your fishin' rod and some bait to catch Slimy Eel in the swamps at level 28.

steps.text: If the player is on a members world and has level 38-45 Fishing:

steps.npc: You can use your fishin' rod and some bait to catch Cave Eel in the caves below Lumbridge Swamp at level 38.

steps.text: If the player is on a members world and has level 46-49 Fishing:

steps.npc: Bass can be caught at level 46 in your big net if you wander along to Catherby.

steps.text: If the player is on a members world and has level 50-99 Fishing:

steps.npc: Tuna and Swordfish can be harpooned - if you're good enough - from the thrivin' fishing village of Catherby, or if you can get in try the Fishin' Guild. Level 35 for Tuna and 50 for Swordfish.
You can also go talk to Murphy and see if you can use his trawler to catch Manta Ray and Sea Turtle if you're really good... Gar!

standard-dialogue-in-miscellania-before-.npc: Greetings. Get your fresh fish here!
I've heard that the Etceterian fish is stored in a cow shed.

standard-dialogue-in-miscellania-after-c.npc: Greetings, Your Royal Highness. Get your fresh fish here!
I've heard that the Etceterian fish is stored in a cow shed.

standard-dialogue-in-etceteria.npc: Welcome [Fremennik name]. My fish is fresher than any in Miscellania!

checking-approval-before-royal-trouble.player: Can you tell me how the kingdom approves of me?

checking-approval-before-royal-trouble.npc: Kingdom? Etceteria is ruled by a Queen and we don't approve of you.

checking-approval-after-royal-trouble.player: Can you tell me how the kingdom approves of me?

standard.player: Wow, are you okay? What happend to you?

standard.speaker: fishrunner82
standard.text: Ugh... Well met, adventurer. I wouldn't go down there if I were you. That trap is an absolute nightmare! The one who created it must be a sadist. I don't know of anyone who has cleared it.

steps.speaker: fishrunner82
steps.text: Oh? Are you pulling my leg, adventurer?

steps.player: I'm fairly certain that if I did that, it would fall off!

steps.speaker: fishrunner82
steps.text: No need to add salt in the wound.

steps.speaker: fishrunner82
steps.text: Although I am curious, how did you beat the trap?

steps.player: I just made sure to prioritise looking out for the arrows. The fire was fairly easy to get through if I just made sure to take one step at a time.

steps.speaker: fishrunner82
steps.text: I see, you're clearly more skillful than I. I'm not sure if I'd be agile enough to do that. Do tell, what was on the next floor?

steps.player: The place looked magnificent, gold lion statues, coffins untouched by anyone else and plenty of Hallowed marks compared to these floors. Although, the traps were significantly harder than the one below.

steps.speaker: fishrunner82
steps.text: I see. Well, I guess I'd better brush up on my skills if I want to see it for myself. Nothing worth having in life comes easy right?

steps.player: That's very true, I wish you the best of luck!

options.text: No one has cleared it? How hard can it be?

steps.player: No one has cleared it? How hard can it be?

steps.speaker: fishrunner82
steps.text: Well, unlike the rest of the traps I've seen so far, you have to deal with both an arrow trap and a fire trap at the same time.

steps.player: Wow, that does sound hard. Do you have any tips for me?

steps.speaker: fishrunner82
steps.text: Well, individually they aren't that hard to do. The fires are always swapping between on and off. I think that if you run to where the fire just was you should be safe.

steps.speaker: fishrunner82
steps.text: The hardest part for me is the arrows. You have to look forward to watch the fire trap whilst also looking over your shoulder to see where the arrows are.

steps.speaker: fishrunner82

steps.text: Before The Blood Moon Rises:

steps.npc: I'm hoping to get back to civilisation and see what the lands of Misthalin look like.

steps.text: After The Blood Moon Rises:

steps.npc: Well, now that the vampyres aren't a problem, I reckon there might be a hope of actually making it through the swamps and starting a new life over in Misthalin.

options.text: Could you defend yourself if we met enemies...?

steps.player: Could you defend yourself if we met enemies on the route to Paterdomus?

steps.npc: Let's just say that I'm somewhat experienced and I'm happy to take on my fair share of bad guys. You don't need to worry about that.

standard.npc: Welcome to GPDT!

options.text: Can you open the shop please?
options.condition: If the player has asked Gabooty what he does in Tai Bwo Wannai:

steps.npc: Not much really... I run a local shop which earns me a few trading sticks, but that's about it. I keep myself to myself really.
They're the local currency Bwana, it's used in Tai Bwo Wannai, there's usually some odd jobs that need doing around the village which you could do to earn some trading sticks.
Or, if you have something which the local villagers might like, you could sell it to me and I'll pay you for it in trading sticks.

options.text: What sort of things do the local villagers like?

steps.player: What sort of things do the local villagers like?

steps.npc: Gnome cocktails! It's amazing but we all just love them! Luckily I've managed to get stocks of the gnome made cocktails and I supply those to my favourite customers. However, many of the customers really like the cocktails
made by the adventurers passing through this way. If you ever happen to have any, bring them my way! I'll give you a good deal on it that's for sure!

steps.player: How did the villagers ever get to try any gnome cocktails?

steps.npc: I think it was that gnome pilot who crashed his glider, perhaps he had a little mini-bar on board? Come to think about it, you'd expect the little guy to get his stuff together and move on out of here wouldn't you? He
must love the jungle to have stayed here so long!

options.text: I want to ask another question.

steps.npc: Yes, it's the Tai Bwo cooperative... catchy name huh! We sell a few local village trinkets and tools. Also, there are a few items that we're actually looking to stock for the locals' sake.
If you happen across any of them please bring them to me, I'll pay a good price for them. I'm sure you'll find the prices very reasonable.

options.text: Can I take a look at what you have to sell?

steps.player: Can I take a look at what you have to sell?

steps.npc: Sure you can...which shop would you like to see? The Cooperative or Drinks store?

steps.target: Gabooty's Tai Bwo Wannai Drinky Store.

options.text: Why do you only take one sort of Gnome cocktail?

steps.player: Why do you only take one sort of Gnome cocktail?

steps.npc: It's funny that actually. I've managed to get a good deal with the pilot of that gnome glider. He can supply me directly now. However, it's really interesting that the local villagers really like the gnome cocktails made by the
adventurers passing through this way.

I think it may just be that they're made fresher, or there is a slight twist in the flavour of the drink, you know, a little more of this, a little less of that, it all adds up and makes for an interesting tipple!

options.text: Can I take a look at what you have to sell?
I want to ask another question.
I want to ask another question.

steps.player: I want to ask another question.

steps.npc: Sure, what do you want to ask?

options.text: Is there anything interesting to do here?

steps.player: Is there anything interesting to do around here?

steps.npc: Sorry Bwana, I'm already busy, why not go and talk to Murcaily! He's around the village somewhere.

options.text: I've been doing some work around the village.

steps.player: I've been doing some work around the village.

steps.text: If the player can claim trading sticks from Gabooty:

steps.npc: Yeah, you've been doing a lot of good work around here. Let me give you something for your time and effort.

steps.text: [amount] trading sticks

steps.npc: I've already given you some trading sticks and I don't have any more on me at the moment. Why not go and talk to some of the other villagers and get some contributions?

treasure-trails-medium.npc: Hey there. If you can solve a question for me then you can move on.

standard.npc: Hey it's the Hero! Wow! You're amazing, how on earth did you manage to tackle those two juvinates and Gadderanks? And the town is lovely, you've done a great job!

steps.npc: I'm Gabriela, I'm looking after my husband who isn't feeling too well!

options.text: How do you like your town?

steps.player: How do you like your town?

steps.npc: It's just perfect, thanks so much for your efforts.
Oh, not much really, we're all still hiding from the vampyres and eking out a living from this terrible place, hopefully soon we'll be strong enough to make the journey to the temple on the Salve.

options.text: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: Not as far as I know, we have some basic amenities now which is so very useful, we're all incredibly grateful to you. I've never really seen or known a hero before, so I have nothing to compare one to, but I suspect in
most people's judgement, you would be one! I for one am very pleased to have met you.

after-the-blood-moon-rises.npc: Hey, it's the hero! Thank you so much for everything you've done, not just for us, but for all of Morytania!

steps.npc: I'm Gabriela. I'm looking after my husband who isn't feeling too well!

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Well, I'd be lying if I said life was suddenly perfect, but it's nice to no longer live in constant fear of the vampyres.

steps.player: What will you do now that you don't have to worry about them?

steps.npc: Well, quite a few of us are working on making the town a bit nicer. Not that there's anything wrong with the work you did of course.
Some of the others don't want to stick around. They reckon it might be safe enough to make the journey up to Paterdomus now. I think they want to start a new life across the Salve.

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: With the town? No, I don't think so. You've done enough to help us anyway.
I suppose if you did want to help in some way though, you could maybe assist those who want to get to Paterdomus. The swamps can still be pretty dangerous.

steps.text: other

standard.npc: Welcome to the Mining Guild. My name's Gadrin and I'm the Guildmaster. Can I help you with anything?

options.text: What have you got in the guild?

steps.npc: All sorts of things! There's plenty of coal rocks along with some iron, mithril and adamantite as well.
Deeper in the guild you'll find even more rocks including some runite! The best bit though is our amethyst mine, the only one in the land!
There's no better mining site anywhere!

options.text: What do you dwarves do with the ore you mine?
What do you dwarves do with the ore you mine?

steps.player: What do you dwarves do with the ore you mine?

steps.npc: What do you think? We smelt it into bars, smith the metal to make armour and weapons, then we exchange them for goods and services.

steps.player: I don't see many dwarves selling armour or weapons here.

steps.npc: No, this is only a mining outpost. We dwarves don't much like to settle in human cities. Most of the ore is carted off to Keldagrim, the great dwarven city. They've got a special blast furnace up there - it makes
smelting the ore so much easier. There are plenty of dwarven traders working in Keldagrim. Anyway, can I help you with anything else?

options.text: What have you got in the guild?
Can you tell me about your skillcape?
options.condition: If the player does not have 99 Mining:

steps.player: Can you tell me about your skillcape?

steps.npc: Sure, this is a Skillcape of Mining. It shows my stature as a master miner! It has all sorts of uses including a skill boost to my Mining skill and a chance of mining extra ores. When you get to level 99 come and talk to
me and I'll sell you one.
Is there anything else I can help you with?

steps.text: other

options.text: Can I buy a Skillcape of Mining from you?
options.condition: If the player has 99 Mining:

steps.player: I believe I can buy a Skillcape of Mining from you?

steps.npc: You believe right, miner. You have earned the right to wear one and when you do you'll have a small chance of finding an extra ore, but I'll need 99000 coins from you first.
I'm sorry you feel that way; come back if you change your mind.

steps.text: If the player does not have at least 99,000 coins:

steps.player: But, unfortunately, I don't have enough money with me.

steps.npc: Well, come back and see me when you do.

steps.text: If the player has at least 99,000 coins but not enough inventory space:

steps.npc: Unfortunately all Skillcapes are only available with a free hood, it's part of a skill promotion deal; buy one get one free, you know. So you'll need to free up some inventory space before I can sell you one.

steps.text: If the player has at least 99,000 coins and enough inventory space:
a Mining cape and hood

steps.npc: Thanks very much, master miner.

standard.npc: Welcome to my home. It's rare for me to have guests! Would you like a cup of tea? I'll just put the kettle on.

standard.text: Brother Galahad hangs a kettle over the fire.

options.text: Are you any relation to Sir Galahad?

steps.player: Are you any relation to Sir Galahad?

steps.npc: I AM Sir Galahad.
Although I've retired as a Knight, and now live as a solitary monk. Also, I prefer to be known as brother rather than sir now. Half a moment, your cup of tea is ready.

steps.text: Sir Galahad gives you a cup of tea.

options.text: Do you get lonely here on your own?

steps.player: Do you get lonely out here on your own?

steps.npc: Sometimes I do, yes. Still not many people to share my solidarity with, as most of the religious men around here are worshippers of Saradomin. Half a moment, your cup of tea is ready.

steps.text: Sir Galahad gives you a cup of tea.

standard.npc: No time to talk I'm afraid.

after-the-depths-of-despair.player: Could you remind me where I can find that book on the Accord?

steps.npc: You know, there are so many different ways to greet people. Hello, 'ello, hello there...

steps.player: That still only counts as one!

steps.npc: Hello. How are you today?
Hello! What a day it is in the crystal city, huh?
What can I do for ya?

options.text: What is there to do around here?

steps.player: What is there to do around here?

steps.npc: All kinds of things! The towers are a wonderful sight to see.
On a day like today, I'd recommend visiting the market.

overhead-dialogue-failed-pickpocket-atte.npc: What do you think you're doing?

steps.npc: If I were as ugly as you I would not dare to show my face in public!
Out of my way, punk.
Hmm... you smell strange...
Like a human!

steps.player: Oh! Er... I just ate one is why!

steps.npc: Leave me alone.
Don't talk to me again if you value your life!
Get lost!
I don't have anything to give you so leave me alone, mendicant.
Have you no manners?
I don't have time for this right now.
I have no interest in talking to a pathetic meat bag like yourself.
I bet you have wonderful paws.
A very miserable day, altogether... enjoy it while it lasts.
If you catch anyone promise me you'll share.
I haven't smelt you around here before...
You smell familiar...
Seen any humans around here? I'm v-e-r-y hungry.
You look to me like someone with a healthy taste for blood.
Good day to you, my friend.
Fancy going up to the castle for a bit of a snack?
Give me a moment, I have a bit of someone stuck in my teeth...

standard.npc: Welcome to the vinery. Can I help you?

steps.npc: Let's see... First, you'll need to treat the soil with saltpetre. Dig it into the patch with a trowel. The minerals are good for the fruit.
Then plant a grape seed, and just let it grow. I'll look after it, so it won't get diseased.
When your grapes are ready, pick them and clear the patch so you can grow a new vine.
Does that seem clear, or would you like help with something else?

steps.text: other
If the player has not completed A Kingdom Divided:

steps.npc: I'm the vintner. I helped Lord Hosidius to develop this land as a vinery, and now it's complete he's put me in charge of production while he works on a new project.
His son, young Pandur, works here too. Pandur checks the wine I produce. But if you've got any questions about the farming, don't ask Pandur. Ask me instead. He checks the wine too much.

steps.text: continue
If the player has completed A Kingdom Divided:

steps.npc: I'm the vintner. I helped the late Lord Hosidius develop this land as a vinery. He put me in charge of production once it was completed.
The new Lord Hosidius used to work here as well. He has new duties of course, but that hasn't stopped him coming down to check the wine I produce.

steps.text: continue

steps.npc: So can I help you with anything?

steps.text: other

steps.npc: It's short for 'Gallows'. When I was young, a boy made some improper suggestions to me, so I grabbed him by his neck and held him in the air until he learnt some manners.
Now, dear, do you need help with the vinery? I'm enjoying the chat, but I have work to do.

steps.npc: Another human? Do what you need to and then be gone from here.
Every day they let more of your kind in.
Hmph!
I don't talk to you lot.
Not interested!

standard-dialogue-man-in-leather-body.npc: I'm ruined, all because of that stupid cat! It has ruined me.
Why did it have to get itself killed? Why?

standard-dialogue-man-in-leather-body.player: Aside* I think I should leave him alone. He seems a little upset right now.

standard-dialogue-shirtless-man.npc: Trying to win my shirt back. I lost it last night in a silly bet.

standard-dialogue-shirtless-man.player: Well I hope your luck improves. I doubt it can get any worse.

standard-dialogue-shirtless-man.npc: Well I've little left to lose, maybe some more hair and my trousers.

standard-dialogue-shirtless-man.player: I really think you should try hold on to them.

standard-dialogue-man-with-top-hat.player: I was just wondering what you were doing here?

standard-dialogue-man-with-top-hat.npc: I ask myself the same question often.
What am I doing down here in these pits along with these filthy dregs of society?

standard-dialogue-man-with-top-hat.player: And do you ever come up with an answer?

standard-dialogue-man-with-top-hat.npc: I'm here taking their money, that's what.

standard-dialogue-man-with-feathered-hat.npc: Just a bit of drinking, a bit of fighting and a few people trying to win big.

standard-dialogue-man-with-feathered-hat.player: Nothing but good clean family fun.

standard-dialogue-woman-in-green.npc: Nothing much. Just keeping myself occupied, placing a couple of wagers here and there.
Yes in the sense that I'm not as bored as I was and no in terms of the number of coins in my purse.

standard-dialogue-woman-in-grey.npc: Trying to win back some money.
In every bet there is a fool and a thief and I'm beginning to think that I'm not much of a thief.

standard-dialogue-woman-with-pink-beret.npc: Having fun. It's such a blast I've already won 5 thousand gold coins today, my cat just keeps winning.

standard-dialogue-after-the-specific-gam.player: So how do these rat pits work?

standard-dialogue-after-the-specific-gam.text: If in the Ardougne rat pit:

steps.npc: Things work simply in the Ardougne ratpits.
If you have a kitten and at least 100 coins you can challenge someone else who also has a kitten and some spare change.

steps.player: That sounds simple enough so far.

steps.npc: You then agree on a wager. It's rumoured that some ratcatchers can talk to their own cats and give them tactics to aid them.

steps.player: So then how do you win the challenge?

steps.npc: I was just getting to that. Both the challengers' cats are placed inside the arena, and whichever kills 5 rats first wins.

steps.text: continues

standard-dialogue-after-the-specific-gam.text: If in the Varrock rat pit:

steps.npc: It's simple.
In Varrock if you have a grown cat and a couple of coins you can challenge someone else who also has a grown cat and some spare change.

steps.player: That sounds simple enough so far.

steps.npc: You then agree on a wager. It's rumoured that some ratcatchers can talk to their own cats and give them tactics to aid them.

steps.player: So then how do you win the challenge?

steps.npc: I was just getting to that. Both the challengers' cats are placed inside the arena, and whichever kills 7 rats first wins.

steps.text: continues

standard-dialogue-after-the-specific-gam.text: If in the Port Sarim rat pit:

steps.npc: The Port Sarim pits are quite fussy, no lazy cats allowed in here.
You know if you neglect a wily cat, it gets fat and lazy? Well, they're not allowed to fight in here, only wily cats.

steps.player: That sounds simple enough so far.

steps.npc: You then agree on a wager. It's rumoured that some ratcatchers can talk to their own cats and give them tactics to aid them.

steps.player: So then how do you win the challenge?

steps.npc: I was just getting to that. Both the challengers' cats are placed inside the arena, and whichever kills 11 rats first wins.

steps.text: continues

steps.npc: It's a cruel world and the pits are no exception.
Each to their own, I say.

steps.text: other

options.text: It sounds a little dangerous for my cat.

steps.player: It sounds a little dangerous for my cat.

steps.npc: I agree. Cats have been known to be killed in fights.

steps.player: Oh how terrible. Is there nothing you can do to save your cat?

steps.npc: Of course there is, you can instruct it to be cautious, and it will leave once it feels as if it is in danger.
That depends on how you value your cat.
Well if your cat dies or it runs away you lose.
So the longer it stays in the fight the better chance you have of winning.
I don't know about that.
One thing I know though is that it's a quick way to make and lose money.

options.text: Is there a limit to how much you can bet?

steps.player: Is there a limit to how much you can bet?

steps.npc: Hmmm... let me think. I don't think that's ever arisen but I think it's 20,000.

steps.player: Hmm, that sounds like a silly amount of money to bet on a cat fight.

steps.npc: You'd be surprised what some people would be willing to bet.
There is a minimum bet of 100 coins too.

options.text: Can I challenge you and your cat?

steps.player: Can I challenge you and your cat?

steps.npc: No, not now, we don't really bet with outsiders.

steps.player: But I'm not an outsider, am I not inside in the pits now?

steps.npc: I don't know, maybe once you've done something to win over my trust.
What?
No. Regular townsfolk don't like us, which leads us to distrust them and anyone else.

standard.npc: Ello there. I'm Gamfred, the engineer in this here guild. Have you seen my catapult?

options.text: That's not a catapult, it's a large crossbow.

steps.player: That's not a catapult, it's a large crossbow.

steps.npc: WHAT!? I'll have you know that is the finest piece of dwarven engineering for miles around! How DARE you insult my work!
Nice to meet someone who appreciates fine work, have you tried it out yet?
What did you think?
Well I guess not everyone will like it.
Glad ta hear it. Try it again sometime. We have more tests to run.
Well I guess not everyone will like it. But give it another chance before you go.

steps.npc: Silly muffin, you have one already!

standard.npc: Hello there. Don't see many people around here. The name's Garl.

standard.player: Hey. What are you doing here?

steps.text: It's called Ver Sinhaza. They say it was once the home of a Saradominist queen. Now it belongs to Verzik Vitur, a vampyre noble.

steps.speaker: Garth
steps.text: Beneath the castle you'll find the Theatre of Blood. Every day, citizens of Meiyerditch take on various challenges set up by Verzik, all the provide entertainment for the vampyres.

steps.speaker: Garth
steps.text: The citizens don't need to be forced though. Anyone who survives the Theatre is promised freedom from the vampyres. It provides a little bit of hope in this dark place.

options.text: Can you tell me about the Sanguinesti region?

steps.player: Can you tell me about the Sanguinesti region?

steps.speaker: Garth
steps.text: Yep, that's where we are at the moment. The region is split into two cities, Meiyerditch in the south and Darkmeyer in the north.

steps.speaker: Garth
steps.text: Meiyerditch is just one large ghetto. The city is split into sectors so that the vampyres can collect blood tithes on a rotational basis. That way they don't kill everyone off in one go.

steps.speaker: Garth
steps.text: Darkmeyer is the vampyre capital. Humans aren't allowed there unless they're a personal slave of some lord or lady. They say the vampyres there live very luxurious lifestyles.

options.text: What do you know about the vampyres?

steps.player: What do you know about the vampyres?

steps.speaker: Garth
steps.text: Not much really. There seems to be three main types, juveniles, juvinates and vyres.

steps.speaker: Garth
steps.text: Juveniles seem to be the lowest form of the vampyre. No one around here knows for sure but the general consensus is that they're former humans who've been converted in some way.

steps.speaker: Garth
steps.text: Juvinates are initiated juveniles who've had some training and are starting to gain some powers.

steps.speaker: Garth
steps.text: Then you have the vyres. Very nasty and very powerful. I wouldn't get on the wrong side of one if I were you.

steps.npc: I am Gelin, the greatest assassin ever to train in Al Kharid. If you have not heard of me, that is because my victims never live to speak of me.
In my years as a warrior of fortune, I have fought in many lands, meeting fighters of all calibres, and I found they all had something in common:
Every single one had a soul-gripping fear that they would suffer a humiliating defeat at the hands of their foes.
They did not fear the pain, you understand. They feared the diminishment that comes with defeat.
To see one's wealth in the hands of another. To see one's skills decrease, as the hard-earned experience is lost. That is what they all feared.
Thus I was inspired to create this life insurance brokerage. I can protect your Hitpoints experience, so that you will not lose so much of it when you are defeated.
I cannot protect other skills, and I have no intention whatsoever of protecting anyone's items - a victor deserves their spoils.

steps.text: other

steps.player: Why do you sell life insurance in a graveyard?

steps.npc: There is no more fitting place! The graves of the dead remind the living that their lives are fragile, and that death is the inescapable fate of all mortals.
That is exactly the frame of mind that encourages people to buy life insurance from me.

first-interaction.text: If the player has never trapped goats before:

steps.npc: Ah, what'm'ah gonna do with these damn goats...

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help?

steps.npc: Hrm... ye are an outsider... but ye do have a look about ye. Tell me, d'y'ave experience herdin' goats?

steps.text: If the player has not yet completed Sheep Herder:

steps.npc: Ah, a damn shame. If ye get some experience under yer belt, come back, but these goats aren't for the weak handed.

steps.text: You need to have completed the Sheep Herder quest to hunt goats.
If the player has completed Sheep Herder:

steps.player: I have experience herding sheep, if that counts for anything?

steps.npc: Aye? Well, I s'pose I should take what I can get. Feel like helpin' out with the goat problem?

steps.player: How can goats be a problem?

steps.npc: When there's too bleedin' many of 'em!

As yer can see, on this hill, there's a... large goat herd. We think the wyrms used to eat 'em and keep the numbers down, but since we moved in, we think they've just kept spawnin' and... well, you can see what happens.
Best plan o' action we came up with is the goat pit. It ain't pretty, but the goats are dumb enough for it t'work.

steps.player: So how does goat herding come into this?

steps.npc: You herd the goats into the pit and they're dumb enough t' jump right in.
There's a pile o' spikes right 'ere. You'll wanna grab yerself a set of them and line the pit with 'em first.
The other pile 'ere is a bunch o' cattleprods. You can use one of them, or if ye fancy yerself one of them mages, me pal Jeff reckons ye might be able to pull 'em around wit' a spell or two.
Telly knee rectric grab? Dark le hure? I don't remember. If those names mean anything to ye, don't tell me. I'm better off not knowing.

steps.player: So I just prod the goats into the pit?

steps.npc: Aye, but the pit can only hold so many goats at a time. I reckon ye could fit more in if ye get better at animal handlin', but ye'd need to inspect the pit to tell, I reckon.
Once ye've got goats in t'pit, ye'll need t'sort out the carcasses. Feel free t'keep any horns or fur ye can salvage. Just remember t'line the pit with spikes again once yer done.

steps.player: So, line the pit with spikes, herd the goats into the pit, sort the carcasses and repeat. Got it, thank you!

steps.npc: Aye, ye could reduce me speech into a single line, ye bloody outsider...

first-interaction.text: If the player has trapped goats before first speaking to Geoff:

steps.npc: Have ye been pittin me goats without permission?!

steps.player: Sorry, I didn't realise that I-

steps.npc: Ha! I'm just pullin' yer leg, outsider. Ye've got nothin' t'worry 'bout!
Glad t'see ye've figured out how t'use the pit, at least. If ye need help with anythin' else, we can talk later, else I'll leave ye to it.

subsequent-conversations.player: What am I meant to be doing here?

subsequent-conversations.npc: Ye wanna grab a set of spikes from this pile o'er 'ere and line the pit wit' 'em.
Then take a prod and shove the goats in t'pit. Me pal reckons you could use a 'telly knee rectric grab' or a 'dark le hure' to do it, but I don't go fer that magic nonsense.
Ye can probably fit more goats in t'pit if ye get better at herdin' animals, but eventually it'll get full regardless.
Once it is, ye'll need to sort the carcasses. Ye can keep any furs or horns ye salvage as ye clear 'em out. Then ye can just re-line the pit and keep at it.

standard.npc: Can I help you?

options.text: What can you tell me about the people here?

steps.player: What can you tell me about the people here?

steps.npc: Let's see... We currently have Herman & Franklin Caranos, Arnold Lydspor, Devin Mendelberg and Ramara du Croissant. And me, of course.

Herman and Franklin are brothers, as you'll know. Herman's always been a fishing nut. Franklin's not all that bothered about fishing, but he does like tinkering with machinery. They're originally from East Ardougne.
Arnold's a bit more of a mystery. We think he might be from one of the barbarian tribes, but he never talks about that. He's always up for a chat, if you can understand his accent.
Devin Mendelberg comes from some town in Morytania - ghastly place! I'm not surprised he moved about as far west as he could go! He helps Franklin with the machinery, among other things.

Ramara's another Ardougnian. Her father's a baker there, but she didn't want to spend her whole life baking and doing his accounts. Also, you probably know what Ardougne's crime rate is like - it can't be easy running
a market stall in that city! I went there once, and some wannabe adventurer started following me around trying to pick my pockets! I kept hitting him, but he kept coming back again and again!

steps.player: You haven't told me about yourself yet.

steps.npc: Oh, I used to work with my sister, Emily, in the Rising Sun in Falador, but I wanted an outdoor job. The pay's better out here too, and the work's not too bad.

options.text: What is there for me to do here?

steps.player: What is there for me to do here?

steps.npc: You can fish! But I'd be very glad if you could go and do something about the skeletal magi in the dormitories. They've kept appearing there ever since the trolls left.
Also, if you're into glassbowing, you'll probably want a bit of seaweed. It catches in our nets all the time, so you'll usually find some in the machinery down by the shore.
Ok, but come and talk to me anytime.
If I were as ugly as you I would not dare to show my face in public!
Out of my way, punk.
Hmm... you smell strange...
Like a human!

steps.player: Oh! Er... I just ate one is why!

steps.npc: Leave me alone.
Don't talk to me again if you value your life!
Get lost!
I don't have anything to give you so leave me alone, mendicant.
Have you no manners?
I don't have time for this right now.
I have no interest in talking to a pathetic meat bag like yourself.
I bet you have wonderful paws.
A very miserable day, altogether... enjoy it while it lasts.
If you catch anyone promise me you'll share.
I haven't smelt you around here before...
You smell familiar...
Seen any humans around here? I'm v-e-r-y hungry.
You look to me like someone with a healthy taste for blood.
Good day to you, my friend.
Fancy going up to the castle for a bit of a snack?
Give me a moment, I have a bit of someone stuck in my teeth...

standard.npc: Good day to you traveller, are you here to fish or just looking around? I've caught some beauties down here.
The last one was this big!

options.text: I'm here to talk about Combat Achievements.

options.text: Could you explain what they are?

steps.player: Could you explain what they are?

steps.npc: Combat Achievements are a set of tasks for all adventurers to try and accomplish. They range from simple missions to kill various creatures, to challenges that will push you to your limits.
The purpose of these tasks is for you to grow and improve, experience all that Gielinor has to offer, and become stronger in the process.
Is this something that sounds interesting to you?

options.text: Yes, tell me about Combat Achievements.

steps.player: Yes, tell me about Combat Achievements.

steps.npc: Combat Achievements are broken down into six tiers: Easy, Medium, Hard, Elite, Master and Grandmaster.
As you complete tasks, you'll earn points. Tasks in higher tiers give more points than easier tasks. Your rank depends on how many points you've earned.
Whenever new tasks are added to the list, there are more points available to earn, so the threshold needed for each rank will increase. Keep completing tasks to maintain your rank!

steps.text: This is the icon for the summary panel. Within it there is a section for Combat Achievements.
Clicking on the section will open the Combat Achievements interface, where you can browse tasks, bosses and rewards.
Some tasks will require numerous criteria to be completed, so make sure you read them carefully.

steps.text: Other gods fight for their own reasons, but Big High War God fight for war itself!

steps.speaker: Ghost
steps.text: Me chosen prophet of Big High War God. Before I have prophecy, goblin tribes fight one another very much.

steps.speaker: Ghost
steps.text: Long ago we fight other people: beardy-short-people, pointy-hat-short-people, tall people with keen blades. Other people build cities with walls, and we not able to attack them any more.

steps.speaker: Ghost
steps.text: There not enough food for all tribes, so tribes with no food attack tribes who have food. Goblin war last many many years. Finally all tribes meet at this place, where temple is now.

steps.speaker: Ghost
steps.text: It rain many days. But rain not stop goblins. Goblin feet churn up ground with rain and goblin blood. All ground turn to mud. That why it called Battle of Plain of Mud.

steps.speaker: Ghost
steps.text: Battle last many days. Both sides same size, none win, none lose. Goblin bodies everywhere. Many dead.

steps.speaker: Ghost
steps.text: Me not important general, not mighty sergeant. Me just normal goblin. But one night, me have dream.

steps.speaker: Ghost
steps.text: Me see throne of Big High War God. He shine with light so bright me cannot see him, but me hear his voice.

steps.speaker: Ghost
steps.text: He say, 'Stop the fighting!' He say, 'Fighting good, but not if all my followers die! You must not fight one another so much you all die!'

steps.speaker: Ghost
steps.text: Then he say, 'Today I cannot lead you, but some day I will send Chosen Commander to lead you.'

steps.speaker: Ghost
steps.text: I see Chosen Commander in dream. He wear shining armour and stand at front of army of goblins. Behind Chosen Commander, goblins stretch to horizon. Many goblins, too many to count.

steps.speaker: Ghost
steps.text: I see banners of every tribe. Banners of all tribes, even Dorgesh tribe.

steps.speaker: Ghost
steps.text: Other races, they run away from mighty goblin army! Chosen Commander make goblins build siege machines and they break down walls of cities. Then goblins march in and kill everyone!

steps.speaker: Ghost
steps.text: And when all dead, Big High War God himself appear and sit on great throne of bronze and rule over all, with Chosen Commander beside him.

steps.speaker: Ghost
steps.text: Then I wake from dream. I know it true vision from Big High War God. I run to general of my tribe, and he call other generals for emergency meeting.

steps.speaker: Ghost
steps.text: I tell all generals what I see. They decide to stop fighting so goblins not all die. By this time, so many had died that there enough food for all.

steps.speaker: Ghost
steps.text: Then generals set goblins to work building temple on site of battle. It sink into mud, so they turn it into underground temple, and keep it secret from others.

steps.speaker: Ghost
steps.text: Goblins write my vision down in goblin holy book, along with history of goblins and commandments of Big High War God.

options.text: Tell me about the Big High War God.
Tell me more about the Chosen Commander.

steps.player: Tell me more about the Chosen Commander.

steps.speaker: Ghost
steps.text: Me not know much more. In vision, Chosen Commander wear heavy armour and big helmet that cover face. Me not know what he look like. I see him give orders, but he far away so me not hear his voice.

steps.speaker: Ghost
steps.text: Me think Chosen Commander will be great goblin general, but Big High War God chose me to have vision, not great general, so Chosen Commander could be anyone.

standard-dialogue-ghost-at-the-chaos-gol.speaker: Ghost
standard-dialogue-ghost-at-the-chaos-gol.text: I've been doing some research into our new foes. Rumour has it they once lived in a great city in the far north. The city fell and now they are homeless.

standard-dialogue-ghost-at-the-chaos-gol.speaker: Ghost
standard-dialogue-ghost-at-the-chaos-gol.text: It seems they have been promised a new home here in return for wiping us out. We must take great care. We may be fighting for our home, but it seems they are as well.

standard-dialogue-ghost-at-the-chaos-gol.player: Right... And err, how's the fight going so far?

standard-dialogue-ghost-at-the-chaos-gol.speaker: Ghost
standard-dialogue-ghost-at-the-chaos-gol.text: You tell me, I'm no warrior. That said, I did hear that they'd managed to turn some of our own golems against us. If they can do that, I fear what else they may do.

standard-dialogue-ghost-at-the-chaos-gol.speaker: Ghost
standard-dialogue-ghost-at-the-chaos-gol.text: Indeed. We have increased our offerings tenfold, but I fear they fall on empty ears. Perhaps our lord really has gone.

standard.npc: Greetings, traveller. Welcome to 'The Green Ghost' Tavern. What can I do you for?

steps.npc: Sorry, but our pumps dried up over half a century ago. We of this village do not have much of a thirst these days.
I suppose, as long as you keep it to yourself...
You see Gravingas out there in the marketplace? He speaks for the silent majority of Port Phasmatys, for those of us who would prefer to pass over into the next world.

options.text: What happened to the folk of this town?

steps.player: What happened to the folk of this town?

steps.npc: That's a long story, my friend, but you look like you have the time...
Do you know why ghosts exist?

steps.player: A ghost is a soul left in limbo, unable to pass over to the next world; they might have something left to do in this world that torments them, or they might just have died in a state of confusion.

steps.npc: Yes, that is normally the case. But here in Port Phasmatys, we of this town once chose freely to become ghosts!

steps.player: Why on earth would you do such a thing?

steps.npc: It is a long story. Many years ago, this was a thriving port, a trading centre to the eastern lands of Gielinor. We became rich on the profits made from the traders that came across the eastern seas.
We were very happy... until Lord Drakan noticed us.
He sent unholy creatures to demand that a blood-tithe be paid to the Lord Vampyre, as is required from all in the domain of Morytania. We had no choice but to agree to his demands.
As the years went by, our numbers dwindled and many spoke of abandoning the town for safer lands. Then, Necrovarus came to us.

He came from the eastern lands, but of more than that, little is known. Some say he was once a mage, some say a priest. Either way, he was in possession of knowledge totally unknown to even the most learned among us.
Necrovarus told us that he had been brought by a vision he'd had of an underground source of power. He inspired us to delve beneath the town, promising us the power to repel the vampyres.
Deep underneath Phasmatys, we found a pool of green slime that Necrovarus called ectoplasm. He showed us how to build the Ectofuntus, which would turn the ectoplasm into the power he had promised us.
Indeed, this Ectopower did repel the vampyres; they would not enter Phasmatys once the Ectofuntus began working. But little did we know that we had exchanged one evil for yet another - Ectopower.
Little by little, we began to lose any desire for food or water, and our desire for the Ectopower grew until it dominated our thoughts entirely. Our bodies shrivelled and, one by one, we died.
The Ectofuntus and the power it emanates keeps us here as ghosts - some, like myself, content to remain in this world; some becoming tortured souls who we do not allow to pass our gates.
We would be able to pass over into the next world but Necrovarus has used his power to create a psychic barrier, preventing us.
We must remain here for all eternity, even unto the very end of the world.

initial-dialogue.npc: Hello, welcome to Aluft Aloft, the gnome food delivery service. We deliver gnome foods to customers all over Gielinor. Do you want a job? We are always looking for new staff.

steps.npc: First of all you will need some basic Gnome Cooking and Cocktail making training. Go and talk to my Father, Aluft Gianne snr. and Blurberry, if you haven't already, and they'll tell you what you need to do.
Once you have got recommendations from both of them I'd be happy to take you on at Aluft Aloft!

Once you are working for us, I will give you a choice of either an easy or hard job. I will then ask you to make a piece of Gnome Cuisine, and tell you who ordered it, with some information about how to find him
or her. Don't take too long, the order is only valid for a short period of time.
If you complete the delivery successfully, you will be given a tip by the customer and credit towards your own 'free delivery token'.

options.text: What's the difference between an easy and a hard job?

steps.player: What's the difference between an easy and a hard job?

steps.npc: The foods that you need to cook for the easy jobs are more straight forward than the hard ones, and the customers will be within the Gnome Stronghold, or one of the Gnome Glider Pilots on duty. You will get one
credit for completing a delivery, and the tips you get will be a small amount of cash.

The hard jobs could require you to cook any piece of gnome cuisine or cocktail. The customers could be anywhere in Gielinor, If you are going to complete the delivery in time, you'll probably have to use some form
of transport. Gnome gliders are especially useful here.

For the hard jobs you will be given more time to complete the delivery though. You get three credits for completing it, and the tips you get tend to be useful objects, and even a few unusual items, that you won't
be able to get hold of anywhere else!

options.text: What are these free delivery tokens?

steps.player: What are these free delivery tokens?

steps.npc: I'll give you a free delivery token when you earn 12 credits. You can then use the token to make a food order yourself! This is a great privilege, we normally only deliver to gnomes. You may only have one token
at a time, and they are non-transferrable.

If you gain more credits then for every 12 extra credits you earn, you will receive an extra item of food or drink per delivery, up to a maximum of ten items. You can continue to make deliveries after this, but you
will not get any more credits - just the normal tip and cooking training.
Once you call for a delivery your token will be used up, and you'll have to earn another one, if you want another delivery.

steps.player: Will this help me with my cooking?

steps.npc: You will be able to develop your cooking skills during deliveries - you'll get the normal training for making the items, but also a bonus for successfully delivering the goods.

if-a-reward-token-has-been-earned-and-is.npc: Well done. You have worked hard for Aluft Aloft Delivery, and as a reward you are now eligible for a food delivery token that you can use to get food delivered to you!

if-a-reward-token-has-been-earned-and-is.prompt: Do you want me to explain how to use the token?

steps.npc: If you activate your token, a delivery rider will arrive and try to deliver some food to you. This uses up your token. If you want another delivery, you will have to earn more credits from Aluft jnr.

You may only have one token at a time. When you first earn a delivery token (having gained 12 delivery credits, you will be able to receive a single random gnome food or cocktail as your order. If you continue
to earn credits, you will receive an extra random item per 12 credits.
If you have enough credits to get more than 10 you can still play the game, but you will not get any more delivery credits - you may pick up a nice tip though.
These tokens are not transferrable by the way - this is just a bonus for hard workers!

steps.text: If the player did not complete the 2022 Pride event:

steps.npc: I know! It didn't always look like this though. It used to be dull and grey!

steps.player: Dull and grey? How did it become so colourful?

steps.npc: An adventurer came along and helped me out. We cast a magic spell using flower seeds, and it created this lovely sunburst!

steps.player: Oh, I'd have liked to have seen that spell. It sounds impressive!

steps.npc: It was! The news travelled far. I've been getting lots of visitors. Many flower traders from across the lands have paid the meadow a visit.

steps.text: continues
If the player completed the 2022 Pride event:

steps.npc: I know! Thank you again for your help with it. It fills me with happiness to see so much colour.
I've been getting lots of visitors too. Many flower traders from across the lands have paid the meadow a visit.

steps.text: continues

steps.npc: I've even traded with a few for some new flower seeds with different colours!

steps.text: If the player has not yet received a flower crown:

steps.player: That's really cool. What do you do with all the flowers?

steps.npc: I make flower crowns in many different colours. I'm wearing one right now!

options.text: Can I have a flower crown?

steps.npc: You're welcome to have one if you'd like, just come back and ask me, anytime!

steps.player: Thank you. I might do just that!

steps.text: If the player has already received a flower crown:

steps.npc: Well as you may have noticed, you can change the colours of the flowers on your flower crown now!
Turns out the spell we cast was more powerful than we first thought.
So powerful that it made eight new colourations, all as beautiful as the first!

steps.player: That's amazing! And all because we wanted a little splash of colour.

steps.npc: Don't underestimate the power of a little splash of colour!
Lots of things! It's been pretty busy. There was even a huge colourful parade with thousands of people, and they chose this meadow as the starting place!
You were? I didn't see you!

steps.player: It was super crowded. I was the one in the colourful outfit.

steps.npc: The one in the colourful outfit...?

steps.player: Ah, yes, like everybody else. I forgot, we were all in colourful outfits!

steps.npc: Yes! Did you have a good time?

steps.player: I did thank you. It was really nice to see so many adventurers coming together to bring a splash of colour to Gielinor.

steps.npc: It truly was, and so many flower crowns too! I was a bit worried the large pile I'd made of them would go to waste, but in the end I almost ran out!

steps.text: continues

steps.player: Really? That's cool! What made it colourful?

steps.npc: Everyone turned up in colourful outfits, it was like a sea of rainbows.
So many flower crowns too! I was a bit worried the large pile I'd made of them would go to waste, but in the end I almost ran out!

steps.text: continues

steps.player: Sounds like a nice problem to have! Will you be making more for the next parade they do?

steps.npc: The next parade?

steps.player: Yes, I'm sure they'll do another one. If so many people turned up, it must have been a great success. Why wouldn't they want to do it again?

steps.npc: That is a good point. I'll get to making some more right away.

steps.player: Maybe it'll become a yearly thing. A chance to show off some colour, and of course your fancy flower crowns, to all of Gielinor!

steps.npc: Sounds good to me, gives me time to get lots made in advance.
Right, well I clearly have work to be getting on with. See you soon!

standard.npc: Hello, I'm Gillie the Milkmaid. What can I do for you?

steps.npc: My name is Gillie Groats. My father is a farmer and I milk the cows for him.

steps.player: Do you have any buckets of milk spare?

steps.npc: I'm afraid not. We need all of our milk to sell to market, but you can milk the cow yourself if you need the milk.

options.text: Can you tell me how to milk a cow?

steps.player: So how do you get milk from a cow then?

steps.npc: It's very easy. First you need an empty bucket to hold the milk.
Then find a dairy cow to milk - you can't milk just any cow.

steps.player: How do I find a dairy cow?

steps.npc: They are easy to spot - they are dark brown and white, unlike beef cows, which are light brown and white. We also tether them to a post to stop them wandering around all over the place.
There are a couple very near, in this field.
Then just milk the cow and your bucket will fill with tasty, nutritious milk.

Reaching Challenger status will allow you to respawn in Civitas illa Fortis if you so desire.
Reaching Gladiator status might persuade some of the more shady folk around the city to give you more money for... Let's just say illicit valuables.
Reaching Hero status will allow you to travel to the Colosseum via the Ring of Dueling.
Reaching Champion status will grant you free herb patch protection just west of the city.
And reaching Grand Champion status will unlock you the Fortis Salute emote.

steps.player: What's the history of Gnome ball?

steps.npc: Be more precise, stranger.
Strangely enough, by accident.
Don't interrupt!
A great many years ago, before I was even born, there were two young Gnomes. Brothers to be exact.
They were always arguing with each other over the most trivial things - who was the faster runner or who was the tallest.
One day they were up at the swamp throwing stones at the toads.
Yep. You know nothing tastes better than toasted toad?
Anyway, they decided to compete to see who could kill the most toads. This gradually became a daily game, to which they invited friends and family to join in.
It all evolved from there. Creating a playing arena, making up teams and leagues.
Anything else?

options.text: What is the ball made from?

steps.player: What is the ball made from?

steps.npc: Toads of course

Well, of course. You humans know nothing!
Anything else?
Ah, made from the finest thread in all the land.
Gnome hair.
I have no time for jokes. It's a serious matter, we go through plenty of nets every day.

steps.player: So that's why you don't see many Gnomes with long hair?

steps.npc: Exactly.

steps.player: The world makes sense at last.

steps.npc: Anything else?
Well of course, like what?
There's the good old one-two tactic.
You don't know anything do you? You pass the ball onto a team mate, giving him all the attention of your opposition, and giving you the chance to run further ahead.
Well, he passes back to you and you've made an advantage. It's useful in a variety of situations!
Anything else?
Well, don't forget that you can block the opposition whilst a team mate has the ball. Very useful if you want to stop or slow down anyone approaching him.

steps.player: Block for team mates. Got it.

steps.npc: Anything else?
You'd look better if you were shorter.

steps.player: I meant in regards to scoring more goals!

steps.npc: I see. Your agility is important if you want to avoid being tackled, so that would be a good attribute to improve. Also many Gnomes say that being able to attack well with a ranged weapon makes you better at
scoring goals.

steps.npc: Yes, although playing the game itself will improve these skills too. Also you should remember that your distance from the goal affects your chance of scoring, so get close enough and your ranged ability won't matter as
much.
Hmm, some general facts?
OK. Have you noticed the different colour clothes for your opposing Gnomes?

The colours correspond to their skill level. The red ones are the professionals. They've been playing since before you were born! The orange ones are in the middle of their careers, whereas the yellow players know very
little. Just like you!
It's always good to get a group of friends to play with you. That way you can score goals more easily, and if you take it in turns to score the goals you'll all reap the rewards.
You mean you've never heard of Speedy Sam The Striker or Norda 'Steal Arms' van Druman?

standard.player: I didn't know the Varrock Museum was familiar with this continent. What research are you conducting?

standard.npc: We're studying the history of the region, origins of the lizardmen and how it all connects to Xeric.
We've wanted to study this place for a while, but haven't been able to explore due to lizardmen blocking the way.
But now that the Shayzien Army have cleared the path and discovered the Chambers of Xeric in the process, there is much to explore!

steps.npc: Xeric was an incredibly powerful dark mage. He ruled Great Kourend for ten decades.
If you'd like to find out more you should visit the Historical Archive at the Grand Library.

steps.text: other

options.text: What are the Chambers of Xeric?

steps.player: What are the Chambers of Xeric?

steps.npc: At the summit of this mountain we've found an ancient temple and a vast network of caves that we believe were formed by Xeric and his followers.
The discovery of the Chambers tells us Xeric invested significant time and resources here, yet it was never documented.
While much of Kourend's history under Xeric remains unknown, it is very surprising to discover such a huge area that was previously undiscovered to us.
Of course, though be careful. The dangers of the Chambers of Xeric are as yet unknown. You should take a strong group of companions with you.

steps.text: other

options.text: What do you think Xeric used this area for?

steps.player: What do you think Xeric used this area for?

steps.npc: When he ruled Kourend, we know Xeric performed experiments on the living, using power drawn from the Dark Altar. After he was overthrown, he would have needed a new source of power.

steps.text: If the player has not completed Tale of the Righteous:

steps.npc: We believe he came here to seek it. Xeric would also have required a source of many creatures for these experiments, and the Chambers certainly contain many of those!
He must have also had some form of teleportation in order to reach the temple unnoticed.
With time and careful study we will uncover these secrets and be able to answer these questions.

steps.text: If the player has completed Tale of the Righteous:

steps.npc: We believe this altar is that source. It seems to act as an amplifier for the Dark Altar.
As for what he used the Chambers for, that we still don't know. There's a lot of creatures in the Chambers. Maybe he used them in his experiments.

steps.text: other
other

after-completion-of-tale-of-the-righteou.npc: The discovery of this cave could change everything. We might finally be able to discover the link between the lizardmen, the Chambers of Xeric and Xeric himself.

This is the Dorgeshuun Council chamber!
Whenever a decision needs to be made, the seven members of the Dorgeshuun Council meet here. The last meeting was when they decided to open up the city to surface-dwellers.
In between meetings, I work here writing up the minutes of the meetings and working on the definitive history of Dorgesh-Kaan.

steps.player: Can you tell me about the history of the city?

steps.text: If goblin scribe previously thought the goblins worshiped an unknown god:

steps.npc: Before Dorgesh-Kaan, the Dorgeshuun lived on the surface with many other goblin tribes. All goblins were ruled over by an evil god whose name has been forgotten.

steps.text: If the goblin scribe thinks the war was for the gods' own entertainment:

steps.npc: The gods became bored and decided to make the mortal races fight for their amusement. The goblins were sent to fight in many bloody battles against each other and other races.
The war lasted for thousands of years, and millions of goblins died. Eventually, the evil god sent the Dorgeshuun tribe to fight a battle that they could not win.
But General Bloodfist of the Dorgeshuun refused to fight in this battle. Instead, he commanded the Dorgeshuun army to march down into a fissure in the ground.
General Bloodfist stood at the mouth of the fissure and defied the might of the evil god.
The evil god smote him with a mighty blast that shook the earth, but that blast also closed the fissure, sealing the Dorgeshuun away from the reach of the gods.
Lieutenant Strongaxe, now the leader of the Dorgeshuun, led the tribe deeper into the caves. They found this cavern, and here they founded Dorgesh-Kaan, city of the Dorgeshuun.

steps.text: If the goblin scribe thinks the war was because Zamorak attacked the other gods:

steps.player: Can you tell me about the Dorgeshuun civil war?

steps.npc: Certainly!  *Ahem*
At first, Dorgesh-Kaan was ruled over by generals, just as the tribe had been when it was on the surface. Each general succeeded the last by defeating him in combat.
The generals were advised by a council of elders, but the Dorgeshuun were no longer an army, and many of the people felt that the Council should have authority.
The people voted to become a republic, but General Bonehelm refused to give up power, and so the Dorgeshuun Civil War began.
The republican faction was larger, but the military faction contained most of the trained warriors and controlled the magical equipment that the tribe had brought from the surface.
General Bonehelm was driven from the city, but dug his own base out of the caves nearby.
General Bonehelm's army attacked the city using archers mounted on giant frogs. There was a bloody battle, and General Bonehelm was driven back again into his base.
But General Bonehelm's mining had weakened the stone around his base, and the retreating army's footsteps caused the roof to collapse, crushing his army.
That was the last time one Dorgeshuun has raised arms against another. Since then, the city has been ruled peacefully by an elected council.

steps.npc: Ah, this is where you come in!  *Ahem*

In the twenty-ninth century since the founding of the city, one of the miners broke through a wall into the cellar of a surface dwelling. The miners blocked up the tunnel and went back into their mines.

options.text: How do I use the Grand Exchange?

steps.player: How do I use the Grand Exchange?

steps.npc: My colleague and I can let you set up trade offers. You can offer to Sell items or Buy items.
When you want to sell something, you give us the items and tell us how much money you want for them.
We'll look for someone who wants to buy those items at your price, and we'll perform the trade. You can then collect the cash here, or at any bank.
When you want to buy something, you tell us what you want, and give us the cash you're willing to spend on it.
We'll look for someone who's selling those items at your price, and we'll perform the trade. You can then collect the items here, or at any bank, along with any left-over cash.
Sometimes it takes a while to find a matching trade offer. If you change your mind, we'll let you cancel your trade offer, and we'll return your unused items and cash.
That's all the essential information you need to get started. Would you like to trade now, or exchange item sets?

steps.player: What do I have to do in this room?

steps.npc: Have you noticed all the bones around the room? These are teleported here from all over Gielinor to help clean up the landscape of countless bones left behind from combat. What better use for these bones than to convert them to nutritious fruit to be eaten by you mortals? You have to use your Bones to Bananas spell to convert the bones and then place them in the holes on the walls to earn Graveyard Pizazz Points. Unluckily for you, your health will constantly decrease from getting hit by these dropping bones so you will probably want to eat some of the bananas yourself to increase your stay here.

You will get experience from casting your bones to bananas spell and you will get Graveyard Pizazz Points when you put the bananas through the wall. Occasionally you will also be credited with a runestone to help you in your future spell casting.

options.text: Got any tips that may help me?

steps.player: Got any tips that may help me?

steps.npc: Different bones will provide you with different numbers of bananas, so try to find the best type. Collect enough points and you will be able to buy a 'Bones to Peaches' spell from my fellow guardian above the entrance hall. This spell can be used here just like the bones to bananas spell, except this spell will give you even more experience and the peaches will restore more health!

Oh, and a word of warning: should you decide to leave this room by a method other than the exit portals, you will be teleported to the entrance and have any items that you picked up in the room removed.

standard.text: Hail, Group Iron Man! My name is Tony, and I'm here to teach you everything you need to know about Group Iron Men. What can I do for you?

options.text: What is a Group Iron Man?

steps.player: What is a Group Iron Man?

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: Group Iron Man is a game mode where you do everything as a group. You can only trade items with player's in your group, take their items and accept their help.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: This means if your friend in the group has something you want to borrow, you can - assuming you have Individual Prestige status or are a Hardcore Group Iron player! But don't confuse Individual and Group

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: Can I help you with anything else?

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: Individual Prestige is automatically awarded to you the very first time you create a group. It is proof that you were one of the original members of that group.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: This proof is displayed as a gold star next to your name on the group sidepanel. Note that if you join an existing group, you will not be considered an original member.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: The limits are gold and items worth up to 1,000,000 coins for the 1st week, 20,000,000 coins for the 2nd week, 50,000,000 coins for the 3rd week and 100,000,000 coins for the 4th week.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: During these 5 weeks you will also have restrictions to what you can equip: certain items will require you to have killed the monster that drops them.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: Can I help you with anything else?
other

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: Non-Hardcore groups can show their dedication to the group through Group Prestige. This status can be viewed on the group's sidepanel, just below the group's name.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: Group Prestige is lost upon inviting new members into the group, or upon doing certain activities with players outside of your group.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: Can I help you with anything else?
other

options.text: What is a Hardcore Group Iron Man?

steps.player: What is a Hardcore Group Iron Man?

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: Hardcore Group Iron mode is a more challenging version of the regular mode, in which you have only a set number of lives for the entire group.

steps.speaker: Group Iron tutor
steps.text: If you die in an unsafe area, you will lose one of your group's lives. When your shared lives hit 0, you will all be downgraded to regular Group Iron players.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: That's a relief. Have a nice day.

steps.npc: You have five minutes to explore the treasure rooms and collect as many artefacts as you can.
The artefacts are in the urns, chests and sarcophagi found in each room.
There are eight treasure rooms, each subsequent room requires higher thieving skills to both enter the room and thieve from the urns and other containers.
The rewards also become more lucrative the further into the tomb you go.
You will also have to deactivate a trap in order to enter the main part of each room.
When you want to move onto the next room you need to find the correct door first.
There are four possible exits, you must open the door before finding out whether it is the exit or not.
Opening the doors require picking their locks. Having a lockpick will make this easier.
