first-time-talking.npc: Oh, hello there newcomer. I'm Guild Scribe Verity. Do you need me to explain the work we do here?
So it's nice and simple. Just chat to any of the hunters in here to help them out. They're all following reports that I've split up amongst them.
Indeed. There are all sorts of interesting creatures to hunt out there. Sometimes we get reports of a particularly unique example. When that happens, one of the hunters will set out to find it.
If you do decide to take a job from any of the hunters, they'll tell you what type of creature they're looking into. Hunt that creature until you encounter the unique specimen.
Once you've caught it, bring some proof back to the hunter that sent you out in the first place. I'm sure they'll reward you for your time.

first-time-talking.player: I see. Thanks for the information.

steps.npc: I wouldn't know what to do with myself out there, so I like to stay back here with my scrolls.

standard.npc: Welcome to the farming guild. How may I help you?

steps.npc: After the Shayzien Army cleared out the lizardmen in this area, I founded this guild with some fellow Hosidius farmers.

steps.player: Why here? Why not within the safety of Kourend?

steps.npc: The heat of the volcano allows us to grow things here that would never survive in the climate of Kourend. The discoveries we have made are worth the extra risk.

steps.player: Fair enough, anything else I should know about the guild?

standard.npc: Welcome to the woodcutting guild. How may I help you?

steps.npc: I founded the woodcutting guild when I retired from the Shayzien military. I spotted the ancient redwood trees in the hills many years ago from the Shayzien camp, and decided to construct the guild around them.
You can find them to the West, just follow the path.

However, if you're skilled in combat, or simply afraid of heights, the ent cavern may be more suited for you. The ents dwell deep beneath the ancient redwoods, and can be accessed through the cave to the North-West.
Is there anything else I can help you with?
My name is Lars, and I am the founder of the woodcutting guild. I originally grew up in a Shayzien camp, and was raised on the battlefield.
As I grew older, I found peace in Hosidius, and the joys of skilled labour. I turned in my battleaxe for a hatchet, and set up a guild for those also talented in the skill of woodcutting.
Is there anything else I can help you with?
Sure, let me know if there's anything I can do for you.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Hello Buoy and Gurl!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Hello sir!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: How do you know our names?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: I had a chat with your dad. He's super busy, so he's asked me to help you build a snowman!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Really? We get to make a snowman?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Yes! And I'm going to build whatever snowman you want!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Yay! Can it be three snowballs tall?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: But I want it to be five tall!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Five is a bad number, it should be three tall!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: You're a bad number. Five is so much better.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Okay, okay, wait a second. Why don't we meet in the middle. How about four snowballs tall?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Buoy and Gurl think for a second.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Fine, it can be four tall.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Yes, four tall is okay.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Great. Now, we need to pick what size snowballs we want for each tier. Why don't you take it in turns? You can do two each.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: The bottom one should be a huge snowball!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: The next one should be big!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: This is working nicely, we're half way! What about the top two parts?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: The next one should be a small snowball!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: No, it should be little!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: But it needs to be small, little would look bad.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: It wouldn't look bad. Small is better for decorations.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: My decorations will fit on a little one.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Why do you always ruin everything?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: You ruin everything with your silly ideas!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Okay, okay, wait. This clearly isn't working, and I don't want you two to fall out. It's Christmas, we shouldn't be arguing!
How about I make you both a snowman? It can be whatever height and size you like. One each!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: So mine can be five snowballs tall?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: And mine can be three snowballs tall?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Yes, I'll make you both whatever snowman you like!
What would you both like?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: I'd like mine to be three snowballs tall please! And I want the bottom one to be small, the middle one big, and the top one huge!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: I'd like mine to be five snowballs tall please! I want the bottom one to be humongous, then large, then normal, then big, and then a little one for the top!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: That's two very different snowmen, I see why this didn't work before!
What do all these different sizes mean? Humongous? Normal? Little? How big are those?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: You silly billy! Humongous is the biggest snowball of course!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Normal is the normal size that you get when you make a snowball normally. It's easy!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Right, thank you for clearing that up. I'll figure something out.
What are you two going to do for decorations?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: I already know what I want mine to look like!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Me too!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Why don't you guys find some decorations while I build the snowmen? Then you can add them once I'm done.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Okay sir!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: We will do that!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Buoy and Gurl go back to playing in the snow.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Well, that seems sorted. I should speak to Larry again, and see if he has any advice about building the snowmen.
Hello there!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Have you started making the snowmen yet?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: You should talk to dad if you need some help, he knows how to make snowmen!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Yeah, he always used to make really big ones with us!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Maybe I'll go talk to him and see what advice he has.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: He'll say, make them really tall!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: He'll say make them shorter, because that's better!
Buoy and Gurl wander off, arguing about what size snowman is the best.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: I should go and speak to Larry. I'm sure he has some handy advice for me!

2021-christmas-event-making-snowmen.speaker: Buoy/Gurl
2021-christmas-event-making-snowmen.text: That looks good! It needs a [size] snowball next!

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.npc: Yay! Can we decorate them now?

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.text: Yes! Can we decorate them now please [player name]?

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.player: Of course you can. Are they what you wanted?

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.text: Mine too. It's just how I wanted it.

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.player: I am happy to hear that. It was harder work than I thought.

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.npc: You did a good job. Thank you very much [sir/madam].

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.player: It was no problem. Merry Christmas to you both!

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.text: Buoy and Gurl go to their snowmen to start decorating.

2021-christmas-event-when-finished-build.player: I should go and speak to Larry. Hopefully he has that festive white wine ready for me.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Those snowmen look amazing!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Thank you! Decorating them was quite hard!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Yeah, they took ages to do! Do you like mine?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: It's really good! Reminds me of something actually.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: What about mine? Do you like it?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: I like yours too. They both remind me of something!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Mine is Thermy! My favourite monster! She's so big and scary, makes me go woah!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Mine is Tempy! My favourite monster! He lives in the water, a huge mass of angry wet!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: They're both amazing! I didn't know you guys would be so good at decorating.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Dad lets us decorate every year. We get a lot of practice!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Last year we made them into the Fragment of Seren and the King Black Dragon!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: What... really??? I'd like to have seen that. Those sound even more difficult than these two!
How do you know all these monsters anyway? There is no way your dad would let you anywhere near them!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Dad reads us lots of stories, and we hear about them from passing adventurers, like you.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: You must meet some interesting and cool adventurers!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: Not as cool as you though; none of them helped us make our snowmen!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Yes, you're the first to help us make them!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Well, you're welcome. I really enjoyed it. What are you guys going to do now you're finished?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.npc: We're going to go and play! And maybe visit the festival. Will you be there?

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: I sure will be. Maybe see you there!

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.speaker: Buoy
2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.text: Bye sir, Merry Christmas.

2021-christmas-event-after-talking-to-la.player: Merry Christmas, have fun!

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: Look, here come 'nother wan'be jubbly chaser.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: Be nice, Gurt, or you'll scare off another one!

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: Me's big boss of of dis boatsie skill test. Call it Jubbly Jive. Only best wiv boatsies can hunt da jubblies.
Gurtob is da bestest jubbly hunter in all of da seas. No one surpass Gurtob.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: Boatsies? Jubblies? Skill test? What's going on here.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: I'll take it from here, Gurt.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: Dis... Sorry, this corner of the Shrouded Ocean is where we Barracudas like to challenge ourselves to a fun Barracuda Trial called the Jubbly Jive.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: While he may not look it, Gurtob here is actually an expert sailor and trial master for the Barracudas.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: Not at all! He may be rough around the edges and difficult to understand at times, but he's a fantastic sailor and that's the only thing us Barracudas care about.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: I see. So what do I do here? What's the challenge?

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: Creatures talk... talk... long. Go da fastest, grab da toadies, throw da toadies, trick da jubblies, eat da jubblies. Dat's it.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: The goal of this trial is to use balloon toads to lure jubblies. First up, you'll want to sail west to collect da... sorry, collect the balloon toads from a boat of ours.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: On your way, keep an eye out for any lost supplies. You'll need to collect all of them to complete the trial.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: Sailing over rapids will give you a burst of speed! Try to go over as many as you can. The more rapids you go through in quick succession, the faster you'll go!

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: As you continue sailing west, keep an eye out for the jubblies. Remembering where they are will help you later in the trial. They tend to be perched on top of rocky outcrops or trees growing out of the water.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: The total number of them will depend on the rank you're going for. They're also fairly consistent, so your experience should be the same during each trial attempt.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: Once you've sailed far enough west, you should be able to spot the boat where you can collect the balloon toads from. The maximum amount you can collect depends on the rank you're going for.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: Once you've collected some balloon toads, you'll want to start sailing back this way so you can begin luring the jubblies.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: As you sail, watch out for the extra thick stagnant patches of water. They'll slow down any boat, so do your best to avoid them.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: As you keep making your way back, you'll want to start luring the jubblies back with you. The goal is to lure all of them back to us here.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: To lure a jubbly, look out for empty outcrops similar to the ones they like to perch on. If you throw a balloon toad at one of these outcrops, a nearby jubbly will move to it.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: It's worth noting that jubblies will only travel to the closest outcrop to them, so you'll need to lure them one outcrop at a time. Make sure to keep track of where you've thrown toads and where the jubblies started.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: When attempting higher ranks, you may want to set up balloon toads at multiple outcrops ahead of time!

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: While the jubblies are important, don't forget to keep collecting the lost supplies as you come back as well.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: If you can lure all the jubblies and collect all the lost supplies in the time given, you'll be awarded a Barracuda rank! Each trial has three ranks: Swordfish, Shark or Marlin. Each rank is harder than the last.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: For this trial, you'll be asked to lure additional jubblies and collect even more lost supplies as the rank increases.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: You can't attempt the next rank until you beat the one before it. You can also try unranked if you'd like to warm up beforehand.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: See, is like Gurtob said so. Go da fastest, grab da toadies, throw da toadies, trick da jubblies, eat da jubblies. Dat's it.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: I see. Do you have any tips or tricks for me?

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: Of course!

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: First up, you're going to need a boat with at least a mithril helm in order to withstand the strong rapids here, but don't forget, provided you can withstand them, they'll give you a burst of speed!

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: Secondly, you really want to try to avoid the fetid pools around us. They won't harm you or your boat, but they will completely kill all momentum you've built up.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: The only way to get across them is by using a wind catcher, but even then the timing is tricky, so we only give those out to sailors who have achieved at least Shark rank here.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: Thirdly, trim your sails frequently to build up even more speed, but be careful! While it's important to go fast, doing so can make it harder to navigate around the fetid pools.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: If I were you, I'd consider briefly lowering your speed for those tricky turns to avoid getting your boat stuck.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: Hah! Gurtob sail never go down. Only go fastest.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.speaker: Ros
first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.text: Finally, and you probably don't need to be told, but watch out for those rocks, hitting them will put a stop to all of your momentum, just like the pools.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: Thanks for the advice. I'll bear that in mind.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: The objective of this trial is to imbue large crystals dedicated to the different elven clans. You do that by sailing through portals linked to them. To get started, head out into the course in search of the portals.
While you're out there, keep an eye out for any lost supplies. You'll need to collect all of them to complete the trial.
The portals you're looking for are found next to the large crystals. Once you find one, just sail right through it. As you do, the portal will teleport you elsewhere in the crystal-flecked waters.

After being teleported, you'll need to find a second portal to return to the trial area near me, ideally corresponding to the one you went through. The portal you choose to return through determines which crystal
is imbued.

As you sail around, you'll find crystal motes all across the crystal-flecked waters. If your boat is kitted out with an activated wind catcher, you'll be able to turn their energy into wind motes, allowing you to go even
faster.
In order to complete the trial, a specific number of crystals will need to be imbued. Each one is imbued in the same way - by traversing the portal linked to it.
The number of crystals that need imbuing will depend on the rank you're going for. The higher the rank, the more you'll need to imbue.
This course will truly test your capabilities as a sailor. You'll find yourself alternating between navigating narrow spaces and vast wide open ones with the required speed and grace.
While navigating the more narrow spaces, you should be wary of resonance crystals. These old ship defence systems can crystallise your helm, damaging those holding it.
If your helm does get crystallised, you should be able to break the crystals with three swift strikes.
When using the portals, you'll find that each crystal near me has a pair of them near it. Both will send you to the same location.

However, upon using a return portal, your arrival location will depend on which portal you first picked. Choosing which portals to use and planning ahead of time are critical for overcoming this trial.

If you can imbue all of the crystals and collect all the lost supplies in the time given, you'll be awarded a Barracuda rank. Each trial has three ranks: Swordfish, Shark or Marlin. Each rank is harder than the last.
For this trial you'll be asked to imbue additional crystals and collect even more lost supplies as the rank increases.
You can't attempt the next rank until you beat the one before it. You can also try unranked if you'd like to warm up beforehand.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: I see. Do you have any tips or tricks for me?

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: Of course, that's why I'm here.
To start, traversing the portals will reward your boat with an incredible burst of speed, so use that to your advantage.
Additionally, be aware that the portals will both displace your boat and change which direction it is headed for.
Aligning yourself properly before going through is not required, but you should try to anticipate where you'll end up and react quickly.

Next, avoid the resonance crystals in the area. They will target the helm of your boat. If you do get hit by them, make sure to break the crystals rapidly. Doing so will grant your boat a small speed boost.
Another thing to look out for are the crystal motes. If you have a wind catcher or gale catcher activated on your boat, they will be converted into wind motes and charge it up for you.
If you don't have a wind catcher, I'd suggest attempting the Jubbly Jive trial over in Backwater.
Finally, keep your sails trimmed and try not to get lost out there. The portals can be disorientating at first, but I'm sure you'll learn the layout of the course over time.

steps.player: Can you tell me about the Gwenith Glide?

steps.npc: Certainly. The large crystals you see around us are actually remnants of large ships that were destroyed during the Siege of Prifddinas.
Elven ships are not constructed from wood and metal, but are instead sung and woven into life over many moons from extraordinarily rare crystal seeds.
The process is incredibly intimate and time consuming. Each ship created represents not just our goddess, but also the individual who brought it into existence.

Like all Barracuda Trials, the Gwenith Glide exists to push your sailing skills to the limit. However, it also acts as an opportunity to honour not just those that died here, but also the ships themselves.

steps.npc: The objective of this trial is to imbue large crystals dedicated to the different elven clans. You do that by sailing through portals linked to them. To get started, head out into the course in search of the portals.
My name is Gwyna of the Hefin Clan. I'm a trial master for the Barracudas and I provide guidance and counsel to those who attempt this trial, the Gwenith Glide.
It is my job to see that those who died here are honoured and that the sanctity of the course is upheld.

steps.player: Do those goals ever conflict? I'm not sure how the sanctity of the course is upheld as sailors race around the place.

steps.npc: I appreciate your concern, but you need not worry. Respect for the dead can be upheld in many ways. All who take on the trial have my blessing to proceed as they wish.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Hi [player name]. You woke me up, I was fast asleep!

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Hello then. Can I help you with anything?

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Hello [player name]. Did you need something?

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: Nothing important. I'd like to ask you a question if that is okay?

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Ask away.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: Why did you pick the kitchen as your spot to sleep? It must get quite noisy sometimes?

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: It does during meal times, but it's also lovely and warm near the fire, and look at all the food!

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: Good point. Now it seems like the best spot in the house!

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: You catch on quickly, for a human! Now I am going to go back to sleep, unless there is something else I can help you with?

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: That was all I wanted to ask, thank you.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.text: Hannibal curls up on the stool and goes back to sleep.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Oh, hello [player name]. Did I hear a bark?

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: There is, sometimes...

It seems to come and go. I can't figure out why or how.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: That is indeed strange. I'll keep an eye out for it.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: There it is again, did you hear it?

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: I can't say I did.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Maybe I'm imagining it.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.text: Hannibal settles back down and is sleeping in moments.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Hi [player name].

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: How are you doing?

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: Oh, that wasn't me.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Must have been Gem then. She often plays the piano when she thinks nobody is listening.
She's actually quite good.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: I'll have to keep an ear out.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.text: Hannibal stretches and goes back to sleep.
(Future conversations with Hannibal will use response 5.)

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Hi there, [player name].

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: I have another question for you, if that is okay?

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Go ahead.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: Do you ever leave the hall? I've only ever seen you in here.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: I do sometimes. If I do go out, it's normally at night.
I much prefer it in here though. Nice and warm with good food. There is even a bank, if I ever needed a bank for anything.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: That's fair enough. The world can be a pretty scary place out there anyway.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Exactly. It's much nicer to relax here, even with the occasional adventurer disturbing me.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: That'll be me! Sorry, I'll let you get back to sleep.

steps.npc: Like most people who come to Edgeville, I am here to seek adventure in the Wilderness.

steps.text: If the player has 1-11 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: Well, you don't look like you have the skill to make a canoe.
You need to have at least level 12 woodcutting.
Once you are able to make a canoe it makes travel along the river much quicker!
It's really quite simple. Just walk down to that tree on the bank and chop it down.
When you have done that you can shape the log further with your axe to make a canoe.

steps.text: If the player has 12-26 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: I can sense you're still a novice woodcutter, you will only be able to make a log canoe at present.
A log will take you one stop along the river. But you won't be able to travel into the Wilderness on it.

steps.text: If the player has 27-41 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: You are an average woodcutter. You should be able to make a Dugout canoe quite easily. It will take you 2 stops along the river.

steps.player: Can I take a dugout canoe to reach the Wilderness?

steps.npc: You would never make it there alive.

steps.text: If the player has 42-56 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: You seem to be an accomplished woodcutter. You will easily be able to make a Stable Dugout

Only a Waka can take you there.
Come and ask me when you have improved your skills as a woodcutter.

steps.text: If the player has 57-99 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: Your skills rival mine friend. You will certainly be able to build a Waka.
A Waka is an invention of my people, it's an incredible strong and fast canoe and will carry you safely to any destination on the river.
Yes, you can take a waka north through the underground portion of this river.
It will bring you out at a pond in the heart of the Wilderness. Be careful up there, many have lost more than their lives in that dark and twisted place.

If I told you it would spoil the surprise!

steps.player: Ok ok... so how do I earn and claim these tokens?

steps.npc: You can earn them simply by using the training exercises around the guild, the staff will then enter this into a ledger as you play. You can claim them by simply asking any of the staff at the training areas, or
myself.

Why I could best any person alive in a rapier duel!

have. You might even collect enough tokens to be allowed in to kill the strange beasts from the east!
Farewell [brave warrior/fair lady], I do hope you enjoy my guild.

steps.npc: I've lost two of my dear friends, [player name]. This old place doesn't seem to be the same since they're gone.
Nonsense, my friend! They both died bravely fighting against a great evil! There is no blame on you for that.
Remember them for who they were and what they stood for. Mourn their loss, but never bear the burden of their death, for that is not what they would want.
Ah, now that is a topic we could debate for many moons, my friend. Still, regardless of the reason, know that when the time comes, I will fight beside you against Lucien once more.

steps.npc: I am Hatius Cosaintus, the taskmaster for the Lumbridge & Draynor Achievement Diary.

It's a diary that helps you keep track of particular achievements. In the Lumbridge and Draynor area it can help you discover some quite useful things. Eventually, with enough exploration, the inhabitants will
reward you.
You can see the list of tasks on the side-panel.

options.text: I have a question about my Achievement Diary

steps.player: I have a question about my Achievement diary.

steps.npc: Well, there are four different Explorer's rings, which match up with the four levels of difficulty. Each has the same rewards as the previous level and some additional benefits too... which tier of rewards would you like to
know more about?

steps.player: Tell me more about the Easy rewards please!

steps.npc: If you complete all of the easy tasks in Lumbridge and Draynor, your ring can recharge half of your run energy twice per day and cast low level alchemy without runes 30 times per day.

steps.player: Tell me more about the Medium rewards please!

steps.npc: In addition to the easy rewards, your ring can restore half of your run energy and teleport you to the Draynor cabbage patch three times per day.

steps.player: Tell me more about the Hard rewards please!

steps.npc: In addition to the easy and medium benefits, the ring will have unlimited cabbage teleports and four charges to restore half your run energy. Collecting Tears of Guthix will provide increased experience.

steps.player: Tell me more about the Elite rewards please!

steps.npc: In addition to the previous tiers of rewards, you can block an additional slayer target with slayer masters, recharge all of your run energy three times per day and cast high level alchemy thirty times per day. The
Culinaromancer's chest is 20% cheaper, you can use Fairy rings without needing a dramen or lunar staff and you'll receive double wire when thieving in Dorgesh-Kaan.

options.text: How do I claim the rewards?

steps.player: How do I claim the rewards?

steps.npc: One should complete the tasks in Lumbridge and Draynor so they're ticked off, then speak to me to be rewarded.
Toodles.

This ring is a symbol of your exploration of Lumbridge and Draynor. It can recharge half of your run energy twice per day and cast low level alchemy without runes 30 times per day.
If you ever lose your ring, come back to me to reclaim it.

steps.npc: We're working for King Lathas of East Ardougne. He has tasked us with containing the accursed plague sweeping West Ardougne.
We also do our best to ease these people's suffering. We're nicknamed mourners because we spend a lot of time at plague victim funerals, no one else is allowed to risk attending.
It's a demanding job, and we get little thanks from the people here.

standard.npc: You offered yourself to Zulrah as a sacrifice, yet here you stand before me. Did Zulrah reject you?

options.text: Have you any advice for surviving against Zulrah?

steps.player: Have you any advice for surviving against Zulrah?

steps.npc: I think you have misunderstood the nature of the sacrifice, human. Never mind, the mighty Zulrah will make the matter clear to you.
Zulrah is the all-powerful snake god of the southern wastes. He rises from the swamp to show his divine majesty and to accept our homage.
Long ago, our forebears came to this place, not realising that they were trespassing in Zulrah's domain. He arose from the swamp in wrath, and many were slain.
But Zulrah, in his mercy, allowed some of those transgressors to live, sparing them the punishment they deserved, and allowing them the chance to repent.
Then my mother, oldest and wisest of the tribe, dared to intercede with the mighty Zulrah on behalf of her people, and thus a sacred contract was declared.
Zulrah granted us the right to dwell in his lands, and to eat of their bounty. None shall ever drive us out, for Zulrah protects us.
All he asks in return is a periodic sacrifice at his sacred shrine. As long as the sacrifices continue, Zulrah will let us live peacefully in his lands.
Willing volunteers are never hard to find, for their sacrifice buys peace for the tribe, and I grant their families extra rations of food.

options.text: Have you any advice for surviving against Zulrah?

steps.npc: The southern wastes are a perilous place where travellers often become lost. Elves from the woodland villages, gnomes from the eastern caves, and many others.
Some find their way here, like my forebears did. They eat of the sacred swamp eels that Zulrah sends, and become one with the tribe.
Their original families and tribes shun them as unclean creatures once they have tasted of the sacred swamp eels, so they remain here to worship Zulrah.

steps.npc: Using the enchanted amulet is easy; open up the amulet and you'll see a cat's face, use the whiskers to rotate the cats nose. You'll see the nose move and the new direction highlighted. When the nose points in the

direction that Bob is in, the eyes will light up and the mouth will open. You'll need to head in that direction and then check the direction again. If you are very close to Bob then the eyes and mouth will animate no
matter which way the nose is pointing. That's all there is to it, good luck!

standard.npc: Hello there!
Aha, interested in my crossbows are you?

They're dwarven engineering at its best. If you've got enough skill in crafting, smithing and fletching, you can even make them yourself. You can buy some of the parts here and make the rest yourself.

options.text: How do I make one for myself?

steps.player: How do I make one for myself?

steps.npc: Well, firstly you'll need to chop yourself some wood, then use a knife on the wood to whittle out a nice crossbow stock like these here.

Then get yourself some metal and a hammer and smith yourself some limbs for the bow, mind that you use the right metals and woods though as some wood is too light to use with some metal and vice versa.
Wood and Bronze as they're basic materials, Oak and Blurite, Willow and Iron, Steel and Teak, Mithril and Maple, Adamantite and Mahogany and finally Runite and Yew.

steps.player: Ok, so I have my stock and a pair of limbs... what now?

steps.npc: Simply take a hammer and smack the limbs firmly onto the stock. You'll then need a string, only they're not the same as normal bows. You'll need to dry some large animal's meat to get sinew, then spin that on a spinning
wheel, it's the only thing we've found to be strong enough for a crossbow.

Well.. I don't rightly know... us dwarves don't work with magic, we prefer gold and rock. Much more stable. I guess you could ask the humans at the rangers guild to see if they can do something but I don't want
anything to do with it!
Take care, straight shooting.

You can smith yourself lots of different bolts, don't forget to flight them with feathers like you do arrows though. You can poison any untipped bolt but there's also the option of tipping them with gems then
enchanting them with runes. This can have some pretty powerful effects.

steps.npc: Well, my intrepid friend, through those broken bars lies a most remarkable discovery! I named it Scurrius, The Rat King!
This is no ordinary rat. It is a magnificent creature of evolution, forged by the unwitting contributions of adventurers who entered its cave.
It absorbed their combat abilities, transforming itself into an obscene monster. Nature's response to intrusion, you might say! How utterly fascinating!
Ahem, anyway you'll be absolutely fine, of course! Your victory awaits, I'm sure. I shall observe your progress with interest... for science, you know.
Oh, and if you happen to come across Scurrius' spine, please bring it to me.

using-scurrius-spine-on-historian-aldo.npc: Ah, a Scurrius spine! A captivating subject indeed. I'll eagerly take them off your hands, and rest assured, you will be well rewarded.

steps.npc: Ah, I'll need one of Scurrius' spines to do that. Perhaps you could fetch me one?

right-click-trade-option.text: If the player has Scurrius' spine:

steps.prompt: Trade Scurrius' spine for a combat lamp?

steps.text: Aldo gives you an Antique lamp for Scurrius' spine.

right-click-trade-option.text: If the player has Scurrius' spine and the materials to make a bone weapon:

steps.prompt: Trade your Scurrius spines for a bone weapon or combat lamp?

standard.player: Hello. What are you doing here?

standard.npc: Duffy's the name. I'm a natural historian from Varrock Museum. My team and I are here to explore this mountain.

standard.player: It's just an old mountain isn't it? What natural history are you hoping to find here?

standard.npc: Bahaha, you adventurers are all the same, never seeing past the fights and treasure...
This Mountain is steeped in natural history, but our main focus is to study the lizard creatures that surround this area.
Indeed, they're a fascinating species! We're hoping to learn about their origins and how they've evolved.
However, we're not very familiar with this region so we've enlisted the help of the Kourend Grand Library to aid us in our research.

standard.player: What have you learned so far?

standard.npc: Well, we have a theory that lizard creatures aren't natural at all, but were created by dark magical experiments.
Right now we're looking for evidence to prove this theory, but's it's proving somewhat difficult.
No thanks adventurer, natural history studies are delicate and precise... but if we ever need something haphazardly destroyed we'll let you know.

standard.player: Not all adventurers only care about fighting, you know... I was only offering to help.

standard.npc: We don't need your help. Run along now, go and play in the dungeons with the other adventurers. I hear they're full of monsters to fight!
Try not to get yourself killed, it would be such a tragedy!

after-completion-of-tale-of-the-righteou.npc: Good thanks. Now that we've found this cave, we're learning more about the lizardmen than ever before.

standard.npc: Hello there, welcome to Varrock Museum! Can I help you?

steps.npc: Well, as you can see we have recently expanded a great deal to cope with the influx of finds from the Dig Site. Also, of course, to prepare for the new dig we're opening soon.

options.text: Tell me about the new dig.

steps.player: Tell me about the new dig.

steps.npc: Well, we recently had a large chunk of funds donated to us, so we sent out all sorts of explorers - I'm sure you'll meet them as you go around the world. People like Simon down in the desert near the pyramid as well

as Aristarchus in Pollnivneach, Varmen and, of course, Anna Jones. Anyway, we think we have discovered an island that has massive archaeological significance. We can't say much beyond that at this point, as we haven't
researched it. If you have the qualifications and help us out around the museum, I'm sure we could offer you a place on the dig when we're ready to go.

options.text: I have some information which might be of use in your displays.
Tell me about other sections of the Museum.
I have some information which might be of use in your displays.

steps.player: I have some information that might be of use in your displays.

steps.npc: That's grand! We're always glad to have more facts. Now, tell me what you know...

steps.text: If the player has Demon Slayer completed:

steps.player: Well, I recently defeated Delrith, a demon! I did it by using a sword called Silverlight, which is apparently the only sword that could do it. I can give you a description if you want?

steps.npc: Delrith! Incredible! I am grateful to you for letting me know. Please tell me more about Silverlight and I'll get a display erected. Display number 25, 5th Age, year 20.

steps.text: If the player has Shield of Arrav completed:

steps.player: Well, I infiltrated one of the gangs here in Varrock...

steps.npc: We have gangs?

steps.player: Erm, yes...anyway, I managed to get half the shield back.

steps.npc: Only half?

steps.player: Yes. The gangs had a bit of a tiff, you see. A friend helped me get the other half and I returned it here to get my reward.

steps.npc: Yes, yes, we were most pleased to have the shield returned - as was the King, I imagine. This is wonderful news, I shall make sure the display is updated at once! Display number 24, 5th Age, year 700-800.
Oh, and before I forget, we found this old lamp lying around...and since you've done such a sterling job, we'd like you to have it.

steps.player: Oh, random bits of tat, thank you very much.

steps.npc: You're welcome!

steps.text: If the player has Rune Mysteries completed:

steps.player: I helped the Order of Wizards rediscover how to access the Rune Essence Mine.

steps.npc: Ah, I heard about that. Tell me more.

steps.player: Hmm. I can't tell you much, but I do know that this mine is hidden away. You can only get there by teleportation.

steps.npc: Sounds like magic to me! I'll get a display put up immediately. Display number 21, the first display of the 5th Age.

steps.text: If the player has Observatory Quest completed:

steps.player: I helped to rebuild the Observatory near Ardougne. I had to fight to do it, and learn how to use the telescope too. I can draw you a diagram of the Observatory if it would help.

steps.npc: That would help immensely. Restored it, eh? And it works, you say? Excellent, perhaps we can get to some real stargazing now! Display number 17, 5th Age, year 70.

steps.text: If the player has Merlin's Crystal completed:

steps.player: I helped to free the wizard, Merlin, by using Excalibur...

steps.npc: Is that some kind of spell?

steps.player: No, it's a sword. King Arthur's sword.

steps.npc: What kingdom does he rule then?
Where on Gielinor is that?

steps.player: It's not! That's what I've been trying to tell you. I found that King Arthur and his knights are really biding their time here in Gielinor until they are called back to their own world, when they are needed!

steps.npc: That's amazing! So he's really from another world! Well, this is interesting, I'll make sure a display is put up immediately. Well done, [player name]! Display number 9, 5th Age, year 132.
Oh, and before I forget, we found this old lamp lying around...and since you've done such a sterling job, we'd like you to have it.

steps.player: Oh, random bits of tat, thank you very much.

steps.npc: You're welcome!

steps.text: If the player has The Grand Tree completed:

steps.player: I helped to save the gnomes' Grand Tree!

steps.npc: Oh? You mean those little green fellows with their gliders?

steps.player: Yes. I uncovered this nasty character called Glough and ended up being ambushed by a black demon...

steps.npc: A black demon! How did you survive!?

steps.player: Oh, I was fine. After the demon it was downhill all the way, and King Narnode allowed me to use the mine under the Tree, and free passage on gnome gliders.

steps.npc: You mean that those flimsy things can fly with more than a gnome in? That is unexpected. I shall update the display immediately. Display number 10, upstairs in the middle of the room!

steps.text: If the player has Priest in Peril completed:

steps.player: Some disturbing and heroic news from Morytania, concerning the River Salve and the Temple Knights.

steps.npc: Ahh, the Temple Knights...little is known of them.

steps.player: Yes, it seems that these seven knights drove back the nasty things coming out of Morytania, and Saradomin blessed the Salve to stop them getting back.

steps.npc: Quite worrying that it's just a bit of water keeping them there, but Saradomin will protect us I've no doubt. Thank you for the information, I'll get a display put up. Display number 23, 4th Age, year 1100-1200.

steps.text: If the player has In Aid of the Myreque completed:

steps.player: Some disturbing and heroic news from Morytania concerning the River Salve and the seven priests.

steps.npc: Oh?

steps.player: Yes, it seems that these seven priests were also warriors and drove back the nasty things coming out of Morytania. Then Saradomin blessed the Salve to stop them getting back.

steps.npc: Quite worrying that it's just a bit of water keeping them there, but Saradomin will protect us, I've no doubt. Thank you for the information, I'll get a display put up. Display number 23, 4th Age, year 1100-1200.

steps.text: If the player has A Tail of Two Cats completed:

steps.npc: The little black cat that used to wander around sometimes? Sure, I remember him.

steps.player: I found out a lot about his background...turns out he was once human and helped to defeat a dragonkin once!

steps.npc: Dragonkin?
Tell me more!

steps.player: Well, you see, it started when Bob went missing...and involved a big sphinx in Sophanem, the City of the Dead, and me taking care of Unferth...

steps.npc: This is starting to sound familiar...

steps.player: It must...you know Reldo, the Varrock librarian - he knows all about Robert the Strong.

steps.npc: You mean that was Bob? Wow... I will get a display erected immediately about the history of this brave warrior. Display number 20, 4th Age, year 1-100.

steps.text: If the player has Making History completed:

steps.player: I found out more about King Lathas's ancestors.

steps.npc: Oh? I'd be interested to hear this, we have a painting of him upstairs.

steps.player: Indeed, it turns out that there was a big battle in the year 98 of the 5th Age. One of his ancestors became king because he survived it...

steps.npc: Ahh, is this relating to that small museum near Ardougne?
Ahh yes, we've been meaning to make a display on that for some time. They sent us some information, too; I'm glad you reminded me, I'll get that done now. Display number 46, 5th Age, year 98.

steps.text: If the player has Temple of Ikov completed:
If the player sided with the Guardians of Armadyl:

steps.player: Well, I was asked to retrieve the Staff of Armadyl, from the Temple of Ikov, by Lucien, but instead, I helped the guardians of the staff and banished Lucien from this plane of existence, so that he could never again return.
I saw the staff and can describe it to you if you want?

steps.text: If the player sided with Lucien:

steps.player: Well, I was asked to retrieve the Staff of Armadyl, from the Temple of Ikov, by Lucien. When I returned it he grew in power unimaginably. I held the staff and can describe it to you if you want?

steps.npc: Yes! Please do!

steps.text: You describe the staff in detail while the historian takes notes.

steps.npc: That's excellent, I'll get a display put up straight away! Display number 28, end of the 2nd Age.

steps.text: If the player has Curse of the Empty Lord completed:

steps.player: Well, I found out more about the Staff of Armadyl from a ghost. It seems that Zamorak was a mortal when he got hold of the staff, and he used it to, well...spear Zaros, and somehow ended up becoming a god. It was

steps.npc: Now that is what you call a story. Tell me more so that I can put it up on the display.

steps.text: You recount the tale of the battle between Zaros and Zamorak as you heard it from the ghostly swordsman.

steps.npc: This is wonderful, I shall have a display made immediately to go with the staff model. Display number 28, end of the 2nd Age.

steps.text: If the player has Hazeel Cult completed:

steps.player: I discovered the truth behind the Carnillean family fortune!

steps.npc: Oh? Is that the family over near Ardougne?

steps.player: Yes. I got a bit involved in family business...

steps.npc: And?

steps.player: I found a secret cult in Ardougne and found that the Carnillean family started building the city of Ardougne from a house they'd captured from a Zamorkian lord.

steps.npc: How exciting, I'll get a display put up immediately. Display number 7, 5th Age, year 7.

steps.text: If the player has What Lies Below completed:

steps.player: I discovered a tunnel and a cult of chaos mages here in Varrock!

steps.npc: Oh! Whatever can we do!

steps.player: Calm down, I have arrested the ringleader.

steps.npc: Oh, thank Saradomin for that. So, tell me the story!

steps.player: Well, I met Rat and he asked me to fill his folder, and I got mixed up with Surok....

steps.npc: A rat asked you to fill a folder?

steps.player: No, no, no - Rat Burgiss. But anyway, it turns out that this cult has been trying to get to the King, but I stopped them.

steps.text: If the player does not have the book Dagon'hai history in their inventory:
The historian looks a little overwhelmed, but also skeptical.

steps.npc: I don't suppose you have any evidence of this cult?

steps.player: Not with me, but there is a book I can get you from the library.

steps.npc: That sounds good - bring me that and we'll create a display.

steps.text: If the player has the book Dagon'hai history in their inventory:
The historian is scribbling furiously on his pad, and finally turns to you.

steps.player: Actually, to save you some writing, I have this book here that has lots of information. You can have it if you want...

steps.npc: Why, thank you... Yes, this is a bit of a revelation! I'll get a display put up immediately. Display number 3, 5th Age, year 70.

steps.text: If the player has Defender of Varrock completed:

steps.player: Well, we got rid of the marauding zombies.

steps.npc: That's handy. Zombies do tend to leave horrible muddy footprints around the place. So what actually happened with them?

steps.player: Well, Zemouregal the Mahjarrat sent his zombie army against Varrock. However, we figured out how to stop him.
I found out that the descendant of the founder of Varrock could use the shield to stop the zombie army. It turns out that Dimintheis was that descendant, so he was able to defeat the zombies.

steps.npc: My, my, that is all very interesting. I shall make sure the display is updated at once! Display number 24, 4th Age, year 700-800.
Oh, and before I forget, we found this old lamp lying around. Since you've done such a sterling job, we'd like you to have it.

steps.player: Oh, random bits of tat, thank you very much.

steps.npc: You're welcome!

steps.text: You receive an old lamp.
If the player has no new quests to report:

steps.player: On second thoughts, you seem to have everything I know covered here!

steps.npc: No matter. I'm sure you'll find more. Look around the Museum, explore the city and maybe do some quests, and I'm sure you'll find out something worth telling.

steps.player: Yes, I'll go do some quests or something...

options.text: Tell me about other sections of the Museum.

steps.player: Tell me about other sections of the Museum.

steps.npc: I'd be delighted to; which areas are you interested in?

steps.player: Tell me about the Natural History exhibit.

steps.npc: Ahh, our newest expansion. The Natural History exhibit in the basement was set up to inform our citizens of the weird and wonderful diversity in our environment today. Indeed, I am sure you will recognise some of
the creatures down there. Hopefully, our lectures will teach you some things you didn't know about them!

steps.player: So where does the 'history' bit come in?

steps.npc: Ahh, I see. The 'history' refers to that of the species - it doesn't necessarily mean it's died out. After all, we have human history and we're still here!

steps.player: Tell me about the Dig Site exhibit.

steps.npc: Ahh, those. We're slowly filling them up with the help of people who have their Earth Sciences exams completed at the Dig Site. If you have, feel free to give us a hand. We'd appreciate it.

steps.player: Tell me about the Dig Site find cleaning area.

steps.npc: The cleaning area, yes. Well, we have some really good archaeologists on site right now. They're cleaning up the finds that are shipped over from the Dig Site to the east of here. If you have the right qualifications, you can help them clean the finds.
Level 3 Earth Science exams. You can take them over at the Exam Centre on the Dig Site.

steps.text: If the player has not passed the exams:

steps.npc: I'm sure you can get them easily enough. Just pop over to the Exam Centre on the Dig Site and speak to one of the examiners there.

steps.text: If the player has not yet taken the exams during The Dig Site quest:

steps.player: Oh, I'm already working towards those!

steps.npc: That's excellent. Keep up the good work and soon you'll be cleaning finds with the best of them.

steps.text: If the player has passed the exams:

steps.npc: That's excellent. If you feel like helping us out, pop downstairs and clean up some finds for us.

steps.player: Tell me about the Timeline exhibit.

steps.npc: Ahh, my speciality. Being a historian, matters of the past are my passion. Collated on this floor and the one above are just part of my life's work. I am still working on updating and finding out more everyday, so if you find
any information on your travels that may be useful, please do let me know.
You can follow the timeline of the history of Gielinor from the creation of the world to the present day, simply by walking around this display. A wondrous journey, I think you'll agree!

steps.player: Wow, that's a lot of information. I'm sure in my travels and quests I'll pick up a few bits of information for you.

options.text: Can you tell me why you're here?

steps.player: Can you tell me why you're here?

steps.npc: Of course. I plan to assist the forces of Saradomin who will come to our aid, and fight against the legions of vampyres that infest this foul place. These brave mercenaries shall need a guide.
When a guide arrives, I will aid the mercenary by holding their wealth for their eventual return. The mercenary will repay the guide by giving [him/her/them] a token for items which I am holding.
I shall give such items to the guide as payment for their services once I'm handed the token.
Oh, the range of items is very varied. Mercenaries tend to hold raw materials in high esteem and so will deposit those with me. They also seem to be good bartering items.
Generally, things like uncooked lobsters, coal, silver bars, bow strings. Things which are useful! Plus the odd tome of experience, which are considered incredibly useful.

standard-dialogue-after-darkness-of-hall.npc: Hello friend. What can I do for you?

options.text: Could you exchange my tokens for me?
options.condition: If the player has a reward token (Burgh de Rott Ramble) in their inventory

steps.player: Could you exchange my tokens for me?

steps.npc: No need, friend. You can do that yourself.

options.text: Do you know what these nail beast nails are used for?
options.condition: If the player has nail beast nails in their inventory

steps.player: Do you know what these nail beast nails are used for?

steps.npc: Hmmm, not really sure. They do look disgusting though..oh, actually, I remember some other adventurers taking some of these to Sanfew now...something about being able to make a potion with them.

steps.player: Ok, so perhaps Sanfew knows then?

steps.npc: Maybe. It's worth a try. Next time you're in Taverley, pop in and ask him. I think I remember some adventurers saying something about a serum though, some sort of potion that can be made with them.

options.text: Can you tell me why you're here?

steps.player: Can you tell me why you're here?

steps.npc: Of course. These mercenaries are here waiting for someone to take them down to Burgh de Rott. They want to do their bit against the vampyres.
I hold some items for these good hearted souls so that the guide can be recompensed when the job is done.

standard-dialogue-after-the-blood-moon-r.npc: Hello friend. What can I do for you?

options.text: Could you exchange my tokens for me?
options.condition: If the player has a reward token (Burgh de Rott Ramble) in their inventory

options.text: Do you know what these nail beast nails are used for?
options.condition: If the player has nail beast nails in their inventory

options.text: Can you tell me why you're here?

steps.player: Can you tell me why you're here?

steps.npc: Of course. Now that the vampyres are no longer a threat, these warriors are keen to test their mettle in the Theatre of Blood.
However, given they're not familiar with the area, they're waiting for someone to help guide them down to Burgh de Rott.
I hold some items for these good hearted souls so that the guide can be recompensed when the job is done.

using-items-on-hiylik-myna-using-nail-be.text: You show the priest the nail beast nails.

using-items-on-hiylik-myna-using-nail-be.player: Do you know what these are? Or what they're used for?

using-items-on-hiylik-myna-using-nail-be.npc: Hmmm, not really sure. They do look disgusting though..oh, actually, I remember some other adventurers taking some of these to Sanfew now...something about being able to make a potion with them.

using-items-on-hiylik-myna-using-nail-be.player: Ok, so perhaps Sanfew knows then?

using-items-on-hiylik-myna-using-nail-be.npc: Maybe? It's worth a try. Next time you're in Taverley, pop in and ask him. I think I remember some adventurers saying something about a serum though, some sort of potion that can be made with them.

using-items-on-hiylik-myna-using-a-rewar.text: You show the priest the token.

using-items-on-hiylik-myna-using-a-rewar.npc: Oh well done! Thank you for aiding our citizens.

standard.npc: This is private property! Please leave!

standard-dialogue-after-murder-mystery.npc: Thank you for all your help in solving the murder.

standard.npc: What? Oh, hello. I was deep in thought. Did you want me to show you the prices of weapons and armour?

steps.npc: Sorry, I'm just deep in thought. I'm waiting for many deals to complete today.

steps.player: What sort of things are you selling?

steps.npc: Good old weapons and armour! My people - dwarves, you understand - are hoping I can trade with humans.

steps.player: It looks like you've come to the right place for that.

steps.npc: I have indeed, my friend. Now, can I help you?

options.text: Yes, show me the prices of weapons and armour.
Yes, show me the prices of weapons and armour.

steps.player: Yes, show me the prices of weapons and armour.

steps.text: Grand Exchange: Weapons and Armour opens

options.text: Can you tell me about the bank's auto-charging services?

steps.player: Can you tell me about the bank's auto-charging services?

steps.npc: Hm? Oh, yes. If you don't want to charge your items yourself, you can have the bank attendant do it for you on withdrawal.

steps.player: How do they know how many charges to add?

steps.npc: You can tell them how many you would like for each item. Or if you'd like, I can let them know a minimum threshold for all items.

steps.prompt: Set a global minimum charge threshold?
Are you sure? Some charging resources may not be retrievable.

steps.player: I don't think that's necessary, but thank you for offering.

steps.npc: Alright then. Where was I...?
Thank you, I have much on my mind.
Wow, that's cheap.
Oh. That didn't sell so well.
Hmmm. If I spend twenty thousand on that, then...
Jackpot! I'm in the money now!
Hahaha! Trading the likes of which I have never seen.

standard.npc: Woooo wooo wooooo woooo

standard-dialogue-with-ghostspeak-amulet.npc: Oh how splendid! Every time I come back here I try to talk to people, but no one seems to understand.
I was telling my friend Bob this the other day in the afterlife. At least he can relate to the struggle of people not understanding.

standard-dialogue-with-ghostspeak-amulet.text: If the player has not completed Dragon Slayer II:

steps.npc: Yes, it really is.

standard-dialogue-with-ghostspeak-amulet.text: If the player has completed Dragon Slayer II:

steps.player: Wait a second. Your friend Bob... does he happen to be a cat?

steps.npc: Why, yes, he is! Do you know Bob?

steps.player: I do! How is he doing?

steps.npc: He's alright, all things considered. He did speak of a human friend he misses though. I suspect that's you.

steps.player: I miss him too. Could you tell him I said hi? And tell him I'm sorry he got killed. I wish I could have saved him.

steps.npc: I will tell him that you miss him. Regarding his death, he said it was necessary, so please don't feel bad about it.
He never explained why, only said that it had to be that way.

options.text: What can you tell me about Eve?

steps.player: What can you tell me about Eve?

steps.npc: Eve? One of the greatest witches I know. Also the oldest person I know. She's been around for practically forever.
It is said that when she was alive she was a hard working witch, mastering advanced spells at a very young age.
Unfortunately she died while still a young adult. That's why she looks so young now, despite being centuries old.

steps.player: How can she still be around after all these years?

steps.npc: Like I said, she mastered spells at a very young age. She took some of that magic with her into the afterlife.
The sad truth about Eve is that she spent all her life working and striving to achieve great things.
But she never got to relax and appreciate how far she had come. That is why she is so obsessed with partying now.

steps.player: I understand. That really makes you think, doesn't it.

steps.npc: Indeed. Enjoy the moment while you can, because you may not get another. Take it from me, I'm a ghost.
Goodbye.

standard.npc: Well hello. Beautiful day isn't it.
Just smell that sea air... beautiful.

standard-dialogue-after-starting-the-slu.npc: I don't know what to do without my boat.

standard.npc: Oh, hello.
Crossbows, are you interested?
Are they any good?! They're dwarven engineering at its best!

options.text: How do I make one for myself?

steps.player: How do I make one for myself?

steps.npc: Well, firstly you'll need to chop yourself some wood, then use a knife on the wood to whittle out a nice crossbow stock like these here.

Then get yourself some metal and a hammer and smith yourself some limbs for the bow, mind that you use the right metals and woods though as some wood is too light to use with some metal and vice versa.
Wood and Bronze as they're basic materials, Oak and Blurite, Willow and Iron, Steel and Teak, Mithril and Maple, Adamantite and Mahogany and finally Runite and Yew.

steps.player: Ok, so I have my stock and a pair of limbs... what now?

steps.npc: Simply take a hammer and smack the limbs firmly onto the stock. You'll then need a string, only they're not the same as normal bows. You'll need to dry some large animal's meat to get sinew, then spin that on a spinning
wheel, it's the only thing we've found to be strong enough for a crossbow.

Well.. I don't rightly know... us dwarves don't work with magic, we prefer gold and rock. Much more stable. I guess you could ask the humans at the rangers guild to see if they can do something but I don't want
anything to do with it!
Take care, straight shooting.
Take care, straight shooting.

You can smith yourself lots of different bolts, don't forget to flight them with feathers like you do arrows though. You can poison any untipped bolt but there's also the option of tipping them with gems then
enchanting them with runes. This can have some pretty powerful effects.

steps.player: Oh my poor bank, how will I store all those?!

steps.npc: Find Hirko in Keldagrim, he also sells crossbow parts and I'm sure he has something you can use to store bolts in.
Take care, straight shooting.

after-tower-of-life.player: Hi there, you mentioned something about creating monsters...?

after-tower-of-life.npc: Good! I gain know from alchemists and builders. Me make beings.

after-tower-of-life.player: Interesting. Tell me if I'm right. By the alchemists and builders creating you, you have inherited their combined knowledge in much the same way that a child might inherit the looks of their parents.
So what do you need me to do?

after-tower-of-life.npc: Inspect symbol of life altars around dungeon. You see item give. Use item on altar. Activate altar to create, you fight.

during-creature-creation.text: If the player does not have the correct ingredients:

steps.npc: You no haveee the two materials need.

during-creature-creation.text: If the player has the correct ingredients:

steps.npc: You haveee materials need. Here goes!

standard.npc: You here for the...stuff?
Look [miss/pal] I got the goods if you have the cash.
We talkin' the same language yet?

options.text: Yes, I am here for the stuff.

steps.npc: The sort of stuff you use in brewing.
The sort of stuff the Cooking Guild banned last year.
The sort of stuff that (if added to a vat of brewing ingredients just before the hops) has a higher chance of producin' a mature batch of whatever ale you wanted to make.
That sort of stuff.

steps.player: What was that bit about adding it to something?

steps.npc: I said, it's the sort of Stuff you add to a brewing vat after you have put the water and barley malt in.
THEN you add the sort of stuff I'm talking about, followed by the hops and the yeast.
Then, when whatever you are making brews it will have a higher chance of being a mature batch of ale.
That clear enough for you or am I going to have to start drawin' pictures on the wall of the hut?

options.text: Yes, I am here for the stuff.

steps.npc: Then sling yer 'ook!

standard.npc: What are you doing in our village, outlander?

steps.npc: Bah! Go down to the longhall, and there you will find excitement aplenty! Our finest warrior, Gunthor the Brave, will give you a rousing welcome!
Bah! You cannot hope to learn anything of us just by strolling through our village! We are an ancient tribe, our ways date back to the time before Avarrocka was founded!

steps.player: Would you care to tell me more?

steps.npc: Oh? You are not so ignorant as I thought. Very well, I shall speak of our tribe...

Our elders remember that about a century ago we were living in the lands far to the west. We were a large nomadic mountain tribe, settling wherever there was food, moving on when it had run out. As the tribe

grew larger, it was hard to find enough food for everyone, and we were forced to shift our camp more and more often. In time, a warrior called Gunnar took his friends and their families and left the larger tribe,
moving south in search of new places. They eventually settled here and built this village, finding that the old nomadic traditions were no longer needed.
Our current chieftain, Gunthor the Brave, is a direct- line descendent of Gunnar.

However, our ways have changed little in the last century. Although more and more people use magical powers, we do not believe it is wise to take upon oneself the power of the gods in this way. To this day, we fight

with the mighty sword, the vicious axe and the swift arrow on the wind. Some of our young, wishing to try so-called 'civilisation' and the softness of city life, abandon the tribe and move to the cities. It is sad to
see them go, but we do not prevent them; we live here in our village because we love this life - we do not force it on those whom it does not suit.
There, I have said enough.

steps.player: How do I get hold of a weasel?

steps.npc: Not with large quantities of rice and treacle as many people would have you believe. Besides, the Feldip weasel isn't technically a weasel, but, as is typical with any sort of colloquial name, it's been called that often enough

Anyway, the Feldip weasel's main survival technique is in hiding; other than that, it's pretty stupid. So, if you can actually find one, then you've probably got a fairly good chance of catching one.

steps.player: And how would I actually go about finding one?

steps.npc: The best place to start would probably be just south of here. You'll find lots of kebbit burrows there. Take a close look at some of them, follow the trails and you can't go far wrong.

options.text: I'd like to ask about another creature...
How can I improve my chances of making a capture?
Where can I get clothes and equipment like yours?
Well, seeing as you seem to like larupias so much...

steps.player: Well, seeing as you seem to like larupias so much...

steps.npc: Ah yes, yes, larupias are fun; just think of them as big kittens.

steps.player: Uh huh, big kittens that just want to rip your throat out!

steps.npc: Indeed, and you can use this to your advantage. If a larupia is keen to chase you then let it; that way you can happily lead it straight into your trap without any fuss or waiting around.

steps.player: Into what sort of trap should I lead it?

steps.npc: A pit trap should do you. There are some appropriate pits to the east of here that you can use. Cover one with a few logs and branches, tease the kitty and then lead it to the pit. Simple.

options.text: I'd like to ask about another creature...
How can I improve my chances of making a capture?
Where can I get clothes and equipment like yours?

steps.npc: They do sound interesting, don't they? Unfortunately, they're actually just another type of kebbit; those things get everywhere. Still, the tails of these particular kebbits can be useful for fishing.

steps.player: So, how would I go about catching one them?

steps.npc: Just squash them with a boulder, quick and simple.

steps.player: What, you mean just pick up some boulders and start throwing them at kebbits? That doesn't sound simple.

steps.npc: No silly, you let the creature squash itself. Just use some sticks to hold a boulder in a nice precarious position, place some bait underneath and let the creature knock itself out.

options.text: I'd like to ask about another creature...
How can I improve my chances of making a capture?
Where can I get clothes and equipment like yours?
What on earth is a chinchompa?

steps.player: What on earth is a chinchompa?

steps.npc: Awwww, chinchompas are great. They're highly volatile little balls of fluff. Cute as you like, but for some reason they do have this tendency to spontaneously combust.
Probably something to do with the fact they'll eat anything and everything, especially spicy food.
Anyways, if you want to capture a chinchompa, I suggest using a box trap. That way, if the little fluffball does explode, then at least most of the blast will be contained within the box.

options.text: I'd like to ask about another creature...
How can I improve my chances of making a capture?
Where can I get clothes and equipment like yours?
Somehow butterflies don't strike me as your sort of thing.

steps.player: Somehow butterflies don't strike me as your sort of thing.

steps.npc: Not really, but some people like them. The ones around here are at least vaguely interesting, though. The black ones are supposedly magical butterflies.

steps.player: Doesn't that make them harder to catch?

steps.npc: Not particularly; you can still catch them using an ordinary butterfly net. Oh, and you'll probably need some butterfly jars in which to keep them as well.

options.text: I'd like to ask about another creature...
How can I improve my chances of making a capture?
Where can I get clothes and equipment like yours?
How can I improve my chances of making a capture?

steps.player: How can I improve my chances of making a capture?

steps.npc: There are four key factors that will affect your chances: what bait you use, how close to the trap you are, your appearance and your smell.

Unfortunately, creatures don't just jump into traps for the fun of it nearly as often as we as Hunters might like. However, it is possible to improve those odds. If you can find the right bait to use on your trap,
something your prey really craves, then hunger overrides fear and the creature is just that little bit more likely to bounce to its furry little doom.

steps.text: other

options.text: Why is it important how close I am to the trap?

steps.player: Why is it important how close I am to the trap?

steps.npc: However well you might be blending in, if you're standing with your nose pressed right up against your own trap, the poor little critters ain't going to go anywhere near it. So, you need to make sure you put
a sensible distance - I'd say at least four strides - between yourself and your trap.

steps.text: other

options.text: Why would the creatures care about my appearance?

steps.player: Why would the creatures care about my appearance?

steps.npc: You're a human. From the point of view of a lot of creatures, you're big and scary. So, it'd be best if the furry little monsters didn't notice you. You need to blend in like the creatures themselves.

steps.player: And how do I do that?

steps.npc: Easy, dress up like one of them. Even easier, dress up using the furs of the creatures themselves; then you're bound to get the colour right. And, I suppose, if you don't fancy just slinging a dead fur over your
shoulders, you can probably get them made into something more appealing. I hear there are tailors in Varrock who are good at that sort of thing.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: I'm sure there's nothing wrong with your smell...from a human point of view. But to your prey, any trap that you've set up will reek of human, and that's going to work against you if you don't do anything about it.

You need to mask that lovely human scent of yours with something else. Smoke works well. Take a lit torch and waft it around the trap a bit. You'll quickly overpower most of the other smells around the trap.

steps.text: other

options.text: Where can I get clothes and equipment like yours?

steps.player: Where can I get clothes and equipment like yours?

steps.npc: Well, the equipment isn't too hard to get hold of. You've got specialist shops like Aleck's in Yanille that'll see you right. He's a bit pricey, mind, but it's pretty decent kit.
The clothing is a tad trickier to get hold of, the materials required being rather difficult to seperate from their reluctant owners.
But, if you can get the furs, there are shops like the tailor's in east Varrock that can help you.

options.text: I think I'll give it a miss right now.

steps.player: I think I'll give it a miss right now, thanks.

steps.npc: Suit yourself!
What's a larupia? You don't know? You mean you really don't recognise the significance of these clothes I'm wearing?

steps.player: Well, they're certainly decorative...what about them?

steps.npc: Well, these are the furs from a larupia. Caught the creature myself I did, and these make me blend in better, see?
If you want to be successful as a hunter you've got to be as stealthy as a kyatt, as quiet as a mouse and blend in like a, well, like a larupia, I guess!

standard.player: What is this cave here for?

standard.speaker: Hunting expert
standard.text: Ah, a few of the most hunted creatures around here have been captured and secured in this cave to allow the most esteemed hunters to catch them with ease.
If the player has completed the hard tier of the Western Provinces achievement diary:

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Yes, you can. Head inside to hunt in peace.

standard.text: If the player has not completed the hard tier of the Western Provinces achievement diary:

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
