standard-dialogue-attempting-to-enter-th.speaker: Hunting expert
standard-dialogue-attempting-to-enter-th.text: Sorry, but only those who've completed the hard set of the Western Provinces tasks may enter my private hunting ground.

standard.speaker: Hunting expert
standard.text: Ah, this is a wonderful area for a spot of hunting, don't you think?

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Oh absolutely; there's a huge variety of creatures to catch around here. You've got butterflies, polar kebbits, sabre-toothed kebbits, birds and even kyatts! Surely one of those piques your interest?

options.text: Where would I find polar kebbits?

steps.player: Where would I find polar kebbits?

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Funnily enough, you've just put your finger right on the problem. With polar kebbits, finding them is the hardest part! You'll have to track them down.

steps.player: How would I go about doing that, then?

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: The easiest way to get started is by looking somewhere you can be sure a kebbit will have been and then working from there. You see the holes around here leading down into the ice? They're kebbit burrows!

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: You'll be hard pressed to catch a polar kebbit in its home, but if you search around the entrance to a burrow then you might be able to find a trail.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Now, kebbit trails are usually fairly easy to follow once you've found them, but if the trail does peter out, you should try inspecting the surrounding scenery for clues as to where the creature may have gone.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Good places to look for clues include hollow logs in which the kebbit may have hidden or vegetation which may have been chewed or damaged.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: There are also tunnels running through the ice here that the kebbits use, so you should check those out as well.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: What's more, these tunnels can often help to shelter a trail from further snow, making it even easier for you to pick them up again.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Eventually, of course, the kebbit will have probably hidden somewhere. Polar kebbits don't hang about in the open for long for fear of their natural predators.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: If you suspect a kebbit is close by, try looking around for signs of disturbed snow. Polar kebbits will often bury themselves in snow drifts as a means of hiding.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: If you think you've found a kebbit, use a noose wand to haul the creature out from the snow.

steps.player: Wow, that's quite a lot to remember.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Don't worry; if you find yourself struggling to follow a trail, just come and ask me and I'll see if I can help.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: But remember, the best place to start is by searching around their burrows.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Ah, you can get cunning little bird snares for just that. You should be able to find them in specialist Hunter shops. Try to lay them in fairly open areas with lots of birds.

steps.player: Do I need to place any bait on these traps?

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: No, that's not necessary. The idea is that the bird will see the trap as somewhere to perch. If the bird lands on the trigger stick, it should drop away and a small loop of wire should close around the bird's feet.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: And remember, it's important to collect any captures from your traps fairly quickly; otherwise, you risk losing them to various wild scavengers.

options.text: I'd like to ask about another creature.
How can I improve my chances of capturing a creature?

steps.player: How can I improve my chances of capturing a creature?

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Ah, the key there is concealment, both of yourself and your traps.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: The most obvious point is to stay out of sight of your own traps. If possible, hide around a wall, hedge or similar. Failing that, make sure you're a good few feet away from your trap.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: You can hide yourself even better by wearing clothing appropriate to the area in which you are hunting.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Your best bet is to use the skins of creatures native to the area. There is a very good tailor in east Varrock who may be able to help you with making clothing out of such skins.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Finally, a lot of creatures may avoid your traps if they can smell a human scent on them. This is where smoking a trap can be useful.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: It takes a bit of practice, but by using the smoke from a torch, you can mask any other scents that may surround a trap.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: You're welcome, good luck with the hunting.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: That depends entirely on the butterfly.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: I'll admit that the activities of many butterflies may be of no interest at all. However, we are lucky in having around here some fine examples of rare thaumic butterflies.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: These butterflies reputedly have magical powers that, when released, can make a person stronger or heal otherwise critical wounds.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: At this point, I should offer a note of caution, however: it is also said that these powers will not manifest themselves if the butterflies are captured for selfish purposes.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Rather, they are gifts that must be used by one person to aid another. Of course, you'll have to catch them first.

steps.player: And how do I do that?

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Why, with a butterfly net of course! You should also carry some empty butterfly jars with you in which to keep the butterflies.

options.text: I'd like to ask about another creature.
How can I improve my chances of capturing a creature?
How can I capture a sabre-toothed kebbit?

steps.player: How can I capture a sabre-toothed kebbit?

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Ah, now for these creatures I would recommend using a deadfall trap. Deadfalls are quite easy to set up, and yet you can catch some very reasonably sized creatures with them.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Deadfall traps basically work by having a large dead weight, such as a boulder, positioned so as to be delicately balanced above some form of bait.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: You will need to make sure you have a knife and some wood with you to create appropriate supports and a trigger for this sort trap.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: In the case of sabre-toothed kebbits you should use some form of raw meat to bait your trap, but other animals may prefer other baits, such as fish or vegetables.

options.text: I'd like to ask about another creature.
How can I improve my chances of capturing a creature?

steps.player: Oooh, kyatts sounds interesting. I want to catch one of those.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Well, you've set your sights high, kyatts are incredibly fearsome creatures, but with determination like that I'm sure you'll make it.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Now, you're not going to be able to catch a kyatt with just a small box or a noose on a stick. You need a much bigger trap.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Pit traps are a good bet. You'd be best off finding a natural dip in the ground as the basis for your trap. If you dig a pit yourself, you risk creatures noticing the disturbed ground nearby.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Once you've found an appropriate spot, you'll need some logs and a knife. The logs serve two purposes.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Some can be carved into sharp skewers for the bottom of the pit; hopefully the kyatt will die when it falls onto these. Others can be used to conceal the trap.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Of course, even then the pit is going to look suspicious, so you're going to need to lure the kyatt onto the branches in some way. What actually tends to work best for this is, well, yourself!

steps.player: What? I don't like the sound of that.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Yes, that's the normal response, but I kid you not. If you really want a kyatt to follow you over that pit then just give it a good poke!

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Of course, I suggest you use something long to poke it with. Poking a kyatt with your finger is likely to end in unfortunate limb loss.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Fortunately, you can get very good sticks for poking from most Hunter shops.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Once you have...got the creature's attention, try to lead it to one of your traps. Make sure to jump the branches when you reach the trap yourself, of course; it would be embarrassing to fall into your own trap.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Then, if the kyatt is giving you all of its attention, hopefully it won't notice the trap, and with any luck, it will stumble right into the pit.

steps.player: That sounds a bit hit or miss, and kind of suicidal too!

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Well that's what makes it exciting, isn't it? But honestly, if you want to capture a kyatt, that's your best bet.

How can I improve my chances of capturing a creature?
Can you teach me how to hunt?

steps.player: Can you teach me how to hunt?

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Why certainly. I reached the peak of my abilities some time ago, but I'm more than happy to help newcomers to the field. Was there anything in particular you had in mind?

options.text: Where's the best place to start?

steps.player: Where's the best place to start?

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: I always say a good starting point is to learn how to follow the creatures you want to capture. Around here, that means practicing on polar kebbits.

steps.player: So how do I track them down, then?

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: The easiest way to get started is by looking somewhere you can be sure a kebbit will have been and then working from there. You see the holes around here leading down into the ice? They're kebbit burrows!

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: You'll be hard pressed to catch a polar kebbit in its home, but if you search around the entrance to a burrow then you might be able to find a trail.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Now, kebbit trails are usually fairly easy to follow once you've found them, but if the trail does peter out, you should try inspecting the surrounding scenery for clues as to where the creature may have gone.

options.text: What sort of creatures are there to hunt around here?

steps.player: What sort of creatures are there to hunt around here?

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Well, there's pretty much anything you could want to hunt. You've got butterflies, polar kebbits, sabre-toothed kebbits, birds and even kyatts! Surely one of those interests you?

options.text: Where would I find polar kebbits?
How can I capture a sabre-toothed kebbit?
How can I improve my chances of capturing a creature?
Sorry, I'm not that keen on hunting.

steps.player: Sorry, I'm not that keen on hunting.

steps.speaker: Hunting expert
steps.text: Really? What a shame, you looked like someone who could have had some promise.

standard.npc: A crossbow, are you interested?

options.text: How do I make one for myself?

steps.player: How do I make one for myself?

steps.npc: Well, firstly you'll need to chop yourself some wood, then use a knife on the wood to whittle out a nice crossbow stock like these here.

Then get yourself some metal and a hammer and smith yourself some limbs for the bow, mind that you use the right metals and woods though as some wood is too light to use with some metal and vice versa.
Wood and Bronze as they're basic materials, Oak and Blurite, Willow and Iron, Steel and Teak, Mithril and Maple, Adamantite and Mahogany and finally Runite and Yew.

steps.player: Ok, so I have my stock and a pair of limbs... what now?

steps.npc: Simply take a hammer and smack the limbs firmly onto the stock. You'll then need a string, only they're not the same as normal bows. You'll need to dry some large animal's meat to get sinew, then spin that on a spinning
wheel, it's the only thing we've found to be strong enough for a crossbow.

Well.. I don't rightly know... us dwarves don't work with magic, we prefer gold and rock. Much more stable. I guess you could ask the humans at the rangers guild to see if they can do something but I don't want
anything to do with it!
Take care, straight shooting.
Take care, straight shooting.

You can smith yourself lots of different bolts, don't forget to flight them with feathers like you do arrows though. You can poison any untipped bolt but there's also the option of tipping them with gems then
enchanting them with runes. This can have some pretty powerful effects.

steps.npc: Horology is the study and measurement of time. Specifically, I study how time and dates have been historically recorded.
For example, the date convention in Great Kourend is to state the number of days and decades since the signing of the Royal Accord of Twill.

steps.player: Days and decades? That's a bit confusing.

steps.npc: Yes, it's an interesting convention. Truth be told, most in the kingdom prefer to use the same date format as you'll find used elsewhere.
However, as this is the Historical Archive, we stick to the dates used historically within Kourend.

options.text: Tell me more about the Royal Accord of Twill.

steps.player: Tell me more about the Royal Accord of Twill.

steps.npc: The Royal Accord of Twill was signed by the rulers of each of the houses 139 decades ago, following the great famine.
The Accord declared that each house will, in turn, rule the Kingdom of Great Kourend for one decade in rotation, based on lots drawn.

steps.text: If the player has not completed A Kingdom Divided:

steps.npc: You may find a book in the Grand Library with further information. Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: Is the Royal Accord of Twill still honoured today?

steps.player: Is the Royal Accord of Twill honoured today?

steps.npc: Our kingdom has advanced somewhat over the many decades since the Accord. Though some parts of the Accord remain intact, the Kourend Council now rules Great Kourend.
Indeed it was. In the 13th decade, King Shayzien III seized control of Kourend using the military under his command.
The full set of laws within the Accord haven't been followed since. However, some of them were reinstated in the 47th decade, by King Byrne I.

steps.player: Fascinating. What happened during that time?

steps.npc: During the 20th decade, King Shayzien VI married the daughter of Lord Hosidius. Four decades later their son was crowned king.
He took the name King Hosidius IV in an attempt to distance the family from the breaking of the Royal Accord of Twill.
King Hosidius IV followed by his son, King Hosidius V ruled Kourend until the early days of the 33rd decade.
It was then that King Shayzien VII took control of the kingdom. His rule was a notably violent one.
King Shayzien VII was killed some five decades later during the Battle of the Concourse. He was succeeded by the dark mage, Xeric.
Xeric ruled Kourend for more than ten dark decades using an army of lizardmen. This time period was known as the Age of Strife.
Xeric was eventually killed during the 47th decade and succeeded by King Byrne I.

steps.player: Can you tell me more about Xeric?

steps.npc: Ah, I do not have much more information on him. You should speak to Ektheme, our Xerician expert.

steps.text: If the player has completed A Kingdom Divided:

steps.npc: The Royal Accord of Twill no longer plays much part in the rulership of Kourend. It was breached in the 13th decade when King Shayzien III seized control of the kingdom. It hasn't been honoured since.
That said, it was the basis for Rose's Accord, which sets out how the kingdom is currently ruled today. As decreed in Rose's Accord, the Hosidius family are now the royal family of Kourend.

We have the original Royal Accord of Twill safely stored here. Although it's not available for public viewing, there are copies available within the Grand Library. Is there anything else I can help you with?

standard-dialogue-carrying-2.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-carrying-2.text: Master says move this rock, move that rock. I said no, much more fun to smash 'em. Master didn't like that. Kicked me into lava. I obey for now.

standard-dialogue-carrying-2.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-carrying-2.text: One day I get big revenge. Masters lair will be mine!

standard-dialogue-carrying-2.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-carrying-2.text: Methinks redecorate. More cages, more skulls.

standard-dialogue-carrying-2.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-carrying-2.text: Of course! You not like yours? Make donation?

standard-dialogue-carrying-3.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-carrying-3.text: Urgh... So... Heavy... But toiling makes me big and strong like master, yes?

standard-dialogue-carrying-overhead.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-carrying-overhead.text: Where did I need to take this?

standard-dialogue-carrying-overhead.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-carrying-overhead.text: Can't wait to start smashing again...

standard-dialogue-carrying-overhead.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-carrying-overhead.text: If I deliver this in time, master won't give me the hoof!

standard-dialogue-carrying-overhead.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-carrying-overhead.text: So much to do. So little time.

standard-dialogue-carrying-overhead.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-carrying-overhead.text: Must work hard... Mustn't get clobbered...

standard-dialogue-carrying-overhead.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-carrying-overhead.text: Me remember everything, me not forget faces.

standard-dialogue-carrying-overhead.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-carrying-overhead.text: Did I pick up the right relic?

standard-dialogue-tinkering-1.speaker: Imps
standard-dialogue-tinkering-1.text: Hey, you're hitting my half of the relic!

standard-dialogue-tinkering-1.speaker: Imps
standard-dialogue-tinkering-1.text: So that's my half! That's what!

standard-dialogue-tinkering-1.speaker: Imps
standard-dialogue-tinkering-1.text: If it's your half, why am I hitting it?

standard-dialogue-tinkering-1.speaker: Imps
standard-dialogue-tinkering-1.text: Grrrrr! I hate working with you.

standard-dialogue-tinkering-1.speaker: Imps
standard-dialogue-tinkering-1.text: Maybe you go take a break, then I can smash the whole thing!

standard-dialogue-tinkering-1.player: What you two need is some conflict resolution!

standard-dialogue-tinkering-1.speaker: Imps
standard-dialogue-tinkering-1.text: Yeah! Keep your eyes off our relic!

standard-dialogue-tinkering-2.speaker: Imps
standard-dialogue-tinkering-2.text: This looks so much better already!

standard-dialogue-tinkering-3.speaker: Imps
standard-dialogue-tinkering-3.text: We can flickedy flam these stones better than anyone else! A-boom-boom-boom!

standard-dialogue-tinkering-3.speaker: Imps
standard-dialogue-tinkering-3.text: Do you feel the rhythm? Start dancing, human!

steps.text: The player performs the dance emote.

steps.speaker: Imps
steps.text: Wow, terrible!

steps.speaker: Imps
steps.text: Worst moves me ever see!

steps.player: Absolutely no way am I dancing for you!

steps.speaker: Imps
steps.text: Grrr.

steps.speaker: Imps
steps.text: We make you dance one day, somehow...

steps.speaker: Imps
steps.text: Me know humans don't like pointy sticks!

steps.speaker: Imps
steps.text: Ooh yes, we prod them good!

standard-dialogue-reading-1.player: Hi there little fella, what's on that scroll?

standard-dialogue-reading-2.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-reading-2.text: D - E - Z - Y - O - G - T - O - N.

standard-dialogue-reading-2.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-reading-2.text: Dezyogton? What's that mean? Me too stupid to read.

standard-dialogue-reading-2.player: Can I take a look at that scroll?
Terrible handwriting, I can see why you're struggling.

standard-dialogue-reading-2.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-reading-2.text: Struggling? Me's a foolish little imp! Of course me struggle!

standard-dialogue-reading-2.player: It says destruction of the mortal mind.

standard-dialogue-reading-2.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-reading-2.text: It does? What else does it say? Keep reading.

standard-dialogue-reading-2.player: Erm... In full, it says that reading this scroll will cause destruction of the mortal mind.

standard-dialogue-reading-2.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-reading-2.text: Oh really? That's not good! You probably shouldn't have read it! Teehee!

standard-dialogue-reading-2.player: It also says that I stink?

standard-dialogue-reading-3.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-reading-3.text: Sitting by the fire, reading my favourite scroll, this is the life!

standard-dialogue-reading-3.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-reading-3.text: It's called 'an introduction to flaying'. I like the pictures.

standard-dialogue-reading-overhead.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-reading-overhead.text: This is pointless. I should be stealing things.

standard-dialogue-reading-overhead.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-reading-overhead.text: I'll throw this into lava soon...

standard-dialogue-reading-overhead.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-reading-overhead.text: Argh. I can't make sense of these symbols!

standard-dialogue-reading-overhead.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-reading-overhead.text: Do I really need to be able to read?

standard-dialogue-jumping-1.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-jumping-1.text: Hop! Hop! Take that you stupid rock!

standard-dialogue-jumping-2.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-jumping-2.text: Me wrecky relic! Me wrecky relic! Hahaha!

standard-dialogue-jumping-overhead.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-jumping-overhead.text: Oh no, is the relic starting to break? Oops!

standard-dialogue-jumping-overhead.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-jumping-overhead.text: I can jump higher than you all!

standard-dialogue-dying-in-yama-s-lair-f.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-dying-in-yama-s-lair-f.text: Gratz on your Nightmare Mode loss

standard-dialogue-dying-in-yama-s-lair-f.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-dying-in-yama-s-lair-f.text: Seriously, you died to a 1? Eat a cabbage next time, then you might survive. Yuck.

standard-dialogue-imp-in-a-box-2.player: Hey imp, can you hear me?

standard-dialogue-imp-in-a-box-2.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-imp-in-a-box-2.text: Of course I can hear ya, ya great big ape. You know, 'veres not even enuf space to swing Bob about in 'ere. How about a breather? You know, stretch me pins for a bit?

options.text: No, I'm going to keep you in there.

steps.player: No, I'm going to keep you in there. I might keep you as a pet.

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Pet!! Nah mate. I fink you'd find dat you'd be my pet!! We is not makin good pets.

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Coz...errr...

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: We bite! Yeah we is biting and...and...er...

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: We is fire risk! Yeah dat's it! We be burning down your housey and stealin' all ya shiny gems. Oh, and da beads!! Mmmm, beads.

steps.player: Fire risk? How does that work?

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Is those wizzies. Dey don't like de imps so dey make us go BOOOM!!

steps.player: It's not that bad. You've got four big windows, charming company...er...

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Yeah, we's love tiny, crampt space. It be magical. But I is a busy imp, innit? Dragons needin' ticklin', shiny relics needin' stealin', you know how it goes.

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: So, if you's know whas good for ya, you'd be lettin' me go, right?
other

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Nah, mate. Dunno what you're chirpin' about.

steps.player: Well, you're a magical creature aren't you? Surely I get some wishes for capturing you, or releasing you, or something?

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: I'm finking dat you be a bit confoosed. I is an imp, not some namby-pamby genie or some kinda fairy. Ye can tell by the horns.

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Sayin' dat, I don't fancy being cooped up like one of me uncle's pigeons. Tell you what, is there anything you need deliverin' to the bank? I may not be no cunjerer or sommink like dat, but I can get about nice

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: an quick like. If you let me scarper, I'll take a couple of fings to the bank for ya. You game?

options.text: Surely it should be three items?

steps.player: Surely it should be three items? Then it's one item per wish.

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: I've already told ya, I ain't no bloomin' fairy. Besides, you know wot dey say, three's a crowd innit? I don't fink I can hop about carryin' more dan 2 fings.
other

options.text: I've got nothing I need banking right now.

steps.player: I've got nothing I need banking right now.

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Great, just blinkin great, dat is. I'll just sit about countin' zombie sheep then. One...two...two and a bit...three and a bit more... I don't fink sheep 'ave dat many legs...

standard-dialogue-imp-in-a-box-1.player: Hey imp, are you still there?

standard-dialogue-imp-in-a-box-1.speaker: Imp
standard-dialogue-imp-in-a-box-1.text: An who's fault is that, eh? EH? I got betta fings to do dan sit ere waitin' for ya. 'Ave ya made up ya mind what else I'm luggin about?

options.text: No, I'm afraid you're going to have to wait a bit longer.

steps.player: No, I'm afraid you're going to have to wait a bit longer.

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Dat's alright guv'nor. I'll get back to me luvverly dream about beads. Big shiny beads. Love it!

steps.text: What use would that be in a bank? You'd be better off leaving it in yer house.

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Ow! That's hot! Put it in yer bank yerself!

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit a looting bag:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: No way, I can't bank your looting bag.

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit a bloated toad:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Nope, between me and you, that toad doesn't look stable.

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit a book of knowledge:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: What good is banking that book? Just read it or throw it away!

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit a glowing fungus:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: I'm no expert, but when a mushroom glows that much, I'm guessing it's dangerous. Keep it away from me.

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit a gnomeball:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: I'm not touching a gnome ball; that's a vicious game! I might die!

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit Karamjan rum:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Don't you know? You can get into trouble for giving alcohol to minors, and I'm pretty small, it has to be said.

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit skeletal gorilla bones:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: There's something weird about those bones; I ain't touching them.

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit a stick:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: It's a flipping stick; why bother banking that? You humans are crazy sometimes.

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit a lamp:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: I know what lamps like that contain; I'm not touching it. I might get hurt.

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit an unholy symbol:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Sorry, I'm not going to risk upsetting someone by bundling random holy symbols I don't recognise into bank vaults.

attempting-to-bank-unbankable-items.text: If the player attempts to deposit Ana in a barrel:

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: Hey, if she wants to use the bank, why can't she use her own two legs? Besides, she's too big.

standard-dialogue.text: If the information clerk has rewards for the player:

steps.npc: Ohh, hello there, I see from our records that you've helped us out a bit, and I'd love to give you a bit of a reward for that.
My father knew a lot about Prayer, Mining, Crafting, Smithing, Slayer and Hunter, and I learnt some of his tricks... would you like me to share a little of my knowledge?

options.text: Yes, teach me something in those skills.

steps.player: Yes, teach me something in those skills.

steps.text: If the player has between 51-100 Kudos:
You feel more knowledgeable in the Mining skill.
If the player has between 101-150 Kudos:
You feel more knowledgeable in the skills Mining and Crafting
If the player has over 150 Kudos, and has claimed the previous rewards:
You feel more knowledgeable in the skills Crafting, Smithing, Slayer, Prayer and Hunter.
If the player has over 150 Kudos, but has not claimed any of the previous rewards:
You feel more knowledgeable in the skills Mining, Crafting, Smithing, Slayer, Prayer and Hunter.

steps.npc: You're most welcome. Now, is there anything else I can help you with?

steps.text: continue

steps.npc: Okay!

standard-dialogue.text: If the information clerk does not have any rewards for the player:

steps.npc: Welcome to Varrock Museum. How can I help you today?

steps.text: continue

options.text: Take a map of the Museum

steps.text: You reach and take a map of the Museum.
museum map

options.text: Find out about the Dig Site exhibit.

steps.player: Could you tell me about the Dig Site exhibit please?

steps.npc: Of course. The Dig Site exhibit has several display cases of finds discovered on the Dig Site to the east of Varrock.

steps.text: If the player has not completed The Dig Site quest:

steps.npc: Unfortunately, you haven't passed your Earth Science exams, so you aren't qualified to help us on the dig. If you're interested, visit the Education Centre on the Dig Site to the east and talk to the examiners there.

steps.text: If the player has completed The Dig Site quest, but has not helped with the exhibit:

steps.npc: As you've passed your Earth Science exams at the Dig Site, you can go through into the cleaning area and clean off some finds. This will help our Dig Site display floor to give a more accurate view of life back in the
3rd and 4th Ages, as well as earning you Kudos. If you'd like to know more about cleaning finds, just ask the archaeologists.

steps.text: If the player has completed The Dig Site quest, and has partially completed the exhibit:

steps.npc: I see you've already helped out in the Dig Site exhibit. Our picture of life back in the 3rd and 4th Ages in that old city is really becoming clearer. There are still a few displays that need updating, though. If you'd like to
know more about cleaning finds, just ask the archaeologists.

steps.text: If the player has completed The Dig Site quest, and has completed the exhibit:

steps.npc: You have really helped out a lot. I see all the nice clean finds with their information are in the once empty cases. I'm sure we'll get some more cases in soon for you to fill. For now, perhaps you should investigate the
rest of the Museum.
Have a good day!

options.text: Find out about the Timeline exhibit.

steps.player: Could you tell me about the Timeline exhibit please?

steps.npc: Why, yes. The Timeline exhibit has lots of display cases showing things from the beginning of time right up to the present day.

steps.text: If the player has not contributed to the timeline exhibit:

steps.npc: You could help out in the Timeline exhibit upstairs. By providing information you may have gathered on your travels around the world, you can help to make our displays more comprehensive and earn yourself Kudos
too.

steps.text: If the player has contributed to the timeline exhibit:

steps.npc: I know you've helped out a bit in the Timeline exhibit upstairs, but I'm sure you can help more. When you're out on your travels being a brave adventurer, remember that you can come back to the Museum
after some quests to let us know important historical facts. This will help us to update the displays and make the Museum a more informative place! You'll earn yourself Kudos too.

steps.text: If the player has completed timeline exhibit:

steps.npc: I see you have filled up the display cases we have, and given us large amounts of information for the Timeline exhibit. At the moment, you have left us nothing to do ourselves, but I'm sure we'll be getting some new cases
in soon for you to help us out with! For now, perhaps you should investigate the rest of the Museum.

steps.player: Okay, thanks. One more question: why are the display numbers all out of sequence?

steps.npc: Ahh, that's due to the numbering being done as we were constructing the cases and putting the displays in them, then shuffling them into the right places. We thought rather than renumbering them all - such a
boring job, writing labels - we'd leave it. They all have unique numbers and future displays would mess up the consecutive numbering anyway.

options.text: Find out about the Natural History exhibit.

steps.player: Could you tell me about the Natural History exhibit please?

steps.npc: Why, yes. The Natural History exhibit has displays of various creatures you can find around Gielinor.

steps.text: If the player has not corrected any of the display cases:

steps.npc: Downstairs, in the Natural History exhibit, you can answer quizzes about animals to show us your knowledge and earn Kudos at the same time. Talk to Orlando, I'm sure he'd appreciate your knowledge.

steps.text: If the player has completed at least one display case:

steps.npc: I see you have already demonstrated some of your knowledge of the natural world in the Natural History exhibit, so why not pop down and do some more quizzes with Orlando! You can earn Kudos at the same time.

steps.text: If the player has corrected all of the display cases:

steps.npc: You really know your stuff when it comes to animals, don't you! Orlando tells me you have exceeded his teachings. For now, perhaps you should investigate the rest of the Museum.

options.text: But what's Natural History got to do with existing animals?

steps.player: But what's natural history got to do with existing animals?

steps.npc: The study of natural history is simply the study of the history of the species. The species doesn't necessarily need to be an extinct one.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Kudos is a measure of how much you've assisted the Museum. The more information you give us, Dig Site finds that you clean and quizzes you solve, the higher your Kudos.

Well, recently we found a rather interesting island to the north of Morytania. We believe that it may be of archaeological significance. I suspect we'll be looking for qualified archaeologists once we have constructed our
canal and barge. So, we're using Kudos as a measure of who is willing and able to help us here at the Museum, so they can then be invited on our dig on the new island.

steps.text: If the player does not have enough Kudos:

steps.npc: Unfortunately, you haven't earned enough Kudos yet, so you aren't qualified to help us on the dig. If you're interested in helping us out and getting that Kudos, simply help out around the Museum.

steps.text: If the player has enough Kudos:

steps.npc: Why yes! You've helped us so much around the Museum and you have the necessary qualifications from the Earth Sciences exams you took. When the canal is ready, we'll let you know.

steps.player: Thank you, I'll look forward to it!

Me too.

steps.text: other

The substance. It's almost like taking a finger off a human and assuming it will stay alive I guess. The sample sort of... goes inert once we take the sample from the main body of the pool.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Yes, we've had a bit of progress there. We've tried adding in a lot of things with varying results. The accident was the best though.

steps.text: Irene looks embarassed.

steps.npc: Well, I slipped and dropped a fossilised leg bone from something in the pool. It... well it kind of ate it away.

Oh yes, it was quite interesting. It's as if it restored some of the biological content of the bone and stripped all the mineralisation of fosilisation away. The bone was, rather floppy though. Like when you remove all the
calcium and phosphate from it.

steps.player: Have you tried putting calcium in the pool?

steps.npc: Calcium and phosphate are highly reactive - you'd never find just those in any quantity! You could maybe find some within minerals around this island that could work.

steps.npc: When you play as an Iron[man/woman], you do everything for yourself. You don't trade with other players, or take their items, or accept their help.
As an Iron[man/woman], you choose to have these restrictions imposed on you, so everyone knows you're doing it properly.
If you think you have what it takes, you can choose to become a Hardcore Iron[man/woman].

In addition to the standard restrictions, Hardcore Iron[man/woman] only have one life. In the event of a dangerous death, your Hardcore Iron[man/woman] status will be downgraded to that of a standard Iron[man/woman], and your
stats will be frozen on the Hardcore Iron[man/woman] hiscores.
For the ultimate challenge, you can choose to become an Ultimate Iron[man/woman], a game mode inspired by the player IronNoBank.
In addition to the standard restrictions, Ultimate Iron[man/woman] are blocked from using the bank, and they drop all their items when they die.
You're a standard Iron[man/woman]. You can downgrade yourself to a normal player if you like.

standard.player: Hey, what do you do here?

standard.npc: I help the main man over there. He can get a bit cantankerous. Every now and then he'll just start attacking people without warning. I act as a sort of home help...

standard.player: Yes, yes, I know the sort...full of themselves aren't they.

standard.npc: Exactly! They come in all, 'Have at thee! ' and 'Death to you evil one', it's all a bit too dramatic for me to be honest.
Anyway, he'll often end up getting killed and nothing get's done around the house while he's awaiting his mortal return.
Well, it's kind of interesting the first few times, but it's like falling off a bike...

standard.player: What, you graze your knees a lot?

standard.npc: I was going to say that you soon get fed-up with it. I guess it's one of those perks of the job though, ability to raise yourself from the dead.
You'd think he'd do better things with a gift like that, but all he tends to do is get angry at people who come into his house without being invited and then he's off again 'raising the dead'.

I don't know if that's true... I think the ents would stop any monsters! But mummy and daddy get all grumpy if I don't listen.

steps.npc: This is the Library Historical Archive. Here you'll find historical documents and texts from all eras of Great Kourend's history, dating all the way back to the first decade.

steps.player: What can you tell me about the Wintertodt?

steps.npc: The Wintertodt, or the Winter beast as it was often known at the time, terrorised northern Kourend for five decades.
Logios is currently studying the Wintertodt Invasion, and we have various texts from that era.

options.text: What can you tell me about Mount Quidamortem?

steps.player: What can you tell me about Mount Quidamortem?

steps.npc: Our first records of the mountain date back to the 36th decade where a Shayzien patrol discovered the mountain during a survey of the Kebos Lowlands.
King Shayzien VII was keen on conquering more land for Kourend and demanded his people explore suitable territories.
The mountain became known as Mount Quidamortem after it was realised venturing towards the summit resulted in certain death.

Gnosi is our expert on Mount Quidamortem, but I'm afraid she's currently on an expedition to the temple near the summit of the mountain. However, we do have some texts available detailing the great expedition.
Is there something else I can help you with?
My name is Istoria. I'm the chief historian and curator of the Library Historical Archive.

It is a small crescent-shaped island just north-west of here, outerlander.
We have many legends about it, such as the tale of the broken sky, and the day of the green seas.
The reason I am travelling there is more serious Fremennik business, however. I doubt an outerlander would be interested.

standard.npc: Nilsal, [player name]. How are things going?

standard.player: Pretty good, thanks. How about you? Made any more discoveries down here?

standard.npc: More than you can count! I've found so much new information on the Old Ones and naguanil. The museum are hoping to include it all in some new exhibits soon!

standard.player: Sounds awesome! I'll be sure to keep an eye out for them. On that note, I'll let you get back to it.

standard.npc: Hello friend.

standard.player: Hello, what are you doing here?

standard.player: Nice to meet you. You must know this area very well then.

standard.npc: I do. There're all sorts of interesting creatures around here. Be careful, some of them are not very friendly. A lot of travellers have become their victims.

standard.player: I see. Thanks for the warning.

standard.npc: No problem! Safe travels my friend.
Hello, I don't recognise you. We don't get many newcomers around here.

standard-dialogue-after-plague-city.npc: I'm surprised you're still here. Not many like to stick around this place if they have the choice.

standard-dialogue-after-getting-rid-of-t.npc: Not bad, the city is still a mess but we've finally got the chance to change that now the mourners have gone.

standard-dialogue-after-getting-rid-of-t.player: Good to hear, all the best.

standard.npc: Hello there. Welcome to the Temple of the Lesser Gods.

options.text: Could you tell me more about the lesser gods?

steps.player: Could you tell me more about the lesser gods?

steps.npc: Of course. The lesser gods, or avatars as some call them, were born from the dreams of Tumeken. They are Apmeken, Het, Crondis and Scabaras.

options.text: Could you tell me more about Apmeken?

steps.player: Could you tell me more about Apmeken?

steps.npc: Apmeken is the goddess of companionship. She is known to be the most mischievous, playful and unpredictable of the minor deities. I'd say she's my personal favourite.

steps.player: So I shouldn't trust you then?

steps.npc: Apmeken can appeal to the most erudite scholar or the most barefaced liar. I'd like to be considered amongst the former category.

steps.player: I see. What does she look like?

steps.npc: She has the head of a monkey, or sometimes an ape. It changes depending upon what nature she is displaying. For example, the orangutan represents wisdom, while the baboon represents mischief.

steps.text: other

options.text: Could you tell me more about Het?

steps.player: Could you tell me more about Het?

steps.npc: Het is the least strange of our deities to foreign eyes, for he looks just like us. I suspect this is why his shrines are particularly targeted by thieves like that infamous Templeton.
Het is the god of health, both in mind and body. He is quite popular amongst soldiers as a result, especially up in Al Kharid.
Not at all! Like I said, the wellbeing of the mind is also key to Het. Many great orators also look to him for guidance. I imagine his teachings help with some of their strenuous speeches.

steps.player: How did his followers react to the plagues here?

steps.npc: With many arguments. They really couldn't decide whether it was a punishment from Het, or an affront to him. I stayed out of that debate.

steps.text: other

options.text: Could you tell me more about Crondis?

steps.player: Could you tell me more about Crondis?

steps.npc: Crondis is a ferocious lady with the head of a mighty crocodile.

steps.player: That must be awkward when buying helmets.

steps.npc: Luckily for her, I don't think deities have much need for them.

steps.player: So what is she the goddess of?

steps.npc: Resourcefulness. A word which seems to be open to large interpretation.
Most consider her to be a teacher of modesty. They say we should be resourceful by only taking and using that which we absolutely need.

steps.player: But there's others with a different interpretation?

steps.npc: Some believe she is actually the goddess of pleasure. They claim that the idea of modesty came from a misinterpretation, and that to be resourceful is to take all that you can.
No. It is a more recent take that I suspect was born in Menaphos. There are many in that city with more wealth than they'll ever need. Modesty is not an ideal they'll ever embody.

steps.text: other

options.text: Could you tell me more about Scabaras?

steps.player: Could you tell me more about Scabaras?

steps.npc: There are many opinions out there on Scabaras, but general knowledge isn't always the most accurate.

steps.player: Well what are the absolute facts then?

steps.npc: Scabaras is the god of isolation. He takes on the appearance of a man with the head of a scarab. Both he and his followers were driven into hiding long ago.
And that's it. You asked for the absolute facts. Anything beyond that is just speculation.

steps.player: But there must be more. The High Priest told me that Scabaras tried to conquer these lands.

steps.npc: So it is said, but the written accounts that exist contain many inconsistencies when it comes to what role Scabaras actually played. Of course, most would not know that.
Many of the writings are only available to us priests. That does of course include the new High Priest, but perhaps he is yet to read them. They are definitely... illuminating.

steps.text: other

standard-dialogue-attempting-to-climb-do.npc: Hey! You don't have permission to go down there.

steps.npc: Mum says I not to talk to strangers.
So I's can't says my name is Jill.
We's be new here, on the bana plantion.
Yeah, we's be new here. Anyway, I gonna go play now.
Jill!
Yes, that's me.
We play here.
Yeah, it's fun. Bye.
No, I not say. You have to guess.
How d'ya know that? Are you magic?

steps.player: Not really - just call it a gift.

steps.npc: If you were magic, you would know why the sea is blue... are you magic?

steps.player: Nope, I'm not magic, and I have no clue why the sea is blue.

steps.npc: Oh, well. That's a bit sad. I was hoping you were magic and could magic me some sweets. But you can't, so I go find someone else who's magic. Bye.

after-the-event.npc: Thanks so much for saving us from those stinky gublinch. They were awful! I hope Shanty gave you somefing cool for your efforts.

standard.speaker: Imp
standard.text: Ah... Another wayward traveller.

standard.speaker: Imp
standard.text: You are not the first to make your way down here. Undoubtedly, you will not be the last.

standard.speaker: Imp
standard.text: My aeternal name, given to me long ago, is Jimp.

standard.speaker: Imp
standard.text: Yes, though my many centuries upon this realm have taught me that the newer tongues struggle with its pronounciation.

standard.speaker: Imp
standard.text: So you may call me Jim.

standard.speaker: Imp
standard.text: I see you still have questions. Before I answer them, I will need you to swear to secrecy.

standard.player: Hang on... why would I do that?

standard.speaker: Imp
standard.text: I believe you will find my cooperation helpful. Perhaps I shall find yours helpful one day too.

options.text: I've already entered one dubious contract.

steps.player: I've already entered one dubious contract.
I'm not sure I should be signing any others.

steps.speaker: Imp
steps.text: You will find the nature of my contracts refreshing, then. My terms are simple: do not endanger me or take what is mine, and I shall do what I can to help you.
continue
continue

standard.text: You sign the crumpled looking document.

standard.npc: Excellent. It is a pleasure to make your acquaintance, [player name].

standard.player: Wait, how do you know my name? Was this a trick?

standard.npc: No, friend, you signed it right here.

steps.npc: I suppose since you already know my name, you are asking who I am in the context of history and society.
I am afraid other agreements bar me from telling you much of my past. Nowadays, I am a humble servant of Yama, existing only to do as he pleases.
Mostly fetching records, and dying. When I am not doing that, I rest here. The features of this isle remind me of those I once knew.
I already skirt as closely as I can to what I am disallowed from sharing. I apologise, but I cannot answer further.
This isle is a small wonder. The rock formations here bear a slight resemblance to those from my own realm.

steps.player: The rock looks like it's crumbling.

steps.npc: Yes, infernal shale is kept together largely by the pressure from above. Once a piece is broken off, it can easily be broken down with a hammer and chisel.

steps.player: That's good to know. What about the smithy?

steps.npc: I can say nothing more than that it was not here when I arrived.
I cannot say.

steps.text: If the player has never received Jim's wet cloth:

steps.npc: Yes, the unique composition of this chasm does create a warm environment.

steps.player: I can see my sweat turning to vapour as soon as it appears.

steps.npc: Yes, water is an ineffective coolant at this temperature. Perhaps I could offer an alternative.

steps.text: Jim hands you a cloth dripping with blackened liquid.

steps.npc: The liquid will only offer a brief respite from the heat, but I find it can help to apply it frequently between bursts of exertion.

steps.player: I see, thanks. I'll give that a try.

steps.npc: I can see you eyeing the liquid. It is best you do not ask.

steps.text: If the player has previously received Jim's wet cloth:

steps.npc: Have another cloth. Remember, it only offers a brief respite from the heat. You'll want to time bursts of exertion right after using it.

options.text: Why is there a smithy down here?

steps.player: Why is there a smithy down here?

steps.npc: I cannot speak to the purpose the smithy has, but I might be able to shed some light on the purposes it could be given.
The furnace is capable of extremely high temperatures. Whilst not very helpful for your ores, it can melt metal from our realm.

steps.player: Like the rocks on this isle?

steps.npc: Not quite, though they are necessary to power the furnace. Nobody but Yama has access to the kinds of ores it was designed for.

steps.player: But if I were to get my hands on some, I could work them here?

steps.npc: Yes. The process is quite involved. Smaller shards must be melted into nuggets for stability, and then combined into chunks.

steps.player: I see. Maybe I can give that a go.

options.text: You're very friendly for a demon.

steps.player: You're very friendly for a demon.

steps.npc: I am not alone in this amongst my kind, but I understand that I am rare. I have my reasons for being this way.

steps.player: Well, if there is anything I can do for you, let me know.

steps.npc: Thank you. There is little I can ask of you given the nature of my other agreements, but watching you work on this isle does bring me some comfort.
Safe travels, [player name].

You can adopt an ultra defensive strategy, which increases your cat's hitpoints and defence but causes it to flee sooner.

If the player has not asked Juna to tell them a story before:

steps.npc: The Third Age of the world was a time of great conflict, of destruction never seen before or since, when all the gods save Guthix warred for control.

The colossal Wyrms, of whom today's dragons are a pale reflection, turned all the sky to fire, while on the ground armies of foot soldiers, goblins and trolls and humans, filled the valleys and plains with blood.

In time the noise of the conflict woke Guthix from His deep slumber, and He rose and stood in the centre of the battlefield so that the splendour of His wrath filled the world, and He called for the conflict to cease!
Silence fell, for the gods knew that none could challenge the power of the mighty Guthix -- for His power is that of nature itself, to which all other things are subject, in the end.
Guthix reclaimed that which had been stolen from Him, and went back underground to return to His sleep and continue to draw the world's power into Himself.
But on His way into the depths of the earth He sat and rested in this cave; and, thinking of the battle-scarred desert that now stretched from one side of His world to the other, He wept.
And so great was His sorrow, and so great was His life- giving power, that the rocks themselves began to weep with Him.
Later, Guthix noticed that the rocks continued to weep, and that their tears were infused with a small part of His power.
So He set me, His servant, to guard the cave, and He entrusted to me the task of judging who was and was not worthy to access the tears.

steps.npc: I will tell you the story of the light-creatures.
Myriad and beautiful were the creatures and civilizations of the early ages of the world. Gielinor was a work of art, shaped lovingly over the millennia by the creative mind of Guthix.

Only the sturdiest races survived the Godwars, and even then only by abandoning their high culture and gearing their societies towards war. Of the more delicate races there is now no trace, and almost no memory.
One such race had bodies as fragile as snowflakes, yet they built crystal cities that stood for a thousand years.

The wind would whisper through the spires and fill them with sweet harmonies, and the rising sun would shine through the precious gems that studded the towers and create inter plays of light as if rainbows were dancing.

Indeed, so marvellous was this light-show at its height that the patterns of light themselves became alive, and great flocks of luminous creatures rode along the gem- cast beams, each drawn to its own colour.
The creatures you see floating in this chasm are the last sorry remnants of that age. I do not know how they made their way here and survived to this time, but I am grateful for their company.

steps.text: If the player has asked Juna to tell them a new story twice before:

options.text: Tell me about the Tears of Guthix

steps.npc: Not long after the start of my vigil a party of goblins happened on my cave. These were the ugly brutes of the gods' armies, but their armour bore a faded patch where the symbol of a god had been removed.
They looked around hesitantly, squinting in the light of crude torches, but as soon as they saw me they raised their spears and charged.
No one may access the Tears of Guthix by force. I sent them tumbling into the chasm.
Two hundred years later another goblin found me. This one was unarmed, and although she was very wary I succeeded in engaging her in conversation.
Since then I have had many more visits from the descendants of those lost warriors, and over the centuries I have seen them change.
They have become timid rather than aggressive, and I have seen the light of intelligence grow in their bulging eyes.
Their stories are repetitive and grim, of scraping a living out of the harsh rock and through ingenuity and toil shaping it into a home.
I have followed the progress of their race, but their individual stories hold little interest for me.

options.text: Do you have any tips on how I can become a better sailor?

steps.player: Do you have any tips on how I can become a better sailor?

steps.npc: To be frank, mate, I'd say you're already at the top of your game. Still, I guess I can probably chuck a few pointers your way. Let's have a butchers...
Yeah, I reckon I can probably chuck a few pointers your way. Let's have a butchers...

Right, you've got all sorts of ways you can buff up your sailing skills. There's port tasks, sea charting, shipwreck salvaging, Barracuda Trials, deep sea trawling, and probably loads more I've gone and forgotten about.

options.text: Can you tell me more about port tasks?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about port tasks?

steps.npc: Sure thing, mate. You'll find that a lot of ports will have a notice board where folks have gone and stuck up some ads for jobs they want sorting.
Might be they want some cargo lugging about, or maybe they're after someone to pop out and do a bit of killing for them.

steps.player: And is there anything I should keep in mind while doing these tasks?

steps.npc: Well, after you've gone and accepted a task or two, you'll want to keep your captain's log handy. It's good for keeping tabs on what jobs you're currently grafting away at.

Also, if you're doing a bit of courier work, you might find it handy to get a couple of crewmates on board. They can help you shift the goods about so you're not knackering yourself by carrying one crate at a time.
No worries, mate. Wanting any other tips?

steps.text: other

options.text: Can you tell me more about sea charting?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about sea charting?

steps.npc: Well, mate, sea charting is all about heading out and improving your own knowledge of the sea itself. Your captain's log has all sorts of cracking tips on how to do so.
If you want to know more, your best shout's going to be heading down into the cave on the island for a chinwag with Charles. He's the local expert on this sort of stuff.

steps.player: I might just do that. Thanks, Jim.

steps.npc: Not a problem, mate. Do you need any more tips?

steps.text: other

options.text: Can you tell me more about shipwreck salvaging?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about shipwreck salvaging?

steps.npc: Well, as the name suggests, mate, it's all about salvaging old shipwrecks from the sea. Keeps the place nice and tidy, and allows you to snag some swag from those that don't need it anymore.
To get started, you're going to want to head over to the shipyard and sort yourself out with a proper nice salvaging hook. The flashier the hook, the quicker you'll be able to salvage.

Once you've got your hook all nicely set up, it's time to head out and find a shipwreck. You've got plenty of different types to pick from. Once you spot a good one, just use the hook to get stuck in.
You'll want to keep salvaging until you're feeling chuffed with your haul. Then you just need to use a salvaging station to sort through it all. Any half-decent port's going to have one.

steps.player: I see. Thanks for the information.

steps.npc: Always a pleasure, mate. Wanting any other tips?

steps.text: other

options.text: Can you tell me more about Barracuda Trials?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about Barracuda Trials?

steps.npc: Sure can, mate. The Barracudas are a top group of daredevils, but they're also proper show-offs. They like to head out in their fancy boats, giving it proper beans and pushing them right to the limit.
If you're a bit of a cheeky sod yourself, you might want to get involved in one of their trials. All of them are about speeding around and clocking the best time possible.

Anyway, if you fancy it, the nearest one is just south of here in the Storm Tempor. Just don't go being a lemon and jumping in without a boat that's up to the task. Last thing you want is to go and sink!

steps.player: I'll be sure to keep that in mind. Thanks, Jim.

steps.npc: No worries, mate. Need any other tips?

steps.text: other

options.text: Can you tell me more about deep sea trawling?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about deep sea trawling?

steps.npc: To be honest, mate, it's not something I'm properly clued up on. The basic gist though is that it's all about heading out in your boat to snag some fish that you wouldn't normally be able to get your mitts on.
Still, you don't need to worry, mate. I may not be able to help you, but word is there's a geezer who can over in Port Roberts. Kellan is his name apparently.

steps.player: I see. Thanks for the information.

steps.npc: Not a problem, mate. Do you need any more tips?

steps.text: other

options.text: Is there anything else I should keep in mind?

steps.player: Is there anything else I should keep in mind?

steps.npc: Well, mate, you're going to want to keep taking full advantage of the shipyard. If you don't keep regularly upgrading your boat and the facilities on it, you're just holding yourself back for no good reason.

Speaking of which, don't be afraid to sort yourself out with more than one boat. That way you can have different ones with different facilities on them. Do that, and you'll be golden regardless of what you're up to.
Another thing to remember is that you don't need to go it alone. Get yourself a proper bang up crew, mate. They'll be able to help you with all sorts of things on your boat.
Just speak to the Crew Registrar down the docks and she'll get you properly sorted out.
Finally, mate, while self-betterment is ace and all that, don't forget to kick back, chill out, and enjoy yourself! Sometimes it ain't about the destination, it's about the journey!
Always a pleasure, mate. Need any other tips?

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: Arceuus.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: The name of a liar.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.npc: They came to us. Two of them.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: The brother and the husband.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: But they misused it. And the world suffered.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: In a way. But it was not meant for that.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: Time was what it was meant for. But time still runs out.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.npc: They put an end to time. They endangered the balance.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: For every death, there must be life.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: As all things should be.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: For without balance, the world burns.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.player: You're very confusing, you know that right?

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: Perhaps.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.npc: Perhaps our knowledge is beyond your understanding.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.player: Well thankfully I didn't come here for knowledge. I came here for help. The Dark Altar is failing and the people of Arceuus are in danger. I need you to help me find the cause.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: The people of Arceuus have had their time.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor

I've done this enough times to know that everyone wants something, even the masters of life and death.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: Interesting. Maybe the human is not as stupid as it looks.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.player: Well I've been known to have my moments.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: Very well human.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: We admit, the Arceuus people do have their uses.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.npc: Their work with souls has been useful in helping to maintain the balance.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: We will help them. But first, you will serve us.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.player: Excellent. What do you need from me?

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.npc: To the south lies a battlefront.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: There is a grave there. Within it lies a soul, trapped inside a corpse.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: Free this soul. In return, we will provide our help.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.player: So you just want me to kill a zombie?

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: A zombie is soulless. An empty shell, reanimated by magic.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San
during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.text: This is a soul. Trapped in this world, when it should have long departed.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.npc: Its existence is an affront to the balance.

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Mej-San

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor

during-the-ascent-of-arceuus-first-encou.speaker: Kaal-Ket-Jor

options.text: Can you explain the fundamentals again?

steps.player: Can you explain the fundamentals again?

steps.npc: Indeed I will...
Herblore is the skill of working with herbs and other ingredients, to make useful potions and poison.
First you will need a vial, which can be found or made with the crafting skill.
Then you must gather the herbs needed to make the potion you want.
You must fill your vial with water and add the ingredients you need. There are normally 2 ingredients to each type of potion.
Bear in mind, you must first clean each herb before you can use it.
You may also have to grind some ingredients before you can use them. You will need a pestle and mortar in order to do this.
Herbs can be found on the ground, and are also dropped by some monsters when you kill them.
Let's try an example Attack potion: The first ingredient is Guam leaf; the next is Eye of Newt.
Mix these in your water-filled vial, and you will produce an Attack potion. Drink this potion to increase your Attack level.
Different potions also require different Herblore levels before you can make them.
Good luck with your Herblore practices, and a good day to you.

steps.speaker: King Black Dragon (left head)
steps.text: There are no monsters more powerful than us!

steps.speaker: King Black Dragon (middle head)
steps.text: We're the top monster of all Gielinor!

steps.player: No you're not. The Kalphite Queen is more powerful than you!

steps.speaker: King Black Dragon (middle head)
steps.text: Kalphite Queen? What's that?

steps.player: She's a giant insect who lives in the desert.

steps.speaker: King Black Dragon (middle head)
steps.text: An insect?

steps.speaker: King Black Dragon (right head)
steps.text: Ha ha ha ha!

steps.speaker: King Black Dragon (left head)
steps.text: No insect could be tougher than us! We're the best!

steps.player: No, she's way tougher than you!

steps.text: I don't believe it!

steps.speaker: King Black Dragon (left head)
steps.text: Never heard of it!

steps.speaker: King Black Dragon (right head)
steps.text: You're making it up!

steps.speaker: King Black Dragon (middle head)
steps.text: Now then, how do you know you're not just making all these monsters up to demoralise us?

steps.player: All right then, what about me?

steps.speaker: King Black Dragon (left head)
steps.text: Puny human! You're not a fearsome monster!

steps.player: I defeated you, didn't I? So I must be stronger than you!

steps.speaker: King Black Dragon (left head)
steps.text: You got lucky! I'll get you next time!

steps.player: Now that you're a stuffed head? I don't think so!

steps.speaker: King Black Dragon (left head)
steps.text: I am!

steps.speaker: King Black Dragon (right head)
steps.text: Shut up! I am!

steps.speaker: King Black Dragon (middle head)

steps.player: But you don't even know what I was going to say!

steps.speaker: King Black Dragon (middle head)
steps.text: It doesn't matter. I'm the strongest, cleverest, and most attractive. Whatever it is, I am the most of it!

steps.speaker: King Black Dragon (left head)

steps.speaker: King Black Dragon (middle head)
steps.text: Good point. What is it you were going to say? Because if it's something good, I'm it, but if it's something bad then it's one of these two ugly mugs.

standard.npc: Hello! Nice day we're having today. You here for business, or just a drink?

standard.player: Well, actually I just sort of washed up here.

standard.npc: Ah, it was the same for me. After I left the Great Conch I didn't really have too much of a goal in mind to be honest. I decided to just explore the world. I started swimming and ended up here!

standard.text: If the player has not completed Troubled Tortugans:

steps.npc: It's where the tortugans, my people, live. Well, it's where the juveniles and elders live at least. Us adults leave the island to find our calling in the wider world.
I'd tell you to visit, but you don't get many humans allowed on the island. My people prefer their privacy. Who knows though, maybe one day you'll be one of the lucky few who get to go there!
Anyway, I shouldn't keep you. I'm sure you've got plenty to be doing. See you later!

standard.text: If the player has completed Troubled Tortugans:

steps.npc: Anyway, even if you did just wash up here, I'm sure you'll find something to keep you around. There's all sorts of opportunities here on the Pandemonium. On that note, I won't keep you. See you later!

standard-dialogue-during-the-fremennik-i.npc: Oh, hello stranger. If you're new to town you should speak with our ruler, King Gjuki Sorvott IV. He'll want to meet you - he always wants to have a chat with any strangers in town. They could be spies you know.
Yes, spies from Neitiznot. They're everywhere. Apparently. That's what the King says anyway.

standard-dialogue-during-the-fremennik-i.player: So what do you do here?

standard-dialogue-during-the-fremennik-i.npc: Me? I'm a cook. Fish dishes a speciality. I hate fish. But fish is about all we have. Except for yak. But we're not allowed to eat yak.

standard-dialogue-during-the-fremennik-i.player: Why not, is yak meat bad for you?

standard-dialogue-during-the-fremennik-i.npc: Certainly not! Yak meat is both sweet and delicately flavoured. Yak is juicier than buffalo and elk - but never gamey. It goes wonderfully well with a glass of red wine, and it's healthy too!

standard-dialogue-during-the-fremennik-i.player: So why aren't you allowed to eat it?

standard-dialogue-during-the-fremennik-i.npc: King's orders. They breed and eat yaks on Neitiznot, so WE'RE not allowed to. It's unjust I tell you! I had a dream last night about a juicy fillet of yak, served on a bed of deep-fried seaweed and topped with a garnish

standard-dialogue-during-the-fremennik-i.player: That's a little sad. So do you have any cooked food I could buy?

standard-dialogue-during-the-fremennik-i.npc: No. It would only be fish anyway. Why would you want to eat fish?

standard-dialogue-during-the-fremennik-i.player: Well, I wouldn't mind a few shark and swordfish steaks as back-up you know.

standard-dialogue-during-the-fremennik-i.npc: If you insist. Sorry the stock is so low, but I just can't be bothered to cook any more.

standard-dialogue-after-completing-the-f.npc: Go away and let me wallow in self loathing.

standard-dialogue-after-completing-the-f.player: Do you want any help with that? I can loath you as well.

standard.npc: Hello there. The name's Keith. I'm the farmer here.

standard.player: You're pretty far out of the way here. How come?

standard.npc: It's a peaceful life. Out here I can avoid the drama and politics of the big settlements.

standard.player: Aren't you worried about how close the lizardmen are though?

standard.npc: The Shayzien troops keep them busy. They've not tried coming up this way.

standard.player: Fair enough. I'll leave you to it.

steps.npc: Get away! One day we'll have our revenge on you all!
Spare us your fake pity. I spit on Khazard, and all who do his bidding.
You're brave coming in here. If the guards get you, you'll be the next one in a cell.
You're not safe here, traveller. Leave while you still can.

I was thinking about the crystal spires of Prifddinas.

steps.npc: I have never seen it, all I know are the stories. I hope that changes one day.

standard-dialogue-prifddinas.speaker: Lady Kelyn Ithell

standard.npc: I am no man! They changed me and cursed me to remain here...

steps.player: What do you mean they changed you?

steps.npc: I was once a free man, powerful and wealthy. I owned several apothecaries across Kourend and sold the tastiest potions in the land.

One of my greatest inventions, it was going so well. I spent days finding the right herbs, I travelled across all of Kourend to find the most exotic weeds. Once I had gathered them all, I put them in a potion and mixed in
the final ingredient.

steps.text: If the player has not travelled to Great Kourend:
If the player has travelled to Great Kourend:

steps.player: Kourend? Oh yeah, I've been there.

steps.npc: Yes, yes... The potion tasted delicious but it was missing a tiny something so I added Magic roots to the potion. It started to pulsate and glow! I took a sip and I felt like a million gold! A few seconds later my eye sight
began to blur, my brain was throbbing. I fell and hit my head on my worktop, then it all went black.

steps.player: Ouch! But, you still haven't said who changed you?

steps.npc: Will you let me finish?

I woke up screaming in pain. Blue foam streaming out of my mouth, my eye sight worse than before, the only things I could make out were 3 tall figures with green banners - they were of the Arceuus Elders. They

muttered to each other in Archaic Language after trying to get up several times. I lost hope and stared at the sky. I had given up when the tallest of the figures bent over and brought his face right to mine and spoke
very softly 'We can save you, but it will come at a cost'.
Yes of course they saved me but look at the cost! I have horns coming out of my head and I'm still blind and stuck here... forever alone.
