standard.npc: Hello there.

standard.player: Hello, Longramble. How goes the hunt for the edge of the world?

standard.npc: Truth be told, I've found myself getting a bit side- tracked. The potential discovery of Arposandra is quite an exciting one!
Yes, that's why I've not dared go inside again. It's much safer out here. Slightly less smelly as well.

standard.player: Slightly being the key word there.

standard-dialogue-once-after-completing-.npc: Hello there. How goes the hunt for Arposandra?

standard-dialogue-once-after-completing-.player: I think I've found an entrance to the city, but it's too well defended. There's all these traps, and some talking terrorbird guards!

standard-dialogue-once-after-completing-.npc: Talking terrorbirds? There must be some strange magic being practised in there. What do you plan to do?

standard-dialogue-once-after-completing-.player: I don't know. I think I've hit a dead end for now.

standard-dialogue-once-after-completing-.npc: That's a shame. Still, you've made a big discovery. It will be quite the tale to tell... assuming anyone believes a story about talking terrorbirds, that is.

standard-dialogue-when-delivering-a-tang.text: You hand over the tangled toads' legs to the very grateful-looking gnome. He stuffs them straight into his mouth and hands you a mint cake in return.
Longramble continues into his standard dialogue.

attempting-to-grapple-the-tree-without-a.player: I appear to have misplaced the grappling equipment I need to cross the river.

attempting-to-grapple-the-tree-without-a.npc: That wasn't very clever, was it?
Well, it's a good job explorers like me know how to use their surroundings. I have an idea!

attempting-to-grapple-the-tree-without-a.text: Longramble explains, in huge detail, a wildly complicated plan to get you across the river. It involves using various items scrounged from the local flora and fauna.

Before you know it, you find yourself on the other side of the river with a bump on your head and no recollection of how you got across. You wonder what Longramble's plan was. It must have been very clever.

standard.npc: What do you want?

steps.npc: This path leads to the Doors of Dinh. You should be careful if you wish to travel any further.

options.text: Tell me about the Doors of Dinh.

steps.player: Tell me about the Doors of Dinh.

steps.npc: They're to keep the Wintertodt at bay. No-one knows what it really is, but centuries ago it came out of the northern wastes to terrorise the kingdom.
The Doors were created by Dinh, a master smither, to imprison the Wintertodt.
Now we keep a watch on the pass, so that the armies can be summoned if the Wintertodt ever escapes.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: I'm the duty look-out on the northern pass. It's the worst assignment there is.
As if the cold weren't bad enough, the snooty Arceuus magi always look down their noses at the Shayzien armies, just because we use muscle and steel rather than fancy magicks.

standard-dialogue-after-sins-of-the-fath.npc: You! You're the one that lost me my tithes. Get out before I have you killed!

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-is-not-d.npc: Human! Get back to the slave pens before I call the guards!

standard-dialogue-after-the-blood-moon-r.npc: Then be on your way. I have a meeting with Lord Vitur soon and I don't need any distractions.

if-the-player-is-disguised-and-has-not-y.npc: Tell me, [player vampyre name], what blood tastes the best?
You misunderstand me, I mean what kind of human?
What? I mean, yes. But what else?

if-the-player-is-disguised-and-has-not-y.player: I don't know... What's the actual answer?

if-the-player-is-disguised-and-has-not-y.npc: Love. Blood tastes best when it comes from one who loves.
Too many around here treat their tithes with discontentment. When they do, they miss out on the full potential blood has to offer.
Treat your tithes with respect instead. They will come to love you, and their blood becomes so much better as a result.

if-the-player-is-disguised-and-has-not-y.player: I see. I'll keep that in mind.

after-song-of-the-elves.npc: The city is flourishing, largely thanks to you. There's still some mistrust for the Iorwerth clan, but overall I'd say it's been over a thousand years since our people were doing this well.

after-song-of-the-elves.player: That's great to hear. What about you though?

after-song-of-the-elves.npc: I still mourn Glarial every day, until the end of time a part of me will be missing, never to be replaced.
But I know now that I can't let that impact the elves here. Many of them never even knew their former queen. My grief is mine alone, they need not bear it.

To them, I'm trying my best to be a leader they deserve, to correct the mistakes of the past. Lord Iorwerth believed we were nothing without Seren. We need to prove that we have a future with her gone.
Thankfully I have the other elders to help this time. Ruling is not as hard when you share out the responsiblities.

after-song-of-the-elves.player: Well I'm glad to hear things are going well.

after-song-of-the-elves.npc: And we are glad to have you here with us. None of this would have been possible without you.

standard.speaker: Damien Leucurte
standard.text: You may speak.

standard.npc: Oh, yes yes, I'm fine.

standard.player: You look a little beat up.

standard.npc: These scratches? Don't worry, just a disagreement with a thorn bush.

standard.speaker: Damien Leucurte
standard.text: Is there something you wanted, bloodbag?

standard.speaker: Damien Leucurte
standard.text: Well, I'd prefer you did it elsewhere, Crombwick is busy entertaining his guests.

standard.npc: What want you, with the Lord of the Kinshra? Speak!
Then begone knave, before I have my Knights put you to the sword!
Greetings [player name].

standard.player: Hey Iestin. So they made you the new Lord Iorwerth?

standard.npc: Indeed. Apart from Morvran, I am the closest living relative of the previous Lord Iorwerth.

standard.player: Did Morvran not want the role?

standard.npc: No. That's probably for the best though. Morvran was very close to my predecessor. It would have made many uncomfortable if he had taken on the role.

standard.player: How have things been since the city was reformed?

standard.npc: The others still hold a lot of mistrust for our clan. It will take a long time for those rifts to be repaired. We are on the right path though.

standard.player: That's good to hear. All the best.

standard.npc: Likewise.
Good day [player name]. Have you come to hear the song of the elves?
Do you not hear it? The sounds of a city in harmony. It is the song of the elves, the story of our people.
The last few verses were dark and quiet, but now our city is restored, we find ourselves singing a new verse, one of joy and light.

standard.player: I see. I guess I've never been the type to reflect on that sort of thing.

standard.npc: More of a fighter? We have a song for that too. If you wish to sing it, head to the Gauntlet and put yourself to the test.

standard.player: I might just give it a shot. Thanks.

standard.npc: Sorry, can't stop to talk. So much to do, so little time.
Hello there.

steps.npc: I am Kandur Hosidius and I am the lord of Hosidius, the city of farmers and chefs. I live here with my wife, Elena, and my two sons, Artur and Pandur.
My family and I have a peaceful existence here. That's mainly because I care not for the politics of the other houses. I instead devote my time to more meaningful pursuits.
Ensuring that Kourend is well fed. We may live in gentle times now but who knows how long it will be that way. Sooner or later another war or long winter will hit us. History has proven that.
Anything else I can help you with?

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Hosidius is home to the farmers and chefs of Kourend. We are the main food supplier to the kingdom and we ensure that her people are fed.
We also own more land than the other Kourend houses. We need the extra space for all of our crops.

steps.player: Do the other houses not get annoyed at how much land you have?

steps.npc: Sometimes. They know it is necessary though. There was once a time when the land was shared equally. But then the great famine came, and Kourend did not have the food to last through it.
After that, more space was given to Hosidius. We've had the most land ever since.
Anything else I can help you with?

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Plans? My only plan is to keep providing food to this kingdom.

steps.player: But what of the Royal Accord of Twill? You must have kept it for a reason.

steps.npc: I did. The Accord has the potential to be a powerful weapon, for words cut deeper than a blade ever can. However, I have no need to use this weapon, not unless the other houses give me reason to.
Anything else I can help you with?

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Until next time.

if-the-player-lost-the-memoir-page-befor.npc: I assume you're after that reward I promised you. Here you go.

standard.npc: Isn't it just!
This and that... But mostly, I'm looking for a good place to mobilise my army.

standard.player: That's awfully specific, you sure this is a good place for it?

standard.npc: I don't see why not!

standard.player: I'm not sure there's enough land, to be honest.

standard.npc: Tish tosh! I'm importing sand from Al Kharid, there'll be a base camp here in no time, do not fret!
The tithes are growing weak. That werewolf needs to do a better job of keeping them fed.
There's no shortage of corpses around here. The dead can still have some uses.

standard.player: You're feeding them corpses? No wonder they're becoming weak. That meat must have all sorts of problems.

standard.npc: What else would you have me feed them? If I give them nicer food, I'm wasting more money than if I were to just kill them and buy some more.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-is-not-d.npc: Human! Get back to the slave pens before I call the guards!

standard.npc: Hello there young one. Interested in getting your hands dirty?
Ah don't worry, it's nothing sinister. We leave that kind of thing to clan Iorwerth. I speak in a more literal sense, of the ground beneath us and the trees over us.

standard.player: Oh, I see. So it's your clan that looks after the plants of the city?

standard.npc: Indeed. We maintain the farms and manage the trees. The produce we grow goes to the Meilyr clan to feed the city and the wood we provide is used by the Ithell clan in construction.
Feel free to join us. Our farming patches are open to you, as is our sawmill.

after-creature-of-fenkenstrain.player: I stole the Ring of Charos from Fenkenstrain.

after-creature-of-fenkenstrain.speaker: Rologarth
after-creature-of-fenkenstrain.text: I saw him climb up into the Tower to hide it. It doesn't matter - soon the werewolves will come for him, and his experiments will be forever ceased.

after-creature-of-fenkenstrain.player: Do you want the ring back? It is yours after all.

after-creature-of-fenkenstrain.speaker: Rologarth
after-creature-of-fenkenstrain.text: No, you keep it, my friend. Werewolves hunger for the scent of live flesh - I have no need for the ring. I have my castle back, if not my soul.

steps.npc: Well citizen, you are speaking to Lord Shiro Shayzien. I am the ruler of Shayzien and the commander-in-chief of the Shayzien Army.

steps.player: How long have you held this position?

steps.npc: Since my father passed away four years ago. He was a good man who took the defence of Kourend very seriously. I have been working hard to continue his legacy.
Anything else I can help you with citizen?

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Most citizens of Shayzien are part of the Shayzien Army in some form or other. We are responsible for defending Kourend against external and internal threats.

steps.player: What are the current threats against Kourend?

steps.npc: Externally, we have recently being dealing with increased lizardman activity. We've also been keeping a close eye on Varlamore to the south, just in case they try anything.
Internally, we have seen a rise in gang crime across the kingdom. It seems to be especially prevalent in Port Piscarilius.

steps.player: How do you tackle these issues?

steps.npc: By doing what we do best citizen. There's no threat that can't be defeated by a Shayzien soldier with a sword in their hand.
Anything else I can help you with citizen?

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Our war plans? I'm afraid most of that is confidential.
What I can tell you is that our main focus right now is the lizardman threat. We've moved a great number of troops into the Kebos Lowlands to combat the issue.
Absolutely, we've pushed the lizardmen back to the point where we're finally able to allow citizens such as yourself into the region.

steps.text: If the player has not completed A Kingdom Divided:

steps.npc: Anything else I can help you with citizen?

steps.text: other
If the player has completed A Kingdom Divided:

steps.npc: Apart from the lizardman, we are also preparing to support the King in the hunt for his father's killer. Once we know who they are, they will face the full might of the Shayzien Army.
Anything else I can help you with citizen?

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Farewell citizen.

standard-dialogue-prior-to-starting-tale.npc: Can't talk right now citizen. I'm very busy.

if-the-player-lost-the-memoir-page-befor.npc: Here citizen. Your reward for helping with the expedition.

standard.npc: Good day friend.

steps.npc: I am Trobin Arceuus, lord of Arceuus. It's a position I've held for a thousand years, ever since the Ascent of Arceuus.

steps.player: That's a long time. I guess you've seen quite a bit.

steps.npc: Indeed. I've been present at some of the most notable moments in Kourend's history.
I was there when King Agata IV was deposed, I was there when Kharedst the Builder opened Kourend Castle and I was there when Emperor Imafore was executed.
I tend to keep out of public affairs these days though. My presence is often more of a distraction than a benefit. It also means I can focus on my work in peace.
The freeing of souls. There are many souls that find themselves trapped here after death. My people and I do our best to release them.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: If you find something magical in Kourend, chances are it came from Arceuus. Our people have lived for a thousand years. The knowledge we've gained in that time has resulted in many a magical discovery.
Most of our discoveries start with the Dark Altar. It is the source of our immortality and our people dedicate their lives to studying it.
Our people also serves an important role in the wider world. We work to free trapped souls so that they may pass on to the next world. It is a crucial task that the Dark Altar helps us to perform.

steps.player: Was the Dark Altar always here?

steps.npc: Impossible to say. The Dark Altar has been mentioned in records dating back to the earliest days of Kourend. Before then, who knows.
No. The Ascent of Arceuus didn't occur until after Xeric's Age of Strife, hundreds of years after Kourend was formed.

steps.text: other

options.text: Tell me about the Ascent of Arceuus.

steps.player: Tell me about the Ascent of Arceuus.

steps.npc: It was a thousand years ago, during the time of King Byrne II. I went to my people and shared the secrets of immortality with them.
Not all of them accepted this gift of course, as was their right. Those that did, were granted new bodies to house their souls. These bodies are sustained by the Dark Altar.

steps.player: It wasn't you that discovered this secret though was it?

steps.npc: No. It was granted to us by the Tasakaal. They are ancient beings, ones that make us seem like mere children.
Their age and experience have granted them knowledge over life and death that we can only dream of.

steps.player: The Tasakaal don't like you very much. They called you a liar and claimed you misused the knowledge.

steps.npc: The events that led to the Ascent of Arceuus are more complicated than even the Tasakaal know. But that is a story for another day.

steps.text: other
If the player has not completed A Kingdom Divided:

steps.npc: I had one of my people recover the remains of that device. The one that was absorbing the Dark Altars power.
We're performing tests to see if we can learn more about it. We haven't made any meaningful progress yet though.
Once we've learnt more about it, we'll be in a better position to determine our next move.
I admit, the idea of someone sabotaging the Altar is more than a bit concerning. I hope we can make some progress soon.

steps.text: other
If the player has completed A Kingdom Divided:

steps.npc: Now that we know Xamphur was responsible for the device that was absorbing power from the Dark Altar, we're hoping we can use it to help locate him.
Alas, so far we've had no luck. We're also scanning for energy that matches what we observed during that earthquake he caused, but again, nothing has been discovered so far.
It seems this work will take time. I assure you though, we will find him and his master.
We've begun an investigation into their order, but we have little to go on. Hopefully we find a good lead soon.

steps.player: Well just let me know if you need my help.

steps.npc: I will, thank you.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Farewell.

standard.player: Hello, I wonder if you could help me on this whole brewing thing...

standard.npc: I might be able to - what do you need to know?

steps.npc: Well first off you need to fill the vat with water - two bucketfuls should do the trick. Then you'll need to put in two handfuls of barley malt - that's roasted barley by the way.

Lastly you pour a pot full of ale yeast in, which'll start it off fermenting. Then all you have to do is wait for the good stuff.

options.text: I'd like to know more about security.

steps.player: I'd like to know more about security.

steps.npc: First I must warn you to take every precaution to keep your RuneScape password and PIN secure. The most important thing to remember is to never give your password to, or share your account with, anyone.

I can also tell you about password security, avoiding item scamming and in-game moderation. I can also tell you about a place called the Stronghold of Security, where you can learn more about account security and
have a bit of an adventure at the same time.

options.text: I'd like to know about password security.

steps.player: I'd like to know about password security.

steps.npc: Well, the first thing to remember with password security, which I can't stress enough, is to never tell your password, bank PIN or authenticator details to anyone, not even if they claim to be Jagex staff. Real

Jagex staff will NEVER ask for your password. Sharing your account is a very bad idea, even if you think that you know and trust the person you are sharing with. Players have lost items and even their
account this way. Sharing accounts is also against the rules.

steps.player: Is there anything else to be aware of?

steps.npc: Yes, also be careful where you enter your password. Be aware that fake Old School RuneScape websites exist. These are sites that claim to give things such as item/stat upgrades, free items, beta testing and
moderator applications. Jagex do not offer any of these services.

Also be aware of trojans and keyloggers. These nasty programs can send everything you type into your device back to the computers of malicious people, so you can lose more than just your Old School RuneScape

password in this way. To avoid getting these on your device, be very wary of what you download, especially when it comes to downloading third party software. Also be very wary of email attachments and instant
messenger file transfers, which can contain such things.
Finally, remember the game doesn't censor your password or bank PIN when you type them; anyone who tells you otherwise is probably trying to steal your character or items.

steps.npc: There are many nice and helpful players in Old School RuneScape; unfortunately, as in real life, there are some who aren't so honest. Some people may try to trick you out of your items. Try not to fall for this as

Jagex policy is to never return lost items to players that have been scammed. Doing so just encourages users to claim they lost items they never had to gain an unfair advantage. However, people carrying out such
scams will get banned as it is against the rules.

When trading, you have a second trade confirmation screen. Always double check that you are getting the items you expect on this page as some people may try and change what they are trading at the last minute on
the first trade screen. Remember when you have clicked accept on the second trade screen, the trade is not reversible.

Try and find out from someone else what an item is before spending a lot of money on it. Not all merchants are honest about the rarity or the uses of their wares. For example, some people try to pass off spinach rolls as
rare when in fact they're as common as cabbages!

Be wary of people offering to improve your items. For example, some people will claim they can add a trim to your armour or upgrade your sword to a more powerful one. This is not possible and they are trying
to steal your hard-earned equipment.

staff characters in game - these can be identified by a gold crown next to their name and are the people who work in the Jagex offices. They might be from Customer Support, or they might be a tester or a

programmer. You may also see player moderators - these can be identified by a silver crown next to their name. Player moderators are trusted players of Old School RuneScape that help keep in-game behaviour in
line with the Old School RuneScape rules.

steps.npc: Well, if you're sure then.
It all started in my youth when I was part of the Order of Wizards. I frequently spent time travelling across Gielinor, which kept me away from my beloved who worked here in Lumbridge.
Due to being apart, I would often send her gifts. This locket was one of them.

steps.player: I see... I'm not sure I like where this story is going. How come I found the locket in a magic rift then?

steps.npc: As I said, my research often kept me away from home. During one of my trips away, our house was robbed. My dear Thenia tried to stop them, but they took her life in return. The locket was taken in the robbery.

steps.player: Oh my... I'm so sorry for your loss.

steps.npc: I appreciate your kind words, but this was a long time ago. The pain of losing a loved one never fades, but in time you come to live with it.
Anyway, after that I stepped down from the Order of Wizards. I now spend my days offering guidance to those who come through Lumbridge.

steps.player: I'm still curious to know how it ended up in some rift. Do you have any theories?

steps.npc: Well... where was this rift?

steps.player: In an ancient temple. Most things in the rift came from the Abyss.

steps.player: They hadn't until recently, but the Z.M.I. found a way there.

steps.npc: The Z.M.I.? But could that mean...

steps.player: It's called the Temple of the Eye. It was built by Saradominist wizards long ago to house a powerful artefact.

steps.npc: The Eye?
Only stories, of which there are very few. Still, I always believed them to be real. After all, why else would an eye be the symbol of the Order of Wizards?
Ah, but that reminds me, I was not the first in my family to join the order. This amulet was passed down from generation to generation.

steps.npc: As soon as you mentioned it, I wondered if there might be a connection.
The origin of this amulet was something I spent much time puzzling over when I was younger. I'm glad you have answered the question I couldn't.
I'd be happy to give you this amulet in return for that locket. I have no use for it, but that locket is something which holds a lot of sentimental value to me.

steps.text: After receiving temporary permission from the council:

steps.npc: Excellent. I see you already have permission from the council.
Most of the people wandering around the market want to buy food. Since the passage to the surface opened up there's been a craze in exotic food from up there.
To sell something, simply use a piece of food on one of the gourmets in the market, then name your price, and the gourmet will tell you how many they are interested in buying for that price.
If you want a rough idea of how much something will sell for, show it to me and I'll try to estimate.
But you should also take into account the gourmet's reactions when naming your price. If someone likes the look of a food, they will pay more for it.
Also remember that the novelty of new foods quickly wears off. If people have been eating a lot of something lately, then they won't pay as much for it.
If someone especially likes your food then you might even start a craze for it! If there's a food that's in fashion like that, then the gourmets will pay more for it.
If you want to sell food in the market, you'll need to renew your permission from the council first. The councillor in charge of giving permission at the moment is [councillor].

standard.npc: Hey it's the Hero! Wow! You're amazing, how on earth did you manage to tackle those two juvinates and Gadderanks? And the town is lovely, you've done a great job!

steps.npc: Well met! My name's Luscion, I do a bit of this, a bit of that. Just try to survive really, there's nothing much else we can do.

options.text: How do you like your town?

steps.player: How do you like your town?

steps.npc: It's just perfect, thanks so much for your efforts.
Oh, not much really, we're all still hiding from the vampyres and eking out a living from this terrible place, hopefully soon we'll be strong enough to make the journey to the temple on the Salve.

options.text: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: Not as far as I know, we have some basic amenities now which is so very useful, we're all incredibly grateful to you. I've never really seen or known a hero before, so I have nothing to compare one to, but I suspect in
most people's judgement, you would be one! I for one am very pleased to have met you.

after-the-blood-moon-rises.npc: Hey, it's the hero! Thank you so much for everything you've done, not just for us, but for all of Morytania!

steps.npc: Oh, my name's Luscion. I just help out around here, you know, gathering food and so on.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Well, I'd be lying if I said life was suddenly perfect, but it's nice to no longer live in constant fear of the vampyres.

steps.player: What will you do now that you don't have to worry about them?

steps.npc: Well, quite a few of us are working on making the town a bit nicer. Not that there's anything wrong with the work you did of course.
Some of the others don't want to stick around. They reckon it might be safe enough to make the journey up to Paterdomus now. I think they want to start a new life across the Salve.

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: With the town? No, I don't think so. You've done enough to help us anyway.
I suppose if you did want to help in some way though, you could maybe assist those who want to get to Paterdomus. The swamps can still be pretty dangerous.

steps.text: other

standard.npc: Hello I'm Luthas, I run the banana plantation here.

options.text: Could you offer me employment on your plantation?

steps.player: Could you offer me employment on your plantation?

steps.npc: Yes, I can sort something out. There's a crate ready to be loaded onto the ship.
You wouldn't believe the demand for bananas from Wydin's shop over in Port Sarim. I think this is the third crate I've shipped him this month..
If you could fill it up with bananas, I'll pay you 30 gold.

options.text: That customs officer is annoying isn't she?

steps.player: That customs officer is annoying isn't she?

steps.npc: Well I know her pretty well. She doesn't cause me any trouble any more.
She doesn't even search my export crates any more. She knows they only contain bananas.

steps.player: Really? How interesting. Whereabouts do you send those to?

steps.npc: There is a little shop over in Port Sarim that buys them up by the crate. I believe it is run by a man called Wydin.

options.text: What did I have to do again?

steps.player: What did I have to do again?

steps.npc: There's a crate ready to be loaded onto the ship. If you could fill it up with bananas, I'll pay you 30 gold.

steps.npc: Well come back when it is.

options.text: So where are these bananas going to be delivered to?

options.text: That customs officer is annoying isn't she?

treasure-trails-medium.npc: Congratulations.

standard.npc: Greetings.

steps.npc: Well, friend, I'm Arls Lutwidge of the Moonlight Broadsword! Renowned all over Gielinor!

steps.player: Can't say I've heard of you before.

steps.npc: You haven't... heard of... That's madness!
Surely you've heard of my feats, but perhaps not the name?
And yourself?

steps.player: An adventurer mostly, but I've slain some dragons and I've conquered some nightmares.

steps.npc: Very good, young one! Very good indeed!

steps.player: So... where's this famous sword of yours?

steps.npc: Gone. I gave it to a fledgling when I retired and the damned fool went and died fighting some great monster in a far off land.
Say... if you find it, could you bring it to me? I won't pay you, as holding such a magnificent weapon should be payment enough.

steps.player: I think you need to work on your bartering skills.

steps.npc: Perhaps.

options.text: What grand feats are you known for?

steps.player: What grand feats are you known for?

steps.npc: I peaked rather early and most know me for my first act of heroism when I defeated the Moonfly. It may sound cute, but it killed many of the smallfolk and their livestock, for it was a vile creature.
It was I that discovered the creature. I pulled it from the Lum during a fishing trip of mine.
As young and foolish as I was, I dropped it down a dried up well and went for help. However, upon my return, the creature was gone.
Many years passed until suddenly there were sightings of a winged demon around the River Lum. Some claimed it was an overly large heron and that it was nothing to be worried about.
As time went on, folk started to go missing and I knew I had to return home and face this demon.
I had wars to fight, glory to be won and all that rubbish. Upon my return I spoke to an old crone who lived in the swamps and she gave me some advice.
She told me to spike my armour and described how to lure the creature toward me.

steps.player: And you defeated it? The Moonfly?

steps.npc: Some bard wrote a poem of the events. The telling of the battle is a little embellished and rife with errors. The poem can be found in this library somewhere, providing it has been returned.
And did I defeat the creature? I wouldn't be here if I hadn't!

steps.player: I'll be sure to keep an eye out.

steps.npc: Please do! And come to me if you have any burning questions about it.
I've grown old, friend. Heroes need to know when to throw in the towel, so they say. I've always enjoyed a good book, so it seemed fitting to stay here as librarian for the guild.

steps.player: Hmm... the books are very interesting. I thought there would be more though...

steps.npc: Well, that's why I'm here! So many of you adventurers help yourself to any old book and never return the damn things!
If I could have it my way, you wouldn't be allowed to wander off with them, but I'm not the guildmaster, as Alec likes to remind me.

steps.player: Certainly sounds like you have a problem.

steps.npc: Well fear not. I'm working on it!
I'll see you around.

using-lutwidge-and-the-moonfly-on-lutwid.npc: Yes! Fantastic! Did you enjoy it?

using-lutwidge-and-the-moonfly-on-lutwid.player: Yeah it was alright. Some of these words are a bit odd though. Did you really cover your sword in sheep blood?

using-lutwidge-and-the-moonfly-on-lutwid.npc: Ah, a slight misunderstanding... I soaked it in sap from a yew tree, but I guess blood is a bit more dramatic.
The crone, long dead now, I suppose... She claimed to be from the same world as the creature and knew of the ritual to summon it.

using-lutwidge-and-the-moonfly-on-lutwid.player: The poem does mention sheep though, at the end?

using-lutwidge-and-the-moonfly-on-lutwid.npc: Perhaps some locals claimed to have lost some sheep, but my guess is that the bard was searching for a rhyme. Either way, I doubt it's a detail worth fretting over.

steps.npc: Fine... Ajjat gave me unlimited teleports to his Warrior's guild and Kamfreena lets me fight her Cyclopes without needing those annoying tokens.
Melee combat tutor added a ring of life function and the armour salesman at the Ranging guild added a magnet and undead chicken thing.
Brother Jered attached a holy wrench and Wizard Sinina enchanted the cape so I can change me spellbook.
Aubury attached all of the runecrafting tiaras, an estate agent sold me some teleports and one of the nurses at the Emir's Arena made it give me faster hitpoints.
Agility Arena guy with a Parrot pet made it lighter for me and Kaqemeex convinced the Nardah herbalist to make potions for me if I wear it and he attached a pestle and mortar, toos.
Martin Thwait made the cape better for being sneaky and the Master Crafter added a teleport to his guild before Hickton attached some grapples and a crossbow.

standard.speaker: mad melvin96
standard.text: Hey there! Do you have a grapple I can borrow?

standard.player: I might have one, but I need it myself. Why do you need a grapple?

standard.speaker: mad melvin96
standard.text: I need it to grapple to that pillar over there and get some treasure of course. What else could I need it for?

standard.player: I mean that makes sense I suppose. How did you end up here?

standard.speaker: mad melvin96
standard.text: Well, I made my way to Morytania in search of a place called the Ba... Barlows? I've heard it's a great way to earn gold.

standard.speaker: mad melvin96
standard.text: Yeah, that's what I said!

standard.speaker: mad melvin96

standard.speaker: mad melvin96

standard.speaker: mad melvin96

standard.npc: Ah, greetings. What can I do for you?

steps.npc: I'm Madam Sikaro.
Why shouldn't it be? You asked who I was, and I answered.

steps.player: I was hoping to learn something about you, like what you were doing here...!

steps.npc: Well, perhaps next time you'll ask a more direct question.
Making a wizard hideout.
A wizard hideout! You know how some wizards have their own towers? Think that but underground.

steps.player: So why not just get a tower?

steps.npc: Land price. Kingdoms want you to pay an extortionate amount of money to build on 'their' land, it turns out.

steps.player: So instead you ended up in the basement of a tavern.

steps.npc: Yep. Camarst said I could have it as long as I don't hurt any of his customers too badly.
Not that I actually plan to hurt any of his customers.

options.text: I have this part that looks like it's from a weapon...
options.condition: If the player has a part of the Voidwaker:

steps.text: If the player has less than three parts of the Voidwaker:

steps.player: I have this part that looks like it's from a weapon...

steps.npc: Ah yes, that does look like a part of a particularly powerful weapon.

steps.player: Can I do anything with it?

steps.npc: You? Perhaps not, though if you could bring me all three pieces, I suspect I could put it back together for you.
There should be a hilt, a blade and a conduit gemstone. Oh, and I'll want 500,000 coins as payment as well. Good hunting!

steps.player: Do you know where I could find the other parts?

steps.npc: I suspect the Wilderness would be a good place to start. There are monsters out there that have grown immense over time.
Seeking out the strongest of them is where I'd start, anyway.

steps.text: If the player has all three parts of the Voidwaker:

steps.player: I have these parts of a weapon, do you think you could assemble it for me?

steps.npc: Hmm... yes, these are the parts of a particularly powerful weapon indeed. I can reassemble it... for a fee, of course. 500,000 coins, no less.

steps.text: If the player has less than 500,000 coins:

steps.player: I don't have that much on me...

steps.npc: Well, if you come across some more, come find me again.

steps.text: If the player has at least 500,000 coins:

steps.prompt: Have Madam Sikaro assemble the Voidwaker for 500,000 coins?

steps.text: Madam Sikaro takes the components off you and, in a flash of white light, fuses them together to form the Voidwaker.

steps.npc: Curious, you come to me with all of the parts and the coin, yet you change your mind at the last second.
I do rather get the feeling you're toying with me. Very well, I shall do my part in playing with you.

steps.text: You feel the contents of your inventory shift slightly.

steps.npc: Now, do talk to me again if you'd like to proceed more sensibly.

options.text: What are you doing with the money?
options.condition: If the player has had Madam Sikaro assemble the Voidwaker:

steps.player: What are you doing with the money from combining the Voidwaker?

steps.npc: I'll spend some of it improving the hideout. The rest on general expenses.
Living isn't free, you know? A woman my age has expenses. Food, clothing, protection... It all adds up.
You walked up to me just to say goodbye? Ok, sure, goodbye.

standard-dialogue-using-the-voidwaker-on.player: So what exactly is this sword, anyway?

standard-dialogue-using-the-voidwaker-on.npc: Well, that largely depends on who you ask and when you ask it. The sword is not unique, but many like it have been referenced in folktales.
Some tell of great and prideful warriors roaming the lands, cutting down all who oppose them in great crashes of lightning.
Others tell of lovers, one bound by oath, the other free as the wind, cruely torn apart by fate.
Others still tell of three great beasts that alone were powerful, but combined could destroy Gielinor.

standard-dialogue-using-the-voidwaker-on.player: Are we still talking about the sword?

standard-dialogue-using-the-voidwaker-on.npc: Amazingly, yes. In all of these tales, the sword is there, potential shining through the metal, thunder rolling in its wake.

standard-dialogue-using-the-voidwaker-on.player: Are any of these tales... true?

standard-dialogue-using-the-voidwaker-on.npc: Oh, I'm sure there are elements of the truth buried in there, but folklore being what it is, I'm inclined to not believe any of it.
Aside from the bit where it can summon lightning. It can absolutely do that.

standard-dialogue-using-the-voidwaker-on.player: What about the name? You called it Voidwaker?

standard-dialogue-using-the-voidwaker-on.npc: Well, in a lot of these tales, it's only ever reffered to as someone's sword. Like, [player name]'s sword.
So, I chose a name for it.
There are multiple reasons. I suppose you could say the sword is so powerful that it leaves a void in its wake.

standard-dialogue-using-any-other-item-o.npc: No thank you, I'm currently on a diet.

standard.npc: Good morrow, adventurer.

steps.npc: You guess? The sun is shining, the sea breeze is salty, what's not to enjoy?

steps.player: I don't know... The sand? It's coarse and rough and irritating, and it gets everywhere.

steps.npc: Hmm, well my spa isn't quite ready yet, but when it is, I'm sure that'll solve all of your sand related issues!
I am Madame Caldarium! A pirate's life was for me, but lately I've been looking to expand my business, I'm getting old, ya see.

steps.player: A spa business? Do you really think these Corsairs are the washing type?

steps.npc: Ha! That's what the Rum is for!
I'm more concerned of their laziness, 'Can't work today Madame, I'm cursed!'. Bunch of idiots, the lot of 'em.

steps.player: Surely you never expected this lot to be any different... They're either stealing, killing or both!

steps.npc: Yes... I have plans adventurer, the local cave dwelling population are... Let's say, sorting something out.

steps.player: Interesting, I'm sure that'll be an entertaining turn of events.

steps.npc: We'll see...
Farewell, adventurer.

treasure-trails-medium-when-talked-to-ag.npc: Please enter the answer to the question.

steps.npc: No, try again.
Correct!

steps.text: You have obtained [another clue/a casket]!

standard.npc: Is he still out there?
That angry captain. His boat got damaged and he blames my husband for not providing a weather report. The thing is, my husband's missing!

standard.player: I'm sorry to hear that. Maybe I could help try and find him?

standard.npc: Thank you for the offer, but there's already plenty of people looking for him. I'm sure they'll find him soon. I'm sure he'll be fine.

standard.player: I'm sure he will be as well, and if they need more help, I'm always happy to get involved.

standard.npc: Thank you.

steps.npc: Hello. How are you today?
Isn't it wonderful? So many books, so much knowledge to be absorbed!
Where did I see that book? It can't be far...
I'm sure it was around here somewhere...
What can I do for ya?

options.text: Got any good books to recommend?

steps.player: Got any good books to recommend?

steps.npc: I've always found Prifddinas' History to be fascinating!
I've always found The Journal of Randas to be fascinating!
I've always found Big Book of Bangs to be fascinating!
I've always found The Great Divide to be fascinating!
I've always found Ode to Eternity to be fascinating!
You know, there are so many different ways to greet people. Hello, 'ello, hello there...

steps.player: That still only counts as one!

steps.npc: Hello. How are you today?
Hello! What a day it is in the crystal city, huh?
What can I do for ya?

options.text: What is there to do around here?

steps.player: What is there to do around here?

steps.npc: All kinds of things! The towers are a wonderful sight to see.
On a day like today, I'd recommend visiting the market.

overhead-dialogue-failed-pickpocket-atte.npc: What do you think you're doing?

standard.npc: Welcome to Elder Raley's Herblore Stall. Would you like to buy some herblore supplies?

steps.text: Elder Raley's Herblore Stall opens.

steps.npc: No. Elder Raley's teaching me to become a herbalist myself, but he's always quite busy, so I normally look after the stall for him.
So, would you like to buy some herblore supplies?
Okay, well, you know where to find me if you change your mind.

standard.npc: Hello friend. I wish to slay evil and avail them of their loot! Take me to Burgh de Rott!

options.text: Are you prepared enough to fight the evil down there?

steps.player: But you do realise that the vampyres in Morytania are immune to everything except silver?

steps.npc: Er...well, I've not heard mention of that fact, but I have faith that Saradomin will provide the means to furnish me with suitable weapons when I reach Burgh de Rott.

steps.player: And if we happen to run into some vampyres on the journey down there?

steps.npc: I trust that you will help us to avoid them. You are a guide after all, aren't you? Anyway, you look like you can handle yourself. I presume you've fought such creatures before and won? How hard can it be?

steps.player: It can be pretty difficult, actually. But you're right, I'll be your guide so I should be able to handle the situation.

options.text: Why do you want to go to Burgh de Rott?

steps.player: Why do you want to go to Burgh de Rott?

steps.text: Before The Blood Moon Rises:

steps.npc: I'm going down there to teach those vampyres a lesson or two. I've heard about the terrible conditions down there and I intend to put a stop to it.

steps.text: After The Blood Moon Rises:

steps.npc: I want to have a go at this Theatre of Blood everyone keeps talking about!

options.text: Could you defend yourself if we met enemies...?

steps.player: Could you defend yourself if we met enemies on the route to Burgh de Rott?

steps.npc: Let's just say that I'm somewhat experienced and I'm happy to take on my fair share of enemies. You don't need to worry about that.

options.text: I can take you to Burgh de Rott.

steps.player: I can take you to Burgh de Rott.

Oh really? That would be great! I'll give you a small reward once we reach our destination.

steps.text: Burgh de Rott Ramble begins

steps.npc: Ok, which route should we take?

standard-dialogue-when-a-piece-of-accept.npc: Ah, so you want to give me some supplies, eh? Let me just open me backpack.

steps.npc: This place is a bit grim. How can people live here?
Do you visit Burgh de Rott often? You seem to know the route well.
When are we going to get to Burgh de Rott?
We don't have all day to stand around chatting; let's press on. I have loot to get.
Oh, I hate this trip, but it's better than the opulet life styles forced on us adventurer types. I'd much rather be up to my eyes in mud and having a good fight!

burgh-de-rott-ramble-dialogue-during-com.npc: Can't you see I'm being attacked...

standard-dialogue-after-completing-enter.npc: Ah, you again. What do you want?

options.text: About that incantation your initiate gave me...
options.condition: After Temple of the Eye:

steps.player: About that incantation your initiate gave me...

steps.text: If this is the first time using this option:

steps.npc: Ah yes, the one to trace that amulet. Don't think I didn't notice that you modified the transmission spell I put on it. Next time you need help, we might not be so willing.

steps.player: Well maybe you should have asked first! Besides, you wouldn't have got anything useful out of it. In tracing that amulet, we accidently managed to open an uncontrollable rift to the Abyss.

steps.npc: And does this 'we' include the Order of Wizards?
I knew it! It's just like them to play with magic they don't understand. First they burnt down the Wizards' Tower, now they're opening uncontrollable abyssal rifts!
Perhaps the fools should leave the dangerous magic to us next time!

steps.player: Oh, that reminds me. That incantation didn't appear to be written on parchment. What was it?

steps.npc: Hmm... probably the flesh of an abyssal creature. Why do you ask?

steps.player: Oh, I just thought it might be human flesh. I'm relieved it wasn't!

steps.npc: You've been spending too much time with your friends in the Order of Wizards! I know that we Zamorakians have a bad reputation, but do you really think we'd be so barbaric?

steps.text: other
If this is not the first time using this option:

steps.npc: Ah yes, the one that led those fools in the Order of Wizards to open an uncontrollable abyssal rift! Perhaps they should leave the dangerous magic to us next time!
Not to mention that they tried to convince you that we wrote that incantation on human flesh! Their lies never cease to amaze me!

steps.text: other

options.text: Can you tell me more about the Abyss?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about the Abyss?

steps.npc: It is a hard place to describe. We often refer to it as another plane, but that isn't quite accurate. If anything, it is more like a plane that sits between all other planes.

steps.player: Right... And what does it have to do with runecrafting?

steps.npc: In truth, nothing at all. However, it has everything to do with teleportation. You see, time and space work differently in the Abyss.

For example, you can travel to the Abyss, walk a few steps and then exit, only to find yourself somewhere completely different from where you entered. You might even find yourself on a different plane.
You can also enter the Abyss and spend days there, but on your return, only moments have passed.
This is why the Abyss is so useful. It can be used as an effective hub for teleportation. In fact, all teleportation that we know of uses the Abyss, you just don't realise it.

steps.player: Wait... So when I teleport, I'm actually travelling through the Abyss?

steps.npc: In some ways, I suppose you are. Whenever you use a teleport spell, that spell is actually travelling through the Abyss and using it to link two places together.

steps.player: So did you discover the Abyss?

steps.npc: No. Knowledge of the Abyss has existed for a long time, hence it being used for teleportation. However, we believe we may be the first to have properly gained access in centuries.
By complete accident. One of our initiates was performing a routine teleportation experiment when something went wrong. Instead of ending up at their destination, they found themselves in the Abyss.
Now, did you want something else?

steps.text: other

options.text: Can you tell me more about your group?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about your group?

steps.npc: I suppose you have proven yourself trustworthy. We are a group of mages in service to Zamorak. Our group is called the Zamorak Magical Institute, or Z.M.I. for short.
Few actually know of us. Saradominist groups like the Order of Wizards hold sway over these lands, so we are forced to work in the shadows. However, make no mistake, our power far exceeds theirs.

steps.player: You don't seem to like the Order of Wizards very much.

steps.npc: And why would we? Did you know that the Order of Wizards wasn't always a Saradominist group? Once they allowed mages of all faiths to study with them, but they became greedy.
They started to desire more control. They banned Zamorakian wizards from certain areas of study, claiming them to be too dangerous. In reality, they just wanted that knowledge for themselves.
It all went wrong for them, of course. A Zamorakian wizard made a great breakthrough in teleportation magic, but the Saradominists stole his research.
They used it to perform a ritual, but their lack of understanding caused it to go wrong. The entire Wizards' Tower burnt down. Many were killed, and years of research was destroyed.
Naturally, they blamed the Zamorakians. Claimed we intentionally burnt the tower down. After the tower was rebuilt, we were banished from the Order of Wizards and forced underground.

steps.player: And that's how the Z.M.I. was formed?

steps.npc: Exactly.
Now, did you want something else?

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Very well.

standard-dialogue-while-wearing-god-item.npc: How dare you wear such disrespectful attire in this holy place? Remove those immediately if you wish to speak to me.

standard.player: How'd that work out for them?

standard.text: Pretty well - only one died. Still, they got it working...sort of. This ancient technology can be tricky.

steps.text: Before level [#] Magic:
The spellbook panel is opened.

steps.npc: This is your spell book, this contains all the spells you can cast. To cast a spell, you will need to have the required magic level and have the right amount of the runes used to cast the spell.
To check the level and runes required to cast a spell, hover your mouse cursor over the spell.
If you have the right amount of runes and the magic level the spell will light up, meaning you will be able to cast it.
When you have a combat spell available, click on it once, then select your target. A good target would be a monster that is below your combat level.
Try rats in the castle or, if you're feeling brave, the goblins to the west have been causing a nuisance of themselves.
Nemarti, the Ranged Combat tutor and I both give out items every 30 minutes, however you must choose whether you want runes or ranged equipment.
To claim runes, right-click on me and choose Claim, to claim ranged equipment right-click on the Ranged Combat tutor and select Claim.

steps.text: Before level [#] Runecraft:

steps.npc: As you're fairly new to runecrafting you should start with air runes and mind runes.
You will need a talisman for the rune you would like to create. You can right-click on it and select the Locate option. This will tell you the rough location of the altar.
When you find the ruined altar, use the talisman on it to be transported to a temple where you can craft your runes.

To make one, take a tiara and talisman to the ruins and use the tiara on the temple altar. This will bind the talisman to your tiara.

steps.npc: I am the great Malignius Mortifer, wielder of strange and terrible powers. These lowly followers of mine are dedicated students of the magical arts. Their business is to follow me and learn all they can.
You may believe that, but even if you strike one down, another will rise up within minutes.

steps.text: If Rune Mysteries has been completed:

steps.npc: Ah, you are an inquisitive fellow. I shall speak of the great Wizards' Tower, destroyed by fire many years ago...
Many say it was the greatest building in the history of Gielinor, a magnificent monument to human ingenuity.
Yet when humans are offered great power, they so often buy it at the cost of their principles.
Wizards who claimed allegiance to Saradomin began to insist that magic be restricted to the few they deemed 'worthy' of such powers.
Before long, those who did not share their fatuous obsession with Saradomin were excluded from the Tower completely. This state of affairs could not continue.
One dark night, a brave band of magi loyal to the great Lord Zamorak stormed the Tower. Despite heavy losses, they fought their way up the levels until they reached the Great Library.

Alas, they were trapped and could not steal the precious records. But before they could be defeated, the bravest of them took it upon himself to blast the writings into nothingness, destroying the library.
The ensuing fire raced through the tower, and none escaped its fury. Some say that Lord Zamorak himself fanned the flames to ensure the destruction of his enemies!

steps.npc: Much of that knowledge was lost, and some has never yet been rediscovered. Still, your efforts on behalf of my colleagues have not been wasted! Once again, the forces of Zamorak can create unlimited runestones!

I bid you farewell for now.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: Wow! You'd do that for me?

steps.player: On second thoughts, I think I'll keep them for myself.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: Oh... You didn't have to tease me like that.

steps.player: Sure. I'll probably find more while I'm down here anyway.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: I can't thank you enough! I can finally escape this place!
You hand over the 100 hallowed marks and the man departs.

steps.player: It feels nice to do the right thing.

standard-dialogue-after-giving-him-100-h.player: Wait, why are you still here? I gave you the 100 Hallowed marks you need to escape.

standard-dialogue-after-giving-him-100-h.speaker: Man

standard-dialogue-after-giving-him-100-h.speaker: Man

steps.speaker: Man

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: Phew, I made it! Time for a break.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: Thank Saradomin that mysterious stranger gave me this ring or I'd be toast!

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: That trap was harder than I thought! Perhaps I'm not cut out for this.

standard.text: Excuse me!

standard.player: Oh sorry, what did I do?

standard.speaker: Man

standard.speaker: Man
standard.text: Get over it.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: It stinks down here.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: Can't you just leave me alone.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: I don't trust that fish monger.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: Lighting fires in an enclosed space is probably not a good idea. Oh well.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: I guess it's not all bad down here. At least we have a pub.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: I'll leave this place one day. You'll see.

standard-dialogue-variant-1.speaker: Man
standard-dialogue-variant-1.text: An outsider! Can you get me out of this hell hole?

standard-dialogue-variant-1.player: Sorry, that's not what I'm here to do.

standard-dialogue-variant-2.speaker: Man
standard-dialogue-variant-2.text: Go away. People from the outside shut us in like animals. I have nothing to say to you.

standard.speaker: Man
standard.text: We don't have good days here anymore. Curse King Tyras.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: His army curses our city with this plague then wanders off again, leaving us to clear up the pieces.

options.text: I'm looking for a woman called Elena.

steps.player: I'm looking for a woman called Elena.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.text: Not heard of her.

standard.npc: Nilsal.

standard.player: Hello there. You don't seem too happy.

standard.npc: It's far too cold up here. Ralos' Rise is cold, but this is something else! I have to be here though. If this beast has any connections to the Old Ones, it might also have connections to Ralos and Ranul!
Me being here also keeps the dwarves a bit happier as well. They keep claiming they're the ones doing all the work and that there needs to be more humans up here helping.
I don't think so. I've seen plenty of people come up here and get involved. The dwarves don't actually do any of the fighting anyway. They just go in and do some mining once the danger has passed.

standard.player: I can't imagine they'd be happy to hear you say that.

standard.npc: Good point. Forget I said anything.

standard.player: Who are you and what is this place?

standard.npc: My name is Mandrith.
I collect valuable resources and pawn off access to them to foolish adventurers, like yourself.
You should take a look inside my arena. There's an abundance of valuable resources inside.

standard.player: And I can take whatever I want?

standard.npc: It's all yours. All I ask is you pay the upfront fee.

standard.player: Will others be able to kill me inside?

standard.npc: Yes. These walls will only hold them back for so long.
Haha! For the right price, I won't deny any one access to my arena. Even if their intention is to kill you.
My arena holds many treasures that I've acquired at great expense, adventurer. Their bounty can come at a price.
One day, adventurer, I will boast ownership of a much larger, much more dangerous arena than this. Take advantage of this offer while it lasts.

standard.npc: Do not think me rude outerlander, but our customs forbid me talking to you. All contact with outerlanders must be vetted by our chieftain, Brundt.
He is standing just over there. He will speak for the tribe.

after-the-fremennik-trials.npc: Hey! It's [Fremennik name]! Let me buy you a drink!
There ya go! Anyone who can drink like you earns my respect!

standard.npc: You! I bet you're with them!
The frogs!

standard.prompt: Start The Ribbiting Tale of a Lily Pad Labour Dispute quest?

steps.player: Frogs? What are you on about?

steps.npc: Ah, I see. So you're going to play dumb are you? Well I won't fall for your lies!

steps.player: I promise I have no idea what you're on about. If you explain, maybe I can help you?

steps.npc: It's those frogs on the other side of the oasis! They're out to get us! All of us! If someone doesn't kill them all, we'll be living our lives as their slaves!

steps.player: I see... How about I head over there and take a look?

steps.npc: You want to go near them? Well then you're a fool! I will watch from a safe distance as they dine on your corpse!

steps.text: The Ribbiting Tale of a Lily Pad Labour Dispute quest is started.

steps.player: Okay then... Well provided that doesn't happen, I'll be back shortly to let you know what I've found.
I think I'm just going to go now. You clearly have some... issues that you need to get on top of.

steps.npc: That's it! You walk away! Just remember, I know the truth!

standard-dialogue-once-after-completing-.npc: Hello again. You helped forge my alliance with the frogs against those disgusting flies. Please feel free to use my farming patch in return. It's the least I can do.

options.text: Would you look after my crops for me?
Can you give me any farming advice?

standard.npc: Hello. Here for a drink? You've picked the right place if so.

standard-dialogue-dialogue-1.npc: Hi there. So much to see here!

standard-dialogue-dialogue-1.player: Yep, could be looking all day!

standard-dialogue-dialogue-1.npc: Yes, I just learned more about some priestly warriors and a staff of the gods.

standard-dialogue-dialogue-1.player: Sounds fun, how did you do that?

standard-dialogue-dialogue-1.npc: Ahh, I'm big on quests me, love questing. So when I've done one, I check here with 'Historian' Minas to see if I can help the Museum out with some information. Sometimes they already know it, or don't want to know,
and sometimes it earns me a reward or two.

standard-dialogue-dialogue-1.player: That sounds really good. Perhaps I should do the same!

standard-dialogue-dialogue-1.npc: You should, as well as everything else there is here in the Museum. Did you know they have a really fun- looking display down in the basement? I love monkeys.

standard-dialogue-dialogue-1.player: I'll check it out. Got to get going now, nice talking to you.

standard-dialogue-dialogue-2.player: Hello, what are you doing here?

standard-dialogue-dialogue-2.npc: Oh, just taking a look at these displays. I'm a bit of a history buff.

standard-dialogue-dialogue-2.player: Really? Tell me something I didn't know!

standard-dialogue-dialogue-2.npc: Well, did you know that Bob the Cat is... no, no... you'd never believe me anyway.
No, no. Couldn't possibly ruin the surprise.
If you really want to know, go talk to Unferth in his house in Burthorpe.

standard-dialogue-dialogue-3.npc: Oh, hello. I was just looking at this display here.
Yes, one I just updated by talking to 'Historian' Minas. I'm a bit of a quester you see.

standard-dialogue-dialogue-3.player: Okay, I'll let you get on then.

standard-dialogue-dialogue-3.npc: Hmm, yes. Okay. Don't forget to check out the Natural History exhibit - you could learn a lot.

standard-dialogue-dialogue-4.npc: Yes, that's it, just like that. Mustn't forget the map either....hmm...what else?
Oh, hello there. Sorry, was a bit engrosed in updating this display. I've just been out questing and thought I'd stop off here you see. It's quite rewarding too.

standard-dialogue-dialogue-4.player: Yes, well, no need to ignore me.

standard-dialogue-dialogue-4.npc: No offence intended, my dear chap. Just very interested in this history stuff, that's all.

standard-dialogue-dialogue-4.player: Okay. Have you seen the Natural History exhibit in the basement?

standard-dialogue-dialogue-4.npc: Oh, yes, marvellous isn't it! I particularly like the wyvern, very interesting considering they've never found a live specimen. And to think they could possibly have been flapping around at one time!

standard-dialogue-dialogue-4.player: A bit like the crazy gnomes and their gliders. Have you seen the model they have upstairs?

standard-dialogue-dialogue-4.npc: Yes, very intricate isn't it? Worrying to think some people risk their lives in them! You wouldn't catch me up in one. Had a chat with Jacques while I was up there, the art critic...he's a bit funny in the head.
Well, he thinks he's going to get an entire portrait gallery to himself!

standard-dialogue-dialogue-4.player: Who knows, the Museum just got really big and appears to have cash. They might entertain him with his very own floor - we'll see.

standard-dialogue-dialogue-4.npc: I guess so. Wonder what poetry he'll come up with then! Still, I must get on with this display. See you around I hope!

if-the-player-hasn-t-completed-the-dig-s.npc: Yes, good aren't they! Have you done the quest?
Oh you should, it lets you get into that bit where they clean the finds, and you can join in!

if-the-player-hasn-t-completed-the-dig-s.player: Sounds fun, I should probably check it out.

standard.npc: I do not speak to outlanders.
Maybe you should speak with Rellekka's Chieftain.

after-the-fremennik-isles.npc: I am Maria Gunnars. What can I do for you?

steps.npc: Sure.

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: Well, as I have mentioned, I am from an island called Jatizso, while my wife is from another island called Neitiznot. Neitiznot is a far less sophisticated and successful island which will not see reason with Jatizso.

steps.npc: Ne it iz not!

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: Ja it iz so!

steps.npc: Ahem, anyway, the islands are in a small volcanic archipelago north of here.
Along with the main isles there are numerous small islands and a frozen northern island that was recently overrun by trolls.

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: Jatizso is rich in minerals, and trades extensively, while Neitiznot has stolen all the decent arable land.

steps.npc: Only because Jatizso hogs all the wealth.

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: Well, that wealth is needed to buy the food from Neitiznot at extortionate rates!

steps.npc: Only because Jatizso hogs all the wealth!

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: Ok Maria, stop that!

steps.npc: Ok dear!

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: Thank you!

steps.npc: Where was I? Yup, that covers the layout of the islands.

options.text: Tell me about the islands' history.

after-the-fremennik-isles.player: Tell me about the islands' history.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Well now, the history of the isles is a bloody tale. When told in its intended form it takes 9 days and 9 nights. However, I will give you the abridged version.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Four generations ago there was a mighty king who ruled wisely and was loved by all.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: He had many sons, most of whom proved themselves in the usual Fremennik ways of fighting, sailing, drinking and so on.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: His youngest two sons, however, were a problem. Ever since they were old enough to hit one another they had bickered and fought.

steps.npc: Their names were Jatizso and Neitiznot.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Hey! Who's telling this story?

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Ahem. At the time it was customary for the Kings' sons to claim a prize from his treasury when they came of age.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Each brother rallied support and strode out to confront the other on the field of battle to claim the same prize.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: The brothers met on the field, limbs were bruised, bones were crushed and heads clashed.

steps.npc: They probably didn't notice the head-clashing bit. Too thick skulled!

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Can I finish the story without interruptions?

steps.npc: Carry on dear.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Anyway, long into the night they fought, until they stood alone, facing each other.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: On the second day the old king, whose patience was exhausted, strode out onto the field and demanded to know who had claimed his prize.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso looked at his father and told him yes, it was his, to which the other called out 'No! It's not'.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: And so, the argument continued through to the third day, with the sounds of 'Jah! 'tis so!', 'Ne! It's not!' echoing over the field, becoming more hoarse as the darkness enveloped the brothers.

steps.npc: Bah! What they needed was a good clip round the ear.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: At the end of the third day, when the brothers lay unable to move, let alone stand, the King stood between them in shame.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: As punishment for their squabbling he banished his sons from his realm, ordering that neither should return until they had conquered lands of their own.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso set sail with a band of loyal followers, sailing into the east, while Neitiznot went west.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso ventured far into uncharted oceans, his crew dwindling as the trials of sailing and sea monsters took them.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso's ship limped through the frozen wastes, in need of repairs, fighting off pirates who thought them easy pickings.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: At last a promising land was sighted, a land rich in minerals, deep fjords and sweeping mountains.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso claimed the land and named it after himself.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: A mighty citadel was constructed to protect his land; then Jatizso set forth to explore his new kingdom.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Crossing a few fjords, Jatizso spied an island which remained green and fertile, even at such latitude.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: With a mighty cheer Jatizso and his men marched on the island. Upon reaching the island, however, they discovered a wooden stockade.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Determined to be master of all the land, Jatizso stood in front of the gates. He looked up and demanded that those within the stockade surrendered.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso was horrified when his brother appeared on the battlements and cried 'This is my land! Go find yer own'. To which his brother replied 'No it's not!', throwing some rocks for good measure.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: And so the blood feud continued.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: The fighting between the towns has continued for generations with little sign of improvement.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Quite recently a massive troll army seized one of the islands to the north, while our townships' militias were busy fighting one another.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: They marched down and razed Neitiznot to the ground while Neitiznot's troops laid siege to Jatizso.

steps.npc: The smoke damage was atrocious, I had to replace my entire wardrobe.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Yes, dear.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Anyway, a hasty sort of peace has been agreed until the trolls are dealt with.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: But you can still see the bitter rivalry as guards hurl insults between the towns.

options.text: Tell me about Burger Mawnis Burowgar.

steps.player: Tell me about Burger Mawnis Burowgar.

steps.npc: Well Burgher Mawnis Burowgar is a gentle soul at heart. His kinsfolk are happy and content with their lot.

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: 'Soft' is the word we use in Jatizso.

steps.npc: Well a soft Burgher is better than a stupid King.
Anyway, there was a time when Burgher Burowgar was similar to King Sorvott.
Argumentative, short tempered; I am sure you know what I mean.
The change happened when the trolls came and razed Neitiznot to the ground.

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: You mean while Neitiznot's militias were assaulting Jatizso.

steps.npc: Yes, well our tribes have been at war for nearly four generations now.
Anyway, the Burgher lost his wife and youngest son in the trolls' raid and has been a changed man since.

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: May their journey to our ancestors' halls be swift.

steps.npc: Personally, I am much happier with the considerate Burgher we have now.

options.text: Can you ferry me to Neitiznot?

steps.player: Can you ferry me to Neitiznot?

steps.npc: Let's set sail then.

steps.text: Leaving Rellekka for Neitiznot.

steps.player: I just stopped to say hello.

steps.npc: Thanks, and good luck with the Burgher's tasks.
Bye

talking-to-maria-gunnars-on-neitiznot.npc: Hi, [Fremennik name], you should speak with Burgher Mawnis Burowgar in the main chambers. Do you have any questions?

talking-to-maria-gunnars-on-neitiznot.prompt: What do you want to know about?

steps.npc: My husband is a typical Fremennik, being both headstrong and brave.
We fell in love when we were young, but as there was a war between our isles, we were ordered to stop seeing each other by our parents.
This didn't stop Mord climbing the wailing tower, on his side of the channel between our isles, to sing to me every night.
After Mord's voice broke, his singing voice was lost, but I still listened to his terrible sonnets each and every night.
Until one night there was no singing! Then, far below me, I heard a gentle voice calling my name.
Mord had stolen his father's boat to come and fetch me from my prison
and from that day forth we have lived in Rellekka.
My husband does not speak of the inhabitants of the isle of Jatizso much.
He has little positive to say about his parents, so he chooses not to speak of them in my presence. The only thing I've noticed is that everyone on that island seems very sad...

steps.prompt: Who do you want to know about?

options.text: Tell me about King Sorvott IV.

steps.player: Tell me about King Sorvott IV.

steps.npc: King Sorvott IV follows in the footsteps of a line of kings who have reigned since Jatizso himself passed away. It is rumoured that the King has no heir and is seeking a bride to bear him children. Given his
personality I'm not surprised he hasn't found a bride yet!
To be honest with you, I do not keep up to date with all the goings on here now that I have a home in Rellekka.
However, Neitiznot seems a happy place! The Burgher seems a wiser rule than King Sorvott, although I believe he is worried about the trolls at the moment. They seem to be a big threat.

options.text: Can you ferry me to Rellekka?

steps.player: Can you ferry me to Rellekka?

steps.npc: Sure.

steps.text: Leaving Neitiznot for Rellekka.

options.text: I have nothing to ask you right now.

steps.player: I have nothing to ask you right now.

steps.npc: Fare thee well.

options.text: Can you give me any farming advice?

steps.player: Can you give me any farming advice?

steps.npc: The only way to cure a bush or tree of disease is to prune away the diseased leaves with a pair of secateurs. For all other crops I would just apply some plant-cure.
Tree seeds must be grown in a plantpot of soil into a sapling, and then transferred to a tree patch to continue growing to adulthood.
You can put up to ten potatoes, cabbages or onions in vegetable sacks, although you can't have a mix in the same sack.
You can buy all the farming tools from farming shops, which can be found close to the allotments.
Bittercap mushrooms can only be grown in a special patch in Morytania, near the Mort Myre swamp. There the ground is especially dank and suited to growing poisonous fungii.
Supercompost is far better than normal compost, but more expensive to make. You need to rot the right type of item; show me an item, and I'll tell you if it's super- compostable or not.
There is a special patch for growing Belladonna - I believe that it is somewhere near Draynor Manor, where the ground is a tad 'unblessed'.
Applying compost to a patch will not only reduce the chance that your crops will get diseased, but you will also grow more crops to harvest.
If you want to grow fruit trees you could try a few places: Catherby, Brimhaven, Gnome Stronghold and the Farming Guild all have fruit tree patches.
You can fill plantpots with soil from any empty patch, if you have a gardening trowel.

Hops are good for brewing ales. I believe there's a brewery up in Keldagrim somewhere, and I've heard rumours that a place called Phasmatys used to be good for that type of thing. 'Fore they all died, of course.
Vegetables, hops and flowers need constant watering - if you ignore my advice, you will sooner or later find yourself in possession of a dead farming patch.
You can put up to five tomatoes, strawberries, apples, bananas or oranges into a fruit basket, although you can't have a mix in the same basket.
Don't just throw away your weeds after you've raked a patch - put them in a compost bin and make some compost.

standard-dialogue-after-a-kingdom-divide.npc: Indeed. I never thought I'd be back here.
We won! The Council are out, and we have what Kourend really needed. We have a king!
Of course, King Artur ended up taking the throne from his father a little faster than anyone expected, so he needs plenty of guidance. That's where I come in!

standard-dialogue-after-a-kingdom-divide.player: So you're helping to advise the King?

standard-dialogue-after-a-kingdom-divide.npc: Exactly! When the people voted on Rose's Accord, they voted for the Hosidius family to become the new royal family. From a technical standpoint that means they voted for King Artur.

standard-dialogue-after-a-kingdom-divide.player: But in reality it was his father they expected to rule.

standard-dialogue-after-a-kingdom-divide.npc: Precisely. My job is to advise King Artur and ensure his actions have a positive impact on the people that he now rules.
Not too bad. While he lacks experience, the King has a good heart. He wants to do the right thing, and he has the support needed to do it.
Mind you, he could do with listening to his mother less. She's always whispering things in his ear. She forgets that he's the one in charge, not her.
Still, I'm sure he just needs time to adjust. I have no doubt that under King Artur, Kourend will prosper like never before.

standard-dialogue-after-a-kingdom-divide.player: I'm sure you're right. See you around Martin.

steps.npc: Only a king can right the wrongs of the Council! And only you can make that happen!
How long will you keep your eyes closed? Their corruption surrounds you!
This kingdom will never be safe while the Council rule!
You deserve the truth! They won't give it to you!
The Council have wronged you! It's time to make things right!
Together, we can bring an end to the treachery of the Council!
The Council care only for themselves! It's time for a ruler who cares for you!
Kourend is a kingdom! A kingdom needs a king, not a council!
Democracy? What democracy? It's all a façade!
People of Kourend, you have been lied to!

standard.npc: Hey newbie! I'm the Master Navigator - let's teach you how to get around.
Ha. You've worked your way around to me, but this island is bigger than you think! I will show you by teaching you how to use the world map. First things first, you will need to open your world map.
You can find this in the top right side of the screen, look for the flashing globe icon.

standard-dialogue-after-looking-at-the-w.npc: Well done, you have found your world map.
The world map can show where you are in the world, as well as where other places are. You can find where you are by looking for the yellow X icon.
You may have noticed all the icons on the map, these icons have a meaning behind each one. You can find out what the icon means by looking at the map key.
To open or close the map key you will have to click the scroll looking icon in the bottom left part of the map.
Once opened, you will see a list of all the different icons on the map, as well as some text next to the icon telling you what the icon is. You can click on an icon in the key.
Every icon that is the same as the one you just selected, will start to flash.
Lastly, next to the key you will see there is a search bar. You can click on the search bar and type in a location. You can then press enter and the map will move to the specified location.
Now you know the basics of the world map, I am going to task you with making your way to the Quest Guide. You can find him just north of here. Go out the door to the west and follow the path.

Remember that your world map is just a larger version of your mininmap, with the difference that you can click on your minimap to navigate around. You will also see icons on your minimap as well, just like the world map.
