steps.text: If the player has level 1-20 Smithing:

steps.npc: You're going to need to get your hand on some metal bars. You could do this by mining your own ores and smelting them at a furnace.
There is a furnace located in Lumbridge, just north of the castle opposite the general store.
If you are looking for some ore, there is a mine east of Varrock. There you can find some copper and tin ore. Don't forget to bring a pickaxe.
When you have your bars, bring them to an anvil to open the smithing interface. If the item name is in black, this means you do not have the level to smith the item.
If the item name is in white, this means you do have the level to smith the item. You will see the bars required to smith the item underneath the name of the item.
If the number of bars is in orange, this means you do not have enough bars to smith the item. If it is in green, this means you have enough bars for the item.
Is there anything else you would like to know?

steps.text: other

As you get better you'll find you will be able to smith Mithril and eventually Adamantite and even Runite. This can be very lucrative but very expensive on the coal front.
It may be worth you stockpiling coal for a while before attempting these difficult metals or even sticking to good old reliable iron by the bucket load.
If you want to stop yourself from failing to smith iron, I suggest purchasing some rings of forging. Be aware that they will break after a certain number of bars are smelted.
If you want to save on coal, you could try smithing your bars over at the Blast Furnace in Keldagrim.
If you are looking for something more interesting to smith, you could talk to Otto Godblessed about smithing hastae.

steps.player: What kind of things can I smith?

steps.npc: There are many things you can make, from weapons to your good old fashioned armour.
Weapons are the cheapest to smith. They range from a measly one bar, all the way to three bars.
Armour can be the costliest item to smith, the cost of each item ranges from a measly one bar all the way up to a whopping five bars.
Some weapons and armour, such as darts, will require you to have gained knowledge on how to smith them. This is due to the complex nature of the weapon.
You might find that other items don't require conventional bars you would gather. Some may require you to piece blades back together or even infuse a crystal into a piece of armour.

When I'm not being drained of blood I'm fixing up the ghetto.
I just try to make a living the best way I can. You haven't got some food have you?

Why do you wanna know?

Life's so very hard here. Before too long they'll be wanting to have another blood tithing and then I'll feel just awful again.
You must be new here, else you'd know for sure. It's where we have to give a blood tithe to the vampyres. They do it on a weekly basis, a different sector each week so they don't kill us all off.

steps.npc: Yep, that's where we are at the moment. This place, Meiyerditch, is just one large ghetto.
The city is sectioned off so that the vampyres can collect blood tithes on a rotational basis. That way they don't kill us all off in one go.

options.text: What do you know about the vampyres?

steps.player: What do you know about the vampyres?

steps.npc: They're monsters, I know that much. I've never known anything else, but I have a feeling it might be nice to not have to live in fear the whole time. Worrying if I'm going to make the next blood tithe quota.
I know that the juveniles are the lowest form of the vampyres. Apparently they were human once, converted by the vampyres.
Then you have juvinates. They're initiated juveniles who've had some training and are starting to get some powers.
After that you have the vyres. They're nasty... really nasty.

options.text: What do you know about Drakan?

steps.player: What do you know about Drakan?

steps.text: Before completing A Taste of Hope:

steps.npc: Drakan? Which one: Ranis or Vanescula?

steps.player: Well, I was referring to the main Drakan, you know, the overlord of Morytania.

steps.npc: Hmm, nothing has been seen of him for many years now. Some people say they occasionally see Ranis or Vanescula flying about, but it's not too often.

steps.text: continue

steps.npc: Vanescula?

steps.player: Well, I was referring to the main Drakan, you know, the overlord of Morytania.

steps.npc: Hmm, nothing has been seen of him for many years now. Some people say they occasionally see Vanescula flying about, but it's not too often.

steps.text: After completing Sins of the Father:

steps.npc: No one had seen anything of him for years, they say he's back now though. We shouldn't talk of him any more though, the vyrewatch might not like it.

options.text: What is there to do around here?

steps.player: What is there to do around here?

steps.npc: To do? Around here? Survive! Eke out an existence and just live for another day, that's it really.

The juvinates organise work crews to mine the daeyalt, fix the walls, the castles and so on. If we refuse to do the work, they put us on double tithes and you can't do that for long before you dry up.
If you want to escape, there's only one way. Anyone who survives in the theatre gets to leave. It's pointless though. No one survives.

options.text: Is there anything I can do to help?

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help?

steps.npc: It's very nice of you to offer, my friend, but I shouldn't expect that you could do anything. The vampyres are just too powerful to overcome.
They say this place once had a Saradominist Queen. Even she could not withstand the vampyres. Anyone who has challenged their power in the past has come undone.
I've been working on getting some things fixed up around here. Hopefully we can eventually make a proper home out of this city.
Just trying to make a living really. Things are a lot better now the vampyres aren't taking our blood, but it's still going to be a long time before we get this place in a good state.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Well, the vampyres aren't taking our blood anymore, and they've promised to help us rebuild the city. Still, it's going to take a long time to fix this place up. Most people have chosen to leave instead.

It's nice that they let us watch the performances in the Theatre now. It's fun seeing how good some of those warriors from Misthalin are!

standard.npc: Greetings adventurer, I am the Melee combat tutor. Is there anything I can do for you?

steps.npc: Well adventurer, the first thing you will need is a sword and a shield appropriate for your level.
Make sure to equip your sword and shield. Click on them in your inventory, they will disappear from your inventory and move to your worn items. You can see your worn items in the worn items tab here.
When you are wielding your sword you will then be able to see the correct options in the combat interface.
There are four different melee styles. Accurate, aggressive, defensive and controlled. Not all weapons will have all four styles though.

steps.player: Interesting, what does each style do?

steps.npc: Well I am glad you asked. The accurate style will give you experience points in your Attack skill, you will also find you will deal damage more frequently as a result of being, well, more accurate.
Next we have the aggressive style. This style will give you experience points in your Strength skill. When using this style you will notice that your attacks will hit a little harder.
Now for the defensive style, this style will give you experience points in your Defensive skill. When using this style you will notice that you get hit less often.
Finally, we have the controlled style. This style will give you the same amount of experience as the other styles would but shared across all three of the combat skills.
If you were using the training sword for example, there are four different attack types. Stab, lunge, slash and block.
Each type uses one of the attack styles. Stab uses accurate, lunge and slash use aggressive and block uses defensive.
To find out which style an attack type uses, hover your mouse cursor over the style button.

steps.npc: If you are in a clan, you should gather some clan members and try out clan wars. There you can see which clan is better than the other by fighting each other in an arena.
Both activities are safe minigame, which means if you die you will not loose any of your items. You can get to them by using the teleport option in your minigames tab.
There is also the wilderness. The wilderness is north of Varrock and you can fight other players there. But bare in mind if you die to another player in the wilderness you will lose your stuff.
But this also means that if you kill another player you will be able to take their stuff too.
Only go into the wilderness with items you are willing to lose and pay attention to the wilderness level you are in. The higher the level you go, more player will be able to attack you.
You can find which player can attack you by checking your combat level.
Minus the wilderness level from your combat level to find the lowest level that you can attack, then add the wilderness level to your combat level to find the highest level that you can attack.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-destroys.speaker: Messenger
standard-dialogue-if-the-player-destroys.text: Look, you can destroy that letter as many times as you want, but it won't change anything. The sender isn't the kind of individual who takes no for an answer, so for both of our sakes, please just read it.
The messenger has given you a letter... again.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-destroys.speaker: Messenger
standard-dialogue-if-the-player-destroys.text: Please... don't keep doing this. You don't know who you're dealing with...
The messenger has given you a letter... again.
The messenger says nothing as he hands you another letter. However, the fear in his eyes is clear to see.

standard.player: Hello, I wonder if you could help me on this whole brewing thing...

standard.npc: Woooo wooo wooooo woooo.

standard-dialogue-with-ghostspeak.player: Hello, I wonder if you could help me on this whole brewing thing...

standard-dialogue-with-ghostspeak.npc: I might be able to - what do you need to know?

steps.npc: Well first off you need to fill the vat with water - two bucketfuls should do the trick. Then you'll need to put in two handfuls of barley malt - that's roasted barley by the way.
After that you'll be putting your main ingredient in - this will decide which ale it is you're brewing. There should be some good guides around with recipes in.
Lastly you pour a pot full of ale yeast in, which'll start it off fermenting. Then all you have to do is wait for the good stuff.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: First you'll need some apples. You'll need to crush them using this cider-press - four apples should make a full bucket of apple-mush. Take four buckets of mush and fill up the vat.
After that you pour a pot full of ale yeast in, which'll start it off fermenting. Then all you have to do is wait for the good stuff.

steps.text: other

options.text: What do I do once my ale has matured?

steps.player: What do I do once my ale has matured?

steps.npc: Well, once you've got a full vat of the good stuff, just turn the valve and your barrel will fill up with eight pints of whatever your chosen tipple is. Mind it's an empty barrel, though.

steps.text: other

options.text: Do you have any spare ale yeast?

steps.npc: Well, as a matter of fact I do, although I wouldn't describe it as spare. This ale yeast I've got is the best you can get - if you've got a pot I'll fill it for you for 5 ectotokens. Coins are of no use to me.

steps.text: Without an empty pot or 5 ectotokens:

steps.player: I don't have an empty pot, or enough ectotokens I'm afraid.

steps.text: other

options.text: That's all I need to know, thanks.

standard.npc: She angs out int souf east of ouw island.
Huh?
Yeah? Need something?

steps.npc: Rock. Lots of it.
Rock. This here is Stonecutter Outpost. We get rock, cut it, then sell it.

steps.player: So you're pretty far from home then?

steps.npc: What? No. We go back to Cam Torum sometimes, but this is home.
Need something else?
Then why you keep staring? Get gone!

standard.npc: Oh... Nilsal. Unusual to see someone up here. What can I do for you?

options.text: What do you do around here?

steps.player: What do you do around here?

steps.npc: I used to work downstairs... but I started using the lab after hours for my own projects and the supervisor found out. Now I've been assigned to rooftop duty to look after the plants.

steps.player: Sorry to hear that. At least the view is good!

options.text: Do you have any tips for potion production?

steps.player: Do you have any tips for potion production?

steps.text: If the player has not joined the Alchemical Society:

steps.npc: I do, but only for fellow members of the Alchemical Society. Perhaps you should join up if you're interested in Herblore.

steps.text: If the player has joined the Alchemical Society:

steps.npc: Yes... Make good use of the digweed once they're ready to pick. Choose which potion you use it on wisely!
Oh, and the processing tables can be sped up a bit if you use them correctly. You might need to do some experimenting to figure that out.

options.text: Thanks! I'd better be going now.

steps.player: Thanks! I'd better be going now.

standard.npc: My husband is serving near the Lizardman Canyon. I'm worried that something might happen to him.
And I lost my job last week. I need to find another one before my savings run out.

standard.player: Oh, that is bad. I'm sorry to hear that.

standard.npc: Well, it's a difficult time for a lot of people I guess. The war with the lizardmen never ends.

standard-dialogue-using-a-guthix-balance.npc: Thanks so much for saving me from being a vampyre. Here, take this certificate, I'm sorry but it's all I can offer as a reward.

standard-dialogue-using-a-guthix-balance.text: You're handed a certificate of treasure as a reward.

standard-dialogue-talking-to-them-again.npc: Thanks for changing me back, it must have been hard for you. I must be off now.

standard.npc: Oh, hello there. I'm afraid I don't have time to talk right now. I'm rather busy. Come back some other time please.

standard-dialogue-after-talking-to-ruper.npc: Who am I? Why, how impertinent! I am a princess and I will be spoken to like one. Now be off with you. I have no time for scruffy adventurers like yourself!

standard-dialogue-after-talking-to-ruper.player: I notice there is a dwarf up in the tower there. Why is he up there?

standard-dialogue-after-talking-to-ruper.npc: I do believe that is none of your business, young scallyrumpit! Now kindly leave.

standard-dialogue-after-completion-of-gr.npc: Thanks again for finding my pendant. I felt so lost without it.

standard.npc: Hey it's the Hero! Wow! You're amazing, how on earth did you manage to tackle those two juvinates and Gadderanks? And the town is lovely, you've done a great job!

steps.npc: I'm Mihail, I'm trying to stay warm by this fire.

options.text: How do you like your town?

steps.player: How do you like your town?

steps.npc: It's just perfect, thanks so much for your efforts.
Oh, not much really, we're all still hiding from the vampyres and eking out a living from this terrible place, hopefully soon we'll be strong enough to make the journey to the temple on the Salve.

options.text: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: Not as far as I know, we have some basic amenities now which is so very useful, we're all incredibly grateful to you. I've never really seen or known a hero before, so I have nothing to compare one to, but I suspect in
most people's judgement, you would be one! I for one am very pleased to have met you.

after-the-blood-moon-rises.npc: Hey, it's the hero! Thank you so much for everything you've done, not just for us, but for all of Morytania!

steps.npc: I'm Mihail. I'm just trying to stay warm.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Well, I'd be lying if I said life was suddenly perfect, but it's nice to no longer live in constant fear of the vampyres.

steps.player: What will you do now that you don't have to worry about them?

steps.npc: Well, quite a few of us are working on making the town a bit nicer. Not that there's anything wrong with the work you did of course.
Some of the others don't want to stick around. They reckon it might be safe enough to make the journey up to Paterdomus now. I think they want to start a new life across the Salve.

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.npc: With the town? No, I don't think so. You've done enough to help us anyway.
I suppose if you did want to help in some way though, you could maybe assist those who want to get to Paterdomus. The swamps can still be pretty dangerous.

steps.text: other

standard.npc: Arr? Be ye wantin' te go on account with our gang o' fillibusters?
The powder monkey be takin' a caulk after gettin' rowdy on bumboo, so there be plenty of room for ye.

standard.player: I'll just be over here if you need me.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy.npc: Wanna buy some clothes? Good quality, none of yer rags.

Silly me.

steps.npc: If I say yes will you buy it?
Then no, I was not cleaning it with a blood-covered scimitar.

steps.npc: Found em.

steps.npc: Dunno. There are a load of islands out this way, and a lot of them have little bits and pieces like this scattered around.
The way I see it, there must have been some people out here at one point, then they went away.
Search me.

standard.npc: Hello Adventurer. Welcome to Mill Lane Mill. Can I help you?

steps.npc: I'm Miss Millicent Miller the Miller of Mill Lane Mill. Our family have been milling flour for generations.

steps.player: It's a good business to be in. People will always need flour.

steps.npc: This is Mill Lane Mill. Millers of the finest flour in Gielinor, and home to the Miller family for many generations
We take grain from the field nearby and mill into flour.

Making flour is pretty easy. First of all you need to get some grain. You can pick some from wheat fields. There is one just outside the Mill, but there are many others scattered across Gielinor. Feel free to pick wheat
from our field! There always seems to be plenty of wheat there.

steps.player: Then I bring my wheat here?

steps.npc: Yes, or one of the other mills in Gielinor. They all work the same way. Just take your grain to the top floor of the mill (up two ladders, there are three floors including this one) and then place some grain into the hopper.
Then you need to start the grinding process by pulling the hopper lever. You can add more grain, but each time you add grain you have to pull the hopper lever again.

steps.player: So where does the flour go then?

steps.npc: The flour appears in this room here, you'll need a pot to put the flour into. One pot will hold the flour made by one load of grain

And that's it! You now have some pots of finely ground flour of the highest quality. Ideal for making tasty cakes or delicous bread. I'm not a cook so you'll have to ask a cook to find out how to bake things.

steps.npc: They work by our very own Dorgeshuun magic!

If you ever see a lamp that's gone out, you can fix it by replacing the light orb. You can make new light orbs out of glass, and use a piece of wire on them to add the filament.
There's a machine in the south of the city that makes the wire you need.

first-time-dialogue.npc: This place...? Why, This is the great Fortis Colosseum!
Adventurers come from near and far to test their might within these walls.
Indeed it is. If you are victorious in the Colosseum, the whole of Varlamore shall hear of your name.

first-time-dialogue.player: I imagine its quite the challenge then?

first-time-dialogue.npc: It'll put your skills to the test alright.
Just head through that tunnel behind me and we'll get the show started! Make sure you've got everything you need. Once you're in you can't leave until the end of a wave!
Come and ask if you have any other questions.

options.text: Can you tell me about modifiers?

steps.player: Can you tell me about modifiers?

steps.npc: Yes! After all, they were my idea...
Every time you complete a wave, I'll offer you a choice of three modifiers.
Each modifier will increase the challenge for the rest of the run - So choose wisely!
Some modifiers can be offered multiple times, with the effects then growing in power!
Was there anything else?
Well it's a bit different to just killing monsters and picking up items, as I'm sure you're used to...
After each wave inside the Colosseum, I'll show you the rewards you have earned, as well as what you'll earn from the next wave...
If you aren't confident that you can complete the next wave, you can claim your existing rewards and exit early.
However, if you're confident you can beat the next wave, you can risk your whole reward pile to get even more!
Be careful though. If you die or leave the arena before claiming your loot from me, you will lose all of the rewards you've earned.

steps.player: So I'm guessing the higher the wave, the better the rewards?

steps.npc: Oh, you're good. Exactly that!
Even better - if you manage to finish all of the waves and the final challenge, then you'll be awarded with Dizana's Quiver.
It's a handy piece of kit that you wear on your back to store extra bolts or arrows.

steps.player: That does sound handy! Thanks for explaining all of that.

steps.npc: Anytime, Rookie. Anything else?
It's the measure of your progress inside the Colosseum.

steps.npc: I'm Minimus. It's not my real name of course, but it seems to have stuck. I started out competing here as a gladiator when I was a young'n. After that I became one of the lanistas.
The ones responsible for overseeing the selecting and training of the gladiators.
Eventually, the kingdom gave me the role of Colosseum Master. I still make sure to fit some fighting in, but now I have the honor of managing the fights themselves.

steps.player: So are you not training like the rest of the gladiators?

steps.npc: I have no need! I'm already one of the greatest fighters to grace this arena.

steps.player: Are you at a disadvantage because of your height?

steps.npc: No! How dare you even suggest that! Those spindly human bodies are unfit to go toe to toe with a fine dwarf like myself!
Now, did you need anything else?
Farewell, Rookie.

steps.npc: As you're already here, have a pick so that you can mine the rocks around me.

steps.text: a bronze pickaxe
continue
If the player does not have a pickaxe equipped or in the inventory and has no inventory space:

steps.npc: I'd give you a pick to mine the rocks around me, but you don't have room in your inventory.

steps.text: continue
If the player has a pickaxe equipped or in the inventory:

steps.npc: As you already have a pick, you can mine the rocks around me.

steps.text: continue
If the player is logged into a members' world:

steps.npc: Investigate the mining guild, the entrance to this is in the east of Falador down some steps. It could be most useful to you!
You might also like to check out the coal mine west of Seers' village. This will enable you to use the coal trucks.
I could show you where either of the places are on your map if you like?

options.text: Can you show me where the mining guild is?

steps.player: Can you show me where the mining guild is?

steps.text: The world map opens and pans to the location of the Mining Guild.

options.text: Can you show me where the coal mine is?

steps.player: Can you show me where the coal mine is?

steps.text: The world map opens and pans to the location of the coal truck mining area.
If the player is logged into a free-to-play world:

steps.npc: Investigate the mining guild, the entrance to this is in the east of Falador down some steps. It could be most useful to you!
I could show you where the mining guild is on your map if you like?

steps.text: The world map opens and pans to the location of the Mining Guild.

options.text: Are there any mining related quests?

steps.npc: Oh yes, if you haven't already, speak to Doric who can be found around the anvils north of Falador. I'm sure he can help you out.

steps.text: If the player is a member:

steps.npc: You could investigate the Dig Site east of Varrock, I'm sure you'll find something rewarding there.

steps.text: continue

options.text: Tell me about different rocks and picks.

steps.player: Tell me about different rocks and picks.

steps.npc: Ok then.. here goes....

steps.text: Clay can be mined in many places. Try south west of Varrock or the crafting guild. See the crafting tutor upstairs in Lumbridge Castle for more information on what you can make with clay.
Rune Essence can only be mined at secret places... I don't know where these are but you can speak to the Duke of Lumbridge to find out more.

steps.npc: You can make all sorts of things from clay, if you have the crafting skill. Rune Essence is used for magic to cast spells.

steps.text: Rocks which yield copper ore can be found around here, and other places such as Al Kharid, Rimmington or Varrock mines. They're quite common.
Tin ore is much the same as copper. It can be found around this area as well as Varrock, Al Kharid and the Barbarian Village.
Iron can be mined around Rimmington, Al Kharid and Varrock. It's tricky to smelt though - see the boy at the furnace in Lumbridge for tips.
Look for this icon on your minimap to find the furnace.
You'll need to be a fairly good miner before you can start mining coal. You can find it in the Dwarf mine, Al Kharid and quite a few other places.
Silver can be mined to help you with your crafting. You can find it in the Crafting guild, Al Kharid and many other mines.
Gold requires quite a lot of experience in mining before you can successfully extract it from the rocks. It can be found in Al Kharid, the Crafting guild, Rimmington and other places.
Mithril and Adamantite rocks are fairly rare and require great skill to mine. You can find them in Al Kharid, the Dwarven mines, Lumbridge Swamps and other places.
Runite is the most prized of ores and is very rare. I'll leave you to find where to mine it.

The Bronze Pick is your basic tool of the trade. You can buy one from Bob's Axe shop very cheaply, that's north of here in Lumbridge, I also heard that exploring the castle walls may yield a surprise or two.
The Iron and Steel Picks are faster than the bronze pickaxe, but you will need to progress with your mining a little before you can use them. You can buy them from Nurmof in the Dwarven mines.
Mithril, Adamantite, and Rune Picks may be used as you progress with your skill of mining. They can be obtained from Nurmof in the Dwarven mines.

initial-dialogue.player: Excuse me, I just want to-

options.condition: Before starting The Giant Dwarf:

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Oh, you don't know?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: [He/She] doesn't know?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: [He/She] doesn't know!

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: It is our glorious city!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: The grand city of the dwarves!

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Sparkling jewel of the mountain!

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Keldagrim, our home!

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Oh no, we can't do that.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: We're far too busy.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: You have to keep busy, you see.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Always keep busy, is what our good father used to say.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Besides, there's been some weird going ons in the city.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Don't tell [him/her] that! None of [his/her] business!

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Only fair if [he/she] wants to go into the city.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Oh yes, they only just cleaned up the mess from the last little incident.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: So watch out if you ever do manage to travel to the city! Weird things could happen!

options.text: Any good spots to fish around here?

steps.player: Any good spots to fish around here?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Fish?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Fish?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: What are fish?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: No fish around here.
After Fishing Contest:

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Say, you're the Fishing Champion, aren't you?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: That must be why you were talking about fish then...

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: What are fish?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: But this water here, you see, it comes dripping down from above.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Molten snow, you see.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: What are fish?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Oh, they're these small wriggly things that live in the water.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: But they're not all small! Some can be large!

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: And they don't breathe air.
After Fishing Contest:

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: But [player name] could tell you all about it! After all, [he's/she's] the Fishing Champion!

options.text: What are these mines used for?

steps.player: What are these mines used for?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: What does it look like they're used for?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Isn't it obvious?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: For mining of course!

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: These mines are actually the territory of one of the eight major companies of the mining Consortium.
Before The Giant Dwarf:

steps.player: Mining companies? Where are they at then?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Oh, they all have their headquarters in the city.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: First floor of the palace.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: No need to give [him/her] directions.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: We haul all our goods to the city by ship, you see.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Since the mine carts don't come here.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: But because the river goes right to the city, this is just as easy.

options.text: Can you help me with this rock?
options.condition: During Between a Rock...:

steps.player: Can you help me with this rock down in the mines?
It seems to be unbreakable. I need to know why.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Say, is that Dondakan's rock?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: That big unbreakable rock?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: That's what [he/she] said, isn't? Pay more attention!

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Oh, you're not going to get through there I'm afraid.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: It's unbreakable, you see.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Dondakan's been there for...

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: How long would you say he's been there, Miotvednir?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Eighteen years, Derni, and not a year shorter!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: That's some dedication!

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: But look at what it got him.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Nothing, that's what.

options.text: What material would break that rock?
options.condition: During Between a Rock...:

steps.player: What material would break that rock? You know, the impenetrable one?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Well... have you tried a rune pickaxe?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: An adamantite tool?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: What about a bronze pickaxe?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: A bronze pickaxe??

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: What good would that do?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Well, you never know...

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Don't you think that's the first thing they tried?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Hey, it was just a suggestion!

options.text: Do you know anyone named Rolad?
options.condition: During Between a Rock...:

steps.player: Do you know anyone named Rolad? Some kind of a dwarven scholar?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Sorry, doesn't ring a bell.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Oh yes, I know Rolad!

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Oh, stop winding up the human, Dernu!

steps.player: Do you know where he is right now?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: No idea, why?

options.text: Dondakan wants to shoot me out of a cannon!
options.condition: During Between a Rock...:

steps.player: Dondakan wants to shoot me out of a cannon!

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Oh dear!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: How awful!

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: That's terrible!

steps.player: He thinks I'm actually going to fly through it and land on the other side.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: That sounds a bit daft.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: How would that work?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: I think you're going to hurt your head.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Old Dondakan might have finally lost it.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: He was always obsessed with that rock.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: And gold.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Right, and gold.

options.text: Any tips on how to defeat an evil demon?
options.condition: During Between a Rock...:

steps.player: Any tips on how to defeat an evil demon?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: An evil demon, you say?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: I'd run away if I ever ran into an evil demon.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Don't be such a coward, Dernu!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Well, what would you do then?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: I don't know, I've never encountered an evil demon.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: I once met a good demon though.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Oh yes, what did he say?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: He gave me a puzzle box and then went off again.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: I think you must have had too much dwarven stout in you.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Could be, could be, but there's no telling, is there?

options.text: I defeated the spirit of the rock!
options.condition: First time after Between a Rock...:

steps.player: I defeated the spirit of the rock!

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: That's amazing!

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: That's fantastic!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: What rock was that again?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Pay attention for once, Dernu! It's Dondakan's rock!

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: That's quite impressive, Player. How did you manage to do that?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: What kind of question is that to ask? With [his/her/their] great might of course!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Or vast magical skills!

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: No, you're more a ranger, aren't you Player?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Anyway, this calls for a celebration.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Oh yes, we should go down into Keldagrim to celebrate.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Tonight, of course, not now. We're on duty now.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Right... and I'm sure traffic here will pick up soon with that rock broken.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: I heard there's vast amount of gold inside!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: The company is going to be rich!

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Now don't you go and discuss company business in front of this human, Dernu.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Right. Let's get back to work.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Anything else you wanted, Player?

options.text: I need some help with this statue...
options.condition: During The Giant Dwarf:

steps.player: I need some help with this statue... King Alvis' statue, to be precise.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Oh yes, what's the problem then?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: It was knocked down, remember? Parts of it nearly landed on our heads?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: A terrible noise it made too!
Before helping Blasidar:
While helping Blasidar:

steps.player: This sculptor has got me looking for a lot of items, you see.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Items eh?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: We love items.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Can't get enough of them.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: I got this puzzle box once, you know.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Oh, not that story again.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: You have told that story before, Dernu.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Well forget about it then. I'll shut up if you don't want to hear about it.
After helping Blasidar:

steps.player: Well, the sculptor only needs to build the head now. But I need to get the Consortium to help me with that.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: The Consortium, you say?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: You're going to talk to the Consortium?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: My, you're certainly moving up in the dwarven world, aren't you?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: What do you need us for then?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: We are but simple dwarves.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Especially you, Dernu.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Now now, Derni, there was no need for that.

options.text: I have rebuilt the statue for the [company name]!
options.condition: First time after The Giant Dwarf:

steps.player: I have rebuilt the statue for the [company name]!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: What, really?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Of course, really! Player wouldn't have said it otherwise, would [he/she/they]?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: And didn't you see Blasidar working on the statue?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Oh yes, he was out there for quite a while.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: That must have been a huge task.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Nothing's too difficult for old Blasidar.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: He truly is a master builder.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: We can all take an example to his hard work and dedication.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Speaking of, shouldn't we get back to work ourselves?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Quite right. Anything else you wanted, Player?

options.text: Do you know about this drunken dwarf...?
options.condition: During Forgettable Tale of a Drunken Dwarf:

steps.player: Do you know about this drunken dwarf...?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Drunken dwarf?

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Yeah, we know a drunken dwarf!

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: In fact we know plenty!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: There's this one really annoying dwarf though, he sometimes throws rocks at me for no reason.

steps.player: The one I mean is his relative, living in the northeast of Keldagrim. I wonder if you could help me with him.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Ah yes, him.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Such a sad case, poor fellow.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Who is he?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Don't you know anything?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Now now, there's no reason to get angry.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: I suppose you're right. Well, he's a drunk dwarf that talks about kebabs a lot.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Has some pretty odd tales to tell too.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: And I understand he's the relative of that dwarf I mentioned earlier.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: I hope that helped, Player?

options.text: I have this unforgettable tale to tell you!
options.condition: First time after Forgettable Tale of a Drunken Dwarf:

steps.player: I have this unforgettable tale to tell you!

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: A tale!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: We love tales!

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: We live for tales!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Like, there was this one time when I lost my spanner in the mines...

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Player wants to tell a tale!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: But my spanner... it's a very interesting tale you know.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: I think we've heard it before.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: It was pretty forgettable.

steps.player: Excuse me, do you want to hear my tale or not?

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: Happy to.

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Would love to hear it.

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: As long as it's better than my spanner story.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: So, what's your tale like?

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Must have been pretty forgettable as well then.

steps.player: I must be off now, thanks for the chat.

steps.speaker: Miodvetnir
steps.text: No problem!

steps.speaker: Dernu
steps.text: Glad to be of service!

steps.speaker: Derni
steps.text: Come back any time!

options.text: Why do the Dorgeshuun live underground?

steps.player: Why do the Dorgeshuun live underground?

steps.npc: Our ancient legends say that goblins were created by an evil god in order to fight in a huge war. This god sent the Dorgeshuun tribe to fight a battle where all would die.
But our ancestors escaped by hiding in a deep hole in the ground where our god could not find us. Eventually an earthquake sealed the hole and they were forever safe.

You flesh-temples always assume you can receive guidance merely by asking someone for it. But in this land there is a power that can teach us far more than any mere teacher could.
I speak of the Dark Altar. For generations our wisest scholars have studied it, yet still it has capacities beyond our comprehension.
The Dark Altar can distort the dimensions, warping the fabric of reality as you perceive it, and even bridging the gap between life and death.
But you are still a flesh-temple; you require a corporeal body to house your soul, and you perform disgusting bodily functions to maintain it.
We of Arceuus have learnt, through the power of the Dark Altar, to move beyond the need for such a flesh-temple to house our souls.
In the crypt below us, we freed our souls from the flesh-temples that had imprisoned them, and we took the form you see now.
Perhaps, if you allow the Dark Altar to work on your mind, one day you too will be able to ascend to our higher form.

When you see someone on top of the glowing mark, then hit the button on the right hand panel, as this will send the claw down to pick them up.

options.text: Tell me more about Jatizso's history.

steps.npc: Well now, the history of the isles is a bloody tale. When told in its intended form it takes 9 days and 9 nights. However, I will give you the abridged version.
Four generations ago there was a mighty king who ruled wisely and was loved by all.
He had many sons, most of whom proved themselves in the usual Fremennik ways of fighting, sailing, drinking and so on.
His youngest two sons, however, were a problem. Ever since they were old enough to hit one another they had bickered and fought.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Their names were Jatizso and Neitiznot.

steps.npc: Hey! Who's telling this story?
Ahem. At the time it was customary for the Kings' sons to claim a prize from his treasury when they came of age.
Each brother rallied support and strode out to confront the other on the field of battle to claim the same prize.
The brothers met on the field, limbs were bruised, bones were crushed and heads clashed.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: They probably didn't notice the head-clashing bit. Too thick skulled!

steps.npc: Can I finish the story without interruptions?

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Carry on dear.

steps.npc: Anyway, long into the night they fought, until they stood alone, facing each other.
On the second day the old king, whose patience was exhausted, strode out onto the field and demanded to know who had claimed his prize.
Jatizso looked at his father and told him yes, it was his, to which the other called out 'No! It's not'.
And so, the argument continued through to the third day, with the sounds of 'Jah! 'tis so!', 'Ne! It's not!' echoing over the field, becoming more hoarse as the darkness enveloped the brothers.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Bah! What they needed was a good clip round the ear.

steps.npc: At the end of the third day, when the brothers lay unable to move, let alone stand, the King stood between them in shame.
As punishment for their squabbling he banished his sons from his realm, ordering that neither should return until they had conquered lands of their own.
Jatizso set sail with a band of loyal followers, sailing into the east, while Neitiznot went west.
Jatizso ventured far into uncharted oceans, his crew dwindling as the trials of sailing and sea monsters took them.
Jatizso's ship limped through the frozen wastes, in need of repairs, fighting off pirates who thought them easy pickings.
At last a promising land was sighted, a land rich in minerals, deep fjords and sweeping mountains.
Jatizso claimed the land and named it after himself.
A mighty citadel was constructed to protect his land; then Jatizso set forth to explore his new kingdom.
Crossing a few fjords, Jatizso spied an island which remained green and fertile, even at such latitude.
With a mighty cheer Jatizso and his men marched on the island. Upon reaching the island, however, they discovered a wooden stockade.
Determined to be master of all the land, Jatizso stood in front of the gates. He looked up and demanded that those within the stockade surrendered.
Jatizso was horrified when his brother appeared on the battlements and cried 'This is my land! Go find yer own'. To which his brother replied 'No it's not!', throwing some rocks for good measure.
And so the blood feud continued.
The fighting between the towns has continued for generations with little sign of improvement.
Quite recently a massive troll army seized one of the islands to the north, while our townships' militias were busy fighting one another.
They marched down and razed Neitiznot to the ground while Neitiznot's troops laid siege to Jatizso.

steps.npc: Yes, dear.
Anyway, a hasty sort of peace has been agreed until the trolls are dealt with.
But you can still see the bitter rivalry as guards hurl insults between the towns.

steps.npc: That's the spirit.

options.text: In future, please don't give anything too tough.

steps.player: Let's talk about the difficulty of my assignments.

steps.npc: The Slayer Masters will take your combat level into account when choosing tasks for you, so you shouldn't get anything too hard.

options.text: That's fine - I don't want anything too tough.

steps.npc: Okay, we'll keep checking your combat level.

options.text: Stop checking my combat level - I can take anything!

steps.player: Stop checking my combat level - I can take anything!

steps.npc: Okay, from now on, all the Slayer Masters will assign you anything from their lists, regardless of your combat level.

options.text: What kind of modifiers can I expect if I slay for you?

steps.player: What kind of modifiers can I expect if I slay for you?

steps.npc: Modifiers? You mean mortifiers! Coined that term myself a few centuries ago.

steps.player: Okay... so what mortifiers can your tasks have?

steps.npc: For most adventurers, I'll assign tasks which either have increased or decreased assignment lengths, or I'll give you some Slayer Points for your troubles.
If you prove yourself to me and complete, say... 15 of my assignments, I'll start offering you tasks against creatures which have an increased chance to drop clue scrolls.
At 25 assignments, any superior creatures you slay will become more likely to drop their special loot.
As long as you're up for the challenge of fighting them of course!
Then at 40 assignments, I'll offer tasks against creatures which are more educational to fight against, to help advance your slayer training at an expedited rate.
And finally, if you complete 50 of my assignments, I'll give you three different tasks to choose from instead of my normal two!

steps.player: So, how many of your tasks have I completed so far?

steps.text: Less than 25 tasks completed:

steps.npc: By my records, I count [X]. You've got a ways to go. Better get slayin'!

steps.text: 25-39 tasks completed:
40-49 tasks completed:
50+ tasks completed:

steps.npc: By my records, I count [X], so you've already proven yourself more than capable of handling all my mortifiers!
What do you mean?

steps.player: Well, I don't understand how a Slayer Master would even have the power to affect creatures in the way you do.

steps.npc: Shhh! Keep it down. Are you trying to undermine my position here? If word gets out that I'm not the one responsible, then my whole niche as a Slayer Master becomes undermined!

steps.player: Okay... so how is it done? If you tell me, I'll keep this between us.

steps.npc: Well, the truth is, I feel it in me bones.

steps.player: Feel it in your bones? You're pulling my leg!

steps.npc: I'm being deadly serious. When my big left toe gets cold, I know there are more treasure trails about. When my right knee starts quivering, it's a tell that a creature will provide more slayer insights.
And when I get phantom pains in my right arm, you can bet your gilded socks that there's a superior creature right around the corner.

steps.player: I see... so there's no real secret to it. It's all just a hunch?

steps.npc: Well, I haven't been wrong yet, have I? And as long as that's true, I'll be in the business of slayin' for years to come!

via-the-astral-contact-spell.npc: Well, well, well. Up for some more slaying?

options.text: Let's talk about the difficulty of my assignments.

via-the-astral-contact-spell-if-the-play.npc: I may be a skeleton, but I still have feelings! Come talk to me face to... face.

standard.npc: Well look who it is! The hero of Prifddinas!

standard.player: Why do I feel like you're being sarcastic?

standard.npc: That's likely due to the fact that I am being sarcastic.

standard.player: Well you're no hero either. You blindly served Lord Iorwerth right to the very end. You're lucky the other elves pardoned you.

standard.npc: You seem upset by that. I served Lord Iorwerth because I didn't have a choice. The other elves realised that, hence the pardon.
Do we?
Yes, but you're a mercenary. You're lucky enough to be able to side with the highest bidder. Not all of us are so privileged.
I was born into the Iorwerth clan, Lord Iorwerth was my uncle. Do you think I had a say in what my life would be? Do you think any of us did?
We served Lord Iorwerth because he was our leader. We may not have agreed with all that he did, but that didn't matter. He was in charge and we were not.
Had I been born into the Cadarn clan, I'd be considered a hero right now. But I wasn't, so instead I am the villain.

standard.player: You can make excuses, but Iestin served Lord Iorwerth and he switched sides.

standard.npc: He did. Iestin was brave, I respect that. His bravery has rewarded him with leadership over our clan. But bravery comes easy when you have nothing left to lose.
But I can see I will not change your mind. That's fine, I don't need to.
That said, you'd do well to remember that the actions of Lord Iorwerth should not be used to judge our entire clan.
Sorry Bwana, I cannot help you at this time. Go and talk to Trufitus at Tai Bwo Wannai, I believe he needs some help.

standard-dialogue-after-shilo-village.npc: Greetings Bwana! We've removed the threat of Rashiliyia and though there are still some random outbreaks of undead activity we are more than able to deal with it.
You're welcome to enter the village now Bwana, shall I show you the way?

first-talking-to-him.player: Would you be able to guide me up and down the mountain?

first-talking-to-him.npc: I don't see why not. I've not much to do while the historians are exploring.
I make many trips each day so whenever you'd like to travel, just speak to me here, at the Shayzien outpost, or south of the mountain.

standard.npc: Of course. Where would you like to go?

steps.npc: Okay. Come back if you change your mind.

standard.speaker: Mourner
standard.text: Stand back citizen, do not approach me.

mourner-headquarters-guard.speaker: Mourner
mourner-headquarters-guard.text: Back away citizen. Only mourners are allowed inside the headquarters.

standard-dialogue-in-east-ardougne-befor.speaker: Mourner
standard-dialogue-in-east-ardougne-befor.text: Do you have a problem traveller?

standard-dialogue-in-east-ardougne-befor.player: No, I just wondered why you're wearing that outfit... Is it fancy dress?

standard-dialogue-at-the-ardougne-wall-b.speaker: Mourner
standard-dialogue-at-the-ardougne-wall-b.text: I'm guarding the border to West Ardougne. No one except we mourners can pass through.

standard-dialogue-at-the-ardougne-wall-b.speaker: Mourner
standard-dialogue-at-the-ardougne-wall-b.text: The plague of course. We can't risk cross contamination.

options.text: What brought the plague to Ardougne?

steps.player: What brought the plague to Ardougne?

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: It's all down to King Tyras of West Ardougne. It started came back from one of his visits to the lands west of here.

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: Some of his men must have unknowingly caught it out there and brought it back with them

steps.player: Does he know how bad the situation is now?

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: If he did he wouldn't care. I believe he wants his people to suffer, he's an evil man.

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: He's not my king.

options.text: What are the symptoms of the plague?

steps.player: What are the symptoms of the plague?

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: The first signs are typical flu symptoms. These tend to be followed by severe nightmares, horrifying hallucinations which drive many to madness.

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: It gets worse. Next the victim's blood changes into a thick black tar-like liquid, at this point they're past help.

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: Their skin is cold to the touch, the victim is now brain dead. Their body however lives on driven by the virus, roaming like a zombie, spreading itself further wherever possible.

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: Maybe...

standard-dialogue-at-the-ardougne-wall-a.speaker: Mourner
standard-dialogue-at-the-ardougne-wall-a.text: This is no place for sight-seeing. Don't you know there's been a plague outbreak?

standard-dialogue-at-the-ardougne-wall-a.speaker: Mourner
standard-dialogue-at-the-ardougne-wall-a.text: Then I suggest you leave as soon as you can.

options.text: What brought the plague to Ardougne?
What are the symptoms of the plague?

standard-dialogue-in-west-ardougne-befor.speaker: Mourner
standard-dialogue-in-west-ardougne-befor.text: Hmmm, how did you get over here? You're not one of this rabble. Ah well, you'll have to stay. Can't risk you going back now.

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: We're working for King Lathas of East Ardougne. He has tasked us with containing the accursed plague sweeping West Ardougne.

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: We also do our best to ease these people's suffering. We're nicknamed mourners because we spend a lot of time at plague victim funerals, no one else is allowed to risk attending.

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: It's a demanding job, and we get little thanks from the people here.

options.text: I haven't got the plague though...

steps.player: I haven't got the plague though...

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: Can't risk you being a carrier. That protective clothing you have isn't regulation issue. It won't meet safety standards.

options.text: I'm looking for a woman named Elena.

steps.player: I'm looking for a woman named Elena.

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: Ah yes, I've heard of her. A healer I believe. She must be mad coming over here voluntarily.

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: I hear rumours she has probably caught the plague now. Very tragic, a stupid waste of life.

standard-dialogue-talking-to-movario-or-.npc: I don't know. It's giving strange readings...
I'm not even sure it's working any more.

standard-dialogue-talking-to-movario-or-.speaker: Darve
standard-dialogue-talking-to-movario-or-.text: This is a wild goose chase! We trek halfway across the world and there's nothing down here but this bunch of useless goblins!

standard-dialogue-talking-to-movario-or-.npc: I am sure my triangulation calculations indicated that the source of power was in this rough area...
I find it encouraging that it's pointed to somewhere where there actually are caves.

standard-dialogue-talking-to-movario-or-.speaker: Darve
standard-dialogue-talking-to-movario-or-.text: This part of the world is riddled with caves! It's hard not to hit a cave around here! Are you sure you're not just picking up these goblin lanterns or something stupid?

standard-dialogue-talking-to-movario-or-.npc: You should have more faith in my skills as a mage! I've been working on this for years-

standard-dialogue-talking-to-movario-or-.speaker: Darve
standard-dialogue-talking-to-movario-or-.text: Gah! We have an eavesdropper! Buzz off, adventurer - go talk to the goblins or something.

steps.npc: That's what I like to see: a polite adventurer! Now, where was I...

steps.speaker: Darve
steps.text: None of your business!

options.text: Hey, I'm one of you guys! See this pendant?
options.condition: If the player is wearing the pendant of Lucien:

steps.player: Hey, I'm one of you guys! See this pendant?

steps.speaker: Darve
steps.text: Where did you come from? Who sent you? I'll have you know I'm the mage's bodyguard for this job. We don't need anyone else!

options.text: No one sent me, I'm just nosy.

steps.player: No one sent me, I'm just nosy.

steps.speaker: Darve
steps.text: Well stick your nose somewhere else!

steps.npc: I'm sorry, but pendant or no pendant, this is a secret. I'm sure you understand.
He did not! If he had, I would be aware of it!

steps.speaker: Darve
steps.text: Don't try to lie to us! Now go away!

options.text: (Charm) I'm sure you're a much better bodyguard than me...
options.condition: If the player is wearing the Ring of Charos(a):

steps.player: I'm sure you're a much better bodyguard than me, but perhaps I can help in some non-bodyguarding way?

steps.npc: Well, we don't know how big this thing is. If we find it, I suppose we might need someone else to help us carry it.

steps.player: So, what are we looking for?

steps.npc: You're not very well briefed, are you?

steps.speaker: Darve
steps.text: To be honest I'm still a bit hazy on that point too.

steps.npc: sigh*
Lucien has asked us to search for artefacts that give off a very specific type of energy. After many years of research, I think I'm finally drawing near.

steps.speaker: Darve
steps.text: You don't sound very sure.

steps.npc: Bah! My detection device is totally shot. I don't understand it.
I wouldn't hang around for now, adventurer. It could be a long while before I can get a clear reading.

steps.player: Okay, I'll be on my way.

standard.npc: Can I help you, outsider?

steps.npc: This is the headquarters of Supplies's Supplies, a global chain of world class equipment providing outposts that effectively synergise with local corporate needs.
Excuse me, I wasn't done.
This business has been stimulating local economies for over one generation, and represents a core pillar of every community in which it operates.
We have locations at every major settlement on Wyrmscraig and a diverse portfolio of other business interests in the area.
Supplies's Supplies has recently opened its own production facility for high tensile strength fastening cords.
I bought a yak and I'm using its hair to weave rope.

standard.npc: Welcome to the Emir's Arena! What can I do for you?

steps.npc: This is the Emir's Arena, recently renovated with his coin. Here, you can fight for glory and prestige in individual duels and tournaments.

options.text: Where did this Arena come from?

steps.player: Where did this Arena come from?

steps.npc: The original building was excavated by the Varrock Museum a while ago. It dated back to the Second Age!

When the archaeologists moved out, a group of warriors, headed by myself, bought the land and converted it to a set of arenas for duels. The best fighters from around the world would come here to fight!
More recently, the Emir of Al Kharid acquired the Arena and had it renovated to the state it's in now. He's kept me on to handle day-to-day running, though.

steps.player: What would the Emir want to do with a bunch of fight pits?

steps.npc: Something about a rowdy group of match-fixers, so I heard. I think the guards would know more about it than I would.

steps.text: other

options.text: How do I get a fight?
What kind of fights are happening today?
How do I get a fight?

steps.player: How do I get a fight?

steps.npc: You can participate in Duels and Tournaments. These may be ranked, if you want rewards and prestige, or unranked if you're just fighting your friends for fun.

steps.text: This is the icon for the Grouping tab. Within it you'll find the PvP Arena options.
There, you can click Find to seek the official group for ranked Duels or Tournaments.
Once you've found it, click Sign up to sign up to one, and you'll be considered for an invitation to a Duel or Tournament, whenever one begins.
Ranked Duels and Tournaments take place on designated worlds, with stats and items provided to you on those worlds.

steps.npc: Win or lose, you'll earn Reward Points for taking part in ranked Duels and Tournaments. You can trade your points here for supplies that might help in the Wilderness, or such places.
Now, if you want to choose your opponents, you can have an unranked Duel or Tournament instead, just for the fun of beating them.
Use the recruitment boards outside the hospital to set up your own unranked tournament, or to apply to an existing one.
For an unranked Duel, look around the Arena for someone you wish to fight, and challenge them...

steps.text: You'll see a 'Challenge' option when you right-click other people around the Arena. Use that to set up an unranked Duel.
On PvP Arena worlds the Arena will supply stats and items for your fight. You'll get to choose your load-out from a menu.
On other worlds, like this one, you must bring your own items, and fight with your own stats.

steps.npc: Ho! Ho! Ho!

options.text: What kind of fights are happening today?
What kind of fights are happening today?

steps.player: What kind of fights are happening today?

steps.npc: Every week, we'll rotate the active build, meaning you'll have access to a different set of stats and items. This week, the active build is [Zerker/1 Def Pure/Max/Med].

steps.text: other

steps.npc: See you in the Arena!

standard.npc: Can I help you, human?

steps.npc: Why, it's my little shop. I supply all kinds of items that the Lovakengj workers need. Though if you need pickaxes, you should visit Toothy in the sulphur mine.
Now, can I help you today?

steps.text: other

standard-dialogue.text: First time after completing Jungle Potion:

steps.npc: Hello there...thanks for helping out Trufitus commune with the gods Bwana. We've been able to return to the village thanks to your help.

standard-dialogue.text: First time after hacking away at jungle if the fence hasn't been repaired yet:

steps.npc: I see that you've been hacking away at the jungle...good, now if you have some thatching spars you can go and fix the fence. It's just to the south near the jungle, again, you'll need a machete for this.

standard-dialogue.text: First time after repairing the fence:

steps.npc: Great, I saw you were fixing the fence earlier, it looks like you've got the hang of this now! Let me give you something for your effort!

steps.text: You get [amount] trading sticks. You are left with [percentage] favour.

steps.npc: Well, I tend the hardwood grove nearby, you can enter if you like and harvest some of the very fine hardwood that grows within.
Apart from that I'm a simple Tai Bwo Wannai villager...I like to try and find out what's going on in the mainland and the rest of the known world.

options.text: Is there anything interesting to do here?

steps.text: If the player hasn't hacked away at jungle:

steps.npc: Well Bwana, if you're stuck for something to do, you could always do a bit of handymanship about the village and cut away the jungle that lies here about.
If you's is good with da machete Bwana, you's can get's some thatching spars and put them to use repairing the run-down village fence.

steps.text: (Show options below.)
If the player has hacked away at jungle:

steps.npc: Apart from cutting back the jungle and repairing the fence, I think we've got most things covered now Bwana.

options.text: Ask about cutting back the jungle.

steps.text: (Show options below.)

options.text: Do I get anything for doing this?

steps.player: Do I get anything for doing this?

steps.npc: Yes Bwana, you gain experience in woodcutting. In addition many members of the community will reward you with trading sticks, our local currency, for your efforts.
Correct Bwana, trading sticks! It's our form of local currency! Everything you do to help out in the village will give you some favour, but there's a maximum limit!
When you've reached one hundred percent, you cannot gain any more favour, you need to cash in your favour for trading sticks before you can increase your favour again.

options.text: Who do I get trading sticks from?

steps.player: Who do I get trading sticks from?

steps.npc: Well Bwana, there's a good ten villagers I know of who would show their appreciation for your effort. Who do you want to ask about?
Sharimika is married to Mamma Bufetta, Bwana. They live in the houses just in front of the tribal statue.
Mamma Bufetta lives with her family in the building that faces the stone statue, she lives there with her husband Sharimika and her daughter Layleen.
Layleen is a young girl, the daughter of Mamma Bufetta and Sharimika, she lives with her parents.

Karaday is a young man and his chosen profession is fishing, he follows after his father Safta Doc in that respect. You can find him usually around the center of the village, that is when he's not off fishing.

Safta Doc used to be a fisherman, but he's just about retired now. He has an interesting profession which you might like to talk to him about. You'll find him usually near the building with the anvil in it.
It's just slightly north of the village statue.
Gabooty is a bit of a mystery, no one's sure where he came from! He's quite helpful though, you can find him in the middle of the village enclosure, to the south of Sharimika's house.
Fanellaman was a fisherman, he's retired now, but he'll try and regale you with tales of his salty sea dog days. He's often walking up and down the western beach.

initial-dialogue.npc: You're wondering what's in it for you I suppose. The citizens of Meiyerditch come here looking for freedom, but I can tell you're no citizen.
Don't worry, you're not the first to sneak in. The guards here turn a blind eye to that sort of thing. Outsiders generally perform better in the Theatre, so make for more interesting entertainment.

initial-dialogue.player: Where are you going with this?

initial-dialogue.npc: You're strong enough to survive the Theatre, but you need a reason to try. I have a little proposition for you.

initial-dialogue.player: Go on...

initial-dialogue.npc: The Theatre is owned by Lady Verzik Vitur, a vampyre noble. I represent a party that has certain... interests in Verzik.
Enter the Theatre and beat the challenges within. Doing so would be quite the embarrassment for Verzik, something that my associates would very much appreciate.

initial-dialogue.npc: Be aware, this will be no easy challenge. While you may well succeed alone, the guards will let you enter in a group of up to five. I suggest you take advantage of this.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: Welcome adventurer, to the Hallowed Sepulchre. Are you here to claim some of the treasure within? It seems like the kind of activity one like you would appreciate.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Treasure? What treasure? And what do you mean by 'one like me'?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: If the player is not wearing a full set of vyre noble clothing:

steps.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
steps.text: I mean you're not one of the inhabitants of this city. We could use someone of your talents.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: If the player is wearing a full set of vyre noble clothing:

steps.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
steps.text: I mean you're not one of the inhabitants of this city... although you do smell and look like one. We could use someone of your talents.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Oh? I can't say I'm not interested. What do you propose?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: This place was built long before the city of Darkmeyer existed, back when this land was known as Hallowvale.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: The Sepulchre was used as a resting place for Hallowvale's loyal followers of Saradomin.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: Before they were driven out by the vampyres, the Saradominists used their magic to safeguard this place.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Safeguard how?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: The dead here were buried with the wealth they had in life. To protect these riches, the Saradominists enchanted the statues within the Sepulchre to create various defences.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: Many have tried and failed to obtain the prizes buried here.
Before The Blood Moon Rises:

steps.player: Okay... So I presume you want me to get some of this treasure for you? How should I go about doing it?

steps.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
steps.text: We don't care for a lot of what is kept here. We are only interested in the old currency of this land.
The mysterious stranger pulls a coin out of their pocket and shows it to you.

steps.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
steps.text: If you find any of these Hallowed marks, I'd be willing to take them off your hands. In exchange, I can provide tools that can help you within the Hallowed Sepulchre.
continues

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: After The Blood Moon Rises:

steps.player: Okay... So I presume you want me to get some of this treasure for you? Does Efaritay know about this? It doesn't seem like the kind of thing she would appreciate.

steps.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
steps.text: It was actually on her orders that we first started doing it. She was very keen for us to gather as much of the old currency of this land as possible.
The Mysterious Stranger pulls a coin out of their pocket and shows it to you.

steps.player: Hallowed marks... But why do you still need them? Drakan is gone now.

steps.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
steps.text: Yes... There was some debate over if we should end our work here. It is true that the icyene in particular was keen to see it come to an end.

steps.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
steps.text: However, the tombs have already been desecrated. That cannot be undone now, and while Drakan may be gone, it is wise that we be adequately prepared for any possibility.

steps.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
steps.text: So, with that in mind, if you find any hallowed marks, I'd be willing to take them off your hands. In exchange, I can provide tools that can help you within the Hallowed Sepulchre.
continues

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: You can keep whatever else you find for yourself.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: You should know, only the most agile of adventurers will have success down there. You'll need to use your reflexes to overcome the traps within.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: The Sepulchre has five floors in total, each more dangerous than the last. I hope you prove competent enough to make it all the way down.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Do you have any information about what kind of traps I can expect?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: The statues have been enchanted to shoot fire, lightning and arrows. Some also throw swords. There are also tiles that when stepped on, will teleport you somewhere else.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Sounds like the perfect challenge for me! Is there anything else I should know?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: Yes... It seems that there is another safeguard which prevents anyone from spending too long within the Sepulchre.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: You'll only have so much time before the magic within seals both the coffins and the stairs leading to the next floor.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Hang on a second... If the doors to the next floor close, then how will I escape?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: The priests who built this place had a teleportation system. The magical obelisks they used can be found at the end of each floor. These obelisks can be used to transport you back here.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: However, we have found that the obelisks only respond to those they perceive to be followers of Saradomin. I'd strongly advise against wearing items of any other god.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: I see, but what if I'm in the middle of a floor and can't make it to an obelisk?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: I see you are cautious adventurer. That is wise. You can use any teleport spell to escape from the Hallowed Sepulchre. However, you may also find these of use.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: These teleport crystals were enchanted using the magic of the obelisks. They can be used to teleport to this lobby. I can sell you more when you run out.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Thanks! I'll make sure to put them to good use.
Thanks for the information. I'll keep an eye out for some of those Hallowed marks.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.speaker: Mysterious Stranger
standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: That would be... appreciated.

steps.speaker: Mysterious Stranger

steps.speaker: Mysterious Stranger

steps.speaker: Mysterious Stranger

standard.npc: You ain't getting nuthin' off me, surface-dweller!

steps.npc: Well, first up there's the normal bone club and bone spear. Good, solid frog-bone, and the spear has an iron tip. Can withstand a lot of punishment, if you know what I mean!
But if you're after something a bit fancier, a bit more sophisticated, there's the bone crossbow and dagger.
These are specially good for getting your prey unawares, but you're not going to get the best out of them unless you've been taught the special technique.
So, you interested?
Special aiming technique. If you hit an enemy with it their defence will get weaker so you can hit them again!
Plus, if you use this technique on an enemy who isn't expecting it, you'll always hit them! Pretty good, eh?
'Course, there's only a few people who know it, so unless you can get someone to show you you won't be able to do it.

steps.player: Zanik showed me how to do it!

steps.npc: Good for you! So, are you interested?
Yeah, you stay out of trouble.
Well, y'know, it's not the most reputable profession, is it? Selling weapons?
Well, they're used to hurt people, aren't they? That's not considered very, y'know, respectable. Even though the guards use them, and the hunters, they're still considered a bit, y'know, dirty.
Isn't it like that where you come from?

steps.player: No, on the surface weapon-making is considered a noble profession.

steps.npc: I don't know, you surface people are strange!

standard.npc: 'Narf'? You think that's funny? At least I don't call myself [player name]! Where did you get a name like that?

steps.player: So the guards wouldn't let you back?

steps.npc: They were still allowing citizens from Sophanem to return at that point, but I foolishly chose to stay. I was scared of catching the pox.
By the time I'd changed my mind, they'd stopped letting anyone through. Thankfully, I had some friends there with a spare bed.

steps.player: I guess not everyone was as lucky?

steps.npc: No. Many didn't have anywhere to go. Violence broke out in some parts of the city.

steps.player: I'm sorry you had go through all of that. Menaphos definitely took a hard stance on the plagues.

steps.npc: They were brutal. They even shut off the port from the rest of the city over fears of the plague getting in that way. Many of their own citizens are still trapped there.
