standard.npc: Hello there and welcome to the Natural History exhibit of the Varrock Museum!

standard.player: Hello. So what is it you do here?

standard.npc: Well, we look after all of the research in this section.
When I'm not doing that, I'm teaching people like yourself about how wonderful the natural world is.

standard.player: Nice. So then, I've got a few questions for you.

standard.npc: Well, fire away and I'll give you an insight into the exciting world of animals.

dialogue-in-the-northern-section.npc: Hello again, [sir/madam], how can I help you on this fine day?

dialogue-in-the-northern-section.player: I was hoping you could tell me about something.

steps.npc: Ahh lizards, the scaly carnivores.
If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.

steps.text: The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the lizard display case with a teacher and pupil and schoolboy.

steps.npc: Contrary to popular belief, even though most lizards have a yellow belly, they are not in fact cowardly. Most Gielinor lizards will not shy away from a good fight and can be very tough.

steps.text: The natural historian poses as a lizard...

steps.npc: This is due to a very thick and tough hide, made from thousands of thick scales. Most people who claim to be hunters have a very hard time trying to dispatch lizards.
In fact, the only people to successfully discern how to kill these tough little squamatas are the five legendary Slayer masters, although we assume they must have some kind of natural predator.
Interestingly enough, these scales are made from the same substance that your hair is comprised of. This substance is called keratin.
Lizards have a very well developed sense of vision and hearing. Some people think that some lizards have a third eye!
A tiny, light-sensitive, transparent structure on top of the head that helps them regulate how long they stay in the sun.
This is vital for the cold-blooded lizards who have no means to regulate their internal temperature.
Like many cold-blooded creatures, if they are subjected to a sudden decrease in temperature, they will become sluggish and sleepy.
And this concludes my short lecture on lizards. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.

steps.text: End cutscene

steps.npc: Ahh tortoises, the armoured ancients.
If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.

steps.text: The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the tortoise display case with a teacher and pupil and schoolgirl.

steps.npc: The tortoise is a very well defended beast. It uses an armoured shell just like its aquatic cousins the terrapin and the turtle.

steps.text: The natural historian poses as a tortoise...

steps.npc: Tortoises can vary in size from about as long as your hand to as big as a unicorn. Most land tortoises eat nothing but plants in the wild.
Did you know you can tell how old a tortoise is by the number of rings in its shell, just like a tree.
Most land-based tortoises eat plants, feeding on grazing grasses, weeds, leafy greens, flowers, and cabbages.
Tortoises generally live as long as people, and some individual ones are known to have lived longer than 300 years.
Because of this, they symbolise longevity within some cultures, such as gnomes who also breed them for battle.
The oldest tortoise ever recorded was Mibbiwocket, who was presented to the King Healthorg the Great, by the famous explorer Admiral Bake, shortly after its birth.
Mibbiwocket is still in the care of the gnomish royal family.
And this concludes my short lecture on tortoises. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.

steps.text: End cutscene

steps.npc: Ahh dragons, the mighty hunters of the sky.
If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.

steps.text: The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the dragon display case with a teacher and pupil.

steps.npc: The dragons of Gielinor are a most confusing species. Standing at approximately twelve feet tall, these imposing predators strike fear into the hearts and minds of most sane folk.

steps.text: The natural historian poses as a dragon...

steps.npc: However, if you delve a little deeper into their history and lifestyle, a few things stick out as very unusual.
With most species there is a line, an ancestry if you will, whereby you can track how a creature has come to be in its present form.
For instance, you can trace the ancestry of the common house cat back to the same creature that became the sabre-toothed kyatt.
However, with the dragon, no such root ancestor can be found.
There are many forms of dragon, such as the common coloured and the metallic, or ferrous, dragon.
They colonise many areas of Gielinor, though most notably, sites of ancient battles and small dank caves.
Eating habits tend to vary, with the majority of their food being meat. However, it has also been noted that they can consume metals just as easily, with runite being thought of as a delicacy.
Throughout history, dragons have appeared in myth and legend as fearsome adversaries and cunning creatures.
However, modern evidence does not support this. Most young dragons are largely creatures of instinct with a strong vicious streak.
The lifespan of the common dragon is as yet unknown, as no dragon has ever been observed dying of old age.
Although, it has been mooted that spontaneous combustion could be considered a natural cause of death for this species.
And this concludes my short lecture on dragons. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.

steps.text: End cutscene

steps.npc: Ahh, wyverns. The extinct lizards.
If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.

steps.text: The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the wyvern display case with a teacher and pupil and schoolgirl.

steps.npc: The wyverns' tale is a sad one. This now extinct species is presumed in some way to be related to the dragon.

steps.text: The natural historian poses as a wyvern...

steps.npc: In that they are both large flying reptiles. The wyvern stands much shorter than the adult dragon and only has two legs as opposed to the dragon's four.
Much of the evidence for wyvern behaviour comes from the reconstruction of old bones in the icy mountains of Asgarnia.
One is that Asgarnia was at one time a much more temperate climate than it is now. The other is that wyverns could generate fire internally in much the same way as dragons.
If they follow the dragon paradigm, then they would have been carnivores, feeding on cows, sheep and other livestock animals.
How and why the wyverns became extinct is something of a mystery. Though if you consider the theory that the climate of Asgarnia changed suddenly, then this could provide an explanation.
There are some inconsistencies in the findings we have for the wyverns, such as the odd wear patterns of some of bones, which really could only have happened after the creature died.
Also the bones we have collected remain a little below room temperature wherever they are kept.
They have also been shown to radiate a very weak magical aura.
I'm sure that in due time, these mysteries will be solved.
And this concludes my short lecture on wyverns. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.

steps.text: End cutscene

options.text: That's enough education for one day.

steps.player: That's enough education for one day.

steps.npc: Nonsense! There's always room for more.
And remember, science isn't dull!

dialogue-in-the-eastern-section.npc: Hello again, [sir/madam], how can I help you on this fine day?

dialogue-in-the-eastern-section.player: I was hoping you could tell me about something.

steps.npc: Ahh snails, the gelatinous gastropods.
If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.

steps.text: The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the snail display case with a schoolboy and schoolgirl.

steps.npc: Snails move like worms by squishing up and stretching out, very, very slowly. They also make a lot of slime, in order to aid moving by reducing friction.

steps.text: The natural historian poses as a snail...

steps.npc: They also use slime for protection. For instance, snails can use their slime to crawl over razor-blades without being hurt. It also helps keep away dangerous insects like ants.
When they hide in their shells, snails secrete a special type of slime, which dries to cover the entrance of their shells like a 'trapdoor'. This is called an operculum.
The snails of Morytania are the most malignant molluscs ever to have been studied.
They are broken down into two distinct species: achatina acidia and achatina acidia giganteus or, as they are more commonly known, the acid-spitting snail and the giant acid-spitting snail.
Both of these varieties are voracious carnivores, using their mutated mouthpieces to spit a glob of powerful acid to kill their foe.
They then simply have to wait, whilst the digestive juices make short work of the poor creature. Then, they simply slurp up what remains.

How these strange creatures came to be is still something of a mystery. The most prevalent theory suggests that they mutated, as a reaction to an 'as yet unknown' pollutant that has appeared in the swamps.
The local populace has capitalised on the appearance of these strange species, using their shells to fashion a rudimentary helm that is fairly resistant to the snails acid.
Other known uses of snail by-products include a tasty local delicacy and a fireproof oil.
And this concludes my short lecture on snails. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.

steps.text: End cutscene

steps.npc: Ahh monkeys, the simian collective.
If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.

steps.text: The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the monkey display case with a teacher and pupil and schoolboy.

steps.npc: A monkey is a member of either of two known groupings of simian primates. These two known groupings are the Karamja monkeys and the 'harmless' monkeys.

steps.text: The natural historian poses as a monkey...

steps.npc: Because of their similarity to monkeys, apes such as chimpanzees and gibbons are often called monkeys by accident.
Though some natural historians don't consider them to be monkeys. Also, a few monkey species have the word 'ape' in their common name.
The Karamja monkeys are rumoured to be fairly cunning and intelligent creatures, although rumours that they have learned human speech is anecdotal at best.
In appearance, they stand much shorter than a human and tend to move in a hunched fashion. Karamja monkeys also sport a red mohawk, though it is unknown whether this is an affectation or not.
They are very fond of bananas and bitternuts, eating them in huge quantities whenever they can get their paws on them.
The harmless monkeys of Mos Le'Harmless are a very similar, but in some ways entirely different, breed. They stand roughly the same size but are a lighter colour.
Interestingly, Karamaja monkeys have a deep dislike of seaweed, though this may stem from the actions of a number of irresponsible people.
And this concludes my short lecture on monkeys. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.

steps.text: End cutscene

steps.player: Tell me about the sea slugs.

steps.npc: Ahh sea slugs, the cute crustaceans.
If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.

steps.text: The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the sea slug display case with a teacher and pupil and schoolgirl.

steps.npc: The term 'sea slug' is something of a misnomer. Whilst these small creatures have a soft body like that of a slug, they also possess a very hard shell like a snail.

steps.text: The natural historian poses as a sea slug...

steps.npc: Very little is actually known about the sea slug, as we have, as yet, been unable to procure a sample for observation and study.

For some reason all expeditions we have sent have either vanished mysteriously, or those on the expedition have sent letters back announcing their desire to leave the Museum and go on to other things.
It is presumed that the species is native to the very deep waters around the eastern Ardougne coastline.
There must be some natural resource in the area that the sea slugs are using, as the underwater habitat there is much the same around many coastal areas on Gielinor.
Through looking at similar species we have determined that the sea slug is a harmless little creature. It spends much of its life grazing on seaweed and other plant life.
There are reports that these reclusive animals have two large fangs at their front, though this is assumed to be either for decorative or defensive purposes.

If they do follow the same pattern as other similar creatures, the shell will be nigh on impervious to most attacks. The exposed soft skin may have a number of nematocysts, or stinging organs, similar to jellyfish.
It is typical of prey animals such as these to develop some kind of unique defence mechanism that allows them to survive.
If only we could acquire one for study. I'm sure we would find this mechanism to be truly unique.
And this concludes my short lecture on sea slugs. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.

steps.text: End cutscene

steps.npc: Ahh snakes, the slithering squamata.
If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.

steps.text: The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the snake display case with a teacher and pupil and schoolgirl.

steps.npc: Serpentes, or ophidia, is the suborder under squamata that snakes belong to, like a big family.

steps.text: The natural historian poses as a snake...

steps.npc: Unlike lizards, snakes have no limbs whatsoever; not that this limits them. Snakes live in or near every habitat in the world.

Found in nice tropical forests, temperate lattitudes and even in the ocean - some have adapted specialised stomach juices that they inject into their prey as venom, while others prefer to grab and crush their food.
While others still are fast hunters who use speed and strength to overcome their prey.
The sense of smell in snakes has been enhanced in an amazing way. With most animals, like you and me, tiny particles are filtered through the nose.

However, instead of using just their nose, these animals use their tongues as well. When a lizard or a snake wants to smell it's surroundings, it will wave its tongue around and pick up the particles in the air.
The tongue then returns to the mouth and the tips of the tongue are pushed up against two tiny pits in the roof of the snake's mouth.
Since these pits are split apart from each other, the tongue itself also has to split. This is why snakes have forked tongues.
So the next time you see a snake sticking it's tongue out at you, remember, it's sniffing the air, not trying to bite you.
And this concludes my short lecture on snakes. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.

steps.text: End cutscene

options.text: That's enough education for one day.

dialogue-in-the-southern-section.npc: Hello again, [sir/madam], how can I help you on this fine day?

dialogue-in-the-southern-section.player: I was hoping you could tell me about something.

steps.npc: Well, the field of natural history covers a wide range of sciences.
So we use biology, the study of living things, botany, the study of plants and zoology, the study of animals.
Though the field is growing all the time and we're also using techniques from magic, astrology and numerology.
A person interested in natural history is known as a naturalist.
Ahh terrorbirds, the fastest bird on two legs.
If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.

steps.text: The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the terrorbird display case with a teacher and pupil and schoolgirl.

steps.npc: Terrorbirds live in nomadic groups of between five and fifty birds that often travel together with other grazing animals.

steps.text: The natural historian poses as a terrorbird...

steps.npc: They mainly feed on seeds and other plants. They also eat insects such as locusts if they can catch them.
They have no teeth to chew with, so they swallow pebbles that help to grind the swallowed foods in the gizzard.
They can go without water for a long time, exclusively living off the water in the plants. However, they enjoy water and frequently take baths when they can.
Terrorbirds are known to eat almost anything, particularly in captivity, where opportunity is increased.
Terrorbirds usually weigh a little less than a small unicorn. The feathers of adult males are mostly green, with some white on the wings and tail.
There are claws on two of the wings' fingers and their strong legs have no feathers. The bird stands on two toes, with the bigger one resembling a hoof. Its feet have no claws.
This is an adaptation unique to terrorbirds that appears to aid in running. Their legs are powerful enough to kill even large animals.
The gnomes in particular, prize the terrorbird for its fast running speed, using them as mounts whenever possible.
There are a number of recorded incidents of people being attacked and killed. Big males can be very territorial and aggressive, and can attack and kick very powerfully with their legs.
A terrorbird is so fast, it can easily outrun any human athlete.
And this concludes my short lecture on terrorbirds. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.

steps.text: End cutscene

options.text: Tell me about the Kalphite Queen.

steps.player: Tell me about the Kalphite Queen.

steps.npc: Ahh kalphites, the insectoid eating machines.
If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.

steps.text: The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the Kalphite Queen display case with a teacher and pupil and schoolgirl.

steps.npc: The kalphites, otherwise known as the kalphiscarabeinae, are perhaps the largest species of insect on the face of Gielinor. Their queen is called kalphiscarabeinae pasha.

steps.text: The natural historian poses as the Kalphite Queen...

steps.npc: Most of the early documentation and research on this fearsome predatory species was performed by the noted bug hunter Iqbar Ali-Abdula.
This, of course, was before he was driven insane by his research and ran off into the desert, screaming.

Kalphites are related to beetles and scorpions; they are mainly green in colour. Some have remarkable antennae which can detect the slightest movement. Their carapace is composed of armoured plates called lamellae.
This shell can be compressed into a ball or fanned out like leaves, in order to sense odours. The front legs are adapted for digging the enormous tunnel systems that serve as their nests.
They exist in a caste-based society, with the soft shelled larvae at the bottom, up through the workers, soldiers and finally the queen.
Voracious carnivores, a pack of adult workers can strip the flesh from a full grown camel in a matter of seconds, leaving nothing but a few bones and strips of fur for other scavengers to pick over.
They typically live in large nests marked by the rock hard pillars found in hot, arid deserts, such as the one south-west of Al Kharid, which rise out of the sands like the tombs of desert pharaohs.
Indeed, there is some relationship between the Kalphite Queen and the desert god Scabaras, but no one is really sure what.
During the early part of the fourth age, Scabaras proclaimed himself omnipotent and outlawed worship of all other gods save him.
When the people eventually revolted against his repressive rule and banished Scabaras, it is said his blood washed over the scarabs and transformed them into the kalphites we know today.
Of course, any right-minded scientist discounts these myths as mere stories, with no historical basis in fact.
And this concludes my short lecture on kalphites. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.

steps.text: End cutscene

options.text: That's enough education for one day.

dialogue-in-the-western-section.npc: Hello again, [sir/madam], how can I help you on this fine day?

dialogue-in-the-western-section.player: I was hoping you could tell me about something.

steps.npc: Ahh camels, the ships of the desert.
If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.

steps.text: The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the camel display case with a teacher and pupil and schoolgirl.

steps.npc: The term camel refers to either of the two known species of camelid.

steps.text: The natural historian poses as a camel...

steps.npc: There is the bactrian, which has two humps and can be found throughout Al Kharid. It also refers to the Ugthanki, or one-humped camel.
Camels are ill-tempered beasts at the best of times, requiring a great deal of time and effort to tame.
This would explain why used camel salesmen are in such a hurry to be rid of them.
In the wild, camels have been known to lie in wait and ambush hapless travellers, before devouring them.
This is quite surprising, as most domestic camels are happy eating nothing but vegetables.
Camel milk is much more nutritious than cow milk and goes well in the strong desert drink akin to tea.
Another useful camel by-product is dung. Their dung is very dry, due to the highly efficient metabolism of the camel.
Scientific research has also shown that chilli has a disastrous effect on a camel's digestive system, which produces toxic dung.
And this concludes my short lecture on camels. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.

steps.text: End cutscene

steps.npc: Ahh leeches, the haemophagic parasites.
If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.

steps.text: The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the leech display case with a teacher and pupil and schoolgirl.

steps.npc: Leeches are fascinating creatures and are very similar to worms in most respects.

steps.text: The natural historian poses as a leech...

steps.npc: They like to inhabit streams, rivers and seas, but their preference is for stagnant pools of water.
One of the most common misconceptions is that all leeches feed on blood.
Most leeches are meat eaters, feeding on a variety of invertebrates such as worms, snails, insect larvae and snails.
Those that do feed on blood have developed an amazing method of doing so. Firstly they latch onto the skin using a ring of tiny teeth, before injecting their prey with an anaesthetic.
Then they bite into the skin using a Y-shaped mouthpiece and introducing a chemical that stops the blood from clotting.
They will then feed until they are completely full, sometimes doubling in size!
Most leeches are very small, measuring no more than the length of your middle finger. An exception to these are the leeches of Morytania, which can reach the size of a dog.
They are much more mobile than their smaller cousins and are able to jump rather high when attacking.
Quite how these leeches came to be so big is something of a mystery.
All we can assume is that there is some kind of environmental influence, which has governed their immense growth.
And this concludes my short lecture on leeches. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.

steps.text: End cutscene

steps.npc: Ahh moles, the mammalian mountain makers.
If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.

steps.text: The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the mole display case with a teacher and pupil and schoolgirl.

steps.npc: Now, moles are small mammals of the talpidae family. These subterranean burrowers mainly live on a diet of slugs, snails and insects.

steps.text: The natural historian poses as a mole...

steps.npc: They vary greatly in habitat and can be found in almost every part of Gielinor. Some species have even known to be aquatic!
Male moles are known as boars with the females called sows. Should you come across a group of moles, you would call them a labour.
Moles are considered to be an agricultural pest in most places, digging up the ground and leaving molehills all over the place.
This has been highlighted in Falador by Wyson the Gardener who, after using some Malignus Mortifer's Super Ultra Flora Growth Potion, managed to create Gielinor's only known species of giant mole.
This fearsome beast has huge claws, wicked teeth and a penchant for shiny objects. It is a very tough animal with a thick protective hide and an ill temperament.
That said, they do benefit the soil by aerating and tilling it, adding to its fertility. Contrary to popular belief, moles don't eat plant roots.
And this concludes my short lecture on moles. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.

steps.text: End cutscene

steps.npc: Ahh penguins, the cunning birds of the sea.
If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.

steps.text: The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the penguin display case with a teacher and pupil and schoolgirl.

steps.npc: This often-maligned aquatic bird is known to be native to the ice fields of Etceteria, although they have been known to live as far as the fields of Lumbridge.

steps.text: The natural historian poses as a penguin...

steps.npc: These aquatic birds seem to spend the majority of their time eating and fostering their young.

For creatures with such small brains, they do seem to have a disproportionate capacity for forward thinking and planning. As this serves no natural purpose, scholars are divided as to how this evolved.
Their diet consists mainly of fish, squid and a small shrimp-like creature called krill. However, some have developed a taste for the mushrooms that grow around fairy rings.
Penguins primarily rely on their vision while hunting. What we don't know is how penguins locate prey in the darkness, or at great depths.
Some theories suggest that penguins are helped by some sort of extra sensory perception; perhaps even precognition.
Penguins spend a long time going without food when they are breeding. In fact, they won't even leave their nests if they can help it.
Fortunately, most penguins build up a layer of fat to keep them warm and provide energy until the moult is over.
And this concludes my short lecture on penguins. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.

steps.player: What can you tell me about this place?

steps.npc: Mistrock? It's a mining outpost. It was set up by Cam Torum after you humans went and had another of your wars. We lost some good mines and needed to find new ones.
It wasn't the first choice, but both humans and dwarves alike were pretty poor after the fighting ended, so we all had to learn lessons in how to compromise.
Still, it ended up not being too bad in the end. We found there was a reasonable supply of coal and iron here, along with some silver and gold.
The location ended up being quite appealing for some as well. It makes for a nice change of scenery for those that appreciate that sort of thing.

steps.player: So what was here before Mistrock?

steps.npc: Nothing much of note. The land here was owned by the Moonrise Brewery and Winery, but they found it wasn't much good for growing grapes.

steps.player: So they were happy to give it up?

steps.npc: Very happy. They saw an opportunity for a new business relationship. In return for giving us the land, we now give them favourable rates on what we mine here.

steps.player: Does a winery have much need for metal?

steps.player: Don't they sometimes call the Devourer the goddess of destruction? You seem to have a lot in common with a goddess that your kind oppose.

steps.player: So you stopped serving her because of that change?

The last of her priestesses gathered and cursed her. Unfortunately, she also cast a spell of her own, condemning us to an eternity of walking Gielinor in her form.
She's as much of a cat as Icthlarin is a dog.

steps.player: What curse did you cast upon her?

steps.npc: We trapped her in a human form, limiting her power. We also cursed her to never be willing worshipped again, though I fear that curse has started to wane.

steps.player: So that's why she's scared of cats?

steps.npc: Indeed. There are fewer of us priestesses left now, but we still hold enough power to be quite the problem for her.

steps.npc: The name's Kellan. Used to be a daft-hand at trawlin' back in m'day before the muscles began achin' and the bones started creakin'. These days are better spent helpin you young'uns get yer foot in the trade.

steps.text: other

options.text: How do I deep sea trawl?

steps.player: How do I deep sea trawl?

steps.npc: Well, it all starts with you buildin' a good ol' trawlin' net on yer boat. Rope will do, but linen, hemp and cotton are preferred. The better ye' net, the deeper ye'll be able t' lower it.
After ye' got a net, ye' need t' find a shoal out at sea. In mos' cases, different shoals 'ave different fish, so make sure yer lookin' for the one ye' want.
Once ye' find a shoal, it'll probably be on t' move. They travel o'er pretty large distances, but ye'll find 'em stoppin' from time t' time. Once they stop, that be when it's time t' start catchin'.

steps.player: So that's when I need to lower my net?

steps.npc: Aye, exactly. However, it's important for ye' to know that different shoals be at different depths, and plen'y of shoals will be swimmin' up and down as well.
Yer gonna need t' lower the net to the same depth as the shoal, but remember, if the shoal is too deep and yer net ain't up to scratch, yer gonna be all outta luck.

steps.player: Okay, so I get a good trawling net, find a shoal, wait for it to stop, and then lower the net to the same depth as the shoal. What else?

steps.npc: If yer wantin' to catch plenty o' fish from a shoal, then yer gonna 'ave to bait it. Best time t' do that is just after it's stopped. For the bait, ye'll be needing lots o' fish offcuts.
Ye' can get some offcuts by cuttin' up any kind o' fish, but fancier fish like shark an' such will give ye' higher quality ones.

steps.player: And I'm guessing the fish in some types of shoals are only going to be interested in higher quality offcuts?

steps.npc: Aye, ye' learn fast, laddie.

steps.player: So these offcuts... Do I just throw them into the water?

steps.npc: Well, sort of, but ye'll need t' proper equipment to do it. Specifically, ye'll want to build a chum station on yer boat. They're what ye' use to spread t' offcuts.
Finally, don't forget that shoals travel o'er big distances. If ye' don't feel the shoals in ye' bones, ye' can build a fathom stone on yer boat. They can help ye' track down a shoals whereabouts.

steps.player: I see. This is all very different to normal fishing.

steps.npc: Well, if trawlin's not yer style, laddie, ye' can always cast a rod o'er the side o' the boat and pray they be nibblin', but it's less effective than nets are an' it burns through yer' supply o' bait.

steps.text: other

options.text: Where can I deep sea trawl?

steps.player: Where can I deep sea trawl?

steps.npc: Ye' can do it wherever ye' can find a shoal. They're all across the ocean and yer got different ones fer different fish. I can tell ye' some good places t' find specific ones.
First up, krill an' haddock are the best shoals for gettin' started. There be a great spot for krill just west o' here in the Great Sound.
Ye' can also find both krill an' haddock down in t' Unquiet Ocean, around places like Red Rock, the Great Conch and t' like.
Next ye' got yellowfin an' halibut. There be plen'y o' yellowfin in the Shrouded Ocean, such as near Deepfin Point. Halibut are extra easy! Ye' can find 'em right outside this here port!
Bluefin are more scattered. Ye' can't really pin 'em down, but I'd try farther south near the waters full of tangled kelp.
And then ye' got marlin. They can only be found in the' frigid Northern Ocean, but only the best o' boats can survive up there.
If yer put off by some o' the risks, ye' can try to get lucky. Shoals like t' migrate, an' sometimes them rarer fish mix and mingle with t' other shoals.

steps.text: other

options.text: What kind of fish can I catch while trawling?

steps.player: What kind of fish can I catch while trawling?

steps.npc: Well, there's giant krill, haddock, yellowfin, halibut, bluefin, and if yer up fer a challenge, the elusive marlin.
These ain't yer normal brand o' fish either. Some say that these are the tastiest fish ye' can get. Some even provide unique effects when ye' eat 'em!

steps.text: other

options.text: Do you have any other advice for me?

steps.player: Do you have any other advice for me?

steps.npc: I'm sure ol' Kellan can think o' some stuff t' help ye' on yer trawlin' adventures, laddie.

First, ye'll want t' get yer hands on some sturdy fish crates t' hold more fish. Skilled craftsmen can make empty crates out o' camphor logs then ye' pack em full o' ice. Them slayer masters often have ice fer sale.
Second, trawlin' is always better with a good crew by yer side to delegate up the workload. If ye' go it alone, ye'll be trying to man both t' net and chum station at t' same time!
Third, remember that them rarer shoals don't just stay at one depth. Yer gonna find 'em swimmin' up and down. Ye' gotta pay attention and make sure yer net matches their depth.
Finally, don't be forgettin' to bait the shoal when it stops! It'll attract more fish to yer' boat.

steps.text: other

options.text: I have a question about Deadman mode.

steps.player: I have a question about Deadman mode.

steps.npc: What would you like to know?
Deadman mode is an incredibly dangerous survival game mode. Anyone can attack anyone, anywhere. Death comes at a huge cost and killing other players can be extremely lucrative.

Killing a player will earn you all of the items they had on them, plus the 10 most valuable items from their bank. The unfortunate soul will also lose half of their experience in most skills, or a quarter if they were not skulled. Regardless, it's quite the set-back.
It is, but it is no simple task to kill someone in Deadman mode.
Very high level guards patrol every major city and bank. They will kill anyone who has a skull. Getting yourself a kill is only half the battle.

options.text: How do I play Deadman mode?

steps.player: How do I play Deadman mode?

steps.npc: You can log into Deadman mode by selecting a Deadman mode world from the world list before you log in.

steps.player: So I don't need a new account to play Deadman mode?

steps.npc: Nope! You can use your existing account on a Deadman world, providing you have membership.

steps.player: Do my stats and items transfer over to Deadman mode?

steps.npc: No, they do not. Your Deadman mode progress is completely separate from normal Old School worlds.

options.text: What happens when I die in Deadman mode?

steps.player: What happens when I die in Deadman mode?

steps.npc: If you die to a player you will lose the 10 most valuable stacks of items from your bank, all items that you have on your person and half of the experience you have gained in any unprotected skills.

If you die to a monster when you have a PK skull you will lose the 10 most valuable stacks of items from your bank, all items that you have on your person and half of the experience you have gained in any unprotected skills.
If you die to a monster when you do not have a PK skull you will lose all of the items on your person except for the 3 most valuable. You will not lose experience or any items from your bank.

options.text: What happens when I kill a player in Deadman mode?

steps.player: What happens when I kill a player in Deadman mode?

steps.npc: When you kill a player you will receive any items they have on their person and you will also be given a key. You can use this key on Deadman chests found in various banks across the map. Within the chest you will
find the 10 most valuable stacks of items from the bank of the player you struck down. From here you will be able to choose the items you would like to keep.

options.text: How can I protect my items in Deadman mode?

steps.player: How can I protect my items in Deadman mode?

steps.npc: You can protect up to 10 items by placing them in your safe deposit box. Items in your safe deposit box will not be lost to a player who kills you, unlike those found in your bank. Remember that you can only place 10 single items into your safe deposit box, no stacks.

options.text: How can I protect my stats in Deadman mode?

steps.player: How can I protect my stats in Deadman mode?

steps.npc: You can protect your levels in up to 2 combat skills and 3 non-combat skills. You can choose which by opening your items lost on death interface found in your equipment tab. Choose wisely!
You should be warned however. If you get killed by a guard, you will lose a tenth of your experience in those skills too!
Gelin over there also has some deals on insuring your hitpoints, speak to her to find out more about that.

options.text: What are safe zones in Deadman mode?

steps.player: What are safe zones in Deadman mode?

steps.npc: Safe zones are areas patrolled by very high level guards which can be found in various places across the map. The guards watch out for any player with a PK skull and will attack them if they're spotted. It is still possible to be attacked inside safe zones but the person doing the attacking will not stand a chance of making it out alive.

steps.npc: Elidinis is one of a group of gods, known as the Menaphite Pantheon. She is wife of their leader Tumeken. She is the Menaphite goddess of growth and fertility and goddess of the river.

options.text: Don't many other towns not follow Elidinis?

steps.player: Don't many other towns not follow Elidinis though? Why did you pick on Nardah specifically?

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: It is true many do not follow Elidinis, but there is more to the story than that. The answers

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: lie in the story of Nardarine. Wouldst thou likest to hear the telling of this tale? It is not a short one.

options.text: Yes I would like to hear this story.

steps.player: Yes I would like to hear this story.

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: Nardarine came from a town towards the north side of the desert which does not exist today. This was in the third age in the time thou callest

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: the God Wars. Her town was once controlled by Saradomin, but there was a great battle there between Saradominist and Zamorakian forces which pretty much levelled the town

steps.npc: to the ground. Most of the human citizens perished. Nardarine had the wisdom to escape into the desert before the fighting got really serious and thus survived. However she found herself wandering lost and alone in

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: the desert. She prayed to Saradomin for help, but Saradomin was too concerned with the loss of a strategic outpost to worry about the fate of one small human. Nardarine had wandered towards the realm of

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: the Menaphite God Pantheon. Elidinis heard the prayers of Nardarine, she took pity on the wandering human and came unto her with water. 'Oh great goddess' exclaimed Nardarine 'I wish not to be involved more in

steps.npc: the wars of the gods for they have caused me so much hardship already, I wish only for a quiet life somewhere'. Elidinis replied 'I will grant this unto thee on the condition that thou swearest to forever pay fealty and

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: homage to me and I grant this also unto thine descendents as long as they too will pay an oath of fealty and homage to me'. Nardarine said 'If you would grant me a safe home, with a

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: supply of food and water, then I would surely do this for it is more than any other God would seem to do for me'. Then Elidinis made

steps.npc: a spring of water appear at Nardarines feet and brought stone from below the sand so that she

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: might have something to build with. She called forth camels which have many uses and taste good in kebabs. She then provided Nardarine with a statuette in her image to worship. Nardarine built up her home. Over

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: time more refugees from the God Wars found Nardarine's home. Nardarine let them stay with her as long as they did make the same oath as her. Hence the town of Nardah was born and Nardarine lived the rest

steps.npc: of her days in the peacefulness that she craved. The oath was passed down the generations for many ages, but now seemeth to be forgotten. Now maybe thou canst see why we are not best pleased.

During battle, you can gather supplies here to aid you and your teammates.
The Soul Obelisk is just a little way from here. Let's continue on; I'll meet you to the east.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-souls.npc: Now, to have a chance against an avatar, you are going to need souls. Lots of souls.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-souls.player: So, where do I get these souls from?

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-souls.npc: You can kill the souls that inhabit the arena ruins and harvest their soul fragments.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-souls-z.npc: When you kill a creature in Soul Wars, they will leave a soul fragment behind, which you can use to charge the Soul Obelisk.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-souls-z.player: You want me to kill him?

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-souls-t.npc: Come on! Kill him already and get that soul fragment.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-the-sou.npc: Here we are at the Soul Obelisk. Now, to reap the full benefit of the soul fragment, you will need to first be in control of the Obelisk.
Various areas of the battleground can come under your team's control. To gain control, you must have more team members than the opposing team in these areas.
If you outnumber the enemy, you will gradually take control. Let's try it out now.
We shall use Zimberfizz to represent an enemy team member.
Come on, give him a good kick.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-the-sou.player: I thought he was dead? Didn't we kill him earlier?

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-the-sou.npc: Ha! He wishes! No, his service to me is far from over.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-area-co.npc: Ha! I'm sure he loves the attention, right Zimberfizz?

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-area-co.text: Note the Obelisk's progress bar in the top-left of your screen. As you gain control over an area, this bar will fill with the colour of your team.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-area-co.npc: Right. Now, go and charge the Obelisk with that soul fragment and see what happens.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-angry-a.npc: Ha! I think not! I'm not about to reward those who don't put the effort in!

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-angry-a.text: Note the orange bar in the top-left of the screen. This bar represents how active you have been during the game.

You can refill the bar by performing actions in the game, such as dealing damage or charging the Obelisk.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-angry-a.player: Oh well. Say, do you think the enemy avatar minds us weakening it like this?

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-angry-a.npc: Hmm, why don't we go find out?

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-angry-a.npc: So, here we are in the enemy base.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-death-t.npc: At least it wasn't permanent! Think of it as an opportunity to learn.
The other team will be after you and any soul fragments you have collected, after all.

They say that an object of great power was once stored in this very cave. Apparently, the presence of this object created the daeyalt deposits.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue-if-th.player: I see. What is the daeyalt used for?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue-if-th.npc: Its main use is as a key component in the vampyrification process. There's other uses though. It can be used to create runes, for example.
The essence mined by the slaves is reserved. If you want some, you'll have to mine your own.
If you do choose to mine the deposits, you should know that the daeyalt shards you'll get are useless on their own. They'll need converting into essence to be used.
Luckily for you, I can provide that service.

steps.npc: Whenever you have shards to convert, bring them to me. Normally I'd send the converted essence straight to your bank, but as you seem to carry all of your belongings yourself, I'll just give it right to you instead.

standard-dialogue-with-no-contract.npc: Quickly, tell me - is it still there?
The THING, the THING! It was just outside my house! Has it gone away yet? Or is it still lurking out there, waiting for me to go outside?

standard-dialogue-with-no-contract.player: I didn't see any THING out there, just a couple of guards. What did it look like?

standard-dialogue-with-no-contract.npc: Ohhhh, it was HORRIBLE! It was an enormous THING, with TEETH and EYES and... and... and THINGS!

standard-dialogue-with-no-contract.player: Um... would you care to be more specific?

standard-dialogue-with-no-contract.npc: I can't. I only saw it in the dark.

standard-dialogue-with-no-contract.player: You only saw this THING in the dark?

standard-dialogue-with-no-contract.npc: I was sleeping peacefully one night, when suddenly I woke up and saw it through the window. It was LOOKING at me! I haven't dared go out since then. It's had me trapped in here for days! I've packed my
bags so I can escape, but the THING's still out there waiting for me to come out! If I have to stay in here much longer I'll go mad! MAD!! MAD!!!

standard-dialogue-with-no-contract.player: There's no THING outside. Just come out and get some fresh air before you go funny in the head.

standard-dialogue-with-no-contract.npc: You want me to go outside?

standard-dialogue-with-no-contract.player: I think you might just have dreamed about the THING.

standard-dialogue-with-no-contract.npc: You want me to believe that it's not real?
No! No! I know what you are! You're in league with the THING! It keeps sending people in here to trick me into going outside! They keep stealing from me too! GO AWAY!

standard-dialogue-with-no-contract.player: I'm not trying to trick you!

options.text: Where does the blood come from?

steps.player: Where does the blood come from?

steps.npc: Throughout the generations, countless people of this land have perished in times of strife, with their bodies left to rot where they fell.
Some were slain by the deadly creatures that roam the land; others perished at the hands of their fellow citizens during the wars of this land.
Their blood flowed into the soil, pooling and percolating unseen in the dark, as the power of the Altar drew it to this sacred place to form the River.

steps.npc: Okay, first you need dynamite. That's got three ingredients...

steps.text: Firstly, you need volcanic sulphur. It comes from Toothy's mine, west of here.
Secondly, you need juniper charcoal. Smoggy's got some charcoal furnaces on the beach in the Hosidius area, near the juniper woods.
Thirdly, you need saltpetre. There are some natural deposits in the Hosidius woodlands, near the juniper trees.
Mix the volcanic sulphur, the juniper charcoal and the saltpetre in a pot to make dynamite. Finally add a string as a fuse.

steps.npc: Once you've got dynamite, use a chisel to excavate a cavity in the hard rock walls, so you can put the dynamite in, then light the fuse.
The dynamite blows ore out of the hard rock. It's very unstable, so you don't have long to get it cleaned before it disintegrates.
Just deposit it into the sack upstream, and my colleague will get it cleaned safely. You can collect your cleaned ore from me.
I work here, in the blast mine. It's a valuable source of minerals for the kingdom, so our work is very important.

The street urchins that roam the streets keep tabs on which houses are vulnerable.
Once you know a house is vulnerable, wait for the owner to leave. Then just simply use your key to get in and steal to your heart's content!
But whatever you do, dont get caught!

steps.player: So... steal keys, use keys on the houses that are ready to be robbed, make buckets of cash and don't be caught?

steps.npc: That's it!

I was an orphan, much like these street urchins you see around the city. I spent my days running around scrounging for food and struggling to find somewhere to sleep.
Eventually, I turned to a life of crime and thievery. Turns out I'm quite good at it.
I took refuge in a small spot in the north east of the city. Out of sight, out of mind.
There I met with other orphans just like me. We all wanted payback. Payback on the city for forgetting about us.

steps.npc: Certainly, though it is quite simple - they are the barbarians of the past who have died in the passing of the years. There are three categories which learned sages claim may describe all spirits encountered.
The majority are at peace, having died with their ambitions sated, even if this ambition was as simple as a glorious death. They can contact those in our world in order to spur us on to glory.
Of course, they cannot or will not contact all inhabitants of these lands, for not all are worthy.

steps.npc: A second category of spirit is made up of those who are not yet at peace. However, all that is needed is for their mortal remains to be laid to rest and they will join the peaceful majority.

steps.npc: Alas, there is a small minority who will never be at rest. These have been slain in moments of insanity by their brothers or by adventurers.

standard.player: Magical traps? What does that have to do with the Historical Archive?

standard.npc: A good question. The Archive is actually part of the Tower of Magic, and was repurposed many decades ago.
Unfortunately, we don't possess full understanding of the Tower of Magic and its many enchantments, so we often discover remnants of traps.
The task has fallen to me to investigate and study what we can of these enchantments in the hopes of understanding their magical power.

options.text: What exactly is the Tower of Magic?

steps.player: What exactly is the Tower of Magic?

steps.npc: The Tower of Magic is a uniquely enchanted building located just west of the library, though many levels and rooms are hidden from sight.
I have dedicated my life to studying the powerful enchantments that conceal the many levels of the Tower, though it proves difficult at times.
Is there anything else I can help you with?

steps.text: other

options.text: Tell me about the history of the Tower

steps.player: Tell me about the history of the Tower.

steps.npc: The Tower was constructed by King Rada III. We don't know exactly when, since dates were not recorded before the Twill Accord.
Following the rebellion of the five houses against King Rada III, the Council of Elders was formed. They used the Tower as a meeting place for the Council.
Since then, it has mostly been used as a residence by the various rulers of the kingdom, with each ruler using the Tower however they saw fit.
Eventually, after Kourend Castle was built, ownership of the Tower was passed over to Lord Arceuus.
Is there anything else I can help you with?

steps.text: other

options.text: This room is part of the Tower?

steps.player: This room is part of the Tower?

steps.npc: Indeed. During the invasion of the Wintertodt, it was feared that all of Kourend might be lost to the cold. In order to preserve the history of the kingdom, this archive was created during the fifth decade.
Unfortunately, as it is a former chamber of the Tower, and we do not fully understand the magic that conceals it, we often discover strange enchantments that we believe to be old traps.
Just recently we lost a scholar when she accidentally activated a portal and fell through it.
Yes, she turned up a few days later, a little confused but physically fine. It happens every now and then, but most people turn up eventually.

steps.player: I guess I'd better be careful then.

standard.npc: Hello, I am the panning guide. I'm here to teach you how to pan for gold.
Let me explain how panning works. First you need a panning tray. Use the tray in the panning points in the water and then search your tray.
If you find any gold, take it to the archaeological expert up in the museum storage facility. He will calculate its value for you.

options.text: Can you tell me more about the tools an archaeologist uses?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about the tools an archaeologist uses?

steps.npc: Of course! Let's see now... Rock picks are for splitting rocks or scraping away soil; you can get one from a cupboard in the Education Centre.
I think you'll find them scattered about pretty much everywhere, but I know you can get one from a cupboard somewhere in the Education Centre, just like the rock pick!

steps.player: Okay, what about a specimen brush?

steps.npc: We have a bit of a shortage of those at the moment. You could try borrowing one from a workman on the site... but I don't think they'd give it willingly.

steps.player: Sounds like I'll need to be sneaky to get one of those, then... Okay - trowel?

steps.npc: Ahh... that you must earn by passing your exams! The examiner holds those.
If you need something identified or are not sure about something, give it to Terry; he's the archaeological expert in the next room.

trying-to-pan-before-getting-permission.npc: We do not allow the uninvited to pan here.

steps.npc: You can of course use this place when you know what you are doing...

options.text: So how do I become invited then?

steps.player: So how do I become invited then?

steps.npc: I'm not supposed to let people pan here unless they have permission from the authorities first. Mind you, I could let you have a go if you're willing to do me a favour.
Well, to be honest, what I would really like is... a nice cup of tea!
Absolutely, I'm parched!
If you could bring me one of those, I would be more than willing to let you pan here. I usually get some from Varrock but I'm busy at the moment.

standard.npc: Aha! Are you here to parley?
Oh, that's a shame.
I parley everywhere! I haven't encountered a single problem I've not been able to parley my way out of.

That's right! Whenever I run into trouble, I just shout parley! To be honest with you, I don't know the first thing about actually being a pirate. All my wealth just comes from parleying all the time.

standard.player: I see. It really feels like that's going to go horribly wrong for you at some point.

standard.npc: Nonsense! At the rate I'm going, I'm going to be the greatest pirate ever to have lived! Parley! Parley! Parley!

steps.npc: We used to be in Seers' Village, far to the west, but we had to move - the seers were complaining about the noise level, and the knights of Camelot got it into their heads that the Party Room knights were making fun of
them.
We're doing well here, though. The people of Falador are happy we're here, and we've hardly ever had the White Knights telling us to keep the noise down.
We're going to turn Falador into the party capital of Gielinor!
I've won the Dance Trophy at the Kandarin Ball three years in a trot!

standard.npc: Ah, a stranger to our island. What brings you here?

standard.player: Well, I've actually come here on a diplomatic mission. I want to try and settle some of the disputes between the Fremenniks and your clan.

standard.npc: The Rremenniks? Pah! They are just too ignorant and stubborn to listen to anything we have to say - how can we possibly associate with a race that won't listen?

standard.player: I think they are very eager to listen, but they feel like you are keeping secrets from them.

standard.npc: Secrets?

standard.player: Yes, as in your magic ways. To be honest, I think it is fear of the unknown.

standard.npc: Well, when the day comes that a Fremennik can prove they have the patience and interest in learning our ways, then we will perhaps share our secrets.

standard.player: I'm hoping I might be able to achieve that.

standard.npc: Good luck. It's far from simple.

steps.player: What does this seed pod do?

steps.npc: Ah, the seed pod of the Grand Tree is a fascinating spirit artefact. It is a very useful thing, though one must treat it with respect, since the Grand Tree has a connection with all of its parts, however distant they
may be. How do you think the Spirit Trees work?

If you launch its seeds in a far flung location, you will be helping the tree survive, so the grand tree will help a gnome glider pilot find you, using the seed burst itself (which marks the sky) and a little magic, and bring you
back home as an act of gratitude. Budding farmers will also find their link with plants to be just a little bit better than before.
However, it takes time for a pilot to find you, and if you are in a real hurry, and I mean a real emergency, you can just squash the seed pod. The Grand Tree doesn't like this, but will pull you back

home straight away. Don't do this if you need to do anything with plants straight away, though - your fingers will be considerably less green for a while after using the seed pod this way, and the journey is not
very pleasant...

steps.text: other

options.text: How do I keep the mine stable?

steps.player: How do I keep the mine stable?

steps.npc: Don't let it collapse!! It's petrifying, it will stick with you forever. The rumbles create a flashback in my mind, arghhh.
There are some vents and chambers in there. Do better than I did with them, you want around a 50% gas level in each chamber.
There are 3 in total, we spent awhile coming up with names, such as 'Vent west of the pillar near the entrance on the left hand side', but decided A, B and C would be easier.

steps.player: Presumably, a western chamber, central chamber and eastern chamber?

steps.npc: Yep! That's right. Block the chamber to let gas build up, unblock 'em to let gas out. Any creatures in there will cause instability too.
Oh, also, if you have more than one rock to mine, keep them going at roughly the same pace too. Everything gets a bit wobbly if you proceed too quickly down one channel.

steps.speaker: Pious Pete
steps.text: I worked in a chapel dedicated to our lord, Saradomin. My task was to light the chapel candles, but I couldn't reach them myself and I kept getting dazzled by the light whenever I tried.

steps.speaker: Pious Pete
steps.text: I'd call adventurers from across the world, summoning them to my chapel to do the task for me. I needed them to light the tall candles, but not the short ones.

steps.speaker: Pious Pete
steps.text: However, adventurers got confused, and thought they should light the short candles as well as the tall candles, so I made them try again. And again.

steps.speaker: Pious Pete
steps.text: Eventually my chapel was closed down. They said I'd trapped adventurers there for too long. All I wanted was for them to light the tall candles without lighting the short candles!

steps.speaker: Pious Pete

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.text: I used to be a language tutor, teaching in a small school just outside of Lumbridge.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.text: However the place closed down due to ill attendance, and so I was forced to take up piracy.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: Wasn't that a bit of a big jump in careers?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.speaker: Pirate
standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.text: Not really, I made my way through via a short stint as a lawyer.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.speaker: Pirate
standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.text: I must return to my duties. Have a nice day!

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.speaker: Pirate
standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.text: What's yer business?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.speaker: Pirate
standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.text: I asked first!

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: And very rudely too I might add.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.speaker: Pirate
standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.text: Fine! Go about yer 'business'!

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.speaker: Pirate
standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.text: Whaz yer bushinessssss...ssss?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.speaker: Pirate
standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.text: I'm not drunk! I'll knock down any man as sayin' I'm been having a drinking on my duties!

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: Well, I think you'll have a hard time explaining your slurred speech, odd behaviour, bitter, nostril dissolving stench and rolling, bloodshot eyes if your not drunk.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.speaker: Pirate
standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.text: Arrr, ye got me. I just can't leave the stuff alone.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.speaker: Pirate
standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.text: Cap'n Braindeath's Ten X With Added Cattle Medication just keeps singin' its siren song to me.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.speaker: Pirate
standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.text: Would ye care fer a drop?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: No.  I would most certainly not.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.speaker: Pirate
standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.text: Suit yerself.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.speaker: Pirate
standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.text: What's yer business?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.speaker: Pirate
standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.text: Fair enough. Off ye go.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.speaker: Pirate
standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.text: What's yer business?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.player: I'm just helping out a friend.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.speaker: Pirate
standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.text: Which friend?

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.speaker: Pirate
standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy-pir.text: Bill hired you eh? He must have been scrapin' the barrel and no mistake.

historical-dialogue.player: Hello!

historical-dialogue.speaker: Pirate
historical-dialogue.text: Keep yer voice down [lass/lad], can't ye see I'm busy?

historical-dialogue.player: First off, it's [lad/lass], and second, other than busy being drunk I can't see what you are talking about.

historical-dialogue.text: I can't feel me brains no more...

standard.npc: Yes it is! Don't look down your nose at me. I have to put up with an awful lot to earn my living, life is a daily struggle.

standard.player: Sorry, I am just curious. Why is life so difficult here?

steps.npc: Just look at the place, rats, flies and all sorts just swarming the area. Doesn't help that I stink but ain't no one who likes using those tin baths right in public view.
It is difficult to make ends meet. There are just so many skilled fishermen here that the competition is too much! Leaves no room for someone like me.
Thieves! Thieves everywhere. Come to think of it, they always look remarkably like you! Adventurers running about stealing our things, get out of my sight.
Look, this is none of your business, I'd appreciate it if you left me to it. I don't want to see another fancy adventurer again!

steps.player: Okay okay! I'll be off now.

steps.npc: Gang crime is everywhere! I see them sometimes... it makes me very uneasy. It becomes difficult to sleep at night, never mind the draft in here.

steps.player: I've heard about those gangs! The Shayzien soldiers do a lot of work to put an end to it.

steps.npc: Don't talk to me about those soldiers, all they ever do is blitz onto these docks with not a care in the world for us folk.

steps.npc: Well you do not look like you have the right skills to make a canoe at the moment. Try using your axe a bit more first.

steps.text: With 12-26 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: Certainly, swing your axe at this tree here. Then cut it into a canoe, easy stuff.
Unfortunately, you will not be able to carve it into a more reliable canoe right now.
By looking at you and your posture holding your axe, you don't have the right skills for that. You will only be able to go to the next stop.

steps.npc: Certainly, swing your axe at this tree here. Then cut it into a canoe, easy stuff.

steps.player: How far will I be able to go in a dugout canoe?

steps.npc: Two stops sounds about right before it sinks.

steps.text: With 42-56 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: Certainly, swing your axe at this tree here. Then cut it into a canoe, easy stuff.
I see, you seem like the type of adventurer who could make a very nice canoe.

steps.player: Really, how far will I be able to go?

steps.npc: A decent distance, but not the whole river.

steps.text: With 57-99 Woodcutting:

steps.npc: Certainly, swing your axe at this tree here. Then cut it into a canoe, easy stuff.
Wow, you seem knowledgeable about the woods, are you a gnome yourself? All joking aside, you will be able to craft the best canoes to go anywhere down the river!

standard.npc: Go away, I'm busy!

standard-dialogue-varrock-library.player: HEY PETE, WHAT ARE YOU DOING HERE?

standard-dialogue-varrock-library.npc: Shhhh! It's a library you know!

Not much, just doing some research on Dwarvern Culture. Did you know that Keldagrim was originally constructed by a long lost clan who embraced the power of magic, and used it to aid with glorious buildings like
Yes. They even stayed down there for 1000 years or more, in a time they call 'The age of Kings'.
Shhhh! That's enough history for one day I think!

standard-dialogue-wilderness-bandit-camp.player: Pete, what are you doing out here in the deep wilderness?

standard-dialogue-wilderness-bandit-camp.npc: Shhh!! Don't let the others see me here! I'm on a top secret mission for the Burth..., no, nothing. Never mind. Oooo, look, the chaos elemental!! Quick, run!!

standard-dialogue-laughing-miner-pub.player: Hey Postie. Hows tricks? Who are you interviewing here?

standard-dialogue-laughing-miner-pub.npc: Everyone deserves a hic break you know. It gets pretty tiring lugging burp letters about all day.

standard-dialogue-laughing-miner-pub.player: I see. Can I join you?

standard-dialogue-laughing-miner-pub.npc: Why, am I hic coming apart?

standard-dialogue-laughing-miner-pub.player: You've been here a while, haven't you?

standard-dialogue-laughing-miner-pub.npc: Maybe I haves, maybe I haves. It all goes straight to my head you see.

standard-dialogue-laughing-miner-pub.player: Yes... I can see that. Bye Pete!

standard-dialogue-castle-wars-lobby.player: Hey Pete what you doing here?

standard-dialogue-castle-wars-lobby.npc: Just doing a quick survey on famous people and their favourite colour. It's a special feature for 'West Wyverns Women's Weekly'.
Here! Are you mad? No, 'fraid I can't do that. Could cause all sorts of trouble.

standard-dialogue-castle-wars-lobby.player: You're a bit mad really aren't you?

standard-dialogue-castle-wars-lobby.npc: So would you be if you could speak over 1000 languages. I bet it's bliss being ignorant of this world's trouble! I'm off!

standard-dialogue-falador-party-room.npc: Just chatting to my big brother Pete. Hee heee!!
Just a joke that he told me. Care to hear it?
2 Parrots sit on a perch. One says to the other 'Can you smell fish'? Hee heheee he ho ho.

standard-dialogue-falador-party-room.player: And so what did the other one say?

standard-dialogue-falador-party-room.npc: Sigh. 2 Parrots sit on a perch. One says to the other 'Can you smell fish'? Hee heheee he ho ho.

standard-dialogue-falador-party-room.player: I see. So... what did the other one say?

standard-dialogue-falador-party-room.npc: You're serious aren't you. Listen again. 2 Parrots sit on a perch. One says to the other 'Can you smell fish'.

standard-dialogue-falador-party-room.player: Fish, right. So, what was the reply?

standard-dialogue-falador-party-room.npc: ARGH!! 2 PARROTS. ON A PERCH. SMELLS FISHY.

standard-dialogue-falador-party-room.player: No, still lost. Is one of them a penguin?

standard-dialogue-falador-party-room.npc: You're doing it on purpose now aren't you? Please leave me alone!

standard-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.player: Hey Pete, what you doing here?

standard-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.npc: Just chatting to my brother Pete. He keeps Parrots.

standard-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.player: Doesn't sound too tough. What's the pay like?

standard-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.npc: Not very good I'm afraid. His bosses are pretty cheep.

standard-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.player: Groan. Don't give up the day job Pete.

standard-dialogue-north-of-port-phasmaty.player: Hey Pete what you doing here?

standard-dialogue-north-of-port-phasmaty.npc: Arrrr. Avast shipmate. Arrr. I Likes the cut of your gibb. Arrr. That it be.

standard-dialogue-north-of-port-phasmaty.player: I have a strange feeling of Deja Vu. I must go now.

standard-dialogue-ice-mountain.player: Hey Postie! What you doing all the way up here?

standard-dialogue-ice-mountain.npc: I was just trying to get some wise words of wisdom from the Oracle. You know, she's been here a long, long time.

standard-dialogue-ice-mountain.player: Yes, I thought as much. What did she have to say?

standard-dialogue-ice-mountain.npc: First she said 'I am the Oracle, And when I open my lips, let no dog bark!'
I didn't know she was familiar with the works of Shakespeare. So I said 'Et tu, brute?'
Well, she started leaping about and pointing to Ardougne, shouting something about betrayal. She was really angry.

standard-dialogue-ice-mountain.player: Cripes! What do you think it means?

standard-dialogue-ice-mountain.npc: Who knows. Always cryptic to the last. See you around.

overhead-dialogue-varrock-library.npc: Reldo, have you found that book I was looking for yet?

overhead-dialogue-varrock-library.speaker: Reldo
overhead-dialogue-varrock-library.text: No, not yet... but I know I have seen it somewhere...

overhead-dialogue-varrock-library.npc: Sure, no problems. See you later.

overhead-dialogue-varrock-library.speaker: Reldo
overhead-dialogue-varrock-library.text: Bye! Say hi to the other Petes for me.

overhead-dialogue-wilderness-bandit-camp.npc: Psssst! How is the plan going?
Great. Now don't forget - nobody does anything until I give the word! OK?

overhead-dialogue-wilderness-bandit-camp.speaker: Noterazzo
overhead-dialogue-wilderness-bandit-camp.text: Sure no problem. We'll be waiting.

overhead-dialogue-laughing-miner-pub.text: 4 Pints coming right up. Are you expecting guests?

overhead-dialogue-laughing-miner-pub.speaker: Barmaid
overhead-dialogue-laughing-miner-pub.text: You want me to put it on your tab?

overhead-dialogue-laughing-miner-pub.npc: That would be great, thanks. Oh cripes! I've left a fire burning! I'll be back in a mo.

overhead-dialogue-castle-wars-lobby.speaker: Lanthus
overhead-dialogue-castle-wars-lobby.text: Easy Pete, calm down. Don't lose your head!

overhead-dialogue-castle-wars-lobby.npc: Cheeky!! If you're not careful I'll get you cursed too!

overhead-dialogue-castle-wars-lobby.speaker: Lanthus
overhead-dialogue-castle-wars-lobby.text: You wouldn't catch me double-crossing a witch!

overhead-dialogue-castle-wars-lobby.npc: But which witch is which! Anyway, I'm late for an appointment with the oracle.

overhead-dialogue-castle-wars-lobby.speaker: Lanthus
overhead-dialogue-castle-wars-lobby.text: Take care and say hi to the kids for me.

overhead-dialogue-falador-party-room.npc: Hey, bro! How's the party business?
Nice. Well, I'm here to talk to some White Knights.

overhead-dialogue-falador-party-room.speaker: Party Pete
overhead-dialogue-falador-party-room.text: Want to take some cake with you?

overhead-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.npc: Mum wants to know if you're coming round for tea.

overhead-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.speaker: Parroty Pete
overhead-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.text: No, I've got another late night here.

overhead-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.speaker: Parroty  Pete
overhead-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.text: Ol' bluebeak's got the flu again!

overhead-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.npc: Oh dear. Nothing too serious I hope.

overhead-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.speaker: Parroty  Pete
overhead-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.text: Well, as long as he hasn't caught anything from that evil chicken.

overhead-dialogue-ardougne-zoo.npc: Got a taste for parrots now too has he?
Sigh.* Will nothing sacred be safe?

overhead-dialogue-north-of-port-phasmaty.npc: Hey Pete. Any news from the fleet?

overhead-dialogue-north-of-port-phasmaty.speaker: Pirate Pete
overhead-dialogue-north-of-port-phasmaty.text: 'Tis all quiet on the eastern front.

overhead-dialogue-north-of-port-phasmaty.npc: Well, you know what to do if something goes wrong.

overhead-dialogue-north-of-port-phasmaty.speaker: Pirate Pete
overhead-dialogue-north-of-port-phasmaty.text: Holler like a bosun without a bottle.

overhead-dialogue-north-of-port-phasmaty.npc: That's it brother, and we'll come a running!

overhead-dialogue-ice-mountain.npc: Well, I'm back. And he said no. Again.
Lemons? What are you talking about?
I swear you get stranger every time.

overhead-dialogue-upon-changing-location.npc: Now, how's this thing work again...?

high-prayer-level.npc: Greetings, [player name]. Can I help you with anything, today?

options.text: How can I train my prayer?

steps.player: How can I train my prayer?

steps.text: If the player has 99 prayer:

steps.npc: I think you should be teaching me a thing or two, shouldn't you?
Well, if you really want my advice...
The most common way to train prayer is by either burying bones, or offering them to the gods at some kind of an altar.
Lots of adventurers build such altars in their own homes, or there are a few frequent places of worship around the world.
Different kinds of bones will help you to train faster. Generally speaking, the bigger they are and the more frightening a creature they come from, the better they are for it.
Is there anything else you would like to know?
The gods look kindly upon their devout followers. There are all kinds of benefits they may provide, if you pray for them!
They could help you in combat, help your wounds to heal more quickly, protect your belongings... There's a lot they can do for you!

steps.text: The prayer tab opens.

steps.npc: You can find out more by looking in your prayer book.
You need to be careful that your prayers don't run out, though. You can get prayer potions to help you recharge, or you can pray at an altar whenever one's nearby.
Is there anything else you would like to know?
Very well. Saradomin be with you!

standard.npc: Hello! Glad to see you're okay. I was worried you might have gone and got stuck down that hole.

standard.player: No need to worry. I'm mostly quite capable when it comes to these kinds of things!

standard.npc: Good to hear!

standard-dialogue-during-desert-treasure.text: If the player never spoke to Ramarno after completion of Below Ice Mountain:

steps.npc: Hello there. Did you see that dwarf by the big forge? I think he wanted to talk to you.

standard-dialogue-during-desert-treasure.text: If the player spoke to Ramarno after completion of Below Ice Mountain:

steps.npc: Hello! Look at this place. Isn't it amazing?

steps.player: It sure is! Not every day you find yourself in a lost city.

steps.npc: So what can I do for you?

steps.player: Does the name Lassar mean anything to you? It was an old fortress that once existed here, long before Camdozaal. I'm wondering if there might still be some traces left down here.

steps.npc: A ruin within a ruin? How exciting! We have found the odd thing that doesn't seem to be dwarven in origin, but it's still early days for us here, so we haven't been able to learn much yet.
One that was particularly interesting was this strange icon I found in the mine.

steps.text: The archaeologist shows you an unusual icon.

steps.npc: Could be a lot more to find over there, but I must admit, I haven't been back since... well...
It's probably nothing, but there's this big sinkhole on the other side of the mine. I'm probably just being silly, but I'm sure I heard a voice coming from inside.

steps.player: Interesting... And if I wanted to go down this hole?

steps.npc: Go down the hole?! You're far braver than I am! There's plenty of rocks around there. I'm sure you could tie a rope to one of them. You'd need a pretty long rope though. Here, you can use mine.

steps.text: The archaeologist gives you some rope.

standard.npc: Hello! What can I do for you today?

steps.npc: I'm Preswylwyr.

steps.player: It's nice to meet you Preswylwyr, I'm [player name].

steps.npc: And it's great to meet you, [player name].

steps.text: other

steps.npc: I'm Gwerin's partner, he runs the mill while it's my job to use up all the flour he produces.

steps.player: You bake? So that's what the wonderful smell is.

steps.npc: Ha ha! Would you care for some bread? There should be some on the table.

steps.player: Really? That's very nice of you, thanks!

steps.npc: No problem! Was there anything else you wanted?

steps.text: other

standard.speaker: Priest
standard.text: Peace be with you, friend.

standard-dialogue-talking-to-a-priest-at.speaker: Priest
standard-dialogue-talking-to-a-priest-at.text: Greetings. May the blessings of Icthlarin rest on your tired shoulders and set you at ease during these strange times.

options.text: What's that place to the south?

steps.player: What's that place to the south?

steps.speaker: Priest
steps.text: That's the old necropolis. It's been abandoned for a long time. In fact, you couldn't even access most of it until fairly recently.

steps.speaker: Priest
steps.text: It was mostly buried under the sand until a storm came in from the south.

steps.player: Interesting... I bet the place is a hotspot for grave robbers.

steps.speaker: Priest
steps.text: Not as many as you'd think. There's a lot of superstition about the place. People say that even the sand is marked by death.

steps.player: You sound like you don't believe them.

steps.speaker: Priest
steps.text: Not really. The sand is probably that colour due to the amount of salt in it. Still, if it keeps people from robbing the dead, that's no bad thing.

steps.player: I see. Thanks for the information.

steps.speaker: Priest
steps.text: Any time, adventurer.

using-a-potion-on-him.speaker: Priest
using-a-potion-on-him.text: Hey, hey, hey! What in the name of sweet suffering Icthlarin are you doing?

using-a-potion-on-him.player: I thought this acne potion might clear up your spots.

using-a-potion-on-him.speaker: Priest
using-a-potion-on-him.text: All that you'll achieve by pouring that potion on me is to ruin my lovely robes.

using-a-potion-on-him.player: Sorry, I was just trying to help.

standard.speaker: Priest
standard.text: I wish there was more I could do for these people.

standard-dialogue-after-song-of-the-elve.speaker: Priest
