standard.npc: You left the shrine. Did Zulrah reject your sacrifice?

steps.npc: Is that what you think? Board the boat again, and I am sure you will find Zulrah has overcome whatever pitiful attacks you used against him.

options.text: Remind me how this ritual works.

steps.player: Remind me how this ritual works.

steps.npc: Once I have brought you to the shrine, I will leave you there as an offering to Zulrah. You cannot use the boat to return.
You can use your magical powers to flee from Zulrah's grasp, though that would defeat the point of the sacrifice, and you'll have to try again.
When Zulrah inevitably kills you, I may be able to retrieve your dropped possessions. If so, I will hold them here.
Now board the boat and prepare to be sacrificed.

standard-dialogue-talking-to-her-before-.npc: Leave me, human, I have a sacrifice to prepare. If you wish for information, go and see the High Priestess.

options.text: But I really want to ride the boat!

steps.npc: You display complete ignorance of our sacred rites. Perhaps the High Priestess will consent to enlighten you.

standard-dialogue-talking-to-her-after-o.player: The High Priestess said I could offer myself as a sacrifice to Zulrah.

standard-dialogue-talking-to-her-after-o.npc: It is rare for a traveller to make such an offer! Very well, I shall explain the ritual to you...

steps.npc: I shall now transport you to Zulrah's shrine and offer your life on behalf of our tribe.

standard.npc: Camdozaal is a shadow of what it once was. We Imcando Dwarves were the finest artisans in the world, but now I am all that remains. Today, you'll only find echoes of our once great city.
But that which was once great can still be great again! We Imcando Dwarves know that better than most. There is hope for the future of Camdozaal. But I need help.
We have a Sacred Forge. You will find none other like it in all the world. Some of the greatest weapons of legend started life here.
The Forge could be the key to Camdozaal's future, but it's going out. If it does, I fear it will never be lit again. I can no longer gather the fuel it needs. But perhaps you can?
Barronite. You'll only find it in these ruins. If you can gather some for me, I can use it to keep the Forge lit. In return, I'll let you take what you want from our Great Vault.
I no longer have use for anything in the Vault. Besides, material possessions mean nothing compared to the fire of the Sacred Forge.

standard.player: So I find barronite in the ruins and bring it to you? Doesn't sound too difficult. Where should I start?

standard.npc: Anywhere you like. The ruins are filled with barronite, so anything you do here should yield some. If you need more information on specific things you can do, just let me know.

steps.player: What happened to the other Imcando Dwarves?

steps.npc: Ah... It's a tough tale to tell. Even though it's been many years since the last of my kin died out, the memory is still fresh.

steps.player: You don't have to tell me if the memory hurts too much.

steps.npc: No, I will. The legacy of my kin must live on.
As you can see around you, Camdozaal was once a great city. Alive with the hum of activity. We dug deep into the mountain and reaped the rewards.
Our methods would often differ from other dwarves. Whereas they just used traditional smithing techniques, we would combine them with magic as well.
Alas, that was ultimately our undoing. We learned of a horde of barbarians pillaging across the land, hunting down and killing anyone who dared use magic.
We underestimated them. We believed our weapons would be enough to keep us safe. We were wrong.
The barbarians brought ruin upon Camdozaal. Most of my kind died as the city collapsed around them. Only a few of us survived until the end. Now, only I remain.

steps.player: The world has changed a lot, Ramarno. Magic is practiced freely. Those barbarians failed to wipe it from Gielinor.

steps.npc: I'm glad they didn't win, I suppose. But it doesn't change much for me. I am still the last Imcando Dwarf.

steps.player: I'm sorry Ramarno. I will do my best to help ensure the legacy of your kin lives on.

steps.npc: Thank you, [player name]. That gives me some hope. If you have any more questions, do not hesitate to ask.

steps.text: other

subsequent-dialogue-if-the-player-has-me.npc: Ah [player name]. I'm sure you have plenty of questions. I will do my best to answer them.

steps.npc: As you can see, Camdozaal isn't the city it once was. That said, there are still a few things around here that might interest you. There's the golem workshop, the barronite mine and the offering altar.

options.text: Tell me more about the golem workshop.

steps.player: Tell me more about the golem workshop.

steps.npc: You'll find it to the east. It was once the forefront of our technological advances. Sadly, it was also one of the major factors that led to our doom.
Camdozaal was built upon the ruins of an older civilization. Little trace of them remained by the time we arrived. However, when building the city, ancient golems were discovered.
These golems were very crude. They were mostly made from clay, of all things. We used our advanced Smithing knowledge to improve their form. Eventually, we were able to get them working again.
We kept pushing with the golems. Many of them we imbued with magical energies. We started with mind and body energy, but eventually moved on to chaos as well.
Alas, the influence of chaos had grave results. We lost control of many. Those that became corrupt had to be locked away, but by then it was already too late.
The barbarians had learnt of our experimentation, and were determined to destroy all traces of it.
Ironically, locking them away meant the golems were among the few things to survive the barbarians. If you fancy a bit of combat, you might want to go take a look.
They're largely made of barronite now, so they're a good source of the stuff.
Their cores are also very interesting. Apparently, the dwarves of the golem workshop once used old cores to craft runes. Maybe you could do the same.

steps.text: other

options.text: Tell me more about the barronite mine.

steps.player: Tell me more about the barronite mine.

steps.npc: You'll find it to the north west. Unsurprisingly, it's the best place to find barronite in the city.
At one time, our miners would work all through the day there to gather the barronite needed to power the Sacred Forge. That was a long time ago.
If you're lucky, you might find other things while mining there. We were not the first to build a home beneath this mountain. Sometimes traces of an older civilization can be found.
You might find some ancient relics encased within barronite. If you do, you can use the anvils here to crack open the deposits.
The relics are of no interest to me. Maybe some of your race would find them interesting.

steps.text: other

options.text: Tell me more about the offering altar.

steps.player: Tell me more about the offering altar.

steps.npc: You'll find it to the south west. It's not something that ever interested me, but most of my kind were followers of Saradomin - the god of order and wisdom.
Many of my kin would visit the altar to make offerings in his name.
First, they'd catch fish from the nearby reservoir. Next, they'd ritually prepare them at tables by the altar. Finally, they'd use the altar to offer the fish.
There's plenty of barronite to be found within the reservoir, so it might be worth checking out. Be warned though: worshipping gods never did my kind any good.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Very well.

steps.npc: An Imcando Dwarf survived outside the city?

steps.player: Yes. He looks to be doing quite well for himself. In fact, he seems to be a master of Smithing.

steps.npc: I can't believe it. I hope to meet him one day. He must be a truly amazing smith to reach such heights.

steps.player: Well he's certainly an interesting dwarf.

steps.npc: I'm afraid not. The Sacred Forge is like none other in existence. Only an Imcando Dwarf could use it correctly.
Truth be told, I don't fully know. It's far older than I am. It was supposedly built in the earliest days of the city.
What I do know is that it's been imbued with powerful magic - some said that of the gods themselves. The Forge powers the entire city, or what's left of it at least.
I've been doing my best to keep it lit over the years. It's not a job I'm capable of any more though. That's why I'm hoping you can help.
Bring me any barronite you find. In return, I can channel enough power from the Forge into the city or even open the Great Vault.

options.text: What will powering the city do?

steps.player: What will powering the city do?

steps.npc: From what I can tell, my ancestors linked the Forge to the entire city.
It truly is the heart of this place. From it, I can channel any barronite you have into empowering different aspects of the city.
The Sacred Forge is a strange beast, but with its arcane power, you'll see an improvement to the various activities you can do in the city.
Would you like to take a look?

steps.text: Ramarno's Shard Exchange opens.

steps.npc: Very well. Anything else you'd like to talk about?

steps.text: other

steps.npc: It's one of the many marvels of this city. We used it to store our greatest creations, along with our most interesting finds.
Of course, I have no use for those treasures myself. I'd happily give them up to keep the Sacred Forge alive.
Now be warned - I won't be able to channel much power into the Vault. I can't afford to waste too much barronite. You'll only have a limited amount of time in there.
Not only that, there's an automatic security system that activates if power to the Vault is lost. If that happens, you'll be removed. I imagine any treasures would be lost as well.

steps.player: How much barronite do you need to power it?

steps.npc: Hmm, for a minute, I suppose 750 barronite shards should do the trick.

steps.text: If the player's Ranged level is below X {{tmissing}} :

steps.npc: To start with you'll need a bow and arrows, you were given a Shortbow and some arrows when you arrived here from Tutorial island.
Alternatively, you can claim a training bow and some arrows from me.
Mikasi, the Magic Combat tutor and I both give out items every 30 minutes, however you must choose whether you want runes or ranged equipment.
To claim the Training bow and arrows, right-click on me and choose Claim, to claim runes right-click on the Magic Combat tutor and select Claim.
Not all bows can use every type of arrow, most bows have a limit. You can find out your bows limit by checking the Ranged skill guide.
If you do decide to use the Training bow, you will only be able to use the Training arrows with it. Remember to pick up your arrows, re-use them and come back when you need more.
Once you have your bow and arrows, equip them by selecting their Wield option in your inventory.
You can change the way you attack by going to the combat options tab. There are three attack styles for bows. Those styles are Accurate, Rapid and Longrange.
Accurate increases your bows attack accuracy. Rapid will increase your attack speed with the bow. Longrange will let you attack your enemies from a greater distance.

You can then hand those tickets in for a variety of goods you can use to train your Ranged skill.

options.text: How do I create a bow and arrows?

steps.npc: Ahh the art of fletching. Fletching is used to create your own bow and arrows.

steps.text: If the player is on a free-to-play world:

steps.npc: To create your bow and arrows you would need to gather some wood, feathers, arrow heads and bow string. The wood would be to make arrow shafts which can be turned into unstrung bows and arrow shafts.
Unfortunately, Fletching is a member only skill so you will have to get your ranging supplies from shops or other players.
Is there anything else you want to know?

steps.text: other
If the player is on a members' world:

steps.npc: It's quite simple really. You'll need an axe to cut some logs from trees and a knife. Knives can be found in and around the Lumbridge castle and in the Varrock General store upstairs.
Use your knife on the logs. This will bring up a menu listing items you can fletch.
For arrows you will need to smith some arrow heads and kill some chickens for feathers.
Add the feathers to your Arrow shafts to make Headless arrows, then use your chosen arrow heads on the Headless arrows to make your arrows.
Now for making bows. When accessing the fletching menu, instead of choosing Arrows shafts, you can make an unstrung bow instead.
To complete the bow you will need to get your hands on a Bow string.
First you will need to get some flax from a flax field. There's one south of Seers' Village. Gather flax, then spin it on a spinning wheel, there's one in Seers' Village too.
This makes bow strings which you can then use on the unstrung bows to make a working bow!

Unfortunately, about a century ago, the once thriving group was wiped out during the barbarian invasions of that time.

'Not much is known about the hero called Robert the Strong. Most folk tales describe him as being taller than the tallest human and far stronger than the strongest warrior.'
'He wields a six foot tall longbow and travels with his faithful panther, Odysseus. He is said to have had a personal crusade against the dragonkin...'
I'm coming to that.
'The stories tell of the dragonkin being an intelligent race of bird-like creatures that walked rather than using their wings. They are said to be immortal, but cannot reproduce.'
'Because of this, they became very afraid of death and shunned all other races.'
'Some even say the dragonkin made corrupted versions of themselves for protection, what we now know as dragons. However, this has never been proven.'
There's no doubt that some elements of these tales have been overexaggerated for storytelling purposes, but you should be careful of outright dismissing them.
Robert the Strong is a name that often comes up in stories from the Fourth Age. There's no reason not to believe that these folk tales are based on events that actually happened.

steps.player: Somebody set up us the bomb!

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Wooowoowoooooo.... Woowoowoo? Woooo, wooowoo wooowooowooo!

steps.player: You have no chance to survive make your time.

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Woo?

steps.player: All your base are belong to us.
Hey, don't think you can talk to me like that!

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Woo! WOO WOOOOO WOOWOOWOO WOO WOOOOO!

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Wooowoowoooooo.... Woowoowoo? Woooo, wooowoo wooowooowooo!

steps.player: Just because you're already dead, doesn't mean I can't find a way to hurt you ghosty!
No, I've never been there in my life and CERTAINLY didn't steal anything when I was!

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Woo! WOO WOOOOO WOOWOOWOO WOO WOOOOO!

steps.player: Are you calling me a liar?!?! I have never stolen a thing in my life, and I resent the implication that I am the kind of morally depraved individual that would steal someone else's hard earned
Or cakes. Or fur. Repeatedly. For long periods at a time.

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Wooowoowoooooo.... Woowoowoo? Woooo, wooowoo wooowooowooo!

steps.player: Well if you are going to take that attitude, then I have nothing further to say on the matter, and bid you good day!

after-curse-of-the-empty-lord.speaker: Mysterious ghost
after-curse-of-the-empty-lord.text: Ah, it be you again! What can I do fer ya?

steps.player: Can you tell me where I can find Kharrim again?

steps.text: If Kharrim is in the Chaos Temple (church):

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Kharrim the messenger... Well, he was always a devoted follower of old General Zamorak, and if I remember rightly Zamorak set up a small base in an old temple near Dareeyak...

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: You might want to check around there.

steps.player: Okay, well I'll try and find him for you then.

steps.text: If Kharrim is in the Graveyard of Shadows:

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Kharrim the messenger... Last I'd heard of him, he'd headed off to Carrallagar to seek his fortune. Ya might want to check around there somewhere.

steps.player: Okay, well I'll try and find him for you then.

steps.text: If Kharrim is in the Lava Maze:

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Kharrim the messenger... The last I'd heard of that weasel he was claiming he'd found some underground deposit of runite ore guarded by demons and dragons.

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: I suspect he was pulling some scam or other, but if you know of such a place, that might be a good place to start checking.

steps.player: Okay, well I'll try and find him for you then.
Could I have more of those ghostly robes you gave me?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: It seems as though the curse that keeps me here extends to my very clothing... which piece do you want?
the requested piece(s) of ghostly robes

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Here you go.

speaking-to-the-wrong-rennard.text: When spoken to in a location not in the player's Curse of the Empty Lord sequence:

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: The endless tragedy of fate... Why must you torment me so?

steps.player: Alright, alright, calm down, calm down. All I said was 'hello'!

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: You can see me?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: And you understand my words?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: This is incredible! How can such a thing have come to pass?

steps.player: What can I say? I'm a professional.

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Hello back at you.

steps.player: So what's a nice ghost like you doing in a place like this?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: I suppose you think that's funny?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: I don't think I want to talk to you anymore.

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Hello stranger. It is rare indeed that I meet one who can see my presence, let alone one who can understand my words.

steps.player: Soooo.... Is it fun being a ghost?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Does it look like fun to you?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Then you are a fool, and I will waste no more words upon you.

steps.player: Sheesh, what a grouch. You'd think you'd have more of a sense of humour being dead and all.

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Mortal... Take heed of my example, and waste not your life, lest you may suffer the same fate as myself...

steps.player: Huh? You mean someone did this to you?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: You have ascertained the truth in my words...

steps.player: So who did it to you? And why?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Events of moons past, I remember not clearly...

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Hello stranger.

steps.player: So.... Invisible ghost haunting the same place for thousands of years, huh?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: You have no idea...

steps.player: Well, bad luck and all that. See ya around!

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Hello.

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: Apparently.

steps.player: In which case I only have one thing to say to you:

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: ...what?

steps.player: Guess you don't have the amulet of humanspeak, huh?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: ...huh?

steps.player: Yeah, that's right. WOO! WOOOWOOO WOO WOOOOWOO! Got no comeback for that, have you?

steps.speaker: Mysterious ghost
steps.text: You are very strange...

standard.npc: Hello there. What are you doing here?

standard.player: Just looking around at the moment.

standard.npc: Well, feel free to talk to me should you come across anything you can't figure out.

standard-dialogue-after-the-dig-site.npc: Hello there! I heard all about your big find; well done!

options.text: Can you tell me more about the tools an archaeologist uses?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about the tools an archaeologist uses?

steps.npc: Of course! Let's see now... Rock picks are for splitting rocks or scraping away soil; you can get one from a cupboard in the Education Centre.
I think you'll find them scattered about pretty much everywhere, but I know you can get one from a cupboard somewhere in the Education Centre, just like the rock pick!

steps.player: Okay, what about a specimen brush?

steps.npc: We have a bit of a shortage of those at the moment. You could try borrowing one from a workman on the site... but I don't think they'd give it willingly.

steps.player: Sounds like I'll need to be sneaky to get one of those, then... Okay - trowel?

steps.npc: Ahh... that you must earn by passing your exams! The examiner holds those.
If you need something identified or are not sure about something, give it to Terry; he's the archaeological expert in the next room.

standard.npc: Nilsal! Welcome to our camp, adventurer.

options.text: That sounds lovely, what tune is that?

steps.player: That sounds lovely, what tune is that?

steps.npc: Oh, this? It's just the beginning of something, still a lot more to come.
I s'pose the working title is...'The Doors of Dinh'.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: We come from Varlamore... We're students of the College of Bards.
Or did you want to know where I'm from specifically? My home was destroyed long ago by an evil saltwater deity.

steps.player: Well, that's certainly a dark and tortured backstory. Say, have you slain any dragons? Wooed a beautiful princess? Sought revenge on the fiend who killed your family?

steps.npc: ...Dragons? Slain. Princesses? Wooed... but revenge, that's still brewing.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: See you around, adventurer.

standard.npc: Wooooo! Ooooooh!

standard.player: I can't understand a word you are saying. Maybe Father Aereck will be able to help.

steps.npc: Well, we find a lot of soaked pages in our nets. If you've got something we really want, I could swap it for 25 soaked pages.

standard.text: Greetings. What wisdom do you seek?

steps.speaker: Rewards Guardian
steps.text: Me? I'm here to grant you rewards for any of the Pizazz Points you may have earned in this training arena. Like my fellow Guardians, I am part of the arena and live to ensure its safe running.

steps.player: Can I trade my Pizazz Points please?

steps.text: Why of course.

If the player has at least 200 coins:
Arena book

if-entrance-guardian-hasn-t-been-spoken-.speaker: Rewards Guardian
if-entrance-guardian-hasn-t-been-spoken-.text: Well, you need to talk to him first.

standard.npc: Oh, hellow adventurer. Can I help you with anything?

steps.npc: This is the prison of Zalcano.
That's right. She's a powerful demon, one bearing an ancient curse.

steps.player: A curse? That doesn't sound good.

steps.npc: Don't worry, the curse only affects her. Because of it, her entire body has been turned to stone.

steps.player: I see. So why is she here?

steps.npc: She came to our lands long ago, before the curse had fully taken hold. We imprisoned her here for study, so that we might learn more about her affliction.
If you want to learn more, you should be able to find a book in the Grand Library about her.
Is there anything else I can help you with?

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Well we could always use some help in keeping Zalcano under control.
Zalcano is formed completely from stone. Because of this, normal weapons won't work on her.
That said, when she's vulnerable, you can still do some damage to her if you use a pickaxe.

steps.player: When she's vulnerable? How do I make her vulnerable?

steps.npc: The ore found within these caverns can be rather volatile, especially when heated. We've found that when imbued, this ore can damage her armour.
You'll want to head on in and mine the ore from the rocks around the prison. Once you have some, you can heat it using the furnace and then imbue it using the altar.
Once you've got some imbued ore, just give it a throw her way and she'll definitely feel it.
Is there anything else I can help you with?

steps.text: other

options.text: What do I get for helping out here?

steps.player: What do I get for helping out here?

steps.npc: Well assuming you are successful of subdueing Zalcano, she has accumulated a lot of ores and magical runes from her time as a demon.

steps.player: Not bad, what if I didn't want these resource? Is there anything you can give me instead?

steps.npc: Well we would always appreciate these resources, in exchange we could bestow upon you our elven knowledge for mining.
We wouldn't be asking for anything special though, just the common resources are what we require.

steps.prompt: Customise Zalcano Loot

standard.npc: Hey! What can I do for ya' today?

steps.npc: I'm Rhoddwr, a simple forest dweller.

steps.player: It's nice to meet you Rhoddwr, I'm [player name].

steps.npc: And it's great to meet you, [player name].

steps.text: other

steps.npc: I'm the leader of this small camp. We live amongst the trees, at one with the forest.
That's because it is! This is where we belong, this is where we began.

steps.player: A nice sentiment, but we can't all live off the land.

steps.npc: Very true! As we expand and grow, nature refuses to adjust to our ways. The only other option is to destroy it to make room for growth.

steps.player: Hopefully nature understands the necessity of it all.

steps.npc: History shows again and again that nature points out the folly of man.

steps.player: Which is why we should learn from the past and avoid making such mistakes.

steps.npc: Indeed, although some mistakes have lasting effects that cannot be undone. Is there anything else you wanted to know?

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Farewell, adventurer.

before-starting-fallen-from-grace-or-aft.text: Rian watches you cautiously, refusing to engage.

after-completing-fallen-from-grace.npc: Cormac's spread the word of what you did for us. I'm glad you turned out not to be a troublemaker.
Good. Keep it that way and most around here will warm to you.

standard.speaker: Ribs
standard.text: Ahoy, young whippersnapper. Have you come to hear a tale from old Ribs?

options.text: Could you tell me about Barnacle Barnaby?

steps.player: Could you tell me about Barnacle Barnaby?

steps.speaker: Ribs
steps.text: He was a cruel and vicious pirate. Orchestrator of the Driftwood Massacre and unleasher of the Plague of Black Mists. He believed himself untouchable, but his arrogance was his undoing.

steps.speaker: Ribs
steps.text: Despite the warnings of many, Barnacle Barnaby attempted to plunder the Skullhorde, but his only reward was a deadly curse. It destroyed the Crimson Kraken, condemning all on board to a watery grave.

steps.player: And you had a map leading to the wreck of the Kraken?

steps.speaker: Ribs
steps.text: Aye! I purchased the map from Ulrich the Unfortunate, the sole survivor of the Kraken, but I had no intention of using it. I knew that no good would ever come from seeking the Kraken.

steps.player: Then why not destroy the map?

steps.speaker: Ribs
steps.text: And risk the wrath of Barnaby's ghost? No. I thought it better the map be locked away, so that neither it nor the curse could harm anyone else, but those young fools put an end to that.

steps.speaker: Ribs
steps.text: Now we can only hope that someone puts a stop to them before it's too late. Who knows, perhaps it will be you who does so.

steps.player: Well, on that note, I'd best be getting off. Until next time, Ribs.

steps.speaker: Ribs
steps.text: As you wish, but you would be wise to learn from your elders. My tales might one day save you from a one-way trip to see Davey Jones!

standard.text: Hello. How can I help you?

options.text: Can you give me any Farming advice?

steps.speaker: Richard

steps.text: My pub's called The Golden Field. It's where all the local workers come to relax and unwind after a hard day. I try to keep it really nice here for them. Anyway, are you drinking?

If The Queen of Thieves has not been started:

steps.text: They say there's trouble in Port Piscarilius. Something about gangs uniting. Might be worth looking into.

steps.speaker: Richard

steps.speaker: Richard

steps.text: Ahh well they make it less likely that you'll accidently attack anyone wearing the same cape as you and easier to attack everyone else. They also make it easier to distinguish people who're wearing the same cape as you

steps.speaker: Richard
steps.text: from everyone else. They're very useful when out in the wilderness with friends or anyone else you don't want to harm.

standard.npc: 'Allo mate! Got a job going? Only 500 coins!

steps.npc: I'm a great cook, me! I used to work with a rat-catcher, I used to cook for him. There's a dozen different ways you can cook rat!

options.text: Tell me about your previous jobs

steps.player: Tell me about your previous jobs.

steps.npc: Well, city warder Bravek once threw a chair at me and yelled at me to get him a hangover cure. So I made it and I think it worked, 'cause then he threw another chair at me and that one hit!

steps.text: If the player does not have at least 20 Construction:

steps.npc: Sorry mate, but I'm not allowed to work for anyone without level 20 Construction. It's a safety 'azard!

after-arriving-to-keldagrim.player: Hello there, what are you doing here?

standard-dialogue-after-the-giant-dwarf.player: I'm glad I don't have to talk to you anymore!

standard.npc: Welcome to the clothes store. How might I help you?

options.text: It's a very interesting island you have here.

steps.player: It's a very interesting island you have here.

steps.npc: Why thank you. It's been our haven for a great many generations.

steps.player: Everything seems to have a magical feel to it.

steps.npc: Of course. We integrate magic into all areas of our lives. It is a part of everyone, so why deny it? It's best to make the most of this innate gift we have all been given.

steps.player: What sort of things do you use your magic for?

steps.npc: Take a look around. We use it in our day to day lives, from making a cup of tea, to travelling around the island. You see our ancestors were the ones that found the first rune essence and put it to use! The various
factions were eventually created, with people having different ideas on how the essence should be used (or not in some cases!)

steps.player: What has kept you so secluded on this island?

steps.npc: It may be a bit beyond you, but although magic comes from within, we are all very strongly linked to the moon and the effects it has on us cannot be denied!
Of course not. This very island has a great link to our moon, which helps us understand ourselves - especially our dreams, which is the path to understanding magic.

steps.player: I think I will just have to take your word on that.

standard.npc: Come to visit my garden then, have you, human?

steps.npc: No no, not quite. But I do look after it. It's the palace garden, you see. I keep it tidy, keep it living.
It's hard to grow much on these hard rocks deep beneath these mountains, you know.

steps.player: I can imagine. Where do you get all your food from? Or even the soil for this garden?

steps.npc: We can grow a little food underground, but most of it comes from the extensive steamcart network that runs beneath the earth.
In the Era of Kings, many centuries ago, it was harder of course. Our steam technology was not developed as far yet and getting fresh supplies of food was always a problem.
Oh, I'm not boring you, am I?

steps.player: Not at all! Please, go on!

steps.npc: Oh yes, as I was saying, it was difficult to make a decent living here. I'm afraid this garden was rather neglected during that time.

steps.player: Why did you dwarves stay so deep under ground, then? Why not simply go above ground?

steps.npc: What, with the wars raging up there?
We dwarves went underground a long time ago, see. For a while the city of Keldagrim was completely cut off from the rest of Gielinor simply waiting out the wars of the humans and the gods.
This made it hard, though, to determine when the wars above the ground were over. Perhaps Keldagrim had remained hidden for far too long.
Only when King Alvis heroically defended the city against an invasion of trolls did we dare to venture out and see how much the world had changed.
Of course, after that...
Ah well, enough history lessons I should say. I must really get back to my gardening.

steps.player: A little, yes. I don't really know what all this has to do with anything.

steps.npc: I suppose it doesn't, really, it's just the mumblings of an old dwarf.
Oh, alright then.
Well, it's funny you should ask that actually, I run the local parcel service to the mainland.
Yes, we sometimes get asked to send items back to the mainland. We can send items to individuals' bank accounts, for a small fee of course.
It costs 10 trading sticks per item, unfortunately, even stackable items cost the same.

steps.player: What are trading sticks and how do I get some?

steps.npc: Trading sticks are our local currency, you could perhaps earn some trading sticks by doing some work around the village.
Have a chat with Murcaily, I think he was looking for someone to help him, he works near the hardwood grove to the east of Trufitus' hut.

Well, I dunno... The village is kind of on the fringe out here, I dunno how up to date the stuff I hear about is...
You want to know about Canifis? I dunno why, not a lot happens here. We're just your typical everyday down at earth werewolf folk, after all...

steps.player: So... everyone here is a werewolf?

steps.npc: Yep. We are as Zamorak made us!
Yeah, he's great isn't he? Every year we hold a big festival to give thanks to Zamorak for keeping us well fed and happy here.
I hear over in the West they worship Saradomin, but I dunno why! What's he ever done to help out us werewolves, huh?
I hear he has all these crazy followers who say things like we shouldn't kill people and eat them! What's up with that?
Aaaah, not for a good few months yet. Come and ask me again nearer to the time, I'll keep some extra meat and mead back from the rest for ya pal.

options.text: Tell me about the land of Morytania.

steps.player: Tell me about the land of Morytania.

steps.text: Before The Blood Moon Rises:

steps.npc: Well, I don't know what to tell you really... This village is called Canifis and lies on the border between Morytania and Misthalin... so we're kind of on the front line if those Saradominists to the west ever decide to
attack us...
No? The Saradominists hate us. It's only thanks to Lord Drakan that these lands are kept safe.
Ahhh... you must be new to these parts if you haven't heard of Lord Drakan! He's the lord of this land, and we all pledge allegiance to him.
In return for our allegiance, and the tithe of course, he keeps our land safe from any invaders and the Saradominists who want to kill us all.

Ah, well, in return for his protection, we have to give Lord Drakan a share of blood every week. If we don't have any to spare from our hunts, then we need to pick a member of the village to give their life in return
for the blood so that the tithe is fulfilled.

steps.player: You mean you kill someone you know in order to meet the tithe???

steps.npc: That's right, but only if we haven't managed to get enough spare blood from our hunts. It's kind of severe if you look at it that way, but frankly, I think the price is fair in return for his protection and his tolerance of
our village. He could probably kill us all if he wanted us gone, so keeping on his good side is worth the sacrifice to us. Lucky we're not human really!

steps.text: If Vampyre Slayer is completed:

steps.npc: He hates humans! Apparently long ago his brother Draynor was trapped in Misthalin and lost much of his powers, and was recently killed by some human!

steps.text: continues
If Vampyre Slayer is not completed:

steps.npc: He hates humans! Apparently his brother Draynor is trapped in Misthalin, and adventurous little human wannabe-heroes keep trying to kill him!

steps.text: continues

steps.npc: Man, I'd hate to be a human around here, that's for sure. Drakan would really enjoy hunting them down and killing them!

steps.text: After The Blood Moon Rises:

steps.npc: Well, I don't know what to tell you really... This village is called Canifis and lies on the border between Morytania and Misthalin... so we're kind of on the front line if those Saradominists to the west ever decide to
attack us...

No? The Saradominists hate us. It was only thanks to Lord Drakan that these lands were kept safe, but now he's gone and we've got some new overlord who apparently wants us to all be friends! Like that's ever
going to happen!

steps.player: So... Are you going to do something about that?

steps.npc: Me? Of course not! Someone really should though...

options.text: Tell me about the shopkeepers here.

steps.player: Tell me about the shopkeepers here.

steps.npc: Hmmm? Why, who did you want to hear the gossip about?

steps.player: Tell me what you know about Sbott the Tanner.

steps.npc: Hey, I won't hear a word said bad about that guy! He's an honest and hard-working wolf if I ever met one! He charges a lot for his job, but he's one of the best tanners I've ever seen - and I'm over four hundred
years old! You need stuff tanning, I recommend him!

steps.player: Know anything interesting about Rufus the food seller?

steps.npc: Ah yeah... good old Rufus... He's kind of getting on in years and doesn't like to come out of his wolf form so often, but let me tell you this: that guy is a hunter through and through. You seen how much food he

catches a day? That takes real dedication! Some of the young pups think just because a wolf has a bit of grey in his fur then he's past it, but I've seen him put those pups to shame in a hunt! He's a real inspiration to us
all!

steps.player: Got anything to share about Barker the clothes seller?

steps.npc: Eh, I don't like the guy much, but you can't knock the quality of his stock. They're some fine quality threads you can get yourself there.
Eh... I can't really tell you to be honest. Something about the guy just gets my hackles up everytime he opens his yap, know what I mean?
Lucky for you. I can't really explain it, I just don't like the guy. Does great clothes though, you got to give him that.

steps.player: I bet you have some juicy gossip about Fidelio the general store owner.

steps.npc: That nut job? Oh sure, we all know about him. He was a real firebrand daredevil when he was younger, always taking risks to make himself a quick buck... he got himself caught up in the smuggling trade, sneaking over
the border into Misthalin and pretending to be a human so he could buy exotic items to sell.

steps.player: Exotic items? From Misthalin? Like what?

steps.npc: Oh man, you name it! Flour... buckets... tinderboxes... chisels... he could get the lot! He's been doing it so long now though, his nerves are shot.
Nowadays he's a disgrace, he can barely string a sentence together and jumps at his own shadow. Makes you feel ashamed to be a werewolf.

options.text: Tell me about the temple to the West.

steps.player: Tell me about the temple to the west.

steps.npc: Well, I'm not old enough to remember the full story behind it, but it was a terrible day for these lands when it was built there.
Apparently, Morytania was once a strong and mighty kingdom, with lands spreading far further west than they do today, and south into the desert as well.

That was all until the day when a sneak attack by the hated human forces who worship Saradomin burned our villages and slaughtered our peoples in mass. To rub salt into the wound, they then cursed the river as well!
Luckily they seem to have calmed down somewhat recently, and tend to stay on their side of the river... but the wrong they have done my people will never be forgotten, and will never be forgiven!
Absolutely! If I ever met one I would gobble him up where he stands! And then chew the bones for dessert!
A story??? Heh, well the only one I can think of right now is one my dear old mammy told me as a pup...
Now how did it go... Ah yes!

Once upon a time a brave young wolf was walking through a forest, when he came upon a human dressed all in red. 'Aha!' he thought to himself, 'Here's a nice easy meal!' But the human talked to him, and as he was
always taught to be a polite wolf, he spoke back to it.

Well, this cunning human told him that there was a better meal that would not run away in a house in the woods. As the brave young wolf could see that this human was not fully grown, he figured maybe he'd

better get a better meal at this house, so he ran as fast as his paws could carry him to the house the human told him about... inside he found an old human lying in bed, and although the meat was a little tough, as the

human was older than he thought, he had a good meal and decided to sleep it off in the house for awhile. He had not been asleep long though, when he was woken by a knocking at the door. The human in red had followed

him to the house! Suspecting a human trap, the brave young wolf put on the old humans clothes and jumped into the bed, so that he could pretend to be human and escape from this terrible trap! Well now, this human

dressed in red came into the house, and pretended to believe the brave wolf was really a human, and began to talk to him. But then the human started asking strange questions of the wolf, because the human knew that it

was not a human at all! The brave young wolf decided to try and escape, for it was only a young human, and not very strong, so the brave young wolf said he would eat the human if they did not let him escape! As he said

this however, the human in red shouted out at him: 'Aha! You are a wolf!' and as the human shouted this another bigger human ran into the room from outside! This bigger human was much stronger and was
carrying an axe, and the poor young wolf died in this terrible trap made for him by the humans.
And do you know what the moral of this story is?
It's 'Never trust humans' of course! My dear old mammy told me that story when I was a pup, and I'm still alive and well to tell it to you today!
Pretty good story huh?

steps.player: Um... yeah. It was great. Really.

steps.npc: ...I don't know why you talked to me if you don't want anything then...

Ah, hello there! I'm just pondering on the wonders of geography.

historical-dialogue-south-of-fortis-colo.npc: Most certainly. Perhaps you could dig around near the mouth of that nearby cave and elucidate its nature for me.

Is there any chance you could dig near the mouth of that cave for me? Let me know if you find anything.

historical-dialogue-south-of-ralos-rise-.player: What should I do with the bandits?

historical-dialogue-south-of-ralos-rise-.npc: I have no qualms with you doing what you must on that front.

steps.npc: What, you haven't heard of Ali M? Possibly the greatest salesman of the Kharidian empire if not all Gielinor?

steps.text: If the player hasn't completed The Feud:

steps.player: I can't say that I have, but he must be the ambitious type to try and set up his own airline.

steps.npc: You know something, I reckon that he's trying to take on those gnomes at their own game and I'd bet good money that he'll probably win.

steps.player: Hah? I think you've gone and lost me now.

steps.npc: You know those small little guys, not the dwarves now mind.

steps.player: Ya... gnomes, I'm with you that far.

steps.npc: Well they have already established an Airline, Gnome Air...
Anyway I think that Ali M's setup here will prove really successful and maybe once we're properly established we could try compete with those gnomes.

steps.text: other
If the player has completed The Feud:

steps.player: Ah yes I remember him now, I went on a wild goose chase looking for his nephew.

steps.npc: Ha! No doubt old Ali M instigated the whole thing.

steps.player: I had a bit of fun though, The whole job was quite diverting.

steps.npc: There's never a dull moment around that man, he's always looking for a way to make a quick coin or two.

steps.text: other

options.text: Tell me about this magic carpet fleet.

steps.player: Tell me about this Magic Carpet fleet.

steps.npc: The latest idea from the great Ali Morrisane. Desert travel will never be the same again.
The carpet or the whole enterprise?

options.text: Tell me about how the carpet works.

steps.player: Tell me about how the carpet works.

steps.npc: I'm not really too sure, it's just an enchanted rug really, made out of special Ugthanki hair. It flies to whatever destination its owner commands.
Do you think I'm mad? Do you think that Ali Morrisane would throw his magic carpet monopoly away?

steps.player: Well perhaps if I offered the right price?

steps.npc: Not a hope. Could you imagine the mess there'd be if people were constantly zooming through Al Kharid and Pollnivneach? It would be chaos. This way, we can keep the carpet traffic outside towns and other busy places.

steps.player: I suppose getting stuck in a carpet jam could get a bit tiresome.

steps.npc: Just think of the friction burns you would get if you were in a carpet crash.

steps.text: other

options.text: Tell me about the enterprise then.

steps.player: Tell me about the enterprise then.

steps.npc: It's quite simple really, Ali Morrisane has hired myself and a few others to set up carpet stations at some of the desert's more populated places and run flights between the stations.

steps.player: So why has he limited the service to just the desert?

steps.npc: I don't think Ali is prepared to take on Gnome Air just yet, their gliders are much faster than our carpets, besides that I think we are in the short haul business, something that would only work in harsh conditions like
the desert.

I suppose because people would just walk. Getting lost isn't too much of a problem generally, but it's a different matter when you're in the middle of the Kharidian desert with a dry waterskin and no idea
which direction to go in.

steps.player: You're right I guess. How's the business going then?

steps.npc: Not too bad, the hubs are generally quite busy. But the stations in Uzer and the Bedabin camp could do with a bit more traffic.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: I'll try to help you as much as I can.

steps.text: At the Shantay Pass:

steps.npc: Well this is a good position for desert traffic. Shantay seems to have a nice little money spinner setup, but I reckon, this could turn out even better.

steps.text: other
At Uzer:

steps.npc: You mightn't realise it, but this is quite a busy station.

steps.player: Who would want to come here?

steps.npc: Well you for one, and besides that we get quite a few archaeologists from the dig site passing through to examine the golem.

steps.text: other
At the Bedabin Camp:

steps.npc: Well besides the obvious - looking after this station, I'm trying to figure out how these Tentis manage to cultivate such delicious pineapples.

steps.text: other
At the north Pollnivneach station:

steps.npc: Well Pollnivneach is the ideal location for setting up a carpet station.
You see it's located halfway between Al Kharid, and the Menaphite cities and close enough to Nardah too, so we get more than enough traffic to keep the business running.

steps.text: other
At the south Pollnivneach station:

steps.npc: I work here renting out magic carpets. I'm from Pollnivneach so it is a handy job, I don't have to commute too far to work every day.
You see it's located halfway between Al Kharid, and the Menaphite cities and close enough to Nardah too, so we get more than enough traffic to keep the business running.

steps.player: So I suppose you're called Ali then.

steps.npc: Not the most remarkable of names, not that it matters, you see everyone in town knows me as Flash.
No.

steps.text: other
At Nardah:

steps.npc: Well I'd preferred to have been running one of the carpet stations at a hub such as Pollnivneach. I was a bit slow off the mark to get that gig though. Still business in Nardah isn't bad for a terminal. At least
people come here for the bank and to see the herbalist.

steps.text: other
At Sophanem:

steps.npc: I look after the carpet station here. The place is a bit dead though. Ha! I'm just too much.
You know, Sophanem, city of the dead and all that?
Aw come on, the joke wasn't that bad.

steps.text: other
At Menaphos:

steps.npc: Until recently I was looking after one of the busiest carpet stations. But that all changed since Menaphos closed its gates.
Right now I have to fill my day trying to come up with reasons why Ali M should keep this place open.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: Ahoy there, sailor, and welcome to the Storm Tempor!

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: Welcome? This place doesn't look very welcoming to me.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: What do you mean? We've got the fresh sea breeze, the spray of the ocean water, a supply of the finest rum around, and one of the fiercest storms in Gielinor to contend with.
What's not to love?

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: Yeah, it's contending with that storm that worries me.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: Aye, it's true that the storm's bested many a sailor around these parts. Still, that's what makes things so exciting! We Barracudas live for the rush, and we trust that our skills will save us from a trip to the locker.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: But why? Could you not just take the safer route around the storm?

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: Well, you see, there's value in sailors with skills like ours. Most common folk would think like you and avoid the storm, but that takes time, and as them merchants say, 'time is money.'
But that's where we come in! Those merchant folk sail up to the south end of the storm, drop off their shipments to one of our boats down there and we make sure it gets up to the Pandemonium!

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: I see. That does make sense, but what's in it for you guys?

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: Why, the thrill of the sport! Sailing isn't just about going places, it's about mastery of the boat, the pull of the sails, the feeling of the helm in your hand and the taste of rum in your mouth!

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: Sailing as a sport? How does that work? What are the rules?

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: Fancy getting involved, do you? Well, we Barracudas have trials set up all across the sea where you can test your mettle against the clock. I'm in charge of this here trial, the Tempor Tantrum.
The objective of this trial is to collect rum shipments and bring them here. To do so, work your way around Tempoross Cove, towards our boat to the south.
While you're out there, keep an eye out for any lost supplies. You'll need to collect all of them to complete the trial.
Sailing over rapids will give you a burst of speed! Try to go over as many as you can. The more rapids you go through in quick succession, the faster you'll go!
The storm isn't going to make it easy for you. Those storm clouds are a nasty piece of work and they'll slow your boat down if they hit you.
Keep a close eye on them. If they are growing in size, that means they are about to strike. However, don't let your guard down once they do, as they always strike twice!
As you make your way around, don't forget your objective. You need to keep picking up lost supplies on route to our southern boat.
Once you reach the boat, collect a shipment of rum from it and then make your way back here.
Make sure you come back the opposite side of Tempoross Cove to the way you went, otherwise you're going to end up missing some lost supplies.
If you can deliver all the rum shipments and collect all the lost supplies in the time given, you'll be awarded a Barracuda rank!
Each trial has three ranks: Swordfish, Shark or Marlin. Each rank is harder than the last.
For this trial, you'll be asked to fetch additional rum shipments and collect even more lost supplies as the rank increases.
You can't attempt the next rank until you beat the one before it. You can also try unranked if you'd like to warm up beforehand.

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.player: I see. Do you have any tips or tricks for me?

first-talk-after-completing-pandemonium.npc: Sure do, sailor!
First up, you're going to need a boat with at least an oak mast built in order to withstand the storm. Your boat's as good as a goner without that.
Second, your boat will also need to have at least an iron helm to withstand the rapids, but provided you can withstand them, they'll provide a burst of speed to your boat.
Third, avoid them lightning clouds! Even with a strong mast they'll still slow you down.
Fourth, keep your sails trimmed to gain even more speed. This aint no shipwreck salvaging. Go fast or go home!
Finally, watch out for those rocks. Hitting them will kill all of your boats momentum immediately.

options.text: Who are you, and what is this place?

steps.player: Who are you, and what is this place?

steps.npc: Well, well, looks like someone is fresh off the boat and no mistake!
A little while ago we had some real problem shipping 'rum' in the island. The Braindeath crew said it had something to do with zombies and the like.
All the pirates on the island got together and decided to make our own still, but of course things got a little out of hand, and now we have two.

steps.player: So with two stills you have plenty of 'rum' right?

steps.npc: Well we would do, if that scurvy, whelk-eating foppish dog wouldn't keep trying to burn our still to the ground!
Neither of us can really corner the 'rum' market at the moment, but we are giving it our best shot.
The code of the island says that we can't attack each other, but after consulting with our fearsome pirate lawyers, we have discovered that destroying each other's property is fine.
Hence, that sniveling, hat-wearing cur keeps trying to burn down my still.
Of course he claims I started this whole thing, but who would trust him anyway?
Yes, probably. I have a bunch of jobs that need doing, if you feel up to it.
What would you like to know about?

steps.player: How do I help you brew 'Rum'?

steps.npc: Well the stills we have set up are based on the ones on Braindeath island... well roughly at any rate.
All you have to do is help put the ingredients into the hoppers and keep the boilers burning.
If you add enough ingredients to the hoppers then you have the ability to pick up a single bottle of rum when it brews.

So, if ye add 5 buckets of water to the hoppers, then ye get access to one bottle. If you add 3 bowls of coloured water you get access to one bottle, and if you add one of anything else you get access to one bottle.
This is cumulative, meaning that if you add (for example) 10 buckets of water, 3 sweetgrubs and 6 bowls of coloured water, then you have a chance to collect 7 bottles of rum for the team.
The boilers are easy as pie to sort out. You just put some logs in, light them with a tinderbox, and then keep putting logs in until they are good and hot.
Three logs should do it, but it's best to keep heaping them in just in case.
The ingredients are; Bitternuts, Scrapey Tree Bark, Sweetgrubs, Buckets of Water and some Coloured Water.
There are plenty of Bitternut trees inside this walled off area. The problem is that the trees are too tricky for a human to climb.
You will need to catch a monkey and send it up the tree to get the nut for you.

steps.player: Send it up the tree? How does that work?

steps.npc: Well, if you were a monkey, and some random person grabbed you, dumped some dye in your fur and shoved you up a tree, you would hurl the closest heavy object at them too.
Yes, you'll need to get a bowl of coloured water and pour it on the monkey. Otherwise you won't be able to tell which team the monkey belongs too.
Anything else?

options.text: Where can I get Scrapey Tree Bark?

steps.player: Where can I get Scrapey tree bark...and why do I get the feeling I won't like the answer?

steps.npc: Inside this walled area there are a few Scrapey trees. They are the big, ill looking ones, you can't miss them.
Basically, you cut them down and then carve the bark off with a knife.
It's pretty simple, except the sap tends so make people feel kind off ill if they get any on themselves.
Don't worry, we aren't talking deadly ill or anything.
It's more like you'll feel quite dizzy and weak for a bit.
Anything else?
Well, lacking any sluglings in the area, we add these little grubs called Sweetgrubs. If you ignore the gag- inducing aftertaste, they are quite sweet.

steps.player: How... how can you drink this stuff?

steps.npc: Quite easily!
Pirates are renowned as being tough for a reason.

steps.player: So where do I get these grubs from anyway?

steps.npc: Well, there are a few sweetgrub mounds inside there. We have a handful of rat meat that you can use on the mounds to draw the grubs to the surface.
Mind your fingers though, they are voracious little things.

steps.player: And here was me thinking that nothing could be more disgusting than Braindeath 'Rum'.

steps.speaker: Captian Braindeath
steps.text: Arr, that's where ye'd be wrong [lad/lass], 'cos new, improved Braindeath 'Rum' Classic is now 200% more disgustin' than any leadin' competitor!

steps.speaker: Captian Braindeath
steps.text: Legal disclaimer; the dangerous amount of disgustin' in new Braindeath 'Rum' Classic be too much for pregnant women, donkeys and anyone with more than seven letters in their last name.

steps.npc: What was what?

options.text: Where can I get buckets of water?

steps.player: Wait, no, that question makes me sound like I haven't a clue what I'm doing.

steps.player: What sort of coloured water are we talking about here?

steps.npc: Well, the other still has an area of waste ground with a flower growing on it. If you go and grab one of the flowers and jam it in the kettle, the water will boil out the colour.
We use the colour to keep our rum easily identifiable.

steps.player: So I just empty the kettle into the hopper, right?

steps.npc: No, no, you'll need to take an empty bowl and fill it from the kettle.
That way you can use the stuff on a monkey if you need to.

steps.player: Use it on a monkey...of course.

steps.npc: Anything else?

steps.player: How do I repair the still?

steps.npc: Well, assuming those scurvy dogs have managed to set any of it on fire, then you'll need to tip a bucket of water on it before you can repair it.
Then, it all comes down to what part of it was damaged.
Well, assuming that they are not on fire, all you need to do is use the heavy lumber patches. They are big enough to cover most holes.
No, just shove it into place and whack it until it lines up.
Anything else?

options.text: How do I repair Pipes and the pump?

steps.player: How do I repair pipes and the pump?

steps.npc: Well, if you use a pipe section on the damaged part you should be able to replace it easily.
No, likely you'll just need to whack the old one out and slot the new one in with your hands.
Anything else?
Well, we have these handy bridge sections you can use to repair the bridges.
The main problem is, while a still will keep working if a bit of it is only damaged, the bridges are completely out of commission if they are even slightly damaged.

steps.player: Is that going to be a problem? I mean, I can jump across I think.

steps.npc: Don't try that! Our lawyers tell us we aren't covered for injuries sustained while jumping over burned bridges.
Seriously, just keep off the bridges until they are fixed.
Anything else?

options.text: How do I get repair items

steps.player: Where do I get all this stuff anyway?

steps.npc: We have a load of items already on a table inside the still. You can also make new ones if you grab some logs.
We have a work table set up in the still. If you use the logs in it you can craft up a handy replacement for part of the still.
Don't worry about them fitting, the things are held together by nails, replacement parts and soot by now.
Anything else?

The wood around here is really dry and flammable, so take one of the torches, light it up, and then go and attack the enemy still with it.
Most of their still is soaked in 'alcohol' and made from tinder dry wood.
Essentially, if it isn't ours, try using a torch on it and see what happens.

steps.npc: Certainly. It was after all, my creation, and mine alone. If anyone should know how to make it, it should be me!
Ok, essentially this potion is a mixture of a cure poison, cure disease and restore stats all rolled into one! Very handy for the adventurers with an eye on conserving inventory space.

steps.player: Ok, I'm sold... How do you make it?

steps.npc: Well, it's very easy really. You take a standard super stat restore potion. Add some ground unicorn horn. Then, add some snake weed from the island of Karamja. Finally, add some nail beast nails. You can
only get these from the area of Morytania, specifically, if you go deep in the Mort Myre swamp.

steps.player: How do you mean, deep into the Mort Myre swamp?

steps.npc: Well, most adventurers avoid the deep Mort Myre swamp, whereas the Paterdomus trek and the Burgh de Rott trek take you through the most interesting areas. These area's often allow the quickest, but potentially
more dangerous routes through Mort Myre. This is where you're likely to encounter a Nail beast.

They can be pretty dangerous. They'll defend for a long time, then attack suddenly and seemingly without warning, landing three viscious attacks at once. This can be pretty lethal. However, the nail beasts themselves
are curiously wounded from the Sanfew Serum itself...very bizzare, that a potion made from their claws should have such a pronounced effect on them.

standard.npc: Adventurer, if you're looking to head back in there, I'd suggest you reconsider.

I won't stop you, but if it all goes wrong, don't expect me to come and save you either.

standard.npc: Well... I suppose we don't really have any magical capabilities. That's more an Arceuus thing. Though of course, they're mostly pacifists. Apparently they didn't even properly fight in the War of the Five Houses.

Lady Piscarilius has little interest in that sort of thing. Lord Shayzien wants to establish a Shayzien Navy instead, but there's a lot of pushback from the rest of the kingdom.
They worry about Shayzien having too much power. It does mean we'll have big problems against any enemy navy, but on their heads be it I suppose.
Anyway, apart from those minor issues, the Shayzien Army has absolutely no weaknesses!

Can I recommend that you purchase a full waterskin and a knife! These items will no doubt save your life. A waterskin will keep water from evaporating in the desert.

And a keen woodsman with a knife can extract the juice from a cactus. Before you go into the desert, it's advisable to wear desert clothes. It's very hot in the desert and you'll surely cook if you wear armour.

To keep the pass bandit free, we charge a small toll of five gold pieces. You can buy a desert pass from me, just ask me to open the shop. You can also use our free banking services by clicking on the chest.

Great, I have just the thing for the desert adventurer. I sell desert clothes which will keep you cool in the heat of the desert. I also sell waterskins so that you won't die in the desert.

standard.npc: Hello there...thanks for helping out Trufitus commune with the gods Bwana. We've been able to return to the village thanks to your help.

steps.npc: I's not doing a great deal now Bwana, as I'm no spring chicken. I do my fair share around the village bwana, though, I could tell you a thing or two about the jungle slashing.

options.text: Ok, tell me about jungle slashing!

steps.player: Ok, tell me about jungle slashing!

steps.npc: Ok Bwana, I will! To begin with you'll need a machete in order to hack your way through the jungle. There are some better gem edged weapons which you may be able to purchase from Gabooty.
Safta Doc makes them for him. You should be aware that hacking away at the jungle is not without its dangers though Bwana. Many times you may find some scary creatures lurking inside.
Ok, to start with there are spiders! These are pretty tough but if you defeat it, you can get a good meal from it, if you know how to cook it that is. My wife cooks them to a turn - Mmmm, delicious.

Yes Bwana, of course. Then there are snakes...these are dangerous because they're poisonous - so be prepared! However, they're not without their uses. A bush snake is large enough to have a useful hide.
Once the hide is tanned you get a snakeskin and you're able to make things from it, the same way that mainlanders use normal leather! However, it's actually still quite small.
You may need several skins in order to make something useful.

Then there are giant mosquitoes bwana, they're fast and agile. You'll need to be quick if you're to hit them at all! However, it certainly does train your reactions. They're not very tough, just difficult to hit.
I also believe that their proboscis is useful in someway, I believe Timfraku's sons sometimes use them for hunting.
Yes Bwana, much much more! What next...Oh yes, the tribesmen...you've probably seen them scouting around the village, sometimes sneaking inside the enclosure to steal our chickens!
They sometimes hide in the jungle bushes waiting for an opportunity to strike when we least expect it! Take care Bwana, these treacherous jungle natives use poison on their spears!

steps.player: Right Ok, good advice... 'poison on spears....' Anything else I should know about?

steps.npc: Yes Bwana... and this is serious... The jungle is very ancient and many unspeakable acts have been witnessed on these lands. Bizarre supernatural curses were placed on criminals and then they were buried alive!
These strange creatures have the curse of the Broodoo on them! They'll rise from their grave with their heads in their chests and move like crazy spirits of the afterlife.
If they're disturbed they will attack anything in the area with their magical abilities! They suffer little from being attacked as they seem to be protected by some form of defence.

However... it is said that the means of their death provides the clue to their destruction. So far three distinct Broodoo have been identified. The Broodoo with a green hued skin is said to have died from poison.
There is a broodoo of yellow hue and a pale skinned broodoo, but little is known of these two!

steps.player: Erk! Well that sounds pretty scary!

steps.npc: Yes Bwana...
Wait Bwana, there's more!

Some of the local villagers have found strange plants which grow here-abouts. If you cut away at the jungle and find one, it's considered a blessing, though the useful part of the plant is usually buried underground.
And also, you may find an uncommon rock type which is impregnated with mineral wealth! Well that concludes all the help I can give you regarding the jungle in Tai Bwo Wannai!

steps.player: I have to say, that's quite a lot of information...thanks very much!

steps.npc: You're more than welcome bwana!

options.text: Is there anything interesting to do here?

steps.player: Is there anything interesting to do around here?

steps.npc: Bwana, if anyone else asks me that question today, I'll explode! Go and ask someone else!
Not that I'm aware of, just sit back and enjoy the sunshine bwana!
Sorry Bwana, I'm already busy, why not go and talk to Murcaily! He's around the village somewhere.
Well, I think that there's some work to be done...perhaps Murcaily can help you. He usually tends to the hardwood grove to the east of Trufitus's hut.
It's just village life as normal around here Bwana, always something interesting to find to occupy your time if you look hard enough.

standard.npc: Why howdy there, sailor! Welcome to this here fine shipyard. Anything I can help ya with?

options.text: Can you tell me more about this place?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about this place?

steps.npc: Why, this is the shipyard, of course! I'd say it's the finest one in all of Gielinor!

steps.player: How many others even are there in Gielinor?

steps.npc: Ha! You're a funny one, sailor! Anyhoo, this here is the place where ya can modify your boat to your heart's content! Ya can do that in two ways.
Once you're on board, you'll find that you've got different spots on your boat for different facilities! If ya can't find what you're looking for, be sure to check the other spots as well!

steps.player: But what if I don't have the right skillsets?

steps.npc: Well now, I reckon we might be able to help ya out there... for a price of course!
Now, the other way ya can modify your boat is by upgrading the core components of it. If ya fancy doing that, you'll wanna use this here schematics board!
Much like with building facilities, ya can use the board to pick the part of your boat ya wanna upgrade!

Now, it's important ya keep in mind that these upgrades are the big ones! They're too much to handle solo, so we'll wrangle up some of the workers to lend ya a hand. They'll also supply the tools for ya!

steps.player: That's very kind of them. What's the catch?

steps.npc: Well, while they're happy to give ya a helping hand, they are going to expect ya to take the lead.

steps.player: And if I'm not skilled enough to take the lead?

steps.npc: Well, we might be able to help ya out there... for a price of course!
Anyhoo, I think that just about covers the shipyard. Anything else I can do for ya?

steps.text: other

options.text: What do you have for sale?

steps.player: What do you have for sale?

steps.npc: I've got a few basic shipbuilding supplies that ya might find handy. Take a look, sailor!

options.text: Could you help me repair my boat?

steps.text: If the boat is not damaged:

steps.npc: Looks like ya boat's already all fine and dandy, sailor.

steps.player: Could you help me repair my boat?

steps.npc: Sure thing, sailor. That'll cost ya [..] coins.

steps.prompt: Have your boat repaired for [..] coins?

steps.npc: Alrighty! Let's call some of the workers over...

steps.text: Some workers make repairs to your boat.

steps.npc: That's all done for ya, sailor.
Alrighty! Let's call some of the workers over...

steps.text: Some workers make repairs to your boat.

steps.npc: That's all done for ya, sailor.
Fair enough, sailor.

options.text: Where can I get materials for my boat?

steps.player: Where can I get materials for my boat?

steps.npc: Well, ain't that the question on everyone's mind, sailor? But to answer, it depends on what materials you'll be wanting.
Ya look like a smart enough sailor to know where to find logs and bars. Nails, ya make from taking a metal bar to an anvil.
For planks, you'll need to take matching logs to a sawmill. I know there's a few around, but I like to get mine from the one north east of Varrock.
If ya need standard hull parts, you'll wanna take five planks to a workbench. We've got one right here, but any good shipwright's gonna have one.
If it's standard keel parts ya need, you'll wanna take five metal bars to any old anvil.
For the larger hull parts or keel parts, don't overthink it. Just grab five of the standard parts and put them together in the same way!
Obviously, some raw materials are rarer than others, and some of them ya might need to go sail that great blue marble to get.
Finally, if it helps ya at all, I've got some basic supplies for sale.

steps.text: other

options.text: I might need help building things on my boat.

steps.player: I might need help building things on my boat.

steps.npc: Well, ya wouldn't be the first, sailor! I reckon ya probably won't be the the last either. Don't worry though, we can help ya out... for a price of course!

steps.player: And what sort of price should I expect?

steps.npc: Well, that there depends on how hard the job is. The more skills needed, the more money you're gonna need to part with.

steps.player: So you're telling me you won't be able to spare your best shipwrights?

steps.npc: Yeah I'd say that's a good way of putting it. In general, we'll only be able to help ya with things that use less fancy materials. Mithril and mahogany are gonna be the limit.
We're also only gonna be able to help ya with the more standard parts and facilities, so hulls, sails, helms, keels, cannons, salvaging hooks and cargo holds.

steps.player: I see. So once things start to get complicated, I'm going to have to do it myself?

steps.npc: Afraid so, sailor. Oh, and don't forget that even when we're helping ya out, we're still gonna need ya to supply the materials.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: See ya later, sailor.

overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.speaker: Shipyard Worker (A)
overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.text: They say a good way of remembering it is that a ship can have boats on it, but a boat can't have ships on it.

overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.speaker: Shipyard Worker (B)
overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.text: But say you have a ship with lifeboats on it, and that ship starts to sink. If all the lifeboats are deployed, it no longer has any boats on it, so is it no longer a ship?

overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.speaker: Shipyard Worker (B)
overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.text: I suppose if it's sinking it probably no longer matters. Still, at the moment it does sink, you could argue that it very briefly stops being a ship and starts being a submarine.

overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.speaker: Shipyard Worker (A)
overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.text: It's not just boats and ships that have this problem. You also have orcas.

overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.speaker: Shipyard Worker (B)
overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.text: More commonly known as the killer whale!

overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.speaker: Shipyard Worker (A)
overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.text: Except by many definitions, they're not really whales at all.

overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.speaker: Shipyard Worker (B)
overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.text: What is it with things at sea being named so poorly?

overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.speaker: Shipyard Worker (A)
overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.text: To be honest, it's not much better on land. Think about trees. You've got oak trees, maple trees, and then you just have... trees.

overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.speaker: Shipyard Worker (B)
overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.text: 'What's your boat made of?' 'Wood.' 'So like oak or...?' 'No, just wood.'

steps.npc: From the moment I was born, all I ever knew was the Nightmare. Every night she would feast upon us, filling our minds with horrors beyond comprehension.
By day, our warriors would enter her lair in the caves beneath the island. We could not hope to defeat her, we knew that, but our survival was dependent on ensuring she didn't grow too strong.
Here's the thing though. Even now, we know little about her. Before she claimed them, my parents would sometimes tell me a story of her origin.
They told me of a group of shamans who performed an unknown ritual in the hope of gaining great power. The ritual went wrong, though, and instead, they unleashed the Nightmare on this world.
I'm not sure to be honest. I suppose it doesn't matter though. We'll likely never know her true origin. But as long as we can defeat her, we don't need to.
Exactly. Thanks to the Nightmare, the caves beneath our home are mostly unexplored. There's all sorts of things down there, provided you're brave enough to enter.
I found the totems deep within the caves. Someone far smarter than you or I had worked out how to make them. But they perished before they could use them against her.
I managed to recover them, and with them, we finally drove her off the island.
Yes. And thanks to the Sleeper Plague, she's far stronger than ever before.

steps.player: Do you know where the Sleeper Plague came from?

steps.npc: No. It was here long before the Nightmare apparently. It resurfaced shortly before she arrived. Probably the work of the vampyres.
Is there anything else you need?

steps.text: other

steps.npc: The name's Shura. I come from an island called Ashihama, in the Pincers.
It's a group of islands within the Wushanko Isles, a large archipelago to the far east. Over here I think the area is more commonly known as the Eastern Lands.
That's right. We rarely come this far to the west, the climate is too cold for our tastes. Although while the Nightmare lives, the climate is the least of my worries.
Back home on the other hand, our numbers equal the humans. Sirens live on pretty much every island in the archipelago.

steps.player: So why were you the only one to come here?

steps.npc: We took up arms against the Nightmare because we had to, not because we wanted to. We are a peaceful race, and most were all too eager to lay down their weapons once the Nightmare was gone.
My kind believe in something called Mo Kal. It means that anything bad that could happen, will happen. The others may have forgotten this, but I have not.
The Nightmare may have left my home, but I won't rest until I know for sure that she can never return.
Is there anything else you need?
