standard-dialogue-when-trying-to-interac.npc: Hey! Don't just go poking her without knowing what you're up against. Come talk to me first.

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.player: What's going on here?

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.npc: Nothing good. This dungeon is tainted and has become the new home of the Nightmare.

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.player: The Nightmare?

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.npc: A being of pure darkness. No living creature is safe from her hunger. She feasts upon her victims while they sleep, draining their energy without even needing to touch them.
Those that she feeds upon experience horrifying nightmares, unlike anything you could possibly imagine. Eventually, they become too weak to even wake. Death claims them soon after.

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.player: Nightmares? Hence the name?

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.npc: Indeed. Our kind are not always the most creative.

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.player: So how did she end up here?

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.npc: For generations, she terrorised the island of Ashihama, my home. I lost a lot of good friends to her. Sometimes, I even thought I would lose myself. For some, the nightmares become too much to bear.
Some of us refused to give in though. Everything has a weakness, including the Nightmare, and eventually we found it. We drove her off the island, but she managed to endure.

The people here are ill, suffering from a deep sleep from which few wake. They call it the Sleeper Plague. The illness made these people easy prey for the Nightmare, so she made this place her new home.

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.player: And you followed her here?

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.npc: While she still exists, my home will never be truly safe. Thanks to the Sleeper Plague, her power has grown faster than it ever did on Ashihama. If she is allowed to grow too strong, there won't be any way to stop her.
I've managed to contain her within this section of the dungeon. She has no desire to leave for the moment. She has no need to, after all.
But make no mistake, I won't be able to stop her if she decides to move on.

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.player: She doesn't look too dangerous at the moment.

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.npc: Looks can be deceiving. The battle with the Nightmare is a mental one, not a physical one. If you try to take her on, she will pull you into her dream - one where she makes the rules.

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.player: But if it's a dream, how can it be dangerous?

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.npc: It's her dream, not yours. Dying in her dream will destroy your mind, killing you in this world as well.

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.player: Sounds lovely. So how can we stop her?

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.npc: If you're willing to help, enter her dream and fight to keep her at bay. Our only hope is to prevent her from growing too strong.
You can go in alone, but I wouldn't recommend it. The more support you have, the better your chances.

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.player: How do I keep her at bay?

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.npc: There are four totems in the area that can be used to harm her. First, you'll need to take down her shield for the totems to have an effect. Once her shield is down, use your energy to charge up the totems.
She won't sit about while you do this though, so you'll need to take care if you want to survive.

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.player: And what's in it for me if I do survive?

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.npc: You mean apart from saving the world? She's claimed many victims over the years. I'm sure she's claimed many items as well. Maybe some of them will be of value to you.

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.player: Works for me. I'd better get started then.

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.npc: Good luck. Return to me if you need more information.

steps.text: If the player has a trowel, a rock pick and a specimen brush in their inventory and also have leather boots and leather gloves equipped:

steps.npc: I see you have your equipment - well done.

To really give us a hand, you could clean some finds for us. They're mostly done - just some fine work to finish off. Take a find from the pile that the workmen are bringing in, then there are spare tables over there
to clean them on. If you find anything interesting, let us know and we'll see if it's good enough to go on display.
Oh? Let's take a look...

steps.text: If the player has a Clean necklace in their inventory:

steps.npc: Interesting...yes...yes...hmmm.... It looks like it's enchanted.

Oh, I think it's just a benign teleportation spell. I tinker in magic when I'm not doing archaeology. I can teach you how to make more necklaces like this. Amazing that they had this kind of knowledge back then.

steps.player: That would be good. Where is the teleport to?

steps.npc: Hmm...all the indications are that it's somewhere to the east of us, but I'm not sure how far. Perhaps it was a teleport back to Saranthium. Let me just take a closer look.

steps.text: The archaeologist takes the necklace and turns it over in his hands, studying it closely.

The archaeologist shows you the techniques for this particular spell, which requires five fire runes arranged around one cosmic rune - and level 49 Magic - then casting the spell on a crafted ruby necklace of your
own.  You can make enchanted ruby necklaces.

steps.player: So I just make a ruby necklace and use five fire runes and one cosmic rune to enchant it.

steps.npc: Yes, indeed. Well done, youngster, thanks for helping us.

steps.npc: What have we here?

Oh! This is very interesting...and confusing at the same time. This coin means that the city that we're excavating on the Digsite - Saranthium - was actually inhabited much, much earlier by followers of Zamorak,
at which time, the city was known as Senntisten.

This is a most remarkable discovery, as we have other evidence indicating that Zarosian followers were resident before the Saradominists took over, but it also seems that Zamorakian forces used it during a battle of some
sort. Still, it allows us to roughly date when the city changed from following Zaros and Zamorak to following Saradomin. Put it in display case 44.

options.text: Can you explain the White Knight honour system again?

steps.npc: Sadly we are not as rich as we once were, and there are many White Knights who foolishly lose their combat equipment.

We do not think it fair to make a profit from our brethren, so we will sell you equipment at cost, and rebuy it at the same cost, but we will only sell equipment to those we consider responsible enough to

Well, there are four different shields of Falador, which match up with the four levels of difficulty. Each has the same rewards as the previous level and some additional benefits too... which tier of rewards would you like to
know more about?

steps.player: Tell me more about the Easy rewards please!

steps.player: Tell me more about the Medium rewards please!

and can access a shortcut within the Motherlode Mine

steps.player: Tell me more about the Hard rewards please!

steps.npc: In addition to the easy and medium benefits, the shield will restore all of your prayer points once per day, you can access a bank deposit box at the crafting guild and a shortcut to the Heroes' Guild fountain. The Giant

using-knight-s-notes-on-him-if-the-notes.player: Sir Tiffy! I got this scroll from a knight near Trollheim. He said I should deliver it to you urgently.

using-knight-s-notes-on-him-if-the-notes.npc: What ho, old [boy/gal/bean]. Well, hand it over and let's have a look, shall we?
Now, let's see what is so urgent. Hmmm...

Well, you've been a great help, so I'll tell you a bit about this, shall I? Several weeks ago, a dwarven explorer, named Nestor Peregrine, discovered the entrance to an ancient cave complex while exploring the

troll mountains. On his return to Keldagrim, he celebrated in a tavern where we have an informant. The dwarf spoke of a great treasure, apparently mentioned in dwarven legend, and of creatures of great

evil, fighting those of great good. I sent Sir Gerry and a small command of knights to investigate the dwarf's stories several months ago and it appears that he has found the resting place of that incredible weapon: the
Godsword.

During the great God Wars, the evil usurper Zamorak gathered many ancient relics and armies to his cause. There were none powerful enough to stand alone before his might, so our glorious Lord Saradomin

gathered a triumverate of gods to stem the tide of evil. They came together and, using great magics, they created the Godsword; a weapon so mighty that it could slay even a god. It was forged in the flames of a

volcano and tempered by the tears of the icyene. The mightiest warriors to stand before the army of evil were the aviansie: birdmen followers of Armadyl. They were a proud and mighty warrior race. To them fell the task of

delivering the Godsword to the holy armies that gathered to oppose Zamorak's evil. Unfortunately, they were attacked by an army of demons before they could reach the safety of the main army. It was a fiendish

stroke by the forces of darkness. At the same time as they attacked the aviansie, they also mounted a huge attack on the main armies that opposed them. Realising their intent, several of the gods that were allied against

Zamorak sent forces to aid the besieged aviansie, who had retreated into a temple in the mountains. The forces of Saradomin and Bandos arrived in the midst of a pitched battle for the Godsword, and it was during this

battle that the sword was sundered. Shortly thereafter, the evil one cast a spell of such devastation that it flattened the entire northern half of Gielinor, reducing it to what we now call the Wilderness. This temple must
have collapsed, sealing the combatants in.

using-knight-s-notes-on-him-if-the-notes.player: Surely, one of the groups would have gained the upper hand by now? After all, it's been thousands of years since that battle.

using-knight-s-notes-on-him-if-the-notes.npc: Apparently not. It appears that a millennia-old battle is still being fought beneath the ruins of the temple, and the prize for winning the battle is the Godsword! Hmm... Well, thank you very much, old [boy/gal/bean]. You've been a
great help. I shall pass it on to my superiors.

using-knight-s-notes-on-him-if-the-notes.player: Is that it, then? Aren't we going to do something?

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.npc: Keeping an eye on Mother.

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.player: Mother?

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.npc: Phosani, the founder of our sect and creator of this sanctuary. She is our mother, and always will be.

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.player: I see... So where is she?

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.npc: She lies in this coffin.

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.player: Oh... So she's dead?

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.npc: Dead? No. She sleeps the everlasting slumber.

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.player: Right. The coffin looks pretty secure to me. Why do you need to keep an eye on her.

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.npc: The creature down there, the one that Siren calls the Nightmare. It has been invading Mother's mind, feeding on her.
Mother is strong, but not strong enough to fight it off alone. She needs help.

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.player: Needs help does she? Maybe I could be of assistance?

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.npc: The offer is appreciated. Luckily for us though, the Nightmare is not present in Mother's mind at the moment.

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.player: Fair enough. If that changes, I'm more than willing to help.

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.npc: Be safe, traveller.

standard-dialogue-first-time-talking-to-.text: If the player does not have at least one normal Nightmare kill:

steps.npc: The offer is appreciated. I fear you do not have the abilities to take on that sort of challenge though.
The horror that has manifested itself in Mother's mind is far stronger than the one fought in the Nightmare's dream.
If you hope to have a chance, you'll want to take on the weaker form first. That Siren down there can help you.

steps.player: Fair enough. I'll be back once I have more experience.

steps.prompt: Would you like to attempt the fight anyway?

steps.npc: That would be appreciated, traveller. You can use the pool here to enter Mother's mind and take on the Nightmare within.

standard-dialogue-attempting-to-use-tele.npc: Hey! What do you think you're doing? Don't go casting that kind of spell anywhere near my tea!  Leave my tea alone you telegrabbing fiend!

standard-dialogue-after-completion-of-zo.npc: Oh, so you're back then, come to gloat have you?

standard-dialogue-after-completion-of-zo.player: Nope, I've just come to ask you a couple of questions.

options.text: How do I get rid of the undead ogres?

steps.player: How do I get rid of the undead ogres?

steps.npc: Haven't I already explained this to you once before?

Ok, similar spells have been cast before and the only way to deal with the resulting creatures is to cordon off the area and not go in there again. The undead creatures usually manifest some sort of disease so it's
best to attack them from a distance with a ranged weapon.
Normal missiles like arrows and darts do very little damage to them because they're designed to destroy internal organs. This is a waste of time with undead creatures like undead ogres.

steps.player: Yeah, clearly so what should we use?

steps.npc: From my research it looks like a flat ended arrow was designed called a 'Brutal arrow'. This does large amounts of crushing damage to the creature.
You can make them by using larger arrows, I think some Ogre hunters make them. But instead of adding an arrow tip, you hammer a large nail into the end of the shaft.

options.text: How do I get rid of the disease?

steps.player: How do I get rid of the disease?

steps.npc: Haven't I already explained this disease thing to you once before?

steps.player: Just tell me again or else I'll turn you back into an ogre!

steps.npc: No...noo...please, I'll tell you.
My research shows that two jungle based herbs can be used, one is found near river tributaries and looks like a vine, the other is found in caves and grows on the wall.
It's quite well camouflaged so it's unlikely that you'll find it.

stat-reducing-attack.speaker: Skeleton
stat-reducing-attack.text: I infect your body with rot...

stat-reducing-attack.npc: I infect your body with rot...

standard.player: Are you all right? You seem a little...incoherent.

standard.npc: Inc'hearnt? Inc'herant! You...you...with yer fancy book- lernin' words. You'd be more than inc'herant if youd seen...
(Dramatic pause)
THEM!

options.text: I'm sure I would as well.

steps.player: I'm sure I would as well.
I'm going over here to talk to non-crazy people now.

steps.npc: Yeah? Yeah? Well when THEY come floppin' into your house and eat your furniture you'll be sorry!
They! Those bloodthirsty, flesh-tearing devils! They are the reason I'm out here every day hurlin' bottles into the sea!
They are the reason I've lost everything, except the horrifying memory of what THEY look like...

steps.player: And what do THEY look like?

steps.npc: Mudskippers!
Aye, Mudskippers! Those ferocious, ravening, evil, beady-eyed terrors of the deep!
I was ambushed by them way back, see. They got the drop on me...I can't remember where, somewhere around here though.

steps.player: These would be the mudskippers, right?

steps.npc: Aye! The mudskippers! Huge they were! Ten feet of glistening, muddy flesh floppin' towards me with white foam flying from their gnashing fangs!
I fought them up and down the beach, with the tide rising and more of them leaping towards me with cutlasses drawn!

steps.player: This is fascinating, but I have to be...

steps.npc: Shut yer' word-hole and listen! I can't remember all the details, as I'm sure they must have hit me quite hard, but the last thing I remember before it all went black...
...was one of those devils rearing over me, its eyes glowin' red with the fires of hell!

steps.player: Fires of hell...right. I believe you.

steps.npc: No you don't! You think I'm crazy, like all the rest! Well, if I'm crazy, how did I get these?

steps.text: Skippy shows you what appears to be massive bite scars on his legs. You're no expert, but they look like... giant mudskipper bites!

steps.player: Giant mudskipper bites! Where did you get those?

steps.npc: I can't remember... I've been drinking to forget the horror, and all I seem to have forgotten is where it all happened...

steps.player: Hmmm...I suppose if I sober you up you may well start to recall.

steps.npc: You'll have a job. I've been drinking this for a week.

steps.player: 'Captain Braindeath's Extra Strength Rum/Drain Cleaner. Now 50% more debilitating'?

steps.npc: It's the extra sheep tranquilizers that gives it that added kick!

steps.player: Stay here and I'll be right back. Try not to move. Or go near any open flames.

before-skippy-and-the-mogres-trying-to-s.player: You know, I could shock him out of it if I could find some cold water...

after-skippy-and-the-mogres.player: How do I annoy the Mogres again?

after-skippy-and-the-mogres.npc: Go south to Mudskipper Point and lob a Fishing Explosive into the sea. You can grab them from the Slayer masters.

after-skippy-and-the-mogres.player: Thanks! So, what are you going to do now?

after-skippy-and-the-mogres.npc: Well, I was planning on continuing my hobby of wandering up and down this bit of coastline, bellowing random threats and throwing bottles.

after-skippy-and-the-mogres.player: I was planning on wandering up and down the landscape, bugging people to see if they had mindblowingly dangerous quests for me to undertake.

after-skippy-and-the-mogres-when-using-t.player: I think he's sober enough. And I don't want to use another bucket of water.

when-using-a-forlorn-boot-on-skippy.npc: Thanks! Now I have two right boots!

I used to have a hidden outpost out near the Bone Yard, somewhere to keep my stuff in an emergency. One day all I come back to is a smouldering pile of rubble.
Next thing I know, someone's snuck up behind me and has put a spear through my back.
Always carry a ring of life, friend! Never know when you'll need it.
Still, the damage was done. Everything I ever owned up in smoke, and even though the wound's fully healed, I can still feel that spear in my back to this day.
Thankfully, Ferox was kind enough to take me in, and I managed to repurpose some of my old storage magic for adventurers like you.

No [lad/lass/kid]!
See, he survived, his bones turned to bananas, as a huge storm blew up and the crew debated what to do with him.

ocean.

No [lad/lass/kid]!

Well, I'll tell ye the story, but it'll take a great deal of convincin' for me to sell you this rapier.
See, gentleman Mallard is a legend in these parts. His family had been rich, shipping all sorts of goods up and down the coast.
Then their rivals got together and had their ships sunk, one after the other, and his business partners were all either bought off or had...accidents.
With no money and only one ship left, he took to the life of a pirate, but no brigand was he.
He took only from those men that had brought about his downfall, was fair with his men, and generous with his loot.
Why, this island would have been wiped out by the shakes if he hadn't turned over his stash to buy medicine.
One day his ship was attacked by a huge sea creature that swept the decks of men with its tentacles.
The crew took to the lifeboats, and the last they saw of him the gentleman was stabbin' at the thing as it hauled the ship under the water.
A week later about ten foot of tentacle washed up on the beach, with his rapier embedded in it to the hilt.

rare-alternate-dialogue.npc: Mankind's variation frightens me.
The way they saw this universe, their modes of impression, differed so greatly from one another that to read their stories, to know their lives, is to wonder if they were not many species in one.
It was as if they had ranged across the actions of a thousand species and taken them for their own.
For nearly two thousand years they dreamed in a creative mania without antecedent.
They looked into the eyes and minds of other species and with their own intellect superseded them.
They destroyed many, coopted others, and in the space between necessity and carelessness, left some to grow as untended as any species could in the wake of their ubiquity.
They swarmed across the continents and oceans of a Gielinor they called their own, and shattered it into a billion imbricate worlds.
And they were, by the twisted jungles of their slaughterhouses, ruthless and aloof beyond measure.
The worst of us.
A superpredator.
A bringer of mass extinction.
All mountains move and all giants are mountains.
We rest upon their shoulders.
The world has grown older, senescent.
We are chimpanzee, we are gorilla, we are orangutan, and we are baboon and more.
We are, whether we like it or not, the blood legatees of humanity.
We are the children of men, but our mistakes will not be their mistakes.
We are telling a story.
We are telling a story of life, of what it means to live together in this universe, with vastly different modes of being, of seeing, of knowing.

Of sharing our own internal worlds with each other and making the universe we live in better for it. The empathy of a mind speaking to another mind, a vastly different mind, and yet each understanding each.
And if not, if the barriers seem too great, then striving to overcome them.
Sorrow in what humanity did to this world, in the horrors they unleashed, in their cataclysm of despair, in the tens of thousands of species that will never walk or swim or fly again.
Extinctions abounded in their wake, and yet look now at this sunbright land, at the joys we have brought to it, to have bound the chaotic climate to our will.
To have thought deeply of the future of this world, a sense of respect, of shared reverence for it and all who live within it.
We have strung the close sky with life.
Be proud.
And empathy, once limited only to mankind and some few species, now extends across all lands, across all time.

standard-dialogue-warhammer.speaker: Soldier
standard-dialogue-warhammer.text: I've been posted here to guard this chasm.

standard-dialogue-warhammer.speaker: Soldier
standard-dialogue-warhammer.text: Not great. There's constant bursts of hot air, demon roars and strange lights coming from inside.

standard-dialogue-warhammer.speaker: Soldier
standard-dialogue-warhammer.text: And then there's the cultists. They just climb out like it's normal to be down there. Try to talk to you like it's business as usual.

options.text: How long are you posted here?

steps.player: How long are you posted here?

steps.speaker: Soldier
steps.text: Indefinitely. We don't know what the cult is up to and we don't want to be caught unprepared.
other

steps.speaker: Soldier
steps.text: No. I signed up to to protect Kourend, even if that means standing outside of a demon nest. Besides, it's not like any demons have come out of it yet.
other

steps.speaker: Soldier
steps.text: Thanks.

standard-dialogue-scimitar.speaker: Soldier
standard-dialogue-scimitar.text: What do you want? Are you with those cultists?

standard-dialogue-scimitar.speaker: Soldier
standard-dialogue-scimitar.text: Good. I've had enough of their games.

standard-dialogue-scimitar.speaker: Soldier
standard-dialogue-scimitar.text: They start off polite, but before you know it, they're trying to get you to agree to something.

standard-dialogue-scimitar.speaker: Soldier
standard-dialogue-scimitar.text: They're not fooling me though. The next one that crosses me is going to regret it!

steps.player: About the cultists... What sort of things do they ask you to agree to?

steps.speaker: Soldier
steps.text: Usually they want you to follow them somewhere private. Some of the bolder ones try to get you to join them inside the chasm.

steps.speaker: Soldier
steps.text: If it were up to me, we'd launch a sortie right now. See how they like it if we come down on our own terms.

steps.player: Aren't you worried about the demons?

steps.speaker: Soldier
steps.text: You sound like the lieutenant.
other

steps.speaker: Soldier
steps.text: I am. If you ask me we should be out fighting lizardmen. That means we need to go on the offensive and wrap this chasm business up.

steps.player: I take it the rest of your squad aren't as keen.

steps.speaker: Soldier
steps.text: You'd be right. The lieutenant is too cautious and the rest are too timid. The way some of them speak you'd think they had demon families.
other

steps.speaker: Soldier
steps.text: If you see any cultists lurking around, let me know.

standard-dialogue-dagger.speaker: Soldier
standard-dialogue-dagger.text: I might as well be if we're going to continue this performance.

standard-dialogue-dagger.speaker: Soldier
standard-dialogue-dagger.text: There are no demons coming out of this chasm. If there were, we wouldn't last long.

options.text: You think the demons would overrun you?

steps.player: You think the demons would overrun you?

steps.speaker: Soldier
steps.text: Demons don't die the same way we do. We could hold back a few of them, but not an endless stream.

steps.player: You seem to know a lot about them.

steps.speaker: Soldier
steps.text: I do, which means I know that guarding the chasm is a pointless endeavour. Not that the lieutenant cares what I think.

steps.speaker: Soldier
steps.text: Launching an attack into the chasm would also be pointless. That leaves us with only one other option.

steps.speaker: Soldier
steps.text: No. We should talk to them. Try to reach an understanding.

steps.player: Somehow I don't think negotiating with demons will end well.

steps.speaker: Soldier
steps.text: If you have a better idea, go ahead.
other

options.text: Aren't you a bit too calm about this?

steps.player: Aren't you a bit too calm about this?

steps.speaker: Soldier
steps.text: No. If they wanted to, Yama and his demons could overrun this little squad.

steps.speaker: Soldier
steps.text: The fact they haven't means they're probably not interested in doing so. As a matter of fact, they seem quite polite.

steps.speaker: Soldier
steps.text: I didn't say that, But there's evidence to suggest that Yama and his cult can be reasoned with.

steps.speaker: Soldier
steps.text: If Lord Shayzien is interested in diffusing the threat, he should consider trying to reach an agreement with them.

steps.player: I've met Lord Shayzien. He doesn't seem like the type to compromise.

steps.speaker: Soldier
steps.text: You've met Lord Shiro Shayzien?

steps.player: Yes, I've met the leaders of all of the houses. Even King Artur Hosidius himself.

steps.speaker: Soldier
steps.text: Interesting. You're quite the worldly fellow. Perhaps King Hosidius would make a more level headed negotiator. Maybe you could talk to him?

steps.player: I imagine he's quite busy at the moment.

steps.text: other

standard.speaker: Soldier
standard.text: Urrrgggh.....

standard.speaker: Soldier

steps.player: Thank you very much! How many charges does each piece give?

steps.npc: Most of them give 3, although the left skull gives 5. Each completed tier of the Varrock achievement diary will get you one extra charge per piece and allow your sceptre to hold 4 more charges.
You can use a chisel to break a sceptre piece into fragments, then use those to charge the sceptre instead. More flexible if you ask me.

steps.npc: I died... Of course, I tried escaping, long before I'd made it to the treasure, but I was shot with arrows just as I approached the exit.

steps.npc: My name's Sorin. I'm just trying to make do I guess. The vampyres might not be a problem, but there's still no shortage of dangers around here.

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help out?

steps.player: Can you tell me about the gods of the Menaphites?

steps.npc: If you wish to know about the lesser gods, you should speak with Jex at the Temple of the Lesser Gods. I suppose I could spare a moment or two to tell you about the main four though.
Tumeken is the god of light and husband to Elidinis. He is the leading god of the Menaphite Pantheon.

steps.player: People don't seem to talk about him much. I'd have thought being the leading god would make him more popular.

steps.npc: A common saying about Tumeken is that you see him wherever you look, but never actually notice him.

steps.player: Okay... And what kind of god is he? The desert is a harsh place, so does that make him harsh as well?

steps.npc: In some ways. You humans sometimes say that 'you have to be cruel to be kind'. That seems a fitting way to describe Tumeken.

steps.player: So he's harsh, but for good reasons?

steps.npc: Indeed.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Elidinis is the goddess of fertility. The River Elid is named in her honour, for it brings life to the whole region.
There are some who even believe the river to be Elidinis herself.

steps.player: That's an interesting take. I guess being a bringer of life makes her quite popular?

steps.npc: More so than many others in the pantheon, but not as much as she once was.
Humans are fickle. Perhaps they grew bored of her?
Well if you're after the human take on things, you'd be better off asking a human.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Icthlarin is the god of the dead. He is the son of Tumeken and Elidinis, and brother to the Devourer. As this is the city of the dead, he's quite popular here.

steps.player: So are you a follower of Icthlarin?

steps.npc: Nothing of the sort. I have no interest in the gods or their followers. Instead, Icthlarin and I have an understanding.
Cats play a significant role when it comes to guarding the dead from the Devourer. As such, they are great allies to Icthlarin.
As a thank you for looking after them, Icthlarin grants me eternal life.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: I'd have thought you'd be more than familiar with her by now.

steps.player: I'm interested in hearing your take.

steps.npc: Very well. The Devourer is the goddess of destruction. As such, she is commonly considered an evil goddess, but this is an oversimplification.
Not everything that destroys is evil. Destruction is often a necessity.

steps.player: Isn't that also an oversimplification? Amascut is doing far more than just destroying. She's a murderer!

steps.npc: Is causing death enough to make one evil? Icthlarin is the god of the dead. By your argument, surely he is the most evil of them all.

steps.player: Icthlarin doesn't actually kill people though. He just looks after those that have died.

steps.npc: You clearly know little of Icthlarin and his past. Are you aware of the Mahjarrat? They once served Icthlarin, before they left him for Zamorak.
Or was it the Empty Lord they left him for... I forget.
Regardless, they are a race that have regularly associated themselves with gods considered evil. Interesting company for one such as Icthlarin to keep.

steps.player: How does that make Amascut good though?

steps.npc: I never said it did. I'm just saying that things are often not as straightforward as they seem, especially when it comes to Icthlarin and the Devourer.

before-completing-the-knight-waves.speaker: Squire
before-completing-the-knight-waves.text: That door leads to the training ground for the Knights of the Round Table.

before-completing-the-knight-waves.speaker: Squire
before-completing-the-knight-waves.text: Of course, my [lord/lady/liege]. But I must tell you the rules first. Would you like to hear them now?

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: The training ground is a melee combat area only. Merlin has cast a spell over the grounds to prevent anyone using Prayer, Ranged or Magic.

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: Upon entering the grounds, you will fight each of the Round Table Knights in turn. Each knight is more skilled than the last, but all have different attack styles that can be exploited. There are eight knights in all, and

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: each will do damage not only to your hitpoints, but also your combat stats. If you should die in the grounds, Merlin will teleport you back here. You will not lose any of your items.

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: If you feel you cannot complete the battle, you may exit the training grounds. However, if you exit or die, you will have to start over with the first knight the next time you enter.

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: If you are a great warrior and defeat Sir Lancelot, mightiest of all knights, you will receive great rewards. Two new prayers will become available to you and your respawn point will be set to Camelot, as well as 20,000

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: XP in to each of your combat stats.

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: If you do not want your respawn set to Camelot, Merlin can change it for you.

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: Would you like me to repeat any of that for you?

options.text: Tell me about the training ground

steps.player: Tell me about the training ground.

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: Only melee combat is allowed within the training grounds. Merlin will prevent the use of Prayer, Ranged and Magic.

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: These grounds are for only the best knights of the land. It is not just testing your combat ability, but your honour and your chivalry. You must face your enemy head on, honourably and bravely.

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: Be watchful of your stats, as the Knights can do damage to your combat stats as well as your hitpoints.

options.text: Tell me about dying or leaving the grounds

steps.player: Tell me about dying or leaving the grounds.

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: As these are only training grounds, we keep our knights safe. If you should die, you will be teleported back to here and all of your items will be safe.

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: However, leaving the training grounds, in anyway, will mean you will have to start from the beginning the next time you enter. These grounds do not favour cowards.

steps.player: I have to start again? What do you mean?

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: You fight each knight of the Round Table, starting with Sir Bedivere and finishing with Sir Lancelot. Leaving means you will have to begin fighting Sir Bedivere again and work your way back up.

steps.player: What if I log out during the fights?

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: If you log out during a fight, upon logging back in you will fight the knight you were fighting when you logged out.

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: King Arthur believes in rewarding his knights for their chivalry. Having proven yourself in combat against his knights, and in your services rendered to Camelot, you will be rewarded with two new prayers, and a new

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: respawn at Camelot, as well as 20,000 XP in to each of your combat stats.

steps.player: What do the new prayers do?

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: Ah, patience is a virtue in knights, my [lord/lady/liege]. Fight in the training ground and earn your reward to find out!

steps.player: Then tell me about the respawn - how will it work?

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: Ah, Merlin has offered, as a reward for your help, to let your respawn in the safety of Camelot, should you befall misfortune elsewhere in the world. Should you wish to change your respawn back to Lumbridge, simply

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: speak to Merlin.

after-completing-the-knight-waves.speaker: Squire
after-completing-the-knight-waves.text: Congratulations on succeeding in the Knight Waves, my [lord/lady/liege].

after-completing-the-knight-waves.player: Thank you. Can I go back inside?

after-completing-the-knight-waves.speaker: Squire
after-completing-the-knight-waves.text: I'm afraid not, my [lord/lady/liege]. Once you have won, you cannot re-enter.

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: Sorry, but I have lots of work to do.

standard.speaker: Squire
standard.text: What do you want?

options.text: Who are you and what are you doing?

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: I'm Vicks, squire to Sir Culler Flife. He's away on a surveillance mission to Burthorpe, so he sent me down here to do some cleaning.

options.text: You don't seem to be cleaning much.

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: Don't tell the knights, but I'm just not in the mood for it! I've served for years, and worked really hard, but they're not even thinking of making me a knight.

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: I don't know what the problem is. At my last review, I heard the examiner muttering something about my name, but I've no idea what he meant by that.
other

options.text: What's your master doing in Burthorpe?

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: Keeping an eye on those Imperial Guard. We can't trust 'em, you know. But I shouldn't talk about his mission.

options.text: What's with the glowing portal thing?
What's with the glowing portal thing?

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: This place? It's the castle crypt. The greatest White Knights are buried here, after a lifetime in the service of Saradomin. At least, that's how it used to be.

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: When I was a new recruit, they brought me here and told me that if I served Saradomin faithfully, and with distinction, maybe I'd earn the honour of burial in this place too.

steps.speaker: Squire
steps.text: But if you think about it, that's never going to happen - there just isn't space for more tombs! Anyway, my plan is to avoid dying, and maybe marry one of the barmaids when I retire.
other

standard.npc: Hi, how can I help you?

steps.npc: I'm a Squire for the Void Knights.
The Void Knights, they are great warriors of balance who do Guthix's work here in Gielinor.
Entry is strictly invite only, however we do need help continuing Guthix's work.
Ah well you see we try to keep Gielinor as Guthix intended, it's very challenging. Actually we've been having some problems recently, maybe you could help us?

Well the order has become quite diminished over the years, it's a very long process to learn the skills of a Void Knight. Recently there have been breaches into our realm from somewhere else, and strange creatures
have been pouring through. We can't let that happen, and we'd be very grateful if you'd help us.
We send launchers from our outpost to the nearby islands. If you go and wait in the lander there that'd really help.
It is the name that Guthix gave to this world, so we honour him with its use.

This is where we launch our landers to combat the invasion of the nearby islands. You'll see three landers - one for novice, intermediate and veteran adventurers. Each has a different difficulty, but they therefore offer
varying rewards.
The intermediate.

Simple. We send a lander out every few minutes, however we need at least 5 volunteers or it's a suicide mission. The lander can only hold a maximum of 25 people though, so we do send them out early if they get
full. If you'd be willing to help us then just wait in the lander and we'll launch it as soon as it's ready. However you will need a combat level of 70 to use this lander.

standard.npc: Too right, Gary! This is much better than being on strike!
Welcome back, my child.

steps.npc: Very good, my child. My disciples are providing a steady supply of their blood for the vampyres. As promised, the tithing of humans has been completely outlawed.

steps.player: And the vampyres are all happy with that?

steps.npc: Most are understanding of the fact that regardless of anything else, the days of tithing humans were running short. However, it is true that some found human blood to be more... appetising.

steps.player: I assume that won't be a problem?

steps.npc: You need not fear, my child. Any that attempt to take blood from a human will be dealt with harshly.

That said, my understanding is that some humans did willingly provide their blood to the Drakans. It is of course possible that could be explored again in future, albeit with very different arrangements.
However, I very much understand that will likely be a... difficult proposal for most to swallow.

steps.player: Yes, I can't see many being up for that sort of thing. Speaking of which, how are the humans of Morytania doing?

steps.npc: The fact that they are not being tithed is on its own a significant improvement to their quality of life. However, their homes are still ruins and these lands are still dangerous.
We are offering our help in building them new homes, but it will take many years, and most are still naturally distrusting of our kind.

steps.player: I'm guessing a lot will be more interested in starting new lives across the Salve.

steps.npc: You are correct, my child. However, while we have established somewhat of an... understanding with your human kingdoms to the west, it is their preference that we try to limit how many humans relocate over there.

They are not equipped to deal with a large number of refugees, and it is also our hope that many humans will realise they still have a place here. We will need their help restoring these lands to glory.

steps.player: That's not going to be an easy undertaking.

steps.npc: It will most certainly take many of your human lifetimes, but I have no doubt we will make it so.

steps.text: other

options.text: I see you've opened a new portal to Vampyrium.

steps.player: I see you've opened a new portal to Vampyrium.

steps.npc: Yes... While my disciples are currently providing blood for the vampyres here, I do not consider that a suitable long-term solution. Haemalchemy, I believe, will be the true answer.

With us having outlawed the practice of vampyrification, we have started using the labs to explore the creation of artificial blood instead. Curiously, we've already had some luck with daeyalt of all things.
It seems that the very substance that is the key to making vampyres can also potentially contribute to feeding them. While it makes sense in many ways, it was also rather... unexpected.

steps.player: Interesting... And how does Vampyrium play into this?

steps.npc: Vampyrium is home to all manner of flora and fauna that cannot be found here. With the threat of Drakan dealt with, my disciples can freely travel to and from there, collecting samples to use in our experiments.

You are more than welcome to use the portal yourself, my child. Blood donations from Efaritay and my disciples keep it well powered, and it may be that you'll find Vampyrium to offer something of interest to you.

standard-dialogue-the-first-time-the-pla.npc: I've not seen your face before. Given they let you come down here, I'm assuming you've been allowed to join the Alchemical Society?
Well in that case, just through there is the lab we use to produce potions for the kingdom. However, before you head in and get started, there's a couple of things to note.
First, I can see you're not from around here, so I'll point out that Varlamorian Alchemy is a little different from the Druidic Herblore that you'll be familiar with.
We discovered that the majority of herbs in the world can be broken down into three alchemical reagents: Mox, Aga and Lye.
When mixed in the correct way, these three components produce drastically different results. As such, in the lab you will be using these components to create various potions.

standard-dialogue-the-first-time-the-pla.player: What potions do I need to make?

standard-dialogue-the-first-time-the-pla.npc: That depends. We get orders in from across the kingdom. You'll need to keep an eye out for what potions are currently desired and ensure you're making the right ones.

steps.npc: Very well... Listen closely.

steps.text: The scene cuts to each part of the laboratory as they are discussed

steps.npc: Start by breaking down herbs or unfinished potions over at the Refiner. This will give you your reagents: Mox, Aga, and Lye paste. The type you get will depend on the quality of what you put in.
Insert the paste into the Hopper and it will become available to use in the Mixer.
From here, you'll need to pull the Mixer Levers to create the right combination of reagents.

steps.player: But how do I know what the combinations are?

steps.text: If the player has mixology lab notes:

steps.npc: I see you've already found our book of lab notes. That'll give you the formulas for our various products.

steps.text: If the player does not have mixology lab notes:

steps.npc: Have a look on the bookshelf for a book of lab notes. That'll give you the formulas for our various products.
To know what needs making, you'll need to check the order list. There will always be three orders to choose from. You can work on just one or them, or multiple. It's up to you.
Just be aware that demand shifts fast here. Every time you fulfil one or more orders, a new set will come through.
Now, once you have set your desired combination of reagents, collect the unfinished mixture from the Mixing Vessel. This will then need to be processed on one of the three tables to finish it off.
The Alembic will Crystalise the mixture.
The Agitator will Homogenise the mixture.
And finally, the Retort will Concentrate the mixture.
After processing, place the finished mixture on the Conveyor Belt and move on to the next order.

steps.player: What if I get an order wrong, or am unable to fulfil any of the orders?

steps.npc: We always have need for spares, so fulfilling an incorrect order will still grant you a small reward and will refresh the orders.
One final thing to mention... We have some Digweed growing in the lab.
These rare herbs will occasionally come into maturity for a short period of time. Harvest them while you can!
Mixing some into your product will increase its potency and grant you bonus rewards.

That's right. As you produce potions, you'll find yourself collecting three types of Resin. The types obtained depend on what reagents are used, with the quantities being determined by the complexity of the
potion.
Potions using Digweed will reward additional Resin, as will handing in multiple potions in one go.

steps.player: Got it! So, refine herbs, deposit into the hopper, mix some products, process them, and then throw them on the conveyor. Seems easy enough!

options.text: I'm sure I can work it out.

steps.player: I'm sure I can work it out.

steps.npc: Suit yourself. I'll be here if you change your mind.

options.text: Can you explain how to make potions?

steps.player: Can you explain how to make potions?

steps.npc: Very well... Listen closely.
As you wish.

options.text: Can you tell me more about the Alchemical Society?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about the Alchemical Society?

steps.npc: Can't imagine there's much to tell beyond what you already know. We exist to bring about advancements in Herblore, but in truth, a lot of what we produce doesn't directly contribute to that.
Instead, many of the potions we make here are simply to sell. Doing so is what provides the funding we need to further our true goals.

steps.player: Makes sense. So how did the society first get established?

steps.npc: For a long time, it was just a couple of us operating out of a makeshift lab we'd built in my garden. Our big break came when the Moonrise Brewery and Winery learnt about us.
They provided us with some initial funding to properly get things going, but more importantly, they provided this lab space. This was actually one of their old wine cellars before we moved in.

steps.player: Why were they so interested in your work?

steps.npc: They never properly said why, just that they were very keen to see us grow. Maybe they're hoping our work can help them create new beers and wines.

steps.player: I see. I suppose that makes sense.

steps.player: Remind me, what's going on here?

steps.npc: Well, the Hueycoatl has awoken.
Huey-co-at... oh, I don't have time for this! The thing you need to know is that it's dangerous and it's coiled throughout this entire mountain!

steps.player: Do you know where it came from?

steps.npc: We're not sure. There are some records of our ancestors having dealings with it, but the details have been lost, assuming they were ever recorded.
Does it really matter how old it is?

steps.player: I suppose not. I guess I just want to get a better understanding of what this thing is.

steps.npc: We don't know how old it is. It could be extremely old, or this could be just one in a lineage of them. Still, we haven't heard of any others so maybe it is some sort of ancient creature.

steps.player: And given that you're here, I assume it poses some sort of threat?

steps.npc: Now you're getting it! While it doesn't seem to be innately aggressive, our concern is the potential risk of it tunnelling into Cam Torum.
Oh, and given that it does lash out from time to time, I suppose it does pose a threat to your nearby human villages. A lesser priority for us, but maybe something for you to care about.
Anyway, for now, our only option is to keep it in check while we figure out what to do in the long term.
Unfortunately, that means recruiting all the help we can get, even from you humans...

steps.text: If the player has not completed Perilous Moons:

steps.npc: Well, despite what some of us may think of your kind, we need all the help we can get.

steps.text: continue
If the player has completed Perilous Moons:

steps.npc: Well, as you've already proven yourself useful to Cam Torum, I'd be glad to have you help here!

steps.text: continue

steps.npc: We need to keep the Hueycoatl under control which, until we find a more permanent solution, means wearing it out through combat.
Don't go killing it, mind you! Not that I think you could, but such a magnificent creature doesn't deserve destruction.

steps.player: Do you have any tips for surviving?

steps.npc: We've found our prayers can protect us from its shards, so keep an eye out for those.
To reach the Hueycoatl's head, you'll need to get it to move its great body out of the way. We've found we can persuade it by giving the exposed parts a helpful nudge!
Once you reach its head, you'll need to work with your comrades and the seer to balance your prayers and weaken the beast.
But I'm sure you'll figure it out!

steps.player: Move the body, then attack the head while keeping prayers balanced. Got it!

options.text: Are there any rewards for helping?

steps.player: Are there any rewards for helping?

steps.npc: Ugh, you greedy humans.
The Hueycoatl displaces a lot of materials as it moves, including all sorts of items and treasures.
We collect as much as we can, so I suppose you can have a share for helping.
Bye.

standard.player: Hi, my name is [player name]. What's wi...

standard.npc: I not be in the mood t' talk, sorry. If ye need anythin', talk to Cap'ain Pudi over by the dock.

after-talking-to-captain-pudi-with-level.npc: I cannot believe that beast ruined me ship.

steps.npc: Was awful, me crew an' I were out on our fortnightly fishin' excursion. We set sail from Al Kharid t' the deep-sea fishin' spot we usually use.
Was nothin' but smooth sailin' all the way, we got t' the spot an' started fishin'.

steps.player: Sounds like a normal day of fishing to me.

steps.npc: Aye, I s'pose it was. After a few days, the crew an' I sailed further t' the Karamjan coast t' catch some sharks. More plunder from sellin' sharks.
While sailin', I noticed there was more debris than usual. Koanee said there must have been a storm recently.
Koanee is in charge of plottin' a course t' our destination an' watchin' the weather. I thought she was good at her job.
We got to our final fishin' spot an' Lauretta let down the net. Almost a whole day went by an' we still 'ad not caught any fish.
In fact, I could not see any fish in the waters at all. Such a strange sight.
Nothin'. We decided t' pack it in for the day an' I told Koanee t' leave the nets down, hoping we would catch some fish overnight.

steps.player: That sounds like a bad idea. What would have happened if your net got too full or your ship started drifting and the net got caught on some rocks?

steps.npc: 'Twas a risk we 'ad to take t' catch some fish.
The next day Koanee woke me up t' tell me a storm was on the horizon, so we lifted the anchor up an' adjusted our course.
Not sure what she was playing at with that decision, but out o' nowhere winds started t' change an' the storm was headin' in our direction, we couldn't outrun it.
'Twas also too dangerous to anchor down, so we 'ad to weather it.
Thick fog rolled in, giant waves crashin' against the ship's hull. So much lightnin', it felt like Saradomin was angry with us.
The lightnin' struck our sails, settin' them ablaze despite the 'eavy rain!
The last thing I see is glowin' fish an' a monster in the distance with a twisted face. Next thing I know, I'm lying on the shore just south of Al Kharid with Pudi waving a kebab in me face!

steps.player: That must have been awful. At least you and the crew survived.

steps.npc: Aye, we survived, but the same cannot be said for me poor ship! Koanee should 'o known better!
Once Pudi and the others helped us back on our feet, the Chancellor sent us 'ere t' setup shop and recruit others.
Not really my area of expertise, mind, but Pudi sorts most of it out!
Anythin' else I can help ye with?

options.text: Can you give me any farming advice?

steps.player: Can you give me any farming advice?

steps.npc: The only way to cure a bush or tree of disease is to prune away the diseased leaves with a pair of secateurs. For all other crops I would just apply some plant-cure.
Tree seeds must be grown in a plantpot of soil into a sapling, and then transferred to a tree patch to continue growing to adulthood.
You can put up to ten potatoes, cabbages or onions in vegetable sacks, although you can't have a mix in the same sack.
You can buy all the farming tools from farming shops, which can be found close to the allotments.
Bittercap mushrooms can only be grown in a special patch in Morytania, near the Mort Myre swamp. There the ground is especially dank and suited to growing poisonous fungii.
Supercompost is far better than normal compost, but more expensive to make. You need to rot the right type of item; show me an item, and I'll tell you if it's super- compostable or not.
There is a special patch for growing Belladonna - I believe that it is somewhere near Draynor Manor, where the ground is a tad 'unblessed'.
Applying compost to a patch will not only reduce the chance that your crops will get diseased, but you will also grow more crops to harvest.
If you want to grow fruit trees you could try a few places: Catherby, Brimhaven, Gnome Stronghold and the Farming Guild all have fruit tree patches.
You can fill plantpots with soil from any empty patch, if you have a gardening trowel.

Hops are good for brewing ales. I believe there's a brewery up in Keldagrim somewhere, and I've heard rumours that a place called Phasmatys used to be good for that type of thing. 'Fore they all died, of course.
Vegetables, hops and flowers need constant watering - if you ignore my advice, you will sooner or later find yourself in possession of a dead farming patch.
You can put up to five tomatoes, strawberries, apples, bananas or oranges into a fruit basket, although you can't have a mix in the same basket.
Don't just throw away your weeds after you've raked a patch - put them in a compost bin and make some compost.

initial-dialogue.npc: Ouch!

initial-dialogue.player: Are you alright?

initial-dialogue.npc: I'm fine, I'm fine. Just a scratch.

initial-dialogue.player: If you're sure. Who are you?

initial-dialogue.npc: Me? I'm Tarik.

initial-dialogue.player: That hat you're wearing doesn't look like it comes from around here?

initial-dialogue.npc: It was a present. My employer thought it would suit me. I'm not sure it does, though it does keep the sun off very well.

initial-dialogue.player: Who is this employer?

initial-dialogue.npc: Simon Templeton. He's an archaeologist. I worked as an assistant for him, though I haven't seen him since the plague business started, so I work for myself now.

initial-dialogue.player: I see. So what have you been up to?

initial-dialogue.npc: Simon suggested that there might be riches to be found in this pyramid.
All I've found so far are injuries though.

initial-dialogue.text: If the player has never played the Pyramid Plunder minigame:

steps.player: Interesting... What can you tell me about this pyramid?

steps.npc: Well, I'm not sure. It's called Jalsavrah apparently. It's a strange place.
First of all, there's something odd about the doors. There's four of them, but three of them lead to an empty tomb.
The other one is guarded by something, and whatever it is, it doesn't like visitors.
The thing is, the doors seem to change around sometimes. It's all quite confusing.

steps.player: What's this thing guarding one of them.

steps.npc: I think it might be a mummy. It's not very friendly, but it does allow you to enter some of the rooms in the tomb. They are dangerous though.

steps.player: Well I'm not afraid of a little danger.

steps.npc: Are you sure? The place is full of poisonous snakes and scarabs along with some rather nasty mummies as well. You could die in there.
I managed to get into one room, but the next room was harder. My lockpicking skills weren't good enough. Maybe I should have taken a lockpick.

steps.player: It all sounds like fun to me. So, is there anything valuable in there?

steps.npc: There are lots of artefacts that you should be able to sell to a legitimate trader...
Of course. He's as 'legitimate' as you can get.

steps.player: Is there anything else of value in there?

steps.npc: I've heard a rumour that there is an ancient magic sceptre somewhere inside.

steps.player: Ah, now you've piqued my interest. What do you know about this sceptre?

steps.npc: Not a lot. It's apparently made of gold and covered in jewels. It's supposed to have some magical powers as well.

steps.player: Magical powers? This sounds good. What are they?

steps.npc: I'll let you know when I find it!

steps.player: Not if I find it first!

steps.npc: Hey! if you find it, I deserve a share of the profits! You wouldn't have known it existed without my help.

steps.player: Yes, it's an odd place, isn't it?

steps.npc: You've been inside? Did you find anything?

standard.npc: Oh, hello. Any luck in the pyramid? I'd appreciate a cut of anything you find.

standard.player: Right... I'll be sure to let you know if I come across anything good...

standard.npc: Great!

using-items-on-him-plundered-artefacts.player: Ah, yes... I'll bring it round later.

using-items-on-him-pharaoh-s-sceptre.npc: Wow! It looks very valuable. What's my share?

using-items-on-him-pharaoh-s-sceptre.player: Well given the work I had to go through to get it, I think I earned it all by myself.

using-items-on-him-pharaoh-s-sceptre.npc: Hey, that's not fair. I told you about this pyramid!

using-items-on-him-pharaoh-s-sceptre.player: The world is a harsh place. Live and learn.

steps.npc: My name is Tarquin Marjoribanks.
I'd be surprised if you haven't already heard of me?

steps.player: Why would I have heard of you Mr. Marjoribanks?

steps.npc: It's pronounced 'Marchbanks'!
You should know of me because I am a member of the royal family of Misthalin!

steps.player: Are you related to King Roald?

steps.npc: Oh yes! Quite closely actually.
I'm his 4th cousin, once removed on his mothers side.

steps.player: Er... Okay. What are you doing here then?

steps.npc: I'm canoeing on the river! It's enormous fun! Would you like to know how?

steps.player: Could you teach me about canoes?

steps.npc: Well, you don't look like you have the skill to make a canoe.
You need to have at least level 12 woodcutting.
Once you are able to make a canoe it makes travel along the river much quicker!

steps.text: If the player has 12-99 Woodcutting:

options.text: What have you learned about the artefacts we dug up?

steps.npc: Bartak used the design of the shield you extracted to recreate a shield like it. Even though the original shield was poorly made, the design itself was a good one.
Perhaps there is some important knowledge that we have lost since the early, more war-like days of Dorgesh-Kaan.
The helmet you helped to unearth has come in useful. I used it as a visual aid when I went to talk to the children in the nursery about our history.
It's amazing that the ancient goblins' eyes were even smaller than a child's!
Oldak examined the axe blade you dug up and found that it had a faint magical aura. It looks like the mace wasn't the only magical weapon our ancestors brought from the surface.

In fact, it could be that a lot of their equipment was magical. This means that either the ancient goblins were skilled magical craftsmen, or some other power was supplying them with magical equipment.
We used the armour fragment you unearthed to reconstruct the shape of the original armour, and with it the shape of the goblin who wore the armour.
This told us a lot about how the goblin body shape changed from its surface form to that of the cave goblins.
When we examined the sword you dug up, we found that the blade is covered in tiny symbols.
The scribe thinks he has enough of them to begin understanding the ancient goblin language, but it will take a while for him to decipher them.

steps.npc: In this room you will see a maze within which one of my fellow Guardians has been turned to stone for the purposes of this exercise. You must move the statue using your telekinetic grab spell to the exit square at

the edge of the maze to bring the Guardian back to life. Simply stand on the side that you wish for the statue to travel towards and cast the spell on the statue. Once you have solved the maze, the statue will change back

into the Guardian and he will award you with Telekinetic Pizazz Points and teleport you to the next maze. You can switch to a better view of the maze by selecting the 'Observe' option on the statue and return
your view to normal by selecting the same option again. There is also a 'Reset' option on the statue just in case things aren't going too well.

As well as the experience in casting magic, you will get Telekinetic Pizazz Points for each maze successfully solved and bonus points for completing five mazes in a row without returning to the entrance.

talking-to-him-while-the-player-is-wield.player: I found out that he was banished, and that the people's hero was trapped in a pyramid and...

talking-to-him-while-the-player-is-wield.npc: So you're the one who found out about that. I've heard the story from my friends in the museum. Well done on being able to wield such an impressive symbol.

talking-to-him-while-the-player-is-wield.text: The dialogue continues to ask about the Digsite quest.

using-items-using-an-ancient-staff-on-hi.player: What do you think of this?

using-items-using-unidentified-liquid-on.text: All unidentified liquids in inventory are replaced with nitroglycerin.

using-items-using-unidentified-liquid-on.player: Do you know what this is?
From one of the barrels at the digsite.

using-items-using-unidentified-liquid-on.npc: This is a VERY dangerous liquid called nitroglycerin. Be careful how you handle it. Don't drop it or it will explode!

using-items-using-nitroglycerin-on-him.player: Can you tell me any more about this?

using-items-using-nitroglycerin-on-him.npc: Nitroglycerin! This is a dangerous substance. This is normally mixed with other chemicals to produce a potent compound.
Be sure not to drop it! That stuff is highly volatile...

using-items-using-ammonium-nitrate-on-hi.npc: Really, you do find the most unusual items. I know what this is - it's a strong chemical called ammonium nitrate. Why you want this I'll never know...

using-items-using-mixed-chemicals-on-him.npc: Hmm, that looks dangerous. Handle it carefully and don't drop it!

using-items-using-mixed-chemicals-with-c.player: See what I have done with the compound now.

using-items-using-mixed-chemicals-with-c.npc: Seriously, I think you have a death wish! What on earth are you going to do with that stuff?

using-items-using-mixed-chemicals-with-c.player: I'll find a use for it!

using-items-using-the-chemical-compound-.player: What do you think about this?

using-items-using-the-chemical-compound-.npc: What have you concocted now? Just be careful when playing with chemicals!

using-items-using-nuggets-on-him.text: If the player has less than 3 nuggets:

steps.npc: I can't do much with these nuggets yet. Come back when you have 3 and I will exchange them for you.

using-items-using-nuggets-on-him.text: If the player has at least 3 nuggets:

steps.text: Player gives 3 nuggets.

steps.npc: Good – that's three; I can exchange them for normal gold now. You can get this refined and make a profit!

using-items-using-a-needle-on-him.npc: Hmm, yes; I wondered why this race were so well dressed! It looks like they had mastery of needlework.

using-items-using-a-rotten-apple-on-him.npc: Ew! Throw them away this instant!

using-items-using-broken-glass-on-him.player: Have a look at this glass.

using-items-using-broken-glass-on-him.npc: Hey you should be careful of that. It might cut your fingers, throw it away!

using-items-using-a-broken-arrow-on-him.player: Have a look at this arrow.

using-items-using-a-broken-arrow-on-him.npc: No doubt this arrow was shot by a strong warrior – it's split in half! It is not a valuable object though.

using-items-using-a-panning-tray-on-him.text: If the panning tray is empty:

steps.npc: I have no need for panning trays!

using-items-using-a-panning-tray-on-him.text: If the panning tray has something in it:

steps.npc: Have you searched this tray yet?
It may contain something; I don't want to get my hands dirty.

steps.text: The expert hands the tray back to you.

using-items-using-bones-on-him.player: Have a look at these bones.

using-items-using-bones-on-him.npc: Ah, yes – a fine bone example... no noticeable fractures... and in good condition. These are common cow bones, however; they have no archaeological value.

using-items-using-buttons-on-him.npc: Let's have a look. Ah, I think these are from the nobility, perhaps a royal servant?

using-items-using-a-cracked-sample-on-hi.npc: What a shame it's cracked; this looks like it would have been a good sample.

using-items-using-an-old-tooth-on-him.npc: Oh, an old tooth. It looks like it has come from a mighty being. Pity there are no tooth fairies around here!

using-items-using-a-rusty-sword-on-him.npc: Oh, it's very rusty isn't it? I'm not sure this sword belongs here, it looks very out of place.

using-items-using-a-broken-staff-on-him.player: Have a look at this staff.

using-items-using-a-broken-staff-on-him.npc: Look at this... Interesting... This appears to belong to a cleric of some kind; certainly not a follower of Saradomin, however.
I wonder if there was another civilization here before the Saradominists?

using-items-using-broken-armour-on-him.npc: It looks like the wearer of this fought a mighty battle.

using-items-using-damaged-armour-on-him.npc: How unusual. This armour doesn't seem to match with the other finds. Keep looking.

using-items-using-ceramic-remains-on-him.npc: Yes, many parts are discovered. The inhabitants of these parts were great potters.

using-items-using-ceramic-remains-on-him.player: You mean they were good at using potions?

using-items-using-ceramic-remains-on-him.npc: No, no, silly. They were known for their skill with clay.

using-items-using-a-belt-buckle-on-him.player: Have a look at this unusual item...

using-items-using-a-belt-buckle-on-him.npc: Let me see. This is a belt buckle. Not so unusual - I should imagine it came from a guard.

using-items-using-an-animal-skull-on-him.npc: Hmm, an interesting find; an animal skull for sure. Another student found one just like this today.

using-items-using-the-special-cup-on-him.text: The expert cleans off the mud.

using-items-using-the-special-cup-on-him.npc: Looks like an award cup for some small find. Perhaps it belongs to one of the students?

using-items-using-teddy-on-him.npc: Why, it looks like a teddy bear to me. Perhaps someone's lucky mascot!

using-items-using-an-old-boot-on-him.npc: Ah yes, an old boot. Not really an ancient artefact, is it?

using-items-using-another-ancient-talism.text: The expert has already seen the talisman.

using-items-using-the-invitation-letter-.npc: There's no point in giving me this back!

using-items-using-stone-tablet-on-him-du.player: I found this in a hidden cavern beneath the digsite.
There is an altar down there. The place is crawling with skeletons!

using-items-using-stone-tablet-on-him-du.npc: This is an amazing discovery! All this while we were convinced that no other race had lived here.
It seems the followers of Saradomin have tried to cover up the evidence of the Zaros altar. This whole city must have been built over it!
Thanks for your help; your sharp eyes have spotted what many have missed. Here, take this gold as your reward.

using-items-using-stone-tablet-on-him-du.text: The expert gives you 2 gold bars as payment.

using-items-using-stone-tablet-on-him-po.npc: I don't need another tablet! One is enough, thank you.

standard.player: Hello there. What do you do here?

standard.npc: Ah, I'm just keeping an eye on things and making sure nothing untoward happens.
One day I hope it will be.

standard-dialogue-after-completion-of-wh.npc: Ah, [player name], it's good to see you again.

standard-dialogue-after-completion-of-wh.player: Hello there, Thaerisk. Any word on Lucien?

standard-dialogue-after-completion-of-wh.npc: Nothing yet, but we're doing everything we can to find him. I hope he's ready for us, because once we do locate him, we're going to give him quite the bloody nose...
... or at least whatever passes for a nose on a Mahjarrat!

standard-dialogue-after-fremennik-isles.npc: Thank you for leading the Burgher's militia against the Troll King.
Now that the trolls are leaderless I have repaired the bridge to the central isle for you as best I can.

standard-dialogue-after-fremennik-isles.player: Thanks Thakkrad. Does that mean I have access to the runite ores on that island?

standard-dialogue-after-fremennik-isles.npc: Yes, you should be able to mine runite there if you wish.

speaking-to-thakkrad-about-curing-hides.prompt: What can I help you with?

steps.npc: I will cure yak-hide for a fee of 5 gp per hide.

steps.text: If the player has no yak-hides:

steps.npc: You have no yak-hide to cure.

steps.text: If the player does not have at least five coins per yak-hide:

steps.npc: You don't have enough gold to pay me!

steps.text: If the player has yak-hides and at least five coins per yak-hide:

steps.prompt: How many hides do you want cured?

steps.text: one cured yak-hide per yak-hide given

steps.npc: There you go.

steps.text: one cured yak-hide

steps.npc: There you go.
Bye.

options.text: Can you cure any other type of leather?

steps.player: Can you cure any other type of leather?

steps.npc: Other types of leather? Why would you need any other type of leather?

steps.player: I'll take that as a no then.

steps.npc: See you later.
You won't find anyone else who can cure yak-hide.

standard.npc: Hi there!

options.text: Can I have some more headgear?

steps.player: Can I have some more headgear?

steps.text: The 'Wedge' gives you some more headgear.

steps.npc: Call me The 'Wedge', I'm the taskmaster for the Achievement Diary here in Kandarin.

It's a diary that helps you keep track of particular achievements. In and around Kandarin it can help you discover some quite useful things. Eventually, with enough exploration, the inhabitants will reward you.
You can see the list of tasks on the side-panel.

options.text: I have a question about my Achievement Diary

steps.player: I have a question about my Achievement Diary.

steps.npc: It's a diary that helps you keep track of particular achievements. In and around Kandarin it can help you discover some quite useful things. Eventually, with enough exploration, the inhabitants will reward you.
You can see the list of tasks on the side-panel.

Well, there are four different Kandarin headgears, which match up with the four levels of difficulty. Each has the same rewards as the previous level and some additional benefits too... which tier of rewards would you
like to know more about?

steps.player: Tell me more about the Easy rewards please!

steps.npc: If you complete all of the easy tasks in Kandarin, the headgear functions as a light source and you have a chance of receiving an extra log when cutting normal trees. You can get the flax keeper to convert 30 flax
to bowstrings each day, coal trucks hold up to 140 coal and you'll find 5% more marks of grace on Seers' rooftop agility course.

steps.player: Tell me more about the Medium rewards please!

steps.npc: In addition to the easy rewards, cutting maples in Seers' village provides 10% more experience. You can spin materials 33% faster at the spinning wheel, get the flax keeper to convert 60 flax to bowstrings each day,

and the Catherby herb patch provides a 5% higher crop yield. Coal trucks will hold up to 280 coal too. You can also use the rope I left at Baxtorian falls, instead of bringing your own, as long as you have completed the
Waterfall quest.

steps.player: Tell me more about the Hard rewards please!

steps.npc: In addition to the easy and medium benefits, Thormac will enchant battlestaves for 30,000 gold and you can move the Camelot teleport location to outside of Seers' bank. You'll find 15% more marks of grace on Seers'

rooftop, receive 10% higher yield from Catherby farming patch, get the flax keeper to convert 120 flax to bowstrings each day, and get 10% more points from Barbarian Assault as well one free daily teleport to
Sherlock. Your chances of having an enchanted bolt use it's special attack has increased by 10% too.

steps.player: Tell me more about the Elite rewards please!

steps.npc: In addition to the previous tiers of rewards, Thormac now enchants battlestaves for 20,000 gold, Otto will provide a 50% discount when converting Zamorakian spears into hastae. You'll get unlimited teleports to

Sherlock and 15% increased yield from Catherby herb patch and can get the flax keeper to convert 250 flax to bow strings every day. The first 200 coal placed in coal trucks every day will be automatically transported
to your bank too.

options.text: How do I claim the rewards?

steps.player: How do I claim the rewards?

steps.npc: Just complete the tasks in Kandarin so they're ticked off, then come and speak to me for your rewards.
See you around.

easy-tasks-completed.player: I've completed all of the easy tasks in my Kandarin Achievement Diary!

easy-tasks-completed.npc: I can see that, well done! You'll be wanting your reward then!

This headgear is a symbol of your exploration of Kandarin. It functions as a light source and you now have a chance of receiving an extra log when cutting normal trees. You can get the flax keeper to convert
30 flax to bowstrings each day, coal trucks now hold up to 140 coal and you'll find 5% more marks of grace on Seers' rooftop agility course.
If you ever lose your headgear, come back to me to reclaim it.
