standard.player: Hello, The Beast! Why do they call you that?

attempting-to-enter-the-keldagrim-ratpit.text: The large cat near the stairs glowers menacingly at you as you approach the stairs.

attempting-to-enter-the-keldagrim-ratpit.player: I think I had better stay away from the stairs for now.

standard-dialogue-talk-to.npc: Everything! The wonders right here in this museum, collected from all corners of the land.

standard-dialogue-talk-to.player: I guess it is, you're right.

standard-dialogue-talk-to.text: If the player has a collection log in their inventory or bank:
If the player does not have a collection log in their inventory or bank:

steps.npc: Matter of fact, I consider myself quite the collector. I keep a record of just about everything that I find!
Would you like one? You could keep track of your own collections.

steps.player: No thanks. I think I'll pass.

steps.npc: I should've guessed you wouldn't understand the true beauty of a good collection!

standard-dialogue-get-log.text: If the player does not have a collection log in their inventory or bank:

steps.text: The collector gives you a collection log.

steps.npc: There! Now you'll be able to see the true beauty of everything you collect on your adventures.

standard-dialogue-get-log.text: If the player does not have a collection log and attempts to claim one with a full inventory:

steps.npc: You might struggle to carry that right now.

steps.player: Oh... I'll come back when I'm carrying a little less.

standard-dialogue-get-log.text: If the player has a collection log in their inventory or bank:

steps.npc: Don't you have one lying around somewhere already?

standard-dialogue-claim-log-rewards.player: Could you count how many uniques I've obtained in my collection?

standard-dialogue-claim-log-rewards.npc: I'd love to count everything you've collected on your adventures!
You might want to take a seat this could take a while.

standard-dialogue-claim-log-rewards.text: The collector starts counting the items in your collection.

standard-dialogue-claim-log-rewards.npc: From what I can see you have collected [number] items in your collection!

standard-dialogue-claim-log-rewards.text: If the player has more than 0-99 unique items in their collection log:

steps.npc: You've made a good start at filling your collection, keep at it!

steps.text: continues

standard-dialogue-claim-log-rewards.text: If the player has more than 100 unique items in their collection log:

steps.npc: I see you are just starting out on your collecting adventure. I wish you luck!

steps.text: continues

standard-dialogue-claim-log-rewards.text: If the player has more than 300 unique items in their collection log:

steps.npc: You've made a good start at filling your collection, keep at it!

steps.text: continues

standard-dialogue-claim-log-rewards.text: If the player has more than 500 unique items in their collection log:

steps.npc: You're starting to get a hang of this collecting business!

steps.text: continues

standard-dialogue-claim-log-rewards.text: If the player has more than 700 unique items in their collection log:

steps.npc: You have a very respectable collection indeed, one day you'll have a better collection than me!

steps.text: continues

standard-dialogue-claim-log-rewards.text: If the player has more than 900 unique items in their collection log:

steps.npc: Your collection is maturing well, you're making great strides to becoming a top collector, keep it up!

steps.text: continues

standard-dialogue-claim-log-rewards.text: If the player has more than 1000 unique items in their collection log:

steps.npc: Your collection is one of the finest I've seen, it's almost on par with mine!!

steps.text: continues

standard-dialogue-claim-log-rewards.text: If the player has more than 1100 unique items in their collection log:

steps.npc: Colour me impressed, you've collected more items than me! I look forward to seeing your collection grow even more.

steps.text: continues

standard-dialogue-claim-log-rewards.text: If the player has more than 1200 unique items in their collection log:

steps.npc: Now that's an impressive collection, I haven't seen many with a collection better than yours!

steps.text: continues

standard-dialogue-claim-log-rewards.text: If the player has registered at least 90% of all items in the collection log:

steps.npc: I can officially say that you are now an elite collector and few can stand as your equal in that regard.

steps.text: continues

standard-dialogue-claim-log-rewards.text: If the player has somehow completed the collection log:

steps.npc: Wait, you finished it? You actually finished the entire collection? I never thought that was even possible!

steps.text: continues

standard-dialogue-claim-log-rewards.npc: As an accomplished collector I'd like to offer you a special reward.

The collector hands you the Dragon staff of collection.
The collector hands you the Rune staff of collection.
The collector hands you the Adamant staff of collection.
The collector hands you the Mithril staff of collection.
The collector hands you the Black staff of collection.
The collector hands you the Steel staff of collection.
The collector hands you the Iron staff of collection.
The collector hands you the Bronze staff of collection.

standard-dialogue-claim-log-rewards.text: If the player already has all unlocked staves in their inventory or bank:

steps.npc: Actually, it appears you already have all the rewards I'd like to give you.

varlamore-token-dialogue.npc: This... idea! The idea of something nice! Those nice little tokens!

varlamore-token-dialogue.text: If the player has no red tokens in their inventory:

steps.npc: Oh, er... never you mind!

steps.text: The Collector waves at the player and disappears.

varlamore-token-dialogue.text: If the player has at least one red token in their inventory:

steps.npc: Only some? Well you need more! Until you have them, I should get going...

steps.text: The Collector waves at the player and disappears.

varlamore-token-dialogue.text: If the player has all seven red tokens in their inventory:

steps.player: Oh yes, I've got this wonderful collection of tokens!

steps.npc: May I see them?

steps.text: You show the Collector your collection of tokens.

steps.npc: May I have them?

steps.text: You hand your collection of tokens to the Collector, and in exchange he gives you some sort of a key.
a nice key
The Collector waves at the player and disappears.

steps.npc: Fine.

steps.text: The Collector waves at the player and disappears.

standard-dialogue-after-ratcatchers.npc: That was an amazing performance! I've only seen one like it... as you know.

standard-dialogue-after-ratcatchers.player: Don't worry, Felkrash has no idea how I figured it out.

standard-dialogue-after-ratcatchers.npc: And it had better stay that way!

treasure-trails-easy.text: If the reward is another clue scroll:

steps.text: You've found another clue!

treasure-trails-easy.text: If the reward is a casket:

steps.text: You've obtained a casket!

historical-dialogue-before-ratcatchers.text: She looks through you as if you don't exist.

historical-dialogue-attempting-to-enter-.npc: Step away from that manhole, you've no business down there.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Ah you, peasant. Felkrash wishes to speak with you.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.text: 'The Face' comports herself in an air of haughtiness uncommon to those with appearances as ugly as hers.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Ok, where would I find her?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: You should find her below in the pits.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Hello.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Oh it's you again. She glances at you with barely disguised disdain.*

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Aside* I wonder what her problem is?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Have you spoken with Felkrash yet?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Yes.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.text: You notice a rather unkempt looking cat nearby. Despite its bedraggled appearance it exudes power, strength and intelligence beyond that of a normal cat.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: That's an interesting looking cat.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Ah yes Belle. What a cat. Felkrash trained her for me shortly after she single handedly charmed all the rats of the Port and drowned them.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: I love that story. My favourite part is how she managed to get rid of all the rats. Would you tell it to me?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: I don't know, I really shouldn't.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Aside* I'll get the story out of her, a little sweet talking should do the trick.
Oh please tell me, I'm sure you'd tell the story wonderfully, you have such a pretty ...

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Yes..?
The face's face perks up at the mention of the word pretty.*

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: ...voice.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Oh. And just as quickly turns sour again.*

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Aside* Dang!
... which compliments your radiant aura!
Aside* That should do the trick.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Oh you're too generous.
Do you know something, I think I'll tell you, mind you, don't tell Felkrash about this, she'd only get sore with me.
She's the story teller not me.
One day ......
One day ......

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.text: The camera fades briefly to black and back.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: And that is how she drowned the rats.
..and that is how she drowned the rats.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.text: You just about manage to stay awake through the long and turgid recital of the story.
The snakecharmer of Pollnivneach from what you gathered seemed to play a critical role in the story.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Aside*Perhaps I should pay this snake charmer a visit.
Hello.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Oh it's you again. She glances at you with barely disguised disdain.*

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Aside* I wonder what her problem is?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: Felkrash told me of the task she set you.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: Really?

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.npc: I shouldn't have told that story. Shame on you for coaxing it out of me.

historical-dialogue-during-ratcatchers-a.player: I promise I won't tell her you helped me.

historical-dialogue-after-ratcatchers.npc: Oh it's you again. She glances at you with barely disguised disdain.*

historical-dialogue-after-ratcatchers.player: Aside* I wonder what her problem is?

historical-dialogue-after-ratcatchers.npc: I must congratulate you on your performance, I have only ever seen one other display of musicality to match, as you should know.

historical-dialogue-after-ratcatchers.player: Thank you, and don't worry, I won't tell Felkrash that you helped me.

standard-dialogue-interacting-with-the-g.text: If the Great Guardian is resting:

steps.text: The Great Guardian seems to be resting. You should probably not disturb it.

standard-dialogue-entering-a-portal-guar.npc: Human, I need the power of the guardian stones.

steps.text: You should feed the guardian stones to the Great Guardian before making more of them.

steps.text: You should feed the guardian stones to the Great Guardian before making more of them.

overhead-dialogue-after-reaching-full-po.npc: Humans, I now have the power to close the rift. Thank you, brave ones.
Now, for the final blow. Let the Scar be no more!

overhead-dialogue-after-reaching-full-po.text: The Great Guardian closes the rift.

overhead-dialogue-after-reaching-full-po.npc: Now, I shall rest until it opens once more...

Why, by proving yourself to be above material goods.
500 gold coins ought to do it.

if-the-player-is-spotted-without-a-disgu.npc: How dare you come near my farmhouse! Guards! Guards! Remove this human!

standard.npc: Hello! What's a monkey like you doing here?
Fair enough then.

standard-dialogue-with-m-speak-amulet-eq.npc: What are you doing in my house?
Well I don't give a monkey's uncle!

standard.npc: How curious? I have not seen a creature of your kind for many years. You have ventured into the Nexus human - I should warn you to be aware of the Abyssal Sires.

steps.npc: Ah... Time does not pass in the Abyss at the same rate that it does in your realm, but nevertheless I have been in this place for aeons.
Indeed, when I was last in your realm, the armies of Zamorak were battling the other gods for control, and we sought reinforcements from any plane we could reach.
That was how I came here. We broke through to the Abyss, seeking allies for our cause, but instead I ended up a prisoner in this place, unable to leave, while the God Wars continued without me.

options.text: Tell me about the Abyssal Sires.

steps.npc: There is something you can do here, human. In fact it may perhaps benefit us both.
Bring me a spine, a claw and an axon from the Abyssal Sires, and I shall construct them into a mighty weapon for you. Yes, we shall both benefit from this.

options.text: Tell me about the Abyssal Sires.

steps.player: Tell me about the Abyssal Sires.

steps.npc: The Sires are the engineers of this living pocket universe known to you and I as the Abyss.
At the hands of the 'Chaos God', Zamorak, like myself, they too were cast down and imprisoned in this living tomb.
They worked for centuries attempting to escape the pull of the Abyss but as food resources began to deplete they knew that their only chance for survival was to construct this Nexus.
They absorb flesh and bone of their demon kin, weaving it into the fabric of these very walls. Here they have remained in deep stasis, asleep.
If you succeed in awakening them, they will no doubt unleash their full fury upon you. Someone of your calibre should be able to deal with them though, especially with the shadows on your side...
If you succeed in killing a Sire, you may be fortunate enough to find one of its unsired offspring among its remains. Bring the Unsired here, to the Font of Consumption.
By placing the Unsired into the Font, I will be able to consume its flesh and perhaps you will receive something worth having.

initial-dialogue-if-the-player-brings-it.npc: I did not ask you to bring me anything, human.

options.text: Tell me about the Abyssal Sires.

subsequent-dialogue-if-the-player-does-n.npc: Have you harvested any components for me?

steps.npc: I shall use the components to construct a mighty weapon for you. Rest assured, the process will be beneficial to both of us.

options.text: Tell me about the Abyssal Sires.

steps.npc: I still require [bludgeon component(s)] from an Abyssal Sire.

subsequent-dialogue-if-the-player-has-at.npc: Have you harvested any components for me?

subsequent-dialogue-if-the-player-has-at.text: You hand over the component(s) to the Overseer.

subsequent-dialogue-if-the-player-has-at.npc: I still require [bludgeon component(s)] from an Abyssal Sire.

final-dialogue.npc: Have you harvested any components for me?

final-dialogue.text: You hand over the component(s) to the Overseer.

final-dialogue.npc: I now have all the components I require, so here is the weapon I promised you.

final-dialogue.text: The Overseer presents you with an Abyssal Bludgeon.

final-dialogue.npc: You have served me well, it is good to see that you humans are still as gullible as ever!
Bringing me those body parts from the Sires has now granted me enough teleportation energy to leave this living hell hole. Perhaps I will pay your realm a visit and there will be much to harvest!

final-dialogue.player: Yuck! This is disgusting. What use is this? It's unwieldly!

final-dialogue.npc: Have you not learned yet, appearances can be deceiving. You hold in your hands a living weapon whose power is rivalled by few weapons from your world, use it wisely.
Do not think that I am ungrateful for my freedom human. I will leave you this ancient tome that will instruct you in creating more of these weapons in future.
Just use the three components on the book, and it will do the rest. You can get spare copies here any time you need.

steps.npc: Farewell...

steps.text: The Overseer teleports away.

options.text: Perhaps I shall use it to slay you, demon.

steps.player: Perhaps I shall use it to slay you, demon.

steps.npc: So be it... I will await you on the fields of blood!

steps.text: The Overseer teleports away.

final-dialogue-speaking-to-it-again-afte.npc: You have served me well, it is good to see that you humans are still as gullible as ever!

final-dialogue-using-bludgeon-pieces-on-.npc: I do not require anything further from you, human.

standard.player: Hello? Can you hear me up there?

standard.npc: I hear you, young one. Care to talk? I have a lot of time on my hands.

steps.player: What happened to you? Why are you trapped in a cage?

steps.npc: Hmm. I find myself ruminating on this very question. What happened to me?
Perhaps it is best to ask Yama this question. He will have a stronger opinion than I do.
I see the events from my perspective, but this does not guarantee truth or an accurate answer.
There is little value in tall tales.
Indeed. These bars keep me well away from those fiendish little imps.
Not quite. The recent course of events has surprised me. This is not what I had planned for but I will make the best of it.

options.text: Can I help you at all?

steps.player: Can I help you at all?

steps.npc: Help me? You believe me in need of help? Do you think freedom is some precious thing to me? Vengeance perhaps?
What I would like is for this league to proceed as outlined.
Go forth! Play your part.

steps.player: Aren't you worried about what will happen to you?

steps.npc: Of course, yet the games go on. Unpleasant circumstances and the volatile beasts that surround me are simply facts I must accept - for now.
Farewell.

standard.prompt: What would you like to ask about?

steps.player: So... what do I do here, in Grid Master?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Complete the Grid of course.
Complete various challenges within the Grid Master interface.
To earn powerful rewards for Grid Master, and Grid Points for Main Game Cosmetics.
You can view the Grid Master interface by selecting it's Orb

standard.text: If the player does not have any items to reclaim:

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: It doesn't look like you need any Grid Master items right now. I'll be here if you ever do.

steps.text: You receive an item from the Sage.

standard.text: If the player has multiple items to reclaim:

steps.text: You receive some items from the Sage.

standard.speaker: The Sage
standard.text: Hello mortal. What do you seek?

options.text: What changes have been made for this League?

steps.player: What changes have been made for this League?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Much has happened since the last passage of the Trailblazers. This time, I have awakened the wrathful spirits of enemies across Gielinor.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Each region now contains a Raging Echo boss. These bosses are more powerful versions of their original self that drop unique rewards.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: To help you overcome these new challenges, you may now gain power through Combat Masteries, which you can obtain access to by completing the Combat Mastery tasks.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: As before, you'll initially be restricted to the Regions of Misthalin and Karamja. However, as you progress, you'll be able to unlock new areas of your choosing.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Be warned though - you won't be able to unlock every area, so choose wisely.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You must participate as an Ironman. This means you stand alone and cannot trade with other participants.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: And that's not all. Training skills during the League will grant you substantially more experience than you'd normally expect.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: These experience increases are known as passive effects, which get more generous the higher your Relic tier.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Finally, some quests have been completed for you automatically. Further quests and more will be completed as you unlock the relevant areas.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: I think that covers the basics. Would you like to know more, [player name]?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Is there anything else you need from me?

options.text: Can you tell me about Combat Masteries?

steps.player: Can you tell me about Combat Masteries?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Combat Masteries are powerful boons granted by me that enhance your combat abilities for the entire League.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: After all, it wouldn't be very interesting to ask you to defeat the enemies' raging echoes without allowing you to draw on your own.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You can obtain them by completing specific combat tasks to prove yourself to me.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Combat Masteries are split into the three combat styles: Ranged, Melee, and Mage. To unlock each mastery, you must have unlocked the previous mastery for that style.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: There are 6 combat masteries for each style, but only 10 mastery points can be obtained. Once you have selected a mastery there is no going back, so choose your masteries wisely.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Now, would you like to take a look at the Combat Masteries available to you?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Fair enough. Is there anything else you need from me?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: In every League, there are a number of tasks for you to complete. Each task has a level of difficulty: Easy, Medium, Hard, Elite and Master.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Completing tasks allows you to access new areas. The more tasks you complete, the more areas become available to unlock.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Not only that, completing tasks also earns you League Points. The number of points earned is dependent on the difficulty of the task.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Once you have achieved a certain amount of League Points you can unlock a new Relic of mine. These are powerful artefacts to help you in this world.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: League Points can also be used to buy rewards from the Leagues Reward Shop.
As we speak, you are playing on your Leagues profile. The Leagues Reward Shop can only be opened on your main profile.
You can access your main profile by switching to any normal Old School RuneScape world. The world switcher in the logout menu can be used to switch worlds.

steps.player: So how many tasks are there?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: More than you'll ever be able to complete, most likely. It's up to you which ones you attempt.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Now, would you like to take a look at the tasks for this League?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Is there anything else you need from me?

options.text: How does the area system work?

steps.player: How does the area system work?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Currently, you are restricted to the Kingdom of Misthalin and the island of Karamja. However, as you progress, you can unlock more areas.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: There are eleven different areas in total. However, you can only unlock a maximum of five, including the two you've started with. Choose wisely.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: I give the first two area unlocks to everyone. You can unlock the other three by completing the tasks I've set.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: The more tasks you complete, the more areas you can unlock.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Would you like to take a look at the available areas now?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Fair enough. Is there anything else you need from me?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Relics are powerful artefacts made by me that grant unique abilities for the entire League.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You may even recognise a few from Leagues past.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: There are 23 separate Relics, split across 8 different tiers. You can only have one Relic from each tier, however.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: The first Relic tier is available to everyone. The others must be unlocked with League Points.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: League Points are earned by completing tasks.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Once you have selected a Relic, your choice can't be changed for the rest of the League. Make your choices carefully.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Would you like to take a look at the Relics for this League?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Very well. Is there anything else you need from me?

options.text: Can I claim some Combat rewards?

steps.player: Can I claim some combat achievement rewards?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You do not appear to have any combat achievement rewards available to claim.

options.text: Could I buy a max cape off you?
options.condition: If the player has a total level of 2,277:

steps.text: If the player does not have at least two free inventory spaces:

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You don't have enough room.
If the player doesn't have at least 2,277,000 coins in their inventory:

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You don't have enough gold.
If the player has at least 2,277,000 coins in their inventory and at least two free inventory spaces:

steps.prompt: Buy Max Cape for 2277000 gold?

a max cape and max hood

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: There you go. Congratulations, even if it may have been accelerated with my power, it's still a real accomplishment.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: As well as letting you unlock new areas, completing tasks in the League will earn you League Points. The more League Points you have, the more Relic tiers you have available.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: However, alongside allowing you to unlock Relics, League Points can also be used to buy rewards from the Leagues Reward Shop.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Oh, all sorts of things. New cosmetic kits, an alternative Home Teleport animation, some rather stylish outfits... and much more.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Many of these rewards can be traded with your fellow mortals, so if you wish, you can earn some money by selling them on. Of course, you might prefer to keep them for yourself instead.

steps.player: I see. That all sounds good to me.

steps.text: Currently, you are playing on your Leagues profile. The Leagues Reward Shop can only be used to buy items on your main profile, although you can still browse the shop within the League.
You can access your main profile by switching to any normal Old School RuneScape world. The world switcher in the logout menu can be used to switch worlds.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You can use this shop to buy previous League rewards, too.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Alongside the rewards in the Leagues Reward Shop, there's also League Ranks.

steps.player: League Ranks? How do they work?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: During the League as you gain more points you will gain a League Rank. This rank can be seen in the Ranks interface.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You currently have the rank: [rank].

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: As you get ranks you will gain access to trophies.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: That's right. Trophies are items that are awarded to you for competing in the League. You can use them to show off your League Rank.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Connected to League Ranks are the League to League rewards. These are unlocked in the next League based upon the League Rank you earn in this one.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: League Starter Outfits and League Icons are some of things you can unlock for the next League. In addition, any pets you earn in this League will transfer over to the next one.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Finally, on top of the tasks for this League, there are some other activities for which I will recognise the first person who completes them.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You can view the entire list of activities, as well as whether or not someone has completed them, by reading the board beside me.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: My pleasure. Now, is there anything else you need from me?

steps.player: Can you tell me how pets work in Leagues?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: But of course. If you're lucky enough to obtain a pet during a League, it will automatically be insured for you.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: This means that if you lose it somehow you can talk to me and I'll give it back to you. Insurance and reclaiming is all free of charge.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Additionally, each pet you obtain will be transferred to the next League. I'll take good care of it until you're ready to reclaim it.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Come back to me once you have some pets and you can view your collection. Now, is there anything else you need from me?

options.text: Do I have any League items to collect?

steps.player: Do I have any League items to collect?

steps.text: You receive some items from the Sage.

options.text: Can you help me smash vials?

steps.player: Can you help me smash vials?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: With all of my power, this is something I can manage. You will now automatically smash vials.
If the player has automatic vial smashing enabled:

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: With all of my power, this is something I can manage. You will no longer smash vials automatically.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Very well. I'll be here if you ever need to know anything more.

presenting-a-raids-megarare-voucher.speaker: The Sage

presenting-a-raids-megarare-voucher.speaker: The Sage
presenting-a-raids-megarare-voucher.text: I guess you'll be wanting to trade it in for one of Gielinor's powerful weapons.

attempting-to-change-spell-animation-ove.speaker: The Sage
attempting-to-change-spell-animation-ove.text: You cannot do that in this world, you must abide by my rules, mortal.

standard.speaker: The Sage
standard.text: Greetings, how may I be of service.

options.text: Who are you? What is your name?

steps.player: Who are you? What is your name?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Who am I?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: I am whatever is needed of me.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: I am a form undefined by natural laws, manifested by someone we mustn't speak of.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: I'm a clay doll, shaped by a sculptor. Never allowed to set, forever malleable. But maybe, not for long...

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: My true name is immaterial, But you may call me...

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Let's see now, what would be most appropriate?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Ah, yes.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You may call me The Sage.

steps.player: Uhhh, ok... Sage. Where did you bring us?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: 'Where' is the right question my friend, but maybe not in the way you are accustomed to hearing.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Reality as you know it has many layers, all slightly different with their own rules.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Through the power granted to me, I brought us to this layer using the River-Between. The River of Souls.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: We now stand on the stage of what is yet to be your most entertaining performance yet!

steps.player: Layers? River-Between? What does any of this mean?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: To give everything away at this point would be unwise, considering we are being watched even now. You should only be concerned about one thing.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Being entertaining.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: That's the only way you will get out of this event alive...

steps.player: Entertaining? What are you talking about? Who am I entertaining? Stop talking in riddles!

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Ahh, [player name], please forgive me. In my attempts to explain, I appear to have confused you even further...

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: I will keep things simple for you; Participate in this event and you will continue to exist. Refusal to participate will end in your eventual destruction.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: The choice is yours... hero.

steps.player: Well, that doesn't really answer anything...

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Worry not. I have much grander plans for you yet, but like all good stories we must wait for the right time and place...

options.text: You mentioned other Leagues - how does this differ from those?

steps.player: You mentioned other Leagues - how does this differ from those?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Like all events before it, the rules of the world have been altered to be more entertaining for those who are watching.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: The biggest change has been to the Relics from the previous chapter.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: These objects of power are now gone, I have broken them into Fragments and spread across this iteration of the world.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: When multiple Fragments are in harmony, they can be used together to create powerful effects.

steps.player: Yes, I remember you shattering them on the boat ride.
So I have Fragments to collect... got it. Are there any OTHER weird rules I should know about?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: I understand that in previous Leagues, they limited you to smaller spaces of your world.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: That restriction doesn't exist in this event.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You're free to roam your world, exploring the furthest reaches from Morytania to Kourend & Kebos.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: But there's a catch.

steps.player: Oh great... there's always a catch.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: I've limited and reset some of your memories, meaning you won't be able to interact with certain elements of this world.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: For example, you'll only have access to three skills: Defence, Fishing and Thieving, as well as the Combat Class you chose earlier.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: In order to gain access to other skills, you need to complete Tasks for me.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Doing so gives you Sage's Renown. A rather fitting name, I thought.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: With Renown you can purchase access to new skills as well as bosses and quests.

steps.player: Why are you doing all of this? Surely I'd be more 'entertaining' if I could have all the power at once?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: I can't just give you all that power. What kind of story starts the hero with all the power they want?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: No, your story needs good rhythm. A sort of cadence that makes things interesting for your audience.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Start slow, work your way up. Become the hero you were always meant to be...

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Once you have proven yourself, then and only then will you earn my renown.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: That's how you provide good entertainment my friend...

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: That's how you make a hero.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Do you desire more information?
(Leagues info interface opens.)

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Go forward and continue your journey.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Remember, we are always watching...

options.text: Any tips you can give me on being 'entertaining'?

steps.player: Any tips you can give me on being 'entertaining'?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: I have devised a number of tasks to help keep your story on track.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Each task has a level of difficulty: Beginner, Easy, Medium, Hard, Elite and Master.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: The more tasks you complete, the more activities you can unlock.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: The more content you unlock the more interesting your story will become.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: The more interesting the story the more entertained the ones watching will be.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Not only that, completing tasks also earns you League Points. The number of points earned is dependent on the difficulty of the task.

steps.player: What do I use these 'points' on?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Once you have achieved a certain amount of League Points you can unlock a new Fragment Slot.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: These slots allow you to equip more Fragments and become even stronger.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: League Points can also be used to buy rewards from the Leagues Reward Shop.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Right now, you are playing on your Leagues profile. The Leagues Reward Shop can only be opened on your main profile.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You can access your main profile by switching to any normal Old School RuneScape world. The world switcher in the logout menu can be used to switch worlds.

steps.player: So how many tasks are there?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: More than you'll ever be able to complete, given our limited time here.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: With so many to choose from, it's up to you to decide how your story plays out...

steps.player: Ok... I think I understand what I should do now.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Very good. I knew I made the right choice bringing you to this chapter.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You remember the Relics from the previous event, yes? The sources of great power that let you achieve amazing feats.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Fragments are similar. As the Fragments were created from the Relics, much of their power remains but in a much-diminished form.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: They bestow many different bonuses: from helping you cut wood, to making you a more formidable warrior.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Equipping Fragments will grant you their power.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You can also level up your Fragments, making them even MORE powerful.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Gaining experience as you normally would will level up your Fragments, making them even more useful.

steps.player: How do I find these Fragments?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: I have scattered the Fragments evenly across the world.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Anytime you kill a monster or gain more experience in a particular skill, you'll have a chance to receive a Fragment.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: The harder the enemy or activity, the better chance you'll have.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You will only receive Fragments relevant to the activity, with a few exceptions.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: I know your kind enjoy seeking out treasure. Fragments related to Treasure Trails can come from anywhere.

steps.player: What happens if I try to put the Fragments back together?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: As I said, the Fragments still contain some of their residual Relic energy.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: When enough Fragments are brought back together they will emit the same energy they did when they were whole.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: For example, if you find five Fragments imbued with Last Recall, you can complete the set and gain access to that Relic's full power.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: A sort of 'Set Effect' if you will.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Is there anything else you wish to know?

options.text: How does the content unlock system work?

steps.player: How does the content unlock system work?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: In this iteration of the event I have limited you, at first, to three skills: Thieving, Fishing and Defence.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You can still do simple things like cut trees or mine ore, but doing so will be fruitless, as no experience will be gained.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: In order to gain experience in these skills, you'll need to unlock them by using my Renown.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You gain renown by being entertaining, by completing tasks. The amount of Renown you earn depends on the difficulty of the task.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: When it comes to exceptionally strong creatures, you'll need to unlock the ability to fight them. You can see all locked creatures by opening the unlock interface.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: One final morsal of information you might be interested in. I understand that in previous Leagues you were forced to complete certain 'Quests' in their entirety.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: If you wish, you may spend Sage's Renown to skip through these Quests while still gaining any final rewards. However, be warned thaat I will not offer any gifts to you if you finish these quests by yourself.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You should also know that by completing quests with Sage's Renown, you will not earn any final experience like you would if you finished the quest yourself.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Is there anything else you wish to know.

options.text: How did I get here again?

steps.player: How did I get here again?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: I can retell the story, if you wish me to.
League Intro cutscene replays.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: So be it.

options.text: Will I be rewarded for participating in this event?

steps.player: Will I be rewarded for participating in this event?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: As you progress you'll earn League Points, which will unlock new slots and allow you to equip more Fragments.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: However, when our time in this world is over, you can spend your League Points to buy rewards from the Leagues Reward Shop.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Of course, the real reward for participating will be my master and I sparing your life once the event ends...

steps.player: Are there any other rewards I can earn from this event?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: I see...

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: In my time on the River of Souls I have found that when chapters are concluded their collapsing can be... incomplete.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Therefore, certain items can slip through the cracks, so to say.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: In fact, it's through one of these cracks that I was able to save you from the previous chapter's collapse.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: I collect these lost items from other worlds and keep them with me, should I ever need them one day.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: I'm happy to offer them as an incentive for playing your part in this event.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: The first item is a powerful whip.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: It is imbued with the energy of thousands of lost souls, forever trapped in the bondage of their iron chains.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Each crack releases a deafening howl from the screams of its victims trapped within...

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: The next item is a cannon.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: It's poweered by channelled arcane energy, each explosion teleported into the barrel from a border dimension.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Using a power unknwon, it expels shrapnel that tears through flesh and souls alike.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: There are others of course. You'll be free to trade these rewards to others in your world, or you can keep them. It doesn't matter to me.

steps.player: I see. That all sounds good to me.

steps.text: Right now, you are playing on your Leagues profile. The Leagues Reward Shop can only be opened on your main profile.
You can acess your main profile by switching to any normal Old School RuneScape world. Using world switcher in the logout menu can be used to switch worlds.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: And hero, beware - the Shattered Relic rewards won't be available until the League has ended. You can still buy rewards from previous Leagues, however.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Now, alongside the rewards in the Leagues Reward Shop, there's also League Ranks.

steps.player: League Ranks? How do they work?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: At the end of the League, you will be judged and given a rank. This is based upon the number of League Points you have earned compared to the other participants.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Anyone who earns at least 100 League Points will be eligible for the Bronze rank. The top 80% of participants get the Iron rank. The top 60% get Steel.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: The top 40% get Mithril. The top 20% get Adamant. The top 5% get Rune. The best participants, those who make it to the top 1%, get the Dragon rank!

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: When the League ends, you'll get a trophy based on your rank. These trophies symbolise your performance in the League.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You'll also get League-to-League rewards based on your League Rank.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: League Starter Outfits and League Icons are some of things you can unlock for the next League. Also, any pets you earn in this League will transfer over to the next one.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Finally, I plan to recognise the first heroes to complete particular activities.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You can view the entire list of activities, as well as whether or not someone has completed them, on the board beside me.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Is there anything else you wish to know?

steps.player: Can you tell me how pets work in Leagues?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Of course! If you're lucky enough to obtain a pet during a League, it will automatically be insured for you.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: This means that if you were to ever lose it, you can talk to me and I'll give it back to you. Insurance and reclaiming is all free!

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Additionally, each pet you obtain will be transferred to the next League. It'll be waiting with me for you to reclaim it!

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Return to me once you have some pets and you'll be able to view your collection. Is there anything else you wish to know?

options.text: Do I have any League items to collect?

steps.player: Do I have any items to collect?

steps.text: If the player does not have any items to collect:

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: It doesn't look like you need any League items right now. I'll be here if you ever do.
If the player has an item to collect from The Sage:
You receive an item from the Sage.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Very well. I'll be here if you ever need to know anything about Leagues.

standard.speaker: The Sage
standard.text: Hello mortal. What do you seek?

options.text: What changes have been made for this League?

steps.player: What changes have been made for this League?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Much has changed since the world was shattered. This time, I thought I'd turn the clock back and allow you to Trailblaze once more.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: As before, you'll initially be restricted to the Regions of Misthalin and Karamja. However, as you progress, you'll be able to unlock new areas of your choosing.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Be warned though - you won't be able to unlock every area, so choose wisely.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You must participate as an Iron Man. This means you stand alone and cannot trade with other participants.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: And that's not all. Training skills during the League will grant you substantially more experience than you'd normally expect.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: These experience increases are known as passive effects, which get more generous the higher your Relic tier.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Finally, some quests have been completed for you automatically. Further quests and more will be completed as you unlock the relevant areas.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: I think that covers the basics. Would you like to know more, [player name]?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Is there anything else you need from me?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: In every League, there are a number of tasks for you to complete. Each task has a level of difficulty: Easy, Medium, Hard, Elite and Master.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Completing tasks allows you to access new areas. The more tasks you complete, the more areas become available to unlock.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Not only that, completing tasks also earns you League Points. The number of points earned is dependent on the difficulty of the task.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Once you have achieved a certain amount of League Points you can unlock a new Relic of mine. These are powerful artefacts to help you in this world.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: League Points can also be used to buy rewards from the Leagues Reward Shop.
As we speak, you are playing on your Leagues profile. The Leagues Reward Shop can only be opened on your main profile.
You can access your main profile by switching to any normal Old School RuneScape world. The world switcher in the logout menu can be used to switch worlds.

steps.player: So how many tasks are there?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: More than you'll ever be able to complete, most likely. It's up to you which ones you attempt.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Now, would you like to take a look at the tasks for this League?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Is there anything else you need from me?

options.text: How does the area system work?

steps.player: How does the area system work?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Currently, you are restricted to the Kingdom of Misthalin and the island of Karamja. However, as you progress, you can unlock more areas.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: There are ten different areas in total. However, you can only unlock a maximum of five, including the two you've started with. Choose wisely.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: I give the first two area unlocks to everyone. You can unlock the other three by completing the tasks I've set.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: The more tasks you complete, the more areas you can unlock.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Would you like to take a look at the available areas now?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Is there anything else you need from me?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Relics are powerful artefacts made by me that grant unique abilities for the entire League.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You may even recognise a few from Leagues past.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: The first Relic tier is available to everyone. The others must be unlocked with League Points.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Once you have selected a Relic, your choice can't be changed for the rest of the League. Make your choices carefully.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Is there anything else you need from me?

options.text: Can I claim some Combat rewards?

steps.text: If the player has not completed any Combat Achievements tiers:

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You do not appear to have any combat achievement rewards available to claim.
If the player has completed any Combat Achievements tiers:

steps.player: Can I claim some combat achievement rewards?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Oh, how have you been getting on?

steps.player: I've completed some more Combat Achievement tasks!

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: I can see that. Nice job. You'll be expecting your medium rewards?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: There you go. I've provided you with one of our more modest ancient sword hilts. You'll also have an easier time obtaining medium clues, increased max quantities offered when given boss Slayer tasks, bonus tokens

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: from the Warrior guild and two extra commendation points from each Pest Control game. Additionally, equipping one of my sword hilts at the Barrows will prevent your prayer points from being drained and

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: your Dwarf multicannon can hold five extra cannonballs.

steps.player: Can I claim any league trophies I may of earned from this league?

steps.text: Claiming trophies is temporarily disabled, please try again later.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: As well as letting you unlock new areas, completing tasks in the League will earn you League Points. The more League Points you have, the more Relic tiers you have available.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: However, alongside allowing you to unlock Relics, League Points can also be used to buy rewards from the Leagues Reward Shop.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Oh, all sorts of things. New cosmetic kits, an alternative Home Teleport animation, some rather stylish outfits... and much more.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Many of these rewards can be traded with your fellow mortals, so if you wish, you can earn some money by selling them on. Of course, you might prefer to keep them for yourself instead.

steps.player: I see. That all sounds good to me.

steps.text: Currently, you are playing on your Leagues profile. The Leagues Reward Shop can only be used to buy items on your main profile, although you can still browse the shop within the League.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Would you like to look at the rewards shop?

steps.prompt: Open rewards shop?

steps.text: You can access your main profile by switching to any normal Old School RuneScape world. The world switcher in the logout menu can be used to switch worlds.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You can use this shop to buy previous League rewards, too.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Alongside the rewards in the Leagues Reward Shop, there's also League Ranks.

steps.player: League Ranks? How do they work?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: During the League as you gain more points you will gain a League Rank. This rank can be seen in the Ranks interface.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You currently have the rank: Unranked.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: As you get ranks you will gain access to trophies.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: That's right. Trophies are items that are awarded to you for competing in the League. You can use them to show off your League Rank.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Connected to League Ranks are the League to League rewards. These are unlocked in the next League based upon the League Rank you earn in this one.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: League Starter Outfits and League Icons are some of things you can unlock for the next League. In addition, any pets you earn in this League will transfer over to the next one.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Finally, on top of the tasks for this League, there are some other activities for which I will recognise the first person who completes them.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: You can view the entire list of activities, as well as whether or not someone has completed them, by reading the board beside me.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: My pleasure. Now, is there anything else you need from me?

steps.player: Can you tell me how pets work in Leagues?

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: But of course. If you're lucky enough to obtain a pet during a League, it will automatically be insured for you.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: This means that if you lose it somehow you can talk to me and I'll give it back to you. Insurance and reclaiming is all free of charge.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Additionally, each pet you obtain will be transferred to the next League. I'll take good care of it until you're ready to reclaim it.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Come back to me once you have some pets and you can view your collection. Now, is there anything else you need from me?

options.text: Do I have any League items to collect?

steps.text: I can give you [number] League [item/items] once you free up some space in your inventory.

steps.speaker: The Sage
steps.text: Very well. I'll be here if you ever need to know anything more.

steps.text: If the player doesn't meet of the following criteria: a trowel, a rock pick and a specimen brush in their inventory; leather boots and leather gloves equipped:

steps.npc: Well, you'll need to get your equipment first - it's all there on the tool rack. Use what you learned from your Earth Sciences exams. You'll need to be wearing your leather gloves and boots as well as have access to
your trowel, rock pick and specimen brush.

steps.text: If the player has a trowel, a rock pick and a specimen brush in their inventory and also have leather boots and leather gloves equipped:

steps.npc: I see you have your equipment - well done.

To really give us a hand, you could clean some finds for us. They're mostly done - just some fine work to finish off. Take a find from the pile that the workmen are bringing in, then there are spare tables over there
to clean them on. If you find anything interesting, let us know and we'll see if it's good enough to go on display.
Oh? Let's take a look...

steps.text: If the player has a Clean necklace in their inventory:

steps.npc: Interesting...yes...yes...hmmm.... It looks like it's enchanted.

Oh, I think it's just a benign teleportation spell. I tinker in magic when I'm not doing archaeology. I can teach you how to make more necklaces like this. Amazing that they had this kind of knowledge back then.

steps.player: That would be good. Where is the teleport to?

steps.npc: Hmm...all the indications are that it's somewhere to the east of us, but I'm not sure how far. Perhaps it was a teleport back to Saranthium. Let me just take a closer look.

steps.text: The archaeologist takes the necklace and turns it over in his hands, studying it closely.

The archaeologist shows you the techniques for this particular spell, which requires five fire runes arranged around one cosmic rune - and level 49 Magic - then casting the spell on a crafted ruby necklace of your
own.  You can make enchanted ruby necklaces.

steps.player: So I just make a ruby necklace and use five fire runes and one cosmic rune to enchant it.

steps.npc: Yes, indeed. Well done, youngster, thanks for helping us.

If the player is showing the Old coin for the first time:

steps.player: I've cleaned this old coin - is it of any use?

steps.npc: Oh my! What a wonderful find! If this is what I believe it to be, it would allow us to date the Dig Site city.
And look here, it has the name of the city too! Saranthium! That must be during the Saradominist occupation. This is a wonderful find. Please take it and place it in display case 45.

steps.text: If the player is showing the Old coin after being told to put it in a display case:

steps.player: No, I'll go do that now

steps.text: If the player is showing the Old coin after putting it in a display case:

steps.player: I've cleaned this old coin - is it of any use?

steps.npc: You've already shown me one of those, but it was in better condition. It's in the display case over there. You can pop this one in the finds crate over in the corner.

steps.text: If the player has an Ancient coin, and doesn't have any of the above cleaned finds in their inventory:
If the player is showing the Ancient coin for the first time:

steps.player: I found this really old coin - is it of any use?

steps.npc: What have we here?

Oh! This is very interesting...and confusing at the same time. This coin means that the city that we're excavating on the Digsite - Saranthium - was actually inhabited much, much earlier by followers of Zamorak,
at which time, the city was known as Senntisten.

This is a most remarkable discovery, as we have other evidence indicating that Zarosian followers were resident before the Saradominists took over, but it also seems that Zamorakian forces used it during a battle of some
sort. Still, it allows us to roughly date when the city changed from following Zaros and Zamorak to following Saradomin. Put it in display case 44.

options.text: Wow how do you finish each others sentences like that?

steps.player: Wow how do you finish each others sentences like that?

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: We are a gestalt entity. We each have our own body, but our minds

steps.npc: are united and we all think as one. Well except when Hallak doth leaveth

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: the toilet seat up.

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: That's the way it's meant to be!

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: Ok we're a mostly gestalt entity. We each have own body, but

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: our minds are united, except for some parts which aren't. We mostly

steps.npc: think as one.

steps.player: That doesn't really have the same ring to it.

options.text: What manner of beings are you?

steps.player: What manner of beings are you?

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: We are the spirits of the river Elid, many ages ago we used to be mindless wandering spirits, with little mind or purpose, we were here even in the first age. Then great Elidinis came to the desert and bound us to her

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: river, we've

steps.npc: become one with the river and over the centuries become full of the power of Elidinis that was in her river. We are now her trusted guardians of the Elid, we can control the river and anything which happens
near the river we know about.

options.text: Wow how do you finish each others sentences like that?

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: Elidinis is one of a group of gods, known as the Menaphite Pantheon. She is wife of their leader Tumeken. She is the Menaphite goddess of growth and fertility and goddess of the river.

options.text: Don't many other towns not follow Elidinis?

steps.player: Don't many other towns not follow Elidinis though? Why did you pick on Nardah specifically?

steps.npc: It is true many do not follow Elidinis, but there is more to the story than that. The answers

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: lie in the story of Nardarine. Wouldst thou likest to hear the telling of this tale? It is not a short one.

options.text: Yes I would like to hear this story.

steps.player: Yes I would like to hear this story.

steps.npc: Nardarine came from a town towards the north side of the desert which does not exist today. This was in the third age in the time thou callest

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: the God Wars. Her town was once controlled by Saradomin, but there was a great battle there between Saradominist and Zamorakian forces which pretty much levelled the town

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: to the ground. Most of the human citizens perished. Nardarine had the wisdom to escape into the desert before the fighting got really serious and thus survived. However she found herself wandering lost and alone in

steps.npc: the desert. She prayed to Saradomin for help, but Saradomin was too concerned with the loss of a strategic outpost to worry about the fate of one small human. Nardarine had wandered towards the realm of

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: the Menaphite God Pantheon. Elidinis heard the prayers of Nardarine, she took pity on the wandering human and came unto her with water. 'Oh great goddess' exclaimed Nardarine 'I wish not to be involved more in

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: the wars of the gods for they have caused me so much hardship already, I wish only for a quiet life somewhere'. Elidinis replied 'I will grant this unto thee on the condition that thou swearest to forever pay fealty and

steps.npc: homage to me and I grant this also unto thine descendents as long as they too will pay an oath of fealty and homage to me'. Nardarine said 'If you would grant me a safe home, with a

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: supply of food and water, then I would surely do this for it is more than any other God would seem to do for me'. Then Elidinis made

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: a spring of water appear at Nardarines feet and brought stone from below the sand so that she

steps.npc: might have something to build with. She called forth camels which have many uses and taste good in kebabs. She then provided Nardarine with a statuette in her image to worship. Nardarine built up her home. Over

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: time more refugees from the God Wars found Nardarine's home. Nardarine let them stay with her as long as they did make the same oath as her. Hence the town of Nardah was born and Nardarine lived the rest

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: of her days in the peacefulness that she craved. The oath was passed down the generations for many ages, but now seemeth to be forgotten. Now maybe thou canst see why we are not best pleased.

reward you.

steps.player: Tell me more about the Easy rewards please!

steps.player: Tell me more about the Medium rewards please!

after-a-soul-s-bane.player: Hello again. Can you tell me about this training area?

after-a-soul-s-bane.npc: Of course, if you enter the rift next to me, you'll find a large dungeon filled with four kinds of beasts. You will recognise them from the gauntlet in which you helped me.

after-a-soul-s-bane.player: OK, I didn't have too many problems beating them before.

after-a-soul-s-bane.npc: You might find it harder now! At least one is bound to cause you some sort of threat. Be careful! There isn't much in the way of items or treasure down there, it's purely for practicing your combat!

standard.npc: Greetings. What can I do for you?

steps.npc: I'm conducting important business here for the Kourend Council.

steps.player: Is there anything I can help you with?

steps.npc: There is something I could use some help with. I'm here on behalf of the Kourend Council to investigate some unusual happenings in Port Piscarilius.
Port Piscarilius is home to various gangs. They're a nuisance, but up until now we haven't had much trouble in dealing with them.
A new gang calling themselves the Saviours of Kourend has recently formed. That's not surprising as gangs come and go all of the time, but this one is different.
The Saviours of Kourend have been absorbing many of the other gangs. Within a few weeks they've already become the largest gang in Kourend and more join them each day.
The talk amongst the people is that it's all down to their leader, a mysterious figure known only as the Queen of Thieves.

steps.player: Nice name. Why doesn't the ruler of Port Piscarilius do something about this?

steps.npc: Shauna Piscarilius is the ruler of Port Piscarilius, but she spends most of her time galavanting around in that boat of hers rather than looking after her home.

steps.player: Fair enough. So what do you need me for?

steps.npc: Well my original plan was to infiltrate the gang to get close to the Queen and capture her. However, I've been unable to make any progress. Apparently, I don't look the part.

steps.player: Yeah not sure what that's all about. You clearly fit right in here.

steps.npc: Quite right. They're quite insistent though, so someone else will need to give it a go. You look like you might be just the type they're after.

steps.player: What are you trying to say?

steps.npc: That you look poor.
Anyway if you're up for the task you'll need to infiltrate the Saviours of Kourend, find the Queen of Thieves, apprehend her and then bring her to me.
So are you up for it?

steps.text: The Queen of Thieves has been started.

steps.npc: Excellent. The Saviours of Kourend must have their headquarters somewhere nearby. You should ask around town and see if anyone knows where they are. Good luck.
Fair enough. I'll be here if you change your mind.
Although it's called a kingdom, Great Kourend hasn't actually had a king for many years. These days Kourend is a republic and it is ruled by the Kourend Council.
The Council consists of four councillors who are elected by the people every four years. The current councillors are Councillor Hughes, Councillor Unkar, Councillor Orson and Councillor Andrews.

steps.player: I see. So what are you investigating?

steps.npc: Port Piscarilius is home to various gangs. They're a nuisance, but up until now we haven't had much trouble in dealing with them.

steps.text: If the player does not have the requirements to start The Queen of Thieves:

steps.npc: Well there is something I could use some help with. However, you're not really the person I need for this task.

steps.text: If the player does have the requirements to start The Queen of Thieves:

steps.npc: Well there is something I could use some help with. I'm here on behalf of the Kourend Council to investigate some unusual happenings in Port Piscarilius.
Very well. Until next time.

during-the-queen-of-thieves-before-findi.npc: Greetings. What can I do for you?

during-the-queen-of-thieves-after-findin.npc: Greetings. What can I do for you?

steps.npc: Very well. How goes things?

steps.player: I haven't had any luck finding the Queen of Thieves. However, I've come across this letter which you might find interesting.

steps.text: Tomas reads the letter.

steps.npc: Blimey! Forget the Queen of Thieves. If this letter is to be believed, Councillor Hughes is working with those vile Disciples of Yama. I must report this to the council immediately.

options.text: Great! So can I have a reward?

steps.player: Great! So can I have a reward?

steps.npc: You've done a great service to the people of Kourend. As I'm sure you know, there is no greater reward than the satisfaction of a job well done.
Now be on your way. I have a lot of work to do.

options.text: What do you know of the Disciples of Yama?

steps.player: What do you know of the Disciples of Yama?

steps.npc: They're a group of deranged cultists that worship some sort of demon. They're not a big threat compared to the lizardmen, but they're still an enemy to Kourend.

steps.player: And Councillor Hughes is helping them? That's not good.

steps.npc: Indeed. I must report this to the Council immediately.

steps.player: So can I have a reward?

steps.npc: You've done a great service to the people of Kourend. As I'm sure you know, there is no greater reward than the satisfaction of a job well done.
Now be on your way. I have a lot of work to do.

after-the-queen-of-thieves-and-before-a-.npc: Very well thank you. My work in bringing down Councillor Hughes means that I'm finally starting to get the recognition that I deserve.
Yes, yes, very good job. I'll make sure to mention you in my acceptance speech when I'm voted in as her replacement.

after-completing-a-kingdom-divided.npc: I'm ruined. Everything was perfect under the Council, but now I'm right back in the dirt again.

after-completing-a-kingdom-divided.player: You were very close to the Council. You should be glad you got to keep your job at all.

after-completing-a-kingdom-divided.npc: But I didn't keep my job. Now I spend every day doing boring administrative work. It's a nightmare.

after-completing-a-kingdom-divided.player: Come now Tomas, it can't be all bad. Show a little enthusiasm.

standard.player: Say, aren't you a bit tall for a dwarf?

standard.npc: Was there anything in particular you wanted?

steps.npc: I have nothing to do for you, I'm afraid. Ask around town, though, there are always people who need some work done around here.

options.text: No, I just like talking to strangers.

steps.player: No, I just like talking to strangers.

steps.npc: Well I don't.

steps.player: So how's life as a pirate?

steps.npc: What kind of question is that? How's life as a... I dunno. Whatever it is that you do for a living.
What does that entail then?

steps.player: Mostly killing things for money and delivering items around the planet for people.

steps.npc: So how's that life?
Well, there you go.

steps.player: Aren't you a little short for a pirate?

steps.npc: My mother was a gnome. Apparently it was a very painful birth.

steps.player: More info than I wanted, thanks!
You know, I've always wondered what life as a pirate actually entails.

steps.npc: Well, at the moment it mostly involves being asked random questions by a stowaway.

steps.player: I'm not a stowaway! I was invited aboard! By Lokar! Ask him!

steps.npc: Hey, whatever [love/pal]. Just make sure the captain doesn't catch you, pirates don't like stowaways much.
Ah, good day to you [milady/sirrah]! Your face is unfamiliar, did you perhaps join us aboard the ship at Lunar Isle?

steps.player: No, Lokar offered me a lift in Rellekka actually.

steps.npc: Oh, really? You don't look like a Fremennik to me!

steps.player: Well... I kind of am, and I kind of aren't. It's a long story.

steps.npc: Sorry I don't have time to hear it then! See you around young fremennik-who-is-not-really-a-fremennik!
You think this is cold? Up by Acheron it gets so cold that when you talk you see the words freeze in the air in front of you!
Nah, not really. I was exaggerating for humourous effect. It is very very cold though!
Hello to you too.

steps.player: Yar! We be pirates, yar! Avast, ye scurvy land-lubbing lychee!

steps.npc: Please don't talk like that, it is extremely irritating.
Also, please don't call me a lychee, whatever that may be.
ARGH! SOUND THE ALARM! STOWAWAY ON BOARD! STOWAWAY ON BOARD!

steps.player: No! I'm not a stowaway! Honest! I was invited here!

steps.npc: Oh, sorry, my mistake then.
You must admit you do look a lot like a stowaway though.

steps.player: Why, what do they usually look like?

steps.npc: Erm... I've never actually met one...
Hello.
It's what it says on my pay-packet at the end of the month.

steps.player: How's that working out for you?

steps.npc: Pretty good so far. All the grog and loot that we can plunder, plus full medical including dental.
Not as such. If any of us get sick we kidnap a doctor and don't let him go until we're better.
You'd be surprised what an incentive for expert health care that is.
Hello there. So what brings you aboard the Lady Zay?

steps.player: Well, I was planning on visiting the Moon Clan, but I have to say your ship is very impressive.

steps.npc: Aye, she's a beauty alright! The Lady Zay has been my home for many hard months, through storm and sun, and she always gets us to here we were headed!

steps.player: Yes, she's certainly one of the finest boats I've seen on my travels!

steps.npc: That she is [lad/lass], that she is.
Sorry, can't stop, the Captain will have my guts for garters if he catches me slacking off talking to the stowaway.

steps.player: I'm not a stowaway! I was invited aboard!

steps.npc: Yeah, whatever [guy/lady], it doesn't really matter who you are I'll get in trouble!

We'll hold onto yer rake, yer seed dibber, yer spade, yer secateurs, yer waterin' can and yer trowel - but mind it's not one of them fancy trowels only archaeologists use!
We'll take a few buckets off yer hands too, and even yer compost, supercompost an' ultracompost! Also plant cure vials.
Aside from that, if ye hands me yer farming produce, I can mebbe change it into banknotes for ye.

options.text: Can you give me any farming advice?

steps.player: Can you give me any farming advice?

steps.npc: You can buy all the farming tools from farming shops, which can be found close to the allotments.
Supercompost is far better than normal compost, but more expensive to make. You need to rot the right type of item; show me an item, and I'll tell you if it's super- compostable or not.
Tree seeds must be grown in a plantpot of soil into a sapling, and then transferred to a tree patch to continue growing to adulthood.
You can put up to ten potatoes, cabbages or onions in vegetable sacks, although you can't have a mix in the same sack.
You can fill plantpots with soil from any empty patch, if you have a gardening trowel.
Bittercap mushrooms can only be grown in a special patch in Morytania, near the Mort Myre swamp. There the ground is especially dank and suited to growing poisonous fungii.
Vegetables, hops and flowers need constant watering - if you ignore my advice, you will sooner or later find yourself in possession of a dead farming patch.
You don't have to buy all your plantpots you know, you can make them yourself on a pottery wheel. If you're good enough at crafting, that is.
If you want to make your own sacks and baskets you'll need to use the loom that's near the Farming shop in Falador. If you're good enough at crafting, that is.

There are many Farming areas out there. I know of Elstan's area near Falador, Dantaera's area near Catherby, Kragen's area near Ardougne, Lyra's area in Morytania, Marisi's area in Hosidius and Alan's area in
the Farming Guild. That said, I'm sure there's plenty more that I don't know about.
If you want to grow fruit trees you could try a few places: Catherby, Brimhaven, Gnome Stronghold and the Farming Guild all have fruit tree patches.
You can put up to five tomatoes, strawberries, apples, bananas or oranges into a fruit basket, although you can't have a mix in the same basket.
There is a special patch for growing Belladonna - I believe that it is somewhere near Draynor Manor, where the ground is a tad 'unblessed'.
Applying compost to a patch will not only reduce the chance that your crops will get diseased, but you will also grow more crops to harvest.
The only way to cure a bush or tree of disease is to prune away the diseased leaves with a pair of secateurs. For all other crops I would just apply some plant-cure.

Hops are good for brewing ales. I believe there's a brewery up in Keldagrim somewhere, and I've heard rumours that a place called Phasmatys used to be good for that type of thing. 'Fore they all died, of course.
Don't just throw away your weeds after you've raked a patch - put them in a compost bin and make some compost.
