historical-dialogue-regular-players.speaker: Town crier
historical-dialogue-regular-players.text: Hear ye! Hear ye! Player Moderators massive help to RuneSc-

historical-dialogue-regular-players.speaker: Town crier
historical-dialogue-regular-players.text: Oh, hello citizen. Are you here to find out about Player Moderators? Or perhaps would you like to know about the laws of the land?

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Of course. What would you like to know?

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Player Moderators are normal players of the game, just like you. However, since they have shown themselves to be trustworthy and active reporters, they have been invited by Jagex to monitor the game and

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: take appropriate action when they see rule breaking. You can spot a Player Moderator in game by looking at the chat screen - when a Player Moderator speaks, a silver crown appears to the left of their name.

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Remember, if there's not silver crown there, they are not a Player Moderator!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to know?

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Player Moderators, or 'P-mods', have the ability to mute rule breakers and Jagex view their reports as a priority so that action is taken as quickly as possible. P- Mods also have access to the Player Moderator Centre.

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Within the Centre are tools to help them Moderate Old School RuneScape. These tools include dedicated forums, the Player Moderator Guidelines and the Player Moderator Code of Conduct.

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to know?

options.text: How do I become a Player Moderator?

steps.player: How do I become a Player Moderator?

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Jagex picks players who spend their time and effort to help better the Old School RuneScape community. To increase your chances of becoming a Player Moderator:

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Keep your account secure! This is very important, as a player with poor security will never be a P-Mod. Read our Security Tips for more information.

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Play by the rules! The rules of Old School RuneScape are enforced for a reason, to make the game a fair and enjoyable environment for all.

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Report accurately! When Jagex consider an account for review they look for quality, not quantity. Ensure your reports are of a high quality by following the report guidelines.

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Be excellent to each other! Treat others as you would want to be treated yourself. Respect your fellow player.

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to know?

options.text: What can Player Moderators not do?

steps.player: What can Player Moderators not do?

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: P-Mods cannot ban your account - they can only report offences. Jagex then take action based on the evidence received. If you lose your password or get scammed by another player, P-Mods cannot help you

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: get your account back. All they can do is recommend you to go to Customer Support. They cannot retrieve any items you may have lost and receive no free items from Jagex for helping moderate the game. They are

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: players who give their efforts to help the community out of the goodness of their hearts! P-mods do not work for Jagex and so cannot make you a Moderator, or recommend other accounts to become moderators. If

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: you wish to become a Moderator, please feel free to ask me how!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to know?

options.text: Tell me about the Rules of Conduct.

steps.player: Tell me about the Rules of Conduct.

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: At once. Take a look at my book here...

options.text: Can you give me a handy tip please?

steps.player: Can you give me a handy tip please?

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Did you know most skills have right click 'Make-X' options to help you train faster?

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Make your recovery questions and answers hard to guess but easy to remember.

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Don't use your RuneScape password on other sites. Keep your account safe!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: If you think someone knows your password - change it!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: The squirrels! The squirrels are coming! Noooo, get them out of my head!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Did you know you burn food less often on the range in Lumbridge castle than other ranges?

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Players can not trim armour. Don't fall for this popular scam!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Feeling harassed? Don't forget your ignore list can be especially useful if a player seems to be picking on you!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: If you're lost and have no idea where to go, use the Home Teleport spell for free!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: If you see someone breaking the rules, report them!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Did you know? Superheat Item means you never fail to smelt ore!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Did you know that at high levels of Runecrafting you get more than one rune per essence?

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Never lend your items out unless you expect them not to come back.

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Never question a penguin.

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Melee armour actually gives you disadvantages when using magic attacks. It may be better to take off your armour entirely!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: If the chat window is moving too quickly to report a player accurately, run to a quiet spot and review the chat at your leisure!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Take time to check the second trade window carefully. Don't be scammed!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Did you know having a bank pin can help secure your valuable items?

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Did you know that mithril equipment is very light?

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: There are no cheats in RuneScape! Never visit websites promising otherwise!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Jagex will never e-mail you. Do not believe any e-mails that claim to be from us.

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: If you're stuck on a skill, talk to the Lumbridge Tutors for help and tips.

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Did you know that you can wear a shield with a crossbow?

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Beware of players trying to lure you into the wilderness. Your items cannot be returned if you lose them!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: If a player isn't sure of the rules, send them to me! I'll be happy to remind them!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Never tell your password to anyone, not even your best friend!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Be careful when fighting wizards! Wearing heavy armour can lower your Magic resistance!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to know?

historical-dialogue-player-moderators.speaker: Town crier
historical-dialogue-player-moderators.text: Hear ye! Hear ye! Player Moderators massive help to Rune... Oh great, a P-mod! I know all about the great job you guys do, would you like me to prove my extensive knowledge to you?!

options.text: Can you show me the Guidelines please?

steps.player: Can you show me the Guidelines please?

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Of course, but I can't let you keep it - I've only got a few copies!

options.text: Do you have a copy of the Code of Conduct?

steps.player: Do you have a copy of the Code of Conduct?

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Oh yes, but I can't let you keep it - I've only a few copies!

options.text: Can you give me a moderating tip please?

steps.player: Can you give me a moderating tip please?

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Add other Player Moderators to your friends list for quick advice and moral support in-game. It does help!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: To avoid reporting the wrong player, add an offender to your friends list, switch your public chat to friends and then use your right-click report from there. Easy!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Did you know that Free-to-Play P-mods CAN visit the moderator forums, by logging into the regular forums at the top right hand side of the forum screen, despite it saying Members only.

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Don't be tempted to report anything you didn't see, no matter how much you trust the player who is informing you.

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Don't eat something messy when on a first date - it won't look good!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Don't forget to add the mute if needed, before selecting the report category. This cuts down on those duplicate reports for one player.

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Feeling harassed? Don't forget your ignore list can be especially useful if a player seems to be picking on you!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: The forums are the best place to keep abreast of any procedure changes that might not yet be included in the Player Mod guidelines!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Got players asking you to unban them or help them retrieve a stolen or hacked account? There's nothing you can do so just send them to the Customer Support Team. If they think you can help, send them to me; I'll

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: put them straight!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Have the P-Mod Oracle open in a separate window when playing Old School RuneScape - that way you'll always have the most up-to-date guidelines to hand!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: If the chat is scrolling too fast for you to see that suspect line you want to double check, just run up a ladder or to a quieter spot to stop the chat screen scrolling. Then you can scroll back and read that

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: suspect line and judge the situation in your own time!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: If the chat window is moving too quickly to report a player accurately, run to a quiet spot and review the chat at your leisure!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: If a player isn't sure of the rules, send them to me! I'll be happy to remind them!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: If you're a new mod, don't forget to read the guidelines before you log into the game! If you've been a P-mod for a while, why not have another read of them to refresh your memory and to get up to date

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: with any changes you may have missed!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: If you've got a player asking you questions about P- mods, feel free to send them to me; I can answer questions about P-mods for you!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: If you get harassed by a player in game, don't take it personally - the player is reacting to your silver crown, not to you!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: If you notice a player trying to buy something common for an extremely high price, look about and see if there's someone else selling the same item for a much lower price. Chances are they're team scamming. If so,

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: write their names down and send your J-mod curators a query!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: If you see a player abusing a bug in game, there's no need to report the player, just submit a bug report via the in-game report form.

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: An important part of being a P-mod is to act as an ambassador for the game. Keeping your cool even when faced with the rudest players goes a long way towards this!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: It's always better to report in secret. Telling a player that you are about to report them rarely makes you a friend, and can often lead to a player being offensive to you!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Make sure you log out of the game and the forums whenever you leave your device. Don't allow others to see confidential info!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Never answer questions if you feel the answer will breach confidentiality.

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: The P-mod forums are your friend! They're the best place to talk to and meet other P-mods and are absolutely packed with useful advice!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Remember, if in doubt, report without a mute! It's very frustrating not to be able to speak if you're innocent!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Remember, if offensive language has been completely filtered out then there's no need to report or mute it!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Think twice before applying that mute. Will it really prevent further damage from surrounding players?

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Use the Jagex PMod team if you need to - they're there to help!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: You'll be amazed how often a bit of humour can diffuse a potentially unpleasant situation, before it becomes too serious.

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Your J-mods are there to help you. If you ever need their advice, send them a query. They are always very happy to help. Don't be afraid to use them!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Your Player Moderator identity must never be revealed on the regular Old School RuneScape forums. However, you're more than welcome to chat about all aspects of being a Player Moderator in the official

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Player Moderator forums!

steps.speaker: Town crier
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to know?
other

standard.npc: Can I help you?

steps.npc: I'm one of Trader Stan's crew. We are all part of one of the largest fleet of trading and sailing vessels to ever sail the seas.
If you want to get to a port in a hurry, then you can charter one of our ships to take you there, if the price is right...

steps.player: So, where exactly can I go with your ships?

steps.npc: We run ships all over the place. Port Sarim, Catherby, Brimhaven, Musa Point and Port Khazard are just a few of our many destinations!

steps.player: If you visit a lot of ports, I take it you have some exotic stuff to trade?

steps.npc: We certainly do! We have access to items bought and sold from around the world. Would you like to take a look? Or would you like to charter a ship?

options.text: Yes, let's see what you're trading.

steps.player: Yes, let's see what you're trading.

options.text: Yes, I would like to charter a ship.
Isn't it tricky to sail about in those clothes?

steps.player: Isn't it tricky to sail about in those clothes?

steps.npc: Tricky? Tricky!
With all due credit, Trader Stan is a great employer, but he insists we wear the latest in high fashion even when sailing.
Do you have even the slightest idea how tricky it is to sail in this stuff?
Some of us tried tearing it and arguing that it was too fragile to wear when on a boat, but he just had it enchanted to re-stitch itself.
It's hard to hate him when we know how much he shells out on this gear, but if I fall overboard because of this getup one more time, I'm going to quit.
Yes... Anyway, would you like to take a look at our exotic wares from around the world? Or would you like to charter a ship?

options.text: So what are you training these tortoises to do?

steps.npc: Tortoises are naturally pacifistic animals that eat nothing but cabbages. I am required to beat those peaceful tendencies out of the softies and turn them into hardened battle-trained killers.
Firstly I acclimatise them to excessive aural stimulation and simple physical confrontation.

steps.player: You shout at them and beat them with sticks?

steps.npc: Of course. Then I re-educate them to become comfortable with riders and military combat situations.

steps.player: You sit on their backs and prod them with sharp pointy things.

steps.npc: If you like.

steps.player: Doesn't seem very fair on the tortoises.

steps.npc: This is War! Fairness is a luxury of the weak.

options.text: Where did these tortoises come from?

steps.npc: Isn't it obvious? Surely even to your untrained eye that giant tortoises are the perfect mobile armoured field unit?

options.text: So what are you training these tortoises to do?

Trouble is they take a lot of skill and time to breed, so we're only just getting them battle ready.

steps.npc: You can buy all the farming tools from farming shops, which can be found close to the allotments.
Applying compost to a patch will not only reduce the chance that your crops will get diseased, but you will also grow more crops to harvest.
Supercompost is far better than normal compost, but more expensive to make. You need to rot the right type of item; show me an item, and I'll tell you if it's super- compostable or not.
Don't just throw away your weeds after you've raked a patch - put them in a compost bin and make some compost.
The only way to cure a bush or tree of disease is to prune away the diseased leaves with a pair of secateurs. For all other crops I would just apply some plant-cure.
Vegetables, hops and flowers need constant watering - if you ignore my advice, you will sooner or later find yourself in possession of a dead farming patch.
There is a special patch for growing Belladonna - I believe that it is somewhere near Draynor Manor, where the ground is a tad 'unblessed'.
Bittercap mushrooms can only be grown in a special patch in Morytania, near the Mort Myre swamp. There the ground is especially dank and suited to growing poisonous fungii.
You can put up to five tomatoes, strawberries, apples, bananas or oranges into a fruit basket, although you can't have a mix in the same basket.
You can put up to ten potatoes, cabbages or onions in vegetable sacks, although you can't have a mix in the same sack.
If you want to make your own sacks and baskets you'll need to use the loom that's near the Farming shop in Falador. If you're good enough at crafting, that is.
Tree seeds must be grown in a plantpot of soil into a sapling, and then transferred to a tree patch to continue growing to adulthood.
You can fill plantpots with soil from any empty patch, if you have a gardening trowel.
You don't have to buy all your plantpots you know, you can make them yourself on a pottery wheel. If you're good enough at crafting, that is.
If you want to grow fruit trees you could try a few places: Catherby, Brimhaven, Gnome Stronghold and the Farming Guild all have fruit tree patches.

Hops are good for brewing ales. I believe there's a brewery up in Keldagrim somewhere, and I've heard rumours that a place called Phasmatys used to be good for that type of thing. 'Fore they all died, of course.

There are many Farming areas out there. I know of Elstan's area near Falador, Dantaera's area near Catherby, Kragen's area near Ardougne, Lyra's area in Morytania, Marisi's area in Hosidius and Alan's area in
the Farming Guild. That said, I'm sure there's plenty more that I don't know about.

steps.npc: No. We sent a scouting party in that direction, when we first established our camp. Some of the men got lost in the swamps. Eventually we listed them as dead.
Then suddenly they returned, with a wild gleam in their eyes, raving about gods and snakes and all kinds of madness.
We had to drive them out, in case their condition infected the rest of the troops. Their wives will be given a full widow pension when we return home.

steps.npc: TzHaar are born from eggs incubated in lava pools. When hatched, we retain memories. Memories and knowledge passed on from ancestors who returned to the lava.
When TzHaar hatch, some memories are lost. Those about earliest ancestors are not retained. We experiment.
This here was once our largest birthing pool. We use it for experiment. We increased the depth at which eggs are incubated. Over time, newly hatched TzHaar had more memories of lost history!
But we kept pushing. We wanted answers, but we went too deep.
Eventually the pool collapsed into a sinkhole. At the bottom we found some sort of ancient incubation chamber, from before earliest memories. We now call it the Inferno.
We decide to experiment more. We take eggs from creatures in Fight Cave and incubate them down there.
When eggs hatched, we see that it was not good decision. They were bigger and stronger, and fought each other for dominance.

steps.text: If the player has sacrificed a fire cape:

steps.npc: Instead of knowledge, we now have chamber of dangerous creatures, and they're not alone. Another being lives in the Inferno, one more powerful than any TzHaar.
We do not know where he came from. All we know is that TzKal-Zuk is hungry. Hungry for memories, memories beyond the Inferno.
We think his goal is the city itself. Lots of TzHaar memories here for him. Luckily, he is trapped in prison down there, and we are keeping him at bay by offering sacrifices.

historical-dialogue.npc: We pushed it too far! JalYt would not understand. The memories, we needed them. Now big Inferno.

steps.npc: This is our birthing pool. TzHaar are born from eggs incubated in this large pool here.
When hatched, we retain memories. Memories and knowledge passed on from ancestors who returned to the lava.

steps.player: Something doesn't seem right... There's a large opening.

steps.npc: We went too far... way too far, we need the memories. JalYt would not understand.

steps.player: Please help me to understand then.

steps.npc: We TzHaar have special ability. When incubated in lava, a hatched TzHaar retains knowledge and memories of ancestors who returned to the lava.
Not all memories though, those about earliest ancestors were not being retained. We experiment.
We increased the depth at which the eggs are incubated. Over time this worked, newly hatched TzHaar had more memories of lost history!

steps.player: That sounds fantastic though, uncovering the past to determine where your species originated?

steps.npc: Yes, but you JalYt do not understand, we kept pushing it. We wanted answers, but too deep we went.
Eventually the pool collapsed into a sink hole, huge Inferno there. This was big ancient incubation chamber.
We decide to experiment. We take eggs from creatures in Fight Cave and incubate them.
We hatched eggs in there and it was not a good decision. They were so different, bigger, stronger and fought each other for dominance.

steps.npc: We can only guess one day he will want to scale up into the city himself. We are keeping him at bay by offering sacrifices for him to feast on.

steps.npc: We fear not. But we hoped you, with your fancy JalYt weaponry, would be able to help hold back his creatures. You proved your commitment by sacrificing your fire cape.

standard.text: I worry that they can't see our guards very clearly in the dark. It is important for a guard to be seen.

standard.npc: You have a point. But I don't think red would be the best colour. It is the colour of blood, so it might give the wrong impression.

standard.speaker: Ur-lun
standard.text: What colour do you suggest, then?

standard.npc: I suggest green. I have heard that the plants that grow on the surface are mostly green, so surface-dwellers might find that colour soothing.

standard.speaker: Ur-lun
standard.text: No, I disagree. Guards should not be soothing, they should be seen as formidable. Red will give the correct impression.

standard.npc: Oh, hello surface-dweller. We were just discussing some council business.

steps.player: Do you want me to pick an armour colour for you?

steps.text: No, thank you. We don't let any one single goblin make decisions, and certainly not an outsider!

steps.npc: But we could do with an opinion. What colour do you think is best?

steps.speaker: Ur-lun
steps.text: Thank you, surface-dweller. That's what I'll be recommending in the next meeting.

steps.npc: Thank you, surface-dweller. That's what I'll be recommending in the next meeting.

options.text: I think the guards are fine as they are

steps.player: I think the guards are fine as they are.

options.text: I think I've been here before...

steps.player: I think I've been here before...

steps.speaker: Ur-lun
steps.text: Oh? How so?

steps.player: This is a lot like a conversation I had with some goblins on the surface.

steps.npc: Really? Which armour colour did they pick?

steps.player: They ended up with the same armour colour that they started with!

steps.speaker: Ur-lun
steps.text: You know, I think that's probably what we'll end up doing.

standard.speaker: Ur-zek
standard.text: I think that Ur-tag is trying to move too quickly. First, he opens the city to humans, and now he wants to invite these dwarves into the city. I think we should exercise more caution in dealing with surface-dwellers.

standard.npc: The dwarves are not surface dwellers. They live in an underground city, like us!

standard.speaker: Ur-zek
standard.text: Why does that mean we can trust them? Are you forgetting the machine that nearly destroyed us was made by dwarves?

standard.npc: You shouldn't judge all dwarves because of that!

standard.speaker: Ur-zek
standard.text: I know that! And I know not all humans want to kill us, but I still never thought we should open the city.

standard.npc: You can't deny it's done some good. Think of how happy everyone is trying surface foods in the market!

standard.speaker: Ur-zek
standard.text: I'm not denying that, I just don't think it's worth the risk. Our guards have their work cut out as it is, protecting us from renegade humans, without having to worry about dwarves as well.

standard.npc: Please don't be offended by my friend's attitude, surface-dweller. I'm sure you understand why we need to be cautious.

steps.npc: But I haven't given you anything recently.

steps.player: Yes you did. You gave me a reward for helping your client.

steps.npc: Client? I don't...

steps.text: Veos suddenly jumps.

steps.npc: Ah I remember now. Apologies friend, my mind isn't what it once was.

steps.text: If the player isn't missing Kharedst's memoirs:

steps.npc: I do remember rewarding you. I'm afraid I don't have anything else for you though.

steps.text: If the player is missing Kharedst's memoirs:

steps.npc: I do have some things for you. Enjoy!

using-items-on-veos-using-kharedst-s-mem.player: What's this old book you gave me?

using-items-on-veos-using-kharedst-s-mem.npc: Ah that. I bought it at an auction a while back. Apparently, it belonged to the daughter of King Kharedst IV, the final king of Great Kourend.

using-items-on-veos-using-kharedst-s-mem.player: Why did you give it to me?

using-items-on-veos-using-kharedst-s-mem.npc: I'd hoped it might have some interesting information in it. Most of the pages are missing though so I have no use for it. I thought you might be able to find something to do with it.

using-items-on-veos-using-wolf-bones-on-.npc: These remind me of a pet I once had. Please... put them away.

options.text: Would you feel comfortable sharing your story?

steps.player: Would you feel comfortable sharing your story?

steps.npc: I once had a wolf, [player name]. His name was Copper. He was loyal. Brave... Gentle. He'd wear this beautiful crimson red collar.
One day, I was travelling on the mainland, nearby a tribe of Fremenniks. Not exactly a spring chicken at this point, my own wolf was pushing 19...

steps.player: 19 years old? That's an incredible amount of time for a wolf to live!

steps.npc: Indeed. Sadly, a group of feral foxes ambushed us. I fought back, along with Copper, though he took wounds that even a young wolf would struggle dealing with.
I ran, [player name]... Like a coward.
I did not... I searched for days, but I was unable to find even his collar.

options.text: I can help! I'll search for Copper's collar.

steps.player: I can help! I'll search for Copper's collar. I'm sure I can find the fox that has it...

steps.npc: Truly? You'd do that for me? Thank you so much, [player name]. I can't thank you enough! My heart's been filled with regret ever since it happened... and I think having a small part of Copper back, would make me complete again.

steps.player: I'll return when I have found Copper's collar. Take care!

options.text: I'm sorry. Thank you for sharing your story.

steps.player: I'm sorry. Thank you for sharing your story.

steps.npc: It's nice to share these kind of things sometimes, [player name].

steps.player: I'll leave you be. Sorry, Veos.

steps.npc: It's fine, [player name]. You didn't know.

using-items-on-veos-using-wolf-bones-on-.npc: How goes the hunt for Copper's collar, [player name]?

using-items-on-veos-using-wolf-bones-on-.player: I haven't had any luck finding it yet, Veos. Where would you recommend searching?

using-items-on-veos-using-wolf-bones-on-.npc: I'd imagine the fox which killed Copper will likely still have the collar in their possession. They were nearby a Fremennik town.

using-items-on-veos-using-wolf-bones-on-.player: Thanks, Veos. I'll return when I have the collar!

using-items-on-veos-using-copper-s-crims.npc: How goes the hunt for Copper's collar, [player name]?

using-items-on-veos-using-copper-s-crims.text: (Player gives copper's crimson collar to Veos)

using-items-on-veos-using-copper-s-crims.npc: [player name]... I can't thank you enough. I don't have a reward, but know that to me, this means so much. Perhaps in the future, I can repay you.

using-items-on-veos-using-copper-s-crims.player: You're more than welcome Veos, and don't worry about a reward. Losing your best friend is always hard. Hopefully that item will bring you some comfort. Take care!

using-items-on-veos-using-wolf-bones-on-.npc: [player name]... I can't thank you enough for what you've done for me. I don't have a reward, but know that to me, this means so much. Perhaps in the future I can repay you.

using-items-on-veos-using-wolf-bones-on-.player: You're more than welcome Veos, and don't worry about a reward. Losing your best friend is always hard. Hopefully that item will bring you some comfort. Take care!

historical-dialogue-docked-at-port-sarim.npc: I am Veos and I've just arrived in Port Sarim from a distant land.

steps.npc: I am from the magnificent kingdom of Great Kourend on the continent of Zeah, to the far west.

options.text: That's great, can you take me there please?

steps.player: That's great, can you take me there please?

steps.npc: Certainly! I hope you don't get seasick, it is a long voyage.

options.text: Tell me more about Great Kourend.

steps.player: Tell me more about Great Kourend.

steps.npc: Great Kourend is a magnificent kingdom comprising of five districts called Houses. The houses are ruled by the Lords of Arceuus, Lovakengj, Shayzien, Piscarilius and Hosidius.
Since our last King died 20 years ago the kingdom has been ruled by an elected council.

Zeah is a huge continent far to the west of here full of new adventures and hidden treasures. Sadly, the kingdom of Great Kourend is besieged by lizard creatures and it is not possible to get out of the kingdom just yet.

historical-dialogue-docked-at-port-tyras.player: Who're you? I've never seen you around these parts before.

historical-dialogue-docked-at-port-tyras.npc: I am Veos. Port master and scout for an elite Triumvirate.

historical-dialogue-docked-at-port-tyras.player: Who? Where? Why have you suddenly docked here?

historical-dialogue-docked-at-port-tyras.npc: These are questions to which you shall not find answers, adventurer.
There are secrets in this world for which you are not ready.

steps.npc: If I were as ugly as you I would not dare to show my face in public!
Out of my way, punk.
Hmm... you smell strange...
Like a human!

steps.player: Oh! Er... I just ate one is why!

steps.npc: Leave me alone.
Don't talk to me again if you value your life!
Get lost!
I don't have anything to give you so leave me alone, mendicant.
Have you no manners?
I don't have time for this right now.
I have no interest in talking to a pathetic meat bag like yourself.
I bet you have wonderful paws.
A very miserable day, altogether... enjoy it while it lasts.
If you catch anyone promise me you'll share.
I haven't smelt you around here before...
You smell familiar...
Seen any humans around here? I'm v-e-r-y hungry.
You look to me like someone with a healthy taste for blood.
Good day to you, my friend.
Fancy going up to the castle for a bit of a snack?
Give me a moment, I have a bit of someone stuck in my teeth...

standard-dialogue-using-a-guthix-balance.npc: Thanks so much for saving me from being a vampyre. Here, take this certificate, I'm sorry but it's all I can offer as a reward.

standard-dialogue-using-a-guthix-balance.text: You're handed a certificate of treasure as a reward.

standard-dialogue-talking-to-them-again.npc: Thanks for changing me back, it must have been hard for you. I must be off now.

standard.npc: Welcome to my clothes stall, can I help you with anything?

options.text: Yes, what clothes do you have in stock?

steps.player: Yes, what clothes do you have in stock?

steps.npc: Not a lot, I'm afraid, most of what I produce goes to my sister. Her shop is in Keldagrim-West.

steps.player: Well, show me what you do have then.

standard-dialogue-pre-quest.npc: Can you please help me? I'm in a terrible spot of trouble.

options.text: Aha, sounds like a quest. I'll help.

steps.player: Aha, sounds like a quest. I'll help.

steps.npc: Yes yes, I suppose it is a quest. My fiance Ernest and I came upon this house.
Seeing as we were a little lost Ernest decided to go in and ask for directions.
That was an hour ago. That house looks spooky, can you go and see if you can find him for me?

steps.player: Ok, I'll see what I can do.

steps.npc: Thank you, thank you. I'm very grateful.

steps.text: Ernest the Chicken is started.

options.text: No, I'm looking for something to kill.

steps.player: No, I'm looking for something to kill.

steps.npc: Oooh, you violent person you.

standard-dialogue-post-quest.npc: Oh he went off to talk to some green warty guy. I'm sure he'll be back soon.

treasure-trails-beginner.text: You've obtained a [new clue/casket]!

standard.npc: We're surviving. That's as good as we can hope for right now.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-not-.npc: Now that was quite the show! I haven't been that entertained in a long time.
Of course, you know I can't let you leave here alive. Time for your final performance...

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-not-.prompt: Is your party ready to fight?

steps.npc: Oh I'm going to enjoy this...

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-done.npc: Back again for more? I admire your perseverance. Shall we begin?

during-the-fight-upon-reaching-phase-two.npc: You think you can defeat me?

during-the-fight-upon-reaching-20-hitpoi.npc: I'm not finished with you just yet!

standard.npc: Hmmph. What do you want?

options.text: I was wondering what was down those stairs?

steps.player: I was just wondering what was down those stairs?

steps.npc: You can't go down there!
Good. Because you can't.
Because you can't. So that's fine.
Yes. Fine.
Well then.
This is the home of the Mountain Dwarves. How would you like it if I wanted to take a shortcut through your home?

options.text: Ooh... is this a shortcut to somewhere?

steps.player: Ooh... is this a shortcut to somewhere?

steps.npc: Well, it is a lot easier to go this way to get past White Wolf Mountain than through those wolf filled passes.

options.text: Oh, sorry, I hadn't realised it was private.

steps.player: Oh, sorry, I hadn't realised it was private.

steps.npc: Well, it is.

options.text: If you were my friend I wouldn't mind it.

steps.player: If you were my friend I wouldn't mind.

steps.npc: Yes, but I don't even know you.

steps.text: If the player is on a Quest Speedrunning world:

steps.npc: I'd rather not, thank you.

steps.text: This quest is not available on Speedrunning Worlds.
If the player does not meet the requirements to begin Fishing Contest:

steps.npc: I'd rather not, thank you.

steps.text: You do not meet all of the requirements to start the Fishing Contest quest.

steps.npc: I don't make friends easily. People need to earn my trust first.

steps.prompt: Start the Fishing Contest quest?

steps.player: And how am I meant to do that?

steps.npc: My, we are the persistent one aren't we?
Well, there's a certain gold artefact we're after. We dwarves are big fans of gold! This artefact is the first prize at the Hemenster fishing competition.
Fortunately we have acquired a pass to enter that competition...
Unfortunately Dwarves don't make good fishermen.
Okay. I entrust you with our competition pass. Don't forget to take some gold with you for the entrance fee.

steps.text: You got the Fishing Contest Pass!

steps.npc: Go to Hemenster and do us proud!

steps.player: You're a grumpy little man aren't you?

steps.npc: Don't you know it.

options.text: You're a grumpy little man aren't you?

steps.player: You're a grumpy little man aren't you?

steps.npc: Don't you know it.

options.text: I'm bigger than you. Let me by.

steps.player: I'm bigger than you. Let me by!

steps.npc: Go away! You're not going to bully your way in HERE!

options.text: I was just stopping to say hello!

steps.player: I was just stopping to say hello!

steps.npc: Hello then.
What if I do! It's no business of yours.

standard-dialogue-after-fishing-contest.npc: Welcome, oh great Fishing Champion! Feel free to pop by and use our tunnel any time.

standard-dialogue-after-fishing-contest.player: Thank you, I think I'll stop by for a beer one day.

using-additional-fishing-trophies-on-him.npc: Well you already gave me one, but I won't say no to another, thank you kindly!

standard.npc: Hey look it's the hero! It's great to have you around.

steps.speaker: Victor
steps.text: Have I seen you before?

steps.player: I don't think so... I've just got one of those faces.

steps.speaker: Victor
steps.text: You're probably right.

steps.speaker: Victor
steps.text: I'm rather busy at the moment. I've got to organise my cupboards of jewels.

steps.speaker: Victor
steps.text: Absolutely not! You stay away from my jewels.

steps.speaker: Victor
steps.text: Interested in buying a house like mine?

steps.speaker: Victor

steps.text: You'll catch on.

steps.speaker: Victor
steps.text: It really is.

steps.speaker: Victor
steps.text: Huh? Are you an encyclopedia salesman?

steps.player: No, sir, I'm a burglar. I burgle people.

steps.speaker: Victor
steps.text: I've got something in the back of my mind telling me I should go back home.

steps.speaker: Victor
steps.text: Lovely day for a stroll, wouldn't you say?

steps.speaker: Victor
steps.text: Sorry, but I don't have time to chat. I've got important errands to run.

steps.speaker: Victor

overhead-dialogue-when-victor-leaves-the.speaker: Victor

overhead-dialogue-if-the-player-is-still.text: You are escorted out of the house as the owner has locked the door.

standard.speaker: Victoria Kebbit Monkfish
standard.text: Hello, land dweller.

steps.speaker: Victoria Kebbit Monkfish
steps.text: The sea has been getting quite busy all of a sudden. I surfaced to see what the fuss was about and found that lots of you seem interested in diving down to the sea floor.

steps.speaker: Victoria Kebbit Monkfish
steps.text: I'm offering my services as a guide, for a price. The price in this case, is knowledge!

steps.player: Interesting... It might be good to add some data about the depth of the sea to my charts.

options.text: Can I dive to the sea floor with you?

steps.player: Can I dive to the sea floor with you?

steps.text: If the player is below 38 Sailing:

steps.speaker: Victoria Kebbit Monkfish
steps.text: I don't think you are practised enough to dive here. I don't want you getting swept away!
You need a Sailing level of 38 to dive here.
If you do not have appropriate diving gear equipped:

steps.speaker: Victoria Kebbit Monkfish
steps.text: You need to be wearing deep sea diving equipment to dive with me!

steps.speaker: Victoria Kebbit Monkfish
steps.text: I want something in return if you're going to dive with me...

steps.speaker: Victoria Kebbit Monkfish
steps.text: I'd like to try making some of your land food. Can you tell me the raw ingredients and tools I need to make an apple pie? Don't worry about water. I have plenty of that.

steps.speaker: Victoria Kebbit Monkfish
steps.text: This puzzle has three answers and you'll need to tell me all of them.

steps.speaker: Answers (any order)
steps.text: Cooking Apple, Pot of Flour, Pie Dish
If you answer incorrectly:

steps.speaker: Victoria Kebbit Monkfish
steps.text: I don't think that's right... You should try again.

steps.speaker: Victoria Kebbit Monkfish
steps.text: I'd like to try making some of your land food. Can you tell me the raw ingredients and tools I need to make an apple pie? Don't worry about water. I have plenty of that.

steps.speaker: Victoria Kebbit Monkfish
steps.text: This puzzle has three answers and you'll need to tell me all of them.
If you correctly guess all three items:
The mermaid, satisfied with your answer, escorts you to the bottom of the sea. You take some depth readings from your diving equipment and note down the interesting local flora and fauna.

steps.speaker: Victoria Kebbit Monkfish
steps.text: There you go. Hope the dive got you everything you needed!

steps.speaker: Victoria Kebbit Monkfish
steps.text: Goodbye, land dweller.

standard.speaker: Guard
standard.text: Hello, human. What can I do for you?

standard.speaker: Guard
standard.text: Protecting the camp from wildlife and thieves.

standard.player: What about the giant monster up there?

standard.speaker: Guard
standard.text: Hah! Why would I rush up there when you foolish humans are more than willing to throw yourself into its jaws?

standard.speaker: Guard
standard.text: Besides, someone needs to keep an eye on the happenings down here.

standard.speaker: Guard
standard.text: It is hungry work though, and we don't have the most interesting supplies up here.

standard.speaker: Guard
standard.text: Got me thinking about those sunlight antelope. Quite an interesting flavour, but I think we can do even more...

standard.speaker: Guard
standard.text: Anyway, I shouldn't really be talking to you. Move along, please.

standard-dialogue-with-raw-sunlight-ante.speaker: Guard
standard-dialogue-with-raw-sunlight-ante.text: Oh, is that sunlight antelope meat you're carrying?

standard-dialogue-with-raw-sunlight-ante.speaker: Guard
standard-dialogue-with-raw-sunlight-ante.text: Come closer, I have a request to make.

standard-dialogue-with-raw-sunlight-ante.speaker: Guard
standard-dialogue-with-raw-sunlight-ante.text: Sitting up here under the looming threat of death at the jaws of a giant beast that tunnels beneath our very feet got me thinking.

standard-dialogue-with-raw-sunlight-ante.speaker: Guard
standard-dialogue-with-raw-sunlight-ante.text: Could we combine the sweet stickiness of redberries with the strong, gamey flavour of sunlight antelope?

standard-dialogue-with-raw-sunlight-ante.speaker: Guard
standard-dialogue-with-raw-sunlight-ante.text: Don't get me wrong, Marla is cooking up some wonderful stuff considering the circumstances. I just need something a little more adventurous, you know?

standard-dialogue-with-raw-sunlight-ante.speaker: Guard
standard-dialogue-with-raw-sunlight-ante.text: I'm sure she'd be happy to experiment if you bring her some raw sunlight antelope and redberries!

steps.player: I suppose I can help out.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Wonderful, thank you! I can't wait to try this!

steps.player: Sorry, I'm a bit busy right now.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Aren't we all? Ah well, maybe another time.

steps.player: I'll see what I can do.

standard-dialogue-with-redberry-antelope.text: Viero enthusiastically takes a large bite and chews thoughtfully.

standard-dialogue-with-redberry-antelope.npc: Well, it's... interesting and complex. Definitely an experience.

standard-dialogue-with-redberry-antelope.text: He takes another bite of the meat.
Viero looks up from his meal.

options.text: Uh, usually there's a reward for doing this sort of thing.

steps.player: Uh, usually there's a reward for doing this sort of thing.

steps.npc: Seriously, human? You couldn't just do this out of kindness? For the enjoyment of the journey and the feeling of helping another?
You weren't helping me out of appreciation for my work here and the service I provide?
Or, at the least, to push the boundaries of culinary achievement?

steps.player: I... uh... of course. Enjoy your meal.

steps.npc: I suppose you can have a bite if you like?
Oh. Yeah, I suppose so.

steps.text: Viero tears off a chunk of meat and hands it to you. The strong, gamey flavour of the meats gives way to a tart sickly-sweetness that doesn't complement it at all.

steps.player: Interesting and complex is a good way to describe it...

steps.npc: An experience!
Oh, thank you! Have a great day!

Well the order has become quite diminished over the years, it's a very long process to learn the skills of a Void Knight. Recently there have been breaches into our realm from somewhere else, and strange creatures
have been pouring through. We can't let that happen, and we'd be very grateful if you'd help us.
We send launchers from our outpost to the nearby islands. If you go and wait in the lander there that'd really help.

So I moved to Nardah and took up this job crushing stuff instead. It's always been a passion of mine, crushing things. I'm a lot happier now.
The world is so much simpler when you're crushing. You know you just have to grind for long enough until you get the job done. It might take hours, but you just grind until you're done.

options.text: It's a bit hot and dry round here for a gnome isn't it?

steps.player: It's a bit hot and dry round here for a gnome isn't it? I thought you gnomes liked your home comforts.

steps.npc: Certainly I miss home cooking, but gnomes are also fundamentally curious people. I'm here exploring the furthest reaches of the world for the King.

Sophanem is a curious place, if you can get into the blighted place. There are several pyramids round here as well. Fascinating architecture, I've heard stories that some of them contain treasure tombs and mummies.
Cats seem to have considerable importance round here, they certainly seem tied into their religion. The Gods round here seem very alien to me - I've never heard of them before.

options.text: What does this mint cake do?
options.condition: If the player has a Mint cake:

steps.player: What does this mint cake do?

steps.npc: Gnomish mint cake is a great source of energy for the gnome traveller. It will give you that extra bit of zip when you are running out of steam.

steps.player: Ooh, that might come in very handy. Do you have any spare?

steps.npc: I need all the mint cake I have, I'm afraid.

options.text: What does this seed pod do?
options.condition: If the player has a Grand seed pod:

steps.player: What does this seed pod do?

steps.npc: Ah, the seed pod of the Grand Tree is a fascinating spirit artefact. It is a very useful thing, though one must treat it with respect, since the Grand Tree has a connection with all of its parts, however distant they
may be. How do you think the Spirit Trees work?

If you launch its seeds in a far flung location, you will be helping the tree survive, so the grand tree will help a gnome glider pilot find you, using the seed burst itself (which marks the sky) and a little magic, and bring you
back home as an act of gratitude. Budding farmers will also find their link with plants to be just a little bit better than before.
However, it takes time for a pilot to find you, and if you are in a real hurry, and I mean a real emergency, you can just squash the seed pod. The Grand Tree doesn't like this, but will pull you back

home straight away. Don't do this if you need to do anything with plants straight away, though - your fingers will be considerably less green for a while after using the seed pod this way, and the journey is not
very pleasant...

standard.player: Why are you in that cage?

standard.npc: That evil witch put me in here! She kidnapped me!

standard.player: That's awful! Why did she do that?

standard.npc: She wanted the secret of my ogleroots, so she did!

standard.player: Your ogleroots? I don't think I understand. What secret is that?

standard.npc: Well now, I have perfected a spell that would grow an ogleroot to an enormous size.

standard.player: That's amazing! But how do you move the ogleroot around if it's so big?

standard.npc: You know, I had the very same problem so I came up with a simple solution. I used a spell I learned from a chap called Larry to shrink 'em down really small so that I could carry whole bags filled with 'em to the
market place.
Then when I got there, I would use the growing spell once more to make 'em huge and sell 'em for a tidy sum.

standard.player: That's amazing! So how does the witch fit in to all this?

standard.npc: Well that old witch - she's a sly one, I tell you. She found out about my spell and kidnapped me along with my bag of ogleroots.
She wants the secret of the spell but I ain't talking! No sir! So she's been feeding my mini-ogleroots to those ugly...things over there.

standard.player: So she hasn't found out the spell yet?

standard.npc: Not yet, no. And I still ain't telling her. But from what I gather, she's started to use them ogleroots in some of her potions for something. I don't know what, though.

standard.player: I see. Can I get you out of there somehow?

standard.npc: No, it's ok. I want to keep an eye on what the witch is up to down here with these odd creatures.
Yes, I'll be fine for now. Good luck with your tasks!

steps.npc: This could be worse I guess. Oh wait... No it can't.
I'm hungry...
Sometimes I wish this thing would just escape. At least we'd have something to do then.
It's so cold...

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Greetings, [player name].

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: So you're a wise old man, huh?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Less of the 'old' man, if you please!
But yes, I suppose you could say that. I prefer to think of myself as a sage.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: So what's a sage doing here?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: I've spent most of my life studying this world in which we live. I've strode through the depths of the deadliest dungeons, roamed the murky jungles of Karamja, meditated on the glories of Saradomin on Entrana,
and read some dusty tomes in the Library of Varrock.
Now I'm not as young as I used to be, I'm settling here where it's peaceful.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: If the player has not completed Vampyre Slayer:

steps.npc: It's a pity about that vampyre that keeps attacking the village. At least Saradomin protects me.

steps.text: continue

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: That's quite an exciting life you've had.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Exciting? Yes, I suppose so.
Now I'm here, perhaps I could offer you the benefit of my experience and wisdom?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Thanks! So you can help me?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Well, I imagine you've gathered up quite a lot of stuff on your travels. Things you used for quests a long time ago that you don't need now.
If you like, I can look through your bank and see if there's anything you can chuck away.
Alternatively, you can bring items here and show them to me. If I see that it's something you don't need, I'll let you know. I might even be willing to buy it.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: So you'll help me clear junk out of my bank?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Yes, that's right. Or I'd be happy to chat with you about the wonders of this world!
