steps.npc: Please do!

steps.player: Could you tell me about the Wilderness, please?

steps.npc: If Entrana is a land dedicated to the glory of Saradomin, the Wilderness is surely the land of Zamorak.
It's a dangerous place, where adventurers such as yourself may attack each other, using all their combat skills in the struggle for survival.
The Wilderness has different levels. In a low level area, you can only fight adventurers whose combat level is close to yours.
But if you venture into the high level areas in the far north, you can be attacked by adventurers who are significantly stronger than you.
Of course, you'd be able to attack considerably weaker people too, so it can be worth the risk.
If you dare to go to the far north-west of the Wilderness, there's a building called the Mage Arena where you can learn to summon the power of Saradomin himself!
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?
As you wish. Farewell, [player name].

steps.player: What can you tell me about jungles?

steps.npc: If it's jungle you want, look no further than the southern regions of Karamja.
Once you get south of Brimhaven, the whole island is pretty much covered in exotic trees, creepers and shrubs.
There's a small settlement called Tai Bwo Wannai Village in the middle of the island. It's a funny place; the chieftain's an unfriendly chap and his sons are barking mad.
Honestly, one of them asked me to stuff a dead monkey with seaweed so he could EAT it!

steps.text: If the player has completed Tai Bwo Wannai Trio:
continue

steps.npc: Further south you'll find Shilo Village. It's been under attack by terrifying zombies in recent months, if my sources are correct.

steps.text: If the player has completed Shilo Village:

steps.player: I've dealt with them, although there are a few still knocking about.

steps.text: continue

steps.npc: The jungle's filled with nasty creatures. There are vicious spiders that you can hardly see before they try to bite your legs off, and great big jungle ogres.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?
Oh, the dwarven realms?
Yes, there was a time, back in the Fourth Age, when we humans wouldn't have been able to venture underground. That was before we had magic; the dwarves were quite a threat.
Still, it's much more friendly now. You can visit the vast dwarven mine if you like; the entrance is on the mountain north of Falador.
If you go further west you may be able to visit the dwarven city of Keldagrim. But they were a bit cautious about letting humans in, last time I asked.

On the other hand, if you go west of Brimhaven, you'll find a huge underground labyrinth full of giants, demons, dogs and dragons to fight. It's even bigger than the caves under Taverley, although the Taverley
dungeon's pretty good for training your combat skills.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What mystical realms can I visit?

steps.npc: Well, you've been to Zanaris. I met a fairy years ago who said she lived there. She was an incredible warrior, considering that she wasn't even a metre tall.
Also, in my research I came across ancient references to some kind of Abyss. Demons from the Abyss have already escaped into this land; Saradomin be thanked that they are very rare!

steps.text: If the player has completed Shadow of the Storm:

steps.player: I've been through a portal into the lair of some ancient demon. It was in the city of Uzer.

steps.npc: Ah, Uzer. A city much favoured by Saradomin, destroyed by Thammaron, the elder-demon, late in the Third Age.

steps.player: Yeah, there isn't much left there.

steps.text: continue

steps.npc: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What's the biggest monster in the world?

steps.npc: There's a mighty fire-breathing dragon living underground in the deep Wilderness, known as the King Black Dragon. It's a fearsome beast, with a breath that can poison you, freeze you to the ground or
incinerate you where you stand.
But even more deadly is the Queen of the Kalphites. As if her giant mandibles of death were not enough, she also throws her spines at her foes with deadly force. She can even cast rudimentary spells.
Some dark power must be protecting her, for she can block attacks using prayer just as humans do.
Another beast that's worthy of a special mention is the Shaikahan. It dwells in the eastern reaches of Karamja, and is almost impossible to kill except with specially prepared weapons.

steps.text: If the player has completed Tai Bwo Wannai Trio:

steps.player: Actually, that one's dead. I've been helping a barmy hunter who'd sworn to kill it.

steps.text: continue

steps.npc: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

options.text: Poison and how to survive it

steps.npc: Many monsters use poison against their foes. If you get poisoned, you will not feel it at the time, but later you will begin to suffer its effects, and your life will drain slowly from you.
Over time the effects dwindle to nothing, but if you had already been wounded you might die before they wear off completely.
Fortunately, followers of Guthix have devised potions that can cure the poison or even give immunity to it.
Should you wish to use poison against your own enemies and those of our Lord Saradomin, there is a potion that you can smear on your daggers, arrows, spears, javelins and throwing knives.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?
As a general rule, tougher monsters drop more valuable items. But even a lowly hobgoblin can drop valuable gems; it just does this extremely rarely.
If you can persuade the Slayer Masters to train you as a Slayer, you will be able to fight certain monsters that drop valuable items far more often.
You might care to invest in an enchanted dragonstone ring. These are said to make a monster drop its most valuable items a little more often.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What are these strange monsters that keep appearing out of nowhere and attacking me when I'm training?

steps.npc: Ah, I imagine you see a lot of those.

Creatures such as the rock golem, river troll and tree spirit dwell in places where adventurers frequently go to train their skills. While you're training you will often disturb one by accident. It will then get angry and
attack you. The safest way to deal with them is to run away immediately, but they sometimes drop valuable items if you kill them.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?
Ha ha ha... There are plenty of heroes. Always have been, always will be, until the fall of the world.

steps.text: If the player has less than 80 quest points:

steps.npc: If you'd do a few more quests, you'd soon become a fairly noted adventurer yourself.

steps.text: continue
If the player has 80 or more quest points:

steps.npc: You're quite a noted adventurer yourself!

steps.text: continue

steps.npc: But I suppose I could tell you of a couple...

Yes, there was a man called Arrav. No-one knew where he came from, but he was a fearsome fighter, a skillful hunter and a remarkable farmer. He lived in the ancient settlement of Avarrocka, defending it from
goblins, until he went forth in search of some strange artefact long desired by the dreaded Mahjarrat.
Perhaps some day I shall be able to tell you what became of him.

But do not let your head be turned by heroics. Randas was another great man, but he let himself be beguiled into turning to serve Zamorak, and they say he is now a mindless creature deep in the Underground Pass that
leads to Isafdar.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: Where did humans learn to use magic?

steps.npc: Ah, that was quite a discovery! It revolutionised our way of life and jolted us into this Fifth Age of the world.

They say a traveller in the north discovered the key, although no records state exactly what he found. From this he was able to summon the magic of the four elements, using magic as a tool and a weapon. He and
his followers learnt how to bind the power into little stones so that others could use it.
in the land south of here they constructed an immense tower where the power could be studied, but followers of Zamorak destroyed it with fire many years ago, and most of the knowledge was lost.

steps.text: If the player hasn't completed Rune Mysteries:

steps.npc: Perhaps one day those lost secrets will be uncovered once more.

steps.text: continue
If the player has completed Rune Mysteries:

steps.npc: I hear you've been very helpful to the wizards who are working on the mysteries of the rune stones.

steps.text: continue

steps.npc: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: I suppose you'd know about the history of today's cities?

steps.npc: Yes, there are fairly good records of the formation of the cities from primitive settlements.
In the early part of the Fourth Age, of course, there were no permanent settlements. Tribes wandered the lands, staying where they could until the resources were exhausted.

This changed as people learnt to grow crops and breed animals, and now there are very few of the old nomadic tribes. There's at least one tribe roaming between the Troll Stronghold and Rellekka, though.

steps.text: If the player has completed Mountain Daughter:

steps.player: Yes, I've met them. They're all mad.

steps.npc: Truly, their faith in natural spirits is rather foolish, but they're a pleasant enough people.

steps.text: continue

steps.npc: Anyway, what was I saying? Ah, yes...
One settlement was Avarrocka, a popular trading centre.
In the west, Ardougne gradually formed under the leadership of the Carnillean family, despite the threat of the Mahjarrat warlord Hazeel who dwelt in that area until his downfall.

steps.text: If the player sided with the cultists in Hazeel Cult:

steps.player: He'll be back, just you wait!

steps.npc: Oh dear, I hope you haven't done anything rash!

steps.text: continue
If the player sided with Ceril in Hazeel Cult:

steps.player: I've foiled a dastardly Zamorakian plot to have Hazeel resurrected.

steps.npc: So I'd heard. Lord Saradomin is smiling on you.

steps.text: continue

steps.npc: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

options.text: The Wise Old Man of Draynor Village

steps.player: Tell me about yourself, old man.

steps.npc: Ah, so you want to know about me, eh?
Mmm... what could I say about myself? Let's see what I've done...
I've delved into the dungeon west of Brimhaven and heard the terrifying CRASH of the steel dragons battling each other for territory.
I spent some years on Entrana, where I learnt the techniques of pure meditation.
I've wandered through the vast desert that lies south of Al Kharid and seen the great walls of Menaphos and Sophanem.

steps.text: If the player has completed Icthlarin's Little Helper:

steps.player: That feline statue you've got on your bookshelf there - I'm sure I saw something like that when I was in Sophanem.

steps.npc: I've always liked to collect little trinkets to remind me of the time when my life was more - ah - exciting.

steps.player: So you've spoken to the Sphinx, then?

steps.npc: Spoken to a sphinx, you say? My dear young lady, you can't possibly be serious!
Ha ha ha! The people who live deep in the shifting sands of the desert will often tell travellers tall tales of strange beasts, but that doesn't mean any of it's remotely true!
Please, adventurer, there is nothing to be gained by interfering in matters you do not understand.
Even if such a creature were to exist...
EVEN IF SUCH A CREATURE WERE TO EXIST it would be terribly dangerous for you to get involved in its business.
I have heard of terrible things happening to travellers in that land, and I would not wish for you to be dragged into anything like that.
Indeed, I have heard of adventurers doing the most shameful and blasphemous deeds believing themselves to be acting on behalf of some false god!
So please do not speak to me of this matter again. Now, I believe I was telling you of my adventurous youth...

steps.text: continue

steps.npc: Apart from all that, I've spent many a happy hour in dusty libraries, searching through ancient scrolls and texts for the wisdom of those who have passed on.
Plus plenty of other adventures, quests, journeys... Is there anything else you'd like to know?

steps.player: I heard that Gielinor has three gods.

steps.npc: Indeed. This is correct: Saradomin, Guthix and Zamorak.
Saradomin, the great and glorious, gives life to this world.
Zamorak craves only death and destruction.
Guthix, calling itself a god of 'balance', holds no allegiance, but simply aids whatever cause suits its shifting purpose.

steps.text: If the player has completed The Dig Site:

steps.npc: What did you say?

steps.player: I discovered a buried altar to a god called Zaros.

steps.npc: Please, do not speak further of this. No good can come of meddling in such things.
Adventurer, my patience is limited. Speak to me no further of this - this - this foolishness.

steps.text: If the player has completed Desert Treasure I:

steps.player: Does that mean I shouldn't ask you about the ancient magicks I learnt in that pyramid north of Sophanem?

steps.npc: ENOUGH! Begone from me, you foul trickster!

steps.text: If the player has completed Temple of Ikov but not Desert Treasure I:

steps.player: I've heard of another god, called Armadyl.

steps.npc: What is this of which you speak?

steps.player: A strange man asked me to go into the Temple of Ikov and steal the Staff of Armadyl.

steps.npc: And what makes you believe in this 'Armadyl'?

steps.player: Well, there were servants of Armadyl living down in the depths of the temple. They'd been there for generations, guarding the staff.

steps.npc: So you trusted the word of these people who had been sitting down a hole all their lives?
I wouldn't worry about this sacred 'armadyllo' anymore. Just another foolish myth.

steps.text: (If the player with the Guardians of Armadyl:)

steps.player: Oh well, the servants rewarded me very kindly for defeating Lucien for them.

steps.npc: That is an impressive feat, adventurer. Truly you must be beloved in the eyes of Saradomin.

steps.text: (If the player sided with Lucien:)

steps.player: It's lucky there's no Armadyl! I've pinched his staff and given it to Lucien.

steps.npc: YOU'VE DONE WHAT?
Adventurer, I beg of you, do not meddle in the gods' affairs. No good can come of it.

steps.text: If the player has completed Icthlarin's Little Helper but not Desert Treasure I:

steps.player: How about Tumeken, Elindis, Icthlarin and the Devourer?

steps.npc: What names are these?

steps.player: Down in Sophanem, they've got a chief god named Tumeken, plus a fertility goddess named Elindis. Icthlarin is their god of the dead and the Devourer...

steps.npc: Adventurer, what folly leads you to think any of these - things, exist?

steps.player: But I've met Icthlarin! He'd got a jackal's head!

steps.npc: It is hot in that land, and the heat can affect a traveller in strange ways. Tell me, when you met 'Icthlarin', had you been feeling at all unwell?

steps.player: Well, now you mention it, I'd just been hypnotised by a weird woman I met in the desert.

steps.npc: So a strange woman interfered with your mind, then you met a man with the head of a jackal, and you decided he must be a god?
Well, make sure you don't get hypnotised again, and I'm sure you'll not meet any more jackal-headed men claiming to be gods!
It'd probably be best if you don't go there again.

steps.player: But you've been all around that area, haven't you? When you were travelling?

steps.npc: Indeed, I have.

steps.player: So you'd know all about their gods?

steps.npc: I know what I know.
And knowing what I know, I do not speak of this matter. Perhaps you would be wise to heed my example.

steps.player: I wanna know about the wars of the gods!

steps.npc: Ah, that was a terrible time. The armies of Saradomin fought gloriously against the minions of Zamorak, but many brave warriors and noble cities were overthrown and destroyed utterly.

steps.text: If the player has completed Shadow of the Storm:

steps.npc: You have visited Uzer, and seen for yourself the damage that could be wrought by an elder-demon in its wrath.

steps.text: continue

steps.npc: Before the Zamorakian forces could be utterly routed, Lord Saradomin took pity on them and the battle- scarred world, and allowed a truce.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?
Very little is written about the tribe of the Mahjarrat. They are believed to be from the realm of Freneskae, or Frenaskrae - the spelling in this tongue is only approximate.
One of them, the foul Zamorak, has achieved godhood, although none knows how this came about.
Other Mahjarrat who have been particularly active upon this plane are Hazeel, Lucien, Azzanadra and Zemouregal.

steps.text: If the player sided with the cultists in Hazeel Cult:

steps.player: Hazeel will rise again, you'll see!

steps.npc: Adventurer, your actions fill me with concern!

steps.text: continue
If the player sided with Ceril in Hazeel Cult:

steps.player: I've foiled a dastardly Zamorakian plot to have Hazeel resurrected.

steps.npc: So I'd heard. Lord Saradomin is smiling on you.

steps.text: continue
If the player sided with the Guardians of Armadyl in Temple of Ikov:

steps.npc: Truly, your bravery exceeds your stature. But I fear his defeat will not be permanent.

steps.text: continue
If the player sided with Lucien in Temple of Ikov:

steps.player: I've met Lucien. He paid me very nicely for bringing him a staff he wanted.

steps.npc: Traveller, I beg of you, do not have further dealings with such creatures! You do not know their power as I do.

steps.text: continue
If the player has completed Desert Treasure I:

steps.player: Azzanadra taught me some ancient magical powers after I unlocked the pyramid where he had been trapped.

steps.npc: Leave me, traveller; I am old, and your words fill me with horror.

options.text: Wielding the power of the gods

steps.player: Can I wield the power of Saradomin myself?

steps.text: If the player has completed Mage Arena I:

steps.npc: I see you are already learning to summon the power of Saradomin.

steps.text: continue
If the player hasn't completed Mage Arena I:

steps.npc: If you travel to the Mage Arena in the north-west reaches of the Wilderness, the battle mage Kolodion may be willing to let you learn to summon the power of Saradomin, should you be able to pass his test.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: I want to ask you about your hat.

steps.npc: Why, thank you! I rather like it myself.

steps.text: If the player has not yet seen the recording of the Draynor Bank Robbery:

steps.player: Did you steal it from the bank?

steps.npc: Me? Steal from the bank? Whatever do you mean?

steps.player: There's been a break-in at Draynor Bank, and I bet you did it.

steps.npc: Oh my goodness, what in the world could make you think I did such a thing?

steps.player: Well, you've been sitting here looking at the bank ever since you moved into this house. Now someone's robbed the bank, and suddenly your house is full of expensive stuff!

steps.npc: Oh dear, oh dear...
So what do you think I did? March across the street, smash the bank wall, knock out the bankers and steal all the money?
I'm an old man! I walk with a stick! How could I possibly have done that?

steps.player: So you didn't rob the bank?

steps.npc: Just run along now, be a good lad, and don't worry yourself about me or my finances!

steps.player: Hmmm... But I'll be keeping an eye on you.

steps.npc: Now you've got that off your chest, would you like to ask me about anything else?

options.text: How can I get a hat like that?

steps.text: If the player has seen the recording of the Draynor Bank Robbery:

options.text: You stole it off that woman in the bank!

steps.player: You stole it off that woman in the bank! You stole all this valuable stuff too!

steps.npc: Stole it? How could you possibly think I did such a thing?

steps.player: I saw you robbing the bank! You killed all those people!

steps.npc: Deary me, [player name], your imagination is running wild! What could make you think you saw me do that?

steps.player: I've seen a security recording that shows you robbing the bank. The bank's guard showed it to me.

steps.npc: You've seen the bank's security recording?
Tut tut tut... Oh well, at least you'll never be able to tell the bank about me. They'll never listen.

steps.player: So you're just going to get away with it?

steps.npc: That's my plan, yes.
Wrong? WRONG? I'll tell you what's wrong!
I've spent my whole life travelling the world, doing quests for people, saving lives, saving villages from terrifying monsters and all that sort of thing.
Now I'm old, and where do I have to live? In this freezing old house next to a pig-sty, with a bunch of yobs outside who can't keep their hands off the market stalls! What sort of reward is that?
So don't talk to me about right and wrong!

steps.player: Maybe someone SHOULD talk to you about right and wrong...

steps.npc: Bah!
Now you've got that off your chest, would you like to ask me about anything else?

options.text: How can I get a hat like that?
How can I get a hat like that?

steps.player: How can I get a hat like that?

steps.npc: You could buy one off another player, or wait until they're next made available by the Council.
Ohhh no, I don't intend to part with this. Would you like to ask me about something else?

options.text: You should give it back, you know.
You should give it back, you know.

steps.player: You should give it back, you know.

steps.npc: No, I think I'll keep it.
Now you've got that off your chest, would you like to ask me about anything else?

options.text: How can I get a hat like that?
How can I get a hat like that?

options.condition: If the player has completed Swan Song:

steps.player: That was quite an exciting quest we did together!

steps.npc: Oh yes, it was certainly a fitting end to my adventuring days. Your fight against the Sea Troll Queen was highly impressive!

steps.player: Are you tempted to go on another quest in the future?

steps.npc: No, I feel I am a bit old for that kind of thing now. New times need new heroes, and I'm sure you'll always be there to answer the call!

steps.player: I'll certainly see what I can do!

steps.npc: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

options.condition: If the player has completed Swan Song:

steps.player: When we finished fighting those sea trolls, you said you'd finished with adventuring, didn't you?

steps.npc: Yes, that's right. I'm an old man, there's no denying it, and I need a nice quiet retirement.
Besides, I think you've proved that the new generation has its own heroes and adventurers - I should step back and let you get on with it!

steps.player: Does this mean you're not going to do any more big robberies?

steps.npc: Well, since you saved my life when we were fighting the Sea Troll Queen, I don't mind telling you... I trust you won't tell anyone about this?
I might just have something in mind. After all, that little bank incident went very smoothly.
I retired from adventuring and questing. The episode in the bank was hardly a quest, more like a shopping trip!

steps.player: Your shopping trip killed 3 bank staff and several innocent bystanders, not to mention the watchman!

steps.npc: I've saved countless villages from unspeakable terrors and slain innumerable evil monsters - surely I deserve some sort of reward in return? Yet what did I get? NOTHING!
You yourself would get pretty angry if you did a long and dangerous quest and didn't get any reward from it, eh? I'm sure you would!
Well imagine how I felt at the end of a long life of questing when was left penniless, and I had to move into this thief-infested village! This little shack was falling apart when I arrived!
You go speak to that hag who keeps looking through my window - she'll show you how it used to look before I could afford to redecorate it!
Being noble and virtuous simply doesn't put food on the table, and I don't intend to sit in banks begging like so many people do these days.

steps.player: So all those quests in the past, when you saved people from monsters and stuff like that... You only helped them because you wanted a reward?

steps.npc: No, it wasn't always like that. I used to be satisfied just knowing that I'd helped, and that was reward enough.

But eventually I realised that people forgot about me as soon as the danger was gone, and I wasn't even getting paid properly for my services. Sometimes they offered training in the various skills, but that's no use to me!
I eventually realised that the only way I could get a proper reward for my life's efforts is if I took the reward myself. So I took up my cape and staff and headed for the bank.

steps.player: And now you're planning to do another robbery? Didn't you get enough from the bank?

steps.npc: Perhaps not... But enough of this matter! Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

using-items-on-wise-old-man.text: If the player has not gone through the initial dialogue first:

steps.npc: Humph! You could at least say hello before waving your items in my face.

using-items-on-wise-old-man-item-with-of.player: Do you think I need to keep this?

using-items-on-wise-old-man-item-with-of.npc: I suppose you could use that in combat.

using-items-on-wise-old-man-item-with-on.player: Do you think I need to keep this?

using-items-on-wise-old-man-item-with-on.npc: I suppose you could use that for defense.

using-items-on-wise-old-man-low-value-ru.player: Do you think I need to keep this?

using-items-on-wise-old-man-low-value-ru.npc: Runes are very useful things, but I'll take some of those off your hands for you.

using-items-on-wise-old-man-high-value-r.player: Do you think I need to keep this?

using-items-on-wise-old-man-high-value-r.npc: Ooh, runes? Yes, they're quite valuable.

using-items-on-wise-old-man-coins.player: Do you think I need to keep this?

using-items-on-wise-old-man-coins.npc: That's called 'money'. Money is fantastically important if you haven't got enough of it, but when you've got as much as I have, you realise that money doesn't matter.

using-items-on-wise-old-man-book-on-chic.player: Do you think I need to keep this?

using-items-on-wise-old-man-book-on-chic.npc: That's mine. I'll take it back, thank you very much!

using-items-on-wise-old-man-the-banker-s.npc: How did you get your hands on that?!
Get out of here this instant.

using-items-on-wise-old-man-items-with-n.player: Do you think I need to keep this?

using-items-on-wise-old-man-items-with-n.npc: Tell you what, rather than you showing me items individually, I'll look through all your possessions to see if I can find anything worth discarding.

using-items-on-wise-old-man-items-with-n.text: (Game opens the Wise Old Man's Recycling Center interface)

searching-through-his-bookcases-without-.npc: It'd be politer to come and talk to me before you start messing around with my possessions!

after-observing-his-telescope.player: I see you've got your telescope pointing at the Wizards' Tower.

after-observing-his-telescope.npc: Oh, do I? Well, why does that interest you?

after-observing-his-telescope.text: If the player has not seen the bank robbery cutscene:

steps.player: It just seems a bit odd.

steps.npc: Odd? There's nothing odd about a fascination with the magical arts. Besides, the architecture of that Tower is truly remarkable, for one who studies such things.

steps.player: So you're not planning to attack the Tower?

steps.npc: No, I wouldn't dream of doing anything of the sort!

after-observing-his-telescope.text: If the player has seen the bank robbery cutscene:

steps.player: Well, you robbed a bank, and I bet you're now planning something to do with that Tower!

steps.npc: No, no. I'm not planning anything like that again.
Well, this is rather embarrassing, but I think there's some kind of monster in my house. Could you go upstairs and get rid of it, please?

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

options.text: Where do I need to go?

steps.player: Where do I need to go?

steps.npc: I think it's somewhere upstairs. It kept me awake all last night.
I need some bronze bars. Please bring me [#].

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: Mine some copper ore and tin ore. The furnace in Lumbridge can smelt them into bars of bronze.

wise-old-man-tasks-delivering-items-to-t.text: If the wise man needs bronze items:

steps.npc: I need a few bronze daggers to keep the goblins at bay. Please bring me [#].
I'd like some maces made of bronze. Please bring me [#].
I need a few bronze arrowheads to complete some arrows I was making. Please bring me [#].
I'd like some bronze knives to throw at goblins. Please bring me [#].
My weapons collection isn't all it used to be. Some short swords made of bronze would be much appreciated. Please bring me [#].
The head fell off my axe when I was chopping wood last week, so I need some more bronze axes. Please bring me [#].
Could you fetch me some big warhammers made of bronze? Please bring me [#].
I could do with some medium-sized helmets. I'd like bronze ones. Please bring me [#].
I need some lengths of bronze wire to repair something. Please bring me [#].

A few lumps of iron ore would be nice. Please bring me [#].

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: It should be easy enough for you to mine some iron ore.
I've found a use for cadava berries. Please bring me [#].

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: Just look around the woods south-west of Varrock.
The hail can be very heavy here, so I'd like a few leather cowls. Please bring me [#].

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: If you get the tanner in Al Kharid to turn some cowhides into leather, you'll be able to make the cowls yourself. Buy needles & thread from the crafting shop in Al Kharid if you need any.
Strange as it may seem, I want a lot of beer! Please bring me [#].

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.npc: There's a pub not far from here that will sell you plenty of that. Go west to Port Sarim.
I don't have a decent larder here, so I can't store food very well. Now I'm out of loaves of bread. Please bring me [#].

steps.npc: Mix some flour and water to make bread dough, then bake it on a cooking range.

I saw an interesting bed in Karamja called a 'hammock'. It seemed to be made out of string, and I'd like some balls of wool so I can make my own. Please bring me [#].

My undergarments are getting a bit worn out. I'll be needing some sheets of silk to patch them. Please bring me [#].

My roof is leaking, so I need some swamp paste to fix it. Please bring me [#].

steps.text: Almost every tree can be chopped down. Normal logs will be produced by chopping 'Trees' and Oak logs will come from chopping 'Oak Trees'. You can find Oak trees in amongst normal trees scattered about the lands.
Willow trees will yield willow logs. You'll find willows like to grow near water, you can find some south of Draynor.
Maple logs can be gleaned from Maple trees. You'll usually find Maple trees standing alone amongst other trees.
Yew trees are few and far between. We do our best to cultivate them. Look for the tree icon on your minimap to find rare trees. Try North of Port Sarim.

options.condition: If the player has level 29-98 Woodcutting

steps.text: Magic trees are... magic. A difficult wood to work with, but worth it for the rewards. Find them in the areas south of Seers village or on the East side of the Mage Arena.

steps.npc: Hollow trees can be found in the Haunted Woods east of Canifis, but be careful of the leeches.

steps.text: Bronze axes are easy to get, simply go visit Bob in his shop in Lumbridge, or talk to me if you have mislaid yours.

steps.npc: As you progress in your combat skill you will find you can wield your woodcutting axe as a weapon, it's not very effective, but it frees up a slot for another log.

steps.text: As your woodcutting skill increases you will find yourself able to use better axes to chop trees faster.... anything up to steel you can buy from Bob's axe shop.
Rune axes can be player made with very high level smithing and mining. They can also be obtained through killing one of the fearsome tree spirits, though this is very rare.

I'll happily exchange them for some goodies I've collected during my time here! You can also keep any bone shards they may have unfortunately chipped off.
Wonderful! To get started, just use the ladder by the wyrm's skull to climb up onto the scaffolding.
Initially the route is the same for everyone, but part way round you'll find a loftier section of scaffolding. If you're skilled, that route might be more appealing to you.
That said, don't go up there unless you know what you're doing. I have work to do so I can't spend all my time patching people up when they hurt themselves!

steps.npc: Very busy, my friend. We have a lot of repairs to be doing, not to mention that there will soon be a new Gathering taking place here.
We did have a creature from down in the caverns try to come up here at one point. Presumably they've been disturbed by recent events. The warriors quickly dealt with it though.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: May the sun light your way, traveller.

standard.npc: Greetings human. Do you seek guidance?

steps.npc: I am Xorrah quo Sihar. I am one of the mystics of the Kahlith.
Yes. At one time we were like you, but then we met the Tasakaal. They taught us to have purpose. They taught us to serve the balance.
Our old lives were left behind. In their place, the Kahlith were born.
Our teachers. They showed us the way and taught us to serve the balance.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: For every death, there must be life. For every life, there must be a death. This is the balance.
Our purpose, as taught to us by the Tasakaal, is to keep this balance, no matter the cost.

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Yes. All Kahlith serve the balance. To do this, we take on one of four roles.
My role is that of a mystic. I learn from the Tasakaal and then pass on their teachings.
This is our home. In your tongue, it is known as Mount Karuulm.
Yes. You speak the language of humans but we Kahlith have our own language.
In the past, we have tried to teach our language to your kind. However, despite the simplicity of our tongue, success was limited.
We find that it is easier to just use your language when your kind are around.
Of our language?
Well you'll find our language is quite a simple one. Our names are a good example of how it is used.
I am Xorrah quo Sihar. The first word, 'Xorrah', is unique to me and it is how I can be identified.
The second word, 'quo', is a basic Kahlith word that translates to 'the' in your language.
The final word, 'Sihar', is my title. There are four possible titles, one for each role in Kahlith society. My title translates to 'Mystic' in your tongue.

steps.player: So in my language your name would be Xorrah the Mystic?

steps.npc: Exactly.

options.text: Can you tell me a bit about skillcapes?

steps.player: Can you tell me a bit about skillcapes?

steps.npc: Sure. You can buy a skillcape when you reach level 99 in a skill. Apart from boosting your statistics in that skill, they can also be used to perform some pretty amazing emotes!
The Cape of Strength also provides you with unlimited teleports to our guild. Is there anything else you would like to know?
Ahh, the shot put is a great test of strength and can be quite rewarding. Mind you do it properly though, you might want to dust your hands with some powdery substance first. It'll give better grip.

steps.player: I'll remember that. What should I use?

steps.npc: I personally prefer ground ashes, it makes a nice fine powder and gives some really good grip.
Basically you'll need to go in there, make sure you've got nothing cluttering up your hands, pick up a shot and throw it.... depending upon your technique, you can get quite long throws.
Ahh that would be telling...

options.text: Why are you wielding a tree branch?

steps.player: Why are you wielding a tree branch?

steps.npc: Well...there's a story to that. You see, I should have an axe but-
My axe. He won it because of a squirrel.
He bet me that I couldn't catch the squirrel while still holding my axe, but that he could... Thing is, he tricked me! When it was his turn, he just chopped the tree down!

steps.player: I see. That doesn't explain why you have a tree branch though.

steps.npc: A barbarian warrior is bound to his axe. I cannot take up another, so I use part of the tree that Sloane cut down as my weapon... It also reminds me of him.
Yes, and a good friend, Still, he would want us to be happy that he is now with his warrior brethren. Can I help you with anything else?

Out of my way, punk.

Like a human!

steps.player: Oh! Er... I just ate one is why!

steps.npc: Leave me alone.
Don't talk to me again if you value your life!
Get lost!

I don't have time for this right now.

A very miserable day, altogether... enjoy it while it lasts.

I haven't smelt you around here before...

You look to me like someone with a healthy taste for blood.
Good day to you, my friend.
Fancy going up to the castle for a bit of a snack?
Give me a moment, I have a bit of someone stuck in my teeth...

standard-dialogue-first-time.npc: Ah... [player name], welcome. I would offer you some water, but we don't get much of it down here.
I take it you have questions.

options.text: You know why I'm here. Stop messing around.

steps.npc: I do, but it is important that it is you who is asking for information, not me that is offering it.

steps.player: Okay... How are you still communicating with your followers?

steps.text: Continues from "Why, through my voice, of course."

options.text: I take it you have answers.

steps.player: I take it you have answers.

steps.npc: I do, but I rarely share them umprompted.

steps.player: Okay, how are you still communicating with your followers?

steps.text: Continues from "Why, through my voice, of course."

options.text: Yes, a few of them actually.

steps.player: Yes, a few of them actually. How are you still communicating with your followers?

steps.npc: Why, through my voice, of course.

steps.player: You know what I mean. How are you still communicating with your voice?

steps.npc: The same way I always have.

steps.player: But the dark nullifier... I thought it was supposed to sever your connection.

steps.npc: Hmm... Yes, if anything could have done so, it would have been the power of the Dark Altar.
However, when your opponents have only one angle of approach, it makes them so predictable.

steps.player: You knew we would try to use it?

steps.npc: Yes. When I heard you would be hand delivering me a connection to the Dark Altar... Why, I was overjoyed.

steps.player: But... I remember planting it! The plan went off without a hitch!

steps.npc: I do not doubt that you remember it that way.
A simple transfiguration of the mind. My disciples granted you a memory of success. A fitting payment for your gratious service.

steps.text: If Icthlarin's Little Helper has been completed:

steps.player: You modified my memory?! That's only the second time someone has done that to me, and I wasn't very happy about it then either!

steps.text: continues
If Icthlarin's Little Helper hasn't been completed:
continues

steps.npc: Yes. And I have now answered five of your questions. I believe my generosity has been both demonstrated and exhausted.

steps.player: You call that gloating generosity? If you didn't want something from me, I wouldn't still be down here. Get to the point.

steps.npc: Hmm... Perhaps you are more astute than I thought. Very well, there is something that I want.

steps.player: Well you won't be getting it from me!

steps.npc: I am Yama. Every mortal desires something of mine. Ancient armaments? Hidden knowledge? Or perhaps a taste of revenge...
These things could be yours.
Face me in combat. If you win, you take it all. Armaments, knowledge, revenge.
I take your soul. For all of eternity.
I see. Perhaps we could lower the stakes then.
I will face you in an inhibited form. I'll even allow you to bring an ally, provided they have entered the same contract.
If you win, I will give you a chance to gain some of my treasures, and of course, you will have sampled your revenge.
When you take your final rest, I shall take your soul for a year. A drop in the ocean compared to eternity.

steps.player: How can I know you'll keep your word?

steps.npc: The same way I will know you shall keep yours. A binding contract. As luck would have it, I had one of my scribes draft one up for just such an occasion.
Sign right here.

steps.prompt: Sign the contract?
Are you sure? A contract with Yama cannot be backed out of.

steps.npc: Excellent... Challenge me when you are ready, [player name]. I very much look forward to it.

steps.player: I'm not sure I want to...

steps.npc: Of course. There is no rush. Leave, with your tail tucked between your legs. If you grow a spine and wish to fulfil your revenge, I will be waiting.

standard-dialogue-after-backing-out-from.npc: You are back. Excellent. I have little time for cowards. If you are ready, I will retrieve the contract.

standard-dialogue-using-the-right-click-.npc: Ah... Yes, let us not get bogged down in the minutiae. Before we start, a quick contract. Nothing but a formality.

standard-dialogue-afterwards.npc: Welcome, [player name]. Have you come to challenge me?

steps.text: Yama snaps his fingers and teleports off his throne.

steps.npc: Of course.

options.text: There's something in our contract about additional contracts...

steps.player: There's something in our contract about additional contracts... Why would I want to sign any more of them?

steps.npc: As outlined in subsection C, if you wish for your revenge to feel more 'real', I am willing to lift some of the restrictions placed by the original contract.

steps.text: If the player is an Ironman or Group Ironman:

steps.npc: You seem to enjoy self-imposed difficulty. I thought I would indulge you.

steps.text: continues
If the player is not an Ironman:

steps.npc: You may not, in which case you can sell them to someone with greater respect for themselves. But if you do, the option is there.

steps.npc: And if you manage to claim victory, there is of course a reward for each contract.

steps.player: Okay, can I see the contracts?

steps.npc: No. For this, I require from you a service. My demons are... Lacking, of late. Unrefined.
They must fight, suffer and reform. If you deliver them specific ends during your 'tasks' in my domain, they may leave behind a contract.
And of course, if you defeat me, I may also reward you with one.
Death by two-handed melee weapons, heavy ranged weapons, magic spells, special attacks, and defeating them whilst bound. Each kind may award a different contract.
If you find yourself eager to obtain any contract, I will use a glyph to indicate my preferred method, which you can utilise for a better chance to receive that contract.

steps.player: What kinds of contracts can I obtain?

steps.npc: Were you more adept at reading you would find the details in our original contract. Otherwise, bring any you obtain to me and I shall explain then.

options.text: Do you keep any record of our fights?

steps.player: Do you keep any record of our fights?

steps.npc: I do, I can have somebody retrieve your file. One moment.

steps.npc: For your reading pleasure.

steps.npc: I hope you are finding the spoils from my treasury to your liking. There are plenty more for you to claim.
Your victories mount. You are getting better at this.
A victory earned. But there is room for improvement, is there not?
Here we go again. I suppose it is entertaining watching you desperately guzzle potions, at the very least.
I must once again commend your strategy. Employing tactics so boring that they put your opponents to sleep is very novel.
Back again I see. I can see how you find these bouts exhilarating, being such a feeble opponent.
Your willingness to wager your soul continues to surprise. I suppose you think of it even less worth than I do.
Honestly, I expected more. That it takes you as long as it does to defeat my inhibited form is rather embarrassing.
You look happy with yourself. How endearing.
You return once more. Excellent.
Ah, you have returned. Your competence matches only your greed.

standard-dialogue-after-battle-victoriou.npc: In any case, [player name], are you here to challenge me?

standard-dialogue-after-battle-defeated.text: One of the following is said before standard dialogue follows. This can appear as an overhead quote if Yama is challenged, which ignores the "In any case" section.

steps.npc: Don't let a single defeat set you back. You could have so many more.
My treasury remains over capacity. And here I was hoping to be relieved of some of its contents.
What a shame for our last bout to have ended that way! Maybe you will do better next time.
Back after being defeated so quickly? I suppose what you lack in skill you make up for with perseverance.
Some losses are unavoidable. Yours, of course, was not.
Your donation is greatly appreciated.
Defeat finds you. Of course, that is hardly unexpected.

standard-dialogue-after-battle-having-es.text: One of the following is said before standard dialogue follows, after which the "In any case" section is played. This can appear as an overhead quote if Yama is challenged, which ignores the "In any case" section.

steps.npc: If you are struggling to achieve victory, I suppose avoiding defeat is the best you can do.
You must be tired, having to run all the way back here.
Back for more? Well, you can always escape again I suppose.
Excellent work evading. Next time, try fighting back.
Our last bout was cut short. Perhaps the next will be more fruitful.
Back again? Watching you escape in such a hurry, I thought you might never return.
Ah, I see your legs have stopped quivering. Perhaps next time you will fight to the end.
I hear adventurers like to boast about their feats. I wonder if people realise how readily they run at the first sight of risk.
A well executed retreat. You must be very practiced.
There is no shame in defeat. There is plenty to be found in your cowardice, however.

steps.npc: After all the confidence you demonstrated... still you lost your nerve. Perhaps I should have included in our contract a clause to cover your cowardly retreats.

standard-dialogue-after-battle-having-es.npc: In any case, [player name], have you come to challenge me?

steps.player: No, I think it might have been somebody else that dropped it. I should really go and find them...

steps.npc: Yes, perhaps it was. Perhaps it belonged to somebody else. Somebody with a semblance of pride or self respect.

steps.player: That's outrageous! You can't hold me to this!

steps.npc: Perhaps you should have expressed that opinion before signing. Indeed, perhaps if you felt that way you should not have signed at all.

using-items-on-yama-meat-pizza.npc: The meat pizza. An adequate if uninspired offering. Hand me it.

using-items-on-yama-anchovy-pizza.npc: Anchovy pizza. Flavourful and bold. Hand me it.

using-items-on-yama-teleporting-or-dying.npc: You thought you could escape with your pizza? I'm afraid not, [player name].

using-items-on-yama-any-contract-histori.npc: I'm afraid my scribes are a tad overwhelmed at the moment. Please, return with your contract soon, I would be delighted to sign once they are unblocked.

using-items-on-yama-any-contract-histori.text: Contracts will be enabled 1-2 weeks after Yama has launched.

standard-dialogue-demonic-pacts-league-i.npc: Make it quick, [player name], I have no appetite for distraction.

steps.npc: You are here for a number of reasons, [player name]. Chiefly because I deign to allow these petty games to play out.

steps.player: Petty games? You mean the League?

steps.npc: Yes, my League.
I confess my curiosity has finally won through. Long have I heard tales of these Leagues, and the lengths mortals like you will go to for a shred of favour from a superior being.
So now I offer you the same bargain that the 'mighty' Sage has struck time and time again. However, I present you with the chance of true power.
Does that intrigue you?

steps.player: Of course! Who wouldn't be interested in that?

steps.npc: Very good. In that case, complete the tasks you have been presented with and we can arrange some appropriate enhancements.
The League awaits you. Impress me.

steps.text: other

options.text: What have you done to the Sage?

steps.player: Why have you imprisoned the Sage? They're usually quite pleasant.

steps.npc: I have seized the Sage just as I have claimed this League.
The Sage has well and truly earned their place in my domain. Such squandered potential...
More than that, do you understand what this League actually is? Where we are?
Hah! You do not. Nor did I before lengthy discussions with my guest.
It is enough to say that I require guarantees for the near future.

steps.player: What does that mean? Should I be concerned?

steps.npc: You are small. When the time comes you will slip through the net and leave this chapter without incident.
I, however, must ensure I have passage at the end.

steps.player: Hmm... I'm not sure I like being called small, but I do like not having to worry!
So what exactly are you going to do with the Sage?

steps.npc: What am I going to do with them? Nothing. Unless they refuse my demands.
You cannot possibly fathom the potential futures I am conjuring for the contents of that cage should they fail me.
If I told you but one element of my intent, your mind would collapse, and your soul would scream with agony for a thousand years.
You simply would not comprehend.

steps.npc: I seem interested to you, do I?

Yes, you deal with me now, and no other. Perhaps I am interested in how you will fare, perhaps not.

steps.player: I think I will do just fine.

What I offer is far greater than what this Sage would dare present to you.

Well, well, well. Here to bask in the warmth of my domain no doubt. Do not linger too long, you have much yet to do.
Ah, [player name]! How goes the League?

You looked like you wanted to speak to me, you halfwit. You dullard.

steps.npc: A giant frog found its way into the mines, but I helped the guards to drive it off!
It got away in the end. But it was the biggest I'd ever seen!
I've been thinking about my destiny...
What was it Juna said to me? 'Your destiny is to lead all goblins into a new age.'
'All goblins.' Not just the Dorgeshuun, all goblins...
And what does it even mean, my destiny? Is it something I'm certain to do, or just something I ought to do? How can I know?
I talked to Juna about it, but she wouldn't tell me anything. She just said, 'You will know, when the time is right.'
I've been helping Oldak with his experiments!
I took his magic ball all over the caves and even to Lumbridge to test what happened when I broke it, and I always ended up back here.
You might find one of those balls useful if you wanted to visit me! Perhaps you should talk to Oldak.
I went on another visit to Lumbridge! I still can't convince other Dorgeshuun to go to the surface with me, though.

options.condition: After completing Another Slice of H.A.M. and if the player has the ancient mace:

steps.npc: You've still got that ancient mace...
It must be my imagination, but I can almost feel the power coming off it, like it's calling out to me.
You should keep it safe, [player name]!

options.condition: After completing Another Slice of H.A.M. and if the player doesn't have the ancient mace:

steps.npc: I thought you had the ancient goblin mace, [player name]. But I found it in the caves.
When I picked it up I felt strange... it was as if someone was watching to me, urging me to do something, but I don't know what!
I gave it to Tegdak. If you want to have it again you should talk to him.

options.condition: After completing Another Slice of H.A.M.:

steps.npc: I visited the goblin village again. I wanted to learn more about their legend of the 'Chosen Commander'.
But I didn't find out any more. They couldn't decide whether I really was the Chosen Commander or not, and they just got into a big argument about it.

standard-dialogue-with-ur-tag.speaker: Ur-tag
standard-dialogue-with-ur-tag.text: Zanik, the council is still very concerned about the city's safety. If you hear of any more H.A.M. activity on the surface, you must let me know.

standard-dialogue-with-ur-tag.npc: Don't worry, I'm sure [player name] will help keep us safe from the H.A.M. people!

standard-dialogue-with-ur-tag.speaker: Ur-tag
standard-dialogue-with-ur-tag.text: And another thing. If you must visit the surface, the council asks that you be careful not to offend the surface-dwellers' customs.

standard-dialogue-with-ur-tag.speaker: Ur-tag
standard-dialogue-with-ur-tag.text: Remember in particular to scrupulously observe the Lumbridge-Dorgeshuun treaty...

standard-dialogue-with-ur-tag.player: Hello, Zanik! What have you been up to?

standard-dialogue-with-oldak.npc: How are your studies going, Oldak?

standard-dialogue-with-oldak.speaker: Oldak
standard-dialogue-with-oldak.text: Oh! Zanik! It's fascinating. These 'runes' store a type of energy I've never encountered before.

standard-dialogue-with-oldak.speaker: Oldak
standard-dialogue-with-oldak.text: Yes. Each type of rune has its power tuned to a different effect, but they are all essentially the same energy.

standard-dialogue-with-oldak.speaker: Oldak
standard-dialogue-with-oldak.text: What I want to know is where this energy came from. The stone that these runes were cut from must be infused with an enormous amount of raw magical energy, but where did that energy come from?

standard-dialogue-with-oldak.npc: Maybe someday we'll find out! Oh, hello, [player name]!

standard-dialogue-with-oldak.player: Hello, Zanik! What have you been up to?

standard-dialogue-with-the-goblin-scribe.speaker: Goblin scribe
standard-dialogue-with-the-goblin-scribe.text: Tell me again about the surface. You said the cavern ceiling was how high?

standard-dialogue-with-the-goblin-scribe.npc: No, there was no cavern ceiling. Just a great expanse of blue sky!

standard-dialogue-with-the-goblin-scribe.speaker: Goblin scribe
standard-dialogue-with-the-goblin-scribe.text: You couldn't see how high the ceiling was because the sky was in the way. I see.

standard-dialogue-with-the-goblin-scribe.npc: No, you don't understand. There was NO ceiling. The surface is right on top of the world! There's no more rock above it!

standard-dialogue-with-the-goblin-scribe.speaker: Goblin scribe
standard-dialogue-with-the-goblin-scribe.text: I'm still having trouble getting my head around this 'surface' idea.

standard-dialogue-with-the-goblin-scribe.npc: Perhaps I should take you to see it?

standard-dialogue-with-the-goblin-scribe.speaker: Goblin scribe
standard-dialogue-with-the-goblin-scribe.text: Oh, no, no, no. I think I'd rather stay here and write about it.

standard-dialogue-with-the-goblin-scribe.player: Hello, Zanik! What have you been up to?

standard.npc: What are you doing bothering me? Don't you think some of us have work to do?

standard.player: I thought you were here to help?

standard.npc: Well... I am, I suppose, anyway... we're very busy here, hurry up, what do you want?

options.text: What is there to do in the Wizards' Guild?

steps.player: What is there to do in the Wizards' Guild?

steps.npc: This is the finest wizards' establishment in the land. We have magic portals to the other towers of wizardry around Gielinor. We have a particularly wide collection of runes in our rune shop. We sell some of the finest
mage robes in the land and we have a training area full of zombies for you to practice your magic on.

options.text: What are the requirements to get in the Wizards' Guild?

steps.player: What are the requirements to get in the Wizards' Guild?

steps.npc: You need a magic level of 66, the high magic energy level is too dangerous for anyone below that level.

options.text: What do you do in the Guild?

steps.player: What do you do in the Guild?

steps.npc: I'm the Grand Secretary for the Wizards' Guild, I have lots of correspondence to keep up with, as well as attending to the discipline of the more problematic guild members.

standard-dialogue-when-ringing-the-bell.text: Zavistic appears next to the player.

standard-dialogue-when-ringing-the-bell.npc: What are you doing ringing that bell?! Don't you think some of us have work to do?

standard-dialogue-when-ringing-the-bell.player: But I was told to ring the bell if I wanted some attention.

standard-dialogue-when-ringing-the-bell.npc: Well...anyway...we're very busy here, hurry up what do you want?

standard-dialogue-after-hand-in-the-sand.npc: What are you doing...Oh, it's you...sorry...didn't realise...what can I do for you?
Thank you so much for helping to lay Clarence to rest and lock up his murderer!

attempting-to-pickpocket-before-haunted-.text: I doubt he's got much of value on him.

options.text: I've done it, I've managed to recreate the salve amulet!

steps.player: I've done it, I've managed to recreate the salve amulet that you spoke of.

steps.text: If the player has not given the zealot his key back:

steps.npc: That hardly seems likely. There is no way you could have made it to the bottom of the mines without the key which is in my possession.

steps.player: I, er... found another way down.

steps.npc: Mock me not, this is a serious task I am undertaking. I don't have the time for your halfwitted attempt at humour.

options.text: Correction, the key that was in your possession.

steps.player: Correction, the key that was in your possession.

steps.npc: My key, where is it? You stole it?
Return that key to me now!

options.text: Ok, I've finished with it now anyway.

steps.player: Ok, I've finished with it now anyway.

steps.npc: Good, maybe all is not lost, despite your apparent lack of common sense.

options.text: Actually maybe I'll just keep hold of it for now.

steps.player: Actually, maybe I'll just keep hold of it for now.

steps.npc: Meddling fool, there are bigger things at stake here than you and your petty thieving intellect can understand.

steps.text: If the player has given the zealot his key back:

steps.npc: Then it is fortunate for us that Saradomin has guided you. Success certainly doesn't seem likely to have stemmed from rational behaviour on your part.

steps.player: You still haven't forgiven me for borrowing your key have you?

steps.npc: Borrowed!? You stole it!

steps.player: Er, maybe I'd better be going now.

options.text: What powers does the salve amulet have?

steps.player: What powers does the salve amulet have?

steps.npc: From what I have heard they would be put to best use in the slaying of the evil undead, the zombies and skeletons that walk this land.

after-haunted-mine-attempting-to-pickpoc.text: I don't want to annoy him any further.

standard.npc: A thousand greetings, sir.

steps.npc: Yes, certainly. I deal in scimitars.
Thank you.

options.text: Could you sell me a dragon scimitar?

steps.player: Could you sell me a dragon scimitar?

steps.npc: A dragon scimitar? A DRAGON scimitar?
The banana-brained nitwits who make them would never dream of selling any to me.

steps.text: If the player has not completed Monkey Madness I:

steps.npc: Seriously, you'll be a monkey's uncle before you'll ever hold a dragon scimitar.

steps.text: continue
If the player has completed Monkey Madness I:

steps.player: Hmmm, funny you should say that...

steps.text: continue

steps.npc: Perhaps you'd like to take a look at my stock?

options.text: What do you think of Ali Morrisane?
options.condition: After Rogue Trader

steps.player: What do you think about Ali Morrisane?

steps.npc: He is a dangerous man.
Although he does not appear to be dangerous, he has brought several men to this town who have threatened me and several others.
One man even threatened me with a hammer, saying that when he set up his smithy, my shoddy workmanship would be revealed!

steps.player: What will you do about these threats?

steps.npc: Oh, I am quite confident in the quality of my work...as will you be if you take a look at my wares.

using-an-al-kharid-flyer-on-zeke.player: Hi! I have this money-off voucher!

using-an-al-kharid-flyer-on-zeke.npc: So I see! Unfortunately, it seems to have expired yesterday! Nevermind.

using-an-al-kharid-flyer-on-zeke.player: But I only just got it!

using-an-al-kharid-flyer-on-zeke.npc: I'm sorry, there's nothing I can do.

treasure-trails-easy.text: When given another clue scroll:

steps.text: You've been given another clue!

treasure-trails-easy.text: When given a reward casket:

steps.text: You've obtained a casket!

standard.npc: Hey, are you wanting to try some of my fine wines and spirits? All brewed locally on Karamja island.

options.condition: During Alfred Grimhand's Barcrawl:

steps.npc: Ah, you'll be wanting some Ape Bite Liqueur then. It's got a lovely banana taste, and it'll only cost you 7 coins.

steps.text: If the player does not have 7 coins:

steps.player: I don't have 7 coins right now.

steps.text: If the player has 7 coins:
You buy some Ape Bite Liqueur.
You swirl it around and swallow it.
Zembo signs your card.

standard.npc: Hello there! I sell plate mail bodies, are you interested?

during-song-of-the-elves.npc: Hello there! I sell plate mail bodies, are you interested?

options.text: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

steps.player: I'm here to tell you about some new taxes.

steps.npc: I'm already paying my taxes though?

steps.player: These are new ones. They are to help pay for the king's upcoming visit to Great Kourend.

steps.text: If the player is wearing Ardougne knight armour:

steps.npc: Well I don't see why I have to pay for that! If the king can't afford the trip, then maybe he shouldn't be going!

steps.player: It's an important diplomatic trip I'm afraid so it has to go ahead. The first payment will be collected soon.

steps.text: If the player is wearing mourner gear:

steps.npc: And he's getting a mourner to tell me this? Nice try.

steps.text: If the player is not wearing mourner gear or Ardougne knight armour:

steps.npc: And he's getting a citizen to tell me this? Nice try.

standard.npc: Wall beast fingers! How about a tasty snack of wall beast fingers? Only 10gp!

steps.text: If the player has enough money:

steps.npc: There you go.

steps.text: If the player doesn't have enough money:

steps.player: But I don't have enough money on me.

steps.npc: Fingers!
Wall beast fingers!
Fresh wall beast fingers!
Lovely wall beast fingers!
Tasty wall beast fingers!

standard.npc: Wotcha guv'na!

standard.speaker: Nomad
standard.text: Hey! Talk to me if you want to know anything worth knowing.

standard.npc: Best talk to his highness over there, 'fore he goes gettin' upset.

options.text: What exactly is the Soul Obelisk?

steps.player: What exactly is the Soul Obelisk?

steps.npc: It's 'ard to say. Me master never told what it is or why he built it.

steps.player: Wait a second... He built it?

steps.npc: I saw 'im build it with me own eyes. I were the one who 'ad to carry his materials to this island!

steps.text: other

options.text: So what is Nomad really up to?

steps.player: So what is Nomad really up to?

steps.npc: Well, me master is as secretive as they come. Af'er all my time here, I still know next to nuffin' about him.
He's been up to summat since I've been here, but 'e had to have been an adventurer at some point. He has a massive stockpile of loot.

steps.player: He seems to know his way around some strange creatures too.

steps.npc: He does. He doesn't seem to care about that sorta stuff no more though. Since I've known 'im, he's only been obsessin' over gettin' as many people to play his game as possible.
Lost if I know. Like I said, 'e's as secretive as they come.

steps.text: other

options.text: Tell me how you got to be here.

steps.player: Tell me how you got to be here.

steps.npc: I don't really know. I just woke up one day and 'ad to obey me master's commands.
Aye. All I can remember before that is a glowing box and sumfin' to do with beads.

steps.player: It sounds like Nomad is quite the hunter.

steps.npc: What makes you say that?

steps.text: If the player is under level 71 Hunter:

steps.player: I read somewhere that skilled hunters can capture imps.

steps.npc: That's sad to hear. It's just so 'ard to ignore shiny beads when I see 'em.

steps.text: other

options.text: I'm quite the hunter myself, and some hunters like to capture imps.

steps.player: I'm quite the hunter myself, and some hunters like to capture imps.

steps.npc: Really? They abuse our love of beads just to test their skills?

steps.player: No need to worry, I'll give you no hassle. I'm only here to chat.

steps.npc: Phew!

steps.text: other

options.text: I'm quite the hunter myself, and I love capturing imps.

steps.player: I'm quite the hunter myself, and I love capturing imps.

steps.npc: Oh no!

steps.player: Only joking! I couldn't resist. Now, where were we?

steps.text: other

steps.npc: Bye!

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-attempt.text: You've got no reason to bother that poor imp.

soul-wars-demonstration-dialogue-near-th.npc: I can't really chit-chat with me Master 'round. Go see what he wants.

steps.npc: If I were as ugly as you I would not dare to show my face in public!
Out of my way, punk.
Hmm... you smell strange...
Like a human!

steps.player: Oh! Er... I just ate one is why!

steps.npc: Leave me alone.
Don't talk to me again if you value your life!
Get lost!
I don't have anything to give you so leave me alone, mendicant.
Have you no manners?
I don't have time for this right now.
I have no interest in talking to a pathetic meat bag like yourself.
I bet you have wonderful paws.
A very miserable day, altogether... enjoy it while it lasts.
If you catch anyone promise me you'll share.
I haven't smelt you around here before...
You smell familiar...
Seen any humans around here? I'm v-e-r-y hungry.
You look to me like someone with a healthy taste for blood.
Good day to you, my friend.
Fancy going up to the castle for a bit of a snack?
Give me a moment, I have a bit of someone stuck in my teeth...

standard-dialogue-when-using-the-right-c.speaker: Zombie
standard-dialogue-when-using-the-right-c.text: Durrrr...

standard-dialogue-when-using-the-right-c.speaker: Zombie
standard-dialogue-when-using-the-right-c.text: Who? Me?
The player performs the beckon emote.

standard-dialogue-when-using-the-right-c.speaker: Zombie
standard-dialogue-when-using-the-right-c.text: Give me a moment...I can't move that fast.

standard-dialogue-when-using-the-right-c.speaker: Zombie
standard-dialogue-when-using-the-right-c.text: I used to be a magician's assistant until the accident...

standard-dialogue-when-using-the-right-c.speaker: Zombie
standard-dialogue-when-using-the-right-c.text: Looook...
The zombie breaks in half at the waist, leaving behind an upper and a lower half.

standard-dialogue-when-using-the-right-c.speaker: Zombie
standard-dialogue-when-using-the-right-c.text: Braaaaains...

standard-dialogue-when-using-the-right-c.player: Zombie, it has come to my attention that you are a fool, a nitwit if you will.

standard-dialogue-when-using-the-right-c.text: The player performs the laugh emote.

standard-dialogue-when-using-the-right-c.player: I propose that your head, instead of being filled with the brains you so crave, is instead filled with a mixture of crushed lemons and kelp!

standard-dialogue-when-using-the-right-c.speaker: Zombie
standard-dialogue-when-using-the-right-c.text: Oh noooo..I'd best take it off then...
The zombie's head rolls off, leaving them headless.

standard-dialogue-when-using-the-right-c.speaker: Zombie
standard-dialogue-when-using-the-right-c.text: Traaa laaa laaa...
The player performs the cheer emote.

standard-dialogue-when-using-the-right-c.speaker: Zombie
standard-dialogue-when-using-the-right-c.text: Aaaaaargh!
The zombie splits in two, then splices the one half and the other half back together.

steps.speaker: Zombie Head
steps.text: What?

steps.speaker: Zombie Head
steps.text: I stuck my neck out for an old friend.

steps.player: You shouldn't get so cut up about it.

steps.speaker: Zombie Head
steps.text: Well if I keep it all bottled up I'll turn into a total head case.

steps.speaker: Zombie Head
steps.text: What?

steps.speaker: Zombie Head
steps.text: Mumblemumblemumble...

steps.speaker: Zombie Head
steps.text: My name is Edward Cranium.

steps.speaker: Zombie Head
steps.text: Har har...

steps.speaker: Zombie Head
steps.text: What now?

steps.speaker: Zombie Head
steps.text: Not any more...

steps.speaker: Zombie Head
steps.text: Because I used to be able to do a handstand for over an hour while juggling cannon balls with my feet...

steps.player: Wow, you were quite the entertainer.

steps.speaker: Zombie Head
steps.text: Yep. Now I can barely roll my eyes...

steps.player: I know what you can do!

steps.speaker: Zombie Head
steps.text: What?

steps.speaker: Zombie Head
steps.text: Don't even suggest it!

steps.speaker: Zombie Head
steps.text: Can't I rest in peace?

steps.player: Would you like a new hat?

steps.speaker: Zombie Head
steps.text: No, but could you screw a handle into the top of my head?

steps.speaker: Zombie Head
steps.text: Because currently you wave me about by my hair, and it hurts!

options.text: Want to go scare some people?

steps.speaker: Zombie Head
steps.text: Will you ever leave me alone?

steps.player: Want to go scare some people?

steps.speaker: Zombie Head
steps.text: Let's leave it for now.

steps.speaker: Zombie Head
steps.text: If I try really hard I might be able to will myself deader...

using-zombie-head-on-dr-fenkenstrain-dur.player: I have a winner for you here, Doctor! Look! It's still moving!

using-zombie-head-on-dr-fenkenstrain-dur.speaker: Zombie Head
using-zombie-head-on-dr-fenkenstrain-dur.text: Nobody knows the troubles I've seen...nobody knows my sorrow...

using-zombie-head-on-dr-fenkenstrain-dur.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
using-zombie-head-on-dr-fenkenstrain-dur.text: If that thing keeps wriggling around, I'll never get the stitches straight.

using-zombie-head-on-dr-fenkenstrain-dur.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
using-zombie-head-on-dr-fenkenstrain-dur.text: ...And who knows what problems will come up if we have an undead head on a truly dead body.

using-zombie-head-on-dr-fenkenstrain-dur.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
using-zombie-head-on-dr-fenkenstrain-dur.text: Bring me another head, one that isn't still moving

steps.npc: What if I start craving brains?

steps.player: Just eat a cauliflower or something!

steps.npc: I don't even know what one of those is!
This is so awful...

steps.player: Hang in there, brother, [player name] is on the case.

steps.npc: Something fell off! Something fell off!
I wish I was back in my own body.

steps.player: I'm working on it, okay? Give me a minute.

steps.npc: I can feel my brain thumping about in here when I shake my head.
I don't want to be stuck this way!
This body feels itchy...

steps.player: Likely that's all in the mind...

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-not-.speaker: Zombie pirate
standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-not-.text: I'm here to guard this ship from any scurvy dogs darin' to loot her cargo.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-not-.player: How did your ship end up here?

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-not-.speaker: Zombie pirate
standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-not-.text: Me hearties and I were enjoying a bit o' grog when we espied a group of landlubbers fightin' on the shore. 'Twas such an exciting battle that our navigator forgot to watch for the rocks.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-not-.speaker: Zombie pirate
standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-not-.text: Now we've run aground, as ye can see.

options.text: Where's the rest of your crew?

steps.player: Where's the rest of your crew?

steps.speaker: Zombie pirate
steps.text: They're searchin' for booty at that temple to the west.

steps.player: Will they return to the ship?

steps.speaker: Zombie pirate
steps.text: They best do! That scurvy lot keep fillin' their lockers with loot and sneakin' off without swappin' places!

options.text: Do you really want to go to the temple?

steps.player: Do you really want to go to the temple? I've heard the mages there have some really annoying spells.

steps.speaker: Zombie pirate
steps.text: Nothin' we can't handle! We've a way of stoppin' their tricksy teleports.

steps.player: How can a group of mindless zombies invent a counter to magic?

steps.speaker: Zombie pirate
steps.text: What we lack in brains, we make up for in gold! We found us a landlubber willin' to share their knowledge... for a price.

steps.speaker: Zombie pirate
steps.text: They wrote us down a spell on some magic scrolls. All we 'ave to do is read one, and then we're properly anchored! Those mages can't teleport us anywhere!

steps.player: Wow, I'm actually impressed. Do you think your friends at the temple will lend me one?

steps.speaker: Zombie pirate
steps.text: Naw, they're too busy fightin' to talk to the likes of ye. Besides, we stash all our spare scrolls in these lockers for safekeepin'.

steps.player: Can I take a scroll from a locker, then?

steps.speaker: Zombie pirate
steps.text: Ye'll need a key for that, matey! One of the crew should 'ave one.

steps.speaker: Zombie pirate
steps.text: And when ye see 'em, tell 'em it's their turn to keep watch!

steps.speaker: Zombie pirate
steps.text: There be plenty o' loot in them lockers, matey. Don't expect to find a scroll right away.

steps.player: Thanks. I'd say 'see you around', but I sort of hope I don't.

steps.speaker: Zombie pirate
steps.text: Aye, the feelin's mutual.

steps.player: Goodbye, I hope your crew comes back soon.

steps.speaker: Zombie pirate
steps.text: Arr, me too matey.

steps.speaker: Zombie pirate
steps.text: Bye, matey.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-lear.player: Do you really want to go to the temple? I've heard the mages there have some really annoying spells.

standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-lear.speaker: Zombie pirate
standard-dialogue-if-the-player-has-lear.text: Nothin' we can't handle! We've a way of stoppin' their tricksy teleports.

standard.speaker: Zombie pirate
standard.text: Arr, I've still not seen any of my crew.

options.text: Can you tell if I've used the Teleport anchoring scroll?

steps.player: Can you tell if I've used the Teleport anchoring scroll?

steps.text: If the player has not used the teleport anchoring scroll:

steps.speaker: Zombie pirate
steps.text: Aye, I can tell by the cut of your jib that ye haven't yet read the Teleport anchoring scroll.
If the player has used the teleport anchoring scroll:

steps.speaker: Zombie pirate
steps.text: Aye, I can tell by the cut of your jib that you've read the Teleport anchoring scroll.

options.text: How many times have I opened your lockers?

steps.player: How many times have I opened your lockers?

steps.text: If the player has never opened the Zombie Pirate's Locker:

steps.speaker: Zombie pirate
steps.text: Ye've never done it even once!
If the player has opened the Zombie Pirate's Locker once only:

steps.speaker: Zombie pirate
steps.text: Ye've done it once, and once only.
If the player has opened the Zombie Pirate's Locker more than once:

steps.speaker: Zombie pirate
steps.text: Ye've done it [#] times.

options.text: I'll leave you to wait for your crew.

steps.player: I'll leave you to wait for your crew.

check-option.text: If the player has not used the teleport anchoring scroll and has never opened the Zombie Pirate's Locker:

steps.speaker: Zombie pirate
steps.text: I can tell by the cut of your jib that ye haven't yet read the Teleport anchoring scroll, and ye've never opened our lockers.

check-option.text: If the player has not used the teleport anchoring scroll and has opened the Zombie Pirate's Locker once only:

steps.speaker: Zombie pirate

standard.npc: It's not often that we see more humans in this place.

options.text: How did you come to be here?

steps.player: How did you come to be here?

steps.npc: General Hining sent us out in a scouting party. We got separated from the rest, and became completely lost. Soon we ran out of rations.
Eventually we stumbled upon this place. They saw we were starving, and allowed us to eat of their sacred eels if we vowed to serve Zulrah.
Since then, we've settled here. We went back up north once, to see how the king's campaign was going, but they drove us out of the camp, calling us unclean.
It's probably the sacred eels that did it. They change you, you know. Once you've tasted them, you're part of the tribe forever.

standard.npc: Nilsal, [player name].
A lot less stressful up here. I think I might leave the adventuring to people like you from now on.
Still, at least it gave me a lot to talk about. Those Moons of Peril are concerning, but exciting! I just wish we knew more about their potential links to Ranul.

standard.player: So you still think there is a link?

standard.npc: Oh yes. It may not have been the one I originally thought, but there must be something! They're called Moons after all!
The all-powerful Ranul wouldn't have just let some random creatures take on a name like that!
Indeed. And on that note, I have some research to do! Until next time.
